articleTitle: Radiation Pattern Correction in Self-Decoupled STAR Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A self-decoupling method is proposed for two hexagonal patch antennas separated by distance 0.004λ0 at 2.54 GHz with the feature of pattern reshaping. The technique blocks fringing field coupling with two groups of shorting pins symmetrically placed along the hexagonal patch's opposite edges. An appropriate offset between two groups of pins brings balance among mutual capacitive and inductive coupling, improving isolation by 27.3 dB. The study demonstrates that the symmetric placement of shorting pins on the simultaneous transmit and receive antenna edge corrects the H-plane radiation pattern by 24° towards the broadside direction (0°).

articleTitle: Miniaturized MIMO Antenna Designed for Biomedical Telemetry System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This research presents an ultra-miniaturized MIMO antenna system tailored for efficient operation within the 2.45 GHz of the industrial, scientific, and medical (ISM) band, specifically addressing the requirements of biomedical implants. The proposed MIMO antenna showcases exceptional compactness, occupying a small volume of 2.65 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> (i.e., <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4.9\ \text{mm} \times 4.5 \text{mm} \times 0.12\ \text{mm}$</tex>). This compact design is achieved through the strategic utilization of meandered resonators. Despite its highly miniaturized form and slotted ground ensuring high isolation between ports, the antenna system attains a good peak gain of -26.8 dB at 2.45 GHz. This achievement is particularly noteworthy, highlighting the antenna's suitability for biomedical telemetry systems. Additionally, the antenna exhibits omnidirectional radiation patterns. This characteristic ensures consistent and reliable signal coverage in diverse orientations, meeting the specific needs of the targeted application. The emphasis on ultra-miniaturization underscores the practicality of this antenna system and its potential applications in biomedical devices.

articleTitle: Non-Invasive Glucose Detection Using a Triple Cell Square CSRR Sensor: Experimental Validation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a microwave biosensor for the non-invasive detection of blood glucose levels is designed. The proposed sensor, sized <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$55.6 \mathrm{x}20\mathrm{x}1.5 \text{mm}^3$</tex>, consists of three cells of square complementary split ring resonators. The proposed sensor is placed on top of an FR4 dielectric substrate. The sensor elements are excited via a coupled 50-ohm microstrip line etched on the bottom side of the substrate. The HFSS has been used for the design and parametric analysis of the proposed Triple Cell Square Complementary Split Ring Resonator (TC-SCSRR). The fabricated sensor is validated by In Vitro experiments in which de-ionized aqueous glucose solutions of different concentrations (70 mg/dL - 1000 mg/dL) are used. A shift of the resonant frequency of transmission response is observed due to the change in input impedance, caused by different levels of glucose in aqueous solutions. The results revealed high sensitivity of the proposed sensor. The high sensitivity, size, and sensing range of operation make the proposed TC-SCSRR a promising candidate for the handheld non-invasive blood glucose monitoring device.

articleTitle: Design of Wideband Flared Wire Monopole for Microwave Imaging of Biological Tissues
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Design and simulation of flared wire monopole antenna inside the imaging tank is presented for biomedical applications. The performance of the proposed monopole is evaluated in the presence of coupling liquid for impedance matching. The surface current density along inner conductor and outer conductor were analyzed to evaluate antenna performance. Electromagnetic (EM) simulations indicate| S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>| less than -15 dB and mutual coupling below -20 dB over 0.5 - 2 GHz in annular arrangement. Numerical simulations of the proposed antenna in the presence of dielectric scatterer with permittivity of breast tissue indicate the feasibility of the using this antenna for imaging applications.

articleTitle: Low-Cost System for the Manual Measurement of the Electric Field Over 3-D Domains
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: We present a system to measure the electric field distribution of radiating systems over domains swept manually by a human operator which provides significant time, cost, and complexity savings with respect to conventional acquisition methods. The system is divided into four main blocks: (1) generation of the signal used to excite the antenna under test, (2) position tracking, to evaluate the location of the field sensor during the sweep, (3) acquisition, which determines the field amplitude during the sweep, and (4) control and data integration, which coordinates the operation of the previous three blocks. The experimental validation of the system demonstrates very good accuracy against reference data using a fast and simple acquisition process.

articleTitle: Highly Directional Scattering of Terahertz Radiation by Cylinders Using Complex-Frequency Waves
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this study we investigate the directional scattering of terahertz radiation by dielectric cylinders, focusing on the enhancement of directionality using incident radiation of complex-frequency. We explore the optimization of the second Kerker condition, which corresponds to backward scattering. Additionally, we present preliminary results on the directional scattering of THz radiation by a magneto-optical cylinder, demonstrating the potential of this approach for advanced control over the propagation of THz waves.

articleTitle: Compact Low-Loss Selective Coupler (CLSC) Concept for Insertion Loss, Mutual Coupling and Size Miniaturization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a new class of feeding network which exhibits compact, low-loss, high isolation. By using multiple stub lines, compact, low-loss, selective coupler (CLSC) is implemented. The proposed CLSC demonstrates a transmission coefficient of over -1.5 dB and an isolation value of over -30 dB across a frequency band spanning from 24 GHz to 50 GHz for demonstration purposes. This study enables miniaturization of the insertion loss, mutual coupling, and overall dimension of the entire feeding network structure and can be applicable to various microwave and millimeter-wave (mmWave) applications.

articleTitle: Dual Band Planar Antenna For Millimeter Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This article presents a dual-band planar antenna printed on an CaO-B2O3-SiO2 glass-ceramics substrate for millimeter-wave applications. The designed antenna has an overall size of 9 mm× 9 mm. The antenna exhibits good performance in terms of bandwidth, gain, and radiation efficiency, making it a good candidate for millimeter-wave (mmWave).

articleTitle: Mixer-Fed Antenna Array for Shaped Beam Scanning with Reduced Beamformers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Mixers are integrated into a phased array feed to allow for beam shaping and beam steering with a reduced number of phase shifters and variable-gain amplifiers. By exploiting the phase-addition properties of mixers, it is possible to feed an antenna array with rows and columns of amplitude and phase-controlled signals. The array can generate the phasing necessary to scan a single beam across the full half-space, and beam shaping can be achieved by controlling signal amplitudes. Compared to a conventional phase array with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{N}^{\ast}\mathbf{M}$</tex> beamformers for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{N}^{\ast}\mathbf{M}$</tex> array elements, this technique only requires <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{N}+\mathbf{M}$</tex> beamformers. Measurements from a proof-of-concept <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$8\mathrm{x}8$</tex> element transmitting array show scanned Chebyshev array factors that closely match the expected patterns.

articleTitle: A Mono-Static RIS Qualification Method Introducing an Ideal Metal Reflector as Reference
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) are expected to improve the connectivity in up-coming 6G mobile networks at a relatively low energy consumption level. They are designed based on reconfigurable unit cells defining a phase taper on the surface that is redirecting an impinging wave into a desired direction to improve the coverage. Generally, their RF measurement characterization is quite cumbersome, since it involves a full bi-static measurement approach (4 dimensional). Moreover, the RIS's exhibits abnormal reflection properties and can therefore not be directly compared to simple metallic references, e.g. an ideal metal reflector of same form factor, since they exhibit only specular reflections. To overcomes these issues, we propose a simple mono-static RIS qualification method and introduce a metallic reference reflector scenario for comparison. Simulation and measurement results are given for a fixed beam reflection surface that emulates an RIS.

articleTitle: Mechanistically Independent Tunable Dual Band FSS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents the conception of a novel dual-band FSS structure with independently tunable passbands. Tunability of each passband is individually achieved through mechanistically altering the coupling capacitance by laterally translating one layer of the FSS. The design procedure and the performance of the FSS analyzed, with the passbands able to be separately tuned in the ranges 2.45 to 2.78 GHz and 3.8 to 4.55 GHz. The FSS also exhibits a very low profile with an overall thickness of 0.75 mm.

articleTitle: Smart-Watch Integrated Flexible Strap Antenna for Enhanced WiFi and Bluetooth Connectivity Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a smartwatch strap-embedded antenna tailored for WiFi and Bluetooth-based applications within the 2.4 GHz frequency bands. Placing the antenna within the smartwatch strap rather than the watch's housing with other electronic components mitigates electromagnetic interference, ensuring optimal antenna performance in wireless communication applications. The antenna exhibits a realized gain of 10.21 dBi in the unbent case and 7.23 dBi when bent at an angle of 125°. The input power of 50 mW (17 dBm) is utilized for specific absorption rate (SAR) analysis when averaged over 10g of human tissue. The SAR result indicates a safe radiation level of 0.90 W/kg, well within the ICNIRP-specified limit of 2 W/kg over 10g of tissue. This research contributes to the enhancement of smartwatch communication capabilities by facilitating the provision for an antenna to be embedded while ensuring compliance with rigorous safety standards.

articleTitle: Near-Field Scanning System for Enhanced Bio-Sensing at Low Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper introduces a near-field scanning system designed for bio-sensing applications, with a primary focus on operating at low frequencies. The system, operating in close proximity, utilizes the near-field scanning method and leverages evanescent waves to enhance resolution and accuracy. By capitalizing on the advantages of low frequencies, the proposed system achieves greater penetration into the human body, revealing finer details crucial for precise bio-sensing, though with a compromise in resolution. Employing a near-field scanning technique, the system detects subtle variations in the biological properties of the human body. This underscores its efficacy in capturing intricate details while compensating for the reduced resolution. Simulations and measurement results highlight the system's proficiency in detecting 10% deviations in physiological parameters, achieved through mechanical scanning steps of 1 cm.

articleTitle: Propagation Path Analysis during Shadowing of a Human Body at 300 GHz
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The study assessed the direction of arrival (DOA) and delay characteristics of propagation waves in a 300 GHz band radio link when the human body interrupts the line-of-sight propagation path. When there is a gap between the torso and the arm, the reflection wave inside the arm exhibited about 17 dB higher amplitude than the diffraction wave at the torso. Furthermore, when the human body was clothed, the DOA of the propagation path expanded in the direction parallel to the arm, and the delay profile widened by more than 0.23 ns.

articleTitle: Modeling and Design of Aperture Coupled Microstrip Patch Antennas with Dual-Offset Feedline
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper describes a methodology for designing feed networks for single-polarized aperture-coupled microstrip patch (ACMP) antennas with dual-offset microstrip feedlines. The method involves characterizing the effective series impedance of the antenna when it is fed in a balanced manner as a function of the distance between the dual feedlines. Fitting equations were generated from the data to relate the effective series impedance to the feed geometry, allowing the design of the matching network for any effective impedance. This work demonstrates that ACMP antennas can be coupled to dual-offset feedlines with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda/4$</tex> transformers and T-junctions with infinite combinations of impedance for the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda/4$</tex> transformer. A 10 GHz single-polarized ACMP antenna was designed and implemented obtaining satisfactory impedance matching.

articleTitle: Non-Destructive Fabrication Fault Detection in Electromagnetic Designs using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Engineers simulate a desired structure and fabricate it once the simulated design gives the desired results. However, due to imperfections in fabrication techniques, most of the time, the fabricated structure does not match the simulated structure. This might be due to differences in the dimensions of simulated and fabricated structures due to fabrication imperfections. However, it is difficult to pinpoint which part or dimension of the structure was fabricated wrong which led to unexpected results. In this work, we propose a machine learning-based approach to assess the dimensional faults in electromagnetic designs. The paper discusses the involved method and its robustness for such fault detections.

articleTitle: Progress in Wave-Controlled RIS: Experimental Demonstration of Biasing Voltage Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: We report on the experimental demonstration of DC voltage generation for biasing varactors of a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) using a novel approach involving the use of multiple resonant standing waves on a biasing transmission line (TL) at a layer below the RF reflective surface. This allows dynamic control of the DC voltage distribution for the individual RIS elements through a single cable delivering a time-domain periodic waveform.

articleTitle: A Novel Quantum Binary Evolutionary Algorithm for EM Applications: bGA-QCO
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: It is possible to effectively study most of engineering optimization problems suitably rephrased in binary via Evolutionary Algorithms. Even so, the fitness function computation, typically dealing with antenna design, may be very time consuming. Therefore, it is very important to speed up the convergency and to improve the performances of these algorithms, and the introduction of quantum computing seems to open new perspectives, where new approaches have to be considered to exploit the specificity of these instruments. In this paper, a novel quantum version of the binary Genetic Algorithm, bGA, has been introduced, bGA-QCO, and tested on a benchmark function and on a thinned array design.

articleTitle: Image Quality Analysis for Different Frequency Sparsity Schemes in Wideband Imaging Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper the effect of random sparsity of frequency samples on the wideband microwave image quality is explored. Three modes of sparsity are developed for a practical imaging system with frequency ranging from 10 to 20 GHz. In each mode, a specific portion of the frequency samples are omitted either from the whole band, the lower half of the band, or the upper half of the band. The measured results show 98.78% agreement between the full image and the image in which 25% sparsity is applied to the upper half of the band, while this agreement is 87.30% for the sparsity applied on the lower half of the band.

articleTitle: History of the Antennas and Propagation Society Commitment to Electromagnetics Education Celebrating AP-S Vision and Pioneering Contributions in EM Education
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Concepts of electromagnetics (EM), so familiar to practitioners, yet so mysterious and challenging to young hands. EM is abstract and highly mathematical subjects but can benefit most from modern computer technologies and software tools The Antennas and Propagation Society (AP-S) played a key leadership role (pioneered) the use of computers and software tools in teaching and learning of electromagnetics IEEE on behalf of AP-S received an NSF grant in 1989 to establish the “Center for Computer Applications in Electromagnetic Education (CAEME) It is through the remarkable vision of APS pioneers; Irene Peden, David Chang, and late Bob Collin that CAEME flourished and provided lasting benefits to EM education. In this paper we celebrate APS visionary achievement and acknowledge those who made it possible. In this presentation we describe CAEME activities, acknowledge key players who contributed to its success, demonstrate CAEME products in software modules, video clips, and multimedia assets, and urge APS community to continue this aspiration, as AI and Chat GPT provide modern enablers to effective teaching and better understanding of electromagnetics.

articleTitle: A Cylindrical Dielectric Resonator Antenna with Elliptical Slots for 5G-Millimeter Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A dielectric resonator antenna is one of the most attractive antenna structures in the field of wireless communications due to its important features. This work proposes a dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) for 5G millimeter-wave applications. The proposed design is excited by two cross slots through a microstrip feed line and is evaluated using High-frequency structure simulator (HFSS) software with an overall size is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{30} \times \mathbf{25} \times \mathbf{0.8}\ \mathbf{mm}^{\mathbf{3}}$</tex>. The proposed antenna offers a simulated impedance bandwidth of 10 to 30 GHz for a 5G millimeter-band wireless communication system. Simulation results show that the proposed structure exhibits a coherent gain of 5 dB and an efficiency value of more than 80%.

articleTitle: Photodiode as Tuning Element for Metasurface Intelligent Reflecting Surface Based on Steer by Image Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: New tuning technology for metasurface intelligent reflecting surface is presented in this study. Photodiode is used as the tuning element in this case. The control over the reflected beam is done by projecting an image to the back side of the reflector rather than using hundreds of D/A channels and FPGA board as it is today.

articleTitle: Experimental Setup for Path Loss Measurements at mmWave Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this contribution we present an experimental setup for the characterization of channel path loss at millimeter wave frequencies and selected results from our measurement campaign. Our channel sounder integrates several hardware and software components, enabling measurements at 26 GHz, a band singled out for the future deployment of 5G systems in the millimeter wave band in Colombia. Some of these experimental results fit very well the 3GPP TR 38.901 standard propagation model.

articleTitle: A Wideband Reconfigurable-Polarization Slot-Ring Phased Array Antenna for Sub-6 GHz
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper introduces a wideband slot-ring phased array antenna for sub-6 GHz applications. Incorporating meandered lines in the slot ring significantly improves the bandwidth performance of this antenna. The operation frequency of this antenna ranges from 2.87 to 4.91 GHz corresponding to a fractional bandwidth of 53%. The spacing between antenna elements in the 2 x 2 array is maintained at 0. 5Ao at the center frequency. This array demonstrates the ability of beam steering to ±30 degrees. In addition, the gain of the 2 x 2 array is shown to be 10 dBi. The coax-to-microstrip feeding technique is used to excite each antenna element. Notably, this array is able to achieve different polarization states (horizontal, vertical, and circular) by simply changing the phase at each port.

articleTitle: A Broadband All-Metal Cross-Dipole Sub-Array for 2G/3G/LTE Base Station Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a lightweight miniaturized dual-polarized (±45°) crossed-dipole antenna element operating in 1400–2700 MHz frequency band (63% FBW) for base station applications. The dimensions of the proposed antenna are 63.6 mm × 63.6 mm × 42 mm which makes the biggest dimension 0.43λ at the center frequency (2.05 GHz). The miniaturization is achieved by bending the edge of the radiating part and increasing its electrical length. Modifications in the power divider section improve impedance matching and tilt the beam to 6°, which is desired for cellular applications. The measured and simulated reflection coefficient and the isolation are better than -15dB and 25 dB in the whole bandwidth, respectively. The realized gain and HPBW are between 8.5 dBi and 11 dBi, and 55 degrees and 75 degrees, respectively which are promising for mobile standards technologies (GSM-1800/UMTS-2100/LTE-1800/LTE-2100/LTE-2600).

articleTitle: Gain Enhancement of a Dual Circularly Polarized Patch Antenna based on Electromagnetic Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper outlines an effective method to enhance the gain of a microstrip patch antenna while preserving its polarization characteristics. The proposed solution features a double coaxially fed circular radiating slot-patch antenna etched on a dielectric substrate, with a metasurface positioned above as a superstrate. The metasurface presence enables a gain increase of approximately 5 dBi, confirming both Right-Hand and Left-Hand Circular Polarizations (RHCP and LHCP) while ensuring their isolation. The numerical results obtained from accurate full-wave simulations show that the configuration can attain an Axial Ratio (AR) below 3 dB throughout the entire Half Power Beamwidth (HPBW), with a gain of 9.6 dBi at 412 MHz.

articleTitle: A Tunable Reflection Surface with Independently Variable Phase and Slope
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) is an essential component in the architecture of the next generation of wireless communication systems. An RIS is deployed to provide a controllability to the multi-path environment between the transmitter and the receiver, which becomes critical when the line-of-sight signal between them is blocked. In this work, we design an electrically tunable linearly polarized RIS at 2.5 GHz that yields a controllable reflection phase and phase-frequency slope; in other words, we add tunability of the phase-frequency slope to the tunability of the resonance center frequency. The proposed design consists of two layers of unit cells placed over a ground plane, with dog-bone-shaped elements in the top layer and patch elements in the bottom layer. Each patch and dog-bone element is loaded with a varactor, whose reverse bias voltage is controlled to provide a phase-frequency profile with a slope value of 9 degrees/MHz or 0.95 degrees/MHz, and a phase shift range of 320 degrees,

articleTitle: Dual and Complementary-Impedance Metasurfaces for Enhanced Line Waves
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a new dual and complementary-impedance metasurface platform for studying Line Waves (LWs), electromagnetic modes at interfaces of different metasurfaces like capacitive and inductive types. The excited states, characterized by efficient one-dimensional propagation and tight interface confinement, hold promise for robust waveguide applications, especially within fifth-generation (5G) technology. The research shows that LW, supporting broadband frequencies, can be tuned through capacitive or inductive properties, with a semi-analytical model developed for in-depth analysis. Additionally, a parallel plate waveguide composed of four metasurfaces demonstrates LW robust transmission capabilities, even under longitudinal warping. This highlights their potential in wearable wireless communications and flexible electronics, showcasing their adaptability and efficiency.

articleTitle: Wide Band, High Gain Substrate Integrated Waveguide Dielectric Resonator Antenna for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In the proposed design, Substrate Integrated Waveguide (SIW) is used with higher order mode Dielectric Resonator Antenna (DRA) which is excited by aperture on the top of ground plane. This design is used for 5G mm wave bands, N257 (28GHz band) and N258 (26GHz band), with impedance bandwidth of 24.15-29.87 (21.2%) due to multiple resonant frequency of DRA modes, X slot excitation. The design provides high gain of 6@25, 7.7@26.2, 8@28.4GHz whereas radiation efficiency more than 90% is observed. In addition, good radiation pattern w.r.t co polarized performance were obtained. All Simulation are done using Ansys HFSS (High Frequency Structure Simulator) version 2023.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized Two-Element Fractal Antenna with Integrated Metasurface Isolator for UWB-MIMO Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a novel two-element antenna based on the Mandelbrot fractal geometry is designed for UWB-MIMO application. By using a fractal radiation patch antenna to miniaturize the size of the broadband monopole antenna, the fractal structure reduces the dimension by about 39.1% compared to a circular radiator and about 48.5% compared to a rectangular radiator. To reduce the coupling between two integrated MIMO antenna elements, a metasurface structured electromagnetic-bandgap with complementary split ring resonator (CSRR) slots is used to enhance isolation. The proposed antenna achieves a wideband from 1.28 GHz to 8.28 GHz, and obtains a high isolation of greater than 19 dB in the desired operating band.

articleTitle: Metasurface-Enhanced Bio-Sensing Radar for Advanced Health Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Introducing a metasurface-enhanced radar system for advanced bio-sensing applications, this paper underscores its potential for non-invasive, real-time wearable health monitoring and precision in detecting physiological parameters. The system utilizes a transmissive metasurface to dynamically shape the near- field radiation of a millimeter-wave radar transmitter antenna, focusing within the human body's skin. Comprising two layers of phase-synthesized unit cells, the metasurface acts as a low-profile near-field impedance matching network, seamlessly integrating with radar operating within the 58 to 63 GHz frequency band and establishing direct contact with the human body skin. Simulations and measurements within a customized phantom closely resembling human skin demonstrate that integrating the metasurface increases the near-field absorbed power density by over 11 dB. This improvement is accompanied by a significant increase of over 11 dB in the received power level reflected from the skin to the radar receiver antenna, enhancing the overall radar signal-to-noise ratio.

articleTitle: 3D Wide-Angle Beam-Scanning Compound Lens Using A Fast Hybrid Optimization Workflow
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a wide-angle beam-scanning 3D compound Gradient Index (GRIN) lens antenna designed with a highly efficient optimization workflow. Compound lenses offer improved scan loss over single-lens antennas through the addition of the second focal lens. The focal lens is close to a flat feed array and improves illumination efficiency by directing feed beams toward the center of the aperture lens. However, compound lens optimization is difficult due to high parameterization complexity and the need to simulate multiple feed positions. To address the optimization complexity, a novel hybrid optimization workflow is proposed, comprising a first stage of fast curved-ray Geometrical Optics (GO) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), followed by a 2D Finite Difference Time Domain (FDTD) method, and finally validated in full-wave simulation. The proposed workflow exploits parallel computing and is capable of exploring a large parameter space and iterating over 50,000 candidate designs in 4 days (>500 large-scale simulations per hour). A demonstration compound lens antenna was designed and achieved a wide beam- scanning range up to ±55°, while maintaining a low frequency- averaged scan loss exponent of 2.25 across the Ka-Band.

articleTitle: A Wideband Co-Linearly Polarized Sub-Grid Array Antenna-on-Display (AoD) Concept for Integration of Sensing and Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents an unprecedented grid array antenna-on-display (AoD) topology featuring wideband and multifunctional properties for the first time in literature. The design features a folded open comb line structure for the traveling wave technique. The proposed AoD is devised, and both passive and active types of feeding networks are devised to validate wideband characteristics. An eight-sub grid array AoD is exemplified and integrated with a real-life OLED display panel. Experimental results confirm that the newly proposed AoD topology achieves a wide scanning angle of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 45^{\circ}$</tex> across the radar and communication spectrum in the 24 to 40 GHz range. This ascertains that the proposed grid array AoD topology is fully compatible with the display panel for high scanning-rate radar sensing and communication applications.

articleTitle: Ray Tracing Simulation Study on a Real 27 GHz Case Scenario
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Fifth generation technologies propose new electromagnetic field propagation scenarios. Predicting the electric field levels generated by new generation systems is a key topic both in terms of coverage and exposure levels assessment. Aim of this work is to present a ray tracing simulation study on a millimeter-wave scenario. Simulations have been performed considering a real urban scenario in which a 27 GHz antenna is located. Simulations have been performed with different software tools and the results showed a good agreement. This work can be particularly useful to compare simulations results with on-site measurements to assess the electromagnetic field levels coverage and coexistence.

articleTitle: Planar Yagi-Uda ESPAR Array for mm-Wave Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A planar Yagi-Uda electronically steerable parasitic array radiator (ESPAR) antenna array is proposed for mm-Wave communications. The array is comprised of three Yagi-Uda antennas, each with a dipole element and a shared ground plane reflector. The design operates with a 30 GHz center frequency and a 20% usable fractional bandwidth. By terminating the parasitic element feeding lines with adjustable reactive loads, the array is capable of beam steering to establish 90° coverage in simulation with 7dBi gain.

articleTitle: Beyond the Scalp: Numerical SAR and Performance Comparison of Two 4-Band PIFAs for Brain Implants
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: We compare the radiation performance and the specific absorption rate (SAR) of two brain-implantable PIFAs operating in the Medical Device Radiocommunication Service (MedRadio) band (401–406 MHz), Wireless Medical Telemetry Service (WMTS) band (1427–1432), and Industrial, Scientific and Medical (ISM) bands (902–928 MHz and 2400-2483.5 MHz). The two antennas have the same total thickness and occupy the same volume, but one is based on a single substrate layer and the other also includes superstrate. A feature shared by the two antennas was that the maximum SAR occurred at the interface between the biocompatible encapsulation layer and the surrounding tissues, whereas neither antenna performed superior to the other in terms of SAR or the radiation performance considering all four operating frequencies.

articleTitle: Robotic Arm-Based Antenna Measurement System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: An in house robotic arm-based antenna measurement system is presented. The need for a flexible measurement system to work at millimeter-wave bands (mmW) is the main motivation of this work. At the moment the system is programmed to perform planar acquisitions of 80 mm × 80 mm up to 67 GHz. Post-processing techniques in order to reduce the effect of the non-anechoic environment and acquisition time have also been implemented. The system has been validated by means of measurements in the K-band with very good agreement with reference measurement performed in a spherical range in anechoic chamber.

articleTitle: Directivity and Mutual Coupling of Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Mutual radiation resistance(MRR) is a real part of mutual impedance(MI), when the currents on the antenna are expressed by a real function. In this study, to consider the MRR and MI functions, the hypothesis stating that “the primitively estimated array gain with mutual coupling considered under the single-mode current assumption (PEAGMS)” corresponds to “the array directivity with an isolated element pattern used (ADIEU)” is presented and verified analytically for a two-element array and numerically for a l0-element array. The results show that the PEAGMS agrees very well with the ADIEU. Thus, from an engineering point of view, calculating directivity using pattern integration is equivalent to considering mutual coupling under a single-mode current assumption.

articleTitle: Data-efficient and Ultra-fast Surrogate Models for Simulating Nanophotonic Power-splitters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper we explore neural-network based surrogate models for simulating the response of nanophotonic power splitters with arbitrary split ratios. In particular we investigate the hypothesis that using internal fields as an intermediate variable helps reduce the data requirements for network training. We deploy the recently proposed U-Net and Fourier Neural Operator (FNO) approaches to learn the relation between a pixel-based input device geometry and the intermediate fields and cascade them with another neural network to arrive at the modal transmittance. We compare our finding against naive approaches that directly learn the relation between the input device geometry and transmittance, and find a six fold reduction in the training root mean square error value. This research opens the route to faster and more data efficient approaches to inverse design of nanophotonic devices.

articleTitle: Bandwidth Enhancement of a Probe-Fed Patch Antenna through Shape Modification Using a Gaussian Function
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Traditional probe-fed patch antennas are narrowband structures. Several approaches have been suggested to improve the bandwidth while retaining the shape of the patch. In this paper, the triangular patch is used as a starting point for investigating bandwidth enhancement by evolving the shape. The shape evolution is dictated by enforcing variations of a Gaussian function on the three sides. It is shown that through the application of a surrogate-based optimization technique, an impedance bandwidth of ~ 12.5 % can be achieved in a probe-fed configuration. Indeed, improving the bandwidth while retaining the simplicity of the feed results in a trade-off regarding the increased complexity of the patch shape.

articleTitle: Coverage Analysis of an RFID System for the Identification and Localization of a Queen Bee in a Hive
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: An analysis of the coverage of an RFID system in the UHF band, in free space and inside a beehive was carried out, in order to prove that the queen bee can be located and identified inside a beehive, without the need to do it visually. A near field link budget was calculated and compared with measurements in free space. The measurement system consists of a reader and two tags, with dimensions <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3\mathrm{x}3\text{mm}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3\mathrm{x}4\text{mm}$</tex>. Results show that there was a significant increase in the reading range distance of the system, when measuring inside of the beehive, with respect to free space.

articleTitle: The Latest Aperture Array Verification System AAVS3 for the World's Largest Radio Telescope
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The mission of the SKA Observatory is to build and operate cutting-edge radio telescopes to transform our understanding of the Universe and deliver benefits to society. To fulfill this mission, the SKA radio telescopes have to deal with challenges never faced before. One of the most challenging aspects, especially for the SKA-Low radio telescope, working between 50 and 350 MHz is the calibration, done at different levels, of such a complex telescope in such a harsh environment. Prototyping of the front end, as well as of some of the backend components, is essential in order to evaluate the real behavior of the aperture array and develop and test calibration procedures and propose improvements to make sure that the requirements needed are achieved. This paper presents the latest SKA-Low Aperture Array Verification System version 3 and how this contributes to the risk mitigation and decision making for some fundamental aspects of the SKA-Low radio telescope.

articleTitle: The International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation: A 60-Year History
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The 60-year history of the International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation is summarized. A list of locations, general chairs, and technical programs chairs from 1963 to the present is presented.

articleTitle: Aperture-Shared Dual-Band Digital Leaky-Wave Antenna for Intelligent Radiation Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This work presents a novel aperture-shared dual-band digital leaky-wave antenna (LWA) for intelligent wireless communications. Inspired by the digital metasurfaces and reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS), the digital coding concept is firstly introduced in the leaky-wave radiation. By periodically loading the switchable microstrip stubs or long slots, the phase states of each element are discretized and they are represented by a 1-bit binary (“0”/0° and “1”/180°) digit. As a result, the aperture distribution of the digital LWA can be manipulated by designing different 0/1 coding sequences. The digital LWA can realize flexible beam steering and beam shaping, which makes it different from conventional LWAs and fixed-frequency scanning LWAs. Furthermore, to further meet the frequency demands of the 5G/6G applications, a dual-band digital LWA is firstly explored. Here, based on the substrate-integrated waveguide (SIW) and the microstrip line, an aperture-shared dual-band periodic digital LWA is implemented. The operating bands of the digital LWA can well cover the X band and the mm-Wave band. The peak gains for these two bands are 12.0 dBi and 16.5 dBi, respectively. The radiation beam for each band can be independently modulated by applying different digital sequences.

articleTitle: Quantitative GPR Imaging via U-NET
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Ground penetrating radar imaging is mostly tackled by resorting to approximate linear inverse scattering algorithms, which provide only qualitative maps of the probed scene in terms of position and geometry of the targets. Recently, the use of deep learning techniques has been proposed to retrieve quantitative information about the targets. These approaches usually learn mapping the radargrams into images describing the geometry and electromagnetic properties of the targets. In this contribution, we apply the popular convolutional neural network U-NET to perform quantitative subsurface imaging. Unlike previous works, the network takes in input tomographic images of the scene instead of the radargrams. Preliminary results based on full-wave synthetic data confirm the potentialities of the proposed reconstruction strategy.

articleTitle: Transfer Learning Based Microstrip Antenna Design
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a computationally efficient data-driven technique for designing multi-band microstrip antennas. The proposed methodology involves a two-step process. First, a pre-trained model, trained on extensive data on air-filled microstrip antennas, is used for knowledge transfer. This pre-trained model is fine-tuned with a limited set of dielectric simulations, reducing data acquisition costs. In the second step, the developed forward model serves as a surrogate to design dielectric-filled antennas using the Modified Binary Particle Swarm Optimization (MBPSO) algorithm. In contrast to conventional methods, this approach enables the design of compact antennas across various dielectrics and frequency ranges, with a significantly reduced number of time-consuming dielectric simulations (86 % fewer simulations).

articleTitle: A Wide-angle and Polarization-independent Plasmonic Absorber for UV to Near-IR Range
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A metamaterial-based plasmonic absorber is designed, fabricated, and characterized. The absorber consists of a periodic array of Ti unit-cells at the top, a layer of Al at the bottom, and a thin SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> layer that is sandwiched between the top and the bottom layers. Simulations and experiments show that the proposed design supports an average absorption of 96% over the wavelength range changing from 280 nm to 1000 nm (frequency range between ultraviolet [UV] and near-infrared [IR]). Furthermore, the absorption spectrum is polarization insensitive and has a large incidence angle tolerance. The proposed absorber has the potential to be used in photovoltaic applications such as solar cells and photo-detectors.

articleTitle: Nulling and Sectorized Jamming with Distributed Compact Antenna Arrays
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Distributed beamforming networks with multiple groups of two transmitters are optimized in terms of beamforming weights and orientations to maximize the radiated power over an angular sector containing an adversary while placing a null towards the client for improved communication security. The antennas in each group may be closely spaced and mutual coupling effects are fully included. Closed-form solutions are presented and numerical simulations validate their effectiveness.

articleTitle: High Power Waveguide-fed Helical Antenna for Broadband Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A broadband, 6.6 to 13.6 GHz, helical antenna array is designed for high power handling in a monolithic manufacturing process. This <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2\times 1$</tex> array antenna is fed by a standard WRD650 double ridge waveguide that is bifurcated into two custom single ridge waveguides feeding two same sense wound monofilar helices. The antenna system is designed for 3D-printing as a single piece and electroplated to achieve wideband, circularly polarized performance with VSWR <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$< 2:1$</tex>, directivity <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$> 12$</tex> dBic, and axial ratio <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$< 3\text{dB}$</tex> over most of the beamwidth.

articleTitle: Accurate Solutions of Electromagnetic Scattering by Penetrable Body-of-Revolution Objects Based on PMCHWT Equations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Electromagnetic problems with homogeneous penetrable objects can be governed by the well-known Poggio-Miller-Chang-Harrington-Wu-Tsai (PMCHWT) equations in integral equation approaches. If the objects are bodies of revolution with an axial symmetry, the PMCHWT equations can be reduced to two-dimensional equations by using the Fourier series expansion with the orthogonality of modes. The resulting equations are usually solved by the method of moments (MoM), but we propose to use the Nyström method to solve them so that the solving process can be greatly simplified. A numerical example is provided to demonstrate the approach and its robustness can be observed.

articleTitle: Enhanced Cross Polarization Conversion Method with Metasurface for Broadband Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a unique method for the design and simulation of a distinct cross-polarization conversion (CPC) metasurface optimized for effective operation in the microwave frequency range. The metasurface design is a reflective broadband CPC metasurface, featuring an arrangement of unit cells each comprising a metallic circular split ring resonator (C-SRR) with an internal circular split ring. This configuration effectively transforms circularly polarized waves into their orthogonal counterparts upon reflection. A notable aspect of this design is the incorporation of three plasmonic resonances at different frequencies, enabling a remarkable 3 dB fractional bandwidth across the 5–15 GHz spectrum. This achievement represents the highest reported bandwidth for a CPC metasurface on an FR4 dielectric substrate and supported by a metallic ground plane.

articleTitle: Battery-Less Approach to Wireless Water Leak Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This study introduces a transformative approach to water leak detection systems, overcoming the limitations of conventional battery-dependent models. Our innovative design integrates advanced nanomaterials with dual-purpose monopole antennas, fulfilling critical roles in Radio Frequency (RF) energy harvesting and Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) data transmission. The BLE system issues prompt leak alerts, while RF -harvested energy provides the system with enough power to send daily “heartbeat” pings, affirming continuous system functionality. The sensor unit, employing an innovative use of a metal sheet in the electricity-generating nanomaterials module, functions dually as an efficient water-leak sensor and an RF ground for antennas, demonstrating a synergy that enhances overall system efficiency. This approach eliminates the environmental concerns associated with battery usage like the need for frequent replacements, recycling complexities, and associated operational costs. This combination of RF energy harvesting and fluid-responsive nanomaterials represents a significant advancement in water leak detection technology, offering a more sustainable, reliable, and cost-effective solution.

articleTitle: Predicting the Number of Line Sources Inside a Cylinder Using Classification Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This study addresses the inverse problem of iden-tifying the number of line sources exciting a dielectric cylinder using machine learning. Solving the direct problem generates the required training data, enabling a classification neural network to accurately predict the number of sources considering a limited dataset. Demonstrating effectiveness, this work contributes to advancing numerical methods for inverse source problems and highlights machine learning's potential for precise outcomes.

articleTitle: An Antenna Architecture with Integrated Autocalibration Network for Phased Array Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a novel phased array architecture including a calibration network in the antenna plate is shown. The proposed architecture allows a real-time and on the field calibration which is performed by some striplines located below each row of the array. Differently by other radiating systems, our phased array antenna has specific lines devoted only to calibration without increasing the surface of the radiating plate. Moreover, it can be calibrated also in closed environments.

articleTitle: Fast Direction of Arrival Estimation Using Subspace-Based Methods for BLE Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach for estimating the direction of arrival (DoA) at any instant using subspace-based classical estimators. The aim is to mitigate the reliance of classical estimators on the quantity of snapshot data. The strategy involves leveraging instantaneous data from multiple channels, treating them as equivalent to multiple snapshots, to effectively address the impact of noise. The proposed approach is tested on a realistic data set generated using the embedded radiation patterns (ERPs), at multiple frequencies, of an antenna array developed for Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) applications. The preliminary analysis affirms the capabilities of the proposed approach in handling noise. Across various levels of noisy data, the performance of the proposed approach consistently surpasses that of standard methods at any given moment.

articleTitle: Approximation Method of Antenna Gain in the Near-Field Region Using Small Dipole Sources
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The antenna gain in the near-field region decreases from that in the far-field region. In this paper, we propose an approximate method to calculate the antenna gain in the near-field region by calculating the received power using two planes of transmission and reception and a small dipole. The measured values agreed well with the proposed method, indicating its effectiveness.

articleTitle: Diagonally Shielded HMSIW based Self-Diplexing Antenna with High Isolation for Microwave and mm-Wave Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this work, a low-profile self-diplexing antenna (SDA) with high isolation is proposed to work in microwave and millimeter wave frequencies. The antenna is designed using diagonally shielded half-mode Substrate Integrated Waveguide (HMSIW) cavity which operates at 5.4 GHz and 29 GHz. The diagonally shielded HMSIW cavity is designed by using a rectangular slot positioned along the diagonal of the square SIW cavity, and a row of vias is used to reduce the radiation losses along the open end of the HMSIW cavity. The cavity is separated into two unequal sized sections by an inverted L-shaped slot, which are excited by two 50 Ω feed lines. The larger and smaller sections are responsible for the radiation at 5.4 GHz and 29 GHz, respectively. The proposed SDA has a gain of 4 dBi and 8.85 dBi at 5.4 GHz and 29 GHz, respectively. Moreover, the proposed SDA achieves a port isolation greater than 33 dB at microwave and 28 dB at mm-wave frequencies, which is high as compared to the existing designs in the literature operating in both sub-6 GHz and millimeter-wave frequency regimes.

articleTitle: Circularly Polarized Antenna Array with Horizontal Open-Short Termination
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A novel scheme is presented for suppression of horizontal propagation from a circularly polarized plane antenna array. A open-short termination has been provided at the peripheral of the array. The distance is kept <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda g/2$</tex> between the open ends of this circuit and the array. Higher electrical characteristics have been proved by 3D computer simulation and an actual hardware of X-band circularly polarized plane antenna array. The hardware was evaluated in unechoic chamber. It is pointed that this structure provides not only suppression of interaction from surrounding objects on x-y plane, but also enhancement of directivity along <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$z$</tex> axis.

articleTitle: Microwave Imaging of Electromagnetic Wave Absorbers in an Antenna Measurement Chamber
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The quality of antenna and radar cross section measurement chambers is strongly dependent on the absorption behavior of the installed wave absorbers. It is demonstrated that the behavior of the absorbers can be assessed and illustrated with excellent spatial resolution by powerful microwave imaging techniques. When the absorbers are subjected to an illumination source, the fast irregular antenna field transformation algorithm (FIAFTA) enables simultaneous reconstruction of equivalent sources for both the illuminating source and the scatterers from near-field measurements. This process effectively implements echo suppression, allowing for the isolation of weakly scattered fields, primarily caused by the wave absorbers. Building upon this foundation, the application of microwave imaging technology enables the visual representation and examination of the absorbers. Experimental measurement results are shown to validate the feasibility of the approach.

articleTitle: On the Modelling and Evaluation of Harmonic Tags
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Passive harmonic tags are used to detect and track targets in highly cluttered environments or when the object of interest is too small to fit an active transmitter. This paper presents an approach to analytically model tag performance based on its equivalent circuit model. Tested on wire-based tags, it shows good correspondence with measurement results.

articleTitle: Discrete Variable Beamforming for Intelligent Reflecting Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we present a novel algorithm called Optimal Partitioning Algorithm (OPA) to solve the discrete beamforming problem where the weight of each unit cell in an IRS is constrained to a binary set. OPA is based on the idea that the optimal partition of the weights must arise due to a separating line in the complex plane. Unlike the conventional quantization methods and evolutionary algorithms that are heuristic in nature, our proposed algorithm comes with proof of optimality while also being very fast due to its linear time complexity, making it vastly superior to its counterparts. Using our algorithm to obtain optimal weights, we analyze the existence of grating lobes and explore various methods to mitigate them, such as the use of triangular lattices and prephasing. We show that our algorithm provides a rigorous framework for the execution of the above strategies.

articleTitle: A Circular Microstrip Patch Antenna Combined with SIW for MIMO Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This work presents a circular-shaped microstrip patch antenna with a Substrate Integrated Waveguide (SIW) for multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) applications. The proposed antenna is designed using HFSS software with an impedance bandwidth of 12.73%, from 7.40 GHz to 9.02 GHz, and provides a considerable gain of 9.84 dBi in the frequency band. The MIMO antenna is examined in terms of performance, including reflection coefficient, gain, and isolation. The proposed antenna design offers a high efficiency of over 98% in the frequency band used.

articleTitle: 3D-Printed Silver-Coated Vivaldi Array with Integrated Coaxial Probe Feeding
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A Vivaldi antenna array is designed for large phased array applications in the 3–6 GHz frequency range and is fed by a novel coaxial probe through the ground plane. The simulated infinite array active reflection coefficient is below -10 dB for an up to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 60^{\circ}$</tex> scan in the E-plane and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 50^{\circ}$</tex> in the H-plane, across the entire frequency range. The measured active reflection coefficient and array pattern for a small-scale <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1 \times 5$</tex> Vivaldi array are in good agreement with the simulations, which validate the infinite array model including the probe feeding concept. Furthermore, the 3D printing and silver-coating fabrication process proves useful for rapid and cost-effective prototyping.

articleTitle: High-Gain Broadband Dual-Polarized Base Station Antenna with Integrated Balun Structures for Ground-to-Aerial (G2A) Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a novel dual circularly polarized base station antenna designed for efficient Ground-to-Aerial (G2A) communications. Utilizing 1 Oz copper on a Rogers 4003C substrate for the top radiating board and incorporating bandwidth-enhanced balun structures on a Taconic RF-35 substrate, the proposed antenna covers 2.75 GHz to 5.25 GHz, which covers the lower side of the C-band. In the proposed dipole-based architecture, augmented with a 2 mm thick aluminum reflector plate, the single antenna attained a high gain of 13.4 dBi. Intended for deployment at base stations, our single antenna element ensures consistent link quality in dynamic unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) flight scenarios. This design sets the stage for future expansion into an array configuration, offering a comprehensive solution for high-performance G2A communication systems.

articleTitle: Miniaturization of a Patch Antenna Using an Artificial Magneto-Dielectric Substrate
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A microstrip square patch antenna is designed by using an artificial magneto-dielectric substrate. Thanks to periodically arranged Split-Ring Resonators (SRRs), an artifical magneto-dielectric substrate with high constitutive parameters is achieved. At 1.575 GHz, the designed artificial magneto-dielectric antenna footprint is 6 times smaller than the conventional <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda/2$</tex> patch antenna. The bandwidth and efficiency of the proposed antenna are compared with that of a conventionally miniaturized antenna which employs high dielectric substrate. Fabricated version of the proposed antenna is measured and results are compared with simulations.

articleTitle: Optimizing Propagation Channels Using Static Scatterers: Modeling and Ray-Tracing Simulations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we consider the possibility of improving the propagation of radio signals in complex environments using a set of simple purely passive resonant dipole scatterers. We use the Matlab ray tracer, amended with a model of dipolar scatterers based on their bistatic scattering cross-section, to analyze the influence of the scatterers on the received power at the user position. The analytical and simulation results show that placing additional scattering elements has no significant impact when a direct link exists. However, in non-line-of-sight scenarios, the proposed technique can significantly contribute to the delivered power. This simple and low-cost method can be an alternative or additional method of channel optimization, complementing the use of reconfigurable intelligent surfaces.

articleTitle: Inverse Design of Frequency Selective Surface Using Physics-Informed Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper uses Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) to design Frequency Selective Surface (FSS). PINN integrates physical information into the loss function, so training PINN does not require a dataset, which will be faster than traditional neural networks for inverse design. The specific implementation process of this paper is to construct a PINN using field solutions of mode matching method, and given the design goal, the PINN can train the shape of the diaphragm. The single frequency FSS that meets the design goal was designed using the inverse design method proposed in this paper without a dataset, verifying the rationality of using PINN to design metasurfaces. Using PINN for inverse design is not limited to single frequency FSS, but can also be used for more complex metasurface.

articleTitle: Case Study on Radar-Based Vital Signs Monitoring and the Effect of Target Aspect Angle
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Continuous monitoring of human vital signs is essential for healthcare applications. Radar systems are commonly used for vital signs monitoring and human activity recognition due to their contactless nature and privacy protection. Many challenges are faced when using radar systems for respiration and heart rate detection, such as the effect of the target aspect angle on the radar system. This work aims to discuss this effect on vital signs monitoring. Time domain and Frequency domain methods have been used to evaluate this effect in the accuracy of Heart Rate (HR) and Respiration rate (RR) estimation. Sixteen angles with steps of 22.5° have been added to the case study to record the variation in HR and RR estimation for each rotation angle.

articleTitle: Design of Multi-Band 8-Port MIMO Antenna With Pattern Diversity for IoT Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This study aims to address the challenge of reliable and stable connectivity in the IoT by proposing an eight-port multiple-input and multiple-output (MIMO) antenna that covers a broad range of 15 GHz in the Ku band, 24 GHz in the industrial, scientific, and medical (ISM) band, and the millimeter-wave bands at 30 GHz, 33 GHz, and 37 GHz. The antenna provides varied patterns and achieves an acceptable level of inter-element isolation. The envelope correlation coefficient (ECC) values are low, and the directivity gain (DG) is more than 9.96 dB in the resonant frequency bands. The proposed MIMO antenna is ideal for IoT applications owing to its multiple frequency bands and its low profile, which provides pattern diversity.

articleTitle: Compact-High Performance Microwave Circularly Polarized Antenna Array at Lower Frequency Band
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A four-layer antenna array is presented for lower microwave frequency band. The Evanescent coupling mode is applied for reduction of distance between adjacent resonators. The electrical parameters are obtained by 3D computer simulation. It was confirmed that novel design provides higher characteristics together with effective size reduction for circularly polarized plane antenna array at lower frequency band 2.8 GHz.

articleTitle: Compact Applicator Antenna for Superficial Microwave Hyperthermia
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: We present a microwave applicator aimed at the hyperthermia therapy of skin cancer types with emphasis on melanoma. Our design consists of a modified folded dipole on a reflector for a uniform and focused footprint on the therapy area. It affords low cost, low weight, compact size, and ease of handling, as required for integration in complex applicator systems. A Simulation and experimental validation campaign on a human phantom model demonstrate good performance in terms of power footprint and power delivery to the tissue under therapy.

articleTitle: A Beam-Reconfigurable Metasurface Based on Dual-Polarized Units
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a novel beam reconfigurable metasurface suitable for dual-polarization mode is proposed. The metasurface contains 8 × 8 units. After being verified by ANSYS simulation software, in the case of two orthogonal polarized waves (TE and TM), the unit can achieve a phase difference of approximately 180° and the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S_{11}$</tex> parameter greater than -0.7 dB between 4.95 GHz to 5.03 GHz by changing the on-off states of the diodes. The metasurface can realize continuous double beam reconstruction in the range of angle -33.6° to -11.9° and angle 12.8° to 34.4° with the fractional phase-coding strategy. Due to its digital dual-beam steering capability, the metasurface has potential applications in wireless communications.

articleTitle: A Wide Scan Dual-Polarized Low Profile Array for Satellite Applications with Axial Ratio Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this study, a novel low-profile X-slot microstrip patch antenna array with wide scan ability and a new approach to improve axial ratio at extreme scan angles are presented. The array is very low profile because of its narrow band and it is able to scan conically up to 60° with reflection performance below −10 dB. Thanks to its low-profile advantage, the array is applicable to conformal phased array applications (curvature satellite platforms). Dual-polarized antenna array elements operate from 13.75 GHz to 14.5 GHz with an axial ratio below 3 dB for boresight scan. Furthermore, axial ratio is improved for all scan angles although there are roughly 1.5 dB rms amplitude errors in attenuators and 10° rms phase errors in phase shifters.

articleTitle: Passive Dual-Band Shared-Aperture Reflective Metasurface with Large Frequency Ratio for Sub-6 GHz/mmWave Band Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper introduces a passive dual-band single-layer reflective metasurface featuring a large frequency ratio of 8 for the first time. The metasurface includes two types of 28 GHz elements and two types of 3.5 GHz elements, all exhibiting stable performance across various oblique incidence angles. The elements exhibit phase shift ranges surpassing <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$300^{\circ}$</tex> amid minimal reflection losses less than 1.38 dB. The measured peak gain for the prototype, consisting of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$24 \times 24 28$</tex> GHz elements and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$14 \times 14 3.5$</tex> GHz elements, are 23.3 dBi with a sidelobe level (SLL) of −14.2 dBi at 28 GHz and 17.8 dBi with SLL of −12.4 dBi at 3.5 GHz respectively. This design marks a promising starting point for single-aperture dual-band reflective metasurface applications in microwave/millimeter wave spectrum.

articleTitle: A Metamaterial-Loaded Pattern-Reconfigurable Antenna with Dielectric Decoupler for MIMO Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a metamaterial loaded pattern-reconfigurable antenna with dielectric decoupler for 4-ports MIMO applications. The dielectric-air boundary (DAB) in the dielectric decoupler generates electric field valleys in specific areas. By placing the ports in the electric field valleys can achieve high isolation characteristics. Cross-shaped cavities hollowed out in the dielectric decoupler also contribute to improved isolation. A loaded metamaterial layer makes the antenna compact in structure. In addition, by exciting its different ports, the MIMO antenna can switch between 4 different radiation patterns. Simulation results shows that the bandwidth at the reflection coefficient of -10 dB is 3.58 - 4.20 GHz, and the port isolation is greater than -15 dB.

articleTitle: Low-Profile Circularly Polarized Beam-Scanning Antenna with Low Sidelobe Level
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a low-profile circularly polarized (CP) beam-scanning antenna for satellite communications. The continuous beam-scanning capability is realized by using a Blass matrix implemented in substrate integrated waveguide (SIW). A symmetrical beam-scanning range is achieved by introducing a gradient phase compensation structure composed of SIW delay lines. To increase the beam scanning range of circular polarization, antenna elements with wide 3-dB axial ratio (AR) beamwidth are used in this design. The proposed antenna also has low sidelobe levels (SLL) in two dimensions, which is synthesized using Taylor distribution. A Ku-band antenna array of 10×14 elements is designed and simulated. Simulated results demonstrate that the designed antenna exhibits a beam-scanning range of ±32° with peak gain of 25.4 dBi and AR lower than 2.4 dB. Furthermore, its SLLs are lower than -20 dB in the entire beam scanning range.

articleTitle: Vision-Aided Channel Prediction with RGB Images for mmWave Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Computer vision has broad application prospects in the field of wireless communication. In this paper, we propose a novel two-stage received power prediction model based on computer vision for mmWave communication networks. In stage 1, images with bounding box, instance segmentation and binary mask are generated by YOLOv8 network from original RGB images and fed into ResNet-18 network at stage 2 to predict received power. Validation results demonstrate that proposed model can map RGB images to received power with root mean square error less than 2 dB.

articleTitle: Designing a Tunable Frequency Selective Surface with Active Components
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Tunable devices are in increasing demand in present-day communication systems. One design with two configurations for tunable Frequency Selective Surfaces are proposed in this work.
