PIN diodes are used as active devices for tuning and control networks are embedded in the structures for biasing the active elements. Electromagnetic simulation has been used to assess the proposed designs. By utilizing the square-shaped unit cells of 18 mm edge length, distinct filtering bands have been produced below 12 GHz.

articleTitle: Ultra-Wideband Dielectric Resonator Antenna Fed By Printed Ridge Gap Waveguide Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper introduces a millimeter-wave ultra-wideband dielectric resonator antenna designed for 5G frequency bands. The study involves an analysis of the performance of a triple-stacked rectangular dielectric resonator. A feeding slot with a rectangular shape is etched on the top wall and is excited via a printed ridge gap waveguide (PRGW) line. The antenna exhibits an impedance bandwidth of 45.62%, covering the frequency range from 28.2 GHz to 45.5 GHz, with a return loss |S11| consistently below −10 dB. At 37.5 GHz, the antenna achieves a peak realized gain of 9.2 dBi, maintaining a realized gain of more than 6.2 dBi across the entire operating band, thus establishing a 3 dB gain bandwidth. Moreover, the radiation pattern remains stable in both the E- and H-planes. These specifications make the antenna as a promising candidate for 5G applications.

articleTitle: A 1-Bit Wideband Electronically Beam Steering Transmitarray for 5G Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a wideband electronically reconfigurable transmitarray unit-cell with 1-bit phase quantization (0°/180°) for 5G Communication Systems. The unit cell consists of one modified patch array on one side (Tx) and two modified patch arrays on the opposite side (Rx). The patches on opposite sides are connected by a metalized via-hole. The results demonstrate minimal insertion loss, consistently maintained across both phase states, along with a wide 3-dB transmission bandwidth (from 24.4 GHz to 32 GHz). Next, a transmit array antenna is built to validate the beam-forming concept. The outcome shows that the beam is controlled to the desired angles with very good sidelobe levels (SLL).

articleTitle: Phase-Space and Complex-Source Methods Applied to Metamaterials Engineering
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The centenary anniversary of Professor Leopold B. Felsen's birth prompts reflection on his enduring scientific legacy. Specifically, we examine how some of his pioneering concepts and tools still find compelling applications in modern wave physics. This overview focuses on recent applications of phase-space and complex-source methods in the realm of metamaterials engineering, with special emphasis on nonlocal and non-Hermitian scenarios.

articleTitle: Low-Power, Secure, Mm-Wave Guided Wireless Communication Exploiting Beam Divergence and Atmospheric Loss
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: It is well known that mm-wave communication can provide high-date rate communication in multi-user crowded environments by providing a large bandwidth. If the available frequency bands could be reused without causing interference, many wireless users can be serviced in congested areas. In wireless systems, the signals inadvertently cover an extended area beyond the intended domain of interest causing security risk and preventing efficient frequency reuse. In this paper, methods that can confine the radiated fields within a box (region) and at the same time with significantly decaying fields outside of the box are investigated. The target application is mm-wave Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) communication in stretch of roads and highways.

articleTitle: Virtual vs Directional Channel Sounder at mmW
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this work, we have experimentally compared two different channel sounding techniques at millimeter-wave frequencies in an indoor scenario with a Line-of-Sight. On one hand, virtual arrays were synthesized using an omnidirectional antenna. On the other hand, a directive antenna was rotated using a 3D positioner. Measurements have been performed in a laboratory of the University and the frequency range was 26 to 40 GHz. Besides, the environment has been carefully simulated using a 3D ray-tracing tool. From results, it is observed that the capacity of the 3D rotor to sound the channel in the elevation plane is better than that of the more complex planar URA with its limited aperture and omnidirectional antenna. This comes at the expense of longer measurements as the number of positions is much larger. Hence, a trade-off must be thoroughly reached prior doing the measurements.

articleTitle: Radiating Source Modeling Using Electrical Infinitesimal Dipole Based on Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: We proposed the methodology for modeling electrical radiating sources employing dual infinitesimal dipoles, aimed at predicting radiating characteristics in both far and near zones. The employed machine learning technique facilitates the construction of a radiating source model comprising dual infinitesimal dipoles. In the training process of machine learning, we utilized the training data that encompasses the radiating fields corresponding to the current induced on the dual infinitesimal dipoles. After confirming that the machine learning model was well learned, we proceeded to validate the proposed modeling methodology. This validation is achieved through a comparative analysis between the simulated radiating fields of a sample antenna and those computed by the predicted source models.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Aided Modelling and Inverse Design for Multi-Port Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: With the prevalence of multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems, multi-port antenna design has become an important research area. In this work, we approach the multi-port antenna design problem to accelerate the design cycle, expanding design space, and finding non-intuitive designs that can potentially yield better performance than existing template-based designs. To achieve these, we rely on the optimization of a discretized surface, which can implement near-arbitrary antenna shapes. However, performing an electromagnetic (EM) optimization with a large number of variables is prohibitively costly. On the other hand, if EM simulations can be replaced by a machine learning (ML) based approach, antenna optimization could be accelerated greatly. To this end we utilize a convolutional neural network (CNN) for the modeling of multi-port pixelated structures. A genetic algorithm (GA) in conjunction with CNN is used to perform inverse design. Example designs for various optimization targets have been shown in support of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Wireless Power Transfer with Metal Object and Coil Misalignment Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Metal objects existing on coils of a wireless power transfer (WPT) system will deteriorate WPT performance or induce safety issues. A dual-band WPT is proposed to detect the metal objects. The lower band is mainly used for power transfer and metal object detection. The higher band can be used to detect the coil misalignment, which is commonly occurring during charging. The simulated and experimental results show that the discrimination between metal object existence and coil misalignment can be achieved simultaneously in this WPT system.

articleTitle: Achieving Omnidirectional Dual-Polarized Sensing with Additively Manufactured Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A monolithic, additively manufactured circular array of curved inverted-F antennas (CIFA) is made dual-polarized by incorporating a discone antenna similarly produced in monolithic fashion by digital light processing. The discone is carefully designed to have minimal impact on the CIFA array characteristics inclusive of impedance bandwidth and radiation patterns, while itself providing omnidirectional sensing and transmitting capability over nearly the same bandwidth. The design of the discone and the mating solution between antenna elements is discussed, highlighting the considerations necessary to make the one-piece 3D-printed fabrication possible. The resulting dual-polarized system exhibits return loss of 10 dB or greater over most of the 2–3 GHz band while maintaining gain of at least 0 dBi at horizon (θ = 90°). Measured results for the fabricated prototype show some disagreement with initial simulations due to effects associated with the stray currents on the cables needed for metrology. Methods to mitigate these issues in future design iterations are suggested and demonstrated in simulation.

articleTitle: Near-Field Diffraction Tomography for Weak-Scattering, Cylindrical Vector Wave Problems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A new method for full vector-wave diffraction tomography in weak-scattering, cylindrical scenarios is proposed. It is based on the standard filtered backpropagation algorithm but it is derived in the framework of electromagnetic vector theory and includes the action of the dyadic Green's function. It is this dyadic that describes mathematically the depolarization processes occurring inside the object of study. The weak scattering phenomena are described within a version of the Distorted-Wave Born Approximation that allows for depolarization effects to take place. The resulting reconstruction algorithm is applied to the well-known Shepp-Logan phantom with excellent results.

articleTitle: A Low-Profile Substrate Integrated Waveguide Cavity-Backed Slot Antenna with 40% Bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This article presents a substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) cavity-backed slot antenna with an unprecedented 40% bandwidth. The antenna is fabricated on a 4 layer Printed Circuit Board (PCB) with a total thickness less than 0.1λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>. Layer 1 contains a slot which is backed by an SIW cavity formed between layers 1 and 3. The cavity is excited by a microstrip to stripline transition from layer 4 to layer 2. Plotting the electric field in the slot reveals that there are 4 coupled resonant modes formed on the slot, out of which three of them are formed by the presence of fictitious shorts. These fictitious shorts are generated by the interaction between the resonances of the cavity, the field in the slot and the currents of the feed. Optimization is used to tune the four modes to be equally spaced and matched to 50 Ohms. The gain and return loss bandwidth are measured to be 40%, with a flat gain response of around 5 dBi over most of the band. The simulated radiation efficiency is higher than 80%. The design is low-profile and compact, making it scalable to an array. The SIW cavity backing provides high field confinement, which results in high isolation from nearby elements. To the best of our knowledge, this design achieves the highest reported bandwidth for a compact, low-profile, cavity-backed antenna.

articleTitle: Compact Implantable Antenna with Ultra-Wide bandwidth for Leadless Pacemaker
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This article introduces a compact antenna designed for leadless pacemakers (LPs), featuring a small size of 8.83 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, and a bandwidth of 4330 MHz, addressing detuning issues. Covering frequencies from 0.67 GHz to 5 GHz, the antenna ensures optimal performance in medical frequency bands. The achievement of ultra-wide bandwidth is attributed to integrating a meandered line in the ground plane and a large rectangular slot in the patch. Moreover, the proposed antenna demonstrates high gain values of -31.3 dBi, -25.7 dBi, and -22.7 dBi at 0.915 GHz, 1.4 GHz, and 2.45 GHz, respectively.

articleTitle: A 150-GHz On-Chip Antenna with 40-GHz Bandwidth in 22-nm FD-SOI CMOS for Automotive Phased Array Radars
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this study, a new on-chip antenna design intended for fully integrated SoCs for automotive phased-array radars is presented. The antenna operates at 150 GHz and is designed in the high-volume 22-nm FD-SOI CMOS technology while meeting all strict manufacturing rules. It exhibits a simulated gain of 1.3 dBi at 150 GHz with a fractional bandwidth of 26.7%. The total area of this antenna is 0.79×0.79mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> (i.e., 0.39×0.39λ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>at 150 GHz). In contrast to traditional microstrip feeding methods, our innovative design integrates parasitic elements. These elements function as resonators, establishing electromagnetic coupling with the driven element and serving to modify the bandwidth of the antenna. Additionally, periodic structures established underneath the antenna used to increase its gain.

articleTitle: Long-Range Reading of Multiple Chipless Sensors from the Isoline Processing of 3D Radar Images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we report the long-range and wireless interrogation of multiple chipless sensors from the isoline processing of three-dimensional polarimetric radar images. A Frequency-Modulated Continuous-Wave Radar operating at 24 GHz is used for the indoor interrogation of four sensors in the basement of a Laboratory. In such cluttered environment, the proposed radar image processing based on isolines computation allows the wireless measurement range of sensors up to 5.8m.

articleTitle: Spherical Dielectric Resonator Fed High Gain Resonant Cavity Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This work presents a new design approach to realize high gain on-chip antennas at K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</inf>-band. The proposed antenna combines a self-aligning on-chip spherical dielectric resonator with a resonant cavity antenna (RCA) to offer increased gain with efficient on-chip coupling. The proposed superstrate layer is fully made of dielectric material with varied radial thicknesses. This finally results in 18.4 dBi of gain at 36.5 GHz along with a decent 4.80% of measured bandwidth considering on-chip limited substrate thickness. A patch antenna fed RCA is also tested to verify the effectiveness of the same proposed superstrate.

articleTitle: 4×4 SIW Based Butler Matrix for Milimeter Wave applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The present needs of the limited spectrum and the expected user/direction coverage are 5G. 5G bands are capable of supporting both the high data throughput and an extensive user. For 5G applications, a 4×4 Butler matrix with multibeam beamforming for radar applications is developed. In this study, a 4×4 butler matrix based on substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) technology is for operation at 60 GHz. The design process includes the creation of a 90° hybrid coupler and crossover. The designed butler matrix is simulated with CST Studio and the results are verified with HFSS. The proposed butler matrix can be easily manufactured using standard methods for the manufacture of printed circuit boards.

articleTitle: Characteristics of an Ultra-high Power Slotted Waveguide Array Antenna for Anti-UAV Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This work performs the characteristics of an ultra-high power slotted waveguide array (SWA) antenna for L-band anti-unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) systems. The array antenna including <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$10\times 10$</tex> slotted elements is synthesized using the 25-dB Taylor distribution to create a narrow beam and focus the power on a flying vehicle. Besides, an improved feeding network is realized to reduce the weight but enhance the bandwidth of the antenna. The proposed antenna is then fabricated and tested with a mobile anti-UAV system. Experimental results indicate that the proposed antenna has an impedance bandwidth from 1.25 to 1.385 GHz (fractional bandwidth of 10.25 %) with a peak gain of 27.4 dBi at 1.345 GHz. Importantly, the antenna works properly with an input peak power of 3.1 MW and can take down UAVs from a distance of up to 400 m.

articleTitle: Optimal Spherical Coil Design for Dual-Site Magnetic Neurostimulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a conjointly optimized dual-target magnetic coil for dual-mode transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) is proposed and validated. The proposed coil design consists of two sub-coils with a low mutual inductance of 1.8% and allows both sequential and concurrent stimulation of the preset brain targets. With focality and depth of the electric field comparable to those of the commercial figure-8 coil, only about 38% magnetic energy is required for the proposed coil to achieve supra-threshold brain stimulation. Varied distances between loci have been discussed. Measurement and simulation results validate our computation model, and reveal that the proposed coil is a preferable solution for dual-site TMS with low energy and mutual inductance.

articleTitle: Multi-Mode Switched-Beam Antennas for Tracking Radar and Communication Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a multi-mode switched-beam structure capable of offering four radiation pattern modes. The pattern diversity is realized by using four 90-deg hybrid couplers and four patch antennas as radiators. The diversified radiation patterns includes three difference patterns and one sum pattern. The developed prototype antennas possesses promising results, including the worst-case port peak gain of 8.7 dB and moderate impedance bandwidth of 15%., making it very suitable for tracking radar and communication applications.

articleTitle: Liquid-Based Reconfigurable $4\mathrm{x}4$ Butler Matrix for Enhanced Spatial Coverage
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a novel design of liquid based reconfigurable Butler matrix is proposed. Based on proposed concept, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4\mathrm{x}4$</tex> butler matrix along with 4-element patch antenna is designed at 2.0 GHz frequency. Re-configurability in design is achieved by using liquid (water in this case) with the help of Polylactic Acid (PLA) structure using loading component method. 15 Liquid channels (having six sets of 5 channels each on both upper and lower sides) were filled in various combinations to vary progressive phase shift of output ports of Butler Matrix, by doing so, enhanced spatial coverage over the scale of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 90^{\circ}$</tex> is achieved while maintaining a -10dB impedance bandwidth from 1.8 GHz to 2.2 GHz (400MHz). In contrast to other re-configurability approaches, the proposed approach offers a low profile, low cost, and compact size solution, making it highly suitable for radar and wireless communication and other tune-able devices applications in S-band.

articleTitle: Electron Energy Loss Spectroscopy for Microwave Characterization of Plasmonic Antennas at 25 – 150 THz frequencies
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The plasmonic behavior exhibited by antenna modes manifests a variety of advantageous properties and present abundant opportunities for antenna engineers, with applications spanning from terahertz to optical frequencies. Nevertheless, at such high frequencies, there is still lack of equipment, such as vector network analyzers, making microwave characterization in terms of scattering parameters and proper design of plasmonic antennas at THz frequencies unavailable. To resolve this gap, we present, for the first time, the novel non-contact characterization method for plasmonic antennas through Electron Energy Loss Spectroscopy (EELS). We designed and fabricated a dipole plasmonic antenna and conducted EELS experiment to verify the antenna's resonances within the frequency range of 25 to 150 THz. A novel microwave interpretation theory for EEL experiment, based on establishing the correlation between EEL probability and absorbed power, was formulated and substantiated through correlation with the experimental results. Furthermore, based on this theory, we describe the algorithm and present the results for S-parameters and input impedance characterization of plasmonic antennas at 25 – 150 THz. Our approach can potentially be extremely beneficial for future design and characterization of THz plasmonic antenna.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Dual Beam Corrugated Substrate Integrated Waveguide Based Leaky Wave Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This article presents a leaky-wave antenna (LWA) with a dual sinusoidal slot array loaded on top of a corrugated substrate integrated waveguide (CSIW) with a cut-off frequency of 20 GHz. The proposed LWA is shown to operate at a frequency band of 22 to 30 GHz, with an efficiency <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$> 75\%$</tex>, gain <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$> 14 \text{dBi}$</tex> and side lobe level <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$< 10\mathbf{dB}$</tex>. The proposed antenna is suitable for beyond-5G and satellite communication applications.

articleTitle: Impact of Element Polarization on the Circular Polarization Purity of Phased Arrays with Sequential Feeding Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The effect of the antenna element polarization on the polarization purity of phased arrays fed using sequential rotation networks is investigated. As a case study, two 4×4 antenna arrays are designed with linear polarized (LP) and circular polarized (CP) elements and integrated with sequential feeding networks. By changing the excitation phase via the feeding network, the radiation patterns are steered to different angles up to 40°. The calculated axial ratio bandwidth demonstrates that the antenna array with CP elements maintains high circular polarization purity for steering angles of more than 20° compared to the antenna array with LP elements, where the onset of polarization purity degradation is observed from small scanning angles. Consequently, it is recommended to use CP elements in sequentially rotated antenna arrays to achieve a purer circular polarization for wide steering angles.

articleTitle: A C-Band 1-Bit Reconfigurable Transmitarray Unit-Cell for Airborne UAV Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The design of a novel 1-bit reconfigurable transmitarray (RTA) unit-cell for C-band (4.4-5 GHz) is presented in this work. The structure is realized by the guided wave approach using a pair of quasi-Yagi elements, an 180° phase shifter designed by a parallel-coupled three-line, and a transmission line with a shorted stub. The numerical analysis results show that the peak of insertion loss in two-phase states is about 0.9 dB at both frequencies of 4.55 GHz and 4.9 GHz, with a 3 dB transmission fractional bandwidth reaching 12.76%. The proposed unit-cell can be adapted for wide-angle beam scanning at both E-plane and H-plane with an oblique incidence angle of up to 45°. The unit-cell design is capable of adjusting the phase values but maintaining the phase difference between the two states of 180°. The design structure is based on a single-layer PCB incorporating four PIN diodes for saving costs. Overall, the proposed RTA with wide-angle beam scanning is a promising candidate for C-band communications between the monitoring ground stations and the UAVs.

articleTitle: Full-Metal High Gain Antenna for SatCom Applications at K/Ka Band
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This communication introduces a high-gain antenna designed for satellite communications (SatCom) in the K/Ka band, covering the frequency range 17–31 GHz. The antennas based on a long slot array, fed by a corporate feed network (CFN). The CFN is tapered to reduce sidelobe levels (SLL) in the radiating plane orthogonal to the long slots across the entire frequency band (<-23 dB). Additionally, a pillbox coupler serves as a line source generator to illuminate the CFN, featuring an integrated parabolic reflector illuminated by a displaceable H-plane horn in its focal plane. The antenna is fabricated using computer numerically controlled (CNC) milling technology in Aluminum to minimize losses. The total size of the antenna is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$44.5\times 33.1\times 6.2\ \lambda_{0}^{3}$</tex> with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda_{0}$</tex> the free space wavelength at 31 GHz. The antenna exhibits a minimum measured realized gain of 34.3 dBi at 17 GHz. The antenna can steer its main beam along the slot plane to cover a field of view exceeding 50° in elevation by displacing the H-plane horn in the focal plane of the pillbox coupler.

articleTitle: Ultra-Thin Wide-Band Multilayer FSS-Based Magnetic Absorber
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This work presents the design of an ultra-thin and wide-band electromagnetic absorber based on a resistive Frequency Selective Surface (FSS) etched within a magnetic substrate. The absorber is conceived by layering an FSS characterized by a triple-loop unit-cell between two commercially available magnetic substrates. The bottom layer of the overall structure is grounded by a metallic sheet. In details, the FSS unit-cell comprises three concentric copper loops opportunely loaded with different lumped resistors. The overall total thickness of the absorber is 3 mm. The structure has been thoroughly evaluated by using an equivalent circuit analysis corroborated by precise full-wave numerical simulations. Although the extremely reduced thickness (λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">max</inf>/16), the structure proves as an effective absorber, with an absorption level exceeding -10 dB from 6.2 to 11.8 GHz, i.e. a 62% fractional bandwidth.

articleTitle: On the Operation Principle of Azimuthal Null Frequency Scanning Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The operation principle of azimuthal null frequency scanning antenna (ANFSA) is revealed by deducing an analytical formula for null scanning range prediction. Two bilateral ANFSAs with short-circuited circumference and under radially symmetric triple-mode resonance are studied to validate the revealed mathematical nature. As can be seen, the perfect agreement between the simulated and measured results well validates the correctness of the operational principle.

Author Keywords: bilateral azimuthal null frequency scanning antenna

articleTitle: Deployment of a Multi-Chip NFC System with Microfluidic for Electrochemical Sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Fast, on-site chemical sensing can be a powerful tool for many applications, ranging from point-of-care analyses to food quality checks. NFC (Near Field Communications) devices capable of chemical sensing have recently become available. However, they are still limited to sensing a single chemical species at a time, whereas usually, an array of species should be quantified during the same analysis. Multi-chip NFC devices are still unavailable for chemical sensing, and the use of microfluidics with delay lines is also necessary for the correct delivery of liquid samples. Accordingly, this contribution explores the layout design of the first multi-chip NFC system integrated with microfluidics for electrochemical sensing using multiple boards simultaneously. The most functional arrangement of the responders is experimentally selected based on their read areas, the quality of the NFC communication, and the microfluidic characteristics. Lastly, a four-channel microfluidic system is integrated with the best board placement and validated by quantification of sodium in standard solution.

articleTitle: Arrival Angle Characteristics at Mobile Station in Mountainous Area for High Base Station Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: High-Altitude Platform Station (HAPS) is attracting significant attention as a new mobile communication platform for ultra-wide coverage area and disaster-resilient networks, because it can provide communication services from altitudes of around 20 km from Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) such as balloons, airships, or other aircraft. In developing a propagation model for HAPS that covers a wide area, it is important to analyze the propagation path due to the terrain. In this paper, we measured and analyzed the arrival angle of radio waves when the mobile station is located in a mountainous area in a high-altitude base station environment.

articleTitle: Feasibility of Alzheimer's Disease Early Detection Through Machine Learning Applied to Microwave Sensing Data Collected from a Realistic Phantom
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This work aims to assess the feasibility of microwave sensing as a tool to allow early non-invasive diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease. In particular, it addresses the use of optimized support vector machine trained to perform a binary classification between the healthy and the pathological cases applied to measured scattering parameters data, collected on a realistic multi-tissue head phantom via a multiport vector network analyzer. The phantom mimics a human head in the healthy and the Alzheimer's disease condition at four different stages. The obtained experimental results are promising and show high accuracy, suggesting the feasibility of the proposed diagnostic technology.

articleTitle: Intelligent Metasurface for Adaptive Controlling the Scattering Waves
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A design of an intelligent metasurface with co-aperture of reception and scattering is proposed to achieve sensing and adaptive controlling of spatial waves. The intelligent metasurface unit cell with cascaded structures mainly consists of three parts, including the patch antenna, reconfigurable phase shifter with varactors and the switching circuit with PIN diode. A prototype of the intelligent metasurface is fabricated and measured. The spatial angle of the incident wave is detected, and customized electromagnetic (EM) functions of retro-reflection and low scattering are realized based on adaptive feedback control.

articleTitle: UWB Antenna with WLAN and X-Band Rejection Based on Metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper introduces a compact Ultra-Wideband (UWB) patch antenna designed with remarkable capability to reject two specific frequency bands, namely: WLAN (5.26-5.87 GHz) and X-band satellite communication (7.30-7.68 GHz). Constructed on FR-4 substrate, the Guitar antenna innovative design incorporates E-shaped metamaterial structures and Split Ring Resonators (SRRs), enabling optimal UWB feature while effectively eliminating undesired frequency bands. Further, the proposed band-notching mechanism is validated through experimental proof. This research brings us closer to realizing the full potential of UWB technology in the realm of wireless communications and signal processing.

articleTitle: Frequency Extension of 3D-Printed Gradient-Index Lenses via Sub-Unit Cell Impedance Matching
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a novel impedance matching method for maximizing the bandwidth of 3D-printed dielectric Gradient-Index (GRIN) lenses. The difference in size requirements between physical GRIN media and impedance matching layers is discussed. To improve the maximum operating frequency up to the physical limits of the GRIN media, a sub-unit cell matching method is described and applied to a triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) gyroid unit cell. The effectiveness of the described method is validated through full-wave simulation.

articleTitle: A Wideband Frequency Selective Surface with Excellent Angular Stability
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a wideband frequency selective surface (FSS) with excellent angular stability is proposed. The angular stability of the FSS unit is improved by increasing the thickness of the dielectric substrate and adding dielectric compensation layers on the basis of the antenna-filter-antenna (AFA)-FSS. Simulated results show that the proposed FSS can achieve a passband range from 2.5 to 3.9 GHz with an insertion loss of less than 0.6 dB, it can retain a stable transmission characteristic with the incident angle ranging from 0° to 60° for both TE and TM polarization. The FSS also achieves a -10 dB stopband range from 0.5 to 2.2 GHz.

articleTitle: Breathing Rate Variability Impact on Heart Rate Estimation Through Radar Sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper explores the influence of breathing rate variability on heart rate estimation through UWB radar sensing. The study leverages a low-power ultra-wideband radar system operating in the 7.29 to 8.748 GHz range with a 1.5 GHz bandwidth. Through meticulous data pre-processing and various deep learning models, the study classifies respiration rates into slow, normal, and fast categories. The results showcase the effectiveness of models such as MobileNet, ResNet50, and VGG19, achieving an impressive overall test accuracy of 93.3%. This research contributes to advancing the application of radar technology in the precise detection of vital signs, offering potential implications for non-invasive health monitoring.

articleTitle: Fast RCS Evaluation of Cone-Cylinder-Flare Shape Using a Machine Learning Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A shape of medium geometric complexity initially designed for computational fluid dynamics engineering is eval-uated for RCS. The RCS is expressed as a function of both geometric and EM wave parameters. A boosted decision-tree (AdaBoost) model is then trained for regression of the RCS function using a limited number of exact RCS computations as training data. The context of this study is to integrate such models into more complex multidisciplinary workflows.

articleTitle: Multi-Objective Optimization of Directivity Enhancing Multi-Band Gradient Index Lenses
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Augmenting the performance of existing antenna systems with lenses and radomes is often preferred over replacing legacy installations due to the associated costs and schedule. To this end, lenses are commonly tasked with enhancing the directivity of existing antennas in order to increase the system's performance across a variety of potential applications. At the same time, multi-band operation is often desired as advanced antenna systems are increasingly tasked with achieving multiple functionalities in a single aperture. To realize solutions that achieve a set of unique performance goals at multiple frequency bands, this paper pairs gradient index (GRIN) lenses with state-of-the-art optimization algorithms to realize bespoke fully freeform designs that outperform solutions designed with transformation optics (TO).

articleTitle: Higher-Order Array Decomposition Method for Arrays with Dielectric Substrates
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The Higher-Order Array Decomposition Method (HO-ADM) has been extended to regular arrays with dielectric substrates. To maintain the multi-level block-Toeplitz Method of Moments (MoM) matrix structure, internal equivalent currents are introduced, ensuring an FFT-accelerated matrix-vector product (MVP). Results demonstrate a tenfold reduction in computation time and lower memory consumption compared to an existing fast method, specifically for a 400-element array of PEC cylinders embedded in a dielectric substrate.

articleTitle: A Preconditioned Inverse Scattering Scheme for High-Contrast Bone Imaging at Microwave Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This work presents a combined quasi-Helmholtz preconditioning strategy for the contrast source volume integral equation (J-VIE) with a Newton-Kantorovich method allowing 2D microwave imaging for high-contrast scatterers. We show that the preconditioning improves the convergence of the J- VIE, reducing the number of iterations required, even for highly inhomogeneous objects. We demonstrate the practical significance of this preconditioned inverse scattering scheme on a realistic human bone and thigh imaging problem.

articleTitle: Effect of Glass Window on Vertically Polarized Plane Wave Scattering by a Building
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Utilizing the Kirchoff approximation, the high-frequency scattering of a vertically polarized plane wave by a building has been analyzed to estimate the glass window effect. The scattering fields can be derived as the summation of radiation fields from equivalent magnetic currents on a virtually closed aperture on the windows and the exterior of the building wall. These magnetic currents are generated by the incident plane wave and the field excited by the window glass interface.

articleTitle: On the Information Content of RFID Fingerprints
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In the realm of physical security methods, finger-printing stands out as a prominent measure in wireless systems and Radio-Frequency Identification (RFID) applications. The conventional approach in the literature is to extract features from the signals received from the device, and use machine learning to develop classifiers that can recognize counterfeit or cloned devices. With the goal of mastering the physical source of electromagnetic signatures, this paper investigates the information content of fingerprints of passive RFID devices by applying Shannon Information Theory to backscattered signals. The study demonstrates that by interrogating the tags with different reader's input powers and frequencies, we are able to enhance the integrated circuit (IC) non-linear behavior, and its impedance modulation will change in a not easily predictable way. Accordingly the device will expose more information, resulting in a higher entropy value, and a richer fingerprint.

articleTitle: Towards Low-Frequency Reconfigurable Computational Magnetic Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a preliminary investigation to show the ability of reconfigurable magnetic metasurfaces to perform analog mathematical operations in the radio frequency (RF) regime. In particular, the operations are implemented over the circulating currents of the active unit-cells selected as inputs. Then, through the other passive metasurface elements, the result of the operation can be read as the circulating current of the output unit-cell. From a practical point of view, the structure is synthetized by exploiting an analytical formulation based on circuital equations. In this way, the loading conditions that must be applied to each unit-cell of the system to implement the desired operation can be retrieved. A numerical test case was conceived to prove the method effectiveness. The model consists in 5 loops capable of performing a linear combination between two input currents whose weighting coefficients can be arbitrarily set.

articleTitle: Circularly Polarized Reconfigurable Omnidirectional Dielectric Resonator Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A circularly polarized reconfigurable omnidirectional dielectric resonator antenna is proposed in this paper. The electric dipole mode of the dielectric resonator and the magnetic dipole mode of the arcs are combined to generate circularly polarized omnidirectional patterns. Six PIN diodes are organized into two groups to control the three arcs, enabling flexible RHCP/LHCP reconfiguration. The proposed antenna achieves circularly polarized radiation with an axial ratio below 2dB, covering the entire horizontal plane. It exhibits 5% (2.38-2.5GHz) -10dB impedance and 3dB axial ratio overlapping bandwidth. The main radiator of the dielectric resonator allows for a compact size <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(0.44\lambda_{0}\times 0.44\lambda_{0}\times 0.14\lambda_{0})$</tex> and high radiation efficiency over -1.2dB. Therefore, it is well-suited for WLAN systems to offer diverse polarizations and extensive coverage.

articleTitle: A 2 × 2 Array at 5.8GHz with Parasitic Elements for Inter-Element Coupling Reduction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A square four element array is enhanced with parasitic elements to reduce inter-element coupling on both principal planes. This is a first step in devising large reduced-coupling arrays for smart antennas able to effectively scan over wide angles. Particular attention is devoted to make the parasitic elements compact so as to allow a tight packing of radiating elements to avoid grating lobes in scanning.

articleTitle: Radar Range Equation for Repeater-Aided Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The use of repeaters for radar applications has been a topic of interest for multiple years because of the need to increase received signal power and the additional degrees of freedom that can be acquired by distributing antenna elements in the spatial domain. This paper focuses on the derivation of the radar range equation in the presence of a repeater that collects and retransmits scattered signals from the scene. We discuss the contribution of repeaters and how they affect received signal power and derive the radar range equation in the presence of the repeater. We include calculated results that show the utility of repeaters in the presence of targets with increased bistatic radar cross-sections that exhibit strong specular reflections.

articleTitle: Gated Reflect Line Self-Calibration Technique for Accurate Material Parameter Extraction with Focus Beam Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper introduces a self-calibration Gated Re-flect Line technique of free-space focus beam systems with experimental results for validation. The procedure assumes same surface of the Reflect standard is used to measure the back scattered channels of each network analyzer port. Equivalent cascaded scattering parameter blocks are then formulated to identify the reflection coefficient of the Reflect metrology standard. The calibration scheme is subsequently updated to include the actual reflection coefficient rather than use the ideal metal plate assumption. Finally, measured results with a 2–18 GHz focus beam system and plexiglass sample are included to compare the self-calibration to conventional technique with a Monte Carlo error analysis. This self-calibration procedure accounts for imperfections in the Reflect standard where any deviations from an ideal perfect electrical conductor result in residual errors. The introduced technique enhances the measurement accuracy and enables loss tangent extraction of low-loss materials.

articleTitle: A High-Efficiency Patch Rectenna for RF Energy Harvesting Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This letter presents a new patch type rectenna with an integrated matching network and rectifier circuit. This system consists of two rectangular patch antennas (RPA), two Schottky diodes, and a RC filter. Non-radiating rectangular patch antenna is used, and the input impedance of antennas is tuned to be matched directly to the rectifier circuit. The proposed rectenna is designed to operate at 2.45 GHz with a maximum power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 71.4% for an input power of 5 dBm and a load resistance of 500 ohm. The results of this study suggest that the proposed patch rectenna can be utilized for energy harvesting and wireless power transmission systems.

articleTitle: Optimizations of Dielectric Slab Surfaces with Genetic Algorithms and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents an efficient combination of genetic algorithms and machine-learning techniques to optimize scattering properties of 3D dielectric (PLA) slabs with surface deformations. The top and bottom surfaces of slabs are optimized to obtain the desired electromagnetic properties while they are represented by Bezier functions so that final designs can be fabricated via 3D printers. The numerical results demonstrate the superiority of the developed optimization environment to reach the desired scattering characteristics.

articleTitle: A S/C Dual-Band Dual-Polarized Shared Aperture Antenna Array for Retrodirective Arrays
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A S/C dual-band dual-polarized wide-scan shared-aperture antenna array for retrodirective arrays is proposed in this paper. Both arrays have a rectangular lattice with the element spacing proportional to the operating frequencies at 3.8 GHz and 5.8 GHz, which meets the configuration requirements of arrays in retrodirective systems with different operating frequencies. Two arrays share the same aperture through height differences of dipole antennas printed on a single layer of substrate. Elements in two arrays are placed perpendicular to each other, exhibiting orthogonal polarizations. Improved isolation between the two bands is accomplished through the filters on the feed lines. Simulated results demonstrate that the proposed array exhibits good impedance match with a relative bandwidth nearly 31%. Optimized parasitic patches enable scanning capabilities of the array up to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm \mathbf{60}^{\circ}$</tex> at two main operating frequencies.

articleTitle: Balanis' Multifaceted Impact on Academia, Industry, Government and Beyond
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Professor Balanis is widely acknowledged for his exceptional research contributions in the field, particularly through his renowned worldwide books on Antennas and Electromagnetics. These books are considered invaluable assets by students and researchers in electromagnetics and antenna studies, reflecting Prof. Balanis' profound impact on the field. Yet, his impact goes beyond academia, reaching into industry, government, professional societies, student mentoring, and personal connections.

articleTitle: Sensitivity-Enhanced CSRR-Loaded SIW Chipless Tag for Real-Time Coating Assessment on Medical Implants
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this study, a new chipless Complementary Split-ring Resonators (CSRR) loaded Substrate Integrated Waveguide (SIW) tag is coupled with a coplanar antenna for real-time sensing and detection. This sensor was created for real-time monitoring of lubricant evaporation on surfaces that have been infused with lubricant. The stability of the lubricating layer is a crucial determinant for the efficient operation of these coatings. The proposed sensor consists of an ultrawide-band antenna as a reader to couple power to the CSSR-loaded SIW sensing tag. The sensor design and operation have been carefully confirmed using both simulation and measurements, confirming its capacity to detect lubricant evaporation with high sensitivity. With 0.1 MHz frequency shift in resonance frequency per 1 µL of lubricant, this sensor stands as a significant advancement in the field of medical implant technology, offering a real-time solution for ensuring the effectiveness of lubricant-infused coatings since their assessment is necessary to minimize complications associated with medical implants, such as the non-specific adhesion of blood components and bacteria.

articleTitle: Electric Energy Balance Evaluation of a 5.8-GHz-Band Wireless Communication with Power Transmission System by Time-Division Operation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper demonstrates a 5.8-GHz-band wireless communication system that is powered by a 5.8 GHz microwave power transmission (MPT) system. Time-division operation method was used for coexistence of the communication and MPT. Two measurements of the coexistence possibility by changing the MPT power, and electric energy balance of supplied DC power from the rectifier and consumption power in the sensor station were performed. As a result, the proposed system successfully demonstrated the compatibility and sustainable energy balance.

articleTitle: A Dual-Band Dual-Polarization Reflectarray Antenna with Large Frequency Ratio and High Aperture Reuse
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a dual-band dual-polarized reflectarray antenna that operates in X-band and K-band. The reflectarray consists of two different sizes of Phoenix rings printed on a double-layer dielectric substrate and stacked to achieve aperture reuse. The bottom Phoenix ring works in the low-frequency band and has low coupling with the upper ring, which enables independent tuning of the dual-band without mutual interference. The array simulation is conducted with two horn feeds in two orthogonal polarization directions and the results demonstrate that the reflectarray can operate at 7.9-8.3 GHz and 19.6-20.4 GHz, achieving a large frequency ratio of 2.5 and supporting dual-polarization. The reflectarray achieves gains of 24.7 and 32.58 dBi, and aperture efficiencies of 49% and 48%, at 8 and 20 GHz, respectively.

articleTitle: Conformal Ultra-Wideband Antenna for 5G-Sub-6GHz Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The design of a planar wideband antenna for a 5G sub-6 GHz application is presented. The antenna is excited by a probe through a microstrip line. Two parasitic strips are coupled to the microstrip feeding line to increase the bandwidth from 14.28% to 21.7%. To further increase the bandwidth, two U-shaped parasitic strips are coupled to the radiating edges of the patch. These strips have increased the bandwidth to 28.57 %. The final proposed antenna with a single element exhibits 3.3 dBi gain and 83.85% efficiency. The proposed antenna's gain and bandwidth are compared to the initial element with two scenario feeding techniques,: series and corporate feeding.

articleTitle: An Electronically Switchable Metasurface for Multifunctional Electromagnetic Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The present paper introduces a multifunctional, electronically switchable metasurface consisting of a passive resistive frequency selective surface absorber combined with an active metasurface, operating in the band 9–13 GHz. By selectively controlling the biasing state (OFF/ON) of the PIN diodes included in the active layer, the response of the overall structure can be dynamically switched from total reflection to absorption mode. The passive absorber, positioned beneath the active metasurface, provides a wideband absorption behavior during the AFSS transparent state. The novelty lies in the hybrid combination of a switchable active surface with a passive and resistive FSS into a single arrangement, resulting in multifunctional characteristics with an extremely reduced number of PIN diodes. By deriving the pin diode equivalent circuit model, accurate full-wave simulations have been carried out. Results confirm the structure's ability to dynamically switch from total reflection to a −10 dB absorptivity level ranging from 9 to 13 GHz, under incidence angles up to 30°. Therefore, the proposed design can represent an effective and robust solution to realize multifunctional structures, essential for regulating electromagnetic wave propagation in manifold applications, as intelligent surfaces and radar cross section camouflaging.

articleTitle: A Dual-Polarized 5G mmWave Micro Base Station Antenna Based on Differential Feed Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a dual polarization multilayer patch micro base station antenna based on a differential feed structure is proposed. The antenna is designed with a three-layer radiation patch structure, with the first layer connected to the feed network through metal through holes, and the second and third layers also connected through metal through holes. Two differential feed networks were designed corresponding to their two polarization modes. The stacked structure of multi-layer radiation patches increases the bandwidth of the antenna from 23.21 to 29.60 GHz, with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S_{11}$</tex> less than −10 dB. And a square ring is added around the first layer of the radiation patch to improve the isolation of the antenna, which can achieve greater than 20 dB. At the same time, the antenna has a stable gain and directional pattern effect, and the gain can achieve a size greater than 7 dBi within the bandwidth range. Therefore, this antenna array has the potential to be a candidate antenna for large-scale millimeter wave array applications.

articleTitle: The General PML in FDTD for Ferromagnetic Component Simulations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A new general perfect matching layer technique is proposed in the FDTD method for computational-Multiphysics. The hybrid computations aim at solving the ferromagnetic material problems, where the simulations are accomplished by electromagnetics and the magnetic dipole moment computations. The new general perfect matching layer decays the propagating waves under the condition of multi-physical simulations in the ferromagnetic material. Full absorption is accomplished by setup of perfect electric conductors outside the perfect matching layer boundary, where the corresponding fields vanish.

articleTitle: Comparative D/Q and Characteristic Mode Analysis (CMA) of Rectangular and Circular Microstrip Patch Antennas for Bandwidth Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The concept of antenna performance characterization has recently been fundamentally augmented to include its near and far field behavior in terms of its impedance (or the quality factor, Q) and directivity (D) parameters, respectively, obtained through full-wave (MoM) solutions. Separately, the antenna performance is also quantified through characteristic mode analysis (CMA) by computing the modal significance from the MoM solution. These two generally different approaches, have been applied here to probe-fed rectangular and circular microstrip patch antennas for a comparative assessment of their respective 2: 1 VSWR bandwidth enhancement characteristics. This assessment is carried out by following an earlier approach of coaxial feed location optimization, and it is shown here numer-ically and experimentally to yield a 2:1 VSWR bandwidth of 33% for rectangular microstrip patches designed on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\epsilon_{r}=6$</tex> substrate (TMM-6). Following a similar approach, the preliminary results here show that the circular patch produces far less bandwidth than a rectangular patch subject to the same design optimization method. The results have a significant impact in practical design of electrically small patch antennas with restricted SWaP (Size, Weight and Power) criteria.

articleTitle: An Ultra-Wideband and Polarization-Insensitive Frequency-Selective Rasorber/Absorber with a Wide Switchable Transmission Band
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a novel active frequency-selective rasorber/absorber with a wide switchable transmission band is presented. The proposed structure consists of two lossy layers and one lossless layer separated by an air gap between each two layers. The design of each layer is rotationally symmetric with polarization insensitivity and can be controlled by the loaded PIN diodes. The entire structure can hereby operate in “rasorber” mode or “absorber” mode under the “OFF” or “ON” states of the diodes. Simulation results show that the continuous 10-dB low - reflection band of the proposed structure under “rasorber” mode covers 1.02-11.89 GHz with a bandwidth ratio (BWR) of 11.66:1, where the 80% absorption bandwidth is 153.40%, covering 0.96-7.28 GHz and the 3-dB transmission window ranges from 8.14 GHz to 12.01 GHz with a relative bandwidth of 38.41 %. In the “absorber” mode, the BWR of the 80% absorption achieves 14.03:1 ranging from 0.90 GHz to 12.63 GHz under normal incidence. Compared with the existing passive rasorbers, absorbers, and switchable structures, the proposed active design has superior performance metrics and exhibits potential for broader applications.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Knee Imaging for Clinical Diagnosis and Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The increasing occurrence of knee injuries highlights the urgent need for early detection and frequent monitoring to prevent severe ligament damage and long treatment periods. This paper explores the requirements for clinical knee imaging, associated challenges, and the potential of electromagnetic knee imaging systems, whether they are portable or wearable. The successful clinical implementation of EMI technology demands a thorough understanding of the system's requirements of imaging antennas and processing algorithms, and associated challenges. This paper summarizes the state of electromagnetic knee imaging systems and discusses the current challenges and potential solutions.

articleTitle: A Single-Layer Unidirectional Antenna for Wearable IoT Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a single-layer unidirectional antenna designed for wearable Internet of Things (IoT) devices. The antenna comprises an active dipole driven through a feeding port and a passive dipole excited by the near fields generated by the active dipole. The antenna achieves a unidirectional pattern by effectively canceling the backward radiation from the dipole elements. Based on this concept, an antenna with a low profile of 0.065 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda_{\mathrm{O}}$</tex> is designed. The antenna achieves a front-to-back ratio (FTBR) of 19.4 dB and a realized gain of 5.85 dBi at 28 GHz. The proposed antenna operates in the bandwidth of 26.7 GHz to 28.8 GHz with an FTBR above 10 dB and S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> less than −10 dB.

articleTitle: Experimental Demonstration of Tissue-Independent Camera Integrated Antenna for WCE
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: For unobtrusive camera integration and robust gastrointestinal (GI) tract performance, a tissue-independent planar stacked meandered antenna along an annular ring substrate is proposed for the 401 MHz medical device radio communications service (MedRadio) band. The proposed topology is showcased through conventional printed circuit board (PCB) technology. Measurement results validate the direct camera integration and excellent tissue-independent performance in terms of impedance matching and radiation.

articleTitle: Indoor Non-Line-of-Sight Target Detection Using Radar Polarimetry at J-band
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a method for identifying non-line-of-sight targets in a radar image is proposed. This method does not require a priori knowledge of the wall location or its presence. The proposed approach relies on the measured difference between co-polarization backscatter of the target. To establish a foundation for this technique, the wave reflection coefficient of drywalls at J-band frequencies is investigated for horizontal and vertical polarizations. Experiments are conducted using a millimeter-wave FMCW radar system at 227 - 228 GHz frequency range for angles of incidence from 40° - 77° to show that VV reflection is higher than HH. Then, noting that the VV and HH backscatter for most targets at J-band is the same, object detection around the corner of a corridor is done for angles of incidence from 30° - 60°. Detection through both single and double wall reflection is demonstrated and the results show a decaying co-pol ratio with increasing angle of incidence.

articleTitle: Efficient Localized-Solution Iterative Solver for Large-Scale Antenna Array Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: An efficient local solution-based iterative solver for the analysis of large disjoint antenna arrays is presented in this paper. Runtimes are shown to be competitive with the multilevel fast multipole method (MLFMM) in the commercial FEKO software suite. The proposed solver is shown to be especially beneficial for the computation of multiple excitation configurations, which is required, e.g., to compute embedded element patterns (EEPs).

articleTitle: Dual-Band Conformal Frequency Selective Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This study addresses the critical design considerations for Frequency Selective Surfaces (FSS) with a focus on achieving band-stop behavior in the fundamental C- and X-band frequencies. The complexity of attaining band-stop characteristics in both bands, along with the effects of conformal configurations, such as concave and convex bending, hemispheric, and conical, pose significant challenges. The research provides a systematic strategy for optimizing the unit-cell properties to achieve band- stop behavior in both bands, ensuring stability in TE and TM modes. The study utilizes CST Microwave Studio for simulation, offering a comprehensive understanding of the complex designs. The results contribute to the creation of flexible and effective FSS designs for band-stop applications in the C- and X-bands.

articleTitle: Combining Equivalent Circuits, NanoVNAs, and Standard EDA Tools for Engaging Electromagnetics and RF Engineering Laboratory Exercises
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: We introduce a reverse-design exercise for electromagnetic, RF, and antenna engineering courses, based on equivalent circuit models. With accurate measurement and modelling skills being the most fundamental and transferable skills in an RF engineering workplace, a series of lab exercises for based on co-simulation and measurements is presented. Combining electromagnetic simulations, closed-form transmission line modelling, and NanoVNA measurements, the exercise allows the student to evaluate different simulation approaches and develop their own lumped equivalent circuit models. This paper introduces the lab hardware design kit, an example structure for a Masters-level course lab exercise, and preliminary insights into the implementation challenges and benefits from a student and instructor perspective.

articleTitle: Integrated Broadside and Endfire Antenna Based on Spoof Surface Plasmon Polaritons
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: With the fine feature of frequency scanning, leaky wave antennas (LWAs) have been widely used in wireless communication systems. However, traditional LWAs are difficult to realize endfire radiation, which limits beam-scanning range. Recently, Spoof surface plasmon polaritons (SSPPs) have attracted widespread attention due to characteristics including high confinement and dispersion controllability. Microwave components and antennas based on SSPPs have been extensively investigated for various applications. In this work, we propose an integrated broadside and endfire antenna based on SSPPs. This antenna achieves a wide switch angle by changing radiation patterns. By controlling the phase difference of feedlines, the current distribution on radiation structure can be regulated. As a result, odd or even mode can be excited on the modulated SSPPs metallic structure, leading to the switch of radiation patten between frequency scanning toward broadside and endfire. We believe that the proposed antenna has potential applications in wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: Simultaneous Design of Element Topology and Switch Placement in 2-Switch 4-State Reconfigurable Reflectarray Unit Cells
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The switch-reconfigured unit cell (SRUC) capable of generating variable phase response is one of the enabling technologies for reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) and beam steerable reflect-/transmit-arrays. Traditional approaches designing SRUC have primarily relied on basic element geometries with specific switch placement. However, these methods lack design freedom and result in excessive use of switches, limitations in performance, and complexity in design. In this paper, we employ binary particle swarm optimization (BPSO) to simultaneously design the element topology and switch placement of the SRUC. Specifically, the design and performance of a 4-state (2-bit) K-band circularly polarized (CP) reflectarray SRUC that utilizes single-layer element and merely two switches is presented.

articleTitle: Miniaturization of Printed Patch Antenna for Ku band Satellite Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper aims to investigate the design of a miniaturized microstrip patch antenna for Ku-band (12–18 GHz) satellite applications. With an impressive return loss of - 43.01 dB and a frequency bandwidth of 0.3 GHz, the antenna ensures good impedance matching. This study set out to examine how array configurations performed in terms of bandwidth, gain, VSWR, and return loss. The comparative analysis revealed that as the number of elements in the array increases. The 1×8 array antenna offered the highest gain, making it appropriate for applications needing improved signal strength and coverage.

articleTitle: Frequency-Controlled Polarization Reconfigurable Antenna: Concept and Design
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A novel frequency-controlled polarization reconfigurable antenna is presented in this work, featuring controllable linear polarization (LP) orientation through an adjustable phase shift. A phase-control model is introduced by substituting a frequency-dependent phase shift to enable a 180° LP reconfiguration by varying the frequency across a tailored bandwidth. Subsequently, an antenna system capable of continuously changing its LP orientation across a wide operating bandwidth is developed. By varying the source frequency from 9.6 to 11.65 GHz, a total 180° LP polarization rotation is achieved. The measured realized gains of the antenna range from 7.0 to 9.8 dBi in the working bandwidth. The frequency-controlled polarization rotation model represents a cost-effective solution for reconfiguring the antenna polarizations, which is well-suited for applications like diverse orientation object identification in sensing and detection systems.

articleTitle: Vivaldi Dipole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this study, we present a new class of Ultra-Wide Band (UWB) antennas which combine the radiating capabilities of electric currents on metal surfaces with those of tapered slots. S-shaped slots with tapered open ends are used to separate the dipole metal screens in the design. In addition to its function as a radiating element, the slot redistributes the current on the dipole screens, so increasing the frequency bandwidth of the antenna. Using this technology, it has been proven that the instantaneous frequency bandwidth of dipole antennas can be greatly increased. As examples, we have designed antennas with a bandwidth ranging from below 1GHz to above 7GHz, and from 380MHz to above 2GHz, as well as some compact antennas with a bandwidth exceeding 100%.

articleTitle: High-Directivity Antenna Based on Highly Homogeneous Zero-Index Metamaterial
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Zero-index metamaterials (ZIMs) can support uniform electromagnetic field distributions at any frequency. Performance of ZIMs-based applications is hampered by the conventional ZIM's homogenization level-only 3 unit cells per free-space wavelength, which is essentially limited by the low-permittivity inclusions <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{r}}\approx 12)$</tex> and background matrix <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{r}}\approx 1)$</tex>. Here, by filling high-permittivity SrTiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> ceramic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{r}}\approx 294)$</tex> pillars in BaTiO3 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{r}}\approx 25)$</tex> background matrix, we demonstrated a highly homogeneous microwave ZIM, leading to an over 3-fold increase in the homogenization level. Based on the uniform distribution of the spatial phase throughout the ZIM, we demonstrated a high-directivity antenna by incorporating our ZIM in a metallic waveguide, approaching the fundamental limit in the antenna directivity when the aperture size varies from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.7\lambda_{0}\times 0.7\lambda 0$</tex> to a very large scale. This antenna has broad applications in wireless communications, remote sensing, and global positioning satellites.

articleTitle: Planar Overlapped Wireless Power Transfer Systems for Spatial Freedom of Multiple Receivers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a two-dimensional (2D) planer overlapped wireless power transfer (WPT) system using high-isolated planar coils for spatial freedom of multiple receivers. The proposed transmitting coil is arrayed with highly isolated coils. The proposed planer overlapped WPT coil can transmit the power to the multiple receiving coils regardless of misalignments. For the performance verification, the power transfer efficiency (PTE) under the misalignments is measured. The proposed WPT system is matched at 6.78 MHz and has a transmission efficiency of approximately 70% in multiple wireless charging and misalignment environments.

articleTitle: Programmable Hybrid Spoof Planar Plasmonic Waveguide-based Fixed Frequency Beam-Scanning Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A hybrid spoof planar plasmonic waveguide (HSPPW) is a microwave device that achieves strong field confinement and a significant reduction in plasma frequency by coupling the electromagnetic wave guided by a dielectric substrate and a structured metallic layer. It is formed by separating a structured metal from a surface plasmon polaritons surface by a small gap. In this research, we proposed a reconfigurable HSPPW-based beam-scanning antenna for fixed-frequency beam scanning. To validate this unique idea, rigorous simulations are performed, and compared with the theoretical analysis. The proposed single-layered, easy-to-fabricate model of HSPPW-based beam scanning antenna shows a wide scanning range of 90° (from −60° to +30°), with a high gain at 4.87GHz.

articleTitle: Design of a Scalable IRS-Assisted Communication System with Generalized Beamforming Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
