abstract: Intelligent reflecting surfaces (IRS) are envisaged to be a prominent part of the next-generation communication networks. To exploit the benefits of the IRS, beamforming is indispensable. In this work, we propose a generalized beamforming algorithm for an IRS-based wireless system, along with the design of a hardware prototype to implement it. The algorithm is versatile enough to be deployed on an IRS array of arbitrary size with unit cells that have any number of discrete phase shifts. A prototype is designed with an array of single-bit phase shifting unit cells and a peripheral control circuit to demonstrate beamforming using the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: 60 GHz Programmable Dynamic Metasurface Antenna for 6G Avenues, Contactless HealthCare, and Smart Factories
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: We present the first-ever design of a digitally coded Dynamic Metasurface Antenna (DMA) at 60 GHz millimeter-wave (mmWave) band. First, a novel fully addressable complementary electric inductive-capacitive (CELC) metamaterial element is designed and embedded with PIN diodes for 1-bit control. Then 16-element 1-D DMA array is designed to synthesize a variety of beam patterns by digital coding using an external FPGA. The proposed 60 GHz DMA prototype allows customized beamforming and signal processing, making it suitable for beyond 5G and 6G applications, such as ISAC, holographic communication, sensing, and imaging, mmWave wireless smart industries as well as contactless healthcare monitoring and sensing.

articleTitle: Additive Manufactured Gap Waveguide Based Antenna for Difference Radiation Pattern in Ka-Band
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This work introduces a study on the application of Additive Manufacturing technology in RF components. Specifically, we evaluate an antenna based on radiating slots, designed to generate a difference pattern in the Ka-band. The antenna topology relies on groove gap waveguide technology, incorporating an integrated feeding network. The numerical and practical results demonstrate good agreement. Hence, additive manufacturing offers a reliable fabrication process, ensuring manageable tolerances and roughness within this specified frequency range.

articleTitle: A Folded Pyramid-Shaped Microstrip Antenna with Improved Bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Microstrip antennas are an indispensable part of modern wireless communication systems and 3D printing has become very popular to overcome the design limitations of traditional microstrip technology. In addition, 3D printing technology provides an affordable cost, ease-of-manufacturing the complex models and easy availability of raw materials. In this study, a pyramid-shaped antenna is proposed utilizing Polylactic acid (PLA) filament. The conventional square (flat) antenna is shaped like a pyramid by folding its corners. So as to prevent surface waves and spurious propagation in the design, instead of increasing the thickness of the entire substrate, only the thickness of radiating square patch area is increased. With the proposed approach the projected antenna resonant size can be minimized up to 50% compared to its flat version. On the other hand, fractional antenna bandwidth has increased from 3.8% to 13%. Furthermore, an increased gain up to 2 dB is achieved in the operating frequency bandwidth with folded design. Simulation results show that the proposed antenna design can be an alternative for X-band applications.

articleTitle: Radial Leaky Wave SIW Slotted Array Antenna for Millimeter-Wave Automotive Radar Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A Substrate Integrated Waveguide (SIW) radial slotted array antenna covering the V band (57 - 61.42 GHz) is presented. The antenna consists of an SIW horn fed by coplanar waveguide transition (CPW) and a slot array with varying lengths that radiate at 60 GHz. The radiation is generated from the slots tapered to have a leaky wave beam. The overall dimension of the antenna is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$9.64 \times 6.96\times 0.16\lambda_{L}^{3}$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda_{L}$</tex> is the antenna's wavelength at 60 GHz. The antenna achieves a bandwidth of 7.5% (4.5 GHz), a maximum gain of 17.15 dBi, an average efficiency of 77.3%, and a 15-degree scanning beam, with low back lobes. The proposed antenna is a good candidate for autonomous radar applications.

articleTitle: Feasibility of Bilateral Joint Flexion Monitoring Using Wearable Loop Sensors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Monitoring human movement is relevant to several crucial sectors, including healthcare, sports, and beyond. Recently, we introduced a new class of wearable loop sensors for monitoring joint flexion that overcomes shortcomings in the state-of-the-art and allows seamless motion capture in real-time without restricting natural movement. The sensor consists of transmit and receive loops coupled via magnetic field. This sensor has been demonstrated for monitoring one joint on one leg at a time. Monitoring knee joint movement on both legs simultaneously can allow monitoring of crucial gait parameters. However, placement of two sensors in close vicinity can lead to interference between the two due to coupling from the transmitter of one sensor to the receiver of another. In this work, we study the condition for non-interference and demonstrate the feasibility of bilateral knee flexion monitoring. Guidelines to improve the non-interference performance are also laid out. This feasibility study opens doors for full-body motion capture using our wearable loop sensors.

articleTitle: Comparison of OFDM and LFM Waveform Schemes for Ranging: A Correlation Perspective
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) waveforms have been employed in communications systems for years and are the key waveform candidates for beyond-fifth-generation (5G) communication networks. In this paper, we compare OFDM waveforms to linear frequency- modulated (LFM) waveforms which are widely exploited in modern radar systems. We discuss the utility of OFDM waveforms for joint communications and sensing but also provide a comparison between the two in terms of their correlation properties. OFDM waveforms exhibit improved cross-correlation properties compared to LFM waveforms which can yield excellent resistance to interference between multiple radar transmitters without any cooperation. We express the theory behind our work and include simulations supporting our claims.

articleTitle: Privacy Preserving Radio Frequency Speech Sensing With Deep Learning Towards Improved Hearing Aids
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Hearing loss is a profound public health issue typically addressed with microphone sensing hearing aids calibrated to compensate for an individual's hearing loss pattern. However, microphones often generate low sound quality in noisy environments resulting in low device adoption. This paper explores use of noise resistant Radio Frequency (RF) radar speech sensing micro-Doppler (µD) shifts generated from a speaker's vocal tract with Deep Learning (DL) speech classification for audio replay. It extends earlier work using a vowels dataset to whole sentences to train and test seven DL model types that gave encouraging accuracy results ranging from 75\% to 91\%. Model training time typically took 4 minutes and no more than 20 epochs to converge with loss rates suggesting potential viability of RF µD sensing for more complex vocabularies.

articleTitle: A Method of Improving Active Impedance Matching of Phased Array Antennas Based on Self-Induced Current
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A method of improving active impedance matching of phased array antennas based on self-induced current in planar array is proposed. To modify the coupling-induced currents on antenna elements, we introduced self-induced currents on the operating elements. This method is simply verified and proved to be feasible in this work.

articleTitle: Full-Wave Simulations Using Fast Hybrid Method for L-Band Microwave Propagation in Forested Areas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: We perform full-wave simulations of propagation of L-band microwave signals in forested areas to study forest effects on microwave remote sensing, wireless communications, and hidden object detection. Initially, full-wave simulations of forests were limited to eight-meter-tall trees. With the aid of computational enhancement by a fast hybrid method (FHM) solving Maxwell's equations, a height of trees extends to 13 m followed by 17 m. The FHM applies to 91 trees of a height of 17 m, where the volumetric space in the simulation domain is equivalent to 133 wavelengths by 133 wavelengths and 80 wavelengths. We will continue to investigate the effects of tapering and bifurcated trunks, as well as the presence of leaves, on microwave remote sensing. We illustrate the spatial distribution of electric fields under forests. Computational efficiency of the FHM is also discussed. The results indicate that L-band microwave signals can penetrate through forests, enabling the detection of soil and objects below, and GPS signals can be successfully received by receivers beneath forested areas.

articleTitle: Dual-State V-Band Circularly Polarized Bull's Eye Antenna Fed by Septum Orthomode Transducer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: We present a circularly polarized (CP) Bull's Eye (BE) antenna integrated with an Orthomode transducer (OMT) operating at the V-band 54 - 66 GHz to achieve Right- and Left-Hand RH/LH CP. The BEA effective fractional bandwidth is 12.9% with a peak gain of 15.2 dBi and an axial ratio below 0.9 dB. The BEA uses three concentric radiating two non-radiating grooves to minimize the edge diffraction effects. Moreover, the OMT consists of 6 graded steps with three different thicknesses.

articleTitle: W-Band 2-Bit Reconfigurable Reflectarray Element for High Data Rate Satellite Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Modern satellite communication systems require high data rate and fast beam forming capabilities, which make designing an aperture for these systems increasingly challenging. However, this paper offers a solution in the form of a novel W-band 2-bit reconfigurable reflectarray element that can meet these demands. This element utilizes vertical integration, which enables high scalability at 94 GHz, and has 2-bit phase control for fast beam forming. The experimental results of the proposed reflectarray element demonstrate good agreement with the simulated results, making it a promising solution for future satellite communication systems.

articleTitle: Shaped Array-Fed Reflector Antennas for Reconfigurable GEO Communication Satellite
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Array-Fed Reflectors are currently considered as the leading technology for the next generation of reconfigurable geostationary communication satellites. The presence of the reflector allows to guarantee high-gain values while keeping the number of radiating elements under control. In this paper, we study the effect of adding a shaping on top of the parabolic reflector to improve the performance of such systems for noncircular coverages. Specifically, two configurations are optimised for an elliptical and irregular coverage. The simulation results confirm that the shaping guarantees a high average gain and uniform input power across the array.

articleTitle: Tri-Mode Dipole Antenna for Enhanced Bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper introduces a tri-mode dipole antenna designed for enhanced bandwidth. Through the strategic placement of stub and capacitive loadings, first order mode frequency is increased and fifth order mode frequency is decreased towards the third order mode frequency. The synergy of these modes contributes to the overall enhancement of the antenna's bandwidth. The proposed antenna operates within the frequency range of 1.2 GHz to 3.8 GHz, representing an impressive bandwidth of approximately 104%. Moreover, the antenna offers a peak gain of approximately 3.5 dBi within a compact size of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.58\lambda_{L}\times 0.12\lambda_{L}$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda_{L}$</tex>, is the wavelength at the lowest frequency of operation.

articleTitle: Wideband Omnidirectional Circularly Polarized Antenna Based on Common and Differential Modes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A wideband omnidirectional circularly polarized antenna (CPA) based on common and differential modes is presented in this paper. To radiate omnidirectionally in a wide bandwidth, a modified monopole antenna (MMA) operating in common mode and a four-dipole array (FDA) operating in differential mode are designed and analyzed. Based on the innate orthogonality and 90° phase difference between common mode and differential mode, the MMA and FDA are combined to form an omnidirectional CPA. The proposed omnidirectional CPA is obtained operates at 2.80~3.55 GHz (23.6<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>) with a 4.4-dB maximum gain and 1.8-dB out-of-roundness.

articleTitle: A Generalized Friis Transmission Formula for Multiport Antenna Arrays
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A generalized Friis transmission formula for multi-port antenna arrays, based on the concept of unnamed power gain, is presented. The examples included demonstrate two key properties of the generalized formula: “symmetry under link direction reversal” and “vanishing sensitivity to terminations for small coupling”.

articleTitle: Exploiting AMC Structures in the Design of Wearable, Platform-Tolerant RFID Tags
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this work we describe a platform tolerant, versatile RFID tag, easily tunable across the global RFID frequency band. The proposed RFID tag incorporates a compact Artificial Magnetic Conductor (AMC) structure, serving as a shielding element for an ungrounded tag antenna. It can be conveniently mounted on materials with low permittivity, metal objects, or attached to the human body for wearable applications, achieving a read range above 11 meters. The tag design prioritizes simplicity in manufacturing, enabling cost-effective production. Detailed design and simulations were conducted using CST Microwave Studio, a general-purpose software for analyzing 3D electromagnetic structures.

articleTitle: Optical-Theorem-Based Intrusion Detection and Tracking in Multipath Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Optical-theorem-based coherent change detection and imaging methods are derived, and conditions for their practical applicability with limited view sensing apertures are derived and discussed with the help of numerical examples. Two broad classes of target regions are identified, namely, coherent versus incoherent regions, and the best detection methods for each class (coherent versus incoherent or energy-detector-based) are examined, both theoretically and computationally.

articleTitle: Characterization of Material Resistivity by Using a Self-Tunable Chip for Gas Sensing Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This work addresses a self-tunable tag specifically for its potential application as a gas sensor. The response of a tag equipped with the chip Magnus S3 in presence of a carbon nanotube (CNT) layer modeled as a resistive sheet is analyzed. CNTs are highly sensitive to gas molecules especially ammonia <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\text{NH}_{3})$</tex>. The study aims at determining the optimal location and size of the resistive sheet within the tag. The variation of gas concentration is modelled by the variation of the sheet resistivity of the thin layer.

articleTitle: High Polarization Purity for Aperture Coupled Microstrip Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A design method to suppress the cross-polarization of an aperture-coupled microstrip antenna is presented. The design consists of three substrate layers with embedded vias in the middle layer surrounding the coupling slots to constrain the electric field. A cross-polarization suppression of more than 20 dB in the orthogonal E- and H-planes is achieved at 20 GHz. Furthermore, the design nearly doubles the impedance fractional bandwidth without adversely affecting the antenna's performance in terms of gain and backlobe level. The proposed design is thus a suitable candidate for antenna arrays with high cross-polarization isolation requirements.

articleTitle: Complex Reflectance Coverage Retrieval of Coupled Resonator Metasurface Unit Cell Using Printed Capacitor Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A novel tunable metasurface unit cell (UC) is described with variable reflective phase and magnitude through the DC-biasing of resistive and capacitive active components. Cuts made to the resonator geometry to facilitate RF-DC isolation between the device terminals has been shown to have detrimental effects on the UC's reflective performance, significantly reducing its complex reflectance coverages. This paper demonstrates a very simple approach to rectify this issue, through the application of a printed capacitor to create an RF short across various isolation gaps within the unit cell. The results of a preliminary full-wave simulation in FEM-HFSS are presented to demonstrate and confirm the concept.

articleTitle: Wideband Multilayer Crossover for Millimeter-Wave Beamforming Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Beamforming networks are essential for direction- finding applications. It could be integrated into multilayer structures to create 2-D scanning beams. This paper introduces a wideband multilayer crossover operating at the millimeter-wave (mmWave) band. A wideband multilayer hybrid coupler is used to design a new mmWave crossover. The proposed crossover presents a compact shape cascading two hybrid couplers while occupying less than half of the typical form. The proposed crossover displays good matching and isolation levels for the frequency range 24–30 GHz.

articleTitle: A Modulation Method for Non-ideal Phase of Time-Modulated Modules
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a compensation method to solve the phase non-ideality in a time-modulated (TM) module. The method focuses on optimizing the suppressed sideband level (SBL) by adjusting the modulation time in the presence of phase deviations. Simulation results for two cases show that the maximum normalized suppressed SBL is reduced from −21.16dB to −26.16dB and from −12.13dB to −17.40dB, respectively, when using the optimized choices of time-shift terms.

articleTitle: Parameterization of Antipodal Vivaldi Antennas Using RSIW Technology Based on Python
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)

authors.preferredName: Priscilla Kadja Pontes De Melo Carneiro

abstract: The use of artificial intelligence in antenna design is in high demand. This paper explores the integration of Ansys HFSS Electronics Desktop software with the Python programming language to streamline the antenna parameterization process and reduce design time. The paper will begin by introducing the theoretical basis of the design method development, followed by a demonstration of the implementation process of HFSS with the Python development tool. Finally, simulated and measured results of the antenna design using RSIW technology will be presented, showing an increase of 2.06 GHz in bandwidth and a reduction of 0.92 GHz in cutoff frequency, when compared to the results obtained with the classic SIW.

articleTitle: Spectral Projection Model Applied to Scattering of Electromagnetic Waves from Conducting Ellipsoidal Surfaces with Arbitrary Cross Sections
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In a previous paper, a new technique named the Spectral Projection Model (SPM) was formulated by the Remote Sensing Group at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth, as an alternate approach to Method of Moments to estimate the fields due to the scattering of electromagnetic waves from cylindrical conducting surfaces [1]. SPM evolved from the decomposition of the Green's function in the electric field integral equation (EFIE) for describing the boundary conditions. The decomposition of the Green's function is implemented using the addition theorem for Bessel and Hankel functions. In this paper, the technique is extended to scattering from three-dimensional, ellipsoidal surfaces. The scattered field patterns are calculated and compared with results using modal expansion technique. The method is verified using simulations of scattering from conducting, ellipsoidal surfaces with arbitrary axial ratios and the results compared with the those from the modal expansion technique.

articleTitle: An Effective Technique for the Characterization of Dielectric Materials Through Terahertz Time-Domain Measurements in Reflection Mode
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Terahertz (THz) devices and applications are recently gaining much attention due to the increased availability of THz sources. Still, the THz dielectric properties of common materials that are extensively characterized at microwave frequencies, are rarely reported in the literature. Recently, we characterized high-permittivity Rogers substrates by means of THz time-domain spectroscopy measurements in reflection mode. Here, we briefly discuss the versatility and accuracy of the employed technique for the characterization of various dielectric materials extensively used in fabrication processes. Experimental results are provided for a common dry resist (Ordyl) film showing remarkable agreement.

articleTitle: An Epsilon Negative Metamaterial Loaded Miniaturized Patch Antenna for 6G Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a miniaturized antenna operating at 165 GHz for 6G communication systems. The antenna, with dimensions of 0.35λ x 0.40λ, is implemented on a Rogers 5880 substrate. The miniaturization is facilitated through the incorporation of an Epsilon Negative Metamaterial (ENG) onto the ground plane of a patch antenna. The achieved performance metrics include a realized gain of 2.71 dB and a directivity of 5 dB. Comparative analysis reveals a substantial 42 % size reduction compared to a conventional patch antenna, showcasing the potential of the proposed design for efficient and compact 6G communication applications.

articleTitle: Investigation of Adaptive Cross Approximation Strategies for the Magnetic Field Integral Equation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: We investigate a recently introduced adaptive cross approximation (ACA) strategy tailored to the magnetic field integral equation (MFIE) in order to handle possible block-structured interaction matrices. The new ACA strategy relies on a hardened convergence criterion and an adaptive pivoting strategy comprising the standard maximum element search, a geometrical approach based on a modified minimization of the fill-distance and a strategy based on the true error of a random set of matrix entries. Our numerical results show that the new strategy remains robust for electrically larger problems and in the presence of near-zero blocks.

articleTitle: Inkjet Printed UHF RFID Humidity Sensor for Metallic Surface Assets
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a low-cost, label-type, ultrahigh frequency (UHF) radio-frequency identification (RFID) antenna for tagging metals and humidity sensing on metallic surfaces. The antenna consists of a feeding loop integrated with two orthogonal slots. This feed configuration provides an impedance match both on metal and air by creating a resonant current distribution due to the transverse slots technique. As a result, the tag exhibits a good omnidirectional radiation pattern in both air and above a metal plate. Additionally, this tag antenna was fabricated on a 0.74 mm thick paper substrate, which enables it to function as a humidity sensor. This design feature contributes to a read range of 2.5 m above a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{200}\times \mathbf{200}$</tex> mm metal plate in a dry state. Notably, the read range reduces to 1 m in a wet state. Therefore, this tag presents a low-cost solution for both tagging and humidity sensing on metallic surfaces, offering increased versatility and functionality for asset management in various industrial and infrastructure applications.

articleTitle: Sidelobe Accuracy from Planar Near Fields
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A main goal in antenna pattern measurement is to estimate the peak gain of a directive antenna, but less work has been reported for off-peak pattern accuracy. An X-band SGH pattern is estimated by multiple simulation approaches as a forward-direction benchmark, and measurements using a planar near field (NF) system, are all compared to get a feel for the accuracy of the far field (FF) sidelobe region.

articleTitle: Reconstruction of Layered Rough Surfaces Using a Two-Step RTM Scheme
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: An imaging scheme, which uses the frequency- domain reverse time migration (RTM) method to reconstruct two rough surfaces between three dielectric media from the scattered field measurements, is developed. The proposed method requires two steps for the reconstructions. At the first step, the RTM function that is computed using the scattered field measurements reveals only the upper rough surface. At the second step, it is first assumed that there is only one surface, the upper one. The forward scattering problem is solved for this scenario. Then, to reconstruct the lower surface, the difference between the scattered fields obtained from this forward scattering problem and the scattered field measurements is used to compute the RTM function of the second step. This second RTM function reveals the lower surface. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed two-step scheme is effective and promising.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Antenna Using AI for Wireless Power Transfer (WPT)
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this study, a novel reconfigurable antenna design is explored and optimized for wireless power transfer in environments with changing ambient frequencies. A pixel-based diode grid is introduced to allow for dynamic frequency adjustment to significantly enhance energy capture. This design is useful for quick adaptation to various frequency bands. While an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) plays a role in guiding the design process, the emphasis is on the antenna's ability to reconfigure itself efficiently, with minimal diode changes, leading to a versatile and compact design. The antenna demonstrates improved frequency coverage, and hence, a crucial step forward in wireless power transfer (WPT).

articleTitle: Broad-beam U-shaped Dielectric Resonator Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A broad-beam U-shaped dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) is investigated for designs of wide-angle scanning phased array antennas. The U-shaped DRA, fed by an underneath slot, is placed in the middle of a ground plane. The fundamental mode of the DRA is merged with the slot mode, broadening the impedance bandwidth. The design was simulated, fabricated, and measured, and the measured results agree reasonably well with the simulated ones. A measured overlapping bandwidth of 10.2% (3.45-3.82 GHz) is obtained, with both the E- and H-plane 3-dB beamwidths being greater than 120° and| S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>| being less than −10 dB.

articleTitle: Dielectric Permittivity Estimation of Liquid Phantoms Using a Coaxial Fixture Based on Hybrid PSO-NLR Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The estimation of the complex dielectric permittivity of liquid solutions employed in the fabrication of liquid phantoms is pivotal to obtain an accurate dielectric profile and avoid wastes during electromagnetic experiments involving the interaction between EM fields and human body. In this paper, the authors propose a cost-effective and accurate complex dielectric measurement system based on a coaxial fixture and a hybrid Particle Swarm Optimization - Non Linear Regression algorithm. The proposed system is an excellent alternative to existing commercial devices.

articleTitle: A Multi-Functional Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface with Integrated Sensing Capability
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: We present a Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface (RIS) topology for sensing and communication. The square unit cell of size <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda/2$</tex> consists of a 3×3 array of electrically small patches interconnected by switches operating at 10 GHz. Achieved wide phase response of this unit cell, enables precise control over the phase distribution of the surface. This characteristic enhances the surface's adaptability and improves its beam steering and beamforming capacities. Additionally, the design includes a sensing array to accurately calculate the direction of arrival of the incoming signals. However, for practical and cost-effective implementation, the number of switches can be minimized to a reduced 1-bit switch version. We demonstrate that an RIS designed with this unit cell can achieve multi-beam generation, diffuse scattering, and beam steering.

articleTitle: Wall Clutter Mitigation Techniques Comparaison for 3D Through-the-Wall Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Through-the-wall tomography stands as a notewor-thy method in imaging targets with precision close to reality. Nevertheless, the wall acts as a spatial filter exerting an influence on the quality of the targets scattered field and affects the quality of the reconstructed image. Various filtering techniques have been devised to differentiate the response of the target from that of the wall. However, they concurrently impact the capacity to image the target and discriminate between multiple targets.

articleTitle: An Investigation of Phase Quantization Effects on Transmitarray Performance for Different Apertures
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive investigation of phase quantization effects on the performance of transmitarray antennas (TAs) having square and circular aperture shapes. The two most commonly used TA aperture shapes are studied in two different sizes (20×20 and 50×50 elements), with equal numbers of lossless unit cell elements (UCEs) on the principal axes in each shape. The aperture phase distributions of TAs are examined using three different phase quantization levels and the continuous phase method. The obtained results are evaluated in terms of gain, side lobe level (SLL), spillover and illumination efficiency. The derived guidelines provide a pre-estimation for the impact of the number of quantization bits, aperture shape, and size chosen in the TA design on the radiation pattern, regardless of UCE losses.

articleTitle: A Pattern-Reconfigurable Antenna Based on DNA-Like SSPPs with Simple Switching Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a circularly polarized reconfigurable antenna based on a DNA-like SSPPs structure. The main radiator of the antenna is a DNA-like structure consisting of a double helix structure and metal strips. The SSPPs mode is excited by placing a pair of electric dipoles at the end of the main radiator. When the electric dipoles are excited in the same phase, the odd mode with an endfire circularly polarized beam is generated at 2.4 GHz. When the electric dipoles are excited out of phase, the even mode with a quasi-omnidirectional beam is generated at 2.4 GHz. The switching of the antenna pattern only requires adjusting the phase difference between two dipoles, which can be used in vehicle communication.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of 3–6 GHz 4-Channel Beam Steering Circuit with 6-Bit Digital Phase Shifters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: To improve azimuth resolution and radar systems, either a narrow beam in azimuth is used, or a MIMO system is used. Each method has advantages and limitations. This paper proposes the design and implementation of a 4-channel beam steering circuit with 6-bit digital phase shifters covering the frequency band 3–6 GHz. The proposed design has the advantage of parallel control through an FPGA for each phase shifter, which enables a high steering speed of up to 10 ns. Moreover, the proposed design is cascadable to achieve higher steering accuracy. The system has a phase accuracy of 5.625°. The proposed design is a 4-layer PCB that has passed through power, signal integrity, and RF simulations to verify its performance.

articleTitle: An Efficient Numerical Method for Determining Main Operating Frequency of Mandelbrot Fractal Patch Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a numerical method to determine the main operating frequency of a Mandelbrot fractal patch antenna. The method involves a conformal transformation, mapping the antenna's complex boundaries in physical space to a simpler computational space represented by a cylinder. This transformation maintains constant electromagnetic boundary conditions, and the finite difference method ensures a transparency of the circular contour in the truncated finite element mesh. This method offers a significant saving on computational resource as validated through analytical, numerical, and experimental tests.

articleTitle: Multiphysics Topological Optimization of a 3D-Printable THz Polymer Leaky Wave Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Topological optimization has drawn significant interest in the design of antennas because of its ability to design novel nonintuitive designs. However, the optimization algorithm often struggles to produce designs feasible for fabrication. Methods incorporating minimum feature size constraints, connectivity constraints and material filters have been employed in an attempt to make the designs more fabricable. However, these methods do not necessarily guarantee the structural integrity of the design. Here we show the combination of structural and electromagnetic optimizations with adaptive biasing can be utilized to produce structurally feasible and fabricable structures. The two optimization regimes utilize rotational symmetry to optimize a two dimensional domain whose performance was evaluated using axi-symmetric FDTD simulations. As a proof of concept a low cost, lightweight, polymer leaky wave antenna was designed, achieving 30 dBi gain at an operating frequency of 284 GHz. The result was a fully connected antenna with no structural weak points.

articleTitle: Development and Testing of High-Temperature Resistant Conformal Microstrip Yagi Antenna for C-Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In response to the challenges posed by high temperatures during supersonic cruising of air vehicles, this study developed a C-band conformal microstrip Yagi antenna with enhanced thermal stability. The antenna utilizes a ceramic-aerogel composite structure for both the radome and the feed dielectric substrate, addressing the deterioration of antenna performance under elevated temperatures. Materials selection, including quartz ceramic, silica aerogels, and TC4 titanium alloy, was optimized for heat resistance, electrical characteristics, and workability. A heat resistance test was conducted, revealing a slight deterioration in resonant frequency and maximum gain post-test. The average gain exhibited only a 5.2 % reduction after the heat resistance test, affirming the antenna's robust performance in high-temperature environments. The findings contribute to the understanding of antenna behavior under extreme conditions and underscore the antenna's efficacy in maintaining radiation performance despite thermal challenges.

articleTitle: High Efficiency OAM Generator Based on Single- Substrate Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a high-efficiency single-substrate meta-atom is proposed for a transmissive OAM generator. Via in-plane rotation, full <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2\pi$</tex> phase coverage together with a high transmission amplitude of 0.9 could be achieved by the proposed meta-atom. A high-performance focused OAM generator with topological charge of 1 is designed and simulated. There is a good coincidence between the simulated results and theoretical predictions, indicating the proposed OAM generator highly applicable for wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: Optimization of IRS Sensing Based on Multi-source Coherent DOA Estimation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This study introduces a novel deep reinforcement learning technique tailored for intelligent reflecting surface (IRS) sensor arrays, aimed at enhancing the identification of direction of arrival (DOA). Utilizing a combination of spatial attributes and correlation properties of the IRS array output, our approach efficiently distinguishes and pinpoints coherent DOAs originating from multiple sources. This enables IRSs to autonomously modify the direction of the reflected beam. The simulations conducted confirm the success of our method in improving target detection capabilities and present a fresh perspective for processing signals in sensor arrays.

articleTitle: Wideband Eight-Element MIMO Antenna System for 5G FR1 Mobile Terminals
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a broadband antenna system for multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) applications in 5G FR1 mobile terminals. The MIMO design consists of eight L-shaped coupled slot antenna elements based on stepped impedance resonators (SIRs) that can generate resonances to achieve wide operating bandwidth. The simulated results of the MIMO system show a -6 dB wide impedance bandwidth of 47% ranging from 3.25 to 5.2 GHz and inter-element isolation level of greater than 12 dB have been obtained for each antenna element with an envelope correlation coefficient (ECC) below 0.05 providing a reliable anti-interference for the MIMO antenna system. In addition, the simulated total efficiencies are higher than 50% across the 5G NR bands; n77 (3.3-4.2 GHz), n78 (3.3-3.8 GHz), and n79 (4.4-5 GHz).

articleTitle: Compressed T-Matrix for Arbitrarily Shaped Objects
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel numerical method for computing the T-matrix of arbitrarily shaped scatterers. Initially, a reference surface is chosen to enclose the object. The rotational tangential component of the scattered field on the reference surface is directly computed from the rotational tangential component of the incident field using the generalized transition matrix (GTM). Then the incident spherical harmonic modes are projected onto the reference surface. The corresponding scattered fields on the reference surface are calculated with GTM and their far fields are expressed in terms of the outgoing spherical harmonic modes. The orthogonality of the spherical vector basis functions is employed to derive the two transformation matrices. The T-matrix for the scatterer is obtained by multiplying them with the GTM. A compressed T-matrix (CT-Matrix) is introduced to collect the response of the significant modes, the size of which is much smaller than that of the T-matrix. Numerical examples are provided to validate the accuracy of the proposed method.

articleTitle: The Radar Cross Section of a Flat PEC Dog - A Tale of Incremental Diffraction Coefficients
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper briefly overviews the theory of Incremental Diffraction Coefficients including the seminal contributions of Arthur D. Yaghjian - and gives a personal note.

articleTitle: A Dual Bandstop FSS with Low Profile and High Polarization Stability for EMC
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A novel miniaturized and low-profile FSS is presented for electromagnetic shielding, which consists of a layer of metal patch and a layer of dielectric substrate, resulting in a small unit and low profile with a thickness of only <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.0054\lambda$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda$</tex> corresponds to the resonant frequency of the first operating band. Additionally, the folded structure not only reduces the unit size but also creates two stop bands, corresponding to around 7.7GHz and 16.7GHz. There is a low-insertion passband between the stopbands, which has a bandwdith of 2G Hz wide. The created FSS allows for signal transmission within the passband while it suppresses unrelated signals incident from both sides.

articleTitle: A Universal Flexible Back-End Circuit for Wearable Sensing Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a flexible back-end circuit that is designed to interrogate radio frequency (RF) wearable sensors and extract the magnitudes of their reflection and transmission coefficients. The seamless integration of this circuit with wearable sensors is due to its integration on a flexible Polyethylene Terephthalate (PET) substrate. The proposed circuit operates from 500 MHz to 4 GHz, and it is composed of three different blocks: an excitation block, a harmonic suppression block, and a detection block. The first part is connected to the input of the wearable sensor and measures the magnitude of the reflection coefficient (S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>), whereas the second part is connected to the output of the sensor and measures the magnitude of the transmission coefficient (S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf>). Finally, the back-end circuit is fabricated and tested while connected to a wearable sensor where its ability to translate the magnitudes of the reflection and transmission coefficients of the wearable sensor to dc voltages is demonstrated. The designed circuit was fabricated and tested where measurement results agree significantly with simulation data.

articleTitle: Dual-Band, Dual-Polarized Continuous Transverse Stub Antenna for SatCom Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A dual-band, dual-polarized, and low-profile Continuous Transverse Stub (CTS) antenna array is presented at K/Ka-band for for satellite communications (SatCom). The antenna is designed to cover the down-link (17.7-20.2 GHz) and the up-link (27.5-30 GHz) bands of the SatCom link. The CTS aperture comprises 8 long slots fed in parallel by a corrugated parallel plate waveguide beam forming network which supports the propagation of two orthogonal modes. The antenna radiates a dual-linear polarization by using these two orthogonal modes. Full-wave results for the proposed antenna concept are validated by a prototype and measurements results for the radiation patterns and input reflection coefficient.

articleTitle: Initial Study of a Sub-THz Reconfigurable Reflector Using Actuated Liquid Metal Droplet
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A 2-bit reconfigurable reflector for potential microfluidic-based implementation of reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) in sub- THz band is proposed. This innovative method capitalizes on the actuation of liquid metal droplets to implement a digitally-coded reconfigurable reflector which operates at 140 GHz. Reflections are designed towards <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$6.4^{\circ}$</tex> and 9.2° using column-controlled unit cells which are reconfigured by actuating liquid metal (EGaIn) droplets filled in cavities of a commercial PCB substrate. Results validated by full-wave simulations indicate that a small height displacement of a flexible surface under each unit cell by between <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$20-35\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> enables the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$90^{\circ}$</tex> phase changes between the four states of the unit cells.

articleTitle: Design of a Field-of-View Enhancing Lens for mmWave 5G Radios Using Gradient Index Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In collaborative effort with Fortify Inc, Rogers Corporation successfully demonstrated application of the GRIN lens design approach to extend beam scanning capabilities of an electronically steered phased array antenna in mmWave 5G radio. This paper shares intermediate results of our demonstration study using commercial off-the-shelf mmWave 5G innovator kit and applying dedicated GRIN lens structure.

articleTitle: Study of Best Antenna Configuration for Axillary Microwave Imaging Prototype
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Imaging the axillary region for detection of axillary lymph nodes metastasised by breast cancer is currently under development using microwave signals. A limited angular view justifies the study of the best antenna configuration for this application. In this paper, we perform a preliminary study to find the best antenna configurations for axillary microwave imaging. The results show the quality of target detection is affected by the choice of antenna configurations, and also that it depends on the position of the target. One of the potential candidates for antenna configuration shows promising results.

articleTitle: Ultra-wideband Antenna Array With Integrated Power Combiner
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: To resolve the element size constraint in a UWB array, a compact ultra-wideband power combiner was proposed in this paper. An array covering 18:1 bandwidth, with the integrated power combiner and 16×16 Balanced Antipodal Vivaldi elements, achieved VSWR about 3 and gain from 5dBi to 24dBi.

articleTitle: On Deep Learning Based Beam Selection in the Presence of Array Imperfections
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Beam selection with predesigned codebook reduces computation complexity and provides efficient solutions for beam alignment between the transmitter and receiver. However, this process is prone to various imperfections in the antenna array which can often occur when deployed in outdoor systems. In this paper we investigate the performance of a deep learning model with respect to selecting the top K beams from a codebook in the presence of array imperfections. Errors such as offset in the amplitude, phase, position, and a random chance of failure in the elements are considered while modelling both the transmitter and receiver. A neural network which is trained on ideal conditions is then tested on such an array with perturbations. We also investigate the network's ability to generalize to different paths taken by the mobile receiver.

articleTitle: A Robust Signal Transformation Classification Method to Improve the Range Resolution of Array FMCW Radar with Element Offset
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this work, a robust signal transformation classification method is proposed to enhance the range resolution of the array frequency modulated continuous wave radar with element offset. Initially, the element offset-induced noise is analyzed to be biased, and the natural noise is unbiased, both of which follow stochastic distribution, and are further assumed to be orthogonal with signal. Subsequently, a projection matrix for finding the target echoes is determined by optimizing a designed objective. An alternate direction multiplier method is adopted for optimization to guarantee the robustness of the proposed method. Finally, the fast Fourier transform is adopted for further angle localization. Given a simulated two-target echo with array position errors, the resolution of the detected target range is enhanced to be 0.01 m, and the signal-to-noise ratio of the processed echo is enhanced by 3.38 dB, showcasing the promising performance of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Accurate Angle-of-Arrival Sensing for Receiving and Scattering Array Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Incorporating sensing capabilities into reconfigurable intelligent surfaces coupled with signal rerouting functionalities provides a promising route to integrating sensing and communication functionalities. In this paper, we propose and numerically demonstrate the feasibility of accurate angle-of-arrival detection in reconfigurable reflectarrays. A theoretical model has been formulated to articulate the sensing ability, drawing upon principles rooted in the receiving antenna theory.

articleTitle: Exploiting Analytic Transfer Matrices to Engineer Resonances in Patterned Dielectric Periodic Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Designing periodic structures with prescribed resonant frequencies is a difficult task if a theoretical model is unavailable. In this paper, it is shown that analytic transfer matrices can be used to engineer resonance properties of an all-dielectric periodic 2D structure that exhibits a sharp transition in reflection-transmission properties at resonance frequencies in the range 1500–1800 GHz, dependent on the angle of incidence of electromagnetic waves between 5 and 85 degrees. The operation of the structure is assessed by full-wave simulation. The proposed all-dielectric periodic surface has potential application to sensors.

articleTitle: Outage-Analysis-Based Receiver Digital Beamforming for Deep-Fading Suppression in Millimetre-Wave Railway Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a receiver digital beamforming method based on outage analysis is proposed to suppress the deep-fading of the receiving power in millimetre-wave railway communications. Initially, with the hypothesis of the two-ray model comprising of the direct and rail-reflected waves, the uniformly linear array-received signal subjected to the Rice channel and its power are modeled. Subsequently, the receiver beamforming is optimized based on the outage probability analysis out of the characteristic of the Rice channel. In contrast to the conventional diversity methods, including minimal ratio combination and least mean square, the proposed method achieves a maximum suppression of the deep-fading of 50 dB down to a maximum of 3 dB in a equal amplitude and in-phase array, showcasing the promising effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Miniaturized Stacked Choke Rings for GNSS High-Accuracy Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel design for a miniatur-ized choke ring structure, optimized for operation in the L5/E5a and L1/E1 frequency bands (1.176 and 1.575 GHz). The choke rings are vertically stacked and can hence be placed in the vicinity of a GNSS antenna, to enable to achieve high gain, minimize back lobe radiation, and effectively reduce multipath interference in challenging environments. The developed structure has been manufactured and measured with a multiband GNSS antenna: its performance is then evaluated and compared to a canonical (horizontally stacked) choke ring structure.

articleTitle: Space-Time Metasurfaces: Unleashing the Potential of Four-Dimensional Wave Engineering
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This study investigates a transformative approach by infusing temporal variation into static metasurfaces, creating dynamic systems capable of four-dimensional manipulation of both spatial and temporal characteristics of electromagnetic waves. We explore recent advancements in the analysis and functionalities of Space-Time (ST) interfaces, metasurfaces, and slabs designed to disrupt reciprocity, generate new frequencies, and amplify signal power. Examining various operational aspects of ST metasurfaces, we explore scattering and diffraction at ST interfaces, ST sinusoidally varying surfaces and slabs, as well as transmissive and reflective ST metasurfaces. The paper high-lights potential applications, offering insights into the promising capabilities of dynamic space-time metamaterials for the future of electromagnetic wave engineering.

articleTitle: An Analytical Formulation for the Mean RCS of an Object Above a Rough Surface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: An analytical expression for the mean RCS of an object above a rough surface is presented. Scattering from the object is characterized in terms of a polarimetric bistatic scattering amplitude, and surface scattering is described using the first order small slope approximation. A four-path model approximation is introduced to express the combined scattered field in terms of a summation of four terms. The approach is applied to produce formulations for the mean RCS expressed in terms of integrations over the target scattering amplitude. Results are computed for an example problem and compared to those obtained from Monte Carlo simulations.

articleTitle: Loaded Waveguide Antenna for Undersea Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A loaded waveguide antenna has been designed, manufactured, and tested to explore potential applications in ocean observation projects. This antenna can operate under high pressure and attenuation in the deep sea with simple techniques to adjust the operating frequency.

articleTitle: A Nonlinear Passive Tag for Location Detection Using Harmonic Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a simulation, optimization, and improved fabrication work for a novel harmonic tag design proposed recently. The proposed design of nonlinear harmonic tags for wireless sensing uses harmonic radar systems that feature multi-element antenna configurations and Schottky diodes, and the tag achieved a 2.04 m in measured distance. The tag design was simulated and refined using Ansys high-frequency structure simulator (HFSS) to validate, observe, and improve its radiation pattern and theoretical gain across its designed harmonic frequencies at 8 and 16 GHz. A new material dispensing printing method replaced the laser-assisted mask-cutting fabrication method. In the same experimental conditions, the tag design tuned with HFSS and fabricated using material dispensing exhibited a 9.4% increase in detectable distance over the laser-cut tag, improving the range from 2.04 meters to 2.2 meters. The gain of the simulated tag was closely aligned with the gain of the experimental tag, as determined from the analyzed measured data. As validated through continuous simulation and optimization processes, the versatility and compact design of these newly developed harmonic tags render them highly suitable for diverse location-based applications.

articleTitle: New Enhancement of Self-Interference Cancellation for Circularly Polarized Patch Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Designing a patch array antenna with circular polarization and high self-interference cancellation (SIC) remains a challenge for in-band full-duplex wireless communication systems. Therefore, this paper explores counteracting modes to enhance self-interference cancellation in circularly polarized patch array antennas. The structure consists of two receiving (Rx) antennas and one transmitting (Tx) antenna, with the distance between the elements of the array less than <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda_{0}/10$</tex>. Using this technique, our simulation results show the SIC can reach a maximum of 60 dB at approximately 4.7 GHz and 50 dB over a bandwidth of 100 MHz. As a result, this technique should be a good candidate for in-band full-duplex communication systems.

articleTitle: Digital Full-Duplex Dual-Polarised Array for Beam Steering and Retro-Directive Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A new dual-polarised antenna array is proposed and developed for beam steering, full-duplex communications, radar, and retro-directive self-steering. The wideband antenna system with isolation values of 50 dB, is comprised of co-located transmit and receive elements and operates from about 2.2 to 2.5 GHz. In addition, each element is fed using a digital software defined radio network where complex weights and channel phase conjugation are applied at baseband. The system demonstrator shows proof-of-concept by measurements of a sum and difference pattern as well as a monostatic test showing self-steering due to an interrogating signal from the far-field. To the best knowledge of the authors, no similar full-duplex array has been designed and tested with a programmable and digital beam-forming system.

articleTitle: UWB Antenna Element on Conformal Substrate for S-Ku Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: We present an ultra-wideband (UWB) antenna el-ement printed on a Rogers/Duroid flexible substrate for S- K, band sensing applications. The element is based on a planar rectangular combination monopole antenna (PRCMA), which obtains UWB operation over a frequency range of 2-18 GHz without significantly compromising the gain compared to a standard monopole design. The PRCMA is based on a simple planar rectangular monopole antenna (PRMA) and obtains wideband operation with a parabolically curved feed structure. The elements were designed at a frequency of 9 GHz, yielding a fractional bandwidth of 160 %. The antenna was analyzed as a function of the radius of curvature of the substrate to evaluate the performance when integrated onto various curved surfaces. The antenna was measured at a maximum curvature radius of 25 cm and minimum of 3.5 cm, The antenna was simulated and measured, yielding a maximum gain of 2.53 dBi across the lower band of 2-6 GHz and 6.24 dBi across the upper band of 6-18 GHz.

articleTitle: Wideband High Gain Shortened Conical Horn Antenna with Fully Metallic Phase Graded Metasurface lens for Millimeter-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper introduces a cost-effective and mechanically robust fully metallic phase graded metasurface (FMPGM) lens, designed to enhance gain and directivity_of shortened horn antennas for millimeter-wave applications. The metalens corrects phase errors on the horn aperture using a near-field phase-transformation approach, employing Swastika slots on a thin conductive sheet. The 2D array of unit cells improves aperture efficiency and enhances gain across a wide frequency band. Demonstrated on shortened horns at 28 GHz, the metalens achieves a 10.5 dB gain enhancement (from 10.4 to 20.9dBi) with a 14.21% 3-dB realized gain bandwidth from 26.4GHz to 30.5GHz.

articleTitle: Gaussian Curve Matching Circuit for Rotman Lens with Patch Array for Millimeter Wireless Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A Rotman lens connected with eight series fed patch arrays is designed at 28 GHz. The input port 5 is not matched properly. A matching circuit based on Gaussian curve is designed and connected to input port 5. The measured return losses at the input ports are below 10 dB at 28 GHz.

articleTitle: Folded Parallel Plate Waveguide Launcher For Surface Wave Antennas Transformable to Different Widths and Heights
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This document details the configuration of a folded Quasi TEM wave launcher, engineered to seamlessly adapt to varying widths and heights. The folded feed seamlessly incorporates any metasurface antenna which needs a quasi-TEM wave launcher underneath, effectively reducing the overall size of the design. To mitigate the impact of the folded structure, the height of the waveguide has been minimized. As a design example a quadrifurcated power divider was integrated with the folded transition of height 10mm and 17mm at 12 GHz and fabricated. A good agreement between the measured and fabricated results was observed.

articleTitle: Modified CSRR Sensor for Magnetodielectric Material Characterization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Complementary Split Ring Resonator (CSRR) based characterization techniques provide a simple and cost effective method for material properties in the microwave regime. Although the structure and its variations are studied extensively in the literature, characterization of magnetodielectric materials still have challenges. Here a modified CSRR sensor is presented for magnetodielectric material characterization. Positioning error and sensitivity of the structure is analyzed.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of RF Lens Designs Suitable for Additive Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper compares the designs of two dielectric lenses: a Zone Plate Lens (ZPL) and a GRadient INdex (GRIN) lens. Each is presented considering its overall design, potential fabrication benefits, and RF performance when considering the same occupying volume.

articleTitle: Linear One-dimensional Inverse Profiling: the Role of a Reflecting Plane in the Background
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a one dimensional inverse profiling problem under a linearised framework is addressed. The aim is to establish the role played by a reflecting plane located in the scattering scenario on the profile reconstructions by studying its impact on the singular values of the scattering operator. It is shown that in presence of reflecting plane, the singular values exhibit a step-like behavior and the Number of Degree of Freedom (NDF) is twice as large as the NDF in homogeneous medium. This entails an enlargement of the class of dielectric profiles that can be reliably reconstructed.

articleTitle: Characteristic Modes for Orthogonal Beamsteering Using ESPAR
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A method based on the Theory of Characteristic Modes (TCM) for finding orthogonal beamsteering radiation patterns of electronically steerable parasitic array radiator (ESPAR) is proposed. This method can be used to design single-radio-frequency (RF) multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems for Internet-of-Things (IoT) applications in next-generation wireless communication. It can directly generate a set of symmetrical and orthogonal pattern basis for beamsteering purpose and demodulated reference signal transmission. In addition, the input impedances of ESPAR are the same for all pattern basis so that impedance matching can be achieved by a fixed matching network. Simulation example of a 5-element circular dipole ESPAR is provided to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Low-Profile Broadband Vertically Polarized Antenna with Archimedes Spiral Slits
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a low-profile antenna with broadband vertically polarized omnidirectional radiation is presented. The bandwidth is broadened by adding Archimedes spiral slits on the outer side of a circular patch located in the center of the antenna. The simulation results show that the antenna fractional bandwidth, related to the values of the reflection coefficient lower than −10 dB, is increased from 7% to 20% when the Archimedes spiral slits are used. The designed antenna has a vertical polarization and omnidirectional radiation and an overall thickness of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.038 \lambda$</tex>, considering the wavelength at the central operating frequency of 5.7 GHz.

articleTitle: Analysis of Excitation Techniques for Electrically Small Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This work provides a comparison between excitation techniques that allow matching the electrically small antenna input impedance to the reference impedance. The paper presents the design of a near-field-excited, electrically small antenna with a magnetic-dipole exciter. The simulation performance of the electrically small antenna shows agreement with other similar design variations with different excitation mechanisms.

articleTitle: A Fast Reconstruction Algorithm for FMCW Circular Synthetic Aperture Radar Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a reconstruction algorithm for circular synthetic aperture radars (CSAR) using frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW) signals. A signal model for the FMCW-CSAR system is developed and formulated as a Green's function integral. Based on the signal model and the Green's function, a 3-step fast reconstruction algorithm is proposed. The first step is a matrix inversion based on the Truncated Singular Value Decomposition (T-SVD), the second step is a matched filter and the last step is a Non-Uniform Fast Fourier Transform (NUFFT). The overall reconstruction is on the order of Nlog(N). Synthetic data is used to verify the proposed reconstruction algorithm, showing significant speed improvements compared to conventional image reconstruction algorithms.

articleTitle: Numerical Tool for the Analysis and Synthesis of Transmitarrays in Fresnel Region
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A numerical model, developed to shape the field in the Fresnel region using transmitarray antennas (TA), is proposed here. This tool allows the prediction of the amplitude of the electric field, taking into account all the characteristics of the elementary building blocks of the system: the injected power, the gain of the focal source, the distance between the focal source and each unit-cell, the directivity of the unit-cell and their transmission coefficients in phase and amplitude. This model is then validated through full-wave electromagnetic simulations at 300 GHz in the case of an array focusing at broadside.

articleTitle: Terahertz Photoemitter Using Plasmonic Inter-combined Tooth Based on MoS2-GaAs Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Due to its excellent dielectric response, molybdenum disulfide (MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) has received more and more attention in the field of optoelectronic materials. In this paper, a terahertz (THz) photoconductive antenna (PCA) based on MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> is proposed, and an inter-combined contact tooth design at the antenna gap is nominated. Studies have shown that MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> enhances carrier absorption on the semi-insulating gallium arsenide (SI-GaAs) surface, boosting the performance in the frequency range of 0.1-2 THz. The directivity and realized gain of the proposed PCA in overall bandwidth are up to 21.3 dBi and 17 dBi. This paper demonstrates the potential of MoS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> in the field of optoelectronics and provides a new direction for the enhancement of PCA.

articleTitle: A Cross-Shaped Tri-Mode Resonance Patch Antenna Design at Ka-Band
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A cross-shaped wideband multi-mode microstrip patch antenna with aperture-coupled feeding is proposed in this paper. Through the incorporation of metalized via holes and surface slots on the cross-shaped patch. The TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf>, TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">30</inf>, and TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf> modes is excited simultaneously the frequencies of these three modes are brought close each other to broaden operating band. The antenna achieves a wide impedance bandwidth of about 29.4% in fraction or 25.8-34.7 GHz under <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\vert \mathrm{S}_{11}\vert$</tex> < 10dB, and its corresponding in-band gain is from 5.2 to 10.1 dBi.

articleTitle: Modeling Magnetotelluric Surveys Based on Stochastic Path Integral
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: We study a probabilistic modeling of magnetotelluric (MT) surveys based on stochastic path integral. Based on the Feynman-Kac formula, the probabilistic solution of Helmholtz equation is formulated by the expectation of path integrals of a series of random walk paths. The studied method based on stochastic path integral transforms the computational bottleneck from solving matrix equations to large-scale matrix multiplication, which is more suitable for massively parallel computing platforms. Numerical experiments show that as the number of paths increases, the numerical error of the studied method can effectively converge, and it also exhibits the considerable potential to efficiently accelerate the computation.

articleTitle: An Enhanced GSTC-DGTD Method for Fast Simulation of Anisotropic Dispersive Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Metasurfaces can control electromagnetic waves beyond the limits of natural materials. Recently, there are many fast algorithms for metasurfaces based on surface susceptibilities model (SSM) and generalized sheet transition conditions (GSTC). We optimize one of the existing methods of using GSTCs in discontinue Galerkin time-domain (DGTD) method, so that this method can now quickly simulate metasurfaces with both anisotropy and dispersion.

articleTitle: Inexpensive 3D Printable High Gain Dielectric Rod Antenna for mm- Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: ─A dielectric rod antenna (DRA) with improved performance and compatibility with inexpensive 3D printing processes is proposed for millimeter wave (mm-wave) applications. The antenna's bandwidth and gain performance are significantly enhanced compared to the previously presented DRAs through careful tapering in a rectangular manner.
