The antenna exhibits a simulated wider bandwidth of more than 20 GHz with a maximum gain of 20 at 30 GHz, which is comparable to or even more than some of the dielectric rods based array antennas. Radiation from the proposed DRA is directed towards the end-fire direction with minimal side lobes, regardless of its use of a low permittivity dielectric. A rectangular waveguide to DRA transition is also designed considering the antenna measurements. The prototype of the proposed DRA was made using a low-cost commercial 3D printer. The simulations and measured results were in good agreement.

articleTitle: Broadband Circularly Polarized SIW-Based H-Plane Horn Antenna for X/Ku Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a circularly polarized (CP) substrate-integrated waveguide (SIW)-based H-plane horn antenna with broader impedance bandwidth and higher peak realized gain (PRG) for armature satellite services (X-band, 8–12 GHz) and broadcast satellite (Ku-band, 12–18 GHz) applications is presented. A tapered microstrip transition is used in the feeding section to obtain the broadband characteristics. In addition, the feeding component of the antenna utilizes three quarter-wavetransformers to enhance impedance matching and widen the bandwidth. To generate the CP, two rows of rectangular slots are etched from both the top and bottom metal surfaces of the design. The antenna is designed, fabricated, and tested. The measured fractional impedance bandwidth of 41.6%, the 3-dB axial ratio bandwidth of 3.8 GHz, the maximum PRG of 6.95 dBic, the maximum radiation efficiency (simulated) of 87 %, and the cross-polarization level below -40 dB have been achieved at the center frequency of 13.2 GHz.

articleTitle: Optimization of the Antenna Mesh in an Indoor Distributed Massive MIMO System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Taking as reference channel data obtained by using a rigorous ray-tracing method for a concentrated multiple-input multiple-output system (C-mMIMO) in an indoor scenario, the objective of this work focuses on the optimization, among a mesh with potential locations, of the set antennas required in a distributed (D-mMIMO) system to meet the same channel requirements as those of the C-mMIMO one considered as reference. The optimization is carried out using a Dandelion optimizer, and the results presented at 26 GHz for the up-link show layouts with a reduction in the number of receiver antennas that depends on the number of users in the pico-cell.

articleTitle: Design of a Biomimetic UWB 3D Antenna for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this work, a new antenna, inspired by a case in the field of acoustics found in nature, is designed. The proposed antenna is based on the external ear of the horseshoe bat, and is designed by using a novel method which takes into account the shape and the characteristics of the surface, materials and loading of the ear. The designed bioinspired 3D, horn type antenna is characterized by ultra-wide band frequency range of operation, which make it a serious candidate for a wide range of RF applications with special interest in the 5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> Generation. Simulation results of the S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> parameter, the directivity and the radiation patterns are presented for the frequency range 3 GHz to 10 GHz.

articleTitle: Upper-Bound Performance of Laser-Induced Graphene (LIG) Antennas on PEEK for Implantable Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Laser-Induced Graphene (LIG) can potentially boost the development of smart prostheses by engraving an antenna on a polymeric precursor without any additional material and structural modification of the implant. A commonly used polymer material in implantable prostheses is the Poly-Ether-Ether-Ketone (PEEK) due to its biocompatibility, mechanical strength, and low weight. This paper experimentally characterizes the electrical features of LIG traces on PEEK with the purpose to identify the upper-bound radiation performance of a reference implanted loop of optimal size by numerical simulations based on measured values of sheet resistance of PEEK samples that have been laser-engraved with different settings. Results revealed that in the case of the lowest sheet resistance <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(R_{3}=5\Omega/\square)$</tex> the maximum gain is just 3 dB lower w.r.t. a reference copper antenna, thus making the concept of engraved prostheses feasible.

articleTitle: Analyses of Electromagnetic Scattering Characteristics of Harbor Scenes Based on Multipath Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a reliable method based on the multipath model is adopted to analyze the electromagnetic scattering characteristics of composite harbor scenes. According to geometrical optics and physical optics (GO-PO) and the facet-based asymptotical model (FBAM), the direct scattering field of the ship target and the sea surface is calculated. Meanwhile, the idea of GO-PO is used to deal with the coupling scattering between the target and the environment. Then, the spatial distributed scattering field of a complex harbor scene under different conditions is analyzed, which can provide a reference for the study of scene identification with synthetic aperture radar.

articleTitle: A Two-Port Implantable Antenna for Simultaneous Wireless Information and Power Transfer for IMDs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a compact two-port implantable antenna is proposed for simultaneous biotelemetry and power transfer. The proposed antenna consists of a loop element operating at 433 MHz (Port 1) for wireless power transfer and a dual-band patch element operating at 915 MHz and 2.45 GHz (Port 2) for biotelemetry. The proposed antenna has a compact size (18 × 18 × 1.27 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>) and is implanted at a depth of 40 mm in a muscle box. The proposed antenna exhibits a fractional bandwidth of 67.17 %, 5.76 %, 7.82 % at 433 MHz, 915 MHz, 2.45 GHz respectively. The proposed antenna demonstrates satisfactory performance in terms of isolation, gain patterns and specific absorption rate (SAR).

articleTitle: A Broadband and Wide-Angle Scanning Planar Phased Array Antenna for Sub-6 GHz Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This manuscript presents a two-dimensional (2-D) broadband and wide-angle scanning phased array antenna with a combined superstrate. The dipole array antenna incorporates arching metal columns that suppress mutual coupling, hence achieving wideband matching and broad beamwidth characteristics in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{E}-\mathbf{plane}$</tex>. A combined structure, consisting of metasurface slabs and a dielectric layer, is positioned above the antenna to augment the beamwidth and improve the impedance matching characteristic. The same effect can be achieved by optimizing the curvature of the exponential curves of the dipole edge to obtain a deformed dipole. To verify it, an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{8}\times \mathbf{8}$</tex> prototype is constructed and tested. The proposed design yields a 62.1% (2.5-4.75 GHz) bandwidth and a 2-D <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm \mathbf{60}^{\circ}$</tex> beam-scanning capability. Gain fluctuation is basically less than 3 dB. The measured results are mostly in line with expectations.

articleTitle: A Planar Microwave Ablation Antenna With Extremely Small Cross-Sectional Area
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This letter presents an inexpensive planar microwave ablation (MWA) antenna with extremely miniature size. The antenna is designed based on the substrate integrated coaxial line (SICL), and for the first time using the pi network matching method in the design of the planar ablation antenna. This probe far-end matching method greatly increase the degrees of freedom designing an antenna. The performance of local small-area ablation of the antenna is verified in simulation and experimental analysis, and because of its extremely small cross-sectional area, it can be used for the tumor ablation or nerve ablation in small animals.

articleTitle: An Interlaced Wideband Antenna Array with Reconfigurable Polarization for Over-the-Air Testing of On-the-Move Ku/Ka-Band Satellite Terminals
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a wideband interlaced antenna array with reconfigurable polarization for a new Comms on-the-move Electronically Steerable Array Testing facility (CESAT). A low-cost, wideband Vivaldi antenna with a simple dielectric lens is presented with operation coverage of Ku and Ka band satellite communication frequencies (10 - 31 GHz). This design is then placed in a circular sub-array to enable reconfigurable linear and circular polarization. This is then integrated into an interlaced antenna array that allows for simultaneous over-the-air transmission and pointing angle measurement in real time.

articleTitle: A Surface Integral Equation-Based Simulator for Resistance and Inductance Extraction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This study proposes a surface integral equation-based simulator for accurate and efficient extraction of the resistance/inductance (RL) parameters under the magneto-quasi-static assumption. The proposed simulator employs a novel centroid-midpoint (CM) basis function and a highly accurate equivalent surface impedance (ESI) model. The utilization of CM basis functions allows for the conversion of edge-based vector potential computations to panel-based scalar potential computation. Such conversion makes the implementation of fast multipole method straightforward and allows drastically reducing the matrix-fill time, matrix-vector multiplication time, and setup time for the preconditioner. Utilization of the ESI model makes the simulator highly accurate for RL extraction at low frequencies. The numerical results show that the proposed simulator requires <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$93\mathrm{x}$</tex> less CPU time and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$14\mathrm{x}$</tex> less memory than Ansys <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{Q}3\mathrm{D}$</tex> for the same level of accuracy while extracting the RL parameters of a 50-port ball grid array package.

articleTitle: Dual-Sense Polarization Reconfigurable Phased Array
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents the development and experiments of a microstrip phased array antenna with polarization reconfigurability. The designed array enables electronic reconfiguration of polarization between right-hand circular polarization (RHCP) and left-hand circular polarization (LHCP) in the main lobe's direction. Employing single-fed microstrip antennas, each loaded with four tunable varicap diodes, the phased array achieves a low axial ratio (AR) at the steering angles. A practical demonstration of the proposed methodology involves the construction of a six-element linear phased array operating at 2.2 GHz. The measurements carried out in an anechoic chamber reveal an AR better than 1 dB for both RHCP and LHCP states across a broad range of steering angles, thereby validating the effectiveness of the proposed array.

articleTitle: Sub-6 GHz Channel Measurement and Analysis for Urban Macrocell
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: With the increasing level of urban intelligence, urban signal coverage has a significant impact on people's lives. To support system design and deployment, precise prediction and modeling of urban propagation are of paramount importance. In this study, we conducted experiments in densely populated urban areas and analyzed the collected data from the road network. The experimental findings provide valuable insights and guidance for the coverage of Sub-6 GHz macro base stations in urban environments. Furthermore, these results serve as a reference for macrocell deployments in other urban areas.

articleTitle: A Versatile Approach for the Optimization of Printed Series Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents the results of a multi-purpose design procedure for designing printed antennas. The proposed approach is based on the multi-objective invasive weed optimization, driven with a semi-open constraint function in MATLAB. As a case study, the proposed approach is applied to a series array of printed patches. This class of antennas are particularly lightweight and easy to manufacture, hence suitable for low-cost and compact architectures.

articleTitle: An Antenna Array with High Detection Capability for Electromagnetic Stroke Diagnostic Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents an antenna array with high detection capability for portable electromagnetic (EM) stroke diagnostic systems. To enhance the detection capability of the antenna array, a planar antenna element is designed, exhibiting improved performance in both impedance bandwidth and near-field radiation inside the head tissues. An effective array layout is selected according to the investigation results of the impact of array layouts on the detection capability of the antenna array. The detection performance of the proposed array is evaluated in a lab-setting EM stroke diagnostic system. The reconstructed 2-D images inside the head demonstrate successful detection of different stroke-affected areas, even as small as 3 mm in radius, significantly smaller than those of reported relevant works under the same validation setting, confirming the high detection capability of the proposed antenna array.

articleTitle: Design a Single-Polarized Patch Antenna Featuring a Diplexer with Out-of-Band Rejection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a diplexer filtering antenna designed for band 7 of the 3GPP 4G standard. Uplink and downlink bands are isolated without a circulator and in the same polarization. Based on an antenna with the elimination of unwanted harmonic radiation, two microstrip filters are implemented. The filters are used to separate the uplink and downlink bands and provide isolation between the ports. Simulated results demonstrate robust separation between each band, with fractional bandwidths of 2.7% and 2.6% for the uplink and downlink bands, respectively. The achieved gain is approximately 6 dBi for both bands. Notably, the isolation surpasses 30 dB near the bands and remains at 15 dB until the fourth harmonic.

articleTitle: Numerical Modeling of Photodetectors Made from Two-Dimensional Materials
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A concise numerical model, based on drift-diffusion equations and wave propagation in a multilayered medium, has been developed to investigate photodetectors composed of two-dimensional materials. Comparisons between the numerical results and experiments validate the precision of the proposed approach in calculating the quantum efficiency as a function of incident wavelength. The formulation also enables the calculation of advanced photodetector parameters such as phase noise and bandwidth.

articleTitle: Rapid Radiation Pattern Estimating Method for Deformed Conformal Microstrip Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Microstrip antennas have gain wide applications for their structural and functional advantages. However, due to the influence of environment loads, the antenna structure can be deformed, and the EM performance will consequently be degraded. If the deformation is too large, the antenna radiation pattern will be seriously distorted. Thus, beam compensation should be carried out in some necessary cases. However, before the compensation is implemented, the degraded far-field pattern should be accurately and rapidly obtained to ensure the compensation precision and efficiency. Therefore, it has an urgent demand to evaluate the antenna performance under external loads. The present study proposes a rapid radiation pattern estimating method for deformed microstrip antennas. By mechanical analysis, the antenna deformation with varied magnitudes and patterns is generated and the corresponding far-field patterns are computed by full wave analysis method. With these data, an experiential formula to estimate the far-field radiation pattern is creatively proposed according to dimensional approach, in which the unknown parameters are solved by the least square method. After applied to an microstrip antenna, the effeteness and efficiency of the proposed method are demonstrated.

articleTitle: An Efficient Approach for a Digital Twin model of Harsh EM Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: An accurate characterization of electromagnetically complex environments is crucial to fully unlock potentialities of the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT). In this context, a preliminary study for the development of an electromagnetic (EM) Digital Twin (DT) aiming to retrieve the power density distribution in reference environments, with the support of an Artificial Neural Network (ANN), is proposed. An approach to properly parametrize the scenario and optimally select training data is presented and applied in a case-study when testing indicative samples.

articleTitle: Dual-Band and Dual-Polarized Antenna System Design for Ka-Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This study presents a dual-band dual-circular polarization feed chain for Ka-band applications such as satellite communication systems. The proposed feed chain consists of a Tx-Rx corrugated antenna, iris polarizer, rectangular-to-square transition, and square-to-circular transition. The design operates within the Ka-band; 17.7-21.2 GHz with 18% bandwidth for Tx and 27.5-31 GHz with 12% bandwidth for Rx. The simulations are performed with CST Studio Suite. The insertion loss of the iris polarizer part is <0.05 dB, the return loss is >23 dB, and the variation is less than 15° around 90° for both bands. The return loss of the whole structure is >20 dB. The directivity of the feed chain is between 17–23 dBi.

articleTitle: Design and Beam Optimization of a Novel 1-bit Transmitarray Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Based on the analysis of the receiving and radiating structure, an electrically reconfigurable 1-bit transmission array is designed. An electric field analysis is conducted on the transmission array metasurface, and the broadband and high gain performance of the antenna is achieved through the analysis of the current characteristics of the ring antenna and the principle of current reversal. An innovative approach based on the NSGA-GSK algorithm is proposed to optimize the beam direction of the transmission array antenna and achieve good results in the case of scattered focusing energy caused by beam pointing deviation and high sidelobe level.

articleTitle: Single Feed Dual-Beam Linearly Polarized Holographic Metasurface Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A single feed, dual-beam linearly polarized scalar and isotropic meta unit-cell loaded holographic metasurface based leaky-wave antenna (HMLWA) is proposed in this work. A near-edge quarter-wave monopole is used to excite the HMLWA. The proposed design demonstrates directive broad beamforming towards <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\theta,\ \varphi)=\{(-26^{\circ},\ 0);(42^{\circ_{9}}0)\}$</tex> with unequal maximum realized gain, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G_{mm}=15.5\text{dBi}$</tex> and 13.8 dBi, respectively. The proposed HMLWA is shown to operate at 15.55GHz with dual-beam radiation pattern having 3dB beamwidths of 4.52° and 6.5° respectively. Unequal object-wave accumulation is performed to achieve unequal gain distribution at the proposed beam directions.

articleTitle: A High-Gain and High-Isolation Single-Antenna for Full-Duplex Applicaiton
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents an innovative single-antenna full-duplex subsystem, incorporating a high-gain microstrip patch antenna unit with a reflector and a high-isolation network. The microstrip patch antenna employs a two-port microstrip radiation unit to maintain consistent input impedance at the antenna feed port. The high-isolation network, consisting of hybrid couplers and circulators, effectively addresses performance issues related to antenna port reflections and circulator-induced energy crosstalk. Through simulation and measurement, the subsystem demonstrates remarkable characteristics, including gain>10.2 dBic, axis ratio<2.4, Tx-Rx isolation>50dB, and VSWR<1.55 within the frequency range of 2.018 to 2.12 GHz. Compared to traditional counterparts, this subsystem exhibits superior gain and Tx-Rx isolation.

articleTitle: Phase-Only Optimization of Beam Efficiency for a Large Scanning Reflectarray
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A fast and efficient method for synthesizing element excitations for very large reflectarrays is presented to be used on a Configurable Reflectarray for Electronic Wideband Scanning Radiometry (CREWSR). CREWSR is a tri-band scanning reflectarray that contains three lattices of antenna elements, each containing 120,000 to 480,000 elements. Applying the fast Fourier transform and the alternating projection method allows for an optimization algorithm that achieves phase-only synthesis, targeting side lobe levels to increase beam efficiency.

articleTitle: System-by-Design for Inverse Problems: Recent Advances and Future Trends
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The computationally-efficient solution of non-linear and ill-posed electromagnetic inverse scattering problems (EM-ISPs) arising in several microwave imaging (MI) contexts is addressed by means of the System-by-Design (SbD) paradigm. The main concepts and guidelines of the SbD as applied to EM-ISPs are summarized, together with an example of a recent SbD implementation jointly exploiting time and space priors for yielding an accurate and robust quantitative imaging and follow-up of brain strokes.

articleTitle: Generation of Microwave Toroidal Pulses
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach for producing toroidal pulses in the microwave frequency range by leveraging electromagnetic metasurface technology. The proposed scheme involves the use of spatial polarization modulation and frequency-selective surfaces to transform broadband plane waves into toroidal pulses. The spatial field distribution generated by this method is illustrated, and the feasibility of the approach is preliminarily validated.

articleTitle: Design of Broadband H-plane Horn Antenna with High-Order Mode Based on Substrate Integrated Waveguide (SIW) Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents the development of a high-order mode, low-profile, broadband H-plane horn antenna utilizing substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) technology to increase its bandwidth. The design strategically modifies the antenna's hO <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{rn}$</tex> dimensions and incorporates high-order modes, thereby introducing resonant frequencies over a range of bands and significantly broadening its operational bandwidth. Furthermore, enhancements in the antenna's bandwidth and radiation properties are achieved through the extension of the waveguide aperture, modification of electromagnetic boundary conditions, and integration of impedance-matching structures. The antenna demonstrates a notable performance, with a reflection coefficient below -10 dB in the 30–52 GHz range, and a relative bandwidth of 53.6%. Additionally, it maintains a consistent gain of over 10 dBi across the operating frequency band with excellent directional radiation characteristics. The proposed SIW-based high-order mode H-plane horn antenna offers high bandwidth, low profile, and ease-of-manufacturing attributes, making it suitable for millimeter-wave applications in the Ka-band.

articleTitle: Multi-Person Hallway Gait Monitoring using mm-Wave FMCW Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a multi-person gait monitoring system tailored for efficient operation in cluttered environments. The proposed method demonstrates robust capabilities in tracking multiple individuals and accurately extracting the walking speed of a participant, even in the presence of other people. Our system achieves remarkable accuracy, with a maximum and minimum error of 0.33 m/s and 0.005 m/s, respectively, compared to a stopwatch, as validated through experiments in 25 walking tests. Its adaptability for real-world applications positions it as a valuable clinical tool, offering insights for predicting health issues in individuals, especially older adults.

articleTitle: BSLR: Bridging Communication Gaps with Wi-Fi Enabled British Sign Language Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Communication is a key means of exchanging information, but many people are unable to engage in verbal communication. These individuals often use non-verbal modes, like sign language. Existing British Sign Language (BSL) systems, primarily camera-based, face challenges such as poor illumination and privacy concerns. This paper introduces the use of Wi-Fi signals to detect BSL, with data represented as Channel State Information (CSI). The CSI is denoised and 15 features are extracted. Six classes Drink, Eat, Help, Stop, Walk, and Empty, are identified, corresponding to situations with the subject seated. Machine Learning (ML) models like Neural Network Pattern Recognition, Ensemble (Bagged Trees), KNN (Weighted KNN), and Naïve Bayes (Kernel Naïve Bayes) process this information. These models effectively classify the gestures, with Neural Network Pattern Recognition achieving a classification accuracy of 100%.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Vertically Polarized Endfire Antenna Array for 5G NR FR2 Bands Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a dual-band endfire antenna is proposed for promising 5G NR mmWave frequency (FR2) bands applications. The antenna design introduces a novel radiating aperture array analogy based on open-end substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) feeding technology to achieve vertically polarized dual-band operation. The simulated -10 dB impedance bandwidth achieves 11.5 % (26.3-29.5 GHz) lower band and 9.6 % (36.8-40.5 GHz) higher band. The peak realized gain is 8.78 dBi and 11.5 dBi in the lower and higher bands, respectively. The mmWave array delivers a scanning angle of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 40^{\circ}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 32^{\circ}$</tex> for a realized endfire gain higher than 5.5 dBi and 8.2 dBi at 28 GHz and 39 GHz, respectively.

articleTitle: Frequency-Agile Sliding Metagratings for Dynamic Wave Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The wave control capabilities of metagratings are extended by allowing them to laterally slide relative to each other. This reconfigurability is implemented by a stack of printed circuit boards (PCBs) containing capacitively loaded wires. The PCBs are slid to different optimized locations to obtain efficient refractive scattering in different directions. Although ideal for beam switching, this reconfigurability can attain frequency agility or compensation for unforeseen fabrication discrepancies. Analytical model predictions compare well with full-wave simulations.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Cost-Effective Screen-Printed Log Periodic Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper a wideband cost-effective screen-printed millimeter-wave log periodic antenna is presented. The proposed antenna configuration is implemanted using a screen printed process on a 100 μm Zeonex thin film ( <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varepsilon_r=2.2$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\tan(\delta)=0.009$</tex> ).The metalization layers are made off nano particles silver ink <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\sigma=3.3\cdot 10^{6}\mathrm{S}/\mathrm{m})$</tex>. Measured performances and simulations are in good agreements (peak measured gain of 6.5 dB and simulated peak gain of 7.5 dB). Overall size of the printed prototype is 15x20 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The obtained results demonstrate the feasibility of cost-effective high-performances screen printed millimeter wave antenna.

articleTitle: Conformal Metasurface for Enhancing and Shaping Magnetic Field in 0.5T Magnetic Resonance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In recent years, mid-field Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) systems have grown in popularity for several benefits, the most important being their relatively inexpensive price. In this context, maximizing the Signal-to-Noise ratio (SNR) is crucial to developing clinically useful images. Here we introduce a conformal metasurface, excited by a closely placed RF coil, able to homogenize the magnetic field distribution at the proton <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>H Larmor frequency for 0.5 T brain MRI; indeed, this solution allows an improvement of the RF magnetic field transmission efficiency and, consequently, the SNR of MR scanners. The conformal structure of the proposed 5×5 metasurface is specifically designed to fit the anatomy under investigation, thus achieving greater tissue penetration and comfort for the patient. To validate the proposed approach, we performed numerical full-wave simulations by including a simplified head model, with and without the metasurface presence. Specifically, we compared the magnetic field distributions transmitted inside the phantom for different cutting planes, confirming a significant magnetic field enhancement as consequence of the presence of metasurface and demonstrating its potentialities for mid-field MRI systems.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic and Thermal Characterization of an Epidermal RFID Sensor Grid for Skin Temperature Monitoring During Microwave Hyperthermia
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Microwave hyperthermia is an emerging anticancer therapy that aims to improve the outcomes of radiation therapy and chemotherapy by applying high-power electromagnetic fields (EM) in the tumor region. However, a significant limitation is the possible occurrence of localized hot spots on the patient's skin due to the interaction with the EM fields. An epidermal RFID sensor grid for wireless and cost-effective skin temperature monitoring was previously introduced by the Authors to mitigate the risk. In this paper, the measurement setup for the full-system validation is presented as well as preliminary results concerning the electromagnetic and thermal characterization.

articleTitle: A Dual-Band Directional Array with 360° Azimuth Coverage to Improve Rural Cellular Data Access
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Herein, the antenna part of a system is introduced to electronically scan the surrounding environment and find the direction and connect to the Base Transceiver Station (BTS) with strongest received signal to improve cellular data access in rural areas. The array is composed of five low-band and high-band elements arranged around a circle with diameter of 35 cm. They have directional beams at both 690–960 MHz and 1695–2690 MHz frequency bands. Also the proposed array elements are dual-polarized and can provide the 2x2 MIMO capability. These interleaved low-band and high-band elements have gain of 6.5 dBi and 8.5 dBi and half power beamwidth of 90° and 65° at 920 MHz and 1800 MHz, respectively. They can be switched in turn and cover the whole 360° azimuth space to find the direction and connect to the BTS with the best signal.

articleTitle: RF-Based Respiration Disorders Sensing and Classification Using Machine Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The advent of real-time wireless sensing technologies holds promise for revolutionising healthcare provision, particularly in incidences requiring continuous monitoring, such as Cardiovascular Diseases (CVD), heart attacks and other infectious diseases affecting the respiratory system. Leveraging Universal Software Radio Peripherals (USRP), this study proposes a Radio Frequency (RF) sensing approach based on experiments to capture respiration data qualitatively. The study methodology involves selecting the frequency subcarrier from USRP raw data, followed by noise removal, data smoothing, and normalisation. Subsequently, relevant features are extracted from the preprocessed data, facilitating the training of Machine Learning (ML) models to enable respiration disorder classification. A comprehensive evaluation of various ML algorithms reveals that Extremely Randomised Trees (ERT) and Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) outperform others in classifying RF-based respiration real-time data, achieving an outstanding accuracy of 100% with comparatively short training duration.

articleTitle: An Electrically Compact Multi-octave Antenna System for Panel Mountable 5G Smartphones
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: An electrically compact multi-octave antenna system is proposed in this paper. The antenna system operates in the mmWave and sub-6GHz bands. The overall dimensions of the two-port system are 39 × 8.5 × 2.1 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, which could be easily integrated to commercia15G smartphones. The mmWave antenna has an impedance bandwidth of 36%, with high pattern integrity across the operating spectrum. The microwave antenna offers close to Omni-directional patterns in the 3.5 GHz band. Mutual coupling is below 20dB across both the bands. extended for dual-polarized system with shared ground.

articleTitle: A Shape Memory Alloy Based Chipless RF Temperature Sensor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This article details the design and simulation of a chipless RF temperature sensor featuring a square-shaped tag on a Rogers Ultralam 3850 substrate. The sensor is meticulously designed to resonate at 2.746 GHz, exhibiting a reflection coefficient of −38.54 dB. Its temperature-sensing capabilities span the frequency range of 2.0-3.6 GHz. Employing Nitinol as the sensing material, the sensor responds to temperature-induced deformation, resulting in a discernible shift in the resonant frequency and a concurrent reduction in the reflection coefficient amplitude. This innovative sensor presents a compelling solution for temperature-sensing applications, as evidenced by a calibration curve derived from data, illustrating a consistent linear correlation between temperature and reflection coefficient amplitude. The comprehensive simulation and analysis of the chipless RF sensor were executed using CST Microwave Studio for simulation and CST MPhysics Studio for in-depth analysis.

articleTitle: A 2-D Space-Time-Modulated Leaky-Wave Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A space-time-modulated leaky-wave antenna that modulates the guided wave in both space and time domains is a promising antenna solution to achieve frequency conversion and high-directivity radiation. This paper introduces an innovative snake-like leaky-wave antenna structure, expanding upon the previously explored one-dimensional (1-D) counterpart to form a two-dimensional (2-D) radiating aperture. The meandering waveguiding structure features etched slot openings along its length, facilitating energy coupling from the waveguide into free space. Each slot element incorporates embedded PIN diodes for controlling its coupling state. The time delays of the control signals applied to the slot openings are meticulously adjusted to enable coherent interference of radiated waves from all slots in the main beam direction. The paper substantiates the proposed concept and design of the 2-D space-time-modulated leaky-wave antenna with experimental results.

articleTitle: Additive Manufacturing-Enabled Chipless Tags for Anti-Counterfeiting Solutions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Additive manufacturing methods, encompassing both two-dimensional and three-dimensional approaches, provide unparalleled design flexibility compared to conventional formative and subtractive techniques, facilitating the creation of advanced chipless solutions for secure radiofrequency identification and sensing. This unique attribute, in synergy with high customization potential, can be effectively utilized to establish additional levels of physical layer security.

articleTitle: Wideband Indoor Channel Characterization Based on Measurements at 285 GHz
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Basic transmission loss and delay spreads were measured in indoor test-room environments at 285 GHz with 20 GHz bandwidth using a VNA and directional antennas. The distances between transmitter and receiver were a few meters not over 5 m, and antennas were rotated 360° with step of 30° at transmitter and step of 5° at receiver. The measurement results were proposed as wideband characteristics of propagation.

articleTitle: Optimization and Machine Learning for Antenna Array Healing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Maximizing antenna array performance has been an area of active research for decades. To this end, numerous statistical- and optimization-based approaches have demonstrated significant improvements to array bandwidth, scanning range, and side lobe levels, among other performance targets compared to conventional array design techniques. However, antenna array elements can fail due to mechanical degradation, environmental factors, electrical interference, or through unintended destructive means. Furthermore, element failures can lead to significant performance degradation and even the creation of spurious beams radiating in unwanted or unsafe directions. Therefore, the ability to overcome array failures is of paramount importance. While existing approaches based on statistical and global optimization methods have demonstrated success in array healing, deep learning techniques offer the potential for near-instantaneous performance recovery. The paper introduces our deep-learning accelerated framework for arbitrary on-demand array-healing.

articleTitle: Flexible Multi-Beam Generation Based on 4-D Antenna Arrays with Low Hardware Complexity
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: High flexibility of beamforming has always been one of the major motivations for antenna array design. However, high flexibility always leads to complex and expensive feeding networks. Regarding this issue, this paper presents an effective multi-beamforming approach based on 4-D antenna arrays. In comparison to the traditional harmonic-based beamforming approach, this proposed approach can arbitrarily change the direction of multi-beams without a complex RF switch structure. By utilizing the design degrees of freedom in baseband, individually steerable multiple beams can be generated only with the simple on-off switches. The effectiveness of proposed approach is validated through theoretical analysis and numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Wideband Circularly Polarized Antenna Based on a SRR Operating with High-Order Modes Using Characteristic Mode Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes the design of a wideband antenna with Circular Polarization (CP) covered for the WLAN, C-V2X, radiolocation, radionavigation and mobile communication applications. The antenna consists of a radiating Split Ring Resonator (SRR) edge-fed through a Coplanar Waveguide (CPW). The excitation of multiple resonances on the SRR is achieved by the Characteristic Mode Analysis (CMA) which gives more insight into the radiating characteristics of the antenna and explains the broadband and circular polarization present in the SRR antenna design. The simulated <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S11 < -10dB$</tex> bandwidth of 4.72 GHz has been obtained. Additionally, the simulated 3dB Axial Ratio bandwidth is 370 MHz without the need to perform major alterations in the antenna with a peak gain of 3.36 dB.

articleTitle: Vitality Detection with FMCW Radar Based SAR Imaging Technique at 24GHz
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Identifying human targets in synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imaging is crucial for security and rescue ap-plications, but it poses range and accuracy challenges. This paper presents a vital-SAR-imaging method developed using a frequency-modulated continuous-wave (FMCW) radar system. A measurement setup is developed to capture reflections from human breathing induced chest movements. The Intermediate Frequency (IF) is processed through an audio port of the PC sound card. The acquired data is processed and matched with synchronization pulse and used to generate SAR images. The experimental results showcase the accuracy and extended range in identifying human targets useful for localization applications.

articleTitle: A Compact Versatile Multi-Band Antenna for WPAN Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This article presents a compact multi-band antenna designed for multi-functionality. The overall size of the antenna is 32×22×1.57 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, which covers the one Industrial Scientific Medical band (2.45 GHz), WiMAX (3.5 GHz) and two 5G bands (4.5 GHz and 5.2 GHz) with bandwidths of 210 MHz (2.39-3.6 GHz), 130 MHz (3.45 3.58 GHz) and 950 MHz (4.38-5.33 GHz). Steady omni-directional radiation patterns are achieved and the simulated realized gains are 2.11 dB, 1.77 dB, 1.98 dB, and 3.86 dB at 2.45 GHz, 3.5 GHz, 4.5 GHz, and 5.2 GHz respectively. The proposed multi-band antenna could be a potential candidate for WPAN applications.

articleTitle: A 3D Finite Element Terminal Simulator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A 3D finite element terminal simulator based on transfinite element truncation is developed in this paper. According to the multi-conductor transmission line theory and the developed automatic generation algorithm of terminal integral path, the terminal-based parameters can be calculated by this simulator quickly and accurately. The Viawizard through-hole structure is used to verify this simulator.

articleTitle: Leaky Wave Analysis in Planar Stratified Media
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Leaky wave radiation has found significant applications in the fields of directive beamforming, vehicle to infrastructure (V2I) communication, terahertz network, etc. The theoretical challenge in determining the leaky wave pole using conventional asymptotic/ transmission line approximation has been recently avoided using an alternate transcendental analytic formulation by the authors. The present work is an extension of the recent leaky pole formulation on analyzing the role of layer numbers on the leaky mode's radiation behaviour. Parametric studies of the beam scanning characteristics have been reported for different number of dielectric layers.

articleTitle: A Parallel Iteration Solution Technique for Large Periodic Structures Based on FETI-Like Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The FETI-like domain decomposition method (DDM) exhibits significant memory advantages in simulating large-scale array antennas. This work optimized its simulation efficiency based on a parallel multilevel preconditioner method. Initially, the “cement” element and Robin transmission condition are introduced into subdomains to generate symmetric matrices, which serve as preconditioner for outer Krylov subspace iteration. Then, the p-type multiplicative Schwarz (pMUS) preconditioner is utilized in the inner iteration for solving subdomain matrix equations. For equations involving larger matrix dimensions, the multifrontal block incomplete Cholesky (MFBIC) preconditioner supersedes the incomplete Cholesky factorization in pMUS preconditioner, leading to improved computational efficiency. The above process is conducted in parallel within subdomains. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method exhibits high computational efficiency.

articleTitle: Exposure Assessment to Wearable 5G Antenna with Multi-Layer Skin in Realistic Human Models
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The aim of the present work is to assess the exposure when the skin is modelled as a multi-layer tissue rather than a homogeneous stratum. Specifically, the study was focused on a new technology that is the wearable antenna, that are posed close to the body user, consequently involving the human tissue in the power absorption. Moreover, the antenna is tuned to 28 GHz, so the power absorption is mostly superficial, involving mainly the skin that has an inner structure. So, the present work is a first attempt to integrate the inner structure of the skin with the anatomy of the human user, by using two realistic human models, the adult male and female models of the Virtual Population. For assessing the human exposure, we have extracted the Absorbed Power Density <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{S}_\text{ab})$</tex> averaged over a square of both <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1 \ \text{cm}^2$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4 \text{cm}^{2}$</tex> according to the international guidelines limits. As a results, the decrease of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{S}_\text{ab}$</tex> from the stratum corneum to the viable epidermis and dermis is, at maximum, of 50%.

articleTitle: Contactless Sensing for Recognizing Common Signs in ASL and BSL
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Deaf-mute people use sign language to communicate using hand movements, body postures and facial emotions. Recognising automatic sign language is still a challenge and is in its early stage of research. For this, sensor-based and vision-based approaches are used; however, they have some limitations (privacy concerns, maintenance and ambient lighting). So, contactless sensing emerged as a promising solution to recognise automatic sign language. This work used contactless sensing to recognise ten common signs(I/me, You, Meet, Hello, Understand, Help, Sorry, Time, Candies/Sweets, and Thank you) used in american sign language and british sign language to make the system more efficient. To the best of our knowledge, recognising two sign languages is a novel work which is not done before. Raw data of a single participant is gathered, which is then converted into a spectrogram using signal processing. Afterward, six pre-trained deep learning models (EfficientNet, InceptionV3, MobileNet, ResNet5O, VGG16, and VGG19) are used for classification purposes. 92% accuracy of classification is achieved using ResNet5O and VGG19.

articleTitle: Beam Steering of Traveling-Wave Slot Array Antenna at Fixed Frequency Using Programmable Metawall
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The main challenge for traveling-wave antennas is how to steer the radiation beam at a fixed frequency. This paper presents a novel method for dynamic beam-steering of traveling-wave slot array antenna at a fixed frequency with sustained gain and good impedance matching. Herein, using the appropriate position of the lateral wall of the waveguide, which is named metawall, a steering beam can be directed in the desired direction at a fixed frequency. Perturbation theory is used to analyze the performance of the structure. The proposed structure can be implemented by using an array of meta-atoms instead of the waveguide lateral walls so that by changing their reflection phase via a bias signal, they behave in the same way as the physical changes of the wall. Therefore, the main beam direction is electronically controlled. In the proposed antenna, scan the main beam between 31° and 60° at 10 GHz. Numerical simulations and theoretical predictions showed excellent agreement with proof-of-concept experiments.

articleTitle: MIMO Array Decoupling with Metamaterial Structure in Joint Communication and Sensing System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The use of weight-beamforming technique has effectively minimized the coupling between joint communication and sensing (JCAS) systems. However, the algorithm's generation of high frequency nulls poses a risk to the integrity of the signal. Therefore, this research investigates the decoupling process from the perspective of antenna array design and proposes a MIMO antenna array design scheme that incorporates metasurface in the physical layout of the antenna and utilizes beamforming algorithms for signal transmission. This integrated approach aims to address the coupling issue between transmitting and receiving antennas, resulting in a reduction of coupling and preservation of system gearbox information. As a result, this endeavor enhances system performance and achieves a 43 dB reduction in coupling.

articleTitle: A Symmetrical UWB Antenna for Near-Field Measurements with Low-Cross Polarization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A symmetrical and compact UWB antennas is proposed and experimentally verified for near-field antenna measurements. The dimension of the antenna is 178mm X 100 mm X 12 mm. The simulated cross-polarization ratio is less than -30 dB from 0.5 GHz to 12 GHz, and less than -20 dB from 12 GHz to 18 GHz. The boresight of the radiation pattern keeps nearly unchanged from 0.7 GHz to 18 GHz. The experiment results show that the cross-polarization ratio is nearly less than - 30 dB from 0.7 GHz to 6 GHz. Further experiment shows the absorbers covering the antenna has great influence on the radiation pattern.

articleTitle: Gain-Enhanced Ultra Broadband Millimeter-Wave Reflectarray Design with Varied Square Minkowski Units for CubeSat Space Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel millimeter-wave reflectarray antenna designed for ultra-broadband frequency operation, specifically tailored for CubeSat space applications. The proposed reflectarray antenna features a circular aperture with a diameter of 310 mm. The proposed design comprises square-based cross-Minkowski unit antenna elements of varied sizes distributed across the circular aperture. The proposed reflectarray design achieves an absolute peak gain of 32.6 dBi with a half-power beamwidth (HPBW) of 2.9 degrees at 60 GHz. The proposed design maintains an overall gain exceeding 24 dBi across an ultra-broad frequency operation range from 30 GHz to 110 GHz. The simulated and measured S-parameter results portrayed <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S_{11}\leq-10\text{dB}$</tex> for the frequency of operation ranging from 30 GHz to 110 GHz. The significant high gain and extensive frequency band coverage, spanning the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Ka, V$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$W$</tex> bands, highlight the suitability of the proposed design for CubeSat-based space applications.

articleTitle: Demonstration of a VLF Time-Varying Electrically Short Antenna with High Speed Switching
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: We present a demonstration of an electrically-short VLF time-varying antenna transmitter previously proposed [1], [2]. The antenna traps pulses near the tip, thereby suppressing reflection and achieving a match without bandwidth limitations of resonant matching. A 275-m horizontal antenna was built, consisting of an arbitrary waveform generator connected to a high voltage direct current power supply to send pulses to a nonreciprocal antenna. A high speed, high power switch was then placed on the line to synthetically increase its' electrical length. Voltage was measured with an oscilloscope which confirmed the electrical operation of the antenna as theorized.

articleTitle: A STAR-RIS with Independent 1-Bit Wave Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a simultaneously transmitting and reflecting (STAR) reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) is proposed. This RIS comprises six metallic layers, including the top and bottom patches, two ground layers, and two middle layers with a reflective-type phase-shift circuit and bias circuit. Two pairs of p-i-n diodes are used to independently control the phases of the reflection and transmission. The reflective-type phase shift circuit consists of a branch-line coupler, with two of its ports each connected to a one-eighth wavelength open circuit stub via a p-i-n diode. Another pair of p-i-n diodes is used in the bottom patch to control the phase of transmitted waves. 1-bit reconfigurable transmission and 1-bit reconfigurable reflection is achieved in this design. A unit cell is designed at 10 GHz and a 180-degree phase difference is simultaneously and independently obtained for reflection and transmission according to the simulation results.

articleTitle: Towards Active Mantle Cloaks for Linear Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this work, we explore the feasibility of designing active mantle cloaks for half-wavelength dipoles, aiming to massively reduce the antenna scattering cross-section while preserving its ability to radiate efficiently. A realistic cloaking device is proposed, consisting of split ring resonators loaded with active circuit elements, and its performance is rigorously validated through numerical simulations. In contrast to passive cloaks designed for antenna systems, the proposed device endows the antenna with stealth capabilities during reception without compromising its transmission performance.

articleTitle: Reducing Simulation Effort for RIS Optimization using an Efficient Far-Field Approximation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Optimization of Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RIS) via a previously introduced method is effective, but time-consuming, because multiport impedance or scatter matrices are required for each transmitter and receiver position, which generally must be obtained through full-wave simulation. Herein, a simple and efficient far-field approximation is introduced, to extrapolate scatter matrices for arbitrary receiver and transmitter positions from only a single simulation while still maintaining high accuracy suitable for optimization purposes. This is demonstrated through comparisons of the optimized capacitance values and further supported by empirical measurements.

articleTitle: A Co-Polarized Millimeter Wave In-Band Full-Duplex End-Fire Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A co-polarized millimeter wave In-band full-duplex end-fire antenna is proposed in this communication. The two radiation beams of the antenna are excited by two back-to-back substrate integrated waveguides (SIW), and the end-shot gain is enhanced by a dielectric guide designed on the substrate. Therefore, each radiation mode has a fully shared radiation aperture. A special decoupling structure with coupling holes is used to improve the port isolation. A simulation case working at 35 GHz verifies the feasibility of the scheme, and the antenna has a port isolation of more than 35dB and an end-fire gain of over 12.5dB.

articleTitle: Smart Antenna System for 5G Customer Premises Equipment
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The design of a smart antenna system for Customer Premise Equipment (CPE) operating in the 5G band is presented. It is conceived for 2×2 Multiple-Input-Multiple-Output (MIMO) systems and it uses switchable radiating elements to achieve quasi-isotropic coverage from each RF port by combining the radiation patterns of the different radiating elements. The aim of the solution is to ensure good coverage for the 5G CPE independently from its orientation with respect to the base station it is connected to. The antenna system exhibits return loss greater than 6 dB, peak gain less than 6 dBi and radiation efficiency greater than 65 % on all 5G frequency bands. The smart antenna systems allows improving the received signal strength from the base station of ~3 dB with respect to an equivalent passive antennas enhancing therefore the CPE coverage and easiness of installation.

articleTitle: Improving Statistical Field Uniformity for RF Heating in Freeze-Drying: Impact of Scattering Surface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper examines the electromagnetic (EM) field uniformity inside an R&D lab-scale freeze-dryer (FD). We design a thin scattering surface to improve the EM field uniformity inside the FD by a factor of 1.73x over 12 GHz – 18 GHz (considering <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sigma_{db}$</tex>). A wideband double-ridged horn antenna radiates the EM waves inside the freeze-dryer while a wideband conical antenna receives the radiated power. The bandwidth is 5 GHz – 19 GHz and 5.5 GHz – 25 GHz for the horn antenna and the conical antenna, respectively.

articleTitle: Chipless and Batteryless Microwave Sensor Cell for Remote Detection of Humidity
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Chipless Radio-Frequency IDentification (RFID) sensors belong to the class of microwave sensors and are a quite innovative sensing solution which provide an added value to sensors operating in an Internet of Things/Everything (IoT/E) era. Research is currently focused in two main directions: studying of the material properties as a function of the transduction mechanism and improving the robustness in the transmission mechanism. Here, the aim is to prove the properties of a sensor prototype based on the Nafion NRE-212 50μm-thick sensitive material, in terms of sensitivity, accuracy, reversibility and real-time response/recovery when the sensor is interrogated wirelessy by a suitable reader. Compared to other sensitive materials for humidity detection, Nafion is comparable in terms of sensitivity to polyvinyl-alcohol (PVA) and paper, but with a real-time response/recovery trends.

articleTitle: Effect of Solar Array Orientation on MRO's Shallow Radar (SHARAD) HF Antenna Impedance Matching
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A detailed electromagnetic model of the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter spacecraft and the SHARAD instrument's antenna, previously developed to compute radiation patterns, is now applied to see how Solar Array orientation modifies the impedance matching between radar TX/RX and the HF dipole antenna.

articleTitle: Eigenvalue Analysis for Two-Dimensional Discontinuous Waveguides
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Classical finite element method has been widely used in solving various waveguide and resonator problems. However, the filled dielectric material or the joint of the waveguide is possibly no longer uniform when the waveguide structure or material is irregular. In this case, the traditional two-dimensional port method will need to deal with following problems, such as boundary matching, energy loss and so on. In order to better achieve waveguide transmission, this paper presents a new eigenvalue analysis for two-dimensional discontinuous waveguides. Firstly, we adopt hybrid basis function form of scalar and vector basis functions to discrete a generalized eigenvalue equation. Secondly, we give a specific implementation of impedance boundary conditions, which can deal with some complex geometry and discontinuous materials. Compared with the traditional waveguide port matching technique, this proposed method can effectively solve the generalized eigenvalue equation, especially for lossy physical problems. Numerical results show that attenuation constant is in accordance with the HFSS software, which illustrates that this method is very convenient for simulation and design of discontinuous waveguide problems.

articleTitle: Radiation Hazards (RADHAZ) Assessment for Synthetic Phased-Array Sensors (SPS) Platforms
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The Synthetic Phased-Array sensors (SPS) on wireless platforms are robust frontiers for the telecom industries. They can be employed on airport traffic and auto-pilot unmanned ground vehicles logistics for wide-view and super-resolution engagement. Practical assessment of the EMI/EMC and the comprehensive radiation hazard evaluations for these type of advanced telecom MIMO arrays and radar sensors are critical and of weighted importance to 5G and Beyond-5G deployment, particularly for public health concerns and safety impact.

Author Keywords: Antenna characterization and site probing measurement

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a Simultaneous Multibeam Fully Dielectric Transmitarray
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A preliminary study concerning the design and fabrication of a simultaneous multibeam fully dielectric transmitarray is addressed. The proposed architecture also exhibits the possibility of achieving the steering of the beam via a linear mechanical scan. The dielectric unit cells are tailored to properly shape the phase profile of a TA panel by using the phase-only superposition principle.

articleTitle: Enhancing PSO: Enabling Dynamic Solution Space Adjustment for Effective Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper introduces an innovative adaptive solution methodology that integrates with the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) algorithm. The methodology is specifically designed to autonomously adjust the solution space, particularly in dimensions crucial to the design space. In situations where the global optimum is beyond the initially defined solution space, the particles may struggle to attain the desired fitness value despite extensive searching. To overcome this challenge, the proposed methodology enables the optimization algorithm to operate efficiently, even when the global optimum lies outside the initial bounds. The performance of the adaptive solution space methodology undergoes evaluation using both mathematical benchmark functions and an antenna optimization application. Additionally, the paper conducts a comparative analysis with a method involving the expansion of the solution space in all dimensions after a specified iteration. The results not only showcase the effectiveness of the proposed method in dynamically expanding the solution space but also demonstrate a significant improvement in convergence speed compared to an unspecified expansion method.

articleTitle: Legendre Quadrature for the Discretization of 2D Radiating Panels
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: We propose a new method to discretize a 2D panel radiating over a prescribed Quiet-Plane (QP) as a nonuniform array. Since the most significant singular functions of the radiation operator supported on the panel are linked to those supported on the QP by means of a radiation integral, a Gaussian quadrature rule is exploited to replace the integrals with weighted summations. The quadrature provides a unique set of nodes, namely the array elements positions, and weights, which are involved in determining the excitation coefficients of the array. To avoid mutual couplings, a proper “pruning” approach has been implemented. Numerical validation is also presented.

articleTitle: Series-Fed Dual-Mode OAM Antenna at 6 GHz
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a uniform circular array with four patches operating at 6 GHz has been designed for dual-mode orbital angular momentum (OAM) generation. The antenna elements are series-fed for a concise and simpler antenna design. The challenges in series-fed design have been overcome with a novel network that ensures equal power distribution and the required phase shift between consecutive elements. The designed antenna is capable of generating vortex beams with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$l$</tex>=±1 mode numbers when fed from one of its two ports. The realized gain of the antenna is 4.39 dBi for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$l$</tex>=+1 and 5.24 dBi for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$l$</tex>=-1 mode, while the simulated bandwidth of the antenna is 400 MHz. The OAM mode purities are calculated over an observation circle with varying radius and distance and are presented in this study. The antenna is designed on Rogers 4350B, with final dimensions of 99 × 109 x 0.813 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>.

articleTitle: Circularly Polarized Plane Metaantenna for Beam-Steering in the Elevation Plane
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a circularly polarized (CP) plane antenna, which is composed of four metalines for beam-steering in the elevation plane. The design process for the metalines is discussed and CP beam-steering across an elevation angle range from -20 (deg.) to 40 (deg.) is realized, according to design. Scanning is performed by selecting which of the metalines is fed using on-off switching circuits connected to the metalines.

articleTitle: Aerodynamic and RCS Comparison of Two Generic UCAV Nozzles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this work, we observe the aerodynamics and Radar Cross Section (RCS) characteristics of both straight and Double Serpentine (DS) nozzles for Unmanned Combat Air Vehicle (VCAV). The newly proposed DS nozzle design aims to reduce the Infrared (IR) and RCS signature, thereby augmenting the survivability of UCAV.

articleTitle: Active Control of Fano Resonance With Phase-Change-Based Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a phase-change-based metasurface absorber that can control the excitation of Fano resonance with temperature variations. The proposed thermally tunable metasurface-based configuration is designed based on strong coupling between the narrowband (discrete state) and broadband (continuum state) absorbers, leading to an excitation of Fano resonance within the infrared region.

articleTitle: Wireless Battery Charging for Implantable Medical Devices Using a Wideband Antenna with a Small Elliptic Reflector
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A new antenna configuration is proposed for wireless battery charging, especially in biomedical applications such as pacemakers. An elastic wideband antenna has been developed as an implantable receiving antenna. With its wideband, it will still be able to function even if its frequency band was shifted because of the human body. The transmitting antenna consists of an elliptic reflector and a small feed antenna. The reflected electromagnetic rays from the elliptic reflector collimate at the implanted antenna from different directions with a wide range of angles. This eliminates the possibility of forming any undesirable hot spots in their way.

articleTitle: Chirped-Guided Mode Resonance Based on Laser Ultrasound for Wavelength Scanning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Wavelength scanning devices with narrow instantaneous linewidth are crucial for optical frequency domain imaging (OFDI) and absorption spectroscopy technology. Here, we have combined a guided mode resonance filter (GMRF) with laser ultrasonic to perform quasi-periodic wavelength scanning for the broadband incident wave. Numerical simulation results based on the finite element method show that our method can achieve a scanning speed of about 5 MHz, a spectral range of about 27 nm and an average linewidth of less than 0.24 nm.

articleTitle: On the Relationship Between Array Lattice and the Active Element Pattern of Antenna Arrays
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The active element pattern is very often assumed isotropic when dealing with antenna array design. This assumption inevitably leads to some incongruences. This paper tries to solve such incongruences showing that a strict relationship exists between the array lattice and the active element pattern of the array elements. Starting from the application of the Power Conservation Law, it is shown that the active element pattern must change with the lattice and assuming the constant/isotropic behavior brings to an unfeasible and un-realistic approximation.

articleTitle: Design of Efficient and High Gain Sub-THz Series-Fed Antenna Array for THz Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a cost-effective, high-performance series-fed 5-element antenna array for terahertz (THz) communications. Additional parasitic patches are etched on the top conducting surface, which enhances co-polarized currents, resulting in an increase in gain from 13.15 dBi to 16.50 dBi and aperture efficiency from 9.18% to 20.47% with the same antenna aperture size. The proposed design achieves a peak realized gain of around 16.50 dBi with minimal fluctuation (less than 0.90 dB) and a peak radiation efficiency of 92.4% at 106.50 GHz, operating within the sub-THz band (95–110 GHz). The antenna geometric design is obtained by the SADEA-I algorithm, a machine-learning-assisted global optimization technique for antenna design.

articleTitle: Dual-Polarized Folded-Transmitarray with Feed Blockage Reduction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a novel <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$16\times 16$</tex> dual-polarized folded transmitarray (DP-FTA) operating at 24 GHz. Conventional FTAs typically allow the transmission of only one polarization while reflecting the orthogonal polarization, thereby making the realization of dual polarization challenging.
