In this study, we propose a novel solution by utilizing DP phase-tuning reflective and transmissive metasurfaces together with a short backfire antenna source to achieve a DP-FTA with feed blockage and profile reduction.

articleTitle: Optically Transparent Substrate Integrated Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents results relative to the transparent design a substrate integrated (SIW) structure which permits unobtrusive deployment as well as colocation of RF front-ends with resources dependent on sunlight, such as solar cells. Full-wave simulations predict excellent performance of the proposed meshed SIW in terms of matching, dominant mode bandwidth as well the preservation of cut-off frequencies compared to conventional SIW structure.

articleTitle: Fabrication and Measurement of a Metasurface for Automotive Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this work, the goal is to fabricate and measure a small-scale version of a metamaterial, capable of efficiently shielding the magnetic field from a Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) charging system designed for automotive applications, therefore in the kHz frequency range. The metasurface, which is passive, is configured in a 2D layout, consisting of resonators, or unit-cells, arranged in a 7×7 square matrix: it will be activated through inductive coupling with the nearby WPT system. Current research in this area is limited, predominantly focusing on the use of homogeneous metamaterials for low-frequency magnetic shielding. Nevertheless, studies indicate that inhomogeneous materials exhibit superior shielding effectiveness. Consequently, this work delves into measuring the performance of inhomogeneous metamaterials specifically for future implementation of it as magnetic shielding.

articleTitle: A Dual-Band Dual-Polarized Reflectarray Unit Cell for mmWave Terrestrial Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The focus of this paper is the introduction of a ver-satile, dual-band, dual-polarized reflectarray unit cell engineered for mmWave applications. This unit cell is realized using cross and ring elements placed in an interleaved format, integrated with line stubs that effectively regulate the phase response. Each arm of the cross resonator accommodates two stubs, while the ring resonator is equipped with a total of four stubs. Through the manipulation of the line lengths, the unit cell demonstrates remarkable adaptability across a broad frequency spectrum, operating from 25 GHz to 35 GHz (yielding a 33.33% fractional bandwidth) in the lower band and from 35 GHz to 45 GHz (showcasing a 25% fractional bandwidth) in the higher band, all while minimizing losses. The unit cell's performance is thoroughly evaluated through comprehensive full-wave simulations.

articleTitle: A Metasurface Approach to Mitigate Misalignment Challenges in Wireless Power Transfer Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Misalignment poses a persistent challenge in conventional wireless power transfer systems, adversely affecting the efficiency and robustness. We propose a metasurface aided wireless power transfer system designed to address misalignment issues. This is a threefold process: first, we optimize the transmitter and receiver design to maximize mutual coupling; second, we analyze system behaviour under misalignment; third, we design a lens-like metasurface to restore the coupling in the presence of misalignment. We demonstrate a specific example in which the power transfer efficiency increases by roughly 47% with the introduction of a metasurface between the transmitter and receiver. We propose an optimization approach to calculate optimal parameters of the transmitter, the receiver, and the metasurface.

articleTitle: Numerical Modelling of Spatially Dispersive Metasurfaces with Normal Surface Susceptibilities
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The Integral Equation (IE) field solver Generalized Sheet Transition Conditions (GSTCs) to model spatially dispersive (SD) metasurfaces as zero-thickness sheets has been extended to include the normal polarization components to generalize the method. This IE-GSTC-SD model thus can model both SD tangential and normal components, and here we show that the SD normal polarizabilities can be modelled using mathematically equivalent purely tangential components, for a uniform metasurface. This equivalence is confirmed and demonstrated using the full-wave IE-GSTC-SD solver.

articleTitle: A Plug-and-Play DGTD Implementation for General Dispersive Media
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A discontinuous Galerkin implementation is presented for accurately calculating the electromagnetic scattering by general dielectric dispersive media in the time domain. To validate the formulation, the two-dimensional scattering of a TMz plane wave by a single pole Lorentz dispersive cylinder has been analyzed. The Fourier transform of the numerical solution in the time domain was compared with the analytical solution in the frequency domain at a given frequency. The results obtained are in agreement with the analytical solution.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Based Frequency Selection to Improve Breast Cancer Detection in MammoWave Device
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: MammoWave, a novel microwave breast imaging device, employs a frequency range spanning from 1 to 9 GHz to acquire dielectric properties information from the breast. This study conducts a comprehensive analysis of various sub-bands to identify those or their combinations that enhance the efficacy of cancer detection. The findings reveal that leveraging the combined information from the 5-6, 7-8, and 8–9 GHz sub-bands yields notable improvements. These results underscore the potential of strategically utilizing specific frequency sub-bands for enhanced performance in breast cancer detection using MammoWave.

articleTitle: MammoWave clinical trials within RadioSpin project: results obtained using microwave images' features approaches with thresholds
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we present preliminary outcomes derived from a prospective multicentric clinical trial focusing on microwave breast imaging involving 336 women. This investigation was conducted as part of the RadioSpin project. Our primary objective was to evaluate the prospective performance of MammoWave, our microwave imaging device, in differentiating between breasts with and without radiological findings, utilizing specific microwave images features' thresholds. Beyond this primary assessment, we explored the use of individual frequency sub-bands to categorize breasts into two groups: healthy (without findings or with benign findings) and non-healthy (malignant findings), drawing on features identified in a previous clinical trial. Our findings reveal a sensitivity of 72% in detecting radiological findings and a noteworthy 78% in identifying non-healthy (cancerous) breasts.

articleTitle: An Evaluation of Anisotropic Ink for Improved Reliability of Printed Electronics
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A major challenge towards fabricating printed, hybrid circuitry on conformal surfaces is the interconnection of a commercial off the shelf (COTS) packaging with printed AM traces. This work details the advantages of implementing COTS anisotropic ink (Creative Materials 124-19A) as method for hybrid AM interconnect processes. The resulting structures were tested for both reliability and in various test-bed applications including discrete, passive components and IC packaging. The designs demonstrate a robust connection on low surface roughness surfaces.

articleTitle: Three-Dimensional Nonreciprocal Beamsteering-Amplifying Coding Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this research, we present an innovative approach to achieving three-dimensional nonreciprocal-beam-steering, signal coding, and amplification using a reflective metasurface. Our proposed metasurface exploits the unique characteristics of interconnected supercells to simultaneously perform three key functions: reception, coding, and non-reciprocal gradient-phase shifting for efficient amplification and transmission. By capitalizing on the inherent properties of the novel supercell arrangement, our metasurface facilitates directive and diverse radiation beams, with the added capability of steering beams through simple adjustments in the bias of the gradient nonreciprocal phase shifters. The structure not only ensures significant wave amplification but also exhibits immunity to undesired time harmonics, resulting in highly efficient beamsteering in the reflective state. This study represents a significant advancement in the development of metasurfaces with multifunctional capabilities for next-generation communication systems and signal processing applications.

articleTitle: Improving Calibration Accuracy of Scattered Field Based on Full Wave Simulation of Microwave Imaging System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The transmission coefficient matrix measured by the vector network analyzer (VNA) needs to be calibrated as scattered field data for quantitative microwave imaging inversion. Before the calibration process, it is necessary to first assume the incident field distribution within the domain of interest (DOI), usually approximated with a spherical or plane wave function. Unfortunately, in the near field imaging system the approximate incident field within DOI is not accurate enough. In this paper, the incident field within the DOI is obtained based on full wave simulation of microwave imaging system, which greatly improves the calibration accuracy of scattered field, because of using the incident field closer to the actual measurement environment. Finally, representative numerical inversion results are presented to validate the superiority and accuracy of the proposed calibration method compared to the approximation method with a spherical wave function.

articleTitle: Wideband RCS Reduction of Vivaldi Antenna Utilizing Polarization Conversion Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A low radar cross section (RCS) Vivaldi antenna based on the polarization conversion metasurface (PCM) is presented in this paper. The PCM unit consists of two pairs of L-shape metal strips and an air chamber is applied to increasing the bandwidth of polarization conversion. The wideband RCS reduction can be realized by periodically arranging the PCM units around the antipodal Vivaldi antenna. The antipodal Vivaldi antenna is operating in 9.2-20 GHz and a 10 dB average RCS reduction is realized in 11–35 GHz (104%).

articleTitle: Meandered Patch Antenna Design for Low-Cost Compact UHF RFID Tags
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This contribution presents a miniaturized patch antenna design, for UHF RFID tags, mounted on a low-cost substrate. The presented tag antenna consists of a meandered patch-like antenna (MPA). The MPA is mounted on a low-cost polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) substrate with dimensions of 25 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{x}21\mathrm{x}3$</tex> mm3. The antenna is designed to obtain the proper impedance matching in the FCC frequency band (902–928 MHz). An analysis of the structure is carried out through full-wave simulations to obtain the current density on the top layer and the near fields within the antenna substrate. The antenna is embedded in a rubber wristband for human identification and tracking applications and is compared to a commercial solution of similar dimensions. The results show that the wristband attains read ranges over 4 meters, instead of the +5 meters attained by the commercial wristband, at a lower manufacturing cost.

articleTitle: A Wideband Transmit Array based on Huygens' Metasurface For Millimeter-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a transmit array antenna employing a wideband metasurface (MTS) with high gain for effective beam steering at millimeter-wave frequencies. The proposed unit cell design is based on Huygens' principle. The unit cell exhibits minimal insertion loss, consistently maintained across different phase states, and a transmission bandwidth spanning from 24 GHz to 30 GHz. Subsequently, a transmit array antenna is constructed. The results indicate successful control of the beam at desired angles with low sidelobe levels (SLL).

articleTitle: On the Feasibility of a 3D-Printable Conductive Filament-Based Antenna Array for Conformal Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: NASA is actively addressing communication challenges, particularly in developing phased array antenna systems (PAAS) within the 2-2.5 GHz frequency band. The initial stages involve designing individual flexible antenna elements and non-phased antenna arrays. To address the issues of conformal phased array antennas, this work presents design enhancements for a 3D-printable microstrip patch antenna using a conductive Electrifi filament. The modifications, informed by recent research, are evaluated for the antenna's return loss and surface current distributions. The adopted modifications demonstrated superior performances in terms of gain and input reflection (S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>). The investigation extends to a 1x4 antenna array based on the modified patch antenna element. Notably, the conformal antennas and the antenna array exhibit low return loss alongside high gain and directivity, suggesting substantial potential for efficient performance in conformal surface applications.

articleTitle: A Low-Profile Dual-Band Dipole Antenna with Hollow Structure Reflector
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper introduces a low-profile dual-band dipole antenna designed for Wireless LAN applications, featuring a flat reflector that ensures a stable directional radiation pattern. The antenna and reflector are fabricated on an FR4 substrate with a relative permittivity of 4.2. Utilizing a multiple stubs structure, the dipole antenna resonates at different frequency bands. Excitation is achieved through a 50 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Omega$</tex> coaxial cable. Notably, the proximity between the antenna PCB and the reflector PCB is maintained at a mere 5mm, corresponding to 0.04 wavelengths at 2.4GHz. Measurements reveal impedance bandwidths of 2.4-2.5 and 5.1-5.89 GHz, ensuring <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S_{11}$</tex> values below −10 dB. The antenna exhibits high efficiency across both bands, boasting a gain of 4dBi at the 2.4GHz band and 6dBi at the 5GHz band. The peak gain direction is easily adjustable to accommodate diverse applications.

articleTitle: Dynamically Reconfigurable Polarizer Implemented Using an Energy Harvesting Triggered Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The manuscript describes the implementation of a mm-wave dynamically reconfigurable polarizer, which is triggered by an energy harvester which controls a reconfigurable cells metasurface (MSF). The polarizer is implemented as a 5×5 MSF array operating in K-band (26 GHz) which is able to control the propagation of incident waves and selectively choose to filter out the y-polarization. The proposed MSF transmits both x and y-polarized components simultaneously when the diodes which are used in the reconfigurable geometry cells are in OFF state. However, upon detecting an incident y-polarized wave, the rectifier provides a trigger signal that activates the DC biasing circuit and switches all the diodes simultaneously to ON state. Under this biasing condition the transmitted wave is strictly polarized along the x direction and the incident y-polarized wave is reflected. In both states of the MSF, the simulation results demonstrate transmission efficiency exceeding 95%. As for the rectifier, it exhibits a maximum RF-DC power conversion efficiency of 56%.

articleTitle: Block Structure Preserving Model Order Reduction for A-EFIE Integral Equation Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A Block Structure Preserving Model Order Reduction approach is proposed for Integral Equations methods based on the Augmented Electric Field Integral Equation. This approach allows for representing the unknown fields with dedicated subspaces. Numerical results show that this leads to smaller reduced-order models and higher accuracy.

articleTitle: Generation of Bessel Beam Carrying OAM Using Broadband Transmissive Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Conventional vortex beams carrying orbital angular momentum (OAM) suffer from the limitation of beam divergence in wireless communications applications. In this paper, a Bessel beam generator carrying OAM components based on a broadband transmissive metasurface is proposed. The metasurface cell achieves full phase and exhibits broadband characteristics, fulfilling an overall transmission amplitude higher than -1.5 dB in the operating bandwidth. The performance of the beam is observed over a broad frequency range from 22 to 34 GHz (about 42.3% OAM bandwidth). The capability of the designed metasurface to generate non-diffracting OAM beams is confirmed through simulations, with an overall mode purity exceeding 69%.

articleTitle: Investigating the Maximization of Aperture Efficiency in a Luneburg Lens Antenna System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this study, an investigation was conducted on feed selection and feed distance to maximize the aperture efficiency of two Luneburg-style lens designs. For a lossless 152.4 mm lens, the aperture efficiency of 90%. When scaled to higher frequency the results were identical. When scaled to a 304.8 mm lens, the aperture efficiency reduced to 85%.

articleTitle: Wireless Power Transfer Based on Zero-Order Bessel Beams Generated Using Huygens Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: To achieve efficient wireless power transfer (WPT) in the microwave band for long-distance applications, a transmissive Huygens metasurface capable of generating highly collimated and confined zero-order Bessel beam is presented in this paper. Firstly, a Huygens unit cell operating at 28 GHz featuring a two-bit phase resolution is designed. Then, two transmissive Huygens metasurfaces are constructed based on the desired phase distribution. Finally, zero-order Bessel beams exhibiting diffraction-free propagation in any direction are obtained. Electromagnetic simulations are conducted to validate the performance of the proposed two-bit Bessel beam generator, demonstrating satisfactory diffraction-free focusing within the designated distance, thereby confirming the effectiveness of the proposed design.

articleTitle: Decoupling of A 1 × 4 Differentially-Fed Antenna (DFA) Array with Symmetrical Feeding Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A symmetrical decoupling network is proposed for reducing mutual coupling of closely spaced differentially-fed antennas (DFA). This differential and symmetrical decoupling network (DSDN) is validated on a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1\times 4$</tex> DFA array centered at 2.45 GHz, reaching isolation enhancements of 40 dB for adjacent DFAs and 33 dB for non-adjacent DFAs. Moreover, the antennas exhibit excellent cross-pol radiation, which is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$< -34\text{dB}$</tex> in the H-plane within the angular range of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-60^\circ < \theta < 60^\circ$</tex>.

articleTitle: A Self-Decoupled MIMO Antenna Using Shared Radiator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A simple self-decoupled MIMO antenna using a shared narrow patch is proposed in this paper. Two planar inverted-L antennas (PILAs) are arranged back-to-back at a certain distance with an original coupling path existing. A narrow half-wavelength patch is added above the PILAs at a proper height to operate as a shared radiator. As a result, a second coupling path is introduced to counteract the original coupling between PILAs, thus a naturally high isolation is achieved for the proposed antenna. The proposed MIMO antenna can achieve impedance matching of -10 dB and high isolation of 20 dB in the frequency range from 3.4 GHz to 3.6 GHz, showing a high total efficiency of higher than 94% and ECC of lower than 0.001.

articleTitle: A Broadband High-Gain Millimeter-Wave Pattern Reconfigurable Antenna With Enhanced Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper demonstrates a broadband high-gain millimeter-wave pattern reconfigurable antenna based on asymmetrical top-loaded monopole. By loading a circular ring, the reconfigurable bandwidth and gain of the antenna are enhanced without changing its size. The antenna covers the Ka band, the beam is reconfigured between about ±30 degrees, and the gain is higher than 7.5dBi. The small size makes it suitable for wide-angle broadband phased array and millimeter wave communications.

articleTitle: A Multilayer Compact Circular Patch Antenna by Additive Manufacturing with Enhanced Bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Additive Manufacturing (AM) has continuously demonstrated development of electronic systems such as single layer board antennas and recently, multilayer stack-ups of AM antenna systems emerged. This paper presents the design of a circular patch antenna, and the proposed fabrication approach of the antenna on a multilayer stack-up with enhanced bandwidth, and using AM. A simple coaxial feed would not achieve the required bandwidth, so tuning stubs were employed to optimize the return loss. Multilayer circuit stack-ups can preserve space in the horizontal direction and can be used to increase bandwidth in antenna systems. Therefore, technological advancements of AM printed multilayer antenna systems will enable increased deployment of AM printed multilayer circuit boards as an alternative to either supplement or replace traditionally fabricated electronics.

articleTitle: An Octave-Bandwidth Dual-Function Array
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This work presents the design of an octave bandwidth array, using stacked microstrip patches fed through aperture coupling. The array features the use of metallic cavities and fences in the elements to reduce surface wave propagation in the substrates and improve the front to back ratio. The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{4}\times \mathbf{4}$</tex> array provides stable radiation patterns with frequency, with a gain of 17.1 dB at 4 GHz, and operating from 2 to 4 GHz with a VSWR<2.

articleTitle: Quasi-Electrostatic Computerized Tomography with Fanbeam Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we present a novel computerized tomography method using quasi-electrostatic fields, instead of x-rays. Employing a physically small electrostatic source for transmitting and receiving electric fields, we demonstrate the feasibility of image reconstruction for the object under test through the application of the Radon Transform. The ray- like behavior exhibited by physically small quasi-electrostatic sources enables the application of image reconstruction methods suitable for ray characteristics. In our prior studies, we examined pencil beam algorithm for image reconstruction. However, in this work, we utilize fanbeam algorithm, resulting in a significant decrease in the number of simulations required for numerical investigations. Additionally, our results show enhancement in the image reconstruction quality when compared to our previously investigated technique, namely pencil beam algorithm.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable SIW Liquid Metal Phase Shifter for mm- Wave Phased Arrays
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper introduces a millimeter-wave (mm-wave) phase shifters based on Gallium based liquid metal (LM), presenting an exceptional low insertion loss (IL) performance. The phase shifter can provide a measured phase shift of up to 180° with a precision of 22.5°. Operating within the 26GHz 5G band, this proposed phase shifter exhibits low IL, measuring below 1.6 dB at 26GHz and it achieves an outstanding figure of merit (FoM) of 117.1°/dB. Advantages of the proposed phase shifter include seamless integration with SIW-based feeding networks for mm-wave phased array antennas. Phase control is facilitated by liquid metal-filled vias, allowing for dynamic reconfiguration. Liquid metal is introduced into the via holes when needed and emptied when the via is no longer required. This reconfiguration approach holds promise for various reconfigurable mm-wave devices across a wide range of applications.

articleTitle: Lens Antennas for 6G and Satellite Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: New generation of communication systems have the challenge of providing data in many diverse scenarios with very different hardware requirements. Here, we explore the potential advantages of combining array antennas with domes featuring lens functionality in some use cases. To reduce the computational cost of the lens design, we developed an efficient ray-tracing model. This model calculates radiation patterns while accounting for losses due to absorption and reflections. To demonstrate the potential of this approach, we present a lens designed to increase the gain from 60 degrees.

articleTitle: Characterizing the Complex Permittivity of an Isotropic Scatterer in a Homogeneous Environment Using an Open-Ended Coaxial Probe
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Electromagnetic-based biomedical technologies often depend on accurately estimating tissues' dielectric properties. The open-ended coaxial probe (OECP) technique is one of the simplest and most commonly used methods to obtain the complex permittivity of tissues over the radio or microwave frequency ranges. However, when considering diseased tissues, we encounter tissue heterogeneities, which alter the measured parameters. To quantify this effect, we focus on characterizing an isotropic scatterer within an otherwise homogeneous medium using OECPs. We present an analytical model relating the reflection coefficient to the scatterer properties and derive a closed-form expression for the effective measured admittance. Based on full-wave simulations, we demonstrate that our theoretical model provides accurate estimates of the scatterer permittivity. We use the analytical model to characterize the sensing depth of different OECP systems, providing a performance guideline.

articleTitle: AI-Based 3D Antenna Pattern Reconstruction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we address the challenge of reconstructing full 3D antenna radiation patterns from limited data scenarios, a task essential yet often constrained by resource and data availability. We present a novel deep learning approach, utilizing a pretrained model to accurately estimate 3D patterns from azimuthal and elevation slices alone. Our approach demonstrates significant advancements over traditional analytical methods, offering a robust solution capable of handling a wide variety of antenna types and configurations. The model's performance has been rigorously evaluated against a diverse set of antennas, achieving impressive results in terms of efficiency and accuracy. The implications of this work for antenna analysis and design are profound, offering a quick and reliable method for pattern reconstruction.

articleTitle: Far Field Reconstruction from Phaseless Hemispherical Near Field Using Dipole Equivalence
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper introduce a novel method to reconstruct the far-field radiation pattern of antennas placed above a large metal plane, from phaseless near-field electric field sampled on a single hemisphere. It utilizes spherical equivalent dipoles as equivalent sources and employs the Linear Correlation Residue (LCR) as the cost function. It is demonstrated that through the iterative search using the Covariance Matrix Adaptation Evolution Strategy (CMA-ES) to minimize LCR, far-field radiation patterns could be efficiently reconstructed from the amplitude-only hemispherical near-field electric field. An example is provided to demonstrate the efficacy of the algorithm.

articleTitle: Differentially-Fed Coincident Phase-Centered Wideband Dipole Array on a Triangular Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A differentially-fed coincident phase-centered wideband dipole array on a triangular grid is presented. One dipole polarization is printed on a horizontal PCB and fed by a 100Ω-differential grounded coplanar waveguide (GCPW) pair, while the orthogonal dipole (droop bowtie) polarization is fed by a 100Ω -differential stripline pair. Infinite array simulations suggest operation over 7-21GHz (3:1 BWR) with good return loss, orthogonal port coupling and low differential-to-common mode conversion out to 45° in the E-, H- and D-planes. Realized gain and cross-polarization isolation levels agree with the ideal cross-dipole predictions.

articleTitle: An Update to the Design of a Millimeter Wave Multiple-Beam Phased Array Antenna Prototype
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper reports the progress in the development of a millimeter wave multiple-beam phased array antenna prototype. As compared to its previous counterpart, the present design increases the number of beams from 4 to 8. But because of the use of multichannel multifunction chips and four-stage blind mate connections between modules, the gross weight of the prototype is reduced from 10 Kg to 7 Kg. Measurement performance meets the specified requirements.

articleTitle: Accurate Model for Active Impedance of Slot-Phased Array Antennas Considering Mutual Coupling Effect
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, an accurate analytical model for predicting the active impedance variation with the scan angle of slot-phased array antennas (S-PAAs). is presented. The model is based on Floquet modes expansion of magnetic currents and its application to phased array slot antennas. The mutual coupling effect is taken into account by considering the variation of magnetic current with the scan angle. The simulation results calculated by proposed analytical model are presented and compared to those obtained by the numerical EM solver (HFSS). A very good agreement is observed.

articleTitle: A Rigid Coaxial Cable-Based Wideband Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a coaxial cable-based antenna with a dipole-like radiation pattern. The antenna configuration involves circular slots and a shorted stub. Simulated and measured results show a good omnidirectional radiation pattern in the azimuth plane, maintaining an azimuth plane gain exceeding 2 dBi and good impedance matching from 2.33 GHz to 3.24 GHz. It is expected that the antenna will find many IoT applications.

articleTitle: Design of Monopole Circularly Polarized Antenna with Polarization Convertor AMC Reflector
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes an AMC surface for polarization rotation, which achieves the bidirectional linear polarization conversion of a monopole antenna to unidirectional circular polarization radiation. The proposed monopole antenna can achieve impedance bandwidth is 47.4% (5.45-8.96GHz), and the axial bandwidth is 6.7% (6.88-7.36GHz).

articleTitle: Two-System Real-Time Radio Propagation Modeling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The two-system theory of human thinking process is applied to the radio propagation modeling and prediction. System 1 corresponds to a quick and intuitive estimation of propagation parameters such as path losses and angles of arrival/departure. System 2 is a more deliberate process that takes more time to ‘think’ and provides more accurate results. In this paper we describe the necessary components of a two-system propagation modeling framework, present initial results, and discuss the challenges.

articleTitle: A Wide Beamwidth Magneto-Electric Dipole Atenna for Wide Beam Scanning Antenna Arrays
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this study, a simple and cost-effective configuration to broaden the beamwidths of the patch antenna has been studied. The proposed wide beamwidths antenna consists of two parasitic magnetic dipoles placed orthogonally to a driven electric dipole. Due to the complementary far-field radiation behaviors of both antennas in their respective E-plane and H-plane, the antenna half-power beamwidth broadens. An excellent wide beam of 138.6° and 110.9° in E-plane and H-plane, respectively, has been achieved at 4.72 GHz. The proposed antenna has been fabricated and tested. Measurements shows good agreement with the simulations. The proposed antenna can find its application for the increasing the scanning coverage of the patch antenna arrays.

articleTitle: Single-bit mmWave Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface with Suppressed Quantization Lobe
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: We introduce a millimeter wave (mmWave) single-bit reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) that allows electronic beamsteering with no quantization lobes. Incorporating an optimized random fixed phase delay pattern across the aperture, we manage to suppress radiation artifacts stemming from quantization errors. Additionally, the RIS design employs a modular approach by using PCB compatible 2.5D packaging. As such, the radiating elements, phase shifters, delay lines, interconnects, and necessary shift registers are integrated within a tile that can be laterally cascaded and form arbitrarily large RISs. We present the RCS measurement results of a 4-tile prototype (1,024-unit cells) with electronic beam-steering up to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 60$</tex> degrees, with more than 10 dB quantization lobe suppression at a center frequency of 27.2 GHz.

articleTitle: Ridged Waveguide Fed Conical Spiral Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A conical spiral antenna (CSA) and feed are designed for wideband operation and fabricated in a monolithic process. The approach, enabled by 3D printing, simplifies fabrication and improves repeatability when compared to the conventional CSA manufacturing paradigm in which antenna and feed are fabricated separately and soldered together. The proposed feed transitions a double ridged waveguide to a tapered twin line, preserving phase balance while matching to the impedance of the CSA. Measurements show good performance across the C band with directivity > 6.4 dBic, axial ratio (AR) < 3 dB within <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 30^{\circ}$</tex>, wobble-on-wave (WoW) < 3 dB within <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 35^{\circ}$</tex>, and VSWR < 1.7. The results demonstrate the potential of additive manufacturing to simplify fabrication of front-end receivers.

articleTitle: Fast Ray-Launching Approach to Estimate Fabry-Perot Cavity Radiation Patterns
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a ray launching algorithm to estimate the Half Power Beamwidth (HPBW) and Side Lobe Level (SLL) of a Fabry-Perot cavity is proposed. The primary objective is to compute the radiated electric field exclusively in the principal planes (E and H) by using a ray-launching technique. This algorithm is deployed on MATLAB® and the results are compared with those obtained through a commercial electromagnetic solver. By implementing representative test-cases, we proved that the developed code allows an averaged computational time reduction of around 1200 times maintaining, at the same time, a mean error of 2.14° and 2.33 dB for HPBW and SLL, respectively.

articleTitle: Towards 3D Scalar Quantitative Imaging of Dielectric Targets via Virtual Experiments
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this contribution, the virtual experiments framework is proposed for the solution of 3D scalar inverse scattering problems. In particular, a new linearization of the relevant data equation is given based on a suitable design of the virtual experiments, and a preliminary test is performed against a simple scenario.

articleTitle: Study of the Maximum Operating Distance of a Quantum Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This study explores the quantum advantage in radar systems by examining the maximum distance at which the quantum radar system maintains a probability of detection error below 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−6</sup>. Investigating optical and microwave frequencies in both air and rainfall conditions, the analysis models entanglement generation, propagation, target reflection, and joint measurement models, considering realistic factors like thermal populations. Monte Carlo simulations indicate an 800m radar range for the optical mode and approximately 60m for the microwave signal in air. The decrease in these ranges is due to the substantial impact that lowering the frequency has over propagation distance, caused by increased thermal photons. Rainfall conditions further intensify photon absorption, resulting in reduced ranges of 20m and 2m for optical and microwave frequencies, respectively.

articleTitle: A Bowl-Shaped Base Station Antenna with Wideband Cross-Band De-Scattering Capability
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper introduces a unique bowl-shaped low-band (LB) antenna operating within 0.80-0.96 GHz (18.2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>) designed for dual-band base station arrays. It incorporates innovative helical filters to achieve a remarkable reduction in radar cross-section (RCS) within the high-band (HB) from 1.36 to 2.72 GHz (66.7<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>). This enables the collocation of HB antennas within the LB antenna without compromising their performance. To enhance impedance matching, the LB antenna is equipped with dedicated LC circuits within its balun. The structural robustness of the LB antenna is guaranteed through the utilization of custom-designed 3D-printed dielectric supports.

articleTitle: Manifold Compressive Sensing 2D-Direction of Arrival Using Single Pixel Programmable Array
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper introduces a new approach for determining the direction of arrival (DoA) of a signal with multi-path reflections based on signal spars representation and the Compressive Sensing (CS) algorithms. Employing CS in DoA enables the use of a single-pixel reconfigurable antenna array to detect multipath signals, thus significantly reducing circuit and hardware complexity by utilizing only one common feeding port with a simple circuit interface, thereby lowering footprint and costs. Utilizing a single-pixel programmable antenna array with a mapping of active array elements through biasing diodes, a dynamic aperture with orthogonal manifold paradigms was achieved. The same map would feature various parts of the numerically constructed sensing matrix for CS-DoA. MATLAB was used to model and synthesize both the dynamic aperture measurements and sensing matrix as essential inputs for the presented CS-DoA algorithm. The results confirmed the effectiveness of this innovative algorithm under various noise levels.

articleTitle: Hybrid-Loop Antenna for Dual-Band Wi-Fi Applications in Mobile Tablet Computers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A dual-band hybrid-loop antenna is proposed for Wi-Fi 6/6E applications in mobile tablet computers. In the proposed antenna, a mu-near-zero (MNZ) segmented loop and a parasitic folded-loop are placed on opposite sides of the substrate. The total antenna, within a planar structure of 64.75mm × 5mm, is placed in a tablet computer with full metal housing. By adjusting the effective permeability of segmented loop through tuning the distributed capacitors, the 0<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup>/1<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">st</sup>/2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup>/3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup> modes of the segmented loop are compressed to achieve a broad bandwidth from 5.15 GHz to 7.15 GHz. Combining with the 2.39-2.49 GHz mode supported by the parasitic folded-loop, the proposed antenna satisfies the Wi-Fi 6/6E bands, targeting communication applications in tablet terminals. Furthermore, the proposed antenna serves as a balanced structure, thereby exhibiting high robustness in practical applications such as different sizes of tablet computers or the impact of hands. The proposed design is presented in this paper with numerical simulation results.

articleTitle: CNN-Based Path Loss Modeling for Massive MIMO System in Underground Mine Scenario
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Modeling path loss for millimeter waves presents a significant challenge in designing fifth generation (5G) mobile communication networks, primarily due to their high susceptibility to various environmental factors. This paper introduces a novel path loss model based on Massive MIMO 28 GHz millimeter-wave channel measurements conducted in an underground gold mine, specifically for Line of Sight (LoS) scenarios. The proposed model, employing a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), demonstrates superior performance in both accuracy and complexity, achieving a predictive accuracy of 92% for unrealized measurements. The experimental results underscore the effectiveness of the CNN path loss model compared to deterministic and empirical methods.

articleTitle: Optimal Efficiency Multibeam Network Synthesis for Non-Orthogonal Beams
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This work introduces a synthesis method to create networks capable of exciting any set of non-orthogonal beams at the optimal efficiency as dictated by Stein's limit. To achieve that, we mathematically decompose the corresponding excitation matrices of these networks into two orthogonal and one diagonal excitation matrices. Notably, the orthogonal matrices are implemented as standard Nolen matrix mutlibeam networks and the diagonal matrix as a set of attenuators. To verify the validity of our design a 4 beam - 2 ×2 antenna network in Ridge Gap Waveguide (RGW) technology is designed and measured at 30 GHz showing excellent results.

articleTitle: Analysis of Inversion Performance of Objects with Varied Scattering Characteristics in Millimeter-Wave Security Inspection under Clothing Occlusion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the inversion performance of objects with different reflectivity under clothing occlusion conditions. First, objects with different reflectivity are reconstructed under occlusion. The results show that for objects with low reflectivity, such as non-metallic materials, the reconstruction quality is affected by occlusion. Therefore, in actual security inspections, the obstruction of clothing should be considered for the detection of non-metal and other low-reflectivity targets.

articleTitle: Correlation Analysis of Two Interval Analysis Methods of Radomes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Interval analysis (IA) has been proven a useful tool in radome tolerance analysis. Compared with the precise amplitude-phase-based IA (IA-AP) method, the real-imaginary-parts-based IA method (IA-RI) method is less accurate but much more efficient. In this work, correlation between the two IA methods is analyzed through comparison under different kinds of errors. Results of a spherical radome indicate that the two methods yield similar variation tendencies, which justifies the usage of IA-RI method in robust variable thickness radome design with evolutionary algorithms.

articleTitle: Tunable Phase Shifter with Large Phase Range Based on Reconfigurable Resonator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A novel tunable phase shifter (PS) with large phase range is proposed based on the reconfigurable resonator. The PS composes of one switchable resonator with compact size and two external coupling networks (ECNs). The resonator is designed to switch between two states with a large constant phase difference and with different matching impedances. The ECNs are used to match the changeable impedance and meanwhile shift the phase continuously. The switchable resonator cooperates with the ECNs to complete the entire PS design, doubling the phase shift range (PSR) to 180°. The systematic design method taking phase performance into consideration is put forward. The designed PS exhibits good performance with 10-dB fractional bandwidth of 13.3%, a large PSR of 0° - 180°, and a low phase error of ± 3.5°.

articleTitle: A Study of a Microwave Waveguide Structure for Hydrocarbon Recovery from Mineral Oil Waste
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The goal of this article is the development a portable system for the neutralization of a ship's tank waste products by heating them exploiting microwaves selective absorption, based on hollow waveguides. The extraction of hydrocarbons from the waste will make them safe for deposit and providing the possibility of easy landfill or recycling. The development of the model requires the simulation of the device using a Multiphysics simulator. The proposed structure is based on the flow of the wastewater through a quartz tubed placed inside a WR-340 rectangular waveguide which will be operated at its fundamental mode at 2.45 GHz. The proposed microwave technique leads to a uniform heating of the material at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$260^\circ C$</tex> with efficient 99 % while maintaining the leaked electromagnetic radiation from the device in safely level. Furthermore, the size of the aforementioned device permits its mounting it to an appropriate vehicle able to arrive and operate on site (e.g. ports).

articleTitle: Efficient Analysis of Wide Monopole Structures
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The scattering analysis with the Electric-Field Integral Equation of perfectly conducting plates has been traditionally carried out through the thin-plate approximation, which models the plate as an open surface, thereby reducing drastically the number of unknowns. This approach exhibits good EM scattering accuracy under non-grazing planewave incidence and for small thicknesses, which suffices in many practical applications. Recently, the so-called thick-surface approach has shown improved accuracy, with moderately small computational overhead, in cases where the thin-surface approach fails. In this paper, we extend such scheme to the scattering analysis of plates vertically oriented with respect to an infinite perfectly conducting ground plane. We show with RCS results that the formulation resulting from the combination of the Image theory and the original free-space thick-surface scheme allows also the accurate analysis of monopole-like structures, with finite thickness, in cases where the original thin-plate approach fails.

articleTitle: Wide Beam Pattern Synthesis for Holographic-Based Leaky Wave Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a wide beam pattern synthesis method for holographic-based leaky wave antennas is presented. The desired beam width in the elevation plane is divided in multiple discrete angular sectors, leading to a non-uniform progression of the transverse modulation period across the antenna aperture. In order to achieve a flatter beam pattern, the division into the discrete elevation angles follows an exponential function instead of the common linear progression. Based on the wide beam pattern synthesis method, a HLWA with a desired 3 dB beam width of 40 o is designed and fabricated on a fused silica wafer for a frequency of 160 GHz. The far field measurements show a gain of 26 dBi, a minimum side-lobe level of 18 dB and a polarization purity of 40 dB at 160GHz.

articleTitle: Quantum Entanglement Computation Using Canonical Quantization in a Waveguide and Scattering Theory
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this work, we propose two approaches of numerical study of quantum entanglement. In the first approach, canonical quantization with numerical mode decomposition is applied to inhomogeneous dispersive media. The initial quantum state is assumed to be a cat state, which is an entangled state with coherent states. Results in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2\mathrm{D}$</tex> modeling will be presented. In the second approach, we study the effect of scattering on momentum-entangled photon pair from spontaneous parametric down-conversion. Scattered two-photon wave function is calculated using computational electromagnetics. Schmidt number is calculated numerically to investigate the enhancement of entanglement after scattering compared to the incident state.

articleTitle: Efficient Ray Tracing Simulation Framework for Massive MIMO Channels
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper introduces an efficient ray tracing (RT) simulation framework for massive MIMO channels using the coarse-refinement scheme. Compared to the brute-force method, i.e., performing RT for each element pair in the massive MIMO array, the coarse-refinement method conducts RT only for sparsely located array elements, and then interpolates the RT results to remaining elements, hence significantly reducing the complexity compared with the brute-force method. The accuracy is guaranteed by capturing sphericaVastigmatic-wave propagation and the spatial non-stationarity (SnS) in the near-field (NF) region. A simulation in an indoor scenario demonstrates that the method can generate almost the same channel as the brute-force method, yet with significantly reduced simulation time.

articleTitle: Open Waveguide Wideband Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A novel wideband antenna design comprising of a slot backed by a cylindrical screen forming an open waveguide is presented. The proposed antennas are well-suited for the UNII WiFi bands. Designs featuring either one or two radiating elements are proposed for 5GHz and 6GHz WiFi bands. A design methodology based on the use of an asymmetrical excitation, of bow-type and tapered slot shapes is developed. An open waveguide antenna with a 39% bandwidth has been developed by using this methodology. Realized gain levels of 8 and 7dB, respectively, of the two- and one- element antennas has been achieved.

articleTitle: Combination of Multiple Radiating Elements for a Wideband Cellular Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A solution to integrate multiple antenna elements resonating at different frequencies into one compact layout to cover both low- and high-frequency bands is presented in this paper. The proposed structure is low profile, compact, and wideband, it is suitable to be integrated into a handset, under the shark-fin cover, or into a small cavity embedded on a vehicle roof. The proposed cellular antenna consists of a diplexer, a printed inverted-F antenna, and a monopole covering the various services in the range between 617 and 5500 MHz. In particular, printed PIFA is used to cover the low-frequency band while circular Ultra-Wideband monopole is used to cover the high-frequency band.

articleTitle: Rotation-Driven Bidirectional Asymmetric Reconfigurable Holography Based on Spatially Cascaded Phase-Only Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: As a new platform for electromagnetic wave modulation, the metasurfaces have demonstrated unprecedented capabilities in wireless communications, information encryption, and holographic displays. Multi-functional metasurfaces dramatically increase the ability of metasurfaces to process complex information. Here, by introducing directional degrees of freedom (DoFs), we design a holographic meta-device consisting of dual-layer spatially cascaded phase-only metasurface with bidirectional asymmetry display. The phase distributions of the dual-layer metasurfaces are optimized through reverse design according to preset targets. In addition, the multiplexing capabilities can be further expanded via the rotation multiplexing scheme. As a proof of concept, a bidirectional asymmetric holography meta-device is demonstrated in the microwave region. The proposed method may provide a new paradigm for asymmetric data burning in communications, large-capacity holographic display, and information encryption.

articleTitle: Dual-Beam Antenna Array Using Multilayer Feeding Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Multi-beam arrays play a crucial role in spatial diversity to enhance the reliability of wireless links and simultaneously cover multiple areas. This approach offers several advantages, such as size reduction and lower power consumption compared to single-beam antennas. In this work, a novel dual-beam radiation pattern for 5G millimeter-wave (mmWave) communications is proposed through a unique multilayer feeding structure. The key innovation lies in a 180° rotation between antennas in different layers, enabling in-phase array excitation to produce a dual-beam pattern. To validate the proposed concept, an in-phase multilayer power divider is employed to excite two end-fire antennas. Obtained results demonstrate that the proposed structure covers a substantial bandwidth of 32.25% for two beams, oriented at ±33°.

articleTitle: A Q/V Dual-Band Dual-Circularly Polarized Shared-Aperture Phased Array Antenna with Limited Field of View Scanning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$8\times 8$</tex> -elemnet dual-circularly polarized (CP) shared-aperture phased array antenna (PAA) with large element spacing (LES), designed for limited field of view applications in Q- and V-bands. The elements operating in both bands follow a unified design method. Left-hand circular polarization (LHCP) and right-hand circular polarization (RHCP) are achieved through a 90° hybrid coupler integrated into the multi-layer printed circuit board (PCB). The radiation pattern is shaped by an umbrella-shaped lens attached to the PCB using a metal block, creating a flat-top active element pattern (AEP) to suppress grating lobes during beam scanning. The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4\times 8$</tex>-elemnet Q-band array (37.5-41.5 GHz) and the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4\times 8$</tex>- elemnet V-band array (47.0-51.5 GHz) are arranged in a staggered configuration within the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$8\times 8$</tex> -element shared-aperture Q-/V -band array. A prototype of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$8\times 8$</tex> -elemnet P AA is designed and measured for AEP. The Q-band array achieves a 24.6-dBic boresight gain with a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 18^{\circ}$</tex> scanning range, a 0.6-dB gain variation, and a -8-dB grating lobe level. The V -band array achieves a boresight gain of 25.4 dBic with a scan range of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 20^{\circ}$</tex>, a gain variation of 1.2 dB, and grating lobes less than -10 dB.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Filter Enabled by EMSIW with Coupled Microstrip Lines
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this work, a dual-band filter based on eighth- mode substrate integrated waveguide (EMSIW) and coupled microstrip lines is presented. The proposed structure consists of two adjacent EMSIW resonators coupled through a slot and the microstrip coupled lines, which can perform two individual resonance modes. Then, a dual-band filter is realized with the proposed structure. Experimental results show that, its lower passband is from 2.15-2.21 GHz with insertion loss of 1.69-2.6 dB, while its higher passband is from 3.33-3.67 GHz with insertion loss of 0.82-1.98 dB. Moreover, the stopband rejection between the two passbands is over 25 dB. All these results have shown the flexibility and suitability of the filter for dual-band applications.

articleTitle: IEEE 802.15.4 Compliant Ultra-Wideband Impulse-Radar for Vital Sign Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper we examine the feasibility of using ultra-wideband impulse-radar for vital sign detection, like breathing and heartbeat frequencies, while complying with the IEEE 802.15.4 standards for ultra-wideband devices. To achieve this, we use an ultra-wideband transceiver that enables secure ranging and radar applications. We examine the system on a human test subject with two sets of different antennas. We measure the vital signs by analyzing both the amplitude and demodulated phase of the carrier signal over slow time and compare the results to ground truth data which was recorded separately. The results show, that accurate vital sign estimation is possible under laboratory conditions, while complying with IEEE 802.15.4 regulations, which heavily limit the bandwidth of the radar application.

articleTitle: A Polarization-Mixed Antenna Array with Wide-Range Continuous Beamwidth Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A reconfigurable dual-polarized antenna array system featuring wide-range continuous beamwidth control (WCBC) is developed based on polarization-mixing method. By combining two linear-polarized radiations and adjusting the phase shift between the two sub-arrays, the total radiation pattern can have its beamwidth continuously varying from 21 ° to 100°. Moreover, the system retains its beam scanning capabilities when the two polarizations are used separately. The system is characterized by its simple configuration and modulation. Whether works in beam scanning or beamwidth control mode, the system can be easily controlled by a phase shift chip. Notably, no additional amplifiers or attenuators are required, and all elements are fully excited, ensuring the high overall efficiency of the system. The WCBC array system is designed, fabricated, and experimentally validated.

articleTitle: Dual-Mode Textile Antenna Using Slotted Bowtie for Knee Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A compact wideband antenna made of textile wearable material is proposed for electromagnetic knee imaging. The antenna is a slotted bowtie embedded in a slotted aperture, backed by a ground plane. The dual-mode antenna has a wide impedance bandwidth ranging from 0.48 to 2.4 GHz (133%). The operating frequency of the antenna provides a reasonable balance between the penetration of microwave signals into the knee and the spatial resolution of reconstructed images. The antenna is designed to be part of an electromagnetic wearable brace in direct contact with the knee. Utilizing Wool felt and conductive fabric, the antenna has compact dimensions of 40 × 40 × 3.22 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. In addition to its wide bandwidth, the antenna achieves unidirectional radiation with a 16 dB front-to-back ratio, thanks to its fully grounded structure. The antenna exhibits safe specific absorption rate levels and a high penetration efficiency of 83%.

articleTitle: On the Impact of Material Losses on Radiation Efficiency and Matching Bandwidth of Electrically Small Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This work demonstrates the material loss impact on ultra-small antennas. The material losses considered are the ones common for printed circuit board manufacturing technology, which are substrate loss (RO4003C) and metal loss (bare copper). The simulation performance for four variations of a shunt-fed circular antenna of ultra-small size with a maximum dimension of λ/30 is presented. The impact is analyzed for future investigations on radiation efficiency enhancements.

articleTitle: Reducing Grating Lobes in Sparse Linear Arrays Using Variable Projection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Fixed-phase broadside arrays often have an inter-element spacing close to a wavelength in order to minimize the weight and cost. The performance of such arrays may be affected by the appearance of grating lobes. In this paper, we propose a simple exponential analysis and variable projection based solution to reduce these grating lobes.

articleTitle: 5G Electromagnetic Field Exposure at 26 GHz: Absorbed Power Density Assessment
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This article investigates the absorbed power density (APD) for a 26 GHz coaxial feed microstrip antenna with a partial ground, utilizing Rogers RT/Duroid 5880 substrate. The microstrip antenna with a dimension of 10.8 mm × 10.8 mm demonstrates excellent performances in terms of reflection coefficient, realized gain, and efficiency with values of −41.55 dB, 8.2 dBi, and 97%, respectively. The APD is assessed by determining the power density on the curve probe lines through a three-layered human head phantom, that consists of skin, fat, and muscle. The head phantom is constructed using CST voxel family data of an eight-week-old female infant and a 4-cole-cole dispersion model. In the APD assessment, the antenna is excited by 6.99 dBm (5 mW) and placed 5 mm from the phantom, and 17 curve probe lines that extend 20 mm in a perpendicular direction from the antenna, are adopted to cover the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4\ \text{cm}^{2}$</tex> averaging area of the phantom. The APD of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2.09\ \mathrm{W}/\mathrm{m}^{2}$</tex> averaged over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4\ \text{cm}^{2}$</tex> exposure area is obtained, which complies with the standardized limit. The proposed APD assessment method could serve as an alternative to mathematical modeling or laboratory measurement. CST Microwave Studio (MWS) is utilized for carrying out all the design and analyses.

articleTitle: A Low-Profile Fully Planar Loop Antenna for Polarization Reconfigurability
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A low-profile fully-planar polarization reconfigurable antenna is proposed. The innovative design utilizes only two PIN diodes sharing a single DC-biasing network. The low-cost antenna offers wide impedance and axial ratio bandwidths. These appealing features and compact configuration result in an antenna that can be easily integrated with modern communications systems. A close agreement has been achieved between measurements and simulations.

articleTitle: A Modified 1-Bit Unit-Cell for mmWave RIS Optimized at Extreme Incident Angle
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a modified wideband reflective unit-cell for Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface (RIS) operating at millimeter-wave (mmWave) n257 band. The unit cell is specifically optimized at extreme incident angles and utilizes dual-polarization reflection with p-i-n diodes for a 1-bit RIS control. The design exhibits superior reflective phase difference close to 180° across most of the 3 GHz bandwidth (26.50-29.45 GHz) and reflects over 74% of the energy even at extreme angle of incidence as high as 70° from the RIS boresight. The enhanced reflectivity minimizes losses, and precise phase control improves beam pointing accuracy crucial for low-complexity 1-bit RIS. Full-wave electromagnetic simulations confirm effective performance. The unit cell is compared with the current state-of-the-art unit cells, in terms of bandwidth, polarization, phase accuracy and operation in extreme angles of incidence.

articleTitle: Dual Mode Multi-band Antenna/Rectenna For Simultaneous Wireless Information and Power Transfer (SWIPT)
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a novel dual-mode multiband antenna design for Simultaneous Wireless Information and Power Transfer (SWIPT) applications. The proposed microstrip patch antenna, co-designed with a high impedance rectenna, efficiently operates across four bands (1800MHz LTE, 2400 MHz ISM, 3500MHz WiMAX, and 5200/5800MHz Wi-Fi). Achieving a compact footprint comparable to a standard microstrip patch antenna, it demonstrates a maximum Power Conversion Efficiency (PCE) of 69% at -2 dBm input power. The design eliminates the need for additional matching networks, making it an ideal candidate for Radio Frequency Energy Harvesting (RFEH) applications in both wearable and non-wearable scenarios.

articleTitle: Simultaneous Doppler Camouflaging and Backscatter Communication Based on 1-Bit Time-Modulated Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a simultaneous Doppler camouflaging and backscatter communication system based on 1-bit time-modulated metasurface. By covering the target with the designed time-modulated metasurface, the metasurface scatters any incident harmonic wave into a phase-modulated wave, as a result, the scattering wave carries the data information and alters its spectrum at the same time. The proposed system is theoretically analyzed and demonstrated by metasurface unit cell design and system simulation.

articleTitle: Transmission Metasurface for X-Wave Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This article proposes a method for generating X- waves through transmission meta surfaces. By decomposing X- waves into three different frequencies and designing three independent sub arrays sharing the same aperture, X-waves can be effectively generated. Sub arrays are independent and complementary, which can generate Bessel waves with the same cone angle in a shared aperture. The simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed design method.

articleTitle: Thinned Prephased Electronically Steered Phased Array with Low SLL and Gain Loss
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Using low-resolution phase shifters, the complexity and cost of electronically steered phased arrays (ESPAs) can be reduced. However, low-resolution phase control results in high SLLs and gain losses in traditional ESPAs. To reduce the SLLs while minimizing gain losses as much as possible, a thinned prephased ESPA (TPESPA) adopting low-resolution phase control and low-dynamic-range-ratio (low-DRR) amplitude control is proposed. The simulated results show that a 2-bit TPESPA with amplitude DRR of 1.5 and sparsity of 30%, can achieve similar SLLs of −20 dB at a gain loss of 2.2 dB.

articleTitle: Design of a Frequency Selective Surface Band-Pass Filter Covering Multi-octave L-S Bands
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, an FSS-based wideband band-pass filter operating within 1–4 GHz range is presented. The proposed filter consists of two Frequency Selective Surface (FSS) layers separated by a 0.5 mm thick dielectric substrate. The design procedure of the FSS unit-cell is firstly investigated, providing guidelines to control the transmission bandwidth. The top FSS layer comprises a vertical I-shaped unit-cell, while the bottom one includes a horizontal I-shaped unit cell. Finally, full-wave simulations were performed, and the results show that the proposed filter achieves a -3 dB transmission band from 1.1 to 3.6 GHz (a fractional bandwidth of 107%) and a -1 dB transmission band from 1.3 to 3.5 GHz (a fractional bandwidth of 91%). Furthermore, the presented structure exhibits stable performance against oblique incidence up to 40°.

articleTitle: Radiation and Stealth Performance Simultaneously Design for Patch Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Nowadays, antennas with low RCS requirements are becoming more and more urgent in some specific application. Conventional antenna design methods mainly focus on the radiation, so it is usually difficult to balance the radiation and stealth performance, and has a strong reliance on the experience of the designer, which makes the design period and the performance have some uncertainness. To address this problem, topology optimization, which takes the distribution of materials as the design variable and achieves the goal of optimization by finding the optimal distribution form of the materials in the design domain, is employed to design the radiation and stealth performance simultaneously design. The above method is applied to an aperture coupled feed patch antenna with the return loss and RCS value at the target frequency point as the optimization target. Numerical results show that the proposed antenna design method has many important new features such as intelligent tunability and designability, which can provide new ideas to meet the continuously updated requirements of antennas in specified fields.

articleTitle: Updates to the Chu-Harrington Limit
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Electrically small antennas are commonly benchmarked against the Chu limit. However, applying the Chu circuit model to analyze the Q of high order spherical modes leads to scenarios with both large Q-factors and wide bandwidths, which is clearly unphysical. This contradiction brings into question the circuit model's validity for lower order modes, as well as all subsequent work that is consistent with Chu's result. At the conference we will present our updates to the Chu-Harrington limit.

articleTitle: Low-Profile Wideband Magneto-Electric Dipole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A compact Magneto-Electric Dipole (MED) antenna for C-band applications is presented. The proposed model provides a stabilized unidirectional pattern, higher gain, and adheres to the low-profile characteristics. The design consists of a microstrip feedline printed on the top of the substrate, slots induced in one of the electric dipoles on the backside of the substrate, and a solid ground (GND) plane at the bottom.
