The induced slots in the electric dipole perturb the magnetic current and help increase the antenna bandwidth. The antenna holds a fixed size of 70 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Simulated results have shown the achievement of 11.7 dBi realized gain over operational frequency bands of 5.5 GHz to 7.4 GHz while VSWR < 1.9.

articleTitle: An Efficient Null Steering Method for Nonuniform Sparse Phased Array Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, an efficient beam null steering method based on nonuniform fast Fourier transform and genetic algorith-m, NUGA, is proposed to solve the low beamforming efficiency in low earth orbit satellite anti-interference null steering. The approximate substitution mechanism is illustrated and the beam null steering performance in accuracy and efficiency is verified. The results show that the average null depth of NUGA is 15 dB lower than that of GA within the same optimization time, and NUGA can complete about 80 more evolutionary iterations than GA in every 5 seconds.

articleTitle: Amplifying CRLH Delay Line for Frequency Scanning Reflectarrays
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: An amplifying composite right/left-handed (CRLH) delay line is presented for frequency scanning reflectarrays. Using a reflection-type amplifier, the reflective unit with the CRLH delay line can maintain the original polarization state. Gain enhancement and scanning is demonstrated by incorporating the measured delay line responses into full-wave simulation.

articleTitle: MIMO Antenna Array with Ultra-Wideband and High Isolation Characteristics for Mobile Terminals
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a broadband terminal antenna is proposed, which is realized by using the characteristic of tight coupling between antennas. Four tightly coupled antenna elements are used as a pair of antennas so as to realize the ultra-wideband and beam-scanning performance. The Simulated results show that the proposed antenna can achieve ultra-wideband performance (−6 dB bandwidth) in the frequency range of 2.9-12 GHz and ± 45° beam scanning characteristics in the high frequency range of 8–12 GHz. Based on the proposed tightly coupled antenna element, two pairs of antennas are placed on the sideboard, and by etching the slot on the ground, an isolation better than 18 dB in the 2.9-12 GHz frequency band can be achieved.

articleTitle: Geometrical Properties Inversion of Quadric Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: We study the uniqueness of solutions in inverse scattering problems, focusing on the inversion of geometric parameters of quadric surfaces, e.g., ellipsoidal surfaces. We delve into the necessary observational conditions required to ensure the uniqueness of solutions in bistatic observation scenarios and analyze various typical radar observation modes. Numerical results validate our conclusions. This study contributes to the understanding of solution uniqueness in inverse scattering problems and lay the groundwork for future investigations into the robustness of these solutions.

articleTitle: A Compact Monopulse Feed Antenna Based on Gap Waveguide at W-Band
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This work presents a compact and low-cost monopulse feed antenna based on gap waveguide at W-band. The proposed antenna is based on a pyramidal horn fed by a comparater network, integrating in double-layer GGW. Hybrid E- and H-plane 3dB coulpers are used to form a very compact comparator network structure, while suppressing energy leakage. The antenna operating band covering 88–100 GHz (13%) with reflection coefficient below -15 dB and isolation below -20 dB. Furthermore, the antenna exhibits a SUM beam gain of 16 dBi and DIFF beam null depth below than -30 dB at 94GHz.

articleTitle: Sub-6 GHz Channel Measurement and Analysis in Undulating Terrain
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, an automated wireless channel testing system was established to conduct Sub-6 GHz radio wave propagation measurements in undulating terrain scenarios. Leveraging airborne LiDAR, both terrain data and propagation measurement data were acquired and subjected to comprehensive analysis. The experimental findings enhance understanding of communication characteristics in undulating terrains, providing references for designing and optimizing communication networks in such environments, and offering data support for research on the impact of terrain on radio wave propagation in relevant domains.

articleTitle: Substrate-Integrated Conical Monopole Antenna for 5G V2X Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A wideband and low-profile millimeter-wave antenna for 5G V2X applications is presented. The antenna is a substrate-integrated adaption of the conical monopole antenna to achieve a wide operating bandwidth. The substrate-integrated conical monopole is designed by discretizing the cone shape using multiple PCB layers and then the number of layers is minimized while maintaining similar impedance-matching bandwidth. The proposed antenna bandwidth covers all the 5G millimeter-wave band that ranges from 24 GHz to 40 GHz. The omnidirectional pattern of the antenna makes it the ideal candidate as an element for a circular phased array with near-end-fire beams. A phased array of the proposed antenna can then be incorporated to achieve high gain and 360° beam scanning around the vehicle.

articleTitle: Wideband Dual-Polarized Antenna Array for Base Station Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A 4-element linear array of wideband dual-polarized printed dipole antenna for base stations is proposed in this manuscript. To make the structure dual-polarized, each antenna element consists of a pair of dipole, at an angle of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 45^{\circ}$</tex>. A metallic reflector is kept on the back side at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda_{0}/4$</tex> to improve the overall gain and to reduce the back radiation of the antenna. Two 1:4 power dividers are also incorporated with the 4-element structure to feed the antenna array. The overall dimension of the proposed structure is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4\lambda_{0}\times\lambda_{0}\times 0.24\lambda_{0}$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda_{\mathrm{C}}$</tex> is free space wavelength at 3.725 GHz. The antenna array shows impedance bandwidth coverage below −15 dB range from 3.05 GHz - 4.4 GHz frequency band, which corresponds to n77 and n78 NR operating bands. A peak gain of 14.71 dBi is attained by the antenna array at 4.1 GHz.

articleTitle: Effect of Substrate Modes Mitigation on The Bandwidth Stability of Binary Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The effect of suppression of substrate modes among the unit cells of a binary reconfigurable intelligent surface is studied with respect to its angular stability. A design with the shape of Jerusalem crosses is used while electric walls are applied along the substrate interfaces to mitigate substrate coupling. Simulations are performed for a wide range of incidence angles and the effect on the reflection phase curves is studied. Results show significant effect on both the position and the width of the operating frequency bands with strong indication of achieving angular stability up to 30°.

articleTitle: Multipath Separation in Split-Step Simulation of Electromagnetic Waves in the Low Troposphere
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The impact of multipath effects on aviation nav-igation and communication systems is significant. This study aims to understand the multipath effects and mechanisms of electromagnetic waves propagating within complex environments. It aims to accurately split electromagnetic waves, computed via split-step simulation methods, into distinct groups with various group delays. The paper details a modeling technique that addresses multipath effects and a method for separating group delays. A numerical experiment showcases electromagnetic wave propagation in a standard atmosphere over an impedance ground, demonstrating successful separation into multip <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{le}$</tex> wave components with diverse path delays, validating the presented methodologies' efficiency.

articleTitle: Stacked Radial Feeds for Dual-Polarized Arrays
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A 7-21GHz dual-polarized array system with stacked dual radial feeds is presented. The concentrically stacked radial feeds interface with the external system through a triaxial to dual coaxial adapter that detangles a triaxial line to a H-pol and V-pol SMPS connectors. A manifold with two isolated stripline layers is used to connect the radially arranged dual feed ports to the 32H and 32V array ports in a square grid. Due to the stacked arrangement, the feed network comfortably fits under the array footprint with minimal manifold trace lengths and routing loss. Through careful full-wave simulations, it is shown that the feed network has better than 1dB loss and VSWR < 2 across the 3:1 bandwidth, resulting in greater than 75% total system efficiency.

articleTitle: Numerical Simulation of Passive Millimeter-Wave Image of Ship Kelvin Wake Using STAR-CCM+
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Passive millimeter-wave (PMMW) detection technology has attracted widespread attention due to its advantages of excellent penetration and concealment. Ship wake covers a wide area and lasts for a long time, which is easier to detect compared to ship, and the morphological characteristics of ship wake are correlated with ship parameters. In this paper, we will numerically simulate the Kelvin wake using STAR-CCM+ software and ray-tracing algorithm in combination with a specific ship model, and analyze the impact of polarization mode and ship speed on PMMW imaging.

articleTitle: A New Rotman Lens Power-Distribution and Phase-Shifting Network Design for a mmWave SatCom Phased Array Antenna Sytem
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A new power-distribution and phase-shifting network design based on a Rotman lens for a SatCom phased-array antenna in the K- and Ka-band is presented. It reduces space con-sumption and meets all the requirements given in aerospace. The new design is presented together with a mechanical engineering model that is used for space-compliance tests. The functioning is proven by simulated and measured antenna patterns.

articleTitle: 3D-DFD: A Driver Fatigue Detection Scheme Using 3D mmWave Imaging Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Driver fatigue refers to the state of reduced mental and physical alertness, impairing a driver's ability to safely operate a vehicle, often caused by inadequate sleep or prolonged periods of driving. Radar is utilized for fatigue detection due to its non-intrusive nature and ability to continuously monitor physiological signals like respiration and movement, which are key indicators of a driver's alertness level. Traditional radars can only focus on 2D information. Using the novel 20*20 Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) radar, the spatial information can be explored which is relavant to multiple human activities including the actions that represents fatigue. In the paper, we proposed a 3D based driver fatigue detection scheme (3D-DFD) with MIMO radar and achieved 81.54% of accuracy on pilot dataset.

articleTitle: A GPU Acceleration Method for Direct Solutions of Electric Field Integral Equations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The method of moments (MoM) as a traditional numerical method has been widely recognized and used in solving electromagnetic integral equations. As the scale of solved problems increases, the computational costs will rise significantly, often preventing it from a direct use. This necessitates the integration of acceleration techniques by either software or hardware. The hardware acceleration is mainly achieved through the central processing unit (CPU) or graphics processing unit (GPU). This paper proposes a GPU acceleration method for the direct solution of electric field integral equations (EFIEs) by the method of moments (MoM). Numerical examples show that the proposed method can be approximately 10 times faster than the acceleration of a state-of-art multicore CPU with an OpenMP parallelism.

articleTitle: Predicting V-Band Attenuation Through a Multiple Input Modality CNN/MLP Hybrid Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A hybrid input deep-learning model utilizing both radar images obtained from the NEXRAD platform along with tabular meteorological measurements was developed to predict V-band attenuation due to the atmosphere and precipitation events. Pairing radar images and tabular data with RF power measurements obtained from a 24- km, 72 GHz terrestrial link, the received power along the link was estimated and compared to an image-only CNN model. The hybrid model demonstrated better performance relative to the CNN model both in terms of overall error and in mean absolute percentage error.

articleTitle: Diffraction-Enhanced MIMO Capacity
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: We introduce a novel technique for the enhancement of MIMO multiplexing based on the boosting of spatial diversity produced by diffractive grating walls.

articleTitle: A Statistical Analysis of Sub-7 GHz Radio Channels Used for IEEE 802.11be WLAN
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)

authors.preferredName: Claudio R. C. M. Da Silva

abstract: This paper provides a statistical analysis of radio channels used in IEEE 802.11be based wireless local area networks (WLANs). Channel measurements were conducted across eight different indoor and outdoor client to access point (AP) communication scenarios for both line-of-sight (LOS) and non-LOS (NLOS) channel conditions. We investigate the path loss, large-scale and small-scale fading across 256 frequency points between 6.425 and 6.445 GHz. In our analysis, we use the popular lognormal distribution to characterize the large-scale fading, and the Rician distribution for the small-scale fading. We also present a set of parameter estimates and summary statistics for the path loss, large and small-scale fading, so our results can be used to assist with future WLAN design.

articleTitle: New Approach to Multi-Band and Compact Antenna: Spin-Resonant Magnetodielectric Substrates
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This study introduces a novel approach for achieving high-performance multi-band and electrically small antennas. The proposed design relies on selective frequency optimization facilitated by magnetodielectric materials exhibiting spin-resonant behavior, resulting in low magnetic loss both below and above the resonance frequency. The research successfully demonstrates the application of this concept in realizing a dual-band Wi-Fi 6/6E antenna, presenting a promising avenue for commercialization.

articleTitle: Compact Multi-Band Vehicular Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A low-profile Ultra-Wide Band (UWB) monopolar antenna is designed for vehicular applications. The proposed antenna design is based on a combination of a UWB wire-discone antenna and a Meander-line Dipole Antenna (MDA). The structure is mechanically stable and has a reduced weight for mounting over vehicles. A coaxial feed method is used. A CST Microwave Studio is used for full-wave analysis. The antenna covers a wide frequency range with more than 4 GHz bandwidth in addition to coverage of 900 MHz GSM band and provides a good Omni-directional radiation pattern. The proposed design is compact and provides UWB coverage, making it suitable for vehicular applications.

articleTitle: A Theoretically Stable FDTD Subgridding Method with Arbitrary Grid Ratios and Material Transitions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A theoretically stable finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) subgridding method with arbitrary grid ratios is proposed to solve electromagnetic problems with material transitions. In the proposed method, the summation-by-parts simultaneous approximation term (SBP-SAT) and the interpolation matrix with arbitrary grid ratios are carefully designed to guarantee the stability. Numerical results validate the accuracy, efficiency and flexibility of the proposed subgridding method with material transitions.

articleTitle: Correlation of Solar and Geomagnetic Indices during Solar Cycle 24 with TEC-Derived Metrics
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Ionosphere modeling continues to be a dynamic research field due to its intricate, non-linear characteristics that are still not completely discovered. The various of factors influencing this space results in a complex multivariate estimation problem. To address this, models are being developed that not only utilize Total Electron Content (TEC) measurements but also incorporate solar and geomagnetic indices such as Sunspot Number (R), F10.7, Solar Lyman-alpha (Sy-α), Kp, Disturbance Storm Time (Dst), and Auroral Electrojet (AE). To shed light on the process of parameter selection for ionosphere modeling, we present a correlation analysis to uncover the relationships among various indices. For the analysis, the data used has a period of 2 hours and covers the entire Solar Cycle 24, from 2008 to 2019. This comprehensive dataset allows for a general examination of the relationships between these indices and the state of the ionosphere. Among the Solar indices (R, F10.7, Sy-α) that exhibit strong inter-correlation, Sy -α demonstrated the highest correlation (p = 0.92) with TEC. Geomagnetic indices showed weaker correlations with derived metrics, emphasizing their association with disturbances rather than TEC intensity. The Dst index stands out among geomagnetic indices with the highest correlation (p = -0.28) regarding standart devitation in Global Ionospheric Maps (GIMs).

articleTitle: An Extended Equivalent Circuit Model for Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The circuit model of a dual polarized resonant reconfigurable intelligent surface is discussed. The RIS is characterized by two resonances where the phase response can be controlled. It is shown that the proposed circuit model provides an accurate prediction of the reflection properties not only for the first resonance but also for the second one.

articleTitle: Fast and Accurate Time Domain Solver Based on the Exact Calculation of Matrix Entries in Boundary Element Method for Scalar Wave Scattering
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this work we present a first application of a novel integration strategy for the calculation of matrix entries in space-time Galerkin discretization of time domain boundary integral equations for wave scattering problems. The strategy is based on using an all-analytical formula for self-interaction and close interaction terms, while a semi-analytical method is chosen for geometrically distant elements. The exact formula is based on a dimensionality reduction procedure of the interaction integrals adapted to the time domain case. Nevertheless, interaction be-tween distant triangle pairs often present challenging geometrical configurations where cancellations between big numbers occur. Hence, a semi-analytical method is preferable in such cases. This hybrid strategy is applied within a marching-on in time algorithm for a scalar wave scattering problem. Computation time resulted to be similar to the full semi-analytical strategy while obtaining a better precision for the interaction elements.

articleTitle: A Modified C-Band Double Biquad Antenna for Airborne UAV Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper performs a modified double biquad antenna by utilizing two shorting pins to connect the top and bottom layers of a printed circuit board (PCB). The proposed antenna exhibits compact sizes of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.79\lambda_{0}\times 1.58\lambda_{0}\times 0.12\lambda_{0}$</tex>. Experimental results show the -10 dB impedance bandwidth of 21.26% (4.12 - 5.1 GHz) covering the entire C-band (4.4 - 5 GHz), the maximum realized gain of 12.16 dBi, the half-power beamwidth of 61.76° at 5 GHz and the low cross-polarization levels (XPLs; <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\leq-25\text{dB})$</tex>. Due to have high gain coefficients, the proposed antenna is a promising candidate for C-band long-range airborne unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) applications.

articleTitle: Constantine Balanis: Celebrating a Legacy of Exemplary Dedication and Remarkable Contributions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This presentation examines Prof. Balanis' continuing impact on advancing electromagnetics, encompassing diverse realms of applied electromagnetics like EMI/EMC, SI/PI, and RF De-sense, extending beyond antennas. Dr. Anuj Modi, who extensively engaged with Prof. Balanis-from taking multiple graduate courses to collaborating closely for years as a Ph.D. student, contributing to the latest editions of his both influential books shaping current and future scholars in these disciplines-provides insights into Prof. Balanis' mentoring and teaching roles. The discussion highlights Prof. Balanis' unwavering commitment to rigorous research standards, meticulous academic preparation, and dedicated teaching (showcasing his steadfast work ethic until retirement). Dr. Modi shares anecdotes exemplifying Prof. Balanis' enduring passion for the field and his exceptional dedication to guiding research endeavours and inspiring students.

articleTitle: Beam-Scanned Reflectarray with Fixed Feed
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Presented in this paper is a mechanically rotated reflectarray antenna designed for a radar scanning scatterometer, with a stationary feed location. The beam-scanning mechanism of this reflectarray antenna is described through the derivation of the theoretical phase distribution and validated through electromagnetic numerical simulations. The simulation results confirm that as the reflectarray antenna is rotated, the main beam dynamically scans following the angle of rotation, while maintaining its inherent radiation performance characteristics.

articleTitle: Design of a Dual-Band SRR for Effective Use in Wireless Energy Harvesting Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A 2D metamaterial is proposed for absorbing scattered waves at frequencies of 2.1 GHz and 5.8 GHz. The results of the suggested Split-Ring Resonator (SRR) exhibit consistent behavior in terms of polarization angle, radiation angle, and even variations in the load resistance. A novel method is employed to collect the surface currents of SRR cells by guiding the surface currents of each row of unit cells to a rectifier. Lumped resistors are used as an alternative to rectifiers and load resistors.

articleTitle: New Method to Generate High Order RF OAM waves Using Microstrip Antennas without Power Dividers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we present a novel RF OAM antenna design method using direct coaxial feed with Circular Microstrip Antenna (CMA). By manipulating cylindrical harmonics through small design modifications, we achieve on-demand generation of desired OAM mode with remarkably simple, planer design, without using a power divider circuit or multiple feeds. The presented method has been demonstrated and verified with simulations and measurements.

articleTitle: Some Notes on the Role of Field Representations in Electromagnetic Information Theory
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Electromagnetic Signal and Information Theory (ESIT) is an emerging field that integrates electromagnetic and information theories to explore the constraints imposed by the laws of electromagnetism on wireless telecommunications systems. This contribution will discuss four different representations of the field in free space. From an electromagnetic point of view, they are equivalent, all allowing an accurate representation of the field. From the ESIT perspective, they play quite different roles, focusing in some cases on field information and other cases on the physical implementation of the ESIT.

articleTitle: Assessment of Human Exposure for New Energy Vehicle Electromagnetic Field
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: With the rapid development of new energy vehicles, the impact of the electromagnetic radiation on the human body requires to be concerned attention. Modeling and simulation of the electromagnetic environment within the automobile are conducted in this study. And the specific absorption rate (SAR) in the human head is simulated and calculated. The assessment of the electromagnetic safety for the vehicle is performed with reference to the International Commission on Non-Ionizing Radiation Protection (ICNIRP) guidelines for limiting exposure to electromagnetic fields.

articleTitle: Huygens Equivalent Principle Based Modeling for Propagation and Scattering Among Domains in Mixed and Stacked PCBs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A Huygens's principle based modeling method is proposed to describe wave propagation and scattering in modern mixed and stacked PCB designs. Generally, complex PCB structures are often decomposed and evaluated in separately distributed domains, and wave interaction among those domains can be quantified by discrete wave ports generated by Huygens equivalent principle located at domain boundary. Analytical formulation and numerical verification are both conducted for the proposed method, and the average error introduced is no more than 0.09dB. The proposed method is promising for evaluation of EM wave propagation and scattering in complex and large PCB systems and practical designs.

articleTitle: Voltage Doubler Topology-Based Rectifier for Emerging Millimeter Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents the realization of a wide-band rectifier operating at the millimeter wave (mmWave) bands from 24 GHz to 34 GHz. The designed rectifier is based on an optimized single-voltage doubler branch topology, with two advantages: such as low-cost and simple implementation. In particular, the realized rectifier showed a maximum efficiency of 50% and around 30% at 29 GHz and other bands, respectively. Thereby, the developed rectifier has demonstrated its potential for various Internet of Things applications.

articleTitle: Accelerating Finite-Difference Time-Domain (FDTD) Solvers using Voxels-in-Cell Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The Voxels-in-Cell (VIC) method was recently introduced for reducing the computational cost of the finite- difference time-domain (FDTD) method with objects composed with voxels. In this paper, we present some applications of VIC method in electromagnetic problems and show that the accuracy of the method is preserved while large reductions of the computational requirements can be achieved.

articleTitle: A Polarization-Insensitive Reconfigurable Frequency Selective Surface Switching and Tuning among Absorption, Transmission, and Reflection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A polarization-insensitive reconfigurable frequency selective surface (RFSS) exhibiting switching and tuning operations among absorption, transmission, and reflection behaviors has been presented. The unit cell includes a single-layer FR4 substrate with metallic patterns on both sides. The switching and tuning characteristics have been achieved using a set of p-i-n diodes and varactors on the top layer and a set of p-i-n diodes on the bottom layer. The simulation results are observed for four different operating modes, such as OFF (p-i-n diode on the top layer)-OFF (p-i-n diode on the bottom layer), OFF-ON, ON-OFF, ON-ON, and the tuning under each state by regulating the varactor. The results show that the OFF-OFF and ON-OFF provide transmission responses tuning in the range of 2.88-4.36 GHz and 3.0-4.97 GHz, respectively, with corresponding insertion losses of 2.4-3.2 dB and 1.3-3.6 dB. During OFF-ON mode, a narrowband reflection having a reflection coefficient less than -2.5 dB results in the frequency range of 3.21-5.49 GHz. An absorption response is achieved in the ON-ON state with more than 90% absorptivity from 3.28-5.78 GHz. The topology is polarization-insensitive as well as angularly stable. The proposed RFSS satisfactorily performs multifunctional characteristics, thus providing great prospects for various applications.

articleTitle: OAM Beam Deflection Control Based on Tensor Impedance Holographic Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The phenomenon of performance degradation due to transceiver misalignment is a common issue in Orbital Angular Momentum (OAM) communication systems. This paper introduces an anisotropic holographic metasurface, which demonstrates the alteration in the deflection angle of the target beam when the relative permittivity of the substrate is adjusted. The metasurface is constructed from subwavelength metallic patches placed on a grounded dielectric substrate. The surface impedance distribution of the proposed holographic metasurface is determined by the interference between the excitation source and the predefined object beam.

articleTitle: Double U-shaped Slot Microstrip Array Antenna for 28 GHz 5G System Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A 2 by 2 double U-shaped slot microstrip array antenna is presented in this paper for 28 GHz band 5G system applications. The U-shaped slot extends the frequency bandwidth of the rectangular patch with simple feeding structure easy for impedance matching in the power dividing network. The final designed 2 by 2 array antenna is built on a printed circuit board in RO-4003C with measured results of 14.6% in bandwidth and 9.87 dB in gain operated at 28 GHz. The connector effect is discussed by simulations for bandwidth and gain performances, and slight improvements are observed in this study.

articleTitle: Breath Rate Monitoring Using Dielectric Resonator Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A novel dielectric resonator antenna-based structure is proposed for respiration rate monitoring, one that can be seamlessly incorporated into clothing buttons for wearable medical technology. This wireless, real-time breath rate monitoring system operates by transforming changes in the relative permittivity of the human lungs to a shift in resonance frequency of the antenna throughout a complete respiration cycle. A nearby reader interrogates the sensor, extracts information, and sends the recorded data to the user or medical personnel. This sensor occupies an area of 30×30×4 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, demonstrating a compact system compared with other breath rate monitoring sensors documented in the literature.

articleTitle: Dispersion-Engineered Space-Time Transitions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Most works on space-time structures limit themselves to nondispersive media, although all physical media have some dispersion, by causality. Here, we consider dispersive space-time media and explore related opportunities, including the existence of plasmonic-like modes with velocity-tunable confinement.

articleTitle: TDL based Digital Equalization Method for Frequency Flatness of Ultra-Wideband mm Wave Channel Emulator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: To avoid the deterioration of in-band flatness caused by radio frequency front-ends such as frequency converters in ultra-wideband millimeter-wave channel emulation systems, this paper proposes a digital equalization method that combines filter coefficients with channel time-varying impulse responses. The channel emulation and flatness filter compensation functions are simultaneously realized through the tapped delay line model without the need to add additional high-order filters, which greatly reduces the consumption of hardware resources and simplifies the structure of the baseband system.

articleTitle: A Super-Massive Planar Phased Array with Full-Space Scanning Capability
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This article presents an X-band super-massive planar phased array with full-space scanning capability. 252 antenna elements are designed with very large space and randomly distributed in an equivalent elliptical radiation aperture of around two-meter by one-meter aperture, and the minimum distance between two elements is 1.5λ at 10GHz. The designed antenna can scan from -85°to 85°in all cutting planes with a maximum sidelobe lower than −10 dB, i.e., the full-space scanning capability. Simulated results show that the scanning loss of 85°direction along E-plane and H-plane is around 2.7dB and 2.4dB, respectively, compared with that of the main-beam direction, i.e., 0°. Experiments have been carried out and verified the design.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Fully Convolutional Networks for Dielectric Profile Reconstruction in Medical Microwave Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The capabilities of deep learning networks in reconstructing the dielectric profile in medical microwave imaging are evaluated. Thus, different fully convolutional networks are trained on unhealthy brain (with lesions) data and then tested to generate dielectric profiles of brains using wideband (0.5-2 GHz) signals generated from a brain imaging domain. The quantitative evaluation results of UNet3+ show the best reconstruction performance not only in unhealthy brain but also in healthy brain (without lesion) tests. This work offers guidance on capabilities and limitations of fully convolutional deep learning networks for dielectric profile reconstruction in medical microwave imaging.

articleTitle: Ultrabroadband 1×8 Vivaldi Array for Beam Steering Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we present a 1×8 array Vivaldi antenna for broadband beam steering applications. The Vivaldi antenna element offers a very wide bandwidth in a single feeding configuration with a lower first resonant frequency of 4.2 GHz and an upper frequency of 37.2 GHz. Each element of the antenna offers a low gain and therefore can produce wide angle fan beam steering.

articleTitle: A Low Scattering Fabry-Perot Cavity Antenna Using a Wideband and Polarization Insensitive Rasorber
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A fabry-perot cavity antenna (FPCA) is realized by employing a wideband, low loss, and polarization insensitive frequency selective rasorber (FSR) as a superstrate on top of a patch antenna. This configuration provides gain enhancement and low scattering in the absorption bands of the absorption-transmission-absorption (A-T-A) rasorber. More specifically, the average monostatic radar cross-section (RCS) reduction is 11 dB and 12 dB in the lower (2 to 4.4 GHz) and upper (7 to 10 GHz) absorption bands, while the maximum monostatic RCS reduction is 23 dB at 2.3 GHz and 20 dB at 8.1 GHz. The integration of the FSR does not affect other important parameters like the radiation of the patch antenna since the insertion loss is very low and on the order 0.6 dB at the transmission band. In addition, the realized gain of the primary patch antenna increases from 7.6 dBi to 11.2 dBi at the transmission frequency of the FSR, mainly due to the reflection characteristics of the bottom FSR layer which acts as a frequency selective surface (FSS) forming the fabry-perot cavity.

articleTitle: Differentially-Fed Large Frequency Ratio Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a large frequency ratio grid antenna with differential feeds. The antenna can simultaneously operate in both microwave and millimeter-wave frequency bands by gridding a single circular metal patch. To achieve low cross-polarization, a pair of L-probes and two coaxial-to-waveguide adaptors are used to excite the antenna differentially at low and high frequencies, respectively. The antenna exhibits broadband impedance matching of better than −10 dB in the frequency bands of 3.01-3.99 GHz (28.0%) and 26.85-29.25 GHz (8.55%). Within the operating bands, the low- and high-frequency gains peak at 6.20 dBi and 9.86 dBi, respectively.

articleTitle: Wireless Deployable Fresnel Rings Signal Booster
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Even with 5G technology to bolster the ability of cellphones to receive signals, there are still locations throughout the world where connectivity remains an issue. To solve this vexing issue, developers at ORC Tech obtained an exclusive license from NASA Johnson Space Center and are adapting technology originally designed for lunar missions to improve cell coverage for people on Earth. The antenna booster consists of a conductive material woven into fabric, making it lightweight and easy to fold for quick storage. When a user encounters a dead area, they just pop open the booster near their cellphone to provide one or two bars (e.g., −109 to −100 dBm up to −99 to −90 dBm) of additional signal strength. In this work we describe the overall technology and will present design challenges, material choices as well as measurement results.

articleTitle: Improved PNN-MLP Model for Estimating the Penetration Depth of EM Waves in Soils
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The improved PNN-MLP neural model is proposed for fast estimating EM field penetration depth in soils based on soil composition (clay, silt, and sand percentages), soil moisture content and EM wave frequency. The model consists of PNN networks, which determine the type of soil; an MLP activation module, which determines which MLP networks are activated based on the evaluation of the type of soil sample; MLP networks, which determine the real and imaginary components of the soil relative permittivity based on the soil moisture content and frequency; and the functional module, which estimates the penetration depth of EM waves based on the values of the relative permittivity and frequency. The model's accuracy is demonstrated by comparing the estimated penetration depth of EM waves in three different soil types with the measured results.

articleTitle: Ultra-wideband TEM Horn Antenna Using Ridge Gap Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this article, a TEM horn antenna is presented as an ultra-wideband (UWB) antenna, which uses ridge gap waveguide technology (RGW) in the initial waveguide feed part of the antenna. The simulation results show that the return loss of the proposed antenna is better than -10 dB in the range of 1.75 to 40 GHz, and the gain of the antenna is between 8.5-16.5 dBi. Also, the maximum side lobe level (SLL) of the antenna in E and H-planes are -13 dB and -8 dB, respectively.

articleTitle: A Multi-Band Efficient Metamaterial Absorber for Millimeter-Wave Band WBAN Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper introduces a highly effective, multi-layered metamaterial-based absorber that operates across numerous millimeter-wave bands for wireless body area network applications. The absorber was created from a single unit cell that was transformed into a metasurface array. The introduction of metallic vias results in the creation of multiple frequency bands and maximum absorption. The metamaterial exhibits double-negative material properties and has maximum absorption rates of 0.98, 0.99, and 0.94 at 28 GHz, 36.64 GHz, and 39 GHz, respectively.

articleTitle: Evaluation and Mitigation of Multipath Propagation in RIS-Enabled Channels
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The popular view of Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface (RIS)-enabled links is that the transmitted signal reaches the receiver after a single bounce off the RIS. However, RISs can act as diffuse scatterers due to their side lobes, leading to unintended multipath propagation effects. We present a systematic evaluation of these effects by simulating RISs with Chebyshev patterns of equal and controllable side lobe levels. Hence, we determine the required side lobe level of an RIS in a specific channel geometry, to ensure that the operation of the link is not compromised by multipath effects in the environment.

articleTitle: Change in Radiation Parameters from Microstrip Antenna Finite Ground Plane Area Variation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In depth, qualitative investigation into the finite ground plane effect is further conducted to include E-plane analysis for the first time and examination of the impact on expanded radiation parameters. In this includes parameters such as gain and polarization with respect to the changing finite ground plane size. This paper presents, for the first time to the best of the authors' investigative knowledge, a comprehensive investigation on the radiation parameters of a rectangular microstrip patch antenna that accounts quantitatively for the finite ground plane effects.

articleTitle: Double Bevel-Cut Vlasov-Type Antenna with Reflectors for High Power Microwave Pulse Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A novel Vlasov-type antenna based on a circular waveguide with a double bevel-cut and two symmetrical side reflectors is presented. Simulation results for the proposed antenna at the operating frequency of 2.5 GHz, carried out by CST Studio suite 2023, show a higher gain with a wider emission angle if compared to classic Vlasov geometries. A sensitivity analysis in terms of different angle and length of the reflectors and a comparison with other Vlasov-type configurations have been carried out and are here reported. The results confirm the promising performance of the novel proposed Vlasov antenna and pave the way for High-Power Microwave (HPM) applications.

articleTitle: Investigation of the Polarization of Wide Band Rectangular Patch Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Wideband rectangular patch antenna has been introduced by feeding the antenna at special position. This makes the design very simple and cost effective for future mobile communication systems. Although a detail analysis has been done, the polarization of the antenna has not been investigated. Here, the polarization of the antenna has been investigated for one of the upcoming 6<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> generation mobile communication system frequencies around 7 GHz. Here, I show how the wide band antenna can be achieved and its polarization characteristics with different methods.

articleTitle: An Aperture Coupled Frequency-Polarization Reconfigurable Patch Antenna Based on Tuning Channelized Liquid Metal
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a polarization and frequency reconfigurable patch antenna utilizing liquid metal (LM) and aperture-coupled technique is presented. The antenna comprises six layers: a circular patch, a foam layer, two Rogers TMM4 substrates, a T-shaped feed line, and a ground plane with multiple aperture-coupled slots. Polarization configuration is achieved by filling the microftuidic channels with liquid metal plugs to modify the T-shaped feed line structure. Frequency reconfiguration is implemented by filling slots on the ground plane, preserving different aperture-coupled channels. By adjusting the structure of feed line and ground plane, seven polarizations and two frequency reconstructions can be attained at the current stage.

articleTitle: Dual-Polarised Digital Phased Array Antenna for Millimeter-Wave Beam Steering Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A dual-polarised millimeter-wave antenna array and digital feeding architecture is reported for 24 GHz operation. This antenna system achieves full element digitisation and external analog feeding circuits are employed to reduce digital hardware costs. The synchronized digital feeding comprises a bank of universal software defined radios for beam-steering as demonstrated at 24 GHz. In addition, by differential feeding and designing the array using substrate integrated waveguide technology, low port coupling and reduced cross-polarisation levels are achieved.

articleTitle: Antenna Mode Scattering Field Suppression Method Based on the Load-Only Adjusting
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A novel antenna mode scattering field (AMSF) suppression method based on the load-only adjusting is proposed in this paper. By dividing the total scattering field (TSF) of the antenna element with open-circuit load and short-circuit load, the field characteristic of “same magnitude, opposite phase” is found between the AMSF with open-circuit load and shortcircuit load. The AMSF suppression is achieved by periodic loading the open-circuit load and the short-circuit load at the end of each element in the antenna array. An 8x8 Vivaldi antenna array is designed to verify this method, and over a 10 dB average antenna mode RCS reduction is achieved in 6-14 GHz.

articleTitle: Practical mmWave UE Performance in RIS-Assisted Wireless Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper investigates the incorporation of Reflective Intelligent Surfaces (RIS) into mm Wave wireless networks for enhancing user equipment (UE) performance. Specifically, it delves into the previously unexplored effect of user interaction with a steerable handheld mm-wave device on system bit rate performance in the presence of RIS, especially in non-line-of-sight conditions and when obstructed by a user's hand. The results emphasize the capacity of RIS to enhance both spectral efficiency and link reliability, contingent on the UE antenna array steering its beam towards the base stations or the RIS. Moreover, the investigation highlights the importance of practical UE for realistic network insights, crucial for effective optimization efforts.

articleTitle: MIMO Assembly of a Meandered-line Antenna for 6G and Beyond Indoor Wireless Frontends
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a 4-element wideband MIMO (multiple-input-multiple-output) antenna operating at 20 GHz and covering a portion of the Ka-band. The use of a slotted ground structure enabled an impedance bandwidth of 16.8 GHz in the range of 19-35.8 GHz with a peak gain of 8 dBi. The mutual coupling effects were reduced by placing the antennas orthogonal to one another. Envelope correlation coefficients well below 0.005 were achieved making the antenna a good candidate for 6G and beyond indoor wireless systems.

articleTitle: A Polarization Insensitive and Angularly Stable Reconfigurable Unit Cell for Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A tunable unit cell is the building block of Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RIS). By controlling the reflection properties of individual unit cells, the propagation of the reflected electromagnetic (EM) wave can be manipulated in a programmable way. In this paper a new reconfigurable unit cell for RIS applications is proposed. The unit cell uses PIN diodes to switch between two reflection states which has a phase difference close to 180° over the frequency range of 7.25 to 8.5 GHz. The design is polarization insensitive, and the reflection responses are stable for oblique incidence of angle up to 45° for both TE and TM modes.

articleTitle: Ultra-Wideband Low-cost Light-weight 3D-Printed Dielectric Rod Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a microstrip-line-excited ultra-wideband dielectric rod antenna manufactured using 3D printing technology. The design adopts a three-stage transition structure from the microstrip line to a 3D parallel lines, to the dielectric rod, and then to free space. Thanks to the flexibility of the 3D printing structure, ultra-wideband impedance matching and gain bandwidth is achieved within a very short transition length (About 1.1λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">min</inf>, Amin is the wavelength at the minimum operating frequency). Compared to traditional waveguide-fed structures, the use of bulky metal structures and complex manufacturing process can be avoided. To verify the proposed design conecpt, the antenna was fabricated and tested. Test results show that the impedance bandwidth covers 6–16 GHz, with gain variation less than 3.5dB within this range, a peak gain of 13.3 dBi, and an efficiency greater than 60%. The overall dimensions of the antenna are 0.3λ×0.8λ×2.6λ @6GHz, with a weight of approximately 42g (excluding connectors). It has the advantages of low-cost, small size, and light-weight, making it very suitable for applications in ultra-wideband devices with small form factors.

articleTitle: A Celebration of Professor Constantine Balanis' Enduring Legacy and Profound Impact
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we celebrate the enduring legacy and profound impact that Prof. Balanis has had on the development of scientists and engineers in the fields of electromagnetics and antennas around the world. Specifically, we provide a review of the graduate students, who were mentored by Dr. Balanis as a major advisor and highlight the impact that his mentoring has had on their scientific training and professional careers. Also, Prof. Georgakopoulos provides, through his own professional journey, a personal glimpse of Prof. Balanis' impact as a mentor and an educator.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Wideband and Wide-Scanning Phased Array Antenna with Unconventional Array of Array Architecture for 6G Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A wideband and wide-scanning phased array antenna operating from 66 GHz to 76 GHz with the unconventional array of array (AoA) architecture is presented in this paper. To meet the requirement of the high-density integration for the sixth-generation (6G) communication systems, the three-dimensional stacked phased array is adopted at first. Then, the unit cells are classified into different categories, including active elements, inactive elements, displaced elements, and clustered elements. It is like making a rearranged array of the phased array, which can be named AoA. It integrates fewer transmit/receive (Tx/Rx) channels, reducing the integration and thermal management challenges. Next, for achieving wideband performance, the multipoint grounded magnetoelectric dipole with the slot-coupled feedline and meta-surface is designed as the antenna element. Finally, a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{16} \times \mathbf{16}$</tex> array prototype is designed, fabricated, and measured to verify the correctness of the theory and simulation. Without breaking the engineering feasibility, it achieves 79.63% Tx/Rx channel reduction and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm \mathbf{60}^{\circ}$</tex> beam coverage.

articleTitle: A Passive MIMO Channel Measurement Platform based on 5G Downlink Reference Signal
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: With the advancement of high-speed railways (HSR), an accurate channel model is crucial for designing and evaluating HSR wireless systems. This paper designs a passive Multiple Input Multiple Output (MIMO) channel measurement platform based on Software Defined Radio (SDR). The platform utilizes Channel State Information-Reference Signal(CSI-RS) to perform channel measurement. The platform's accuracy is subsequently validated against the standard channel model.

articleTitle: Inverse Design of Multi-Wavelength Phase-Controlled Single-Mode Waveguide by TR-PCA Method and Topology Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, the inverse design of a multi-wavelength phase-controlled single-mode waveguide is proposed using the TR-PCA method to obtain initial structure and open-source code SPINS-B to perform topology optimization. The results show that the target transmission performance and phase control are realized successfully.

articleTitle: Bioradar Signal-to-Noise Ratio Enhancement Using 3D-Printed Dielectric Lens Antennas at 5.8 GHz
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The bioradar is a system that measures vital signs using the micro-Doppler effect, presenting a non-contact acquisition method that is less invasive than typical sensors used for monitoring. This paper aims to improve this system using dielectric lens antennas to increase the directivity, reduce side-lobe level, and narrow the half-power beamwidth. Thus, 3-D printed low-cost antennas were manufactured and tested on two subjects, comparing the received signal with the one measured using the Biopac Student Lab system serving as a reference. The results show that the antennas successfully measured breathing patterns up to 3 m of distance, exhibiting superior range, and enhanced signal quality. This solution offers cost-effectiveness and greater flexibility of implementation when compared to state-of-the-art antennas designed for the same application.

articleTitle: A High-Isolation and Broadband Antenna for in-Band Full-Duplex Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper innovatively presents a high-isolation and broadband dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) using a shared radiator for in-band full-duplex (IBFD) applications. By adjusting the dimensions and shape of the dielectric resonator antenna, the two ports of the antenna operate in TE311 and TE131 modes, respectively. Additionally, the observed electric field distribution indicates that the electric field excited by the two ports is mutually orthogonal. Therefore, a decoupling performance is obtained without introducing any additional structures. Simulation results show that the overlapped impedance bandwidth of the two ports reaches up to 20.7<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> (23.3 GHz–28.7 GHz), and the isolation achieves better than 43dB within the entire operating bandwidth. Due to the simple architecture and outstanding performance, the proposed antenna is promising for IBFD applications.

articleTitle: Perfect All-Angle Spatial Differentiators via Asymmetric Grazing-Angle Huygens' Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: We present a perfect all-angle spatially deriving metasurface, overcoming numerical aperture and accuracy limitations of previous devices. While these were designed mainly via qualitative symmetry breaking and heuristic optimizations, we derive exact closed-form susceptibility conditions, highlighting the grazing-angle Huygens' condition as a crucial aspect of this functionality. We tailor proper physical inclusions, based on rigorous electromagnetic specifications beyond symmetry breaking, to validate this concept in simulation. Our excellent results herald a sound paradigm to engineer not only analog computers, but a myriad of novel nonlocal microwave and optical devices.

articleTitle: Data Dense Chipless RFID Tag for Multi-Parameter Sensing Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The research presents a data dense passive chipless RFID Tag for multi-parameter sensing applications as a low-cost solution. The proposed circular tag is designed via approach of dual sided slot embedding. The tag yields 20-bit RCS response while staying in 20mm x 20mm dimensions. The data capacity has been amazingly enhanced compared to previous work. Taconic CER-10-0500 has been used as substrate, whereas copper is deployed as resonator structure on both sides of the substrate. The top layer of the tag yields 14-bits, whereas 6-bits are result of the slots etched at the back side of the tag. The increased data capacity makes the tag suitable for low-cost identification as well as multi-parameter sensing. The battery-free resonator-based highly durable tag is most suitable for multi-parameter analysis in wireless and IoT networks.

articleTitle: Scattering-based Image Encryption
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A scattering-based approach is developed for the encrypted storage and subsequent physically secure retrieval of an object or image. A complex reconfigurable micromedium is used in the field recording stage in order to ensure that subsequent retrieval of the object or image cannot be achieved without involvement of the same micromedium in the associated image retrieval phase. Fundamental limits pertinent to imaging in nonhomogeneous media are discussed which shed insight on the required micromedium characteristics.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Impact of Shipborne HFSWR Platform Motion on Doppler Spectrum
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Compared to shore-based High-frequency Frequency Surface Wave Radar (HFSWR), shipborne HFSWR exhibits superior flexibility. However, the forward movement and six-degree-of-freedom motion of the shipborne platform cause changes in the Doppler frequency of the received ship target echo, thereby affecting target detection. To compensate for platform motion and reduce its impact on ship target detection, we theoretically analyze the effects of various six-degree-of-freedom motions from the perspective of Doppler frequency analysis. Firstly, we establish the motion model of the platform. Then, we use these models to simulate the 6 degrees of freedom motion of the platform. Finally, based on the model, the Doppler spectra of ship targets under different platform movements were analyzed. The results showed that the platform movement has a significant impact on the Doppler spectra, leading to changes in the characteristics of the ship target echo.

articleTitle: Scalable Active Metamaterial Cell with Integrated Gain, Compensation and Power
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: We report on a stand-alone, battery-powered active meta-material gain stage with integrated gain and self-coupling compensation. This meta-material stage does not require any external connection or power, enabling to be used to scale active metamaterials to large and complex arrays without the need for external power, connection, and gain or compensation.

articleTitle: Modeling of Generalized Space-Time Modulation-Engineered (GSTEM) Metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Over the past few years, our group has been exploring the emerging area of Generalized Space-Time Engineered-Modulation (GSTEM) metamaterials. This area involves novel concepts and physics that pose new mathematical modeling questions. The present paper briefly answers some of these questions, while the conference presentation will examine a few of them in details.

articleTitle: On Operator Filtering for Integral Equations: The High-Order Case
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this work, we extend the standard quasi-Helmholtz filters to high-order discretizations in the context of the boundary element method. This generalization allows preconditioning integral equations such as the electric field integral equation (EFIE) in the h-refinement regime while preserving the accuracy gain of high-order discretizations. The theoretical framework will be corroborated by numerical results that validate the effectiveness of the proposed strategy when stabilizing the refinement-dependent spectral behavior of the high-order discretized EFIE.

articleTitle: The Contributions of W. Ross Stone to the IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: W. Ross Stone, Ph.D. was a major contributor in the development of the IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society. He served both the Society and the IEEE as a whole in many capacities, including positions concerning symposia and society administration, but his contributions in the area of publications are perhaps the most significant and the ones that continue to influence the Society and the Institute today.

articleTitle: The Design of Programmable Metasurface for Duplexing Communications with Different-Frequency and Different-Polarization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The develop of the Low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite communication has attracted much more attention in recent years. The design of programmable metasurface for duplexing communications is proposed in this work. The texture of two stacked microstrip patches for achieving uplink and downlink under different-frequency and different-polarization is applied, and the programmable phase shifter composed of four varactors for each patch is located on the back side of the unit cell with considering the easy integration. The unit cell has been verified in our field-circuit co-simulations, and the results that the transmission phase adjusted from 0 ° to 360 ° with a corresponding variation of transmission amplitude of approximately 1.2 dB in the frequency range of 12.25GHz-12.75GHz under horizontal polarization, and the transmission phase adjusted from 0 ° to 360 ° with a corresponding variation of transmission amplitude of approximately 1 dB in the frequency range of 14GHz-14.5GHz under vertical polarization has been realized.

articleTitle: A Multi-Functional Buoy Antenna System for Maritime Ad-Hoc Networks in UHF/BDS/GPS Frequency Bands
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A multi-functional buoy antenna system engineering encapsulation model designed for maritime wireless ad-hoc networks is presented. The antenna consists of a dual-frequency circularly polarized microstrip antenna and a Planar Inverted-F Antenna (PIFA), achieving efficient spatial reuse through rational structural design. Simulation results demonstrate that, in the UHF frequency band, the antenna achieves quasi-isotropic radiation, while exhibiting excellent right-hand circular polarization radiation (RHCP) characteristics in the GPS and BDS frequency bands. The advantages of this multi-functional buoy antenna system lie in its compact dimensions, light weight, and high reliability, making it suitable for a wide range of applications in maritime wireless ad-hoc networks.

articleTitle: A Directional Power Monitoring and Control Feature for EMF Product Compliance of Base Stations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: International standards specify radio frequency exposure evaluation methods to assess compliance of base stations implementing massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) and beamforming techniques. The usage of power reduction factors (PRF) has been introduced to consider the dynamic changes of the antenna pattern, resulting in a time-averaged equivalent isotropically radiated power (EIRP) in any direction of several dB below the instantaneous maximum. In some national regulations, the usage of PRF is subject to the implementation of monitoring and/or control features of the time-averaged transmitted power or EIRP of the base station. In this work, the operation, implementation, and in-situ validation of such a feature is briefly presented. The findings are of interest to regulators, mobile communication service providers, and standardization bodies seeking information on practical implementations of the actual maximum approach described in IEC 62232 Ed3.

articleTitle: Single Layer Hemispheric Frequency Selective Surface for X-Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: An X-Band conformal hemispheric frequency selective surface (FSS) is presented for Radome applications. The proposed FSS is designed for band stop characteristics. A square ring with centered hexagonal patch is used as the unitcell. The single element of FSS with size <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{12}\mathbf{mm}\times \mathbf{12}\mathbf{mm} ( >\mathbf{0.4}\lambda$</tex> @ 10 GHz) is simulated in periodic environment of the CST Microwave studio. To achieve conformability in the FSS, Rogers RT5880 with substrate thickness of 0.508 mm is employed. A plane wave excitation is used. A complete FSS of the size <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{11}\times \mathbf{11} (\mathbf{132}\mathbf{mm} \times \mathbf{132}\mathbf{mm})$</tex> is designed for full-wave analysis. The FSS has an electrical size of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{4.4}\lambda^{2}$</tex> @ 10 GHz. The performance of FSS model is investigated in planar, conformal, and hemispheric mode. The simulated results exhibit that shielding bandwidth (BW) characteristics achieved from the planar, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{11}\times \mathbf{11}$</tex> conformal, and fully hemispheric FSS are 30 %, 10 %, and 2 % (@ 10 GHz). The smaller shielding bandwidth from conformal and fully hemispheric designs compared to planar FSS is justifiable due to non-planar environment.

articleTitle: Computing Intrinsic Cross-Polarisation Ratio (IXR) for Horizontal Crossed-Dipole Polarimeters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper discusses crossed-dipole polarimeters, providing explicit formulas for the radiated electric field from short horizontal dipoles. An alternate representation of these fields using the Ludwig II polarisation basis is discussed. The computation of IXR is outlined and results verified by comparison with published theoretical results.

articleTitle: Additive Manufacturing Exploitation for Wireless Sensing and Radio Frequency Identification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Additive manufacturing includes a vast landscape of different technologies, both 2D and 3D as well as hybrid ones, which provide great flexibility and customization to the designer. Although most of the mature applications that exploit this paradigm takes advantage of the control of mechanical properties of the fabricated objects, additive manufacturing has been recently adopted also for electromagnetic design of innovative identification and sensing devices. This work focuses on the ongoing research activities carried out at the Additive Manufacturing Crosslab of the University of Pisa as tangible proof of the great potential offered by these technologies.

articleTitle: Tunable Spoof Plasmonic Metamaterials with Dual-Band Phase Shifting Capacity
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, tunable spoof surface plasmon polaritons (SSPPs) supported by periodic PIN-diode-loaded unit cells are proposed. The dispersion relation of the proposed unit cell is first analyzed. Two regions can be categorized according to the overlapping frequency ranges in the dispersion diagram. Then, a dual-band phase-shifting functionality is predicted based on the wave vector differences of multiple modes in the overlapping frequency bands. Then, both transmission and phase characteristics are simulated for demonstration. The simulated dual operating band is observed from 3.1 to 3.4 GHz and 6.1 to 9.4 GHz, respectively. In addition, the simulated phase shifts in the corresponding frequency bands vary from 208°to 236°(Region I) and 245°to 271°(Region II)., respectively. Simulation results validate the proposed structure with a dual-band phase shifting capacity, which can enrich the practical applications of active SSPP-based metamaterials.

articleTitle: An Efficient Antenna Decoupling Optimization Method Using Variational Auto-Encoders
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A machine-learning based optimization method is proposed to optimize decoupling structures between antennas. The proposed method uses the Variational Auto-Encoders (VAE) as the main part, and the sampled latent variables of VAE are optimized to achieve decoupling design requirements. A two-element antenna decoupling structure optimization example is shown to validate the proposed method. The simulation results show that the VAE can reconstruct the decoupling structure based on the optimized latent variables, which achieve the optimization of decoupling performance with higher degrees of freedom.

articleTitle: Fast Simulation of Many-Body Rydberg Atomic Systems for Quantum Sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Quantum sensing based on Rydberg atoms is an emerging technology for electric-field measurement. Theoretical and numerical studies were generally limited by the many-body effect in atomic ensembles. In this work, we initially derived a many-body dynamic equation by incorporating the Rydberg- Rydberg interaction into the four-level optical Bloch equation. Particularly, we proposed a fast steady-state solution as an alternative to the transient one. As a result, we ingeniously replaced the computationally expensive matrix operations with a linearly iterative process, enabling rapid convergence within few steps while considering the Doppler frequency shift. This approach made it possible to simulate the interaction of 7000 atoms in less than a minute. Based on the many-body model, we investigated the phenomenon of electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) and Autler- Townes (AT) splitting under varying atomic gas densities; and compared the numerical results with experimental data. The comparison revealed a relatively-low error of 4.59% for the EITAT simulation by the many-body model. Moreover, we found that the linear dynamic range of the quantum sensing shrinks when considering the many-body interaction.

articleTitle: Sub-THz Compact On-Chip Dipole Antennas for 6G Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Two separate designs of a meandered sub-THz dipole antenna having potential for 6G application on a commercial 65 nm CMOS are presented in this article. Meandering of the antenna reduces the length of the antenna and hence the chip area. Widening the dipole arms without violating the design rule checks (DRC) of the CMOS foundry increases the impedance bandwidth.
