A 1-strip meandered on-chip dipole antenna occupies an area of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$554 \mu \mathrm{m} \times 60 \mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> resulting in 32.4 % of fractional <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S_{11}$</tex> bandwidth ranging from 83.5-115.8 GHz with a gain of -2.9 dBi at 100 GHz. A 2-strip meandered on-chip dipole results in 38.2 % of fractional <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S_{11}$</tex> bandwidth ranging from 78.2-115.2 GHz with a gain of -2.5 dBi at 100 GHz while occupying a silicon area of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$582 \mu \mathrm{m} \times 58 \mu \mathrm{m}$</tex>. The proposed on-chip dipole antennas are good candidates for 6G sub-THz communication applications.

articleTitle: Aperture Antenna Focusing Properties Within In-Homogeneous Medium
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper investigates the near-field focusing properties of a linear antenna in terms of the aperture and distance at which focus is achieved in half space.

articleTitle: Investigation of Low-Cost Scotch Tape Graphene for Sub-6GHz PCB Based 5G Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This study investigates the potential use of graphene-based materials in the design of sub-6GHz 5G antennas. Graphene is a highly conductive material known for its unique mechanical, electrical, and thermal properties, making it an ideal candidate for use in electronic devices. The study explores the use of graphene in antenna design, highlighting its flexibility and high conductivity, which can improve signal transmission and reception. The design and characterization of graphene are also discussed, with a focus on the scotch tape method for preparing graphene films. Overall, this study demonstrates the potential of graphene to improve the performance of radiating elements.

articleTitle: Achieving Anomalous Refraction with Truncated All-Dielectric Two-Element Metagratings
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Anomalous reflection and refraction are phenomena in which the respective wavefront is directed into directions that are not predicted by the conventional Snell's law. Artificial structures can be designed for this purpose, which are realized by the periodic repetition of a unit cell. In this work, an all-dielectric metagrating is designed, obtained by the alternation of two different materials and aiming to achieve anomalous refraction. The effect of a finite number of cells is explored, to establish the minimum length of the considered metagrating which can provide the desired refraction response.

articleTitle: Convolutional Neural Networks for Chipless RFID Classification in the Time-Frequency Domain
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to accurately classify chipless RFID measurements in the time-frequency domain via Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN). Magnitude and Phase data of S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> measurements, ranging in distance 50–140 cm from the emitter, are transformed to time-domain signals using the Inverse Fast Fourier Transform (IFFT). A matrix representation of the time-domain signal is then obtained using the Continuous Wavelet Transform (CWT) and used to fit a CNN model. The proposed preprocessing pipeline and the designed CNN architecture achieve up to 86.75% accuracy when used to classify 16 tags, outperforming by up to 10.63% a previously proposed scheme based on magnitude data and Logistic Regression.

articleTitle: Front-end design considerations, analyses, and prototyping for the SKA Aperture Arrays telescope
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The Square Kilometre Array Telescope working at Low Frequencies (SKA-Low, 50–350 MHz) is one of the two interferometric arrays under construction by the SKA Observatory aiming to “build and operate cutting-edge radio telescopes to transform our understanding of the Universe”, The SKA-Low telescope architecture is quite complex and consists of 512 stations. These stations are arrays, each made up of 256 dual polarized log-periodic antennas. For this reason, such complex architecture has gone through a comprehensive set of investigations, design decisions and improvements which has led to the latest updates and considerations presented in this paper, as well as results from the latest phased array prototype.

articleTitle: A Large, Seven-Faceted Reflectarray for Millimiter-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A seven-faceted reflectarray is proposed in this paper to enhance the performance of an electrically large reflectarray. The design procedure is explained, and the antenna is compared to its equivalent planar version. The antenna is optimized at 50 GHz, and is evaluated for operation in the Q-band (37.5 GHz to 42.5) and the V-band (47.2 GHz to 52.4). The results show that the seven-faceted RA achieves a quasi-constant directivity of 44 dBi in the V-band, and keeps the directivity above 40 dBi in the Q-band. In contrast, the planar RA has a main beam falling below 40 dBi across the Q-band, and has nearly the same directivity as the multi-faceted version in the V-band.

articleTitle: Quasi-Helmholtz Projectors for the Low-Frequency Stabilization of the Isogeometrically Discretized Electric Field Integral Equation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In order to low-frequency stabilize the isogeometrically discretized electric field integral equation (EFIE) based on B-splines, we derive quasi-Helmholtz projectors to form a preconditioner. To this end, we show how the projectors can be obtained efficiently for arbitrary polynomial orders of the basis functions. The approach is valid for single- and multi-patch descriptions of the geometry, which can be open or closed as well as simply or multiply connected without the need to search for global loops. Numerical results demonstrate the derived preconditioner's effectiveness in obtaining accurate scattered and radiated fields.

articleTitle: Design of Linear Array-Fed Fabry-Perot Cavity Antennas for High Gain and Low Sidelobe Level
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The design of a linear Fabry-Perot (FP) cavity antenna fed with unequally spaced subarrays is presented. The FP cavity is characterized by its dominant leaky mode and the dispersion curves based on the finite element analysis of the eigenmode problem. The superposition of the excited leaky waves is used to model the array-fed FP cavity antenna. A hybrid optimization method incorporating convex <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\ell_{1}$</tex> -norm minimization and particle swarm optimization is applied to the model to divide the source array into a minimum number of subarrays, while satisfying the radiation and source location constraints. The synthesis results yield a linear FP cavity antenna at 10 GHz with a half power beamwidth of 0.93°, aperture efficiency of 85.1%, and sidelobe level of -17.6 dB, achieved with only a single subarray.

articleTitle: Efficient Numerical Solutions of Electromagnetic Scattering by Bodies of Revolution with Composite Media
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Electromagnetic (EM) Interaction with various objects can be formulated by integral equations and volume integral equations (VIEs) are indispensable when the involved penetrable media are inhomogeneous or anisotropic. If the objects include impenetrable conducting media which can be described by surface integral equations (SIEs), then the volume-surface integral equations (VSIEs) can be formed by coupling the fields from both the penetrable and impenetrable parts. If the objects are bodies of revolution (BoRs), then the VSIEs can be reduced to two-dimensional (2D) integral equations by using a Fourier series expansion and such a case has not been addressed before. The resultant 2D equations are usually solved by the method of moments (MoM), but this paper proposes to use the Nystrom method to solve them so that its merits can be explored. The numerical example has demonstrated the performance of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Source Detection with a Dual-Beam Linear Array and Hierarchical Sweeping at n257 Band
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This contribution explores millimeter-wave communication, emphasizing beam management procedures vital for 5G advancements. It proposes a l×8 linear array of microstrip patches with hierarchical beamforming sweep jointly to dual-beam formation. Experimental tests showcase efficient source detection, demonstrating reduced steps and swift identification of simultaneous sources.

articleTitle: Path Loss Analysis for Near-Ground Mining Communication at 2.4 GHz
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper examines path loss (PL) characteristics of an underground mine's near-ground scenario at 2.4 GHz within a 200 MHz bandwidth for Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs). Measurements were performed with the transmitter (Tx) and receiver (Rx) at heights of 10 cm and 100 cm above the ground and over a Tx-Rx distance ranged from 1 m to 44 m. Utilizing the two-slope model, PL exponents were determined as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathbf{n}1,\ \mathbf{n}2)=(2.5090$</tex>, 1.6995) for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{h}=\boldsymbol{10}$</tex> cm, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathbf{n}_{1},\ \mathbf{n}_{2})=\boldsymbol{(2.0603}, 1.2199)$</tex> for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{h}=\boldsymbol{100}$</tex> cm. Shadow fading standard deviations were found <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\boldsymbol{\sigma}_{1},\ \boldsymbol{\sigma}_{2})=\boldsymbol{(2.6251}$</tex> dB, 1.7454 dB) for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{h}=\boldsymbol{10}$</tex> cm, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\boldsymbol{\sigma}_{1},\ \boldsymbol{\sigma}_{2})=\boldsymbol{(2.4533}\mathbf{dB},\ \boldsymbol{2.4632}\ \mathbf{dB})$</tex> for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{h}=\boldsymbol{100}$</tex> cm. This is the first study that report a near-ground scenario in an underground mine environment.

articleTitle: Beam Tilting Antenna Using Phase Gradient Surface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A beam-tilting antenna using ridge gap waveguide (RGW) technology is presented for X-Band applications. A phase gradient surface (PGS) is integrated with an RGW antenna that steers the radiation beam. The PGS acts as a superstrate, which helps to increase antenna gain and the phase variation surface to collimate the incident RF energy of a fully metallic RGW-based linear 8-element antenna array in the desired direction. A three-layered unitcell is designed for a phase-tuning mechanism where a size variation technique is employed. A phase-tuning surface comprising 16 × 11 periodic unitcells is designed. The proposed technique is investigated to steer from the broadside radiations into the 22° and 45° directions of the H-plane. The expected and simulated beam directions show good agreement. The proposed antenna has the potential to tilt the radiation beam within ±45° off-broadside in the H-plane.

articleTitle: Phased Array Scan Performance Review for SATCOM: Dielectric Resonator vs. Patch Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A comparison of arrays employing dielectric resonator antennas (DRA) and patch antennas as elements is presented. The bandwidth of the arrays under study is over 40% at broadside, covering the K/Ka-band SATCOM and mmWave 5G bands. The element analysis is performed for the principal planes in an infinite array environment. Numerical results suggest the scan performance of DRA phased arrays is limited by the dielectric loading of the array aperture.

articleTitle: A Novel Broadband Reflectarray Unit Cell Using Mandelbrot Fractal Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel reflectarray unit cell based on Mandelbrot fractal geometry. The unit cell is composed of two Mandelbrot fractal-shaped rings, and the center frequency is 15 GHz. This novel structure can realize a size reduction of more than 40% compared to a rectangular unit, and a linear phase shift of 627° is achieved by varying the patch size. The simulation results show that the phase curves for different frequencies in the range of 11.2 - 21.2 GHz are approximately parallel, indicating that the proposed unit cell has good bandwidth performance.

articleTitle: Pattern-Reconfigurable Antenna with Fluidically Controlled Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a fluidically controlled metasurface antenna for beam steering is presented. The proposed reconfigurable antenna system consists of three layers: a 9×9 square rings metasurface, a 3D-printed liquid channel on Polylactic Acid (PLA), and a source antenna. Beam steering within a range of -34° to +34° is effectively accomplished by filling different water channels, achieving a gain of over 9.5 dBi. The designed system operates at a frequency of 8 GHz, maintaining a - 10 dB impedance bandwidth from 7.75 GHz to 8.28 GHz. In contrast to other reconfigurable radiation pattern methods, the proposed approach offers a low profile, low cost, and compact size, making it highly suitable for radar and wireless communication applications.

articleTitle: A Novel Humidity Sensor Based on Slow-Wave Substrate Integrated Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a novel humidity sensor made of slow-wave substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) resonator has been proposed and researched in microwave applications. Microstrip polyline network has replaced the top metallic surface of SIW and a size-reduction of the effective resonant area has been achieved with reference to the conventional SIW counterpart at the same resonating frequency. The proposed humidity sensor which based on SW -SIW resonator has been experimentally demonstrated to have an effective capability for humidity detection over RH range of 30% <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim$</tex> 90<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>.

articleTitle: A K-band Dual-Polarized Phased Array Antenna for Wide-Angle Beam Scanning Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a dual-polarized wide-angle scanning phased array working in the k-band is investigated. A wide-beam antenna element is designed. The metal cavity and the metal walls are loaded on a stacked patch to increase its beamwidths. The element has half-power beamwidths (HPBWs) of 158° and 99° on the E-plane and H-plane, respectively. Based on the proposed wide-beam element, a 1 ×7 linear array is constructed within a small element spacing of 0.44 λ 0. The bandwidth of the array is 15.3% (from 17.9 GHz to 20.8 GHz). An anisotropic decoupling surface is loaded above the array to reduce couplings for both polarizations. The simulation results show that the array has good beam-scanning performance, and the maximum scanning angles are 66°/56° for x- and y- polarization. And the active VSWR remain blow 2.5. Small gain variations less than 2.40dB is observed for both polarizations.

articleTitle: Design of Metasurfaces for Beamforming with High-Efficiency Custom Polarization Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we introduce a simple method that enables the simultaneous manipulation of beamforming and polarization conversion, allowing for the generation and steering of high-directional or multiple beams with custom polarizations. The basic concept behind this breakthrough innovation is to create and explore a pair of metacells with high-efficiency orthogonal polarization responses and independent phase control under the same incidence wave. Based on the combination of these two types of metacells, the superposition of two orthogonal polarizations has been proposed to generate versatile output polarization, simply by adjusting the offset between the two polarization components. Additionally, specific beam with arbitrary polarizations can also be efficiently formed by analytical design of phase gradients.

articleTitle: FPGA Implementation of Range Migration Algorithm for Synthetic Aperture Radar Using Simulink HDL Coder
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The millimeter-wave synthetic aperture radar echo data processing is a vital step in target reconstruction, and this phase is inherently time-consuming, demanding significant computational resources. To expedite the reconstruction process, Field-Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGA) can be employed. Nevertheless, utilizing FPGA for implementation often entails grappling with complex hardware description languages such as Verilog or VHDL, which are difficult and time-consuming to develop. To overcome these challenges, a hardware architecture based on the range migration algorithm (RMA) is proposed in this paper. We utilize the Simulink HDL Coder toolbox to encapsulate the algorithm into an IP Core, subsequently verifying it on the Xilinx XC7Z020. The test results show that operating at a clock frequency of 100MHz, target reconstruction with original data of size 256×151×64 requires approximately 26.74 ms. This represents a notable acceleration, being about 7.2 times faster than CPU processing in Matlab.

articleTitle: Systematic Design Considerations for Single- and Multi-State Reflecting Meta-Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Considerations are made as to how the design procedure for reflective meta-surfaces can be systematically structured. Therefore, three design levels are introduced. The procedures within the design levels are explained and the interrelationships between the system requirements and the levels themselves are discussed. This leads to clear definitions of concepts and provides an insight into the cause and effect relationships.

articleTitle: FDM/FFF Printed Dielectric Farfield Lens Antenna Using Cyclic Olefin Copolymer Filament
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This study investigates Cyclic Olefin Copolymer (COC) as a 3D printable material for ellipsoid lens antennas. We characterized printed COC samples in the W-band and used the obtained parameters to design and print a lens antenna. To benchmark the printed lens antenna, we employ a subtractively manufactured lens antenna made of Polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE). Our results exhibit remarkable characteristics of COC for the examined frequency range and demonstrate comparable properties of the 3D printed lens to the PTFE lens, while weighing less than half as much. Therefore, this work underscores the suitability of COC for rapid prototyping of quasioptical components, showcasing its potential for innovative applications in lens antenna design and fabrication.

articleTitle: 300 GHz Stacked AFSIW LTCC Horn Array Antenna with Integrated Lenses for V2V
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper explores the design of a 220–300 GHz horn array in LTCC technology for vehicular communications. An air-filled SIW approach allows compact horn elements with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.51\lambda$</tex> spacing to avoid grating lobes. The integrated Rexolite plano-convex lenses provide additional gain and sidelobe suppression. The 4×6×2.11 mm 1×4 array has a peak gain of 17.5 dBi from 220–340 GHz, a return loss below −10dB, and cross-coupling below −18dB. At 300 GHz, the gain is 15.9 dBi with 30° × 22° HPBWs. Beam steering up to 18° is achieved with only 1.1 dB gain reduction. The design enables practical sub-THz antennas for connected vehicles.

articleTitle: Direct Antenna Multi-Modulation with Time-Modulated Arrays
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: We present a novel approach to Direct Antenna Multi-Modulation (DAMM) leveraging Time-Modulated Array (TMA) technology, employing a simplified and cost-effective feeding network equipped with 2-bit phase shifters and digitally controlled Variable Gain Amplifiers (VGAs). This technique enables direct implementation of FSK, PSK and QAM modu-lation schemes within the antenna by utilizing periodic linear-phase time-modulating waveforms. Furthermore, in contrast to conventional phased arrays equipped with high-resolution Variable Phase Shifters (VPSs), but still subject to quantized phases, the TMA can deliver Beam Steering (BS) with virtually continuous angular resolution.

articleTitle: Low Cost Circularly Polarized Ka-band Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper we present the scanning performance of circularly polarization probe-fed stacked patch antenna arrays that can operate over the entire Ka-band. The antenna technology is potentially low cost as it is compatible with silicon integration techniques. The array is suitable for millimeter-wave satellite communication links.

articleTitle: Waveform Design for Uncertainty Mitigation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Radar imaging frequently grapples with a uncertainties stemming from diverse factors, including system and imaging algorithm parameters. These uncertainties impact on the resultant image, often manifesting as distortions or shifts of the actual targets positions. Within the context of this investigation, we introduce a novel method aimed at identifying a waveform design for mitigating the impact of these uncertainties on the imaging process, thereby enhancing the overall quality and fidelity of the generated images.

articleTitle: SIW-Based Elliptical Slots Antenna with Wide ARBW for Millimeter-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a substrate-integrated waveguide (SIW) based antenna geometry aiming to achieve a wide axial ratio bandwidth (ARBW) for the n261 (27.5-28.35 GHz) band of mm-wave communication. The antenna design incorporates two perpendicular elliptical slots etched on the top layer of the SIW structure. Through meticulous adjustments in the ellipticity of the slots as well as their locations relative to the SIW cavity axis, the antenna exhibits a wideband right-handed circularly polarized (RHCP) radiation spanning from 27.2 to 28.7 GHz. The performance includes a commendable peak gain of 5.8 dBic in the broadside direction. Notably, the proposed antenna boasts a simple single-layer topology, and low cross-polarization behavior, thereby making it suitable for mm-wave applications.

articleTitle: An Improved Compact CPLWA Array in Adjacent Structure for Confined Space Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The paper presents an improved array configuration called a coaxial periodic leaky wave antenna (CPLWA) array in the adjacent structure. The design is compact in size, exhibits a gain of more than 11 dB at a broadside frequency of 9.8 GHz, and yields a sidelobe level of at least −10 dB from 8 to 12 GHz bandwidth with no open stop band attenuation(OSBA) gain reduction at the broadside frequency. The beam scanning of at least <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$35^{\circ}$</tex> is observed from 8 to 12 GHz. Because of the portable design, the antenna is highly suitable for confined space applications such as ground-penetrating borehole radar. Compared to the other fabricated structure called CPLWA in the parallel array, the simulated results are discussed with significantly reduced size and backlobe/sidelobe levels.

articleTitle: A Distributed Microwave Correlation Interferometer for Fourier Domain Imaging Using Wireless Time and Frequency Coordination
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Interferometric imaging, such as that used in radio astronomy and satellite remote sensing, relies on co-processing signals received by antenna elements with wide electrical separations, yielding samples of the spatial Fourier domain that are used for image formation. Traditionally, this has been done only in fixed systems, either on the ground or on a single platform. In this paper, we demonstrate the ability to sample the spatial Fourier domain using a distributed microwave receiving array with wireless coordination of time and frequency. We implement a two-element receiving system based on software-defined radios that co-process received signals via cross-correlation, yielding samples of the spatial Fourier domain. We measure the complex interference pattern at 2.3 GHz and 3.3 GHz, representing baselines of 7λ and lOλ, respectively. The results demonstrate the feasibility of distributed Fourier domain sampling, a fundamental building block for distributed Fourier-domain imaging.

articleTitle: Two-Stage X-Band Waveguide Polarizer by 3D Printing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper describes a novel two-stage cascaded waveguide polarizer that operates over the full 7.2 – 8.6 GHz SATCOM X band. The polarizer comprises a half-wave polarizer and a quarter-wave polarizer. Following optical achromatic theory, the cascaded rotated polarizers achieve broadband operation. The waveguides are manufactured by 3D printing technology, significantly reducing manufacturing costs and time. Both simulation and measurement demonstrate good results with an axial ratio (AR) of less than 1.7 dB within the operating frequency band and 17% bandwidth. The proposed polarizer provides an excellent solution for X-band satellite communications and the design can be easily extended to multi-stage structures for wider bandwidth.

articleTitle: Analysis of GRIN Lens Antennas through the Lax-Friedrichs Sweeping Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The analysis of Graded-Index (GRIN) lenses involves employing ray tracing algorithms, which address the Eikonal equation to determine phase distribution. Subsequently, the transport equation is solved to retrieve the amplitude. In this paper, we introduce a novel analysis approach based on a numerical technique known as the Lax-Friedrichs Sweeping Method. The concept revolves around utilizing a rapid numerical algorithm that enables the efficient retrieval of both phase and amplitude within a 2D or 3D domain in less time compared to traditional ray tracing algorithms. The implementation of this algorithm is presented herein, along with an analysis of an inhomogeneous lenses, aiming to validate the efficacy of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Circularly Polarized Dual Band Fractal Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper examines the possibility for the design of a market-oriented antenna with circular polarization. The advantages of the suggested structure are cost-efficiency and production simplicity compared to traditional thick, high-epsilon antennas. The contemplated antenna could potentially be integrated into dual-band Wi-Fi antennas.

articleTitle: Multi-Trace Single Source Equations free from PEC Resonances
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This contribution introduces a multi-trace, single source formulation for the scattering of time harmonic electromagnetic waves on composite structure, that does not suffer from resonance in the PEC regions. General single source formulation are well conditioned, but do suffer from internal resonances. By the introduction of lossy ansatz in the interior of the PEC, those resonance can be suppress.

articleTitle: Software Defined Metasurface with Wireless Controlled Unit-cells for Space Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This study investigates the potential application of Software Defined Metasurfaces (SDMs) in satellite technology, emphasizing their capacity for dynamic operational adjustments. SDMs, through a wireless mesh network, enable modification of resonant frequency and beam generation in response to communication requirements. This system's adaptability to frequency shifts, such as the transition from 5G to 6G, is facilitated by Over the Air (OTA) software updates, presenting a cost-effective solution for satellite communication challenges. Additionally, the research explores the deployment of unit cells across a satellite's surface, enhancing aperture efficiency. The incorporation of Software-Defined Radio (SDR) transmitters within each unit cell forms an autonomous network, capable of independent phase and amplitude modulation of incoming signals. This advancement represents a significant contribution to the development of responsive and adaptable satellite communication systems.

articleTitle: Wide-Band mmWave Rotman Lens-AVA for Beamforming Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a 28 GHz wideband Rotman lens (RL) with Antipodal Vivaldi Antennas (AVA) is designed. It features 5 input and 5 output ports, 4 dummy ports, and offers a ±35° beam scanning capability. A new corrugated AVA with improved gain and bandwidth is designed. It achieves over 10 dBi gain across a 10 GHz bandwidth, with maximum gain at 15.7 dBi. Applications include automotive radar and vital signs monitoring.

articleTitle: Design for High Gain of Slotted Waveguide Array RADAR Antenna Combined with Grid Cavity
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A design for high gain realization of a slotted waveguide array antenna combined with a grid cavity for a sea wave monitoring RADAR system was proposed in this paper. The grid cavity on the radiating antenna plays in role to suppress the sidelobe level and to increase the antenna gain. A bandwidth of 2.8% or more based on the - 10 dB reflection coefficients was observed by measurement. Due to the grid cavity, the first sidelobe level was improved by approximately 2 dB. Proposed antenna gain was observed at approximately 30.5 dBi in measurement, which improved 1 dBi compared with the without grid cavity slotted waveguide array antenna.

articleTitle: Sidewall-Integrated Ultra-Wideband ME-Dipole Phased Array for Millimeter-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A sidewall-integrated ultra-wideband ME-dipole antenna array is presented. The antenna array radiation structure is composed of an open-ended substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) and a pair of electric dipoles which are successfully integrated into the PCB edge through a sidewall metallization process. A direct feeding mechanism based on SIW open-ended structure is developed. The integrated feeding approach offers a straightforward yet efficient method of realizing impedance matching over a wideband. The antenna demonstrates outstanding performance with a bandwidth of 94.7% and stable radiation characteristics. Furthermore, by eliminating the scanning blindness, wide scanning angles of ±65° at 30GHz, ±50° at 40 GHz, and ±40° at 50GHz can be achieved, respectively. The measured results exhibit a high degree of consistency with the simulated ones.

articleTitle: A Take-Home Teaching Laboratory for Applied Electromagnetics Courses
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In the past several years the methodology employed to teach applied electromagnetics (E&M) to the Electrical Engineering (EE) students of the University of Southern California (USC) has been revisited. As part of this effort a Take-Home Applied E&M Teaching Laboratory has been developed and is currently successfully being used in the EE curriculum. This article partially discusses this effort, with focus on the developed Take-Home Applied E&M Teaching Laboratory. The various laboratory experiments are also briefly summarized.

articleTitle: Investigations of Electromagnetic Vision at WiFi Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The visual human perception of electromagnetic waves is limited to the so-called visible spectrum. Artificial extension of the human vision, e.g., via infrared cameras, is possible. Due to the expected low resolution at large wavelengths, however, this is rarely done in the low GHz regime. We investigate the quality of images obtained by simply turning a directive antenna across a scene. The procedure is straight forward and can be compared to how the lens in the human eye creates an image on the retina. Simulation data of an exemplary domestic indoor scenario illustrates how mono-frequency vision of WiFi signals might look like.

articleTitle: Swarm-Based Antenna Array Synthesis Through Spin-Based Bifurcation Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Swarm-based antenna arrays offer a promising paradigm for 6G non-terrestrial wireless networks. This paper introduces an efficient antenna synthesis methodology tailored for complex swarm antenna arrays. In our approach, the antenna excitation coefficients are represented by spin variables through binary encoding, while the desired radiated profile is transformed into the ground state of an Ising Hamiltonian function. A novel simulated bifurcation algorithm is employed to rapidly find the optimal antenna excitation coefficients. The performance of the proposed work is demonstrated across various array synthesis and optimization scenarios.

articleTitle: Interleaved Radiating Elements
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In pulsed radar the receiver or receivers (generally there are several receiving channels) must be isolated during the transmission phase. This isolation is achieved by the use of circulators or TIR switches. In the case of an electronic scanning antenna, formed by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex> radiating elements, there will be <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex> circulators or N TIR switches. This note considers a different architecture equally capable of guaranteeing good isolation between the transmitting and receiving sections.

articleTitle: First 3D Results Obtained by a New Born-Approximation Methodology for Media in Motion with Stationary Boundaries
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we present the first results of a previously developed methodology for the solution of three-dimensional electromagnetic scattering problem. The methodology is based on Born approximations for the reliable calculation of the effects of media in motion with stationary boundaries. It places no practical limitations on the values of the velocities of the media. The methodology is applied by using traditional finite element simulators to solve problems of electromagnetic scattering by circular cylinders moving in the axial direction. The obtained results show good agreement with the analytical solutions and are much better than those obtained with traditional techniques.

articleTitle: An Efficient Method for Fast Computations of Scattering Fields in 4-D Antenna Arrays
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A fast computation approach for the scattering fields of four-dimensional (4-D) antenna arrays based on the generalized scattering matrix theory is presented. The instantaneous scattering fields of arrays connected with the time-varying feeding network are deduced and the corresponding frequency-domain scattering fields can be obtained according to Fourier transform. A 16-element E-shape microstrip array is simulated, and the scattering fields at different sideband frequencies are computed based on the proposed approach. Numerical results indicate that the proposed approach is capable of preserving computation accuracy and saving much simulation time as compared to the full-wave simulation approach.

articleTitle: Adaptations of Computational-Intensive Methods for Real Time Vital Sign Detection using FMCW Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Non-contact vital sign monitoring is crucial for minimizing patient interference. This paper introduces an optimized signal processing method for real-time heart rate extraction based on an envelope analysis using an FMCW radar designed for vital sign monitoring. To enhance real-time processing, the proposed method adapts computational-intensive signal processing steps. A Hilbert transform is replaced by a Moving-Rms(Root Mean Square) calculation, and the Fastsmooth function is substituted with a Moving Average Filter. Validation against ECG data (GE Healthcare CARESCAPE Monitor B650) confirms the effectiveness of the adapted methods. Tailored for the 24 GHz ISM band, the signal processing leverages advanced envelope analysis with computational optimizations for enhanced real-time implementation.

articleTitle: Wideband Aperture-Coupled Stacked-Patch Antenna for Scalable Fabrication
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents an aperture-coupled stacked microstrip patch antenna with a very wide bandwidth, suitable for a variety of applications. The dual-resonance antenna oper-ates in S-band with a center frequency of 3.1 GHz. The design achieves a 51% fractional bandwidth for VSWR less than 2.5, operating between 2.27 GHz and 3.84 GHz, with peak realized gain simulated to be 6.5 dBi. Four phase-shifted microstrip feed lines enable circular polarization, with the antenna maintaining a boresight axial ratio of less than 1 dB over the operating band. As an aperture-coupled design, the antenna presents both a wide bandwidth and simplicity in fabrication.

articleTitle: The Integrated Design of RF Front-End Filter and Limiter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Nowadays, the advancement of strong electromagnetic weaponry is becoming increasingly sophisticated, leading to a growing interest in electromagnetic protection technology. In the front end of RF circuits, it is crucial to select an appropriate input signal through frequency selection and amplitude limiting processes to ensure the normal functioning of subsequent circuits. Typically, a filter and a limiter are utilized for achieving these objectives. This paper proposes an integrated design of limiter and filter based on a comb filter design scheme. The simulation results show that in the range of 7GHz-8GHz, the band-pass filtering characteristic under small signal is realized, the insertion loss is less than 2dB, the shielding characteristic under high power is realized, and the shielding efficiency in the passband is greater than 13dB. The nonlinear curve demonstrates that with the increase of input power, the change of shielding efficiency increases slowly and then rapidly, which ensures the communication quality, improves the burn-resistant capability of the filter, and protects the normal operation of the subsequent circuit.

articleTitle: Scaling Power and Efficiency of Direct Antenna Modulation Transmitters using Gallium Nitride Transistors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Energy synchronous (ES) modulation techniques such as direct antenna modulation (DAM) show great promise in improving the ability to transmit wideband signals using narrowband antennas. However, high voltages generated during energy synchronous switching of high Q antennas can limit the power handling of ES-DAM systems. In this work we experimentally compare the performance system using silicon DAM and one using Gallium Nitride (GaN) FETs as the primary mechanism for energy control. Benchtop lab measurements of a DAM transmitter using an antenna equivalent circuit (AEC) of an electrically small <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\lambda/12)$</tex> 1-meter monopole demonstrate a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2\mathrm{x}$</tex> improvement in efficiency at low input RF powers (-20dBm to 5dBm), and a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$5\mathrm{x}$</tex> improvement in efficiency between 5dBm and 20dBm of RF input power, when compared to a silicon FET.

articleTitle: Circularly Polarized Metasurface Superstrate Slot Antenna Array Fed by PRGW
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: We present a wideband circularly-polarized 2-by-2 slot antenna array for X-band applications. The feeding network of the antenna is designed using printed ridge gap waveguide (PRGW) technology as a magnetic ground to suppress surface wave propagation and excite a quasi- TEM wave in the air along the ridge. Then, a single layer linear-to-circular polarization converter metasurface is designed and placed on top of the slot antenna array. The unit-cell of the converter contains two identical metallic layers with a combination of a connected Jerusalem cross (JC) and two parasitically coupled LC resonators. The antenna has a compact structure with a low profile, a −10-dB impedance bandwidth of 26% from 8.6 to 11.2 GHz, a 3-dB axial ratio bandwidth of 14% from 9.3 to 10.7 GHz, and an average gain of 13 dBi.

articleTitle: Wideband Design of a Compact Square Dielectric Resonator Antenna for Improved Radiation Features
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a compact and wideband antenna design using metallic perturbation and features cross-polar reduction. As a result of metallic perturbation and insertion of an RT-Duroid substrate, the design has a low Q-factor, which enhances bandwidth significantly. By using symmetrical slots as the defected ground structure, cross-polarized (XP) radiation is significantly reduced. The impedance bandwidth (2.7-5.3 GHz) is approximately 64% when the XP level is kept below -18 dB.

articleTitle: Scalability Analysis of Reflective Intelligent Surfaces at THz Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper introduces a straightforward method for estimating the gain in Terahertz frequency of a full-scale Reflective Intelligent Surface (RIS) model. The approach utilizes the equivalent circuit methodology combined with transmission line theory, specifically focusing on one of the employed unit cells. We outline a detailed process for deriving the equivalent circuit of the unit cell. By applying array theory principles, the paper demonstrates how to predict the maximum gain as a function of frequency. Additionally, the model incorporates various parameters that influence the overall gain, such as quantization levels, efficiency, and transmission line losses, providing a comprehensive understanding of the factors affecting RIS performance.

articleTitle: Optimal Operating Modes of Rotating Mechanical Antennas in Sea/Air Cross-Domain Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, an optimal mechanical antenna operating mode is proposed based on extreme-low frequency cross-domain communication. Firstly, the mechanical antenna equivalent model is analyzed to determine the operating mode of the mechanical antenna in sea/air cross-domain communication. Then the electromagnetic field of the rotating mechanical antenna in different operating modes in sea/air trans-domain communication is investigated, and the horizontal permanent magnet mechanical antenna is identified as the optimal operating mode of the mechanical antenna. This research provides support for mechanical antennas for extreme-low frequency communication in various application scenarios.

articleTitle: Single-Feed Multibeam 3D-Printed Dielectric Reflectarray Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: 3D-Printed reflectarray antennas consisting of a flat dielectric layer with spatial variation of dielectric constant are proposed for multibeam operation. State-of-the-art additive manufacturing is used to tailor the dielectric constant of the reflectarray unit-cells by creating gyroid unit-cells that effectively create the desired dielectric constant. Two K-band prime-focus fed reflectarrays are demonstrated. The reference design creates a boresight beam. The second design creates four beams at 30° elevation and with azimuthal symmetry. The complete design process is outlined, and single-beam and quad-beam reflectarrays with good radiation characteristics are demonstrated.

articleTitle: Equivalent Circuit for Receiving Lossy Dipole Antennas Using the Poynting Streamline Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The characteristics of the receiving antenna can be analyzed by the Thévenin equivalent circuit, but this equivalent circuit has limitations in determining the loss and scattered powers for a lossy antenna when the antenna is close to a very large load impedance. In this paper, the Poynting streamline method is used to directly model the antenna as a receiver where the flow of the field energy around the antenna can be represented by generating streamlines of Poynting vector field. A new equivalent circuit is proposed for receiving lossy dipole antenna in the response of an incident plane wave to address the limitations of traditional Thévenin equivalent circuits.

articleTitle: Robust Iterative Permittivity Inversion Method Based on Reduced Order Models
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: To mitigate the nonlinearity and cycle-skipping effects inherent in inverse scattering problems (ISPs), we propose a robust permittivity inversion method using the iterative data to Born (DtB) process. The DtB process is based on reduced order models (ROMs) obtained by the Galerkin approximation of wave operators. We incorporate the layer-peeling (LP) strategy to ensure efficient and stable convergence. Furthermore, two regularization techniques are implemented to improve the robustness of the inversion algorithm in noisy environments. The inversion algorithm is validated through a 2D example.

articleTitle: Decoupling Dipole Antennas with Dielectric Resonator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A decoupling method using a dielectric resonator (DR) is investigated for 1 × 2 multiple-input and multiple-output (MIMO) dipole antenna. The decoupling DR is placed between two dipole antennas separated by a half wavelength. It serves as a parasitic element, creating a neutralization path between the two antenna ports. By adjusting the DR size, the isolation level can be improved obviously. A dual-port antenna system is simulated. An overlapping bandwidth (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\vert \mathrm{S}_{11}\vert$</tex> < −10 dB & <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\vert \mathrm{S}_{21}\vert$</tex> < −20 dB) of 9.2% (3.36-3.61 GHz) is obtained. This design method may find applications in base station antenna arrays.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Microstrip Leaky-Wave Antenna with Real-Time Open-Stopband Suppression
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A novel concept of comb-line leaky-wave antenna (LWA) structure is proposed to either perform a fixed-frequency beam-scanning or a frequency sweep at a fixed radiation angle, while suppressing the open-stopband (OSB) at all times. The unit cell consists of a microstrip line with a pair of matching stubs to mitigate the OSB with strategically placed electronically controlled phase shifters. Specifically, the proposed LWA contains two phase shifters per unit cell to perform beam-scanning at a fixed frequency while suppressing the OSB over a wide frequency range. The proposed concept is demonstrated using full-wave simulations using an array of 15 unit cells as an example and was simulated in Ansys HFSS using ideal phase shifters.

articleTitle: Design of a Dual-Polarized Printed Cylindrical Metasurface Cloak
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A unidirectional, penetrable cylindrical metasurface cloaking effective for both TE and TM polarizations is presented. The cylindrical metasurface induces surface waves that accept the incident wave of an arbitrary polarization on the lit side and propagate into the shadow side before reconstructing the incident wave behind the cylinder. Complete tangential fields including the surface waves of both polarizations are constructed and optimized. The optimized total fields define the metasurface by a spatially modulated tensorial surface reactance. A physical metasurface is designed using an array of Jerusalem-cross shaped conductor sheet. A cylindrical printed metasurface design of a 4-wavelength diameter is numerically validated.

articleTitle: A Combined Field Integral Equation for Scattering by Open Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: It is well-established that the magnetic field integral equation (MFIE) cannot be used to model scattering by open surfaces. In the context of multi-trace spaces it becomes apparent that the reason for this is that the MFIE does not uniquely determine the radiating component of the induced current. However, when the MFIE is combined with the electric field integral equation, a combined field integral equation results that can be uniquely solved for the currents on both sides of the open surface. This removes the necessity to compute these two currents in post-processing. It also renders the treatment of closed and open surfaces more consistent in codes for application to general geometries.

articleTitle: Enhancing Radiation Characteristics of Antenna Arrays Over a Sparse Area
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a 2×2 Circularly Polarized (CP) patch array operating in the X-Band frequency range. The array incorporates a Sequentially Rotated (SR) phase feed and utilises a metasurface-based superstrate fed by a parasitic aperture-coupled feeding network. The superstrate comprises an 8×8 array of asymmetric square metallic patches etched on a dielectric substrate, positioned at half-wavelength from the CP array. The proposed design offers significant advantages, including a broad 3-dB Axial Ratio (AR) bandwidth of 39%, high-directivity of 15 dBi, and wide 3-dB directivity bandwidth of 42.5%. Moreover, this antenna design leverages the use of sequentially rotated slots in superstrate-based antennas, making it suitable for implementation over sparse areas.

articleTitle: Setup for Material Characterization in the 110-170 GHz Band
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This work outlines the procedure to establish a system for assessing materials' complex permittivity and permeability within the 110–170 GHz frequency range. We present the employed methodology and the calibration procedure for the system, incorporating a dual approach using TRL (Thru-Reflect-Line) and GRL (Gated-Reflect-Line) methods. Following that, a smoothing technique is used to enhance the accuracy of the results. Tests were conducted on a HIPS sample to validate the system's performance, demonstrating the results' reliability across the entire measured bandwidth.

articleTitle: Single Pin Dual-Band Stacked Patch GNSS Antenna for Integration Under Automotive Glass
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper covers the design, simulation, fabrication, and testing of a single-pin, L1/L5 dual-band stacked patch antenna for GNSS applications. The antenna was designed for tight integration under automobile glass. The inherent dielectric loading of the glass enables size reduction and bandwidth enhancement while utilizing substrates with a relatively low dielectric constant of 9.8. An integrated matching network improves the bandwidth of the L5 band without perturbing the axial ratio. A thin dielectric superstrate is used to correct the axial ratio due to loading when placed under glass. The fabricated antenna demonstrates a bandwidth greater than 50 MHz in both the L1 and L5 bands and can achieve less than 4 dB axial ratio when under glass. The peak measured realized gain is greater than 3.9 dBi and 4.4 dBi for the L1 and L5 bands, respectively.

articleTitle: Improved Procedure for Total Isotropic Sensitivity Measurements in Reverberation Chamber
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: After indicating the phenomena that the normal stepped total isotropic sensitivity (TIS) measurement results in reverberation chamber (RC) are slightly worse than the ones in anechoic chamber (AC), we give the theoretical explanation. Based on that, a modified fast method of attaining TIS from the RC over-the-air (OTA) test system is provided. The lab tests results show that the proposed method could obtain the TIS results matching the ones acquired in AC better in contrast to the normal stepped RC TIS measurements with the significant test time reduction.

articleTitle: Data Distribution for Scalable on-Array Processing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The capacity of multi-beam digital arrays is constrained by data offload and processing bottlenecks, limiting the available degrees of freedom and beam count. These bottlenecks may be overcome by distributing array data across organic processing resources embedded within the array grid. Several on-array parallelization schemes are proposed which provide improved I/O efficiency vs. degrees of freedom relative to existing hierarchical beamformers.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Shared-Radiator Patch Antenna Pair with High Isolation for Mobile Terminals
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A dual-band shared-radiator patch antenna pair with high isolation is proposed for mobile terminals. Rectangular slots are firstly cut on the shared-radiator grounded patch antenna pair, reducing the resonant frequencies of the TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5,0</inf> and TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5,1</inf> modes down to and covering the desired 5G N78 (3.5-3.6 GHz) and N79 (4.8-4.9 GHz) bands, respectively. Based on the hybrid decoupling principles of the LC resonant circuit and the electrical and magnetic coupling cancellation, two capacitors and a bending slot are introduced, which can generate two transmission zeroes in the corresponding dual bands. The simulated isolation of the proposed antenna pair can thus be improved from the originally only greater than 2.5 dB and 4.5 dB to greater than 26.7 dB and 20.5 dB in the 5G N78 and N79 bands, respectively. The proposed antenna pair with compact structure, high isolation, and zero clearance is promising for mobile terminals.

articleTitle: Shared-Radiator Wideband Laminated Resonator Antennas with High Isolation Level
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a design of a two-port laminated resonator antenna (LRA) with a shared radiator. Two modes (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{TE}_{101}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{TM}_{111}$</tex>) are employed to achieve a wideband decoupling design. When the resonator cavity is excited by one feeding slot, the electric field at the location of the other feeding slot is near zero, and thus a high isolation level between two ports is achieved, which is larger than 25dB within the frequency band from 24.7 to 28.4 GHz (14%). The decoupling mechanism is elegant without using an extra decoupling structure, showing the potential for the applications in the full-duplex antenna systems.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Reflectarray with Broadband Polarization Reconfiguration Based on Far-Field Modulation Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a quad-polarization reconfigurable reflectarray (RA) over a wide band. First, the design of the linear-polarized unit cell with 1-bit phase control in the range of 8–18 GHz under different diode states is introduced. Then, the extra 360<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∘</sup>phase shifts can be achieved by changing the global constant phase in working frequency band based on this element. As verification, the full-wave simulation of RA antenna is also carried and showing the good radiation capability of circular polarization at 8, 12, and 15 GHz.

articleTitle: Design of Non-Reciprocal Reconfigurable Meta-Atom with Independent Phase Controls of the Transmitting and Receiving Chains
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a novel design method of the non-reciprocal reconfigurable meta-atom is introduced to realize the independent manipulations of transmitting and receiving (T/R) chains in the same aperture. The structure mainly contains three parts including the antenna, the power amplifier chips (PAs) based circulator for non-reciprocity and two independent active phase shifters with varactors in T/R chains for programmable phase controls respectively. Accordingly, the simulation results of the meta-atom present good nonreciprocal performance and reconfigurable capability in T/R chains, showing great potentials in the future communication systems.

articleTitle: Multi-Beam Switching Lens Antenna Fed by Powercombiner Butler-Matrix Controlling Output Port by Input Phases
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Antennas with a high equivalent isotropic radiated power (EIRP) are necessary to perform high-speed wireless communication in the 300 GHz band. We propose a high EIRP electrically multi-beam switching dielectric lens antenna fed by a multi-port power combiner. We have shown that the direction of the main beam is switched by feeding the input ports of the power combiner with different phases. Furthermore, we showed that the EIRP could be increased as the number of feeding transmitters increased.

articleTitle: Mitigation of Beam Squint Effects for Wideband Beamforming Using Time-Modulated Arrays
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Beam steering in traditional phased arrays is usually realized by introducing incremental phase differences between antenna elements. Due to the dispersion of electromagnetic waves, traditional phased arrays inevitably suffer from beam squint problems for wideband beamforming, which significantly deteriorates the data rate and beam resolution in modern radar systems. To address this problem, we present a novel pseudorandom time-modulated antenna array (TMA) in this paper. A signal-decomposition-based time modulation (SDTM) technique is proposed to decompose the wideband radio-frequency (RF) signal into the superposition of several narrowband signals with different sub-carriers. Numerical results of a Ku-band 32-element linear antenna array show that the beam-pointing error for RF signals with 6.0 GHz instantaneous bandwidth can be reduced from 13° to less than 1°. It well demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed technique.

articleTitle: On a Fast Direct Solver for High Order Integral Equations: Results for Low-to-Middle Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this work, we present a fast direct solver for integral equations-based electromagnetic scattering that is com-patible with spatial discretization of arbitrary order. The proposed approach leverages a suitably preconditioned combined field formulation and involves the regularization of the elliptic spectrum through the extraction of a specifically chosen equivalent circulant problem. The procedure yields a compressed representation of the inverse system matrix in the form of a matrix amenable to fast inversion and a single-skeleton low-rank perturbation. In addition to proposing the fast direct solution framework, this contribution presents the algorithms and ex-plores the intricacies that enable the high-order discretization of the underlying integral equations and is supported by numerical results illustrating its effectiveness.

articleTitle: A Fast Direct Solver for Higher Order Discretizations of Integral Equations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a fast direct solver for the Combined Field Integral Equation using higher-order discretizations. By adopting higher-order polynomials with the Method of Moments, the number of unknowns is significantly reduced. The fast direct solver leverages the efficiency of the Multi Level Fast Multipole Method by combining it with randomized linear algebra to construct low-rank approximations in a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{H}^{2}$</tex> format. The proposed method is fully error controllable and achieves a setup time with computational complexity of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{O}(r^{3}\log N)$</tex>. Numerical results for the scattering problem of a sphere demonstrate high accuracy, and the efficiency is demonstrated on the NASA Almond.

articleTitle: Double-Ridge Five Port Power Splitter Using Gap-Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In microwave engineering, waveguides are a key component when transmitting high frequency waves with low losses. However, these are inherently bulky in size and difficult to integrate with other microwave components. Gap-Waveguides are a good solution for mm-wave frequencies since they are easier to integrate with other components and easier to fabricate since there is no need for a complete physical shield. This work uses gap-waveguide technology to develop a 4:1 power splitter network that can operate from 20 GHz to 40 GHz with very low losses and less than 2:1 VSWR.

articleTitle: Towards Physics-Informed Graph Neural Network-based Computational Electromagnetics
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a generalizable data-driven computational electromagnetics (CEM) framework leveraging graph neural networks (GNNs). The proposed model supports training and inference for CEM scenarios with different simulation domain sizes and electromagnetic properties, while exploiting the locality of GNNs to achieve reduced complexity and enhanced accuracy. Our results indicate that GNNs can successfully infer the electromagnetic field spatiotemporal evolution for arbitrary simulation domain setups, paving the way for fully-fledged data-driven CEM models.

articleTitle: RF Characterization of Antenna Arrays via Open-Air Fixture Model of Backscattered Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A novel RF characterization method for determining key properties of antenna arrays is presented. The proposed technique is based on backscattered RF signal from the antenna array whose N-ports are passively terminated by known standards. As such, the proposed method allows for indirect characterization of antenna array's port impedance, mutual impedance as well as its radiation pattern, without directly exciting any of the array's N-ports. To do so, the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(N+1)$</tex> -port setup is treated as an open-air fixture, there the additional port represents an uncalibrated 1-port reflectometer that is used to illuminate the test array. The measured backscattered RF signal is tabulated for a sufficient number of terminations of the array ports and subsequently used to calibrate the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(N+1)$</tex> -port system. During the data collection, only one active port is needed, which is that of the reflectometer antenna. The test antenna ports are terminated by passive loads, e.g. open, short, and match standards, this can be freely rotated about at any angle without risk of cabling or probing connection issues. As such, the proposed approach can avoid problems that arise in typical antenna array characterization measurements, such as, coaxial cable bending, expensive port connections, or additional support structures that would hinder measurements. With the presented approach, antenna port impedance, array mutual impedances, element patterns, and array pattern can be readily extracted via the calibration procedure. The proposed approach is validated using a two-element Vivaldi array.

articleTitle: Transmission and Reflection Properties of Glass Types at 140, 200, 325, and 450 GHz
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper focuses on the characterization of trans-mission and reflection properties of 4 different glass types (fireproof glass, untinted glass, 50% tinted glass, and 90% tinted glass) at Terahertz (THz) frequencies. Using two frequency domain channel sounding setups, measurements were conducted over 140–144, 200–204, 325–329, and 450–454 GHz bands. Results show that fireproof glass is generally less reflective than other glass types, while transmission coefficients of 50% tinted glass is comparable with untinted glass. The results provided in this work will aid wireless propagation modeling at the aforementioned frequencies for various glass types utilized in homes and vehicles.

articleTitle: Solving Electromagnetic Problems with PINN based on Scattering Equivalent Source Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) based on the scattering equivalent source method. Through unsupervised learning, it addresses frequency-domain electromagnetic problems on two-dimensional metal boundaries, demonstrating a certain level of generalization. The introduced PINN leverages the equivalent source principle to represent metal boundaries effectively. Additionally, an attention mechanism is employed to establish correlations between different equivalent source sampling points, enabling dynamic input-output relationships.

articleTitle: A Novel Dual-Band Shared-Aperture Array Based on Wideband Electromagnetic Transparent Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper introduces a dual-band array antenna designed for base stations. To mitigate the influence of lower band antenna on the radiation patterns of higher band elements, we introduce a broadband electromagnetic transparent antenna incorporating vertically printed frequency selective surface elements. The antenna not only boasts a broad impedance bandwidth but also achieves electromagnetic transparency across a wide frequency band. The proposed lower band antenna obtains a wide impedance bandwidth of 36.9% and exhibits favorable electromagnetic transparency characteristics within the n77 band.

articleTitle: Design of 1-Bit Reconfigurable Transmissive Metasurface for Beam Manipulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper introduces a 1-bit reconfigurable transmissive metasurface antenna operating at 10 GHz. The metasurface unit cell, achieving high transmission amplitude and 1-bit phase resolution, is detailed along with an effective control system for managing multiple unit cells. Fabrication and measurement results validate the metasurface's precise beam steering characteristics.

articleTitle: Field-Based Formalism for Calculating Qubit-Qubit Exchange Coupling Rates for Transmon Qubits
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Superconducting qubits are one of the most mature approaches to realize quantum computers. Unfortunately, existing design approaches use full-wave computational electro-magnetics methods to model these devices in inefficient ways that become impractical if even a few qubits are considered. This work uses a field-based formalism to derive a simple formula for the exchange coupling rate between multiple qubits, which is a key design parameter for creating large-scale quantum architectures. This approach is relevant for the common situation of transmon qubits dispersively coupled via an electromagnetic resonator or environment. Then the accuracy of this approach is validated by comparing it to existing modeling approaches on a realistic superconducting circuit topology.

articleTitle: C-X Band Tunable Water-Based Metamaterial Absorbers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This letter introduces a novel metamaterial wave absorber comprising ring and bulb-shaped flexible resin containers filled with water. The wave absorption rate exceeds 90% within the range of 5.4~11.5 GHz. The water-based metamaterial replaces the conventional collector element, the wave-absorbing-reflecting function is switched by water injection and drainage, and the wave-absorbing band can be reconfigured by changing the water temperature. It retains its stability despite variations in angle within the range of 0~40° incidence and 0~ 90° polarization angles. This absorber has a vast variety of applications potential in such areas as electromagnetic radiation protection and radar target stealth.

articleTitle: Compact Dual-Band Millimeter Wave MIMO Antenna for Wireless Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The article presents the compact dual-band MIMO antenna resonating at 27.5 and 32 GHz. The radiating structure is a rose-shape with elliptical slots and a horizontal slit to achieve the above resonances. The MIMO antenna dimension is 6.2 ×10 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, where an edge-to-edge distance of 1.82 mm separates radiating elements. The ground plane has simple slits to suppress the mutual coupling. The simulation results of the MIMO antenna is validated through measured and diversity parameter results.

articleTitle: Characteristic-Mode-Guided Suppression of Cross-Band Scattering and Coupling in Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Cross-band scattering and coupling in a closely spaced dual-band antenna array are effectively suppressed over a wide band. Guided by characteristic mode analysis (CMA), a segmented spiral is efficiently developed as a dipole radiator to mitigate cross-band scattering and coupling while preserving the radiation performance of the antenna. Assisted by serial resonators, impedance matching of the spiral dipole is achieved within the low band (LB) of 0.69-1.00 GHz (36.7%). In comparison to a traditional tube-based dipole, a reduction in radar cross-section (RCS) is observed for the spiral dipole over 1.10-4.29 GHz (118%). High band (HB) antennas, operating in 1.63-2.83 GHz (53.8%), are collocated with the LB spiral dipole, constituting a dual-band antenna array.
