The array maintains stable radiation patterns without distortions across the HB, and cross-band isolations in the HB are improved to over 20 dB.

articleTitle: Signal Propagation Characteristics at 6 GHz and 60 GHz for Wi-Fi 8 UHR in Future Factories
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Wireless connectivity will underpin industrial automation and factories of the future. One of the limitations of the current IEEE 802.11 family and Wi-Fi for use in industrial applications is achieving ultra reliable and low latency communications (URLLC). IEEE 802.11bn and by extension Wi-Fi 8 ultra-high reliability (UHR) is currently being introduced to address these shortcomings. Key to providing UHR in factory settings will be ensuring an adequate understanding of the signal propagation characteristics which are likely to be encountered. In this paper, we use a commercial ray tracing engine to investigate two hypothetical use cases within future factories; namely inventory monitoring using an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) and movement of stock using a forklift vehicle at 6.745 GHz and 60.48 GHz.

articleTitle: Analysis and Improvement on the Gain of Optically Clear Silver Nanowire Patch Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents an analysis of principle factors that limit the gain of an optically transparent antenna, and subsequently outlines methods for gain enhancement. It introduces a circuit model that predicts a further improvement, and accordingly proposes an efficient and all-clear patch antenna.

articleTitle: Ultra-Thin CMOS-Compatible Artificial Magnetic Conductor for Millimeter-Wave Antenna-on-Chip
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Antenna-on-chip (AoC) is one of the promising solutions in the 6G era. However, it suffers from poor radiation due to the lossy Si substrate. Placing an artificial magnetic conductor (AMC) under the AoC cannot only isolate the AoC from the lossy Si substrate but also provide in-phase reflection. Nonetheless, the ultra-thin stack-up of the mainstream semiconductor technology makes the realization of AMC challenging at the millimeter-wave spectrum. To make the AMC electrically thicker, this paper presents four kinds of thickness reduction techniques (TRT): slot, notch, metallic post, and embedded guiding structure. With TRTs, an ultra-thin AMC (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$15\ \mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> thickness) is realized. With the proposed AMC, the AoC demonstrated a gain of 3.2 dB at 72 GHz. Compared to the standalone antenna, the AMC enhances the gain by 7 dB.

articleTitle: Fully Self-Healing UHF RFID Tag Based on a Slot Antenna for Future Skin-Like Electronics
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Self-healing functional polymers, blends, and composites provide a compelling approach for fully soft, elastic electronics and wireless sensing technologies. In this paper, we present a numerical analysis of an RFID tag antenna employing a self-healing substrate and conductor with conductivity of ~150 S/m. Despite the lower conductivity comparison with the metallic conductors (~60 MS/m), the flexible tag antenna achieves sufficient radiation performance in the UHF band ranging from 868 MHz to 920 MHz for a functioning RFID tag readable at 2.4 meters distance from the reader. To our knowledge, this is the first self-healing UHF RFID tag for versatile applications including healthcare, wireless communication systems, biomedicine, logistics, and different fields in the manufacturing industry.

articleTitle: Highly Flexible and Conformal Stacked Patch Filtering Antenna Using Transparent FEP Films
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: An optically transparent and lightweight stacked filtering patch antenna for conformal and flexible applications is presented. The antenna consists of two layers of patches utilizing optically transparent fluorinated ethylene propylene (FEP) film and polyethylene foam that are stacked for bandwidth enhancement while maintaining a high level of conformability. The antenna is designed for L-band applications and tested for the flat case as well as conformed to a cylinder with a radius of 200 mm, 160 mm, 80 mm, and 40 mm. The antenna has a bandwidth of 16.1% (1.152-1.355 GHz) and the gain varies from 7.4 dBi to 3.6 dBi for different cases of conforming to a cylinder.

articleTitle: A Beam-Steerable Fabry-Perot Cavity by Mechanically Adjustable Partially Reflective Surface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a Fabry-Perot cavity antenna showing beam-steering features by exploiting a mechanically adjustment of the Partially Reflective Surface (PRS) position is proposed. Fabry-Perot antennas are low-profile antennas that can reach excellent directivity with only one feeding point. However, the design of Fabry-Perot cavities becomes much more complicated when beam-steering is desirable. To face this issue, we propose a simple mechanical adjustment of the PRS position to obtain beam-steering, without introducing any modification of the radiating system original design. By performing accurate full-wave simulations over the conceived test-case, we obtained promising results. Even with a tilting beam angle up to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$50^{\circ}$</tex> the maximum Gain is higher than 15 dBi while the Half Power Beam Width has a mean value of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$14.4^{\circ}$</tex>. Thus, the solution configures as an effective trade-off between simplicity and augmented features to be implemented in Fabry-Perot cavities.

articleTitle: An Inversion Algorithm to Reconstruct Star-Like Penetrable Objects from Scattered Far-Field Pattern
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: An iterative inversion algorithm to reconstruct the shape of two-dimensional dielectric objects from far-field measurements is formulated and implemented. The proposed method uses an integral operator to map the unknown boundary of the object onto the far-field pattern of the scattered field. This mapping is inherently ill-posed and nonlinear. Therefore, Newton iterations are used for linearization, and the resulting linear equation at each iteration is regularized using a Tikhonov scheme. Numerical results validate the accuracy and the applicability of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Digital Beamforming Antenna Array for TM Satellite Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a new ground station for TM satellites tracking based on Digital BeamForming Network (DBFN) technology. In this demonstrator, several innovations are presented: the design of the antenna array composed by 256 radiating elements and of the signal digitalization and beamforming solution supports communication at very low elevation for multiple simultaneous satellites. This demonstrator of a DBFN ground station was developed in the frame of the ESA project A WS (Arctic Weather Satellite for EPS Sterna mission).

articleTitle: A Twelve-Element Sequentially Rotated Array for Circular Polarization Links at 5.8 GHz
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The paper presents a hexagonal 12-element array working at 5.8 GHz. The proposed device operates in circular polarization exploiting the sequential rotation architecture. The antenna elements are disc patches and modal degeneration is enforced to attain circular polarization at element level. A hexagonal sub-array is well-suited to be packed in planar space-filling arrangement, as well as in assembling truncated icosahedron, one of the Archimedean solids which are ideal shape for smart antennas with omnidirectional angle spatial coverage. A single layer via-less prototype is simulated considering a commercial FR408 substrate. A realized gain up to 11.6 dBi with a polarization purity exceeding 30 dB at 5.8 GHz is observed.

articleTitle: Quasi-Stationarity Regions Analysis for Maritime Mobile Communication Channel
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: With the rapid advancement of coastal fisheries, marine tourism, and unmanned maritime technology, there is an increasing need for maritime mobile communication. In this research, we conducted measurements on the maritime mobile channel operating at 2.2 GHz. Utilizing the obtained measurement data, we performed an in-depth analysis and evaluation of the quasi-stationary regions within the channel. The measured quasi-stationarity distance of the channel spans from 0.9 m to 22.3 m. The results highlight the susceptibility of the channel's stationarity distance to the surrounding environment and the occurrence of deep fading caused by sea surface reflection.

articleTitle: Optimization of a circular slotted patch with a defected grounded monopole patch antenna using artificial neural networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This article describes the use of artificial neural networks for the estimate of reflection coefficients. In this work, synthesis and analysis are studied where parametric analysis presents the simulated values necessary for training and testing neural networks with HFSS simulation software. The simulation and results produced by ANNs are compared with HFSS simulation. The proposed antenna measures 60 by 70 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Multi-view Beamforming Radar for Random Body Motion Cancellation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The detection of heartbeats using Doppler radars has been studied for decades to remove dependency on contact-based sensors. One of the consistent issues in developing a robust real-life sensing device is the noise generated due to random body motions (RBM). This study introduces a novel technique that combines signals from multiple radars with different view angles to remove the effects of random body motion and enhance the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of heartbeat signals. The proposed method utilizes four radars, with two receiving signals from the subject's chest and the other two from the subject's abdomen. The demodulated signal from each radar was added with weights to cancel the noise from random body motion. Simulation results are presented to verify the theory.

articleTitle: A Progressive Sampling Method for 3-D Reconstruction of DPO-SDF
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The Differentiable Physical Optics Method with Signed Distance Field (DPO-SDF) facilitates the 3-D reconstruction of perfect electric conductors (PEC) using scattered electric fields, achieving high precision with low computational costs. However, its uniform sampling technique leads to an overuse of memory and increased time consumption due to redundant sampling points. As an alternative, this paper proposes a heterogeneous ruleset sampling method, which includes progressive sampling to rapidly approximate the target boundary through an iterative approach, and uniform sampling in the vicinity of the target to ensure accuracy. Numerical experiments indicate that this method achieves a 46.7% reduction in model training time, and the chamfer distance is reduced by nearly 72.4%, indicating a significant improvement in the reconstructed model precision.

articleTitle: mm-Wave Dual-Band Dual-Polarized Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A dual-band, dual-polarized radiating element suitable for 5G millimeter-wave base station antenna arrays is shown in this paper. The operating bandwidth covers the n258 (24.25-27.5 GHz) and n259 (39.5-43.5 GHz) bands simultaneously. Stacking technique is utilized to achieve wide dual band operation and stable radiation pattern. The antenna offers a sharp roll-off and a filter-like response between the two operating bands. Antenna design principle and simulated and measured performance are discussed in detail. The solution proposed shows very promising performance, such as the isolation between the ports and a cross-polar discrimination level that is better than 15dB over the whole Field of View in both frequency ranges. The solution is very stable also respect to different steering conditions.

articleTitle: Non-Invasive Sensor for Grounding Grid Mesh Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The following work presents a spiral geometry antenna operating at 54 MHz for the application of non-invasive sensing of lightning strikes in grounding mesh. The antenna uses the F R4 dielectric, allowing low manufacturing costs and increased accessibility, the structure presents a reflection parameter <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S_{11}$</tex> of -18.3 dB at the desired frequency of 54 MHz, the analysis of the results using a current pulse generator and the developed antenna demonstrate that the structure fulfills the objective of non-invasive monitoring lighting strikes in a ground mesh.

articleTitle: Pressurized Slotted Waveguide Antenna for High Power Microwave Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a novel pressurized high-power slotted waveguide antenna (HPSWA) for directed energy applications. The proposed antenna is designed for 3 GHz and fabricated to ensure the handling of 2 bars of Sulfur hexafluoride (SF6) pressure. The proposed HPSWA is tested, and its performance is closely monitored to ensure that it meets the desired specifications. The results demonstrate that the antenna achieves high gain and is suitable for various applications such as satellite communication, radar systems, and wireless communication networks. Overall, the HPSWA offers a promising solution for efficiently radiating high amounts of directed microwave energy at 3 GHz.

articleTitle: Ultrathin Multimode Microstrip Antenna Using Differential Feed for Smartphone Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes an ultrathin multimode microstrip antenna with a stable broadside radiation pattern across the operating band. Different from previous works using gridded patches with a relatively high profile, the proposed antenna has a much lower thickness of only 0.4 mm (0.008 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{\lambda}_{\mathbf{0}},\ \boldsymbol{\lambda}_{\mathbf{0}}$</tex> is the free-space wavelength at 5.75 GHz). In this case, an undesirable monopole mode will be excited in-band using the conventional L-shaped probe, destroying the broadside pattern. Therefore, a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{\pi}-\mathbf{shaped}$</tex> probe with differential feed is used instead. The original antiphase- <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{TM}_{\mathbf{20}}$</tex> and antiphase- <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{TM}_{\mathbf{02}}$</tex> modes are preserved to enhance the bandwidth to 4.4%. This method can be also extended to the cases of dual-linear or circular polarization, showing potential applications in mobile terminals.

articleTitle: An X-band Antenna With Bandwidth Enhancement and RCS Reduction Based on Polarization Conversion Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a broadband, low RCS antenna based on polarization conversion metasurface (PCM) is designed and simulated. The metasurface unit, consists of a quasi-square patch on the top layer, a notched square ring on the mid layer and a metal ground, can realize cross polarization conversion within 5.87-20.67 GHz (111.5%). By arranging each unit properly, proposed metasurface achieves RCS reduction in the range of 8.21-21.22 GHz (88.41%). Rather than simply being loaded on the top of the antenna, the PCM functions as a part of radiators, which makes it possible to broad the bandwidth and enhance the gain simultaneously. Finally, a broadband antenna operating in the X-band is achieved, with a bandwidth of 7.76-12.59 GHz (47.5%).

articleTitle: A Compact High-Gain Multi-Beam Lens Antenna Utilizing Quasi-Conformal Transformation Optics
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper describes the construction of an innovative multi-beam Luneburg lens antenna with a dielectric structure and suggests a new method for miniaturizing planar lens antennas. This research uses Quasi-Conformal Transform Optics (QCTO) to develop a transformational link between spatial coordinates and the electromagnetic properties of materials to achieve miniaturization of antenna dimensions. The antenna layout consists of a distorted Luneburg lens with a radius of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3.75\lambda$</tex> surrounded by metal plates, and a linear array of seven microstrip antennas operating at 10 GHz. The antenna array enables generating seven separate beams by selectively activating elements, allowing for a scanning range of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 30^{\circ}$</tex> in the azimuth plane. Each beam attains a gain greater than 15 dBi. In contrast to typical planar lens antennas, this antenna has a size reduction of more than 30% and may be fed using a linear array.

articleTitle: Noninvasive Microwave Monitoring of Radiofrequency Hyperthermia with Magnetic Implants
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The monitoring of the radiofrequency hyperthermia treatment of deep-seated tumors using magnetic implants is an open challenge. Temperature probes are invasive, while increases the risk of infections, therefore alternative engineering solutions must be provided. Microwave monitoring can be a noninvasive and cost-effective solution. During the hyperthermia treatment the electromagnetic properties of tissues varies, thus a differential microwave signal based on the dielectric contrast. So far, the feasibility of using microwaves to monitor the temperature changes of the target tissues has been demonstrated using by simulating the forward propagation problem by employing a transmission line model. The results are promising, but to foster the advancement of this innovative microwave monitoring strategy further studies are needed. In this work, 2D multiphysics simulations on a multilayered surface phantom are performed to investigate if and how the microwaves monitoring of the radiofrequency hyperthermia treatment of deep-seated tumors with magnetic implants can be performed. The low-frequency and the heating problem are solved, while the time-evolution of the reflected and transmitted field from a microwave discrete source, working 434 MHz and 915 MHz, are analyzed. The results corroborate the 1D analysis and indicates that changes of ~30 dB occurs during the radiofrequency treatment.

articleTitle: Radiation Beam-Steering Controlled by Water-Filled 3D-Printed Fluidic Channels Underneath a MSF
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A new beam-steering method is proposed for a broadside patch radiator, radiating under a metasurface (MSF) for enhanced gain. A 3D-printed structure that hosts 20 fluidic channels in a 5×4 array is added beneath the MSF. By selectively filling-in the channels with distilled water, a high εrcontrolled-shape block is formed re-directing the main lobe direction. The presented structure consists of a 4.8 GHz patch radiator with 6 dBi of gain. The addition of a 10×10 cells MSF enhances the broadside lobe gain to approximately 14 dBi, and the use of selectively filled fluidic channels can cause 33° of beam tilting in two directions. The gain of the tilted beams remain higher than 10 dBi in both directions.

articleTitle: Radiation Pattern Extrapolation through Generative Adversarial Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Antenna designs play a crucial role in wireless communication systems where high-performance specifications are greatly required. The radiation pattern (RP) specification in both the E-plane and H-plane is important, as it connects the antenna gain along a given direction. This performance is calculated in the entire bandwidth for various frequencies and is time-consuming. To speed up these simulations, a new approach with the help of a generative adversarial network (GAN) is presented, leading to the prediction of the expected radiation pattern outcomes for the determined frequencies. This method is verified for two previously optimized antennas, one operating between 8.8-10.1 GHz and the other working in the 11.3-13.16 G Hz band. The experimental simulation results prove that the mean absolute error is less than 0.35, which yields suitable accuracy for RP predictions.

articleTitle: Mitigating Radiation Pattern Ripples Due to Edge Diffraction in Central Element of a Large Array Using Top Hat Loaded High Impedance Surface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Edge diffraction has been identified as one of the potential causes that downgrade the radiation characteristics in an antenna array, when the ground size is increased to incorporate multiple elements. A study has been conducted in this work, to identify the likely sources of the edge-diffracted waves, which create ripples in the radiation pattern of a centrally placed antenna element in an array. Edge-traveling surface waves, which contribute to this performance degradation has been mitigated using a top hat loaded high impedance surface (HIS). The radiation characteristics of the resultant HIS incorporated structure exhibited a smoother, ripple-free radiation pattern.

articleTitle: Pod-Mounted Antenna Self-Interference Cancellation for Airborne STAR Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a method for self-interference cancellation in the propagation domain, for use in airborne simul-taneous transmit and receive (STAR) systems. A configuration of three dipole antennas operating at 1.8 GHz is simulated in free space, on an aluminum mounting pod, and aboard an F-18 military jet. Two antennas are used to transmit, while the remaining antenna is used to receive. By transmitting signals of equal amplitude with opposite phase, the signals cancel at the receive antenna while the signal of interest is still received. Moreover, we show the isolation improvement compared with a single transmit, single receive antenna setup. We respectively demonstrate -55,-52, and -37 dB coupling in free space, on the pod, and aboard the F-18, all improvements over the single transmit configuration.

articleTitle: Design of a Stacked Circularly Polarized Slot-Patch Antenna for X-band Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper introduces a numerically investigation of a compact stacked Circularly Polarized (CP) slot-patch antenna designed to operate in X-band (8 −12 GHz). The proposed solution features a coaxially fed circular radiating patch etched on a dielectric substrate, which includes two sector notches positioned on opposite sides at a 45° inclination to achieve circular polarization. Two additional dielectric substrates are placed on the top of the radiating patch, with a parasitic passive patch positioned on each, with the aim of enlarging the overall operating bandwidth. The numerical results demonstrated that the configuration is able to cover a 2.2 GHz band, achieving a minimal Axial Ratio (AR) of 1.2 dB and a gain of 7.4 dB at 10 GHz.

articleTitle: LoRa Application for Improving Autonomy of Rural Elderly Inhabitants
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Fixing population in rural areas is currently a big challenge in many countries. Providing digital services to these populations and, so, improving the quality of living in such areas could be a strategy to attract new inhabitants and to keep those who are now there. This contribution describes a proposal in this framework, with the specific characteristic that the population was in the center of the project along all the process. A LoRaWAN application is described along the paper, explaining the developing route based on Design Thinking and the first feedback we gathered. Once the problem was established (elderly people that like to go for a walk around near forests and sometimes they get lost), a solution was defined, deployed and tested, and the lessons learnt are explained along this contribution.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Wideband Horizontally Polarized End-Fire Magneto-Electric Dipole Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a millimeter-wave horizontally polarized end-fire 1×8 antenna array with wide bandwidth and compact configuration. The antenna array consists of eight horizontally polarized end-fire magneto-electric dipole (ME-dipole) antenna fed by substrate integrated coaxial line (SICL) and a 1-to-8 SICL power divider. The radial electric field distribution of the TEM mode in the SICL is utilized here to facilitate the design of end-fire ME-dipole antenna with horizontal polarization. Moreover, top loaded structures implemented to the ME-dipole elements and air slits etched to the substrates between the adjacent elements contribute to realizing an array with compact configuration. A wide impedance bandwidth of 61% and a gain of up to 13.2 dBi have been experimentally verified by a fabricated prototype of the 1×8 antenna array.

articleTitle: A Sparsified Nested Dissection Ordering Preconditioner for Broadband Discrete Exterior Calculus $\mathbf{A}-\Phi$ Formulation Solver
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A broadband preconditioner is proposed for accelerating the convergence of iterative solvers for the discrete exterior calculus <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{A}-\Phi$</tex> formulation solver. Nested dissection ordering (NDO), which takes advantage of the sparsity information of the coupling matrix, is utilized in constructing the preconditioner. In addition, low-rank approximation is introduced to sparsify the matrix after NDO reordering. The proposed sparsified NDO preconditioner works for general complex symmetric and indefinite matrix systems, which is commonly encountered in computational electromagnetics when conductive medium is involved. Numerical examples show the proposed preconditioner has <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$O(N\log N)$</tex> complexity, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex> is the number of unknowns in the problem. More importantly, the efficiency of the proposed preconditioner is independent of parameters such as frequency and conductivity in the system, which indicates the broadband nature of the proposed preconditioner.

articleTitle: Highly Flexible and Conformal Stacked Antenna Using Uneven-Spaced Corrugated Mesh Patterns
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Multilayer flexible and conformal antennas are demonstrated using semi-elliptical-shaped corrugated mesh patterns using copper-clad polyimide film. The antenna consists of corrugated strips with varying corrugation sizes that are joined together to form an uneven-spaced mesh pattern. Two layers of mesh patterns are stacked to provide increased bandwidth. The antenna can easily be conformed to surfaces along the horizontal, vertical, and diagonal directions. An L-band antenna is optimized and tested for the flat case as well as conformed to cylinders with a radius of 200 mm, 160 mm, 80 mm, 40 mm, and 20 mm.

articleTitle: A Compact Passband Filter Based on Folded Split Ring Resonators for ISM Applications at 5.8GHz
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A third order compact printed bandpass filter in the Industrial Scientific and Medical (ISM) band is designed, based on coupled folded split ring resonators. The design allows for a cost-effective vialess single layer realization on a standard substrate.

articleTitle: Single-Probe Antenna Sampling based on Matrix Completion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this work, a single-probe antenna sampling method based on matrix completion is proposed to reduce sampling effort. For the single-probe near-field sampling system, the shortest path for probe movement is determined by integer programming and then matrix completion method is utilized to achieve the near-field reconstruction by exploiting the low-rank properties of radiation field of antenna under test. Numerical experiments show that the proposed method can realize near-field recovery with half of the data required by equiangular sampling.

articleTitle: An Ultrawideband Rectifier Circuit Design for Sub-6 GHz in 5G RF Energy Harvesting Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this study, a rectifier that can harvest energy over a wide band at low input power has been modeled, with a dimension of 13x24 mm. The voltage doubler configuration was employed during the design of the rectifier. The microstrip lines used for connection purposes in the proposed circuit were optimized. The recommended rectifier was designed using the FR4 substrate model and the HSMS2852 Schottky diode model. According to simulation results, the power conversion efficiency of the suggested rectifier has exceeded 26% in the frequency range of 0.1-5.6 GHz at 0.5 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{k}\Omega$</tex> load and 0 dBm input power.

articleTitle: Mode Matching Analysis of Partially Filled Waveguide for Determining Electrical Property Parameters of Biaxial Materials
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, the S-parameters calculation methods of biaxial materials in different partially filled waveguide (PFW)'s filling-type are summarized. The method of calculating S-parameters is discussed when the sample that is biaxial material is filled along the big edge or the small edge of the rectangular waveguide. The modes of propagation in the waveguide are different with different filling-type. The propagation constant of the sample region is determined by solving the transcendental equation by Newton-Raphson Algorithm. By applying the boundary conditions at the interface between the sample region and the vacuum region, the mode matching equations can be obtained, which are solved by using the completeness and orthogonality of the vacuum waveguide modes as test functions.

articleTitle: WideBand Wearable Antenna for ISM Band
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A rectangular microstrip patch antenna with a small size of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{34.5}\times \mathbf{32.5}\times \mathbf{0.8}$</tex> mm3 has been proposed for wearable devices, health monitoring, medical Internet of Things (MIoT) applications. Fig. 1 shows the suggested antenna, where a Split ring resonance (SRR) is on the top of the patch, and numerous 0.5mm thin lines are removed from the ground plane. The designed antenna operates at 5.8 GHz and covers the ISM (Industrial Scientific Medical) bands. From radiating frequency band of 5.31 GHz to 6.44 GHz, the proposed antenna's return loss is less than -10dB, and the antenna indicates wide bandwidth, good efficiency, and gain over the working band. Polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) is used to construct the suggested wideband wearable antenna, which was then put to the test using a vector network analyzer (VNA). The designed antenna is a perfect match for a flexible wearable wideband antenna.

articleTitle: Independent, Concurrent Dual-Harmonic Frequencies Operation of Overlapped Spatial-Temporal Phased Array Using Dual-Functional Radiator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper is the first to introduce a new class of overlapped spatial-temporal phased array, which simultaneously and independently operate at the fundamental and second harmonic frequency, while operating in an identical mode. This concept is exemplified to operate at 24 GHz (fundamental frequency) and 48 GHz (second harmonic) without occurrence of grating lobes at 48 GHz. Utilizing a newly developed dual- functional radiator (DFR) for compactness and high radiating efficiency, a 1 × 4 antenna array achieves peak gains of 9.6 dBi at 24 GHz and 12.5 dBi at 48 GHz, with +/- 45-degree scanning angle at both frequencies. This method allows the realization of a compact, single phased-array topology simultaneously operating across 1:2 beamsteering bandwidth.

articleTitle: Schur Decomposition Fast Direct Solver for Volume Surface Integral Equation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a new fast direct solver based on the Schur Decomposition method. The single-level compressed H-Matrix is factorized into <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{LDU}$</tex> format, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{L}$</tex> is a lower triangle, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{U}$</tex> is the upper triangle compressed block matrix. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{D}$</tex> is the diagonal block matrix. The solution process includes matrix-vector multiplication with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{L}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{U}$</tex>, along with a diagonal block solution of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{D}$</tex>. The high cost of factorization is overcome by using low-rank block matrix operations.

articleTitle: Compact Bio-Inspired Antenna AMC-Backed for WBAN Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents the first investigations of a new compact bio-inspired CPW antenna that is AMC-backed for Wireless Body Area Networks (WBAN) applications. The investigations deal with the air gap thickness between the bio-inspired radiating monopole and the artificial magnetic conductor (AMC). Simulation and measurement results for 3 air-gap variations. As expected, the artificial magnetic conductor shifts down the resonance frequency compared to the bio-inspired antenna in free space simulations, enabling a path to miniaturization without compromising performance.

articleTitle: Cumulative Angular Power Spectrum for Indoor Base Stations Based on 3GPP Channel Models
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Based on the channel models specified by the 3GPP, this study provides distributions of the cumulative angular power spectrum (cAPS) for base stations in the indoor-office (InO) and indoor-factory (InF) scenarios. The cAPS is obtained using Monte Carlo simulations with 5000 randomly distributed user equipment per studied scenario. The cAPS in the elevation direction is fitted by the Rayleigh distribution and Gaussian distribution for the InO and InF scenarios, respectively. The effects of the room size and the frequency dependency from sub-6 GHz to 39 GHz are also investigated. The obtained distributions of the cAPS can offer insights into antenna design and placement of indoor base stations.

articleTitle: Integrated Circularly Polarized Antenna in a 2U CubeSat
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents the integrated antenna design of a 440MHz Circularly Polarized antenna integrated in a 2-unit CubeSat structure. Four elements are integrated in the Zenith face of the CubeSat with a sequential phase shift. Interestingly, the main lobe of the antenna is oriented toward the Nadir face with a peak realized gain of 1.6dBic and 0.4dB axial ratio.

articleTitle: Conformal Four-Port MIMO Antenna for BAN
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents the design and application of a conformal common radiator four-port multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) antenna for the body area network (BAN). Here, the previously designed planar antenna on a Rogers RO 3003 ( <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varepsilon_{\mathrm{r}}=3.0, \tan \delta=0.001$</tex> ) substrate is made conformal to find its applicability in the body area networking (BAN). The simulation strategy for this type of the antenna is discussed. The antenna has a -10 dB impedance bandwidth from 0.7 to 1.01 GHz, 2.6 to 3.18 GHz, 5.3 to 6.06 GHz, and 6.7to 6.94 GHz. Further, the simulated study shows the improvement in envelope correlation coefficient (ECC) for the conformal antennas and thus, it can find its suitability for BAN MIMO applications.

articleTitle: A Pattern Reconfigurable Miniaturized Quarterwave Patch Antenna Design with Isolated Ports
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A novel miniaturized multi-port beam scanning antenna element is presented. The isolation problem of a multi-port antenna is addressed by capacitive or inductive feeding network design. The antenna achieves beam scanning at the same frequency by varying the phase difference between the ports. To reduce port-to-port isolation between elements, the antenna is miniaturized by using a substrate with a high dielectric coefficient and the slots on the antenna surface. These techniques achieve a 61.7% reduction in antenna size. To compensate for the bandwidth reduction due to miniaturization, an aperture-coupled feeding method is preferred. The shorted antenna houses two excitation ports on the same patch, creating an isolation problem. This problem is addressed by developing a novel feeding network that utilizes capacitive or inductive elements to increase port isolation. As a consequence of the feeding network, the| S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf>| parameter is reduced from -5 dB to -22 dB.

articleTitle: A Single-Layer Wideband Dual-Polarized Differential-Fed Filtering Antenna Utilizing Shorting Pins Array and SRRs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A single-layer wideband dual-polarized differential-fed filtering antenna with low profile and high selectivity is proposed. First, the patch antenna excited differential feed is loaded with shorting pins array to adjust the TM10, TM11 and TM12 modes, such that TM10 and TM11 modes are closely positioned to broaden the impedance bandwidth, while the TM12 mode moves out of the passband, resulting in a radiation null. Second, the patch electromagnetically excites surrounding symmetric Vertical Split-Ring Resonators (VSRRs), yielding an extra resonance mode for wide band and a higher edge radiation null for a sharp roll-off rate. Third, Complimentary Split-Ring Resonators (CSRRs) inscribed around two pairs of differential feeds manifest a tunable lower edge radiation null to increase frequency selectivity. Finally, the proposed filtering antenna exhibits a 21.4% operational bandwidth with a peak gain of 9.7 dBi within the passband, the generation of three radiation nulls was observed, and high selectivity.

articleTitle: Design Approaches for Identical Transmitter and Receivers for Long Distance OAM Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we present an analytical solution for determining the uniform circular array transmitter radius in long-distance orbital angular momentum communication, ensuring identical receiver and transmitter radii for a given communication distance. Using the relation between beam divergence and the radius of the transmitter, we derive an equation to ensure identical radii for both the transmitter and receiver UCA. We simulate the generation of an OAM beam at 26 GHz for 50 m and 100 m distances using both modes 1 and 2. Further, we multiplex modes 1 and 2 in a concentric uniform circular array configuration and report the mode purity for a 50m distance.

articleTitle: Arthur Yaghjian Scientific Contributions in Antennas, High-Frequency Diffraction, and Metamaterials
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Dr. A. Yaghjian stands out as one of the most innovative, creative, and influential scientists in Electromagnetics (EM). His remarkable qualities stem from his impressive fundamental background in Maxwell's equations and on his unparalleled ability to formulate complex EM problems in a rigorous and impactful manner. Undoubtedly, he is among the few remaining repositories of knowledge in EM theory. This paper undertakes a review of his primary contributions, with special emphasis on Antennas, High-Frequency diffraction, and metamaterial, that have had a profound impact on the EM community.

articleTitle: ANN-GA-Enabled Method for Decoupling Optimization in MIMO Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, an artificial neural network (ANN) combined with the genetic algorithm (GA) optimization method to decrease the coupling of multiple input multiple output (MIMO) antennas is proposed. First, a model of the connection between the antenna geometric variables and its transmission coefficients (S21) is established utilizing an ANN. Subsequently, the coupling between the antenna elements is minimized by using a genetic algorithm (GA) optimization. During the training process, prior knowledge was used to create initial small datasets which are recursively improved by combining new simulation data from GA optimization. Broadband and narrowband optimizations of S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf> for one antenna are presented which demonstrates the availability of the method. The method is not only effective in reducing the design-related time, complexity, and cost but also in generating high-quality antenna optimization solutions.

articleTitle: A General Method for Designing ESPAR Antenna with Planar Beam Scanning Capabilities
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: We propose a general computational method for guiding the design of an electronically steerable parasitic array radiator (ESPAR) antenna. The radiation field of the 2-element unit cell is calculated to ascertain the port characteristics of the parasitic element, followed by the retrieval of reactive load values as the beam steers. So, DC bias and diode operating parameters have been considered thoroughly. A 9-element ESPAR antenna is proposed to verify the method, with the observed congruence between calculated and measured results validating the method and highlighting its value for designing ESPAR antennas.

articleTitle: Radar Tracking of Small Moving Targets from an Hybrid Detection Algorithm using MUSIC and FFT
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we propose to combine the two-dimensional MUSIC (MUltiple SIgnal Classification) algorithm with Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) to detect small moving targets from raw data collected by millimeter-wave beamscanners. It is shown that this hybrid detection method makes it possible to reduce by factor 3 the computation time required by MUSIC algorithm, at the expense of the reduction by 55% of the detection rate. Measurement results and analyses are given in the case of the tracking of a small mobile cylinder in a cluttered indoor environment from three millimeter-wave beamscanning radars.

articleTitle: A Fist Shape CSRR Loaded Patch Antenna at K and Ka Band for Satellite Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this work, a complementary split ring resonator (CSRR) loaded fist shape patch antenna is proposed to work in K and Ka band for satellite applications. The proposed antenna shows a total volume of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$20 \times 25\times 1.6\ \text{mm}^{3}$</tex>. By using CSRR loading, miniaturization and gain enhancement are achieved. The designed antenna shows a percentage bandwidth of 22.75% (17.25 - 22 GHz) at the lower resonance frequency of 20.87 GHz and 68.54% (23.12 -40 GHz) at the upper resonance frequency of 24.62 GHz, respectively. The obtained radiation efficiency is more than 60% and observed peak gains are 1.67 and 6.29 dBi at the resonance frequency of 20.87 and 24.62 GHz, respectively. The designed antenna is experimentally validated in this work and results are found to be satisfactory towards it used for satellite applications.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study on Homogenization Methods Applied on Periodic Dielectric Structures
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Two different electromagnetic homogenization methods, namely field averaging and S-parameter retrieval methods, are applied to a structure consisting of periodic dielectric spheres. S-parameters of the structure are obtained through simulation of the unit cell for normal incidence of TE mode excitation. The extracted equivalent constitutive parameters and reflection/transmission characteristics of the equivalent homogenized materials are compared. Although the equivalent constitutive parameters are resulted to be different for two different methods, the S-parameter results were the same and they were in good agreement with the original periodic structure.

articleTitle: Chiral Knotted Wire Metasurfaces for Near-Reflectionless Polarization Rotation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This work investigates the asymmetrical electromagnetic radiation of chiral knotted wire metasurfaces. We start with a theoretical analysis, deriving the vector potential for a general knotted wire metasurface. It is shown that if trefoil knots are chosen, the radiated field exhibits asymmetrical radiation, and the radiated field is circularly polarized. We use these characteristics to demonstrate a near-reflectionless polarization rotation metasurface. The proposed concept is numerically simulated, where the transmission and reflection coefficients of the electromagnetic fields are calculated. The design exhibits an almost perfect transmission into the rotated polarization, with a transmission of −0.64 dB.

articleTitle: RFiDARFusion: Enhancing Contactless Activity Monitoring with Radar and RFID Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Indoor human activity recognition (HAR) faces challenges due to the limitations of single-sensor systems in terms of privacy and cost. Our contactless RFiDARFusion system aims to reduce healthcare costs by swiftly identifying unforeseen activities through artificial intelligence and wireless communication. The system accurately discerns complex human activities by employing the LSTM-VAE fusion algorithm for multi-sensor data extraction, proving effective in long-range and non-line-of-sight environments. Two data fusion algorithms were studied across five distinct activities, significantly improving HAR accuracy by a minimum of 4.5% and 6.5% under data and feature-level fusion, respectively. The resulting RFiDARFusion system is contactless, precise, and robust, promising to enhance the quality of life for elderly patients in assisted living.

articleTitle: Wideband Aperture-Coupled Microstrip Array Antennas in Circular Polarization for Ka Band Satellite Communications Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents wideband aperture-coupled microstrip array antenna designs in circular polarization operation for Ka band satellite communications applications. The aperture shape can be adjusted to improve the operating bandwidth, and a H-shaped aperture with proper dimensions is shown to the array designs. Two array cases are demonstrated by simulations where the 1 by 4 array has the operating frequencies from 26.6 GHz to 36.5 GHz and the 4 by 4 array exhibits the frequency range from 20.4 GHz to 38.2 GHz.

articleTitle: Wiener-Hopf Solution of a Backscattering Protected Waveguide: A Tribute to Professor Zich
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This work is dedicated to Rodolfo Zich, a distinguished authority on the Wiener-Hopf technique and a prominent figure in our community, recently passed away. After a thought in memory of Prof Zich, we address the wave propagation phenomena in a parallel plate waveguide with Parity Time-Reversal Duality (PTD) symmetry, and its exact solution using a Wiener-Hopf formulation. The inherent symmetry of these waveguides provides protection against backscattering. Through the combination of the Wiener-Hopf method with a regularization technique, we arrive at closed-form relations that aptly describe the modes within these waveguides.

articleTitle: Characterization of Optically Transparent Two-Metal-Layered Refractive Metasurfaces for 6G Upper-Mid Outdoor-to-Indoor Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper proposed an innovative scenario for reinforcing outdoor-to-indoor (O2I) communication including fixed wireless access (FWA), leveraging optically transparent refractive metasurfaces (TRMs). The proposed TRM effectively refracts incident waves in the desired direction with minimal loss, using only two metal layers. The paper provides a detailed characterization of the TRM, including the minimum unit cell sub-group period, size, and the required transmission phases for each unit cell. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is validated through experimental results in the 6G upper-mid frequency band, specifically in satellite-to-vehicle O2I communication.

articleTitle: A Novel Machine-Learning-Based Method for the Fast Solution of Integral Equations for Electromagnetic Scattering Problems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A novel method is proposed for the efficient and accurate iterative solution of frequency domain integral equations that can be used for large-scale electromagnetic scattering problems. The proposed method uses a novel group-by-group interaction scheme for the fast and accurate evaluation of far-zone interactions based on the one-box-buffer scheme during the matrix-vector multiplication at each iteration. Briefly, subdomain basis functions (that are used to model the scatterer) at each box are replaced by a fixed uniform distribution of Hertzian dipoles, and the dipole-to-dipole interactions are inferred in a group-wise manner by using machine learning algorithms. The efficiency and accuracy of the proposed method are assessed by comparing our results for scattering from several conducting geometries with those obtained by the Mie series and multilevel fast multipole algorithm (MLFMA) solutions.

articleTitle: On the Design of the Optimized Wideband Antenna (OWA) Yagi
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A remarkable method is presented for decreasing the VSWR and increasing the gain and front-to-back (rear) ratio over a larger than typical bandwidth for Yagi antennas. This procedure and a direct dipole 50 Ohm feed were discovered by Prof. Breakall in the early 1990s using sophisticated computer global optimization techniques applied to the NEC4 antenna modeling software. He named this technique the Optimized Wideband Antenna (OWA), and it was first used to increase the bandwidth of monopole and dipole antennas by placing one or more parasitic elements close to the driven dipole or monopole, in a manner similar to the well-known sleeve antenna. The lengths and spacings of these extra parasitic wires are then optimized in a global computer algorithm to minimize the peak SWR in a range of frequencies over some band. The first application was a proposed method of covering several bands on a commercial cell phone at the time with several vertical whip antennas. After this preliminary work on dipoles and monopoles, the method was applied to the Yagi antenna. When applied to Yagis, it is possible to increase the percentage bandwidth with very low VSWR, high peak gain, and very low rear sidelobes with this technique.

articleTitle: In-Nostrils Antennas for Temperature-Based Breath Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Conventional diagnostic monitoring of human breathing involve cumbersome and wired equipment, that is uncomfortable for the user and that, most of the times, do not consider the breathing asymmetries between the two nostrils. This paper presents a fully miniaturized two-channel flexible and epidermal antenna sensor for the passive wireless bilateral monitoring of nasal breathing based on temperature measurement. The device fits the nose as a septum ring and is made of highly flexible and soft biocompatible materials. It comprises two coupled loop antennas whose Ultra-High Frequency (UHF) Radio Frequency IDentification (RFID) temperature-sensing microchips are placed just inside the nostrils to implement both sensing and transmission of the breath data. Parametric electromagnetic design and experimental evaluation of the device are both presented in the paper, providing a maximum reading distance above 50 cm.

articleTitle: Adaption of Subspace Based Optimization Method for Dark Field Microscopy Data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: We apply two-fold subspace-based optimization method for the refractive index reconstruction given coherent dark-field optical microscopy data. Due to the lack of phase information in the measurement data, we compare the results of two adaption methods where the deterministic part of the induced current is optimized in advance or not. Our simulation results show that the calculation of the deterministic part degrades the reconstruction performance and it is better to optimize the entire induced current.

articleTitle: A Pin Diode-Enabled PDMS Antenna for Transition Between UWB and Filtered Narrowband Modes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this work, an ultrawide band printed antenna capable of switching frequency mode is proposed for smart flexible devices. The antenna is developed using Polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) substrate owing to the advantage of transparency and flexibility with an overall size of 40 mm <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times 38$</tex> mm <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times 1$</tex> mm. The antenna radiating structure is composed of an elliptical shape radiator along with a filter, designed to pass lower band while filtering out the UWB spectrum. To achieve mode reconfigurability two pion diodes are inserted between the ports of antenna and radiating structure. Various antenna characteristics are discussed to provide the working mechanism of the antenna. Moreover, a brief comparison with state-of-the-art is performed to show the potential of methodology adopted to design proposed antenna.

articleTitle: Frequency Pulling Technique: A Demonstration of Bandwidth Increase on Dipole Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this work, we use the Frequency Pulling Technique (FPT) to increase the bandwidth of microstrip dipole antennas. Specifically, by properly feeding our dipole through two symmetrically selected points, we achieve a twofold increase in bandwidth compared to its conventional single-fed counter-part, all while maintaining its footprint unchanged. Our results demonstrate excellent performance.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Assisted Design for Series-Fed Microstrip Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: An efficient machine learning-assisted design for series-fed microstrip antenna arrays (SFMAA) is proposed using base element modeling (BEM), network cascade, discrete cosine transform (DCT), and array synthesis. Firstly, the SFMAA is characterized by several types of BE. Each BE is sampled and trained independently, greatly reducing the calculation burden. DCT is introduced for training the BE pattern to further reduce the computational cost. Finally, the responses of the SFMAA are approximated from the network cascade of BEs. Two practical array synthesis examples are simulated to validate the proposed method.

articleTitle: Advancing Spherical Near-Field Probe Technology: Design and Validation of High Precision Wideband 3dB/180° Couplers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A desirable feature of probes for Spherical Near Field (SNF) measurements is the absence of radiated higher order spherical modes in the pattern [1]. This implies that the probe pattern can be fully described by a linear interpolation of its principal plane patterns leading to a significant simplification in the NF/FF transformation when probe pattern compensation is included. Probes with such properties are inherently narrow band. Although probe correction algorithm for NF/FF transformation with any probe pattern are available [2], there is a need for probes approximating first-order performance across a large bandwidth. Traditional first-order probes rely on geometrically symmetric Ortho-Mode Junctions (OMJ) and externally balanced feeding. Such probes utilize couplers that ensure equal amplitude and opposite phase of the balanced feeding scheme [4]. This paper introduces the design and validation of a novel 3dB/180° coupler, based on the natural anti-symmetric properties of the electric field within the coupler to achieve quasi-perfect amplitude and opposite phase distribution. To realize these properties, an architecture based on slot coupling is selected. The coupler concept is suitable for various frequencies and has been realized at UHF to Ku-band, as a stand-alone cased component. The paper includes experimental data specifically at L/S-band, showcasing outstanding coupler performance concerning matching, balance, and isolation, aligning well with full-wave electromagnetic predictions. Furthermore, the study assesses measured probe design improvements due to enhanced coupler accuracy on a 1.4-4.2GHz SNF probe design [1].

articleTitle: Design of a Circularly Polarized Stacked Patch Antenna with Circular Ground Plane
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A circularly polarized stacked patch antenna operating in L-Band is proposed for satellite communications, including the Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS). The complete design process is presented, which consists of successive design steps described and motivated in the paper. Starting from a classical circular patch with dual 90-degree phased feed to achieve circular polarization, proper modifications are made in order to improve the antenna performance in terms of operational bandwidth and polarization purity so as to facilitate the transmission and reception of signals from satellites. The final antenna is a stacked patch consisting of a lower circular patch with circular ground plane and dual 90-degree phased feed, and an upper annular ring patch, separated by an air fill gap. Compared with a classical circular patch, the final proposal strongly extends the frequency range and improves the polarization purity, while maintaining relatively compact size and weight. Simulation results are provided while a prototype is currently being manufactured.

articleTitle: Exploring Similarities Between Inverse Problems in Microwave Imaging and Metasurface Design
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: We review the similarities between inverse problems in quantitative microwave imaging and metasurface design, aiming to facilitate the transfer of inversion techniques and algorithms between these two topics.

articleTitle: Enhanced Transmission through Sub-Wavelength Apertures with Covers of Self-Dual Layers: Theory and Experiment
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Coats of self-dual media (SDM), that cover the surfaces adjacent to small apertures in conducting screens, are capable of collecting electromagnetic energy from around the aperture and force it to funnel through it. This effect is due to the non-reflecting nature of the SDM, that allows no outlet for the energy except through the hole. Compared with a reference bare structure, an enhancement of several tens of dBs are seen in simulations, and close to 10 dB in initial experiment. Coating can reside on either side of the screen or on both sides, with further enhancement in the latter case. This structure is non-resonant, allowing for potentially wide band realizations depending on the bandwidth of the synthesized materials involved.

articleTitle: Revisiting Risley Prism Transmit-Array Antennas Using a Novel Co-Design Phase Correction Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Mechanical beam steering using two independent axially rotating metasurfaces (Risley Prism configuration) have proved to be a cost-effective solution for millimeter wave (mmW) antennas. Adapting this canonical beam steering concept from optics to mmW using metasurfaces (instead of wedge prisms) allows achieving a greater design flexibility. Many works have explored different ways of encoding the required phase correction. All of them implicitly implement three functionalities: i) beam collimation (i.e., plane wave conversion); ii) 1D beam tilting along a given axis; iii) 1D beam tilting along a second direction, the two tilting direction being set to produce the prescribed beam pointing direction. Conventionally, steps i) and ii) are solved by the first operating metasurface, which sets the phase delay profile of the second metasurface. Recently, the authors have shown an alternative approach where the beam collimation is performed by the combined effect of the two metasurfaces. Using 3D-printed perforated slabs we have previously demonstrated that this generalized approach is effective for the reduction of the side lobe level in the conventional case. In this communication, we will present alternative implementations of this concept to demonstrate the wider reach of our findings.

articleTitle: A Multi-Port Polarization Diversity Liquid Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A liquid dielectric resonator antenna is proposed to improve the polarization diversity for Wi-Fi applications at 2.45 GHz taking the advantage of fluidic behavior of the liquids. A combination of conventional and a novel feeding mechanism in terms of extended copper lines with vertical dielectric wall support is proposed to realize five polarization-independent modes of the HEM mode family. The liquid antenna exhibited good MIMO characteristics and decent far-field characteristics with the overall antenna profile being less than 0.24λ0.

articleTitle: RFID-Based Authenticated Parking System for All-Weather Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This article presents a robust packaged radio frequency identification (RFID) utilizing blockchain technology for parking system applications. The RFID tags (915 MHz) designed using a wide-band log-periodic antenna act as wireless markers with RFID readers mounted in the parking space, and record the vehicle and lane marker data with secure authentication. The vehicle user can access the RFID tag information through an embedded reader device for lane parking under snow or zero visibility conditions. These RF tags are designed to perform under all weather conditions with robust integration of RFID IC and antenna. The simulated design performances and measured reflection coefficient are presented as in addition to the fabricated prototype read range and received signal strength indicator (RSSI) measurements.

articleTitle: Hybrid Numerical Modeling Method for Josephson Traveling Wave Parametric Amplifiers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Josephson traveling wave parametric amplifiers are a leading tool for enabling readout of superconducting qubits. However, existing design tools for these devices struggle to effectively model variations in amplifier parameters, leading to inconsistencies between theoretical predictions and manufactured devices. This work develops a 1D hybrid numerical modeling approach for these devices that can easily incorporate amplifier property variations, allowing their impact to be considered in the design process. Here, the formulation of the method is introduced and validated against analytical results for a simple architecture. Future work will extend the technique to more advanced amplifier architectures, as well as develop similar methods for 3D full-wave modeling of these systems.

articleTitle: Time-Switched Metasurface Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This contribution presents the analysis and design of a novel class of metasurface-based antennas, whose radiative capabilities are enabled by the properties of the temporal and time-switched metamaterials. In particular, we consider a thin metasurface supporting the propagation of a surface wave that can switch instantaneously its surface impedance between two different values, resulting in a temporal interface. We demonstrate that the surface wave is instantaneously coupled to free space realizing a directive polychromatic beam at much higher frequency with respect to the frequency of the original surface wave. Analytical formulations and numerical simulations are provided to predict and verify the frequency upshift and the radiation characteristics of the proposed novel antenna.

articleTitle: Thermal Analysis of Implanted Antennas: Effect of Frequency on the Bioheat Modeling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this study, the effects of various terms of bioheat modeling of implanted antennas at different frequencies are studied. We numerically evaluated an implanted dipole antenna and the amount of heat generation in the adjacent body tissues for various frequencies and in each study considered the effect of different terms of the bioheat equation. The goal is to characterize the parameters of the selected thermal model at different operating frequencies to identify the most significant factors in heat generation and temperature regulation inside the body. We considered factors such as (i) blood perfusion, (ii) metabolic rate, and finally (iii) volume and surface thermal losses, at three operating frequencies of 0.433 GHz, 0.915 GHz, and 2.45 GHz. We found that as the operating frequency increases the effects of blood perfusion and volume thermal losses become more pronounced.

articleTitle: Reflecting Metasurface Design based on Statistical Local Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In the future wireless communication systems, Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RIS) and Smart Skins are playing an important role as disruptive metasurface-based technologies. Designing and fabricating such devices requires a precise modeling and construction methods. However, their performances could be impacted by unpredictability in mutual coupling, errors in the fabrication process, mechanical stress, and thermal deformations. These factors alter their local response, affecting the overall electromagnetic response. In this work, we demonstrate that it is possible to consider such unpredictable deviations already during the design process by using a statistically corrected local design approach. We analytically obtain a surface impedance profile transformation function that makes the metasurface to be more robust to such unpredictable errors. A proper set of numerical simulations demonstrates the robustness of such design considering an anomalous reflective metasurface operating at 10 GHz.

articleTitle: A Study on the Use of Convolutional Networks for RF Coverage Evaluations in Urban Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: U-nets are a type of Fully Convolutional Neural Network that has been widely adopted for image segmentation applications. In the present study, U-nets are applied to wide area prediction of radio propagation parameters in urban environment. Coverage maps are generated through simulations in a reference urban environment using a ray tracing tool. The generated dataset is then used to train and test the U-net. Preliminary results look promising.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Coded Holographic Surfaces for Compressive Channel Characterization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Accurate direction of arrival (DoA) estimations are of great importance for channel characterization and, in particular, for beam steering. In this regard, the use of computational imaging (CI) based solutions, such as reconfigurable coded holographic surfaces, can result in a significant hardware simplification with respect to array-based solutions. This contribution analyses the impact on the accuracy of Do <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex> estimations of the number of measurement modes (i.e., the number of significantly distinct radiation patterns considered in a reconfigurable holo-graphic surface) and the aperture size. Results show that medium size apertures and a moderate number of measurement modes enable accurate DoA estimations in the context of a single far-field source, and also when multiple sources are present. Hence, this illustrates the potential of CI-based solutions for DoA estimation.

articleTitle: A Dual-Polarized Filtering Patch Antenna for 60-GHz Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a dual-polarized filtering patch antenna working in the 60-GHz band. By proposing the Y-shaped feeding scheme, the center-shorted C-strips, and the stepped SIW feeding structure, three radiation nulls are generated for a bandpass response. The center-shorted C-strips also contribute to gain enhancement in the passband. Finally, wide impedance bandwidths of more than 20% are attained for both polarization states. The simulated maximum realized gains of Ports 1 and 2 reach 9.9 and 9.77 dBi, respectively. High suppression levels of over 21 dB are obtained in the lower and upper stopbands.

articleTitle: Cross-Polarization Reduction of Shorted Patch Antenna Based on Stacked Coupled Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a cross-polarization reduction design of shorted patch antenna (SPA) is proposed based on a stacked coupled structure. The stacked SPA can introduce coupled resonant modes, specifically the odd mode and even mode. The odd mode with reversed-phase electric field on two SPAs inherently exhibits low cross-polarization level (XPL). A magnetic current analysis is provided to illustrate the principle of cross-polarization discrimination. To ensure the dominance of the odd mode within the desired frequency band, a slot is introduced on the patch in the middle layer, independently lowering the resonant frequency of the even mode. The results indicate that the XPL in the H-plane is exceeds 46.6 dB throughout the operating bandwidth, reaching a peak XPL of 51.4 dB. Compared to conventional SPAs, the proposed antenna demonstrates superior radiation performance in terms of XPL.

articleTitle: Preliminary Study of RF-Induced Heating of DBS and RNS Devices under 1.5 T MRI
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
