abstract: In this paper, a preliminary comparative analysis of the radiofrequency (RF)-induced heating of Active Implantable Medical Devices (AIMDs), specifically Deep Brain Stimulation (DBS) and Responsive Neurostimulation (RNS) devices, is presented following the guidelines outlined in ISO- TSI0974. Combining the device models or transfer functions and the tangential component of the incident electric fields along clinically relevant lead trajectories, the lead-tip heating is calculated in an anatomically accurate human model for simplified DBS and RNS systems. The findings of the study indicate that the clinical routing convention used during shorter RNS device placement can lead to significant e -field cancelations, resulting in lower RF -induced heating under Magnetic Resonance (MR) conditions.

articleTitle: Wideband Wide-Scanning Circular Polarization Reconfigurable Phased Array Based on 45-Degree Polarized Probe-Fed Dipole Element Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A wideband wide-scanning circular polarization reconfigurable phased array antenna (CPRPAA) is proposed in this paper. The 45-degree polarized print probe-fed dipole antenna is used as elements. Sequential rotation is applied to achieve circular polarization (CP). Results show that the infinite array unit cell achieves about 22.2% bandwidth with active <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{VSWR} \leq \mathbf{3}$</tex> when steering <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm \mathbf{60}^{\circ}$</tex> in all planes. Simulation results of an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{8}\times \mathbf{8}$</tex> (64 element) array illustrate that the presented CPRPAA exhibits a gain fluctuation less than 4.9 dB. Furthermore, the ARs are below 3.7 dB when scanning to 60° in all plane over the whole working band.

articleTitle: Distorted Circular Shaped Scalar Impedance Modulated Circularly Polarized Holographic Metasurface Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A Homogeneous meta unit-cell loaded highly directive Scalar Surface Impedance Modulated (SSIM) Holographic Metasurface (HMS) based distorted circular shaped Leaky-wave antenna (LWA) is proposed in this work. Quarter wavelength monopole fed proposed surface gives a highly directive circularly polarized beamforming along θ =ϕ=O° with a peak gain of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G_{max}=24.25$</tex> dBi at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f_{r}=13.25$</tex> GHz. Progressively phase shifted proposed holographic metasurface based leaky-wave antenna (HMSLWA) gives a highly circular polarization (CP) effect at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f_{r}={16.02}$</tex> GHz towards desired beamforming. A half-power beam width (HPBW) and sidelobe level (SLL) of 7.49° & 18.64 dB is reported.

articleTitle: PET Based Flexible Intelligent Reflective Surface for Millimeter-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a novel millimeter wave (mmWave) Polyethylene Terephthalate (PET) based flexible intelligent reflective surface (IRS) unit cell for commercial 5G communication applications. A single bit IRS operation is achieved by employing a switch mechanism in the metasurface to introduce a controlled 180°phase shift in reflection mode of the IRS between ON and OFF states. The geometry of the proposed metasurface unit cell allows for a transverse electric (TE) polarized reflection with an azimuthal angular stability of 20°. The amplitude of reflection is greater than 65% throughout the operational band of 27 GHz to 29 GHz. This flexible and digitally programmable metasurface can be used in commercial 5G applications requiring features such as beam focusing and beam steering.

articleTitle: Optimization of Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces for Enhanced Beam Manipulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Reconfigurable intelligent surfaces can manipulate incident waves in a dynamic way. In this work, a varactor-loaded RIS is designed and simulated for steering and shaping the reflected beam. The design is based on optimization that treats the RIS as a set of surface impedance strips above a grounded substrate and takes into account all coupling effects. This approach leads to a framework with increased accuracy and enhanced beamforming capabilities as enabled by the excitation of near-field interactions. Beam-steering up to ±60° and the realization of a sector pattern are verified with full-wave simulations.

articleTitle: Parallel Accelerated SAR Image Simulation Based on High Frequency Approximation Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The simulation of Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) image is of great significance to the analysis and interpretation of target scattering characteristics. High frequency approximation techniques combined with ray tracing is a very suitable method for SAR image simulation. Compared with the numerical methods, they can calculate the scattered field of electrically large targets in a short period of time. However, both the ray tracing process and SAR's unique pulse accumulation process result in a very long calculation time. Using CPU+GPU parallel computing technology, a SAR image acceleration simulation algorithm based on high frequency approximation techniques is designed in this paper. Both CPU and GPU parallel computing techniques are used to accelerate the time-consuming process of SAR simulation. The experimental results show that the simulated SAR image can be obtained in a shorter time by parallel acceleration of CPU+GPU.

articleTitle: Correlating Mobile Antenna Topologies with Received Signal Strength-based Direction-of-Arrival Estimation Method for Sub-Degree Accuracy within Indoor Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Various types of Indoor Positioning Systems (IPS) are developed to address the limitations of Global Positioning Systems (GPS) for indoor wireless positioning applications. To achieve highly accurate IPS, multiple, high directional antennas are required. However, mobile devices and smart tags cannot accommodate such antenna requirements due to limited space. This work presents a method to utilize conventional mobile antennas to achieve sub-degree accuracy of IPS. Key mobile antenna design factors, such as directivity and tilting angle are incorporated with a newly devised Received Signal Strength (RSS)-based DoA method to achieve high-quality positioning performance. Using the Received Signal Strength Difference (RSSD) slope enables the design and support employment of a realistic mobile antenna featuring a small size and limited directivity for accurate IPS characteristics. The exemplified low directivity antennas achieve a DoA accuracy of 0.87° at 6.5 GHz. Compared to the method in [4], this approach reduces the root-mean-square error (RMSE) of the DoA estimation by one-fifth and halves the electrical size. Consequently, this enables the realization of highly compact portable devices for accurate IPS with the devised exemplified antenna design and allows for expansion to different mobile antenna designs.

articleTitle: An Electrically Small Antenna with Circularly Polarized Electron Spin Precessions (E-Spin)
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents an electrically small antenna (ka = 0.2) that leverages on the circularly polarized electron spin precessions for radiation. The antenna design attains a measured realized gain of −4.5 dB and an axial ratio of 2.8 dB at 3.360 GHz. This antenna configuration is well-suited for direct antenna modulation as it can swiftly adjust resonant frequencies through the modulation on the biasing magnetic field.

articleTitle: Artificial Neural Network Topology for Modelling of Symmetrical Dipole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: We present results for various possible compromises for topologies of artificial neural networks used for modeling of the gain and the input impedance of thin-wire symmetrical dipoles. The maximal electrical length of considered dipoles is 20 wavelengths. Experiments are done using a dataset of 10,000 different dipole antennas, obtained by 3D EM simulations. The results show that deeper networks, with more than six hidden layers, are capable of modeling electromagnetic response of considered symmetrical dipoles with mean absolute errors within 1 % of maximal values, while speeding up the calculation for at least order of magnitude.

articleTitle: Automatic Generation and Substitution of Placeholders for a MATLAB-HFSS Interface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The process of connecting full-wave simulators with numeric computing environments is typically done using application programming interfaces. These interfaces involve replacing the variables in the project file with placeholders, which can be a challenging task for designs with numerous variables. This paper demonstrates a method for automatically generating and replacing these placeholders. The interface between MATLAB and HFSS is used as an example, and it is applied to analyze a patch antenna.

articleTitle: Single Feed Slot-Loaded Dual Band Planar Antenna for CubeSat Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A dual band (S and X) Antenna has been proposed in this article for the communication subsystem of CubeSat, a popular miniature satellite among enthusiasts and researchers. The antenna body has a dimension of 100mm×100mm×24.315mm in total. Using a combination of two planar antenna types, i.e. slot and patch, this compact antenna offers 11.11% of S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>≤ −10 dB bandwidth and 1.33% of Axial Ratio (AR) bandwidth in the S-band, as well as 2.32% of S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>≤ −10 dB bandwidth and 1.16% of AR Bandwidth in the X-band. While the S-band patch demonstrates a high circular polarization (CP) gain of 9.035dB, the X-band slot antenna provides a moderate 4.65dB CP gain. This antenna is suitable for dual band operations enabling uplink and downlink communications from a single antenna, which will reduce the number of antennas needed in the conventional approach.

articleTitle: Unconventional Array Architectures for Next Generation Non-Terrestrial Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this work, the problem of designing unconventional phased array architectures for non-terrestrial networks is addressed. A review of array synthesis methods for cost-effective designs is presented, demonstrating the feasibility of employing simplified and modular array architectures for space-oriented applications. An illustrative numerical example is provided to demonstrate the effectiveness and advantages of unconventional tiled arrays for uplink communication with low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite constellations.

articleTitle: Distributed Memory Parallelization for Fast Volume Integral Equation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we show distributed memory parallelization for the Method of Moment fast volume integral equation using the task bucket algorithm. The fast volume integral equation is computed using Adaptive Cross Approximation based multi-level H-Matrix. The near-field and far-field block matrix is distributed using a task bucket. Individual MPI process computes the near and far-field matrices in each task bucket, and after computation, the matrices can be used to compute parallel matrix-vector products for iterative solutions.

articleTitle: Dual Polarized Broadcast Waveguide Antenna Exploiting 3D Printing Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper a dual polarized coverage with approximate cosecant square beam-shaping antenna array is designed at 39GHz for 6G communication. The beam-shaping feeding network as well as the radiation elements are realized with square waveguide such as both vertical and horizontal shaped beams are produced with an unified antenna structure. This antenna is fabricated with 3D additive printing process. Measured results are compared with simulations. This design is also scalable for higher EIPR or ability to scan in the other plane making this proposed antenna a good candidate for next generation communications.

articleTitle: Characteristic Mode Analysis of Nanostructures using Hydrodynamic Volume Integral Equation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The characteristic mode analysis (CMA) is formulated and implemented for the hydrodynamic volume integral equation (HDVIE) that is used to mathematically model electromagnetic field interactions and conduction current dynamics on nanoantennas and nanoscatterers. The proposed method produces excitation-independent characteristic hydrodynamic currents and the corresponding modal significance curves, providing useful information that can be used to optimize the performance of a nanoantenna. Numerical results demonstrate the reliability and the applicability of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Quantum Optimization Methods for Unconventional Antenna Arrays Design
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this work, a novel methodology for the design of unconventional phased arrays characterized by a thinned layout and aimed at the suppression of interference signals is presented. The Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA), namely a hybrid quantum-classical optimization strategy, is employed to find a thinning configuration able to suppress the interfering power coming from know direction. In order to enable the use of the QAOA, the interference suppression objective is properly reformulated as an Hamiltonian energy minimization problem.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a Planar Lens Antenna Based on a Gradient-Index Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a Ka-band planar 3D-printed metasurface lens antenna based on gradient-index materials. The glide-symmetric unit cells with different values of the infill percentages are utilized to achieve the gradient index and phase-controllable material for alignment of the transmitted wave in the desired direction. The designed planar lens is fabricated and measured at 26.5-40 GHz. The measured return loss and realized gain are about -12 dB and 23 dBi, respectively, which agree with the simulated results. The designed lens antenna is a good candidate for 5G/6G communication and radar systems.

articleTitle: On the Problem of Focused Wave-beam Maximum Wireless Power Transfer beyond a Stratification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this contribution, we state and discuss the problem of focused wave-beam maximum wireless transfer beyond a planar multilayer structure at microwaves and millimeter waves. Moving from a general analytical model of the problem, based on plane-wave expansion of the impinging wave-beam upon the stratification, the wireless power transfer efficiency is firstly defined and then maximized by changing beam relevant parameters. In addition, to preserve beam focalization beyond the multilayer, the problem is formulated in terms of a constrained optimization problem. As a special case, Bessel-shaped beams are considered as impinging beam on the multilayer. The applications of the proposed approach are quite broad, and span from microwave heating to through-the-wall radars.

articleTitle: A 300GHz Mixer-First Receiver with Microbump AoC for Software Defined Radio
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presented a mixer-first receiver for software defined radio at 300 GHz. It employs a differential microbump antenna-on-chip (AoC) with exceptional radiation gain and efficiency. The AoC and mixer are then connected via a matching network, which enhances both conversion gain and noise figure of the mixer. At the RF front-end stage, the receiver achieves a peak mixer conversion gain of 14.6dB, a maximum total receiving gain of 23 dB, and a lowest noise figure of 13dB.

articleTitle: Measurement Considerations of FSS Absorber in Free Space
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Microwave absorber measurement is a quite challenging process. Ideally it involves doing the measurement in an anechoic chamber which itself is quite expensive. This article involves measuring radar cross section reduction of an absorber in the free space. This measurement has been carried out using an X-band absorber and shows good match with simulation as well as measurement in anechoic chamber. If done correctly, this setup can be extended for higher frequencies as well.

articleTitle: Pattern-Reconfigurable SIW H-Plane Horn Antenna Using Extended Metallic Planes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A substrate-integrated waveguide (SIW) H-plane horn antenna with reconfigurable pattern capability is presented. The proposed design utilizes extensions of the upper/lower metal planes that form the SIW horn to reflect the radiated wave in the desired direction. Each extension is loaded with two sets of 6-pin diodes that activate the upper or lower extended metallic planes required for reflecting the wave. The antenna operates at 9.4-10 GHz and has a compact size of 40 × 49.6 × 3.17 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, The antenna can reconfigure its beam in the E-plane to radiate at ±34° with a half-power beamwidth of 68.6<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∘</sup>and a simulated peak efficiency of 92%. The proposed concept facilitates further development opportunities using different configurations.

articleTitle: mm-wave Mobile Handset Antenna with Beam Steering Capability for 5G Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this manuscript, a wideband beam switching capable mm-wave slotted antenna with higher gain is designed followed by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1\times 4$</tex> array for 5G mm-wave applications. The proposed structure operates from 24.2 to 29.6 GHz covering n257 and n258 bands. By switching the PIN diode, radiation switches from broadside to -x broadside direction with peak gain of 11.4 dBi and 10.9 dBi, respectively. The proposed <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1\times 4$</tex> PIN diode controlled slot antenna array can perform beam steering of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 30^{\circ}$</tex>.

articleTitle: A Wideband Bidirectional Filtering Slot Antenna with Three Slots
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a wideband bidirectional filtering slot antenna is proposed. Conventional slot antennas have narrow bandwidth and low frequency selectivity. First, the impedance bandwidth of the slot antenna is increased by using the shorting branch feedline. Second, two parasitic slots are introduced for electronic and magnetic coupling with the driven slot, with radiating nulls on each side of the passband to increase frequency selectivity. The proposed filtering slot antenna achieves <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\vert S11\vert < -10dB$</tex> within the 4.03GHZ-5.96GHZ(38.6%), an in-band gain of 3.91-5.78 dBi and an out-of-band radiation suppression more than 13.73 dB.

articleTitle: An Improved-Gain Omnidirectional Circularly Polarized Antenna Based on Helical Dipoles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a circularly polarized omnidirectional antenna based on an inclined dipole structure. The antenna features four helix-shaped dipoles distributed evenly around the cylinder, exhibiting a helical arrangement with 1.5 turns on the cylindrical surface. By exciting all four pairs of dipoles with equal amplitude and in phase, the antenna achieves omnidirectional circular polarization with an improved gain compared to conventional half-wavelength dipole elements. Optimization of various design parameters has yielded a relative bandwidth of 6.8% (1.54 GHz to 1.65 GHz) with a return loss better than 10 dB, a gain higher than 3.5 dBi, and an axial ratio less than 2 dB. Moreover, the gain variation in the azimuth plane is less than 1 dB.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a Phased Array System for Indoor Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents the development and testing of a compact, low-cost phased array system capable of precise electronic beam steering. Through the integration of digitally-controlled phase shifters into a series-fed antenna array panel, the proposed system enables adaptive directional control of the radiation pattern at 3.75 GHz. Preliminary results obtained from an anechoic chamber validate the effectiveness of the system in reliably steering the antenna beam to specified angles between 0 and 90 degrees. The streamlined architecture, minimizing component count and complexity, demonstrates a scalable and cost-effective solution for emerging beamforming applications, including 5G communications and radar.

articleTitle: MiWEndo: Preclinical and Clinical Trials to Evaluate the Feasibility of a Microwave Endoscopic System to Detect Colorectal Polyps
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper we reported on the iterative process of design, development, and validation of the first microwave endoscopy system from the ideation until its validation in patients. The device demonstrated polyp detection performance in preclinical studies and safety in clinical trials.

articleTitle: Performance of the Radome Enclosed Multi-Beam Phased Array Antenna at Shock Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Multi-Beam Phase Array Antenna are designed to tight tolerances in shock environment. A numerical and standard statistical method can be applied to investigate the variation of the following key parameters; Antenna Gain degradation, Side-lobe perturbation, Beam-width variation and Beam Pointing Error (BPE). Their subsequent effect on operation of the array antenna will be examined in detail. The importance of radome will also be assessed as well.

articleTitle: Design of Vertical SRR Based Absorber for RCS Reduction of Aircraft Equipped with Lightening Strike Protection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a vertical split ring resonator (SRR) based absorber has been designed along with copper mesh for lightening strike protection. The magnetic resonance due to copper mesh has been utilized to design Vertical SRR based absorber. The absorption of more than 90 % is achieved at the resonant frequency of 9.2 GHz and 12.7 GHz. The structure is stable for oblique incidence upto 45 degree and as the structure is non symmetric it give polarization sensitive behaviour. The proposed structure is light weight and ultra thin vertical SRR based absorber with the thickness of 2.5 mm. It can be used with commercially available copper mesh of standard dimensions used in aviation industry.

articleTitle: Millimeter Wave Dual Linearly Polarized Antenna Array for Ultra-Wideband Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A millimeter wave dual linearly polarized microstrip antenna array is proposed for ultra-wideband communications. To achieve the dual linear polarization, the microstrip antenna unit is fed by a two-port slit coupling. The bandwidth of the antenna is expanded by loading parasitic patches. By reasonably designing the feed network of the antenna array, the isolation is improved while realizing efficient feeding. The antenna achieves dual linearly polarized radiation at 33–37 GHz with a maximum gain of 11 dBi and more than 15 dB isolation.

articleTitle: Design of a Smart Watch Tri-Band GPSBluetooth-WiFi5 Square Loop Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A square loop antenna that works for three frequency bands is considered. The three frequency bands are L1 GPS (1.575 GHz), Bluetooth (2.400 GHz to 2.483 GHz), and WiFi5 (5.150 GHz to 5.850 GHz). This antenna has dimensions of 36 mm by 45 mm by 5 mm. It is on top of a 0.4 mm thick dielectric substrate that has copper cladding on one side. The square loop itself is composed of thin copper sheets with a thickness of 0.3 mm. The antenna is designed to have a compact size for potential use for smart watches. It has two shorting strips that connect the ground plane to the loop itself at two different locations. There is also an air gap in the loop. The shorting portions and the air gap create the operating bands in the desired frequencies.

articleTitle: STRx–Transmission and Reception System with Electronical Orientation for LEO SatCom Constellations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This article presents a Portuguese research project (STRx) that developed a transmission and reception phased array system composed of a scalable radiating part integrated with RF electronics, for use in mobile terminals that communicate with LEO and MEO satellite constellations. The modular and compact structure, combined with its great versatility and the operation in the K/Ka bands makes these antennas suitable to the communication requirements for use in such terminals.

articleTitle: Meta-Wall Integrted Substrate Antenna for Millimeter-Wave Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A wideband substrate meta-antenna fitting into the technology of printed circuit boards is presented at millimeter wave. In this design, A novel approach for designing antennas based on meta-wall is proposed for the first time, which is a completely integrated structure. Unlike the classical independent structure, we resolve multiple radiation modes within an entire structure by designing both dielectric and metallic metasurface. The intentional radiation modes can be bound in a fixed part, leading to the similar radiation performance as dielectric resonator antenna. We believe that this design further integrates the design of antenna and metasurface and can provide a reference for future device. The simulated results show that the proposed antenna can form an array easily with wideband and low-profile, which can also provide basic beam scanning characteristics.

articleTitle: 140 GHz Small Horn-type Antenna with Sanchez's Ridge Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper describes Sanchez's ridge waveguide (SRWG), and small horn-type antennas that are fed by the SRWG. The SRWG was manufactured by a resin injection molding method (high productivity, low cost) and a CNC milling method (precision, high cost). Although the injection molding method results in rounded edges, it was confirmed that the same performance as the CNC milling method can be obtained by optimizing the shape. Next, small horn-type antennas for 140 GHz, which were assumed to be integrated into the SRWG, were considered. One was a pyramidal small horn-type antenna and the other was a quadrate small horn-type antenna. The apertures were designed to have a short side of approximately 2 mm considering array antenna integration. The maximum gain was 13.2 dBi with direct waveguide feeding and 12.7 dBi via SRWG.

articleTitle: A 94-GHz On-Chip Metasurface Antenna Through Characteristic Mode Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Antenna-on-Chip (AoC) technology has been increasingly recognized for its multiple advantages, particularly for applications requiring miniaturization and integration. Typically, AoC uses metasurface (MTS) primarily as a reflection component. However, this work presents a compact AoC using the MTS as a radiator. The MTS consists of four strips embedded between two thin silicon dioxide layers. Although individually challenging to isolate, the nine closely spaced modes identified through Characteristic Mode Analysis (CMA) enhance the antenna's versatility, enabling diverse radiation patterns through adjustments in feed type and position. For example, employing a single microstrip yields a maximum gain of 2.5 dB at around 94.55 GHz, while a double microstrip configuration achieves a gain of -0.5 dB at 94.5 GHz with diverse radiation patterns. We use proximity coupling to avoid the modifications to the ground plane, which works as a shield from the lossy silicon (Si).

articleTitle: Instantaneous Creatinine Testing in Urine Using a Modified Bifilar Helix Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a highly sensitive, chemical-free bifilar helix antenna that is dedicated to the instantaneous assay of creatinine in urine. At its core, the proposed antenna structure leverages the behavior of the transmitted and reflected electromagnetic waves propagating through a sample under test and captures the changes in the scattering parameters caused by variations in the composition of the loading sample. To accentuate the sensitivity of the bifilar helix towards changes in the creatinine levels, a slotted cylinder surrounding the sample holding a plastic polyactic acid (PLA) tube is added. The recorded changes in the scattering parameters are subjected to machine learning and data analytics techniques to translate these changes into creatinine level estimations. The proposed resulting sensor is validated on artificial urine as well as animal and human urine samples. Testing conducted on urine samples collected from rats demonstrated high sensitivity towards changes in the creatinine composition. Moreover, clinical measurements on human urine samples reported high accuracy of 93%. These results reveal the outstanding capability of the sensor to provide instantaneous creatinine screening.

articleTitle: Ultra-Wideband and Low-profile Dual-Polarized Linear Array Based on Structure Reuse Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, an ultra-wideband and low-profile dual-polarized linear array composed of folding dipole and slot antenna is proposed. The slot antennas, which are vertically placed on both sides of the dipole, can radiate vertical polarization (VP) waves, and their metal parts can be regarded as perfect electric conductor (PEC) walls perpendicular to the dipole direction. The dipole, which radiates horizontal polarization (HP) waves, is folded to improve impedance matching. By reusing the structure of the slot antenna, we apply PEC boundary compensation to the HP dipole without deteriorating the performance of the VP slot antenna. Compared to previous work, the proposed <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1\times 13$</tex> array does not use high-loss materials such as ferrite, thus achieving higher realized gain. Simulated results show that the proposed antenna achieves a 5:1 bandwidth (0.4-2-GHz) with active VSWR <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$< 3.5$</tex> when scanning up to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 60^{\circ}$</tex> for VP and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 45^{\circ}$</tex> for HP, respectively. The overall array size is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.34\lambda_{\text{low}}\times 0.14\lambda_{\text{low}}\times 0.12\lambda_{\text{low}}$</tex> at the lowest operating frequency of 0.4 GHz.

articleTitle: Design of an Integrated K-Band SWL for Enhanced Bandwidth in Microstrip Circuits
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a new K-band surface wave launcher (SWL) engineered to overcome the conventional challenges of bandwidth and integration in microwave circuits. The design features a fully integrated, planar structure with a novel via perimeter for interference shielding, built on a single-layer Rogers RO3210 substrate. It incorporates a grounded coplanar waveguide (GCPW) line, substrate-integrated waveguide (SIW) structures and transitions, and a multi-slot configuration for mode conversion. Simulation results show the SWL's broad impedance bandwidth of 56%, spanning nearly the full K-band range, and its capability for low-leakage power radiation. The design's scalability and integration potential with various circuit components position it as an advantageous solution for modern high-frequency system designs.

articleTitle: Design of a Multifunctional Protective Cover for X-Band Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This article introduces a vertical cross-polarized antenna array operating in the X-band. To address external-array stealth and internal-array coupling issues, two radomes were designed. The stealth radome consists of two-dimensional passive frequency selection units, optimizing the RCS performance of the array and achieving in-band wave transmission along with out-of-band wave absorption. The decoupling radome is comprised of the array element decoupling surface, recombinant dielectric layer, and frequency-selective absorbing layer. This design simultaneously optimizes the coupling between array elements and improves the overall array performance. The interaction between the two radomes is minimized, resulting in a comprehensive multi-functional protective cover.

articleTitle: Overcoming the Bandwidth-Efficiency Product Limitations of Electrically Small Antennas Using A Class-E, Non-LTI HF Antenna Design
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: We present a switched-mode, non-linear-time- invariant (non-LTI) electrically-small antenna (ESA) designed to overcome the bandwidth-efficiency product limitations governing the performances of passive, LTI ESAs. The non-LTI ESA is designed by integrating a class-E, switched-mode inverter, designed to act as an ideal voltage source, with an electrically- small, resonant radiator. Digitally-modulated waveforms are generated directly at the antenna stage by controlling the bias voltage and/or the gate driver signal of the class-E inverter. We demonstrate that this non-LTI transmitting ESA is capable of offering bandwidth-efficiency product improvement of 10 dB or more over a passively-matched ESA at the HF band.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Modeling of Mechanically-Controlled Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In the ever-evolving landscape of wireless commu-nication and radar systems, Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RIS) have emerged as a transformative technology. This paper investigates the behavior of RIS using mechanical control. The authors performed parametric EM simulations of RIS single elements with different states of mechanical angles within the frequency range of 24–30 GHz. The optimum design of a unit cell for RIS performance depends on the shape of the array elements; hence, the EM simulation of the full array with the optimum element pattern provides valuable insights into the behavior of RIS.

articleTitle: Fully Digital AESA Antennas Testing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Nowadays digitalization is becoming more and more pervasive in most scientific fields. Radar technology is not an exception and fully digital systems are becoming attractive thanks to recent developments of digital architectures. The conventional RF antenna testing approach cannot be applied to fully digital phased array systems. This paper resumes a series of strategies and considerations about the generation of a reference signal in the RF domain to be used to compensate the phase variation over the measurement time. The proposed measurement setup for fully digital AESA (Active Electronically Scanned Array) systems consists of a couple of I-Q modulator and demodulator, locked to the system under test in order to ensure phase coherence of transmitting and receiving pulses.

articleTitle: Multifunctional Reconfigurable Antenna Design Based on Energy Disturbance Characteristics of Parasitic Structures
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This study explores the potential application of utilizing the energy disturbance characteristics of parasitic structures for the design of radiation pattern reconfigurable antenna. The Poynting streamline method is utilized as an auxiliary analytical tool to intuitively analyze the energy flow characteristics of a parasitic dipole under different load conditions. Based on this analysis, a multifunctional reconfigurable antenna with controllable beam direction and beamwidth was designed. The provided simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of this method.

articleTitle: Hybrid Additive-Manufactured Gradient-Index Lenses with Low-Profile and High Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This work combines multiple 3D-printed materials to extend the range of realizable dielectric constants <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(D_{k})$</tex> for compact, additively manufactured GRIN lenses. A low-loss, high-permittivity alumina core allows the lens to be thin relative to the diameter and a low-loss, lower-permittivity resin (Radix 2.8) shell is used to matched the core to free-space for improved efficiency. A 10-inch diameter, 2.1-inch thick, Ku-band (12–18 GHz) prototype lens is presented with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$>$</tex> 57% aperture efficiency and a radiation efficiency <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$>$</tex> 80% across the band. Beam-scan performance is discussed and recommendations for improvements are provided.

articleTitle: Permittivity Inversion from Double Bounce Scattering Using One Co-Polarization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Extending upon previous work, a method for separately inverting permittivities from a double bounce scattering is proposed here which utilizes two independent monostatic RADAR measurements in Hh polarization. The derivation of the method is outlined, which is then followed by validation through electromagnetic simulations. The results emphasize the efficiency of the proposed technique, showcasing its practicality, making it a potential candidate for permittivity inversion from far-field measurements, for example, on Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) images.

articleTitle: Wideband Mm-wave Electromagnetic Absorber Utilizing Resistively Loaded Crosses
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper investigates an ultrathin, single-layer and low-profile wideband absorber based on resistively-loaded high impedance surfaces for low millimeter wave frequency range. The proposed design features a dipole-like resonator incorporating a core component of resistive ohmic sheet. The absorber exhibits remarkable absorption characteristics, achieving an absorption bandwidth spanning from 18 to 40 GHz, maintaining an average absorption rate exceeding 90 %. Moreover, an analytical model based on RLC components for the designed absorber has been developed to verify the precision of the simulation results.

articleTitle: Analytic Differential Admittance Operator for Tangential Dipole Illumination of a Dielectric Sphere
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, the exact differential surface admittance (DSA) operator for scattering analysis of a homogeneous dielectric sphere is constructed. By utilizing two sets of orthogonal vector spherical harmonics as the basis functions for a Galerkin Method of Moments, the operator in question is obtained analytically. In comparison with the Mie series solution for a tangential electric dipole as source, a combination of the electric field integral equation and the DSA is shown to produce the same result within 12 digits of accuracy, laying the foundations for a subsequent analysis into the operator's fundamental properties.

articleTitle: A Simplified All-Frequency Stable Formulation with an Implicit Coulomb Gauge
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A potential-based finite element formulation has been developed in the past to circumvent the low-frequency breakdown issues commonly encountered in electromagnetic (EM) simulations of low-frequency and multiscale problems. In this formulation, the magnetic vector and electric scalar potentials have been employed to express the electric field and magnetic flux, leading to a set of two equations that represents all four Maxwell's equations and the current continuity equation. To enforce the Coulomb gauge, an auxiliary potential has been introduced, which results in a total of three equations to be solved simultaneously. To reduce the number of equations and unknowns needed in a simulation, a simplified formulation is proposed in this paper to enforce the Coulomb gauge implicitly without the need for the auxiliary potential. A numerical example is given to demonstrate the accuracy of the proposed formulation.

articleTitle: Scalability of Full Wave and Asymptotic Solvers for Austin RCS Benchmark Aircraft
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, analysis of the scalability of solvers and parallel processes has been performed for Altair Feko by using the aircraft models from University of Texas (UT) Austin's RCS Benchmark Suite. Simulation runtime and memory requirements were compared between Feko's full wave solvers and asymptotic solvers to analyze the trade-offs of simulations by switching between solvers. Runtime and memory were also compared to see the benefits of increasing the number of parallel processes used for these simulations.

articleTitle: A new DBFN ground station for European Launcher TM Tracking
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a new ground station for European launcher TM communication in S-Band based on a full Digital BeamForming Network (DBFN) technology. This paper will focus on the proposed antenna array shaped for the specific case of launcher tracking. The signal digitalization strategy and beamforming processing will be also presented, with a smart parallelization between the available FPGA and CPU. Finally the simulation demonstrate the DBFN performance, while the capacity to track several launcher stages with one ground station, without knowing the Directions Of Arrivals (DOA) of the TM signals. This DBFN ground station was developed in the frame of the CNES R&T project.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Inversion Regularized by a Plug-and-Play Deep Neural Network Denoiser
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A plug-and-play scheme that relies on a deep neural network for image denoising is used to regularize the nonlinear electromagnetic (EM) inversion. It is shown that any state-of-the-art denoiser can be plugged into the conventional inversion framework as an implicit regularization step. Thus, a pretrained Swin-Conv-UNet (SCUNet) is employed in the EM inversion. SCUNet combines the advantages of residual convolutional layers and swin transformer blocks in accounting for different image priors and it is remarkably effective in image denoising. Nu-merical results obtained using this framework clearly shows its benefits over existing inversion algorithms.

articleTitle: Diagnosis of Array Antennas Element Faults Based on R-CNN Using Near-Field Data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper reports the method of using near-field electric field data to detect array antenna feed faults based on region-based convolutional neural network (R-CNN). Four different models are trained by the same neural network to compare the effects of the element feed faults on the feature extraction and classification accuracy. It is shown that the four types of array antenna radiative state can be detected and classified, and the accuracy is up to 96.93%.

articleTitle: Simulation of Thermodynamic Effect for Packaged Enclosures
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: LDMOS power tubes have a wide range of applications in electronic systems such as radar, communication base stations, wireless broadcasting towers, etc. However, with the increase in operating power, the requirements for heat dissipation and reliability of the packaged enclosure are also more severe. Therefore, in this paper, a thermodynamic coupling method is proposed to analyze the multilayer ceramic housings with the finite difference time domain method. By setting the temperature load, fixed displacement and other boundary conditions, the deformation distribution of the encapsulated shell can be obtained. Thus, the accuracy and the efficiency of the proposed algorithm are verified by comparing the numerical simulation with the commercial software.

articleTitle: A Virtual Test Drive Method for V2X Technology in Automotive Industry
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: With the interest in connectivity and particularly Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) technology emerging in the automotive industry, optimized integration and testing of V2X becomes a key differentiator for car manufacturers. Traditional drive tests require multiple test vehicles, road infrastructure and integrated hardware and software to ensure data collection. In contrast, virtual test drive (VTD) simulation could save thousand hours of physical test drive. It can be performed in a purely virtual environment, which is repeatable and can be used to support antenna selection, package location studies and system performance analysis. In this paper, a V2X VTD test scenario is created to reproduce a physical test drive and demonstrates a high level of correlation.

articleTitle: Optimizing Wireless Power Transfer: Advanced Multi-Relay-Coil Design with Chebyshev Filter Theory
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In current wireless power transfer (WPT) research, one of the focuses is to make the transmission efficiency independent of distance and misalignments or electrically independent of mutual inductances. This paper presents a systematic way of designing such multi-relay coil WPT systems by developing the filter equivalence theory. High filter orders then correspond to multi relay coils for better performances. Simulations and measurements of the prototypes show the proposed design method can achieve a stable transmission efficiency within a defined range of mutual inductance variations, making the WPT system robust against changes in transmission distances and misalignments of the relay coils.

articleTitle: Ray-Tracing Based Inversion for Buried Pipelines in Layered Media Using 3-D Multistatic Imaging Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Detecting and localizing buried pipelines is an important problem in infrastructure mapping and maintenance. As opposed to the traditional monostatic ground penetrating radar (GPR), multistatic subsurface synthetic aperture radar (SAR) provides more information about buried targets through the diversity in incident and scattering angles. However, interpreting the collected data by multistatic subsurface SAR is more challenging especially for extended targets such as pipelines whose scattering phase centers change as a function of the relative position between the transmitter and the receiver. In this paper, a ray-tracing approach is proposed to track the multistatic radar signals as they travel from the transmitter to the receiver refracting through the layered ground media and scattering off buried pipelines. After ray-tracing, focusing based inversion is achieved by compensating for propagation phase associated with the rays and summing the phase compensated signals coherently across multiple receiver positions and frequencies. Full-wave simulation results show significant improvement in focusing performance through multiple layers compared to a simpler inversion that approximates the ground as homogenous medium.

articleTitle: Wireless Programmable Smart-Shield for Implantable Medical Devices Physical Protection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Modern Implantable Medical Devices (IMDs) are provided with wireless connectivity to perform diagnostic efforts quickly and cost-effectively. However, this connectivity exposes IMDs to several cyber and physical threats which can also be life-threatening to the patient. In this paper, we propose an epidermal RFID-based wireless programmable smart-shield as a protection mechanism. The device is conceived as a programmable Frequency Selective Surface (FSS) capable of blocking unauthorized communication with the ICD. Preliminary simulations of the grid unit cell, equipped with an RFID IC and a PIN diode for wireless reconfiguration purposes, demonstrate the feasibility of the idea.

articleTitle: A Dual-Polarized Folded Transmitarray Antenna with Low-Profile and Wide Bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A novel folded scheme is proposed to reduce the profile of the dual-polarized transmitarray antenna (TA). By employing a phase-gradient reflecting surface (PGRS), a focus can be generated, which works as the feeding source to illuminate the TA aperture. Therefore, the profile of the TA antenna can be designed flexibly to satisfy the requirements of low-profile applications. For wide bandwidth, the PGRS and TA element are designed based on magneto electric (ME) dipole structures. To validate the proposed dual-polarized folded scheme, a prototype is fabricated with a height-over-focal (h/F) value of 1/3. The measured peak gain and 3-dB bandwidth are 23dBi and 28%, respectively.

articleTitle: On Using Square-Shaped Fractal Patterns to Reduce the Operating Frequency of Open Complementary Split Ring Resonators on a Single Conducting Layer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Reducing the operating frequency of printed antennas on a single conducting layer has received considerable attention over the years. One method of achieving this reduced operating frequency is to introduce inductive or capacitive elements into a design using open complementary split ring resonators (OCSRR), particularly square-shaped OCSRRs, in specific locations with reduced resonant frequencies. This paper presents a method to further reduce the resonant frequency of an OCSRR using a square shaped fractal pattern. We achieve a 47.3% reduction in the resonant frequency without increasing size of OCSRR.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Electromagnetic Radiation from Ultra-Compact Magnetoelectric Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Ultra-compact magnetoelectric (ME) antennas utilizing stain-mediated magnetization to radiate electromagnetic (EM) waves have been experimentally demonstrated, while the latest investigations arouse controversy over their radiation mechanism. Here, we analyze three kinds of radiation sources in ME antennas at around 1.6 GHz, including ME coupling, equivalent magnetic current, and electric current. Contrasted experiments are carried out, which indicates that the equivalent magnetic current is the predominant radiation source. The ME coupling enhances the receiving voltage by approximately 0.60 dB, which cannot be observed in a non-magnetic/piezoelectric heterostructure as expected. Our results moderately resolve the debate on the ME radiation mechanism and pave the way to develop more efficient ME antennas.

articleTitle: Wideband High-Gain and Compact Cavity-Backed Patch Antenna Array for X-Band
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A wideband, high-gain and compact cavity-backed patch antenna array is designed and simulated for X-band applications. Initially, results are presented for a single cavity-backed patch antenna. Subsequently, the design is extended to form a 1×4 antenna array. For the single cavity-backed patch antenna, the reflection coefficient remains below -10 dB at 8.29 GHz - 10.78 GHz, with a gain of 7.2 dBi at 9 GHz. The 1 × 4 antenna array exhibits a reflection coefficient below -10 dB at 8.26 GHz - 10.73 GHz, with a similar impedance bandwidth and achieves a peak gain of 12.30 dBi at 8.9 GHz. Beam scanning characteristics of the 1× 4 cavity-backed patch antenna array is also investigated.

articleTitle: Design and Fabrication of Inkjet-Printing Transparent Transmitarrays
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This study delves into the development of transparent transmitarrays for the fifth-generation (5G) applications, emphasizing inkjet printing as a fabrication method. Focused on the 28 GHz frequency band, crucial in 5G Frequency Range 2 (FR2), the study designs and fabricates a transparent transmitarray. The fabricated prototype exhibits consistent reflection coefficients and favorable radiation patterns, demonstrating the effectiveness of inkjet printing. Notably, the study highlights the inkjet printing process, showcasing its flexibility in depositing conductive material, surface tension testing, ink compatibility calibration, and the use of nanosilver particle ink. The results underscore the potential of inkjet printing in advancing transparent transmitarrays, contributing to the evolution of 5G communication systems.

articleTitle: 2D Bianisotropic Metasurface Optimization Satisfying Far Field Circular Polarization Masks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Electromagnetic metasurfaces are an exciting area of research due to their capability of performing exotic field transformations, while retaining a low profile and comparatively small cost and complexity with respect to antenna arrays. However, one of the main barriers to their proliferation is they are difficult to design for far field requirements. Here, we present a method to optimize two-dimensional metasurfaces satisfying circular polarization far field masks using the alternating direction method of moments. To demonstrate the method, we synthesize a metasurface performing extreme angle beam collimation with masks on the co-polarized and cross-polarized radiation.

articleTitle: Design of a Cone-Shaped Array for Aeronautical Applications in LEO Satellites
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a cone-shaped array specifically designed for integration into CubeSat satellites. The intended application is air traffic control in the L-band, particularly in areas without base station coverage, such as oceans or deserts, utilizing the ADS-B system. Additionally, the array must support the new LDACS system operating from 960 to 1164 MHz. The proposed cone-shaped array, composed of six unit cells, allows for adjustable azimuth patterns and elevation pointing angles achieved by switching and combining signals from the twelve antenna ports. Each unit cell consists of a cavity-backed antenna with crossed petal-shaped dipoles as radiating elements. Two ports are utilized in each unit cell, enabling the configuration of the crossed dipoles for dual-polarization or circular polarization.

articleTitle: A Scattering Matrix Method for Parallel Cylinders Above a Planar Perfect Electric Conductor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The scattering matrix method (SMM) is an efficient method to solve the canonical problem of computing the field due to a set of different scatterers in free space. In the present contribution, we extend the SMM to the case of cylinders lying parallel to a planar infinite Perfect Electric Conductor (PEC). This scenario occurs in many instances, including the cases of smart skins and metagratings. Thanks to the exploitation of the ‘images’ method, we are able to incorporate the presence of the planar PEC by still using the free space scattering matrix of each (extended) inclusion. This ensures that the scattering matrix of each inclusion is available in a closed form for canonical shapes. A comparison with commercial software is also provided.

articleTitle: High Code Density Orientation Insensitive Chipless RFID Tag for Future Wireless Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this future communication paradigm, we introduce a Chipless Radio Frequency Identification (CRFID) tag designed for high code density, orientation insensitivity, and compactness. The tag geometry, constructed by superimposing two orthogonal ellipses in a nested loop fashion, encodes a 24-bit sequence within the Radar Cross Section (RCS) response spanning from 4.8 to 14.8 GHz. Fabricated on a 1.524 mm Roger's substrate, the tag measures 1.4 × 1.4 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, achieving a remarkable code density of 12.24 bits/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and a spectral efficiency of 2.4 bits/GHz. With its compact form, orientation insensitivity, and high code density, this tag holds promise for future identification, communication & sensing diverse scenarios.

articleTitle: IC-Equipped Programmable Metasurfaces for Multibeam Shaping
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Recent co-development of programmable metasurfaces (PMSFs) and integrated circuits (ICs) recently showed that constraints found in PMSFs, such as limited functionality and high power consumption, can be alleviated. These improvements enable the integration of PMSFs into wireless telecommunications and antennas, enhancing their performance and increasing their functionality. This work focuses on creating a multibeam pattern with controllable polarization, half-power beamwidth (HPBW), and sidelobe levels (SLLs). Despite stringent wavefront requirements, the proposed design achieves an 96.2 % accuracy in comparison to the calculated wavefront.

articleTitle: Design of Ku-band Metasurface Antenna for Beam Steering Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This article demonstrates a novel reconfigurable metasurface antenna designed at 13GHz based on a Partial Reflective Surface antenna and a reconfigurable metasurface with varactor as a spatial phase shifter. As a proof of concept, the main beam was steered to -18°, -28°, and -42° in one plane. The gain of PRS antenna without the reconfigurable metasurface is 16.0 dBi, and gain drop performance in these scanning range are below 3 dB. This work provides a useful references for designing a compact size reconfigurable metasurface antenna

articleTitle: Prof. Leo Felsen Legacy in Electromagnetics
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Professor Leopold B. Felsen had been certainly one of the brightest minds among those who set the foundations of modern Electromagnetism. The breadth and depth of his scientific work on wave phenomena spanning over 50 years from the middle fifties until his death, in 2005 provided impactful contributions in acoustics, electrodynamics, seismology, and mathematical physics. His work elevated concepts in Electromagnetism, introducing ray- wave hybrids, complex source-point descriptions for intricate media, and leaky-wave and hybridized ray-mode descriptions for guided-wave phenomena. A catalyst for systematic knowledge development, Professor Felsen collaborated widely and mentored students globally, playing a pivotal role in shaping wave physics and engineering evolution.

articleTitle: Improvement of GPR-SAR Imaging by Considering the Field Radiated by the GPR Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Ground penetrating radar - synthetic aperture radar (GPR-SAR) imaging algorithms have been widely used for the detection of buried targets as they can retrieve accurate images of the subsoil while keeping simplicity (and thus, computational cost) affordable. These algorithms can be improved by including the field radiated by the antennas of the GPR system, which can be characterized using an equivalent source model. This is of special interest in the case of GPR antennas with large phase center variation, where the application of GPR-SAR processing can be challenging. This contribution shows an application example of GPR-SAR imaging for buried targets detection using a Fourier-based imaging algorithm that considers the field radiated by the transmitting and receiving logarithmic periodic antennas (LPAs) of a portable GPR system.

articleTitle: Wideband Circularly Polarized Folded Transmitarray Antenna Using Characteristic Mode Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a low-profile wideband circularly polarized folded transmitarray antenna (CPFTA) using characteristic mode analysis (CMA). A wideband single-fed circularly polarized (CP) antenna and a polarization-selective metasurface (PSM) are realized by combining three and two pairs of CP modes, respectively. The feed is integrated with the metallic ground, forming a low-profile CPFTA together with the PSM. The simulated results demonstrate that the CPFTA exhibits a peak gain of 22.93 dBic at 10.8 GHz, an impedance bandwidth exceeding 70%, a 3-dB axial-ratio (AR) bandwidth of about 47.7%, and a 3-dB gain bandwidth of 25%, which verifies the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Synchronizing Radar and Auxiliary Data Streams with a Corner Reflector Clapperboard
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The widespread adoption of radar technology in diverse sensing applications, ranging from traffic monitoring over advanced driver assistance systems to healthcare analytics, necessitates robust methods for data synchronization. Although combining radar data with supplementary video or audio recordings enriches scientific analysis, achieving precise synchronization across these systems with varying latencies still can be a challenge. To resolve this synchronization dilemma, we introduce a novel solution: a clapperboard integrated with a corner reflector. Our method is rigorously evaluated, demonstrating its effectiveness in ensuring accurate time-alignment between radar and auxiliary video and audio streams.

articleTitle: Large-Scale Electromagnetic Structure for Ambient RF Energy Harvesting
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This research explores the integration of the Internet of Things (IoT) within a large-scale electromagnetic (EM) structure powered by innovative ambient radio frequency (RF) energy harvesting. The proposed planar Yagi antenna, designed for the GSM-900 frequency range, serves as a foundational element. Simulations reveal its efficiency, achieving a maximum gain of 5.9 dBi within the 930 to 980 MHz band. Building upon this, an 8×4 array of 32 planar Yagi antennas is devised to increase signal strength, aiming for approximately 20 dB gain. A phased-array approach with 60-degree phase shifts enhances adaptability, allowing beam tilting away from the wall. Simulations confirm a 34-degree tilt, validating the array's performance. The large-scale EM structure, with its array configuration and beamforming capabilities, presents significant promise for applications requiring heightened signal strength and adaptability. Prototyping for IoT sensor systems is underway, marking a step toward interconnected, sustainable, and intelligent environments.

articleTitle: Characterizing the Permittivity and Temperature Sensing of Medicaments Using Microwave Sensors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This study investigates the dielectric properties of paracetamol over a range of temperatures(80 °C, 60 °C, 40 °C and 24 °C), utilizing a frequency spectrum from 0 to 8 GHz through an open-ended measurement technique. The findings reveal a significant linear correlation between temperature variations and the real part of the complex permittivity of paracetamol. Additionally, the paper introduces a groundbreaking microwave sensor designed for non-invasive temperature monitoring. This sensor operates by detecting shifts in the resonance frequency of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S_{21}$</tex> transmission coefficient, offering a novel approach for continuous, non-destructive temperature tracking in pharmaceutical applications.

articleTitle: Study on Double Layer Design Method for Reducing RF Reflection using SiC-Fiber Ceramic Composites for High Temperature Exhaust
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The restricted accessibility of heat-resistant materials poses a challenge for stealth applications in high-temperature exhaust systems, rendering them susceptible to easy detection by radar. The lack of materials that can withstand high temperatures is a significant limitation. Silicon carbide (SiC) is a promising material for high-temperature applications. In this paper, ceramic composite combinations based on SiC fibers were investigated in order to identify suitable combinations to avoid radar detection.

articleTitle: Wireless Power Transfer Using Wideband Planar Beam-scanning LWA Antenna for Emerging 5G IoT Autonomous Sensors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Leaky-wave antennas (LWA) have received much attention in recent years for applications in the microwave and millimeter-wave ranges. This is thanks to their compatibility with printed circuit board technology, their low profile, and easiness of fabrication and integration with other planar components. In this paper, a miniature ultrawideband beam scanning LWA antenna is proposed to be utilized for short-range wireless power transfer (WPT) to multiple IoT sensor devices. The proposed LWA covers the frequency range from 15 to 30 GHz while maintaining a stable gain and a high scanning capability by steering its main lobe from −10° to 33°. These features make it a potential candidate for integration into the short-range WPT transmitter architectures (Tx) for powering the emerging autonomous 5G IoT sensors.

articleTitle: Low Cost Efficient Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface (RIS) for 6G Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper reports the development of an efficient low-cost varactor diode loaded, periodically arranged microstrip antenna based Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface (RIS) at C-band for 6G applications. The value of the reverse biasing voltage of the varactor diode controls the overall reflection phase of unit cell having approximately half wavelength periodicity. An array of 10×10 unit cells has been experimentally characterized for amplitude and phase performance for various combinations of biasing voltages. Two optimal voltages are selected for a predefined reflection phase for 1-bit RIS implementation at a specific frequency. The overall RIS power consumption is below 85 mW and is controlled by only two digital to analog converters (DACs) and one Single Pole Double Throw (SPDT) switch per unit cell to achieve low cost highly efficient RIS hardware for real world deployment scenarios. An experimental demonstration is presented to steer/reflect the incident RF signals towards non-specular angles of choice.

articleTitle: Performance Enhancement of Direction of Arrival Estimation Using a Single Port Metasurface Reflector Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper focuses on enhancement of the performance on direction of arrival (DoA) estimation using a single receiving antenna and a metasurface (MS) reflector without active elements. In this paper, two types of MS reflectors, with and without polarization-dependent characteristics, are compared. Because the MS reflector with polarization-dependent charac-teristics can generate different reflection phase distributions by mechanical rotations, the orthogonality of radiation patterns is enhanced. As a result, the performance of DoA estimation is improved.

articleTitle: Dual-Spiral Magnetic Antenna for Implantable Medical Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a dual-spiral magnetic loop antenna tuned to 2.45 GHz for implantable medical devices. It is a predominantly magnetic antenna system miniaturized to 35% of a loop in free-space. Simulations in ANSYS HFSS using a three-layer tissue phantom model demonstrate excellent tuning and impedance matching. The radiation pattern is directed strongly upwards out of the phantom model. When implanted, the device has an efficiency of 0.2%, maximum gain of -23 dB, and a maximum input power of 4.5 mW.

articleTitle: Design of Impulse Controlled Reflecting Surface for Beam Steering in 5G Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this work, an Intelligent Reflecting Surface (IRS) has been proposed for beam steering operation. The reflection phase of the elements of the IRS has been modulated with the aid of impulse sequences applied externally to control the incoming wave. The element phase is considered to be switched between 180° and 0° depending on the impulse instants. The scattering pattern for four different harmonics along with the central frequency at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f$</tex> =28 GHz is obtained with a maximum steered angle of ±54°.

articleTitle: An Aperture-Fed Quad-mode Wideband CP Metasurface Antenna for WiFi 7
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Based on the characteristic mode theory, this study introduces a novel quad-mode operation for capacitive cross-slot coupled circularly polarized (CP) Metasurface antennas, aiming to broaden the operating bandwidth (BW). This approach incorporates four modes: two orthogonal characteristic modes with higher resonance from the radiating patch and two orthogonal magnetic modes with lower resonance from the feeding structure. The strategic pairing of adjacent modes forms three sets of orthogonal modes, significantly enhancing the antenna's axial ratio (AR) BW. Implementing this method, a broadband CP Metasurface antenna with aperture feeding, optimized for WiFi 7, was developed. The constructed antenna underwent simulation, fabrication, and empirical testing, revealing an S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> range of 5.75-7.80 GHz (30.26%) and a corresponding AR. Operating within this BW, the antenna exhibited effective left-hand circular polarization (LHCP) radiation with gains between 5.7 and 8.7 dBi and a radiation efficiency exceeding 85%. Notably, its performance covered the entire 6GHz band (5925MHz-7125MHz), achieving a gain over 7dBi and a total radiation efficiency above 95%. These attributes render the antenna highly suitable for upcoming WiFi 7 applications.

articleTitle: A Wideband Circularly Polarized Transmitarray Using Rotated Dielectric Resonator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a wideband circularly polarized transmitarray antenna (TA) based on a rotated dielectric resonator (DR).
