The sectored cylindrical DR offers a polarization conversion feature for the rotation phasing method, achieving a full 360° phase shift. Additionally, a high dielectric constant of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\epsilon_{\mathrm{r}} =16$</tex> is employed for the DR to miniaturize the element, thereby enhancing the phase resolution. The design and simulation of a circularly polarized TA are subsequently conducted. Results reveal that the proposed TA exhibits broad 1- and 3-dB gain bandwidths of 17.1% (7.32-8.69 GHz) and 35.4% (6.17-8.82 GHz), respectively. A significant 3-dB axial-ratio bandwidth of 19.2% (7.03-8.52 GHz) is also achieved.

articleTitle: A Simple Closed-Form Model for the Pattern of Commercial Massive MIMO Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this contribution, we present a simple closed-form model for the pattern of Massive MIMO antennas. The main advantage of the proposed model, with respect to other models employed in the literature, such as the 3GPP model, is that it can efficiently predict the position of the sidelobes and the variation of the pattern parameters with scanning or the variation of frequency. Some comparisons with the patterns of commercially available antennas validate the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Enhancing Shielding Effectiveness Bandwidth in Core-Shell All-Dielectric Cylindrical Structures
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we developed and applied a method of auxiliary sources (MAS) numerical scheme to compute the scattered fields from a two-dimensional array of cylinders. The cases of dielectric core-shell, and perfect electric conducting (PEC)-dielectric core-shell cylinders were examined. The shielding effectiveness (SE) was computed and it was investigated how the characteristics of the array's elements can lead to the enhancement of the SE for increased frequency bandwidths. It was also shown that, compared to PEC arrays, the PEC-dielectric core-shell arrays have the advantage of offering a frequency passband for electromagnetic waves.

articleTitle: 3D-Printed Dielectric Bifunctional Metasurface Antenna for Millimeter-Wave 5G Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents design and development of an additively-manufactured dielectric bifunctional metasurface (DBMS) antenna for wideband millimeter-wave beamforming in backward and forward direction based on x- and y-polarized incident electromagnetic (EM) wave respectively. Initially, a dielectric meta-element (DME) with a two-line symmetric geometry, suitable for dual-mode operation is designed comprising layer of metallic-strips with uniform spacing which is responsible for reflecting the incident waves with parallel polarization to the metallic-strips (i.e. x-polarized) and transmitting the orthogonal one (i.e. y-polarized). Furthermore, a 2-bit quantized DBMS comprising of four different DMEs arranged in 15 × 15 configuration is designed and spatially excited by a 3D-printed horn placed at a theoretically calculated focal distance f of 40.5 mm. Linear orthogonal polarization of EM fields is manipulated by adjusting the orientation of feed source. The proposed DBMS augments the gain of feed source by 8.5 dB and 7.5 dB attaining a practical peak gain of 22.3 dBi and 21.5 dBi resulting in an aperture efficiency of 76.6 % and 63.7 % in reflection and transmission mode respectively. Also, a practical half-power gain bandwidth of 25 % in reflection mode and 30.6 % in transmission mode is achieved.

articleTitle: A Transmitarray Employing Independent Phase / Amplitude Control Elements
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A transmitarray antenna (TA) employing independent phase / amplitude control elements is presented. The unit cell consists of two perpendicular C-shaped slots etched on opposite sides of a single-layer substrate and it converts the transmission polarization orthogonally with regard to the incident waves. The phase variation is obtained by regulating the element physical parameters while the amplitude modulation is achieved by rotating the unit cell in order to satisfy the Taylor distribution for low sidelobe level (SLL). A transmitarray of 529 elements is designed and simulated. The results demonstrate this design can offer more flexibility by adjusting the phase and magnitude independently, enabling the TA to achieve low sidelobe level directly and efficiently.

articleTitle: Wireless Tracking for Joint Communication and Sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Due to the growing demand for wireless spectrum, the rapid development of a new generation of joint communication sensing systems (JCAS) has been promoted. This integration technology can make more efficient use of spectrum and hardware resources. Based on the increasing demand for high data rates and accurate environmental perception, in this paper, the relationship between phase offset and signal propagation distance based on the LoGait system is expounded, and the time-varying effect of phase difference is verified by experiments, proving the feasibility of calculating target distance. It can provide strong support for future JCAS environmental perception research.

articleTitle: High-Frequency Active Transmit/Receive Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: HRL has been developing an active antenna that overcomes the Bode-Fano bandwidth-efficiency limitations on both Transmit (TX) and Receive (RX) in the HF (3–30 MHz) band. The TX mode uses a switch-mode Radio Frequency Current Source (RFCS) amplifier to efficiently drive a 1-m normal mode helix beyond its natural resonance. The RX mode uses a high impedance buffer, together with the resonant matching network, to enable wideband reception. This paper presents a TX demonstration delivering QPSK to a dummy load with 5-10x more bandwidth-efficiency product than the Bode-Fano limit, and an RX demonstration with > 13 dB higher receive sensitivity than a narrowband conjugate match over most of the HF band.

articleTitle: Distributed Interferometric Radar for Radial and Angular Velocity Measurement
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this work we present a fully wireless coherent distributed interferometric radar for sensing the radial and angular velocities of dynamic targets. We build upon prior work on wireless coordination in both time and frequency by utilizing a high accuracy two-tone frequency transfer method for frequency syntonization and global navigation satellite system-based pulse-per-second timing alignment. The interferometric radar is based on software-defined radios and uses a continuous-wave 3.3 GHz signal to measure the Doppler and interferometric frequency shifts of signals scattered from moving targets. The two nodes in the array are separated by 91 cm (10λ). Coordination between the nodes was implemented wirelessly at 4.3 GHz, and received radar signals were transferred for joint processing at one node at 5.8 GHz. We demonstrate the performance of the distributed interferometric radar by measuring the instantaneous radial and angular velocities of a pedestrian carrying a corner reflector tangentially past the array.

articleTitle: Communication Channels Multiplexing Using Nonuniformly-Polarized Circular Array Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Wave polarization allows for multiplexing numerous channels at the same frequency and time. This is achieved using circular arrays of infinitesimal dipole antennas with uniform excitation amplitude, phase, and spacing but nonuniform polarization distribution. The arrays' far- and near-field radiation patterns are evaluated for their amplitudes and phases. Additionally, theoretical studies and full-wave simulations examine the array's potential to multiplex several channels in a line-of-sight transmitter-receiver system. The suggested antennas work equally well with orbital angular momentum (OAM) antennas, suggesting a promising multiplexing system research subject.

articleTitle: Diffraction by a Circular Aperture: A New Spherical-Multipole Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The paper deals with a new spherical-multipole-based method to solve the problem of scattering and diffraction by a circular aperture in a plane screen. To this end a three-domain problem is set up. Exemplarily, an incident plane wave and a plane screen with a soft (Dirichlet-type) boundary condition are treated. First numerical results are compared to those ones obtained for the complementary case, i.e., the acoustically hard circular disc using elementary solutions of the Helmholtz equation in spheroidal wave functions, and by applying the Babinet principle.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Terahertz Multi-Frequency Low-Profile Waveguide Antenna Based on Micro-Coaxial Feeding
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive theoretical analysis of electric field distribution in low-profile waveguide antennas operating in the Terahertz frequency range. We have developed a micro-coaxial-based, low-profile, multi-frequency waveguide antenna, integrating pin and gradient ridge structures to enhance its performance. The antenna dimensions are 4.7 mm ×13.3 mm × 0.9 mm. The reflection coefficient of this waveguide antenna is below -10 dB within the frequency ranges of 110–130 GHz, 148–156 GHz, and 175–182 GHz. It exhibits excellent directional radiation characteristics at the center frequencies of these three bands. With its compact size, lightweight, and low-profile features, this antenna is suitable for Terahertz high-speed communication applications, providing a practical approach for harnessing the electromagnetic spectrum resources in high-frequency domains.

articleTitle: SARS-CoV-2 and H1N1 Inactivation in Aerosol by Means of Radiated Microwaves with Novel Setup
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper a SRET (Structure Resonant Energy Transfer) system of inactivation for viruses has been studied in a novel aerosol setup. SARS-CoV-2 and H1N1 were the viruses under inactivation test. Such viruses have been exposed to a dedicated MW radiated field treatement obtaining an inactivation close to 90%.

articleTitle: A Passive Component Incorporated Miniaturization Super-Wideband Antenna for EMC Measurement
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A passive component incorporated miniaturization super-wideband (PCIM-SWB) antenna is proposed for EMC measurement, which has a feeding line with passive components, circle-shaped radiating patch, defected ground. The proposed PCIM-SWB antenna is created from a simple monopole, where its defected ground is to enhance its bandwidth. The two passive components are integrated into the feeding to further to improve its bandwidth to cover lower frequency band. By co-simulation and optimization using HFSS and ADS, a -10 dB fractional bandwidth of 163.2% is gotten for the PCIM-SWB ranging from 0.48 GHz to 4.74 GHz with omnidirectional radiating pattern, which can be employed for Wi-Fi and many military applications.

articleTitle: A Design of Series-fed Phased Array Antenna for High-speed Maglev
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In order to satisfy the reliability and delay demands of vehicle-to-ground communications in the maglev train, the current radio system is designed as a millimeter wave system. Besides, the millimeterwave phased array can not only alleviate the shortage on frequency resources and improve data transmission speed, but also change the shape of its radiation pattern in real time. Therefore, the application of millimeterwave phased array in maglev train communication greatly improves scanning speed and flexibility compared to traditional mechanical antennas. In this paper, a millimeter wave phased array antenna for radio system applied to the high-speed maglev trains is presented. With a standing wave series-fed structure as the phased array unit, a one-dimensional 16-element series-fed phased array is designed. The designed phased array can independently perform amplitude and phase modulation for beamforming. The experiment result shows that this system achieves the effects of a main lobe width of 5° and a scanning range of ± 15° on the H plane.

articleTitle: Research on Band-Pass/Band-Stop Filter Metasurfaces with Non-Reciprocity
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This report presents a novel structure for imparting non-reciprocity to planar band-pass and band-stop filters, commonly utilized in the communications field. The proposed structure involves placing metal batches with diverse characteristics on both sides of a ferrite component, exhibiting non-reciprocity. Band-pass and band-stop characteristics are selectively chosen based on the propagation direction. Simulation results validate non-reciprocal filter traits, demonstrating over 10 dB of isolation at the 6 GHz design frequency and on the low-frequency side.

articleTitle: Simulation of RCS Reconfigurable Characteristics for Bistable Glass Fiber Material Printed Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: To meet the varying requirements of radar cross section (RCS) enhancement or reduction for aircraft in different scenarios, a simulation study is conducted on a reconfigurable printed antenna with RCS reconfigurable characteristics based on bistable glass fiber material. This antenna achieves two hollow cylindrical configurations by toggling the states of the bistable glass fiber material. Simulation results indicate that the antenna exhibits excellent RCS reconfigurability within the operating frequency range. Under orthogonal incident waves, there is a significant difference in the bistatic RCS between the two antenna configurations, reaching a maximum value of over 20 dB.The investigated antenna operates in the band of 0.93-1.95 GHz and features a simple structure and flexible switching capabilities. It can adapt its antenna configurations according to practical application needs, presenting promising prospects for diverse applications.

articleTitle: Comparison of Butler Matrix and Rotman Lens Beam-Switching Networks at K-Band
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a comparative study between an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$8\times 8$</tex> Butler matrix and an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$8\times 8$</tex> Rotman lens operating over K-band (24.25 GHz to 27.5 GHz). The Butler matrix is designed based on aperture hybrid coupler and Schiffman phase shifter and printed on a multilayer stack-up to eliminate all the cross-overs and therefore, reduces the size and the insertion loss of the system. The Rotman lens has 8 inputs, 8 outputs, and 2 dummy ports and is designed to provide <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 45^{{\circ}}$</tex> scanning range over the desired frequency band. Both beam-switching networks show less than −10 dB return loss over 24.25 GHz to 27.5 GHz. The designed <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$8\times 8$</tex> Butler Matrix presents less insertion loss and a more compact size compare to the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$8\times 8$</tex> Rotman lens. However, the plotted Array Factor (AF) using the achieved output phase of each network proves that the Rotman lens is True Time Delay (TTD) while beam squint is an inherent characteristic of Butler Matrix.

articleTitle: Ultra-Miniaturized In-Band Full-Duplex Implantable Antenna for Wireless Capsule Endoscopy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This study introduces a novel in-band full-duplex implantable antenna designed for Wireless Capsule Endoscopy (WCE) and operating at the 2.45 GHz Industrial, Scientific, and Medical (ISM) band. The antenna is simulated inside a human body phantom with a depth of 50 mm. The antenna's size is kept ultra-miniaturized <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\pi\times(3)^{2}\times 0.254=7.17\ \text{mm}^{3})$</tex> through the integration of multiple semi-circular slots and shorting pins. The antenna exhibits a nearly omnidirectional radiation pattern at both 2.45 GHz for port 1 and port 2, attaining gains of -44.5 dBi at port 1 and -46.2 dBi at port 2. Achieving higher than 25 dB isolation between the two antenna ports is made possible by using a very thin superstrate and substrate, along with the addition of a middle slot in the ground plane. Thanks to its high isolation, small size, and simultaneous transmit and receive capability, this antenna is found to be suitable for WCE applications.

articleTitle: Antenna Isolation Investigation of an In-Band Full-Duplex System on an Airborne Pod
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Pilot training for defense applications can be enhanced with live, virtual, and constructed (LVC) operations that create more interesting testing scenarios in a cost-effective manner. The added data payload to support the new virtual and constructed elements, however, necessitates more efficient use of the communications links between the ground control station and airborne aircraft. In-band full-duplex (IBFD) technology can be utilized to increase the channel throughput when the resulting self-interference is mitigated. This paper presents an investigation of antenna isolation for an airborne pod that can support future LVC testing. The bare pod was measured to provide roughly 50 dB of isolation between two co-polarized dipole antennas at 1.8 GHz, where this metric can be used to inform the overall IBFD system design.

articleTitle: Silicon-Based Sub-Terahertz Suspended Whispering-Gallery-Mode Resonator Coupled to Strip Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this work, a silicon-based suspended Whispering Gallery-Mode (WGM) disc resonator coupled to a strip waveguide operating in G-band (140–220 GHz) frequency range is presented. A low-cost and high-precision fabrication process, compatible with the silicon-based platform is employed. The proposed design was measured, and the results verify that higher-order WGM modes with high-quality factors are induced in the operational frequency band. The proposed silicon-based WGM resonator has the potential to be used in low-loss, cost-effective and integrated biosensors for biomolecule detection and characterization.

articleTitle: NUIST Near-Field Scanner System Design for RF and Microwave EMC Test
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A near-field (NF) scanner (NFS) was designed recently at NUIST electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) lab. The developed NFS design engineering is described in the present paper. The test bench system is automated by using LabVIEW command interface. The electromagnetic (EM) probe is moved along the surface scanning of the electronic device under test (DUT). Efficient results of magnetic field cartography with two different scanning techniques using passive microstrip DUT VNA and using STM32 digital board with spectrum analyzer are presented. The NFS is used in the future for the 6G printed circuit board EMC testing.

articleTitle: New Design Of IoT-over-Satellite Antenna Based on Silicon Substrate
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The advanced technological developments in antennas have greatly influenced a wireless technology. With the rapid adoption of Internet of Things (IoT) applications in modern communication systems, the demand for miniature antennas is increasing. Microstrip patch antennas are widely used in IoT applications due to their compatibility. The main advantage of microstrip antennas is that they can be easily integrated into IoT devices due to their geometry, light weight, low production cost and compact size. Therefore, in this study, an antenna with a frequency of 5.8 GHz was developed, which can be used for IoT over satellite. The use of copper in the ground and in the patch was deemed appropriate, and silicon substrate materials, is introduced to compared with FR-4 substrate to give more flexibility to this antenna.

articleTitle: Rodolfo Zich: Professor, Scientist, and Innovator with Broad Visions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Rodolfo S. Zich, vice-rector from 1984 to 1987 and rector of the Politecnico di Torino from 1987 to 2001, was professor of Electromagnetic Fields at the Politecnico di Torino from 1976 to 2012 and then professor emeritus until his death on May 8, 2023. He was a great scholar of applied electromagnetics and one of the main architects of the innovation of the university system in Italy. Following in the footsteps of professor Mario Boella, his mentor, he contributed greatly to consolidating the Turin school of antennas and applied electromagnetics, strength-ening institutes and research centers already existing in the area, and creating and leading new ones. Thanks to Rodolfo Zich strategic visions and under his leadership, the Politecnico di Torino, the oldest and already one of the major in Italy, doubled in size. In his professional life he held several high-profile managerial positions and received many honors; among these his induction into the “Accademia delle Scienze di Torino” in 1987 and his nomination to Honorary Life Member of IEEE in 2016. With this writing, all his friends and colleagues at the Accademia delle Scienze di Torino, founded in 1783, honor him by recognizing his successes and scientific achievements.

articleTitle: Single Sideband Time Modulated Circular Array with Multibeam Capability
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a design of a 6-element Time Modulated Circular Array with suppressed unwanted harmonics. The beamforming network consists of three power dividers, one fixed phase-shifter and six RF switches. Harmonic suppression was done by feeding half of the antennas with the phased-shifted time-modulated signal, and by calculating the corresponding time sequences for each RF switch. With this approach, the beamforming network is simplified while obtaining multibeam capacity, with a steered beam on the first positive harmonic pattern.

articleTitle: Mutual Coupling Reduction in Dual Linearly Polarized Cavity-Backed Slot Antenna Arrays
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This work presents a new design approach to realize a dual linearly polarized cavity-backed cross-slot antenna operating around 3.25 GHz. The antenna offers a matching bandwidth of about 250 MHz ranging from 3.2 GHz to 3.45 GHz. The antenna array based on these cross-slots suffers from high mutual coupling and the main objective of this work is to mitigate the coupling. A specially designed high-impedance wall structure is proposed, which improves the mutual coupling remarkably by 10–20 dB to make the dominant couplings below −35 dB within the matching bandwidth. Measured and simulated results depict good agreement.

articleTitle: Phase Shifting Device with a Single Symmetric Control for Application in Reconfigurable Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Great demands are imposed to the upcoming communication systems regarding, bandwidth, latency, and data-rates. This challenging context can lead to the saturation of the electromagnetic spectrum and one way to overcome this is to have reconfigurable communication systems which can operate with different terminals by quickly changing their specifications. This work presents a phase-shifting device, with a single symmetric bias for use in reconfigurable antennas. Two microstrip segments are controlled using PIN diodes, one of them with more <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda/4$</tex> of electrical length. The phase shifter was fabricated and characterized, validating the low insertion losses between both operation states, with an 88.7° phase shift.

articleTitle: Additive Frequency Diverse Active Incoherent Millimeter-Wave Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: We present a technique for active incoherent millimeter-wave imaging that employs frequency diversity to increase the sampling coverage of the system and therefore improve image reconstruction. Fourier domain imaging relies on the correlation of received signals at pairs of antennas in an array. By hopping the carrier frequency to separate bands, the wavelength-dependent sampling function therefore changes, yielding additional samples at each band. Since the sampling function is determined by the array, hardware constraints can lead to low spatial sampling, which can cause poor image reconstruction, particularly for complex scenes. Frequency diversity thus allows imaging systems to collect more samples without changes to the array. We implement a frequency-diverse approach in a 24-element receiver array oriented in a circular pattern combined with a four-element noise transmitter. Transmission of noise ensures that the reflected signals are spatiotemporally incoherent, supporting Fourier domain imaging. Experiments were conducted in 1 GHz frequency steps ranging from 37 to 40 GHz. Images of a set of reflecting spheres demonstrates the improvement in image reconstruction by additively combining the samples across frequency prior to image formation.

articleTitle: A Novel K-Band Tightly Coupled Unit-Cell for Compact AESA Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper a novel tightly coupled radiating element is presented. The antenna is suitable for airborne AESA systems applications, in which reduced size, weight and power are fundamentals. The unit cell presented in this work is designed to reach a VSWR below 2.5 over the operative bandwidth 15:40 GHz (3:1 VSWR bandwidth) with wide-angle scanning properties (up to 60 degrees). The unit-cell is designed to be built using EDM (Electrical Discharge Machining) process but also using innovative manufacturing techniques, like additive manufacturing. The unit-cell achieve a VSWR <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$< 2.5$</tex> in the operative bandwidth and for every scanning configuration.

articleTitle: Differentiable Physical Optics Method for 3-D Reconstruction of Dielectric Objects
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a novel machine learning framework for 3-D reconstruction of dielectric targets from scattered electromagnetic (EM) field data. Our framework comprises two pivotal components: the shape representation part, which utilizes neural implicit surfaces as the continuous geometric representation of the reconstructed model, and the EM parameters storage part, which employs a fully-connected neural network to store the EM properties of the reconstructed model. Our algorithm takes the incident wave configuration as input and outputs the corresponding scattered field computed by the differentiable physical optics method (DPO). Subsequently, we optimize the geometric shape and the EM parameters by minimizing the residual between the output and the measured scattered field. Our numerical experiments demonstrate promising results in 3- <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{D}$</tex> reconstruction tasks.

articleTitle: Generalizable Diffusion Models for Site-Specific Radio Propagation Modeling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Machine learning (ML) methods have been successfully employed to derive efficient radiowave propapagation models in recent years. Recent efforts have focused on artificial and convolution neural networks. In this paper, we present the first diffusion model for indoor propagation. We show that diffusion models have a unique advantage when compared to other ML models, because they can solve at once three problems in propagation modeling: received signal strength prediction, calibration with measured data, and placement of access points.

articleTitle: Ultra-thin Electromagnetic Absorbers Comprised of Magnetodielectric Circuit Boards and FSS Loading
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This work considers electromagnetic absorber design based on commercially-available magnetodielectric circuit boards. Transmission line models are used to predict the absorption characteristics, as well as provide insight into how to retune via reactive loading using frequency selective surfaces. The resulting design methodologies facilitate practical design of ultra-thin absorbers using magnetodielectric circuit boards.

articleTitle: RF Measurements of Reflective Structures
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This study identifies a measurement technique to provide an accurate assessment of the achievable gain of reflective structures. As an example, an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{8}\times \mathbf{4}$</tex> antenna array that could be configured as a Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface is analyzed and is shown to produce a gain of 18.3dBi at 3.5GHz. Integrating this with path loss then shows how to evaluate the signal gain advantage of using a reflective surface to overcome blockage /shadowing that would be present in a practical environment.

articleTitle: Fast Analysis And Design Of Cylindrical Array of Patch Antennas Via Phase Modes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The design and analysis of a cylindrical phase array antenna is a difficult problem that is often limited by computational resources, cost, and time. In this paper, a computer-aided technique is proposed to accelerate the design and analysis of a circular/cylindrical array using a unit cell approach in the Ansys High Frequency Structure Simulator (HFSS). In the proposed technique, the embedded element patterns of the cylindrical arrays are computed in a MATLAB-based framework for each elevation scan using the phase mode concept. The efficiency of the method is verified by comparing the results of the unit cell analysis of the patch antenna with the results of the full array patch antenna analysis in HFSS.

articleTitle: A Reconfigurable Antenna Array with Radiation and Scattering Modulation based on GSO Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This work proposes a reconfigurable antenna array with integrated radiation and scattering modulation. By controlling the PIN diode states on a ladder-shaped patch element, a 180° phase difference can be generated between the radiation mode and the scattering mode. A 4 × 4 array is formed using the aforementioned element. Group Search Optimizer (GSO) algorithm is utilized in this paper to obtain an optimal phase distribution for the array. The array exhibits a peak gain of 16.25 dBi in the radiation mode, and a RCS reduction in the frequency range of 8 – 24 GHz in the scattering mode. The layout of the coding metasurface obtained by the GSO algorithm can result in a more than 5 dB monostatic RCS reduction in the frequency band of 8 – 14GHz.

articleTitle: A Wideband Low-Profile Phase Correcting Metasurface to Improve Directive Radiation Characteristics of Resonant Cavity Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we report the design of a planar phase-correcting metasurface (PCMS), constructed by true-time-delay (TTD) unit cells, that transform the nonuniform aperture phase of the conventional resonant cavity antenna (RCA) to a uniform one, producing highly directive radiation with improved aperture efficiency. We show full-wave simulation results demonstrating the successful generation of uniform phases even when the RCA cavity operates at the non-resonant frequencies. We show that the proposed RCA with the PCMS achieves a 3 dB gain bandwidth of around 35% with a peak gain of 20.2 dBi and an aperture efficiency of 23%. To the author's knowledge, the achieved bandwidth of 35% is the widest bandwidth reported for a class of RCA designed with planar PCMSs. We envision the proposed RCA to find applications in modern communication systems for long-distance communication or satellite connectivity.

articleTitle: An Additively Manufactured Wideband Dielectric Rod Antenna With Integrated Radome
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a wideband dielectric rod (polyrod) antenna operating from 7–18 GHz. The rod's design incorporates an integrated radome, which improves the robustness of the antenna. Recent additive manufacturing techniques, leveraging a new class of low loss dielectric resins, enable the rapid fabrication of the rod. Two units were fabricated, and return loss measurements are presented with comparison to predictions. Gain data indicates good performance even with the atypical integrated radome design.

articleTitle: An All-Metal Folded Reflectarray Adopting Mushroom-Shaped Slot Elements
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: An all-metal folded reflectarray with mushroom-shaped slot elements is proposed. The element is able to realize a linear 360° phase swing by adjusting the slot length and also mirroring its configuration. The folded reflectarray is composed of a bottom reflectarray embedded with a feed and a top polarizer. The electromagnetic waves from the feed are reflected twice between the reflectarray and the polarizer so that the antenna profile is reduced to half of the traditional reflectarray. Simulations reveal that the all-metal folded reflectarray has 1-dB gain bandwidth of 14% with maximum aperture efficiency of 42%.

articleTitle: Dual Band Low RCS Metasurface Sheet Using Nested Rings
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Reducing radar cross-section (RCS) holds critical importance across various military and civilian applications such as EM shielding and sensing applications. This study focuses on the reduction of RCS by introducing two nested metasurface unit cells that leverage polarization for backscattering cancellation in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{C}-\boldsymbol{K}_{\boldsymbol{u}}$</tex> bands applications. The metasurface unit cell comprises two nested octagonal shaped rings printed on grounded substrate having dielectric constant of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{\epsilon}_{\boldsymbol{r}}=\mathbf{2.2}$</tex>. Each demonstrating a characteristic of reflection phase difference, approximately <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{180}^{\circ}\pm \mathbf{30}^{\circ}$</tex>, between the reflected field components in two separate frequencies 12.4 GHz, and 6 GHz. By controlling the dimensions of each octagonal shape separately, two RCS reduction resonance frequency can be achieved. Similarly, a third band can be added by inserting a third octagon. In other words, nesting number of octagonal rings can lead to multiple RCS reduction frequencies. Four AMC block arrays in a perpendicular chessboard configuration are arranged. Simulation results indicate more than 18 dB reduction in RCS within the proposed bands.

articleTitle: Dielectric Resonator Based Resonance Cavity Antenna with Improved Radiation Properties
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A C-band dielectric resonator antenna (DRA)-fed resonance cavity antenna (RCA) with engineered superstrate has been proposed to improve the overall antenna gain and other radiation properties. The experimental results show as much as 19 % matching bandwidth. The peak simulated gain of the antenna is found to vary between 10.1 dBi to 14.8 dBi over its operating band, which is approximately 2.8 dB higher compared to a full metal superstrate. The proposed antenna also exhibits an excellent side lobe level of −12 dB over E-plane and −17 dB over the H-plane.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning and PSO Based Design Method for RCS Reduction Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Based on deep learning and particle swarm optimization (PSO), a method for the design of broadband radar cross section (RCS) reduction metasurfaces without a lot of time-consuming and resource-demanding full-wave simulations is proposed. A one-dimensional convolutional Residual Neural Network-18 is utilized to efficiently inverse design polarization conversion metasurfaces with parametric structures on demand, while PSO algorithms are used to optimize 3-bit coding sequences. The proposed metasurface can realize over 10 dB RCS reduction ranging from 6.4 to 18 GHz. Stable bistatic RCS reduction is achieved for both TE and TM polarizations when the angle of incidence changing from 0° to 30°.

articleTitle: A Fabry-Perot Cavity Antenna with a SiGe On-Chip Feeder for Submm-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper analyzes the performance of a Fabry-Perot cavity antenna fed by an on-chip spiral antenna and compares it with an on-chip antenna designed to be integrated in IHP's 130nmSiGe BiCMOS chip in a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{2}\times \mathbf{2}$</tex> array configuration. The results show the increase in directivity obtained by the combination of the Fabry-Perot cavity and a single spiral antenna versus the directivity obtained by forming a complex sequentially rotated <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{2}\times \mathbf{2}$</tex> spiral array.

articleTitle: A Novel Printed Monopole Antenna With Notched Band Characteristics for Wireless Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A novel ultrawideband (UWB) antenna was reported, which displays dual notched band characteristics. This is achieved by embedding a T-shaped stub in the radiating patch via a hole and etching an inverted U-shaped slot in the microstrip fed line. As a result, the antenna can operate in the UWB range from 3.1 GHz to 13 GHz, with the exception of two notched frequency bands between 3.7-4.2 GHz and 5.9-6.4 GHz. The antenna's design has been optimized and successfully simulated, fabricated, and tested. The proposed antenna features an omnidirectional and dumbbell-shaped radiation pattern in both the H and E-plane. It has stable gain and good time domain characteristics across all frequency bands, making it well-suited for wireless communication applications.

articleTitle: FDM 3D-Printed DRA Array for 5G Millimeter Wave and 6G Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper aims to illustrate the feasibility of Fused Deposition Modelling (FDM) printing technique as an inexpensive open-source 3D printing method for the development of antennas for 5G millimeter-wave (mmWave) and future 6G communication systems. A 2×2 dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) array based on either cylindrical or cuboid elements working at mmWave band are designed and analyzed. The cylindrical DRA array working at 24 GHz could achieve a maximum gain of 11.8 dBi at boresight direction, and ±42°/±46° -3-dB scanning angle at xz- and yz-plane, respectively. The cuboid DRA array working at 28 GHz could achieve a maximum gain of 11.5 dBi at boresight direction, and ±57°/ ±46° -3-dB scanning angle at xz- and yz- plane, respectively. To verify the performance, the DRAs were printed using PREPERM® ABS1000 filament and generally accessible FDM 3D printers. A good agreement between the measured results and the simulated ones is observed, which proves the feasibility of the low-cost open-source FDM 3D-printing method on the development of 5G mmWave and future 6G applications.

articleTitle: Performance Bounds on the Partial Gain to Q-Factor Quotient for Loaded $N$-Port Antenna Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A method based on optimizing current distributions using convex optimization to derive the theoretical performance bounds of antenna systems modelled by the method of moments (MoM) is reformulated to those constructed by loaded <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N$</tex>-port structures. The upper bounds of the partial gain to Q-factor quotient with a given radiation direction and polarization for a lossless rectangular metallic plate are studied in particular. The results reveal good agreement with previous work.

articleTitle: 28/39 GHz Wideband Multi-feed Array Antenna-in-Package for Power Combining Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A multi-feed array antenna-in-package (AiP) is presented for high-power combinations which supports wideband bandwidth covering 28 and 39 GHz. The design of the multi-feed antenna element was conceived with array antennas in mind from the outset. As a result, the suggested antenna offers four input ports, simultaneously achieving impedance bandwidth, port-to-port isolation, and cross-polarization discrimination (XPD). The utilization of a shorted patch and coupled feeder enabled the attainment of an impedance bandwidth of 46% and port-to-port isolation exceeding 10 dB. A 4 × 1 antenna array achieves a gain of up to 11 dBi, a radiation efficiency of 90%, and an XPD exceeding 20 dB.

articleTitle: Simultaneous Modeling of Switched Oscillator and Loading Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Switched oscillators (SWOs) are mesoband sources used in high power electromagnetic applications. SWOs operate by having a weakly resonant cavity that is short-circuited at one and and terminated in a high impedance load, such as an antenna, at the other. In the literature the SWO and antenna are often designed independently to operate at the same frequency. However, in practice, when the two are brought together, the overall system performance is often quite different in terms of resonant frequencies and spectral content. Recently we presented a circuit model that was able to to accurately predict this behavior and compared it with electromagnetic simulation. Here we apply that model to the specific problem of an SWO driving an electrically small antenna and show that the coupled oscillator problem leads to different results than would be expected if the two subsystes were considered separately.

articleTitle: Microwave Monitoring of Parkinson Disease Using a Realistic Human Head Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a widespread neurode-generative disorder characterized by the loss of dopaminergic neurons from the substantia nigra, causing bradykinesia, tremors, rigidity, and postural instability. In this paper, we present a differential microwave imaging study (MWI) for early-stage PD monitoring that uses the dielectric properties of the basal ganglia, particularly the thalamus. The simulations are carried out using two scenarios: one is based on studying the sensitivity of a realistic human head model. The other is the study of differential microwave imaging to monitor the PD based on the dopamine level changes in the basal ganglia. The MWI system contains 24 printed flexible antennas with a custom-made matching medium covering the head model. The obtained results demonstrate that small variations in dielectric properties within the human head, in particular the thalamus, can be detected, which can be used to monitor Parkinson's disease in a very early stage.

articleTitle: Multiple Scattering Theory with Broadband Green's Function for Band Calculations with Non-spherical Scatterers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: We have developed an approach termed Multiple Scattering Theory-Broadband Green's Function (MST-BBGF) for addressing 3D challenges involving vector electromagnetic waves within periodic structures. In this paper we extended the approach to include scatterers of non-spherical shapes. The method is computational efficient and is more than 2 orders of magnitudes faster than COMSOL. To formulate the Korringa-Kohn-Rostoker (KKR) equations using the MST-BBGF method, it is imperative to obtain the T-matrix of the scatterer. In this study, we employed commercial software to simulate the far field scattering amplitudes as a function of frequency of non-spherical scatterers. The resulting scattering amplitudes as a function of frequency are presented, revealing a consistently smooth broadband response that are consistent with photonic crystals that the scatterers are smaller to comparable to wavelength.

articleTitle: On Inconsistent Indexing Methods of Modes in Circular Microstrip Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Inconsistencies in the interpretation of modes in Circular Microstrip Antenna (CMA) have been brought out and explained. The available methods for it are shown to be inconsistent with standing wave equation. It is emphasized that the current or field maxima along radius, diameter or half-circumference, have been incorrectly used to infer the mode indices in books and papers. This paper brings out the disconnection between mathematical model and physical interpretation of CMA modes, and to show that mathematical interpretation is the only available accurate method to ensure consistent interpretation of modes universally.

articleTitle: Performance Enhancement of 6G Millimeter Wave Systems in Indoor Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This abstract delves into the emerging landscape of 6G technology, exploring challenges and advancements in millimeter wave systems. Emphasizing a novel approach for indoor propagation, the paper introduces a threefold strategy: a relay antenna for wide-angle coverage, a lens antenna to mitigate signal loss, and a fabrication-friendly design without reliance on vias. The focus is on overcoming the signal attenuation challenges, particularly at higher frequencies, and presenting innovative solutions to enhance system performance.

articleTitle: Challenges, Solutions, and the Future of High Power Microwave Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: High power antennas are specially designed to direct source power for long range effects in fields such as communication, radar, space, and defense. For defense, specifically high power microwave (HPM) systems, power levels of 100s of MWs to GWs are expected. As power level increases, breakdown in the transmit antenna becomes a leading challenge. The combination of high power and short pulses create fields that often meet or surpass the air breakdown threshold. Minimizing a systems Size, Weight, and Power consumption (SWaP-c) to maximize mobility while maintaining high gain creates a challenging problem space. Recent work in antennas show promise in addressing the common challenges faced by the directed energy (DE) community, shifting the future of HPM antennas.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Frequency Selection Scheme for Miniaturized Backscattering Neural Interfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Distributed neural interfaces with numerous miniaturized sensing implants provide powerful tools to achieve large-scale neural signal acquisition. To facilitate wireless power and data transmission in such systems, antenna miniaturization, electromagnetic safety, and functional feasibility introduce various frequency-dependent considerations. In this paper, we present a frequency selection scheme for designing miniaturized batteryless wireless neural implants, by systematically considering design constraits including antenna efficiency, tissue absorption, RF-to-DC efficiency, implant power consumption, and bandwidth. It is demonstrated that an upper limit of the wireless link operating frequency could exist for such neural implants (within the Federal Communications Commission guidelines), which varies with the architecture of implantation.

articleTitle: A Technique for High-Resolution Radar Coverage Using Multi-Mode Superposition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper outlines a method for 360° circular polarized radar coverage with high angular resolution using a rotating antenna. This method involves synthesizing a previously introduced CP beamforming and steering technique, relying on the superposition of circular waveguide modes. The performance of this method for automotive radar applications is demonstrated through measurements. The method provides high angular resolution similar to LIDAR systems while being able to operate in severe weather conditions similar to conventional mm-wave radars.

articleTitle: On the Near-Field Reactive Helicity and Far-Field Directivity of Circularly Polarized Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, spatial distribution of reactive helicity around in the antenna near-field region is critically examined. Using MoM based full-wave simulation involving crossed dipole antennas backed by PEC (perfect electric conductor) plate and cavity, it is demonstrated that far-field directivity for CP (circularly polarized) antennas bear inherent correlation with reactive helicity in their near-field apertures. Such analysis of reactive helicity will enable engineers synthesize and apply complex magnetoelectric fields for communication as well as sensing applications.

articleTitle: Compact Harmonic Feedback Rectennas for Low Power Battery-Free IoT Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: We propose a novel design of rectennas with harmonic feedback capability, tailored for battery-free IoT applications that operate at low input power levels. This rectenna design is based on the voltage doubler rectification topology. By integrating a quarter-wave stub, the rectifier achieves both DC conversion and harmonic feedback using just two Schottky diodes. We also introduce a single-port design that employs an impedance transformation network. This design allows the RF input and the harmonic output of the harmonic feedback rectifier to share the same port. Consequently, it reduces the number of transceiver antennas required. Preliminary measurement results presented in this work confirm and demonstrate the circuit's capability to efficiently perform RF to DC conversion and harmonic feedback even at lower input power levels.

articleTitle: Wideband and High-gain Rotman Lens-fed Yagi-Uda Antenna Array for Terahertz Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a Rotman lens-based beam-forming antenna design that provides high-gain radiation over a wide bandwidth at terahertz (THz) frequencies. Measurements of the suggested antenna show a flat gain characteristic of more than 16.2 dBi over the entire operating frequency bandwidth of 25 GHz (150 to 175 GHz), including the THz source-to-antenna conversion loss as well as the insertion losses of the Rotman lens and ground-signal-ground (GSG) probe. Radiation gains for all beam-steering patterns maintain a 3 dB-variation within a desired scanning range of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 25^{\circ}$</tex>. The proposed antenna is fabricated to be very compact at 28 mm <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times 28$</tex> mm, consisting of the Rotman lens, Yagi-Uda antenna array, co-planar waveguide (CPW)-to-microstrip line transitions, and additional screw holes to support experiments.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning-Based Imaging of Tree Interiors via a Standoff Radar System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a deep learning scheme for reconstructing the images of tree interiors via a standoff radar configuration. The radar is used to collect the signals reflected from the tree trunk while moving it along a straight trajectory distanced away from the surface of the trunk. Collected signals, stored as B-scans, are then processed and used as training and testing data for a modified U-Net model, which reconstructs the images of the tree trunk interiors. A novel hybrid loss function, consisting of segmental average structural dissimilarity index measure (SA-SSIM) and binary cross entropy (BCE), is proposed to increase the accuracy of reconstructing the fine details on the defect and trunk boundaries. A dataset containing diverse random 3D tree trunk and defect shapes and their corresponding B-scans is generated to train and test the proposed network. The preliminary results show that the proposed scheme achieves a very high accuracy in reconstructing the images of tree interiors. The proposed scheme is the first and foremost imaging technique for monitoring the interiors of tree trunks with defects while moving the radar on a straight trajectory in a standoff configuration.

articleTitle: A Dual-Band, Wide-Angle, Polarization Insensitive Metasurface-Based RF Energy Harvester
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A dual-band, wide-angle, polarization-insensitive metasurface-based RF energy harvester is presented in this paper. The proposed design consists of a circular ring resonator and four split ring resonators (SRRs), which reside inside the circular ring and are connected to it. In the proposed design Vias are used to channel the power to the load. The vias are loaded with 50Ω resistors to achieve 82.5% RF-AC conversion efficiency at 5.8 GHz and 80.2% RF-AC conversion efficiency at 6.8 GHz. A rectifier is designed with 50Ω input impedance, and the efficiency of the proposed rectifier is 60% and 47<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> at 5.8 and 6.8 GHz, respectively. The proposed harvester can harvest energy from WiFi 5 and ISM band (5.8 GHz) and Wi-Fi 6E (6.8 GHz) spectrum.

articleTitle: A High-gain Low-profile Monopulse Antenna Array at 94GHz in Gap Waveguide Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The presented letter describes a low-profile monopulse slot array antenna designed for operation at 94 GHz, based on the gap waveguide (GW). The antenna, with a three-layer structure, comprises a monopulse comparator feed network utilizing the groove gap waveguide (GGW), a power division network based on the ridge-gap waveguide (RGW), and an open-ended slot array for direction-finding applications. The simulated null depth in both difference patterns is close to -25 dB, while the sum pattern achieves a 32 dBi directivity gain with a realized radiation efficiency exceeding 70%. This antenna capitalizes on the advantages of a gap waveguide structure, known for its compactness and ease of fabrication.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Dual-Polarized Smart Electromagnetic Skin for Enhanced mm-Wave Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This work introduces the design of a passive Reflective Intelligent Surface or Smart Electromagnetic Skin (SES) to enhance millimeter-wave 5G communications. The SES operates in dual band at 28 and 39 GHz, supporting dual linear polarization. The impinging field is provided by two different base stations, each operating at a different frequency, and the SES reflects both fields in the direction where the coverage is required. Additionally, the radiation pattern is shaped to achieve a flat top within the desired angular range. Simulations demonstrate a high level of compliance of the SES in shaping the field for both frequencies and polarizations.

articleTitle: Synthesis Approach of Semicircular Passive Huygens Meta-Dome for Patch Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this work, we validate the modeling of a passive Huygens metasurface dome that envelops a patch antenna for the purpose of beamforming manipulation and focusing. Specifically, we demonstrate the effective use of circular array pattern synthesis for modeling the meta-dome by properly discretizing and engineering the phase profile along the dome and by taking into account the actual incident field produced by the antenna.

articleTitle: Efficient Cross-Layer Handover Authentication for Secure Communication in VANETs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper addresses the critical need for secure and resilient handover authentication processes in modern vehicular communication systems, characterised by low latency and high reliability. Introducing a cross-layer handover technique, our approach utilises a physical layer handover method leveraging the substantial decorrelation of channel responses between diverse network terminals. Emphasising the lightweight nature of the solution, our method ensures efficient authentication during vehicular handovers. The proposed methodology, validated through experimental analysis, offers a promising solution to the increasing challenges posed by wireless communication vulnerabilities in the context of modern vehicles.

articleTitle: Rapid Antenna Optimization Using Circuit-Based Transmission-Line Models Tunable in Real Time
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: We demonstrate antenna analysis and optimization using real-time tuning performed on analogous transmissionline models. Tuning is facilitated by adopting circuit-based computational tools and closed-form models, instead of full-wave electromagnetic analysis. The technique is intended for design, as well as educational, purposes, and can be used as an extension or replacement of analytical expressions.

articleTitle: Additive-Oriented Spiral Antennas with Infinite Balun
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Spiral antennas have been widely investigated over the last decades, thanks to wide operative frequency range with stable antenna parameters. With the recent advance of the additive manufacturing processes, the antenna design and realization techniques can be adapted to save production costs and time. In this contribution, a novel spiral antenna realization is investigated with an additive-oriented approach. A full-wave numerical comparison between the classical Equiangular and Archimedean spiral is presented. Wide operative bandwidth and stable antenna radiation pattern are achieved. A strong dependency of the antenna radiating efficiency by the material losses is found, thus imposing an accurate choice of the geometrical aspects of the spiral.

articleTitle: Optimising Optical Transparency and RF Performance in Meshed 5G Vehicular Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: With 5G networks enabling new vehicular connec-tivity services, there is a need for effective antennas to be integrated into automotive glass. As a result, better optically transparent (OT) conductive films are required. This paper analyses micro-scale metal meshes as a promising OT conductor technology. Theoretical analysis suggests that sheet resistance and optical transparency can be tuned using the geometry of the conductive mesh and simulation is conducted. The findings provide design guidelines to optimise the optical and radio frequency performance of metal mesh in vehicle windows.

articleTitle: Direct LEO Satellite-to-Smartphone Network Coverage Compensation with Simultaneous Transmitting and Reflecting Surface (STARS)
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: While employing distributed beamforming with multiple satellites can effectively enhance the link budget for direct Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite-to-smartphone communication, the resultant coverage on Earth may exhibit unevenness attributable to interference. To address this issue, we introduce a Simultaneous Transmitting and Reflecting Surface (STARS) capable of autonomous control over the transmission phase on one side and the reflection phase on the other side. Simulation results demonstrate that the transmission coefficient exceeds 0.7, the reflection coefficient approaches 1, and both exhibit a phase range from 0 to 360 degrees.

articleTitle: Broadband High Gain SIW-Based H-Plane Horn Antenna for Ku/K Band Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a substrate-integrated waveguide (SIW)-based H-plane horn antenna with a broader impedance bandwidth and high peak realized gain (PRG) for broadcast satellite (Ku/K band, 12.5-26.5 GHz) and fixed satellite K band, 18-26.5 GHz) services applications is presented. A tapered microstrip transition is used in the feeding section to obtain the broadband characteristics. In addition, the multistrip transition also helped to enhance the fractional impedance bandwidth (FIBW), radiation characteristics and to improve the PRG. This mechanism of bandwidth increase can be explained by applying the coupled resonators theory. The antenna is designed, fabricated, and tested. The measured FIBW of 16.3%, the PRG of 10.56 dBi at the end-fire direction, the maximum radiation efficiency of 88.56%, and the cross-polarization level below - 35 dB have been achieved at the center freqency of 19 GHz.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized Ultra-Wideband Dual Polarization Vivaldi Antenna Based on Loading Resistors and Parasitic Structures
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: We proposed a miniaturized ultra-wideband dual polarization Vivaldi antenna based on loading resistors and parasitic structures in this paper. The VSWR of the antenna is reduced by adding resistance elements at the ports, while resistive elements are added to the radiator. Optimizing the low band and high band radiation patterns by slotting lines and introducing periodic parasitic patches. Dual polarization of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0^{\circ}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$90^{\circ}$</tex> is achieved by cross-placement. Simulation results show that the antenna covers 0.4 - 13 GHz with VSWR <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\leq 2$</tex>, and the isolation between the two ports is more than 30 dB. The physical dimension of the entire antenna is only <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$70 \text{mm}\times 120$</tex> mm (0.09 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda\times$</tex> 0.16 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda)$</tex>. The radiation pattern of each frequency point has good symmetry, which is suitable for application in various small near-field measurement systems.

articleTitle: Directional Metasurface with Selective Polarization Using Antenna Elements
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A new concept of a directional, non-reciprocal metasurface (MSF) where the polarization of the transmitted wave can be selected at will is presented. Each cell of the proposed MSF has a circularly polarized (CP) elliptical patch on side 1 and a reconfigurable orthogonal (either x- or y-) linear polarization (LP) square patch on side 2. Any random polarization incident wave on side 1 is collected by the array of CP antennas. The signal is transmitted to the reconfigurable LP antennas on side 2 through vias. The reconfigurable LP patches have orthogonal feed from two segments which are connected with the common microstrip line through single pole double through (SPDT) switches. The appropriate switch position results in the preferred polarization of the transmitted wave. Two transistors along the transmission lines of the two antennas ensure the non-reciprocity of the directional metasurface. The proposed design operates effectively in the frequency range 3.4-3.6 GHz and it presents nearly 20 dB enhancement of the transmitted wave with the selected linear polarization in the forward direction and 50 dB isolation as compared to the propagation in the opposite direction.

articleTitle: An Ultrawideband Frequency Reconfigurable Tightly Coupled Dipole Array
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A frequency reconfigurable tightly coupled dipole array (TCDA) based on PIN diodes is demonstrated in this paper. Two different operating bands of the proposed array can be selected by changing the states of the PIN diodes on low-frequency TCDA. Each frequency reconfigurable TCDA unit cell contains a low-frequency TCDA element and 32 high-frequency TCDA elements. The low-frequency TCDA works from 0.35 to 2.1 GHz (active VSWR<3) in the “on” state, and the high-frequency TCDA operates over 2.34 to 10 GHz in the “off” state. Simulation results show a 26:1 frequency-tunable TCDA. In this way, a frequency tuning array is designed for wideband reconnaissance applications.

articleTitle: High Accuracy Decentralized Time Synchronization Using SNR Based Weighting
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: We present a decentralized approach to wireless picosecond-level synchronization of distributed antenna array elements that weights its connections based on the signal-to-noise ratio of the links between nodes. Time synchronization is a critical aspect of distributed phased array performance, and is a principal factor limiting the bandwidth of distributed beam-forming operations. We previously demonstrated decentralized synchronization with picosecond-level accuracy using a consensus averaging approach, where nodes iteratively share information among their neighbors to converge to the global average of the time offsets between nodes. Ensuring that all nodes in a distributed array reach consensus on a common time reference depends on the accuracy of the individual links, however, and low SNR links will generate poor time estimates, increasing the residual error of the converged state. Here, we propose a new weighting strategy based on evaluating the SNR in every iteration to allow for time information sharing only between the nodes with highest received SNR. We evaluate the approach experimentally through the implementation of a six-node system using software defined radios (SDRs), yielding in an order of magnitude improvement in accuracy relative to the case of a fully connected antenna array with a static topology.

articleTitle: Efficient Solutions of Transient Electromagnetic Problems with Generalized Media
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Electromagnetic (EM) problems including generalized media should be formulated by using volume-surface integral equations (VSIEs) in integral equation approach. The conducting medium is described by using surface integral equation (SIE) while the penetrable media are governed by employing volume integral equations, and they are coupled each other by scatted fields. For transient problems, the time-domain version of VSIEs (TDVSIEs) is used to describe them. Although the TDVSIEs can be solved by the traditional method of moments (MoM) and march-on-in-time (MoT) scheme, we propose to use a hybrid scheme combining the Nyström method and Galerkin's method. The proposed scheme can remove the expensive MoM in space domain and late-time instability in time domain. Numerical examples are provided to demonstrate the approach.

articleTitle: An Electronically Reconfigurable Magnetic Metasurface for Low-Frequency RF Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper delves into electronically reconfigurable, low-frequency magnetic metasurfaces, a cutting-edge domain that promises a paradigm shift in the field of electromagnetic engineering. In particular, this work introduces a novel concept of an electronically reconfigurable <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3\times 3$</tex> magnetic metasurface excited by an active RF coil placed in its near-field region and operating at 3 MHz. Reconfigurability is achieved by incorporating a varactor diode on each unit-cell of the metasurface. Experimental measurements were conducted over a fabricated prototype, in which two different unit-cells currents patterns are shown. The dynamic nature of the structure enables easy switching between different configurations in real-time, hence facilitating a wide range of applications including wireless power transfer, sensing, and MRI enhancement.

articleTitle: Enhancing Wireless Connectivity in Underground Mines Through CSI Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This study undertakes a detailed examination of Wi-Fi Channel State Information (CSI) within an underground gold mine, focusing on Line-of-Sight (LOS) and Non-Line-of-Sight (NLOS) conditions. It scrutinizes key metrics including amplitude, phase information, cumulative power loss in the channel (as indicated by squared amplitude sums), Root Mean Square (RMS) delay spread, and mean excess delay. The research delineates the contrasting signal behaviors in LOS versus NLOS scenarios, illuminating the intricacies of wireless signal propagation in subterranean environments. These insights are crucial for refining wireless network models, thereby enhancing the precision, reliability, and efficiency of Wi-Fi communication in specialized settings such as underground mines.

articleTitle: Rectifier Optimization for Low-Power RF Energy Harvesting Tags
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: An optimization technique is proposed for the design of highly efficient radio frequency (RF) rectifiers at low power levels. Therefore, a “Thru-Reflect-Line” calibration kit is designed and used for the de-embedding of the SMS7630-005LF series pair Schottky diodes. Based on these measurements an accurate equivalent circuit is proposed, including all parasitic losses that are introduced from the package and the interconnects in the actual application. This equivalent model is used to design a compact and low-cost rectifier for operation in the 2.45 GHz band. This rectifier employs a lumped component L-type matching network and achieves a power conversion efficiency of 13% and 35% at -20 dBm and -10 dBm, respectively. The proposed rectifier can be seamlessly integrated in active radio frequency identification (RFID) tags to extend their lifetime and improve their performance.

articleTitle: Polarization-Dependent Varifocal Metalens with Achromatic Focusing in THz Region
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Metalenses offer great potential for flexible manipulation of the electromagnetic field. However, metalens with tunable focal length and achromatic performance remains a challenge. This paper constructing a polarization-dependent superposition varifocal metalens with achromatic focusing performance in the THz region (270 - 330 GHz). The focal length of the metalens can be tuned linearly by changing the polarization angle of incidence, allowing for a tunable range of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3\lambda_{c}$</tex> (where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda_{c}$</tex> is the wavelength at 300 GHz). Another key advantages of the varifocal metalens is that it can maintain a stable focal length for a given polarization incidence across a broad bandwidth of 20%. Within the operation band, the varifocal metalens exhibits high focusing efficiency and achieves diffraction-limited spot sizes, ensuring high-resolution imaging and sensing capabilities.

articleTitle: Hybrid RT-MoM Approach for RIS-Enabled Communication Channel Analysis and Optimization in Realistic Environments
