publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a hybrid approach, combining the ray-tracing and method of moments (RT-MoM) techniques, aimed at systematically evaluating reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-enabled channels in real-world environments. Further-more, the method utilizes optimization techniques to configure varactor values on the RIS, optimizing signal strength at 5.8 GHz in a designated region or location for a single-input single-output (SISO) system. Ultimately, at the specific location, we achieve a signal strength improvement exceeding both scenarios: one with-out RIS assistance by 8.5 dB, and the conventional phase-gradient method by 3.2 dB. This validation of the method underscores its effectiveness in enhancing communication performance within practical RIS-enabled channels.

articleTitle: Simulation and Experimental Research of Passive Millimeter Wave Target Detection Based on Polarization Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents an imaging detection simulation analysis method based on the polarization characteristics of target millimeter-wave (mm-wave) brightness temperature. The method employs theoretical modeling and simulation of the brightness temperature of typical aerial and terrestrial targets, and has been experimented by using the passive mm-wave polar-ization imaging system based on the scale principle. According to the simulation and experiment results, the imaging detection method based on the mm-wave polarization characteristics of the target can effectively detect the metal target.

articleTitle: Low Radar Cross Section Metasurface Based on Polarization Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A metasurface based on polarization conversion and phase cancellation is proposed to achieve a low radar cross section characteristic. The unit cell of the metasurface consists of a rectangular patch on the top layer, a cross slot in the center layer, and a ground plane on the bottom layer. The periodic array of the unit cells covers the linear polarization wave to its cross- polarization in the band of 6.49 -12.09 GHz. The rotary lattices of 4 × 4 unit cells form a chessboard metasurface which evidently reduces the scattering in the frequencies ranging from 6.5 to 20.5 GHz.

articleTitle: Temperature-Sensitive Microstrip Patch Antenna Radiation using Large-Area Artificially-Engineered Carbon-Loaded Composites
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Wireless antenna-based sensors are a key enabler of integrated sensing and communications. Nevertheless, materials are yet to be developed for RF sensing. Herein, we present a detailed analysis of the radiation and material properties of a temperature-sensing microstrip patch antenna, based on the first large-area thermistor substrate. Owing to the substrate's behavior as a positive temperature coefficient (PTC) thermistor, up to two orders of magnitude variation is observed in the RF conductivity from 10 MHz to 4 GHz. Furthermore, the substrate's permittivity undergoes up to a five-fold change between room temperature and 240° C. Over 20 dB gain change is measured in the broadside direction for a 140° C temperature increase, resulting in a best-in-class sensitivity of 0.16 dB/°C. The results show that large-area sensing substrates could improve the performance antenna-based sensors beyond state-of-the-start.

articleTitle: Unit-Cell Driven Deterministic Inverse Design of Metasurface Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This contribution presents a metasurface (MTS) design carried on with a current-only optimization approach. The standard MTS optimization in literature treats the impedance profile as continuous, with subsequent sampling at the center of unit cells. Here, optimization is carried out dividing the MTS surface into isolated subdomains that correspond to the intended unit cells, which will make the final unit cell designed easier. This is compared to the case in which the impedance profile is treated as continuous; results show that the synthesized impedance profile and the resulting radiation pattern are comparable, thus paving the way to a better design of the overall MTS.

articleTitle: A Broadband and High-Gain Traveling wave Antenna Array with End-Fire Radiation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A series-fed end-fire antenna array with the advantages of wide band and high gain is proposed in this paper. Based on the coupled feeding of parallel line, twenty couples of loop antenna units arranged periodically and equally spaced are fully excited. The surface of the loop unit antenna is parallel to the parallel transmission line. By optimizing the unit size and spacing, a high-gain end-fire radiation pattern can be obtained at the expected frequency. The simulation results manifest that the proposed antenna has an impedance bandwidth of 49% and the highest end-fire gain of 16.23 dBi, which greatly contributes to the need for long-distance communication.

articleTitle: Toward Clinical Microwave Skin Anomaly Detection: Impact of Dermal Composite Layers on Skin Dielectric Properties
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Variation in skin thickness across different body regions contributes significantly to the inherent tissue dielectric properties. In this study, porcine and human skin dielectric trends are compared with dermal composite layer thicknesses to understand their relationship across the observed sensed volume. The porcine skin dielectric constant is observed to decrease with the increase in epidermal layer thickness. These observations were also coherent with measurements on the human skin. Thus, for robust electromagnetic skin anomaly detection that is suitable for all human body regions, dermal regions should be demarcated into groups of similar epidermal/dermal thickness.

articleTitle: An SIE-GSTC Formulation for 3D Composite Metasurface Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A formulation for the analysis of three-dimensional (3D) composite metasurfaces consisting of homogenized mono-isotropic sheets supported by grounded dielectric spacers is presented. The inhomogeneous scattering problem is recast into two coupled homogenous problems by way of the surface equivalence theorem. Integral equations are written whose solution provides the equivalent currents. An example of a composite metasurface containing 100 unit cells is provided.

articleTitle: Generalized Transition Matrix Method with Physical Optics Approximation for Large Open-Ended Cavities
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel hybrid method for the generalized transition matrix (GTM) method with the physical optics (PO) approximation. The entire structure of an open-ended cavity is divided into the interior and exterior regions by the reference surface on the aperture of the cavity. The PO approximation is applied to the exterior surface, while the interaction of the interior region can be modeled onto the reference surface using the GTM model. The computational complexity and memory usage are reduced by the proposed method. Numerical results are presented and discussed in this paper.

articleTitle: Unlocking the Jones Matrix Full-parameter Regulation Via Bilayer Spatially Cascaded Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The linear modulation of electromagnetic (EM) waves can be fully represented by a Jones matrix, which is a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2\times 2$</tex> matrix with eight manipulated parameters. Unlocking more free parameters means that meta-devices with more functionality can be realized. Many efforts have been devoted to unlocking more free parameters in the Jones matrix. However, unlocking the full-parameters is still a huge challenge. Here, we propose a scheme for unlocking the full-parameter of Jones matrices via the bilayer spatially cascaded birefringent metasurfaces. Moreover, a gradient descent-based inverse design algorithm is proposed to optimize the Jones matrix distribution of the bilayer metasurface. As a proof of concept, a Jones matrix eight-channel regulation meta-device is verified by simulation in the microwave region. The proposed strategy provides a new paradigm for the realization of multifunctional meta-devices.

articleTitle: Enhancing Broadband Performance with a Novel Three-Stage Tapered Slot Antenna Featuring Exponential Curve
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This study introduces an innovative three-stage tapered slot antenna design, incorporating exponential curves to significantly improve radiation performance and maintain a broad impedance bandwidth. By employing a unique combination of increasing and inverted decreasing exponential curves, the antenna effectively minimizes sidelobes and sharpens the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3\mathbf{dB}$</tex> beamwidth beyond the capabilities of traditional Vivaldi and Linear Tapered Slot Antennas (LTSA). Comparative evaluations reveal that this design not only matches but surpasses the radiation gain and bandwidth specifications of its predecessors, offering a substantial advancement for broadband communication and imaging technologies.

articleTitle: An Axisymmetric Secant-Square Beam Shaped Ceiling-Mounted Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes an axisymmetric secant-square beam-shaped ceiling-mounted antenna. Six folded Inverted-F Antennas (IFAs) are positioned on one side of a circular metal ground and are rotationally fed by a microstrip feeding network located on the opposite side of the ground. The vertical components of the folded IFAs primarily radiate the main energy, while the horizontal components radiate secondary energy, a phenomenon analyzable through the mirror principle. By adjusting the height of the folded IFAs, the radiation ratio between the horizontal and vertical components can be tailored, thereby shaping the beam. The Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of the gain curves at 2.4 GHz is 1.66 dB, indicating a strong fit.

articleTitle: Near-Field Synthesis of Shaped Beams via Spectral Factorization and Warping Sampling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: We extend to the near-field case the well-known spectral factorization method, which was applicable until today only to far field. This is done by restoring the bandlimitedness of the field through the adoption of a suitable warping variable. By so doing, it becomes possible, for the first time in the literature, to perform the mask-constrained power synthesis of 1-D shaped beams lying in arbitrary masks in the near field zone by just solving a linear programming problem followed by a polynomial factorization. It also becomes possible a-priori ascertaining whether the size of the source is sufficient to radiate a field lying in the assigned mask, and hence a-priori identifying the minimum feasible size of the source. Finally, the procedure identifies all the sources able to radiate the sought power pattern. An example concerning near field multi-focusing is provided.

articleTitle: Bandwidth Improvement of an Electrically Small Parametric Receiver
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: An electrically small loop antenna loaded on-aperture with a time-varying capacitor was studied. The time-varying capacitor and loop were used as a degenerate mode, negative resistance parametric receiver to achieve gain and higher bandwidth. This particular configuration elaborates on previous work by intentionally detuning the system to acquire more bandwidth than a standard degenerate mode, negative resistance parametric amplifier.

articleTitle: Broadband Microwave Antenna for Imaging and Sensing in Biomedical Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Thanks to their operation band, broadband an-tennas demonstrate applicability and versatility in biomedical sensing and imaging. This work presents the numerical validation of a microwave broadband monopole antenna aimed for work in close proximity to biological tissues, such as the human head. An iterative design starting from an elliptical patch antenna reduces geometry dimensions and enhances bandwidth efficiency. The final design achieves a compact 48×38mm antenna with a dielectrically custom-made 3 mm-thickness matching layer covering a -10 dB frequency band from 1 to 6GHz, which is assessed on top of a simplified multilayer head phantom.

articleTitle: Ka-band Circularly Polarized Phased Array Antenna with Independently Controlled Beams
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A wideband circularly polarized phased array antenna is developed, wherein the number (single or dual), the steering angle, and the sense of the circular polarization (right-handed circular polarization or left-handed circular polarization) of the beams can be independently controlled. A 64-element (8×8) antenna array at Ka-band of 27.5 to 30 GHz is prototyped to demonstrate the capability.

articleTitle: Moxon-Based Broadband Circularly Polarized Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: To meet the challenges of modern radio communication systems, antennas need to be optimized for higher gain, broader bandwidth, smaller size, defined radiation pattern, polarization, and lower cost. The Fano-Chu limits have been extended to larger structures with more conducting elements to yield higher gain. A circularly polarized antenna structure has been developed for satellite communications, RFID tag reader, GPS, and Base Station antennas for UMTS-FDD and E-UTRA-FDD. A coupler element has improved the proposed topology to improve circular polarization gain performance. New elements have been designed to optimize gain, lower cross-polarization, and maintain a low profile with adequate bandwidth.

articleTitle: Achieving Broadband Near-Field Directionality with a Three-Dimensional Active Janus Source
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The Janus source - comprising a pair of co-located, orthogonally oriented electric and magnetic currents with a 90° phase shift - exhibits unique near-field selective coupling. However, the existing Janus sources are limited to ideal current sources or passive particles, hindering their efficient use in near-field directional systems. In parallel, antenna research has focused on the far-field characteristics of a configuration similar to the Janus dipole, named the “quasi-isotropic antenna” due to its far-field characteristic. In this work we show that an electrically small quasi-isotropic antenna is also a 3D active Janus source (we hence term it a Janus antenna). We investigate its near-field directionality and show it achieves near-field directionality over a broad bandwidth of 27.8%. We also demonstrate that, by using the Janus antenna, directional power coupling can be demonstrated with a power efficiency more than 100 times higher than using a passive Janus dipole. Achieving broadband near-field directionality with high power efficiency can find attractive applications in compact and multifunctional directional devices.

articleTitle: SAR Imaging Simulation and Speed Inversion of Ship Wake
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Ship wakes can effectively assist in detecting ship targets at sea due to their large geometric scale, long existence time, non-concealment and strong scattering characteristics. The indirect detection of the ship itself by detecting its wake has been an important direction in the application of SAR imaging in recent years. This paper utilizes the electromagnetic scattering mechanism and combines the scattering characteristics of ship wake to achieve simulation of its SAR imaging. And the ship's sailing speed is obtained through the SAR image inversion of the wake. The study can provide a theoretical basis for applications such as ship information perception, detection, recognition and stealth.

articleTitle: Radar Imaging Deception Based on Diverse Frequency Time Modulated Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this contribution, we present a novel design of diverse frequency time modulated metasurface (DF-MTS) for passive deception in linear frequency modulated (LFM) radar imaging. Thanks to the independent design of both time modulation scheme and diverse frequency concept for each element, a dynamic control of the reflected wave can be achieved enabling the real-time manipulation of the number, amplitude, and position of the false targets generated by DF-MTS. The simulated results show such a radar signature manipulation, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed metasurface to act as electromagnetic countermeasure for achieving radar camouflaging and deception.

articleTitle: Unique Structure to Improve Transfer Distance in Multi-Tx WPT System: Stacked Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The request for wireless power transfer (WPT) has been increasing for several decades, and WPT using multi-coils has recently been in the spotlight for more flexible charging. In this paper, a stacked type of multi-Tx WPT system is proposed for longer transmission distance. Contains stacked type experiments and analysis. To validate our analysis, we produced a prototype of a stacked type of multi-Tx WPT system and experimentally measured and verified it. Moreover, the experimental and theoretical values had a good agreement.

articleTitle: Active Learning Based on Scattering Center Model for Target Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a target recognition method through active learning based on scattering center model. The scattering center models are extracted by least square method from wideband echoes. Then, the active learning method is employed to adaptively expand dataset and improve recognition accuracy based on the scattering center model. The recognition accuracy reaches 92% for the nine satellite targets by the proposed method.

articleTitle: Three Synergistic Decoupling Structures to Improve Antenna Isolation for Bistatic In-Band Full-Duplex Base Station Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, three synergistic decoupling structures are proposed to improve Tx-Rx port isolation of a bistatic dual-polarization antenna array for in-band full-duplex base station application. The introduction of band-stop metamaterials, periodic metal strips and superstrates with high dielectric constant significantly suppresses the propagation of spatial coupling wave, surface wave, and reflection wave caused by radome. The improvement of Tx-Rx port isolation reaches up to 27dB, and all 16 different kinds of Tx-Rx port isolations are better than 60dB in 4.8-5.0 GHz band, with little deterioration in radiation performance and antenna matching.

articleTitle: X-Band Non-Contact Mechanical Waveguide Switch Using Iris Waveguide Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The design of a double-pole double-throw (DPDT) and single-pole single-throw (SPST) X-band waveguide switch for high-frequency applications is presented. The switch consists of two parts, an outer cube and an inner cylinder. The outer cube is fixed and the inner cylinder is located in the cavity inside the outer cube. The signal transmission path starts from the port in the outer cube. The rotating inner cylinder structure is used to provide switching and to complete the transmission path of the signal. There is no physical contact between the outer cube and the inner cylinder. Designing the switch in two parts is preferred for ease of manufacturing, assembly, and switching. Despite the gap structure in the signal transmission path, iris waveguide technology is used to ensure high electrical performance. The return loss of the switch is greater than 26 dB. The insertion loss is less than 0.02 dB and the isolation is greater than 120 dB.

articleTitle: A Dual-Fed Dielectric Resonator Antenna for In-Band Full-Duplex Operation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: We present a new approach for designing dielectric resonator antennas (DRAs) for in-band full-duplex (IBFD) operation. A dual feed is implemented, and the DRA is excited using both probe and aperture coupled mechanisms. The probe excitation uses two probes with a 180<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">○</sup>phase difference to maximize isolation and is created by using a hybrid coupler. In addition, the aperture coupled feed uses a U-slot shape to further improve the isolation. Both feeds excite the TEδ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> mode in the DRA and create a boresight beam with a gain of 7.3 dBi at 3.5 GHz. The proposed antenna satisfies isolation requirements for IBFD operation with an isolation better than 40 dB and is well matched across the band from 3.4 to 3.6 GHz.

articleTitle: MATLAB-Based Fast Vector Spherical Wave Expansion Implementation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: An optimized direct vector spherical wave expansion (VSWE) implementation is presented. The orthogonal spherical bases are generated sequentially, leveraging their linkage through the recurrence formulas. This implementation encompasses three-dimensional field analysis and synthesis scenarios. Different beam types are numerically analyzed for validation and compared with the theoretical analysis. The execution time to compute all VSWE coefficients and beam synthesis is less than 2.5 seconds with a two-degree spatially-sampled far-field. The present study promotes the integration of the VSWE as a standalone essential tool for electromagnetic field analysis within the MATLAB antenna toolbox or scientific computation frameworks built in other script programming languages.

articleTitle: Analytical Expression for Bistatic RCS of Rectangular Loop Resonator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents an analytical formulation for scattering from a rectangular loop resonator based on a circuit/transmission line model which provides the expression of the bistatic RCS. The presented closed-form RCS expression perfectly describes the resonance frequencies and the corresponding peak RCS values at all the resonant modes of the loop scatterer, which can be applied to design chipless RFID tags.

articleTitle: The FDTD Method for Hybrid Computations of the Maxwell and Linear LLG Equations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The FDTD method is utilized for computational-Multiphysics. The hybrid computations are proposed for the 3D component designs based on the ferromagnetic materials combined by electromagnetics and the magnetic dipole moment. The computations hire the Maxwell equations and the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert (LLG) equations for the computations of the electromagnetic and magnetic dipole moment values. The FDTD solver is implemented through the leap-frog processing and under the Courant-Friedrichs-Lewy condition. The simulation results are shown for the field decaying effects of the thin-film ferromagnetic materials.

articleTitle: Full-Range Phase Shift Metalens Antenna Design through ControlNet-Enabled Stable Diffusion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: We leveraged the high-resolution and computational efficiency of the ControlNet-enabled stable diffusion model to automate the inverse design of three-layer unit cells of metalens. Stable diffusion models outperform other deep learning generation models by exhibiting superior perceptual quality and successfully capturing the entirety of the data distribution, can address time-consuming problem of full-wave simulation and generate data beyond what is already present in the dataset. The synthetic unit cells exhibit a full-range phase shift capability while maintaining transmission coefficients less than 3 dB. Availability of full range unit cells can reduce the phase errors of a lens, thereby increasing the efficiency of the antenna. Utilizing these generated unit cells, we designed a horn-fed metalens antenna featuring a diameter of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{D}=10 \ \lambda_{0} \ \times \ 10 \ \lambda_{0}$</tex> aperture and an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f/D$</tex> ratio of 0.5, yielding an gain of 27.7 dBi at 10 GHz with an efficiency of 46.9%. The synthesized antenna exhibits minimal side-lobe levels (SLLs) with values of 23 dB and 24.7 dB in the E- and H-planes, respectively.

articleTitle: Fast SAR Measurement Method Based on R-U-Net
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Specific Absorption Rate (SAR) is commonly used to quantify the electromagnetic exposure of human body. Fast SAR measurement systems based on field-reconstruction techniques have been applied but suffer from ill-conditioned problems. In this paper, a field reconstruction algorithm based on deep learning network R-U-Net is proposed. Inputting sampled electric fields on a planar surface, the electric fields inside the phantom are reconstructed as the network response. The superiority of the proposed method is shown by comparing the reconstruction accuracy and efficiency with the conventional methods.

articleTitle: Revisiting the Impedance Matching Equation of Alfred Lopez
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Impedance bandwidth <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(B)$</tex> is widely known to be inversely proportionate to the loaded quality factor of a load <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(Q_{loaded})$</tex>. Also, impedance bandwidth is determined by the assumed reflection coefficient <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\Gamma)$</tex>, making the evaluation of the unloaded quality factor <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(Q)$</tex> a challenging task. To address this, Alfred Lopez introduced a single equation that uses coefficients which are independent on the reflection coefficient for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma > 1/3$</tex>. In this work, we revisit the impedance matching equation of Alfred Lopez, and we show why this independence is possible. Moreover, we show how cases where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Gamma < 1/\mathrm{B}$</tex> should be handled.

articleTitle: 60 GHz Wideband Circularly Polarized Layered Hemispherical DRA
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A 60 GHz layered hemispherical dielectric resonator antenna (HDRA) is presented with a dual-arm spiral slot that has been designed to feed the antenna through a coplanar waveguide. Matching has been achieved over a frequency range of 38–68 GHz due to adding an outer coat layer. Besides, circular polarization has been achieved over a frequency range of 55.7-61.7 GHz with a maximum gain of7.6 dBic. The achieved bandwidth exceeds those reported earlier for a 60 GHz DRA.

articleTitle: Broadband Miniaturized Vivaldi Antenna for Microwave Imaging System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper proposed a low-profile and compact miniaturized Vivaldi antenna for a non-invasive, rapid, non-ionizing, and cost-effective microwave imaging system. This antenna incorporates both the open and closed slots to provide broad impedance matching from 3.32–8.71GHz. The low-cost FR4 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$38.5\times 47.45\times 0.8\,mm^{3}$</tex> is used as a substrate. The antenna shows 5 to 6 dBi in gain and 90% in radiation efficiency. In addition to the far-field radiation property, the effects at the near field are studied in terms of reflection coefficient and radiation pattern for microwave imaging application. The results shows that the proposed antenna is a promising candidate for a microwave imaging system.

articleTitle: A Fresnel Elliptical Reflector for MMW and THz Near Field Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This article describes the design and simulation of a novel Fresnel elliptical reflector that can assist emerging technologies in the field of millimeter-wave and terahertz security imaging. The analytical expressions that satisfy the corresponding amplitude and phase of each section are presented in a general manner. Two different Fresnel reflectors are designed, and their performance is compared with conventional reflectors using numerical simulations based on the Comsol and Feko software packages. The simulation results confirm the proper focusing of the Fresnel reflector at the desired frequency. Furthermore, the frequency behavior of the designed reflectors has been thoroughly investigated. This study provides valuable insights into the design and simulation of Fresnel reflectors, which can significantly enhance the performance of emerging technologies in the field of millimeter-wave and terahertz security imaging.

articleTitle: Dual-Beam Linearly-Circularly Polarized Leaky-Wave Antenna with Wide Scanning-Range for Far-Field Distributed Wireless Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a new design of a dual-beam Leaky-Wave Antenna (LWA) with a wide range of beam scanning capability in backward and forward regions. The dual-beam radiation with frequency scanning is achieved by exciting simultaneously two radiating modes, which are related to the space harmonics <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta_{0}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta_{-1}$</tex>. The beams scanning range for the fundamental-beam is from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-22^{\circ}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$64^{\circ}$</tex>, while for the harmonic-beam, it starts from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-75^{\circ}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-31^{\circ}$</tex> in the backward region and from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$23^{\circ}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$67^{\circ}$</tex> in the forward region. The designed LWA shows a peak gain of 12.9 dBi for the fundamental-beam and 14.2 dBi for the harmonic-beam. Additionally, the harmonic-beam radiation is circularly polarized in the frequency band (11 GHz-14.5 GHz). With all its radiation characteristics, this antenna is potentially suitable for wirelessly powering multiple devices in a distributed Wireless Power Transfer context.

articleTitle: Autonomous, Enviornment-Adapative Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces with Built-in Direction-of-Arrival Estimation Function
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper explores the use of a low-cost processor for autonomously controlling the bias of a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS). It presents a self-adaptive RIS system through real-time adjustments, using a built-in direction-of-arrival (DoA) estimation system. The simplicity of the system negates any human intervention or complex control circuits, greatly enhancing its practicality. Measurements based on source angular sweep validates near-perfect accuracy of DoA retrievals with only 3 errors observed among 1,600 test data. Based on an environmental information using the DoA system, a realized gain improvement of at least 1.2 dB to a maximum of 3.9 dB is confirmed when comparing the autonomous control to conventional pre-set bias scenarios for RIS. This approach is the first to demonstrate a cost-effective and efficient solution for various RIS usage challenges, leveraging automated operation and simplified hardware for enhanced performance.

articleTitle: Skin Effect in Multiphase Concentric Cylinders
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This study addresses the challenges posed by the skin effect in modeling heterogeneous materials. Focusing on radially symmetric circular composites, we employ numerical simulations to explore the relationship between material properties, geometry, and frequency to model electrical current density distribution. We introduce a novel variable, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\hat{\delta}$</tex>, to represent the depth that contains 90% of total current density, and present a frequency-independent model for this revised skin depth definition.

articleTitle: Bespoke Lens Design for a High Gain Circularly Polarized Leaky Wave Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Radiating elements within leaky-wave antennas (LWA) undergo amplitude reduction and phase change and hence, have beam-scanning characteristics. Such antennas, when used as a feed for dielectric lenses, tend to have poor performance. This article describes a bespoke lens design for an LWA operating at 16–18 GHz that takes individual radiating elements into consideration and achieve a gain increment of approx. 7.5 dB across the operating bandwidth while maintaining circular polarization.

articleTitle: A General Model for Modelling Complex Electromagnetic Problems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Efficient and accurate computational electromagnetics (CEM) modelling tools are crucial for designing electromagnetic (EM) systems as their design process often needs the CEM modelling tools to provide the fast prediction of the EM performance of their design models or prototypes with considering complex environment. To achieve such a goal with developing CEM modelling tools with different functions, a general model is proposed for developing CEM solvers for the solutions of the complex EM problems of scattering, radiation and propagation. The proposed model is useful for understanding the common nature of different EM problems and developing one CEM modelling tool to realize different functions, such as prediction of EM scattering from object in complex environment, fast analysis of microwave circuits and systems, characteristic mode theory for antenna designs, and sub-structure characteristic mode theory for large EM system designs.

articleTitle: Experimental Design of Liquid Crystal Based Intelligent Reflecting Surface For 5G Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, design of Liquid Crystal based Intelligent Reflecting Surface (LC-IRS) for 5G communications of 40 GHz band is performed experimentally. It is found that not only the thickness of liquid crystal but also the thickness of sealing quartz grass substrate affects the reflection coefficient characteristics. Large phase change of 422 degree at the frequency of 39.7 GHz is obtained which enables the phase selection for arbitrary beam scanning direction.

articleTitle: Effects of Antenna Under Test Positioner on the Measured Pattern of Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: To measure the pattern of an antenna, regardless of if this is a near field or far field approach, the antenna under test (AUT) must be rotated in front of the range antenna. To accomplish this a mechanical device is used to rotate the AUT and position it in front of the range antenna. These positioners are typically made from metal or dielectrics. In this paper the effect of a metallic positioner on the pattern of an antenna is analyzed. The positioner is left untreated and then treated with two different configurations of RF absorber. The RF absorber treatments are a minimal coverage and a coverage where almost all the surfaces are treated. The results show that for lower gain antennas a more simplistic absorber treatment is preferrable. For higher gain antennas the treatment if not as critical and a simple treatment is sufficient.

articleTitle: Enhancing Multiband Antenna Performance with an Electromagnetically Transparent S-Band Dipole
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Mutually transparent S and X band antenna elements are presented to improve pattern performance of a co-located multiband antenna system. By selectively removing metallization from the S-band printed dipole, significant performance improvements with only 0.2dB directivity drop and better than 10dB sidelobe levels are achieved in the X-band patterns. The modified S-band dipole maintains its impedance bandwidth, while intentional drooping widens the S-band beamwidth to improve the array scanning range. The modifications to S-band dipole demonstrate negligible impact on S-band patterns due to drooping or X-band array.

articleTitle: Radio Frequency Signal Prediction using Online Generative Adversarial Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Wireless communication using radio frequency (RF) signal is developing rapidly in recent years. Many transmission systems are workingin RF signal range, so RF signal prediction is becoming an emerging topic. Many deep learning methods have been applied to do the prediction exactly. Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) has been the major breakthroughs in deep learning over the past few years, it is a neural network-based generative model which aims to mimic some underlying distribution given a dataset of samples. In this paper, we propose to use online GAN for RF signal prediction. In the future, we will apply online GAN in real scenarios.

articleTitle: Dual Beam High Gain Digitally Coded Huygens Metasurface Lens Antenna for Millimeter Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A high gain dual beam digitally coded huygens metasurface lens (HML) antenna for millimeter wave applications is presented in this paper. The antenna configuration consist of a single layered digitally coded huygens metasurface in combination with the huygens lens antenna and feeding source patch antenna. Firstly, a planer wave front is obtained by integrating the patch antenna with the huygens metasurface lens. The lens forms a highly directive beam along the broadside direction. Furthermore, a digitally coded huygens metasurface is integrated with the assembly of metasurface lens and patch antenna to realized a dual beam radiation pattern. The designed antenna is analyzed and simulated. The simulated results shows a dual beam radiation along ± 10° in the azimuthal plane at 37 GHz. A peak gain of 16.7 dBi is obtained.

articleTitle: A Cavity Backed Slot Array with Gravity Controlled Radiation Pattern Using Conductive Liquid
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper introduces a cavity backed slot antenna array in a spherical distribution that has a constant maximum radiation direction opposing the earth as the spherical array rolls. Two nested conductive spheres constitute the inner and the outer wall of the cavities backing the slots. The side walls are created with shorting pins based on the substrate integrated wave-guide concept. The space between the outer wall and the inner wall is half filled with conductive liquid which is free to move with gravity. The conductive liquid deactivates the slots that face the earth with zero energy consumption. The proposed design operates at the 2.4 GHz ISM band, with a maximum gain of more than 6 dB as the sphere rolls around its local z axis when located horizontally according to the earth surface.

articleTitle: Data Rate Performance of RIS in the Near-Field Regime Considering the Impact of EMI
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this study, we explored the achievable data rate for a single-input-single-output (SISO) uplink communication system based reflecting intelligent surfaces (RIS) in the near-field regime. We analyzed the system model considering the electromagnetic interference (EMI) and the realistic amplitude variation model for RIS. Simulation results have demonstrated the effect of EMI and the practical RIS amplitude variation model on the achievable data rate in the near-field channels. Consequently, the assumption of the widely used unity amplitude RIS model in the literature and ignoring the EMI in RIS-assisted communication systems do not give accurate and realistic measurement for the system performance.

articleTitle: 3-D Printed Wideband Multi-Beam Parallel-Plate Waveguide Folded Geodesic Lens Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A novel wideband and compact multi-beam parallel-plate waveguide folded half-Luneburg geodesic lens antenna is proposed and fabricated based on 3-D printing technology. The dimension of the proposed geodesic lens antenna is reduced by half compared to the original half-Luneburg lens design. This reduction is achieved by introducing an additional reflector on the axis of symmetry, which effectively divides the lens into two layers: the top and the bottom layers. The folded half-Luneburg geodesic lens antenna has realized a wide impedance bandwidth of 42.4% spanning from 26 GHz to 40 GHz, effectively covering the whole Ka-band. By switching the 5 feed elements, the proposed antenna demonstrates excellent scanning performance. It is capable of steering its beam within a range of 55°. The proposed antenna exhibits promising characteristics of wideband operation and compact dimensions, indicating its great potential in millimeter Wave communication applications.

articleTitle: Refinement Free Single Source Formulation of Scattering by Penetrable Objects
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: We propose an alternative discretization of the single source formulation of scattering by penetrable objects. The formulation is based on a previous idea that allows Brezzi-Douglas-Marini and Rao-Wilton-Glisson to be both employed as primal and auxiliary space instead of the common scheme with Buffa-Christiansen and RWG space. As a consequence, this formulation does not need a barycentric refinement. We also show how this formulation is particularly convenient for the single source equation and how it can be improved by an appropriate choice of the finite element spaces.

articleTitle: A Generalized RCS Definition and Its Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Based on the electromagnetic field equivalence principle, a new generalized RCS definition is proposed in this paper, which can be used for both near-field and far-field scenarios. The generalized RCS of typical objects (including the planar, cylinder and sphere object) is calculated and the results agree well with the traditional RCS results when the distance is far enough. Based on the new definition, by replacing the target with generalized RCS data and using the near-field aperture characterized radiation data instead of far field radiation patterns for transmitting/receiving antennas, the Friis equation is extended and a method for calculating radar received power is proposed. The calculated results agree well with the full wave simulated results (by FEKO).

articleTitle: Fast Scattering Analysis of Multiscale Structures in Layered Media Using MultiAIM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: We propose a fast algorithm to accelerate the electromagnetic analysis of multiscale structures embedded in layered media. Traditional acceleration schemes based on the fast Fourier transform (FFT), such as the adaptive integral method (AIM), tend to become quite inefficient for multiscale problems in layered media, because they rely on a regular grid and because the Green's function is no longer translation-invariant in the direction of stratification. We devise a multigrid approach to overcome these issues, generalizing the MultiAIM method to problems in layered media. A speed-up of 2.4× compared to AIM is demonstrated for a metagrating structure placed in a dielectric substrate.

articleTitle: A Penetrable Reactance Surface for Spherical Invisibility Cloaking
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A penetrable tensorial metasurface on a grounded dielectric shell is presented for 3-D spherical invisibility cloaking. The spatially modulated impedance surface transforms the inci-dent plane wave into a surface wave on the lit side and carries the power to the shadow side. Power is continuously released as a leaky wave with a wavefront consistent with the incident plane wave on the shadow side. A numerical design example for a four-wavelength-diameter conducting sphere is presented, and the cloaking effectiveness is validated by simulation.

articleTitle: Investigation on SAR Imaging Characteristics of Submarine Mast and its Breaking Waves
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a method to study the SAR imaging characteristics of a mast and the induced breaking waves. Based on the large eddy simulation (LES) method, the three-dimensional breaking waves caused by a submarine mast are simulated. The scattered field of the composite scene is calculated by the geometrical optics and physical optics (GO-PO) algorithm. Combined with the matched filtering and backward projection (BP) algorithm, a focused SAR image is simulated. Numerical results show that the wake structure can be detected by a SAR detector, which is valuable for the detection and identification of underwater targets.

articleTitle: THz Characterization of Unconventional Materials
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This communication deals with a simple imaging strategy able to provide simultaneously quantitative 2D maps representing thickness and effective refractive index of materials starting from time-domain THz data collected in reflection mode. The strategy exploits the time-of-flight concept, and it is valid for samples whose thickness and electromagnetic parameters are such to assure that the impinging THz wave reaches a metal substrate put behind them. The described strategy is the basis of material oriented approaches for a quantitative characterization of unconventional materials obtained by combining two substances.

articleTitle: Fast Multiphysics Simulation of Maxwell's and Drift-Diffusion Equations for Predictive Micro- and Nano-Device Simulation in the THz Regime
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a novel multiphysics simulation algorithm is developed for co-simulating full-wave Maxwell's equations and Drift-Diffusion (DD) equations in time domain. The proposed algorithm discretizes the gradient and divergence operator involved in both DD and Maxwell's equations in the same way. The discretized operators are further obtained via an analytical means using mesh information. The gradient component and the divergence-free component of the electric field of Maxwell's equations are then co-simulated with the carrier densities of the DD equation. The resultant nonlinear system of equations is formulated as a time-dependent matrix equation and solved efficiently by a backward difference based time marching scheme. Numerical results, along with comparisons with established TCAD tools and experimentally verified device simulation results in the THz regime, validate the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed multiphysics simulation algorithm.

articleTitle: High-Gain In-Situ Active Calibration Target Design for Millimeter-Wave Imaging Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, the design and measurement of a high gain active calibration target (ACT) for millimeter wave imaging system is presented. Increasing the radar cross section in ACT improves the calibration accuracy. For this purpose, we designed a high-gain array antenna, which consists of 32 planar patch elements. The measured antenna bandwidth is 3.5 GHz (26.5-30 GHz) and the peak realized gain is over 19.5 dBi. In addition, in the ACT design, switching between 4 loads instead of 2 loads is proposed to increase the precision of calibration. The measured results confirm the validity of the designed ACT circuit. The implemented ACT can be used for fast in-situ calibration of millimeter wave imaging systems.

articleTitle: A Study of a Microwave Resonant Cavity Structure for Hydrocarbon Recovery from Waste
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The aim of this article is to design a microwave heating device using resonant cavities operating at 915 MHz, which will replace the usual heat treatment devices in hydrocarbon waste refinery facilities. By analyzing the interaction of the waste with electromagnetic fields, selective heating can be achieved, providing the scope for energy savings compared to classical heating methods (e.g. hydrocarbon combustion). Electromagnetic eigen-analysis will be performed to estimate the resonance eigenvectors for the specific cavity, followed by electromagnetic analysis with a power supply. Subsequently, the heat transfer problem is solved by considering the electromagnetic energy absorbed by the material as the source when the waste material flows inside quartz tubes. The resulting temperature distribution determined that the desired heating had been achieved.

articleTitle: Wideband Multichannel I/Q Generation for Circularly Polarized Arrays
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A novel 7-21GHz 1-to- <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N/2$</tex> in-phase (I) and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N/2$</tex> quadrature (Q) radial network is proposed to synthesize circular polarization (CP) from dual-polarized coincident phase- centered apertures. Leveraging insights from antenna theory, a multichannel I/Q generating parallel-plate structure is devised that internally employs an array of alternating monopole and loop antennas to produce multiple copies of wideband 90° phase shifted signals. A BGA LTCC package with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$N=38$</tex> array ports and one connectorized port is designed and connected to a 19-element dual-polarized coincident phased array on a triangular grid through a stripline PCB manifold. Diligent full-wave simulations of the novel multichannel I/Q radial network and the full system suggest that the I/Q signals have ±5°phase error and < 1dB amplitude imbalance, which ensures better than 1dB broadside axial ratio (for ideal dipole array) over the 3:1 bandwidth.

articleTitle: 6G Sparse Transmitarray
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a planar aperiodic sparse transmitarray design for 6G with large inter-element spacings. Leveraging aperiodic arrays enhances beamforming and reduces feed network complexity, aligning with 6G demands. Numerical analysis confirms the feasibility and advantages of the design, paving the way for innovative 6G antenna array systems.

articleTitle: An Efficient Solver for Electromagnetic Scattering of Large-Scale and Complex Perfect Conductor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a novel algorithm is proposed to enhance the computational efficiency of electromagnetic scattering computations, focusing on the widely employed Method of Moments (MoM). The Integral Equation Fast Fourier Transform (IE-FFT) is employed in the Combined Field Integral Equation (CFIE) alongside the multifrontal block incomplete LU decomposition (MFBILU) preconditioner. The MFBILU preconditioner is seamlessly integrated into the IE-FFT process by extracting and decomposing near-field elements. The proposed algorithm effectively reduces the number of iterations required for convergence without adding significant computational burden, particularly beneficial for intricate multi-scale objects. Numerical examples are given to demonstrate the performance of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Generation of Millimeter-Wave 2-D Scanning Airy-Bessel Fused Beam
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The paper presents a mm-wave near-field 2D scanning Airy-Bessel hybrid beam with the property of 2D non-diffraction and self-acceleration. The presented Airy-Bessel hybrid beam that combine the Airy beam and Bessel beam utilizes the linear phase in two directions to realize the near-field 2D scanning beam. In one dimension, the linear phase related to the phase constant is utilized to manipulate the curvature of the Airy beam. Then, the frequency that can control the phase constant is used to control the steering Airy-Bessel hybrid beam. In the other dimension, a multi-ports multi-layers pillbox is used to control the direction of electromagnetic wave in the parallel waveguide, which can generate a linear phase shift between different waveguides. Then, a waveguide slot array antenna is fabricated and measured to validate the beam. The measured results in the S parameter and electrical field are consistent with the simulated ones, which shows that the array antenna can generate the 2D scanning Airy-Bessel hybrid beam successfully.

articleTitle: Radio-Frequency Energy Harvesting using 3D-Printed Rectennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This article introduces a novel rectenna utilizing 3D additive manufacturing and operating at 2.45 GHz. The idea is to optimize the antenna array gain/size factor to harvest the maximum power at a specific power density for a given distance. The proposed energy harvesting system comprises an antenna array, and the rectifier is designed based on a Figure of Merit that considers factors such as gain, size, resistor load, and distance to the transmission antenna. For validation, a rectenna is implemented with a low-cost 3D printing process, and metallization is accomplished directly using metallic tape. The experiment is conducted in an RF ambient environment, resulting in the conversion of 10.5 mW/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> to 0.1 V.

articleTitle: Calibrated Multi-Frequency Microwave Tomography for Clinical Head Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper investigates ways to address challenges facing clinical microwave tomography using a prototype microwave head scanner system. Our investigation concluded that reasonable clinical images can be generated when using a calibrated multi-frequency microwave tomography algorithm, supported by a proper frequency selection. The calibration aims at matching the forward and inverse solvers, whereas frequency selection aligns measurement with simulation. The clinical results are compared with the ground truths (MRI and CT), clarifying the potential and challenges of clinical microwave tomography.

articleTitle: Novel Broadband Quantum Limit Touching Array with AI Functionality Enabling DOA, Multi-Beam and Multi-Null Steering for High Throughput and Secure Space and Terrestrial Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Novel Broadband Condensed Spiral arrays are deployed for enabling a truly broadband multi-beam and multi-null steering. The spirals are resonating from 2.4 GHz - 6 GHz. Using digital complex weighting with adaptive techniques, we have realized over 120 dB Front to Back ratio, touching the quantum limit in the presence of multipath, and have achieved a full space multi beam and multi null steering. The system also has an inbuilt AI for interference / jamming detection and a superfast novel DOA algorithm to pinpoint its location. Our DOA algorithm is able to work in the presence of multipath. Our technology is array-agnostic and capable of functioning with any type of array elements. These elements can be randomly positioned in the x, y, z plane. Additionally, they can also be randomly and or non-uniformly distributed with element spacing exceeding the typical half-wavelength distances. This work also uses AI for signal analysis and jamming detection and has implications for high throughput and secure (LPI - Low Probability of Intercept) space and terrestrial communications. The holistic setup significantly enhances and transforms key attributes - speed, size, power, cost, and eco-friendliness. This makes it ideal for 5G and 6G arrays for civil and defense applications.

articleTitle: Analysis of Frequency Diverse Circular Array for Range Dependent OAM Modes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A circular array with frequency diversity along azimuthal direction is analyzed for range dependent Orbital Angular Momentum (OAM) mode. Based on a novel theoretical formulation of the array factor, analysis and comparison are done between existing formulation and the novel one. It was observed from the simulation results that; OAM mode close to the beam axis is different from the one away from it. Study of the OAM mode order shows spatial diversity in both longitudinal and transverse directions. This approach is more general and poses the challenge of detecting discretized phase variation and hence there will be certain shadow zones for data communication. Study of the constraint condition on OAM mode is also carried out. Due to the applied frequency diversity, range dependent OAM modes are observed without the need of externally exciting the array elements with a particular phase difference, which was necessary for the traditional Uniform Circular Array (UCA) case.

articleTitle: Dual-Beam Forming Based on Physics-Driven Deep Learning Method for Programmable Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Programmable metasurfaces have gained significant interests due to their capacity in manipulating electromagnetic (EM) waves dynamically. Here, we present a deep learning (DL) based approach to address the beam-forming task for the programmable metasurface. A newly proposed macroscopic model for calculating the far-field patterns of the metasurface is incorporated in our approach, in which the coupling between metasurface units is taken into consideration, resulting in more accurate computations of the radiation patterns. The simulation results show that our unsupervised DL method is able to give reliable designs for dual-beam cases without the need for cumbersome dataset preparation.

articleTitle: Retarded-Time Potentials Due to Impulsively Excited CRWG Basis Functions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A scheme to evaluate the time samples of the retarded-time potentials due to impulsively excited curvilinear Rao-Wilton-Glisson (CRWG) functions is presented. The retarded-time potential integrals on the surface of the CRWG functions are reduced to line integrals using the Radon transform interpretation. The resulting line integrals are calculated using the suitable order Gauss-Legendre quadrature rule (GLQR). The numerical examples that demonstrate the accuracy and validity of the proposed scheme are presented.

articleTitle: A Novel Methodology for End-to-End Millimeter-Wave Channel Modeling and Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a new technique for wideband modeling of a channel together with antennas and RF front ends, accounting for frequency dependency, coupling and dispersion, non-linearity, and polarization. The technique is based on coupling a Circuit Envelope RF circuit solver with precalculated Method of Moments (MoM) electromagnetic and Ray Tracing results to allow a full Transmitter-Channel-Receiver system simulation. Results show the importance of this approach for modeling wideband signals. The method is demonstrated on a 5G signal at millimeter-wave (mmWave) to obtain system-level metrics such as Error Vector Magnitude (EVM) and Adjacent Channel Leakage Ratio (ACLR).

articleTitle: Characterization of Near-Ground Radiohelmet-UAV LoRa Links with Transmitter Buried under the Snow
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The LoRa protocol has proven instrumental in advancing search and rescue (SaR) operations within harsh environments wherein current localization technologies underperform or are unusable. Measurement campaigns are hence investigating the radiowave propagation of LoRa to draw limits and opportunities posed by the technology, also when combined with wearable antennas and unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV): This contribution reports a measurement campaign of a LoRa link between a radiohelmet buried under 1 m of snow and a UAV, and then proposes an angular model for the excessive aerial path loss (PL) of this peculiar scenario which has not ever been considered. Indeed, the radiowave propagation in these links when the transmitter is buried under the snow has not been investigated to the best of author's knowledge. The presence of the human body is simulated by using a homogeneous meat phantom and the resulting model is in line with a similar one in mountain canyons, highlighting a significant reduction of the path loss (down to -50 dB) for low depression angles, and a more significant benefit of the use of UAVs than in suburban scenarios.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Antenna with Selective Bandwidth and Fixed Resonant Frequency
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we present a reconfigurable antenna with selective bandwidth and fixed resonant frequency. This antenna offers symmetrical bandwidth adjustment on both sides of the band (upper and lower limits) relative to its central resonant frequency. Furthermore, the antenna maintains the same radiation pattern. The proposed structure includes a simple printed monopole with an operating frequency band between 1.7 GHz to 2.1 GHz. A filtering mechanism is integrated into its ground plane, consisting of a horizontal slot combined with two vertical slots. Real switches, represented by the Pin diodes, were employed for bandwidth reconfiguration to validate the antenna's performance. The manufacturing process for the antenna is simple, and the reconfiguration mechanism is easy to implement. This antenna with its originality is well-suited for cognitive radio systems and 5G NR Sub-6 GHz applications.

articleTitle: A Compact UWB High Efficiency Rectenna for RF Energy Harvesting Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A miniaturized ultra-wideband (UWB) rectenna suitable for Internet of Things (IoT) applications is proposed in this paper. The novel approach of introducing gradient curves and loaded stubs primarily aims to improve the impedance matching performance and to obtain miniaturization features of dipole antenna at the same time. Simulation results indicate that the introduced rectenna can transform ambient radio frequency (RF) energy to DC power with high efficiency, operating across a broadband range of 1.8-3.6 GHz. In another word, the proposed energy harvester exhibits immense application potential, particularly suitable for the case with unpredictable directions of incident waves, low level of input power and a high demand for DC output power.

articleTitle: Electric-field-only FDFD method for large-scope 3D problem
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this work, a full wave analysis of three-dimensional object is proposed by using an Electric-field-only finite-difference frequency-domain (EO-FDFD) method. The improved method greatly reduce memory and calculate time requirement by eliminate the electric-field in Maxwell equations. Numerical examples are presented to demonstrate the accuracy and efficiency of mentioned method.

articleTitle: Ultra-Wideband Antenna Design and Optimization for Constant 10-dB Beamwidth in E-Plane
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The quad ridged horn antenna (QRHA) is designed with constant 10 dB beamwidth in the E-plane over 1 - 19 GHz band. The antenna is occurring from 2 parts which are coaxial to a waveguide adapter and a flare section. Higher order modes are suppressed by minimum of 16 dB using pyramidal back cavity in the adapter section. The VSWR of the antenna is below 2 in range of 2 - 20 GHz. The average of 10 dB beamwidth of the antenna is about 125°with maximum deviation of 9% in the desired band. Also, the phase center variation is below <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda/4$</tex> for the entire band.

articleTitle: Design of High Gain Circularly Polarized Reflectarray Antenna for 1U CubeSat Communication Links at K-Band
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The growing demand for small satellite missions across various domains has led to LEO CubeSats gaining popularity due to their compact size and cost-effectiveness. This paper introduces the design of a single-layer, high-gain, circularly polarized (CP) reflectarray (RA) tailored for one unit (1U) LEO CubeSat applications. The unit cells of the IURA were meticulously engineered using a compact unit cell featuring three plasmonic resonances based on geometric phase theory. This approach effectively mitigates polarization mismatch issues, ensuring more dependable and consistent communication links, which are pivotal for the success of CubeSat missions. The proposed IURA, with dimensions of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$100 \text{mm} \times 100\ \text{mm}^{2},$</tex> is designed to operate in the K-band frequency range spanning from 19 to 27 GHz. The resulting IURA design demonstrates an impressive maximum gain of 26.4 dBi while maintaining low side-lobe levels. Such substantial gain is instrumental in enhancing the overall communication performance of CubeSats, empowering more robust data transmission and reception capabilities. The fabrication of the 1 U RA is currently in progress, and the measured results will be presented at the conference.

articleTitle: Photonic Temporal Differentiator Using Planar Resonator at Terahertz-Frequency
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper introduces a terahertz (THz) temporal differentiator employing a planar resonator with a metal-polar material bilayer, specifically utilizing calcium magnesium carbonate (CaMg(CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>)2). The working mechanism is based on strong interference in the metal and the optical phonon response of the CaMg(CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>)2 thin film. Simulation results indicate that this lithography-free planar resonator exhibits first-order time derivative characteristics, with an operational bandwidth of approximately 400 GHz. The proposed differentiator exhibits potential applications in the domain of ultrafast analog computing and signal processing devices.

articleTitle: A Cascaded Quadruplet Filtering Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a 4<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup>-order filtering patch antenna with a pair of gain zeros on each side of the passband is presented. Three microstrip resonators and a patch are used in this structure. These gain zero are achieved by cross coupling structure formed by the resonators and patch radiator. For validation, a prototype is designed, fabricated, and measured, showing good performance.

articleTitle: Design and Optimization of Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces Using the PEEC Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The design and optimization of Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RISs) are key challenges for future wireless communication systems. RISs are devices that can manipulate electromagnetic (EM) waves in a programmable way, thus enhancing the performance and efficiency of wireless links. To achieve this goal, it is essential to have reliable EM models that can capture the behavior of RISs in different scenarios. This work demonstrates that the Partial Elements Equivalent Circuit (PEEC) method is a powerful tool for EM analysis of RIS-aided wireless links. It might also be integrated with optimization algorithms in order to optimize wireless communication networks.

articleTitle: Near-Field Focused Antenna-in-Package System for Millimeter-Wave Electronic Endorphin Stimulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper aims to present the design of a near-field focused antenna system developed in the V-band (61 – 61.5 GHz) for Micro Electronic Endorphins Trigger (MEET) applications. An antenna-in-package (AiP) system integrating four specific integrated circuits (ICs) has been developed and experimentally characterized in anechoic chamber.

articleTitle: Sliding Slot Arrays for Mechanical Beam Steering of Low-Profile Pillbox Antennas for Low-Earth-Orbit Satellite Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A low-profile pillbox antenna with mechanical beam steering is introduced for millimeter-wave applications. The antenna has two layers of long slots, one fixed and one movable. By sliding the movable layer, different sets of slots are exposed, which allows to generate leaky-wave radiation at different angles. A simple pillbox antenna is used to demonstrate the proposed method. Simulations show that beam steering is realized with the sliding movement. To illustrate the concept, an antenna is designed for operation at 20 GHz with 0.7 GHz bandwidth and 28 dBi maximum gain.

articleTitle: CLD-Based Automatic Frequency Selective Surface (FSS) Inverse Design
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This work presents a deep learning-based method for the inverse design of stopband frequency selective surfaces (FSSs) with the CNN-LSTM-DNN (CLD) model. With the designed model, we can directly obtain the structure geometric parameters by inputting the CLD model with stopband FSS's S-parameters. Two cases of Jerusalem stopband FSS validate the proposed method can quickly fit the requirement.

articleTitle: Design of Dual-Polarization Reflective Impedance Metasurfaces for 3D Beam-Shaping
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Reflective impedance metasurfaces can manipulate the direction and shape of the reflected fields. In this paper, a dual-polarization single-layer metasurface is designed with the aim of independently controlling the reflections of two incident waves with orthogonal polarizations. The metasurface is optimized using an integral-equation framework to perform beam-splitting for the one polarization and anomalous reflection for the other. Full-wave simulations with a realistic copper structure demonstrate the desired functionality for both polarizations.

articleTitle: Analysis of Optimizing Triple-Band Antenna Based on Ensemble Learning Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
