abstract: An ensemble learning model is employed to optimize the miniaturized triple-band antenna in this paper. Compared with traditional models, ensemble learning combines multiple weak sub-models to get a comprehensive framework that provides accurate prediction from training samples. To explore the effectiveness of the ensemble learning on antenna optimization, a miniaturized tri-band antenna with different parameters' order is adopted as an example. Meanwhile, two machine learning models are given and compared with the same antenna case. Experimental results show that the ensemble learning model can not only ensure the accuracy of optimization, but also has good generalization ability, indicating that the method is a competitive antenna design optimization strategy.

articleTitle: Exploring the Potential of Quasi-Conformal Transformed Luneburg Lens for Imaging Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper demonstrates the prospects of using a Modified 3D Spherical Luneburg lens antenna for imaging. The proposed imaging experimental setup comprises the lens fed by a rectangular waveguide to shine directive beams on the targets of different shapes placed in the path of the beams. The 60 mm diameter lens with a maximum directivity of 17 dBi is enclosed in a 160 mm diameter spherical Perfectly Matched Layer. Single-frequency monostatic full-wave simulations were performed at 18 GHz. The scattering parameters and the simulated far-field data are fed to the imaging algorithm based on truncated singular value decomposition, and the reconstructed images show the imaging capabilities of a Quasi-Conformal Transformed Luneburg lens.

articleTitle: Finite Difference Based PINN for Electromagnetic Forward Problem Solving
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINN) has surged in popularity within deep learning. However, automatic differentiation (AD) based PINN may encounter inaccuracies in the explicit functional expression of neural networks regarding inputs, leading to imprecise computations. Moreover, AD is tied to neural network complexity, incurring substantial training costs for solving complex problems. This study adopts finite difference based PINN (FD-PINN) to solve electromagnetic forward problems, reducing computational costs by disconnecting from the influence of neural network scale and prediction accuracy on derivative computation precision. Demonstrated through examples, the feasibility of this approach is solely linked to grid size, offering insights for rapid electromagnetic inverse design in subsequent studies.

articleTitle: FDTD-Equivalent Neural Network Model for Electromagnetic Simulations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel three-dimensional electromagnetic (EM) solver, grounded in theory and enhanced by integrating a convolutional neural network (CNN) with the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method. The proposed solver is designed for efficient and precise full-wave simulation of large-scale structures. By substituting the traditional operators in the FDTD method with convolutional operators, our approach maintains the accuracy and stability inherent to the FDTD method, while also being ideally suited for parallel computations. Compared to existing models, our proposed CNN- FDTD solver demonstrates improved accuracy, efficiency, and flexibility. Numerical validations confirm its superior stability and computational efficiency.

articleTitle: High-Performance MIMO Antenna Array for 6G and Beyond Smart City Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) assembly comprising six antenna arrays with a footprint of 27 × 9 × 0.2 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> is presented. Each antenna array consists of three circular patches fitted in 27 × 54 × 0.2 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> to operate on 25.2-32.5 GHz. The proposed MIMO array shows high isolation and lower mutual coupling, essential for independent operation. The antenna array depicts a consistent realized gain profile with a peak gain of 7 dBi across the maximum part of the bandwidth. The antenna efficiency is above 80% in the entire range. The proposed antenna can be deployed 6G and beyond smart city applications like indoor hotspots and outdoor short-range wireless links.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Coupler for the Detection of a UHF RFID Tag Inside a Metal Pipe
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The detection of a Ultra High Frequency (UHF) Radiofrequency Identification (RFID) tag is usually estimated by using the free-space Friis equation. However, in many scenarios the Friis equation can not be used because the distance between the reader and tag antennas is too short (e.g. the two antennas are in the near-field region each other) or the propagating field can not be considered as a locally plane wave. In this paper, some preliminary results are shown about the detection of a tag placed inside a guided structure.

articleTitle: Optical Wavelength Tunability of Negative Refractive Index Transmission Line Phase Shifter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: An optically reconfigurable phase shifter based on negative-refractive-index transmission line (NRI-TL) metamaterials is presented; the design is suitable for 5G antenna beam steering. Continuous tuning of the transmitted signal's phase is achieved by using varactor diodes for which the biasing is provided via an array of photodiodes placed on the back of the substrate. These are illuminated by a remote optical source whose wavelength can be tuned in the visible range, thus enabling indirect control of the varactor capacitance (and hence the phase shift) while also eliminating the need for a complex biasing network. Three different phases are achieved by illuminating the photodiode array with three different wavelengths (blue, green, and red). The compact size along with simplified biasing network introduced by the inclusion of the optical wavelength tunability has numerous applications in antenna and phased array technology, making the design a suitable candidate for 5G beam steering applications.

articleTitle: Investigation of Modal Characteristics of a Bevel Shaped Printed Monopole Antenna With and Without Slots
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Characteristic mode analysis (CMA) is widely used in antenna design and analysis. In this paper, we have presented a comparative study of the characteristic modes and transmit-receive antenna system transfer function poles for a printed bevel - shaped monopole antenna. The matrix pencil method (MPM) of singularity expansion is applied to extract the poles from the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S_{21}$</tex> of the two-antenna system comprising two identical bevel-shaped antennas and is compared with the characteristic modes of the antenna structure obtained by CMA. Findings show that for a bevel-shaped printed monopole antenna the transfer function poles deviate from the characteristic modes.

articleTitle: Estimating Propagation Clutter in the 3.45 GHz Band
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Effective sharing of the 3.45-3.55 GHz band requires coordination between federal incumbents and commercial cellular systems. Analysis to reduce the risk of interference between systems in the band relies on propagation models that consider realistic clutter loss factors. A method to estimate radio frequency propagation clutter losses that leverages the Irregular Terrain Model (ITM) and Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR) data for aggregate interference analysis is described here. Also included are Refence Signal Received Power (RSRP) results from field measurements for comparison.

articleTitle: Characteristic Modes and Nonreciprocity
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Properties of characteristic modes of lossless scatterers breaking time-reversal symmetry are presented utilizing the scattering formulation of characteristic decomposition. Antennas connected to nonreciprocal circuits and moving material bodies are used as numerical examples.

articleTitle: Broadband Dual-polarized Transition from SIW-to-CWG for mm- Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A Dual-Polarized Substrate Integrated Waveguide (SIW) to Circular Waveguide (CWG) transition design for mm-wave applications is introduced in this paper. Through intersecting ports, the proposed transition efficiently excites double-polarized waves and directs them to the waveguide through two slots without modifying the CWG. Demonstrated at 28.25 GHz, the transition exhibits -10 dB impedance matching of 2.25 GHz bandwidth and more than 20 dB isolation between input ports. The results confirm the effectiveness of the design, offering a reliable solution for mm-wave interconnects and contributing to the development of high-performance, miniaturized devices for mm-wave communication systems. MM-wave antenna excitation can benefit from the design's potential to simultaneously transmit data in both polarizations, which could lead to a doubled data throughput.

articleTitle: Wide-Beam and Low-Sidelobe LTCC Shared-Aperture Antenna for Automotive Radar Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we present a dual-band shared-aperture antenna (SAA) with wide beamwidth and low sidelobes for automotive radar applications, fabricated by low temperature co-fired ceramics (LTCC) technology. At the higher band (HB), an 8-element laminated resonator antenna (LRA) array is excited by an unequal SIW feeding network to minimize H-plane sidelobes. Symmetric slots are added to both ends of the LRA in the E-plane to broaden the beamwidth. At the lower band (LB), a 5-element series-fed grid-shaped patch array surrounds the LRA array to form an aperture-sharing structure, with tapered patch widths to decrease sidelobe levels. As a proof-of-concept, we have designed a dual-band SAA operating around 24 GHz and 77 GHz frequencies.

articleTitle: Ku-Band Patch Antenna on Thick, Aerosol Jet Printed Substrate
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: An aerosol jet printed (AJP) Ku band patch antenna on top of a thick (>250 um) substrate is presented for the first time. The conductive material used is Clariant Prelect TPS 50G2. The area of the patch antenna is 5.82 × 7.16 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The material used for the substrate is Benzocyclobutene (BCB) and is approximately 300 μm tall. The RF circuit will be excited via a CPWG to microstrip transition. The antenna had a simulated gain of 4.95 and a S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>of -34 dB. These results show that AJP is a viable option to create RF structures on thick printed substrates.

articleTitle: A Multiband Reflector Antenna for Rural Areas with the Capability of Generating Any Arbitrary Gain at each Frequency Band
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A multiband-multibeam dual parabolic cylindrical reflector antenna is proposed for all wireless applications, especially in rural areas. The design parameters of the antenna can be remotely controlled such that the antenna covers any area having an arbitrary shape and size. Different feeds can be used simultaneously with the reflectors of the antenna to cover all the required frequency bands for all wireless telecommunication applications. The feeds are dual polarized to reduce the need for MIMO (Multi Input Multi Output) techniques. The isolation between the different feeds is high. The antenna gain at each frequency band can be separately controlled. The antenna can generate any required gain at each frequency band.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Dual-Band Dual Circularly Polarized Antenna Array for Millimeter-Wave Satellite Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A reconfigurable array antenna working at 28/38 GHz exhibiting dual circular polarization (DCP) is presented. The DCP is attained by exciting the inputs of two orthogonally positioned dual-band antenna arrays through a dual-band branch-line coupler (DB-BLC), generating ±90° phase-shifted signals resulting in opposite circular polarization at these bands. An additional 10dB suppression in the side lobe levels at 38 GHz is achieved using an unequal power divider. The reconfigurability of circular polarization at each band is facilitated by toggling the input through a wideband absorptive switch connected at the input ports of the DB-BLC. This antenna array, featuring high gain with < −10 dB S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>., and <3dB axial ratio (AR), reconfigurability, opposite circular polarizations, and improved CP performance at 28/38 GHz, emerges as a promising solution for satellite communication applications.

articleTitle: A CNN-based Material Classification Approach Using Heatmap of a Dual-band Microwave Sensor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The performance of highly sensitive microwave res-onators deployed for material characterization is hindered by the lack of selectivity. This is especially noticeable when dealing with unknown chemicals. In this article, we propose a machine learning algorithm that enables selective sensing based on post-processing of the sensor response. A dual-band planar CSRR is designed at 1.45 GHz and 2.45 GHz, with sizes confined to 20% of the guided wavelength. It is used to discriminate between concentrations of 0-100% of ethanol/methanol in water, with increments of 20%. A convolutional neural network is used for multiclass classification with a high accuracy of 91.5%.

articleTitle: A Nonlocal All-Metallic Metagrating for Engineering the Direction of Electromagnetic Energy Transfer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Herein, a spatially dispersive (nonlocal) all-metallic metagrating is proposed for manipulating transverse magnetic (TM) polarized incident waves at a discrete set of incident angles. The designed device channels most of the energy of normally incident waves to the direction of the zeroth order of diffraction while deflecting most of the oblique incident waves along specific refraction angles, corresponding to higher orders of diffraction. The refraction phenomena do not depend on the sign of the incident angles, making the structure an effective beam diverging device at the considered incident angles and frequency. Some notable advantages of the proposed structure include low material losses, scalable design and feasible fabrication.

articleTitle: Network and Circuit Models in Electromagnetic Field Computation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Hybridization schemes for the systematic, general and efficient evaluation of electromagnetic fields are discussed. The computational space is subdivided in various subregions where different analytical and numerical methods are employed. These methods may also be combined in the frame of the same subregion. The application of such methods to stochastic EM fields and in quantum computing algorithms is also outlined.

articleTitle: A Frequency-Reconfigurable Microstrip Patch Antenna Based on Gravity-Driven Liquid Metal
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a frequency-reconfigurable microstrip patch antenna based on gravity driven liquid metal. The antenna is composed of a dielectric substrate, microstrip feeder, ground plane, and eutectic gallium indium (EGaIn) alloy (liquid metal). The antenna can rotate around the axis, causing the liquid metal inside the cavity to flow and deform. The shape of the liquid metal will vary at different rotation angles, thereby changing the radiation characteristics of the antenna. Simulation results show that the operating frequency bands of the antenna are 4.77~4.84 GHz, 4.01~4.07 GHz, 3.77~3.83 GHz, 4.91~4.99 GHz, and 4.66~4.73 GHz, respectively, when the rotation angles are -90°, -45°, 0°, 45°, and 90°(clockwise rotation angle is positive). Also, different operating frequency bands do not overlap each other and the radiation patterns have very low side lobes. This paper provides a new and simpler approach to realize the frequency reconfigurability by the liquid metal without using a complicated electrochemical control device for the liquid metal.

articleTitle: Optically Transparent Dual-Polarized Metasurface at 150 GHz Using Laser Cutting Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel optically transparent passive metasurface and its fabrication method, aiming at reducing the costs for providing a wide range of reflectors with different reflection angles. The method adopts a common design pattern regardless of the reflection angles, and the design pattern is customized by post-processing using laser cutting technology according to the required angle. We present an optically transparent dual-polarized metasurface reflector composed of a 30×30 array. Simulation results have revealed that desired angles of 27°, 43°, and 63° are successfully achieved at 158 GHz. The proposed method will significantly reduce the manufacturing costs and contribute to the widespread adoption of metasurfaces toward 6G.

articleTitle: Decoupling of Dipole MIMO Antenna Fed by GCPW at X-band
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A decoupling method for dipole multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) antennas fed by grounded coplanar waveguide (GCPW) operating at X-band is proposed in this paper. By loading the metal blocking branch Stub-I, the ground coupling current was truncated, and by loading the metal reflecting branch Bar-I, the spatial coupling current was neutralized. The interaction between the two branches greatly improved the isolation of the MIMO antenna. The measured results show that the antenna achieves <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{S}_{11} / \mathbf{S}_{22}<-10$</tex> dB in band of 7.5-12.1 GHz, with a relative bandwidth of 47%. In this frequency band, the antenna isolation is greater than 19.3 dB, with a maximum isolation of 61.4 dB. The maximum gain of the antenna is 8.47 dBi. This antenna has good radiation performance and high isolation, which can be applied to MIMO communication systems requiring high isolation.

articleTitle: A Scattering Model Derivation Framework for Electrically Large Targets in PolSAR Images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Scattering model is an important basis for polarimetric synthetic aperture radar (PolSAR) remote sensing image interpretation. Nowadays, most scattering models of targets for feature extraction in PolSAR images are summarized according to simple scattering mechanism analysis, and the accuracy and application conditions of those models are limited. In this paper, based on the physical optics (PO) and geometric optics (GO) of high frequency approximation techniques, a framework for scattering model derivation of electrically large targets in PolSAR images is proposed. Based on this framework, accurate scattering model with great applicability of any electrically large target can be derived.

articleTitle: 2x2 Port Super Wide Band Volcano Smoke MIMO Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The Volcano Smoke Antenna (VSA) was introduced in the 1940s by Krauss. However, it was not until the 21st century that this geometry was thoroughly investigated, following the FCC assignment for Ultra Wide Band (UWB) technology. In this conference article, a new Super Wide Band four-port Multiple Input Multiple Output (MIMO) antenna is introduced, utilizing the Volcano Smoke Antenna (VSA) geometry. The antenna, with dimensions of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$65\text{mmx}65\text{mm}$</tex>, achieves levels below −10 dB for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S11$</tex> and −13 dB for isolation <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S1m$</tex> in the band of 2.73-43.38 GHz.

articleTitle: Wideband Adaptive Null-Extended and Frequency-Invariant Beamforming Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A widband adaptive null-extended and frequency-invariant beamforming method based on convex optimization in this paper. The simulation results demonstrate the performance of this method in generating 6° null under the condition of OdB signal noise ratio.

articleTitle: Antenna Mass Production for SKA-LOW
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: For the first time ever, a radio telescope requires the production of more than 100,000 identical antenna systems. This unprecedented situation is encountered in the low-frequency radio telescope of the Square Kilometer Array. The reference antenna is a dual-polarized log-periodic dipole antenna operating between 50 and 350 MHz supplemented by two low-noise amplifiers. The manufacturing of almost half of the target number of antennas has been assigned to an Italian industry, Sirio Antenne, based on a proposed production scheme matching the challenges given by delivery time, cost, reliability, and high-quality performance.

articleTitle: Hybrid-Polarized Resonant Bessel-Beam Launchers: A Leaky-Wave Design Exploiting an Efficient Semi-Analytical Matching Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Recently, hybrid-polarized Bessel beams have been proposed as a valid solution to radiate focused beams in the near-field region at microwaves and millimeter-waves. As shown by the leaky-wave design proposed in this work, such beams can be excited in a resonant cavity by etching a slot on the ground plane which is fed through a rectangular waveguide (RWG). Matching networks are often required to efficiently couple the waveguide to a highly resonant cavity. We thus propose a semi-analytical technique for such waveguide-fed launchers which saves a significant computational burden with respect to full-wave optimizations. The matching technique consists in the numerical choice of the design parameters of two RWG discontinuities after a single full-wave simulation. Hence an optimum solution is found by numerically minimizing an analytical objective. Theoretical results are in a remarkable agreement with full-wave simulations allowing for the efficient design of limited-diffractive Bessel-beam launchers for a variety of millimeter-wave applications.

articleTitle: Passive Channel Measurement and Analysis of High-Speed Railway Station Scenario at 3.5 GHz
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a recent channel measurement campaign for high-speed railway station scenario is conducted by using passive measurement platform. Based on the actual measurement data, the path loss (PL) and root mean square (RMS) delay spread of channel characteristics were analyzed. The results indicate that the PL of high-speed railway stations is affected strongly by penetration loss. The delay spread follows a lognormal distribution and is much larger than the WINNER D2a model. These findings provide preliminary channel information for the study of next generation high-speed railway communication systems.

articleTitle: Wideband Circularly Polarized Antenna for In-Band Full-Duplex Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A wideband circularly polarized (CP) antenna using the partially shared magneto-electric (ME) dipole structure is proposed for the in-band full-duplex (IBFD) application. The CP sense for transmitting (Tx) and receiving (Rx) are the same, and both are right-hand circular polarization (RHCP). The CP operation for Tx or Rx is formed by two orthogonally placed Γ-shaped feed lines and their excitation with the same amplitude and the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$90^{\circ}$</tex> phase difference introduced by the feed network. The operating bandwidth is from 2.01 GHz to 2.66 GHz. The radiation patterns for the Tx and Rx ports are broadside and nearly uniform. These features can satisfy the requirement for future wireless communication.

articleTitle: Decoupling Method of Millimeter Wave Antenna Array Based on Partial Reflection Decoupling Surface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents the design and application of a partial reflection decoupling surface (PRDS) to reduce the mutual coupling in a millimeter-wave (mm-Wave) antenna array. The PRDS utilizes the reflected electromagnetic wave from an isomorphic metal patch structure positioned above the patch antenna array for decoupling purpose. Remarkably, these improvements are achieved without modifying the original antenna array design. The PRDS enhances the isolation of the antenna array elements by up to 15.5 dB. It also improves the gain by 1.2 dB. Moreover, it broadens the operating bandwidth by 17%. Consequently, the proposed high-isolation antenna array holds great promise for mm-Wave wireless applications.

articleTitle: Sequentially-Fed Circularly Polarized Slot Antenna Array Using Printed Ridge Gap Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A wideband sequentially-fed circularly polarized slot antenna array excited by printed ridge gap waveguide (PRGW) technology to eliminate back radiation from the slots is presented. Each slot is coupled to two orthogonal printed microstrip lines from a Y-shaped power divider that equally divides the power with a 90-degree phase difference for CP radiation. Using a sequential feeding structure significantly improves the axial ratio bandwidth of the antenna compared to the single element. The proposed antenna array operates in the Ka-band, and demonstrates a −10-dB impedance bandwidth of 20.4%, a 3-dB axial ratio bandwidth of 20%, and a peak RHCP gain of 12.3 dBic at 33 GHz.

articleTitle: Optically- Transparent EM Skin Meta-Atom for Next-Generation Smart Buildings
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Wireless cellular systems at mm Wave frequencies have been proposed to meet the increasing demand for mobile communication data rates. However, challenges arise in outdoor-to-indoor scenarios featuring mm Wave carriers due to signal degradation from building penetration losses. The possibility to integrate passive field manipulating devices into building walls to overcome such issues has been recently proposed in the Smart Electromagnetic Environment (SEME) framework. This work is aimed at illustrating some of the fundamental challenges within this scenario, particularly focusing on the design of meta-atom architectures ensuring high optical transparency and wide RF phase coverage for sustainable outdoor-to-indoor wireless communications.

articleTitle: D-Band On-Chip Endfire Quasi-Yagi Antenna in 130 nm SiGe BiCMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper introduces a D-band on-chip antenna with endfire radiation in 130 nm SiGe BiCMOS technology. The quasi-Yagi antenna contains a U-shaped dipole antenna as a driver, and the silicon substrate is introduced as the director. Moreover, the guard ring of the SiGe technology is partly removed for gain enhancement. Then, an off-chip copper package and on-chip metal layers are introduced to act as the reflector. Finally, 0.2-4.0 dBi gain could be obtained in the frequency range from 120 to 146 GHz in the simulated results, and the S-parameter is measured for demonstration.

articleTitle: Design and Integration of V2X and SDARS Antennas in Automotive Rooftop Sharkfin Antenna Module
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Rooftop Sharkfin antenna module in modern automobiles incorporates a variety of antennas. In this paper, we address the design, optimization and integration of antennas needed for Vehicle-to-everything (V2X) and satellite digital audio radio service (SDARS). A narrowband omnidirectional monopole that operates over the frequency band of 5.845-5.935GHz is designed for V2X applications. A patch antenna with Left Hand Circular (LHC) polarization operating over the frequency band 2.320-2.345GHz is designed for SDARS applications. Both antennas are designed and optimized to fit within the space and size constraints of a rooftop sharkfin antenna module while meeting the performance specifications such as gain and directionality of the antenna and coexistence with GNSS and cellular antennas.

articleTitle: A Filtenna Based on Gap Coupled Multilobate Design for C-Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A filtenna for operating in the C-band is presented. The proposed filtenna comprises two multilobate patches in close proximity. The main patch is directly fed by a coaxial feed, while a parasitic patch is gap-coupled, exploiting the self-complementary of an original multilobate design. The arrangement of these two patches permits to design an effective filtenna operating in circular polarization for the C-band. The proposed design exhibits a maximum left hand gain of 6.21 dB, a cross polarization discrimination exceeding 15 dB at the frequency of 5.8 GHz. The filtering properties of the antenna shows with a sharp stop-band at 6.2 GHz, where the broadside gain drops below −7.48 dB, meaning 13.70 dB of isolation.

articleTitle: Adaptation and performance of well-known non-linear inverse solvers in optical microscopy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: We have adapted several nonlinear inverse scattering algorithms to reconstruct the three-dimensional profile of the refractive index of the sample given the camera images obtained from a coherent dark-field microscope. Specifically, we applied contrast source inversion method and contraction integral equation based inversion method for this inverse problem where only phaseless and polarization-insensitive data is available. We have also adapted Born approximation for comparison. Our results show that nonlinear inverse scattering solvers are promising for sample reconstruction using microscopy data with only a few illuminations.

articleTitle: Estimating Atmospheric Attenuation Exploiting Noise Power Measurements from Satellite Receivers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A technique for estimating atmospheric attenuation time-series at Ka-band exploiting noise power measurements from a satellite receiver is proposed. The objective is to provide a tool for treating satellite receivers as beacon receivers for the atmospheric attenuation retrieval without the need of additional external sources thus reducing hardware complexity and costs. Results of the attenuation estimated with the proposed technique are in agreement with available simulations with a bias ranging from 0.49 to 0.71 dB.

articleTitle: A Dual-Band Aperture-Shaped Antenna Array Based on Choke Stubs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A dual-band aperture-shared antenna is designed, with the low-band (LB) antenna operating at 1.7-2.2 GHz and the high-band (HB) antennas operating at 3.3-3.8 GHz. To suppress the secondary radiation caused by the induced current, choke stubs are added to the radiation element of the LB antenna, realizing a low-scattering antenna with an operating band of 1.7-2.2 GHz (S11 < -15 dB). For demonstration, the prototype of the proposed antenna array is fabricated and measured. The simulated and measured results prove that stable radiation patterns are achieved by the LB and HB antennas in the dual-band aperture-shared antenna array.

articleTitle: Impact of Near-Field Probe Failure in Antenna Far-Field Pattern Estimation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Accurate pattern measurement requires a near field (NF) facility which is expensive to both acquire and also maintain in ideal working condition. For fast NF measurement, multiple NF probes are often used on the NF aperture with their sampling time-multiplexed. This comes at the cost of the extra electronics and probes but simplifies the precision robotics required for sampling the NF surface. Another cost is an increased failure probability, and so a practical problem with NF facilities is the failure of a NF probe. The impact on the FF pattern estimate may not be obvious depending on the FF pattern shape and the relative location of the failed probe. There seems to be no treatment of this in the literature, so this paper discusses examples for a typical range (Satimo SG64, with 5 m cubed chamber) and a typical antenna where the pattern detail is important, viz., a small C-band fixed-beam slot array used for synthetic aperture radar.

articleTitle: $\mathcal{PT}$-Symmetry Equalization and Time-Space Frequency Mapping in Leaky-Wave Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: We present here the first complete, fundamental and rigorous general resolution of the broadside gain degradation issue, due to the phase matching of oppositely propagating space harmonics, in periodic leaky-wave antennas (P-LWAs). We show that the solution corresponds to a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{PT}$</tex> -symmetry of the complex temporal frequency modes, related to topological unit cell asymmetry, by transforming them into complex spatial frequency modes using analytical continuation.

articleTitle: Dual-Beam Independent Scanning via Time-Moudulated Array
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The existing dual-beam independent scanning technology has problems with complex circuits and low antenna efficiency. Therefore, in order to solve these problems, this paper proposes a multiple time-modulated waveform (MTMW). By simply multiplying time-modulated waveforms with different time delays, the phase of different harmonic coefficients can be independently controlled, so that the independent scanning of dual-beam is achieved. Simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A Way to Improve Polarization Purity Significantly in a Microstrip Sub-Array
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A practical requirement based on a specific feed network has been addressed for a two-element microstrip sub- array. This indeed replaces aperture coupled feed by a corporate probe as commonly recommended for large array geometry. The configuration embodies strategic engineering with ground plane as well as microstrip element geometry to achieve high polarization purity over the entire radiation planes. The proposed design at S-band promises a commercial viability with an overall XP reduction by 7 dB over skewed/diagonal (D-) planes and approximately 10–12 dB across the H-plane, while minimally affecting primary radiation or gain values.

articleTitle: Demonstration of Absorption Performance Beyond the Rozanov Bound through Time Modulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The Rozanov bound dictates strict performance trade-offs for linear time-invariant electromagnetic absorbers. In this paper, we present the design, fabrication, and testing of a circuit-based time-varying absorber. We report the first experimental demonstration that a suitable periodic modulation leads to absorption performance exceeding the Rozanov bound, corresponding to reduced reflections over a broad bandwidth.

articleTitle: A Broadband Filtering Antenna Based on SISL for 5G MMW Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A broadband filtering antenna based on substrate integrated suspended line (SISL) for 5G MMW applications is proposed. The antenna uses the open slot on the patch and the parasitic strips to generate two radiation nulls outside the high and low bands, respectively. The addition of transverse metal strips and the U-shaped strip also introduces two radiation nulls outside the high and low bands. Four radiation nulls make the antenna obtain a good filtering response. In addition, based on the fundamental mode of the patch, the open slot on the patch generates a new resonant point, which improves the bandwidth of the antenna. The antenna is manufactured and tested to cover 25.2-30.9 GHz (20.2%). The peak gain is 7.15 dBi, and the out-of-band suppression level can reach 17.75 dB. The antenna is based on FR4 substrates, which have the advantage of being low-cost.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of a Novel Plasmonic Butterfly-type Nanoantenna: Optical and Far-field Properties
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, the design of a novel butterfly-shape antenna (patent pending) over the 0.1-10 THz frequency range is proposed. The antenna consists of two simmetric gold arms with a lenght of 46.48 μm, a width of 22.40 μm, and a thickness of 200 nm gold separated by a gap of 20 nm. The two-layer substrate is composed of 3 μm of silicon and 50 nm of gold. Simulation results, carried out by CST Studio Suite 2023, show three different resonant frequencies at 2.1 THz, 3.6 THz, and 5.1 THz, respectively, with a −10 dB <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S$</tex> <inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> lower than −18 dB for each resonant frequency and a directivity up to 11.04 dBi. Starting from the design of a single butterfly-nanoantenna, a 2x2 array is simulated and fabricated.

articleTitle: A Reconfigurable 6-Bit Chipless RFID Sensor for Humidity Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Radio frequency identification technology is widely applied in sensors due to its capability of identify multiple targets at same time with high efficiency. Among the research areas of RFID technology, chipless RFID technology is a widely concerned topic, since the lower cost after removing the embedded chips. In this paper, a configurable chipless radio frequency identification (RFID) senor is demonstrated. It is designed based on microstrip patch antenna. On both sides of the patch, six in total, S-shaped split ring resonators (S-SRRs) are located to construct the trap circuit. Besides, PID diode is added in each resonator to achieve reconfigurability. The parameters of resonators are optimized, and six different states of the tag are reported. One resonator coated with humidity-sensitive material, works as sensing unit. Simulated result of resonance frequency shifting with the humidity is presented. Therefore, it has the potential of sensing moisture in environment and working in various scenarios counting on its reconfigurable design.

articleTitle: An Effective Pattern Reconstruction Method for the Under-Sampled High-Frequency Planar Near Fields
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents an accurate and efficient method to reconstruct the far-field pattern of the under-sampled high-frequency planar near field for the antenna under test based on the asymptotic field similarity theory and spatial convolution-deconvolution method.

articleTitle: Volume Manufacturing of 3D Printed GRIN Lenses
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper explores the viability of production scale additive manufacturing of 3D printed Gradient Refractive Index Lenses. Utilizing Fortify's suite of production tools for 3D printing, a production run of 20 62 mm Luneburg lenses, designed with a mid-frequency gain of 22.4 dBi at 22 GHz, was carried out and measured for variability in boresight gain. With a manufacturing yield of 95% and a measured maximum deviation of ±0.16 dBi, the sample run of Luneburg Lenses indicates strong and competitive performance repeatability at production scale manufacturing levels.

articleTitle: 3D Printed Wideband Dual-Polarized Lens Antenna for mm-Wave Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A low-cost three-dimensional (3D) printed wideband dual-polarized lens antenna, useful for communication system design for future millimeter-wave (mm-wave) communications, is presented in this paper. The proposed antenna consists of a feed in a waveguide configuration, a conical reflector, and a dielectric lens to improve the performance of the radiating structure. The antenna works in the 75–100 GHz frequency range, providing a maximum gain of 9 dBi in the azimuth plane. CST Microwave Studio, implementing a full-wave locally conformal finite integration technique (FIT), was employed to characterize the antenna and to guide its physical realization. A good agreement was found between the numerical results and the experimental measurements performed on an antenna prototype. The structure offers the advantages of robustness, cost-effectiveness, and ease of fabrication in waveguide configurations.

articleTitle: Effects of the Ground Plain and of Neighbouring Objects on the Performances of Open TEM Cells
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper a series of analyses aimed at assessing the performance degradation of an open TEM cell operating in presence of the ground and of neighbouring objects is performed. Results show that, despite the scattering parameters being only slightly modified, the field uniformity deteriorates, and this may lead to the violation of the field requirements. In particular, the field uniformity deteriorates less when the neighboring objects are placed close to the port being fed.

articleTitle: A New Type of SIW-Based Linear Slot Array Antenna with Enhanced Impedance Bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a new type of enhanced-bandwidth linear slot array antenna based on substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) is designed in V band. The antenna consists of two Rogers RT/duroid 5880 substrate layers functioning as the radiating layer and the feeding layer, respectively. To obtain an enhanced impedance bandwidth, two signals with the same amplitude and phase functioning as feeding to radiating slots are coupled through two coupling slots placed at one-third and two-thirds of the length of the radiating layer. The proposed linear slot array can realize an enhanced impedance bandwidth of 12.29% (59.18-66.93 GHz) with the maximum gain of 16.01 dBi.

articleTitle: A Compact Broadband 5GHz IoT Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a broadband 5GHz highly compact antenna for IoT applications operating in the band 5.05 to 6.36 GHz is introduced. The antenna maintains a very compact size while covering a range of 1.31GHz. The antenna employs a number of broad banding techniques that include, slotting, near field resonant parasitic elements, and an air gap between the substrate and ground plane. The antenna is designed on a 0.127mm thick Rogers RT/Duroid 5880 substrate. The near field resonant parasitic elements are shorted to the ground with the help of copper pins. A truncated ground plane is also used support wider bandwidth. The proposed antenna has compact size of 10×15× 2.4mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> and provides a wide bandwidth of 1.31 GHz.

articleTitle: An Ultra-Wideband 3D Printable Magneto-Electric Dipole Antenna Fed by a Hollow Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A Ka-band cavity backed magneto-electric (ME) dipole antenna with ultra-wide bandwidth is proposed. An all-metal structure can be easily realized with 3D-printing technology minimizing the errors while assembling the antenna with multiple layers. A gain of up to 14.6 dBi and an impedance bandwidth of 39% from 29.5GHz to 43.8GHz are achieved by the proposed antenna unit cell. Each layer in the proposed antenna contributes to an enhanced performance. The broadband characteristics of the ME dipole is increased by the addition of the cavity backed hollow waveguide feed network. The proposed antenna unit cell can be used to build compact planar arrays in the Ka band by incorporating low loss and wide band T-junction power dividers in the complex feed network. The proposed antenna has an advantage of easy fabrication through 3D printing technology and it can be utilized for wideband millimeter-wave wireless applications.

articleTitle: Single- and Dual-Band FSS with Switchable Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this work, we propose an FSS that electrically reconfigures its transmission spectrum. The FSS is formed by elements based on the four-arms star geometry, and it uses PIN diodes as active components. Three states of configuration of the FSS panel are analyzed. By biasing the entire panel with the voltage, either forward or reversed, the structure shows single-stopband response, while when half of the panel is forward biased and the other half is reserved biased, it shows dual-stopband response.

articleTitle: Differentially-Fed Dual-Band Dual-Pol Microstrip Antenna on Flexible Substrate for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper introduces a compact dual-band, dual-polarized antenna designed on an ultrathin substrate (270 μm thick) with flexible and conformal capabilities, providing band-widths across 27.1-28.3 GHz and 36.8-38.2 GHz. To overcome the challenge of controlling coupling in dual-polarized patch antennas on thin substrates, we propose a differential feeding approach for one port to minimize coupling by introducing out- of-phase currents. The antenna's differential feeding is achieved through the design of a wideband coupled-line phase shifter in a T-junction. Notably, exciting only one port differentially avoids high coupling caused by crossed feeding lines. To mitigate resonance differences resulting from asymmetrical feeding, the patch antenna is intentionally designed with asymmetric dimen-sions' enabling the simultaneous tuning of resonances for both polarizations and frequency bands.

articleTitle: Lithography-Free Tunable Fano Resonator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a lithography-free thermally tunable Fano resonator obtained by strong coupling between the narrowband and broadband resonators. The unique optical phonon response of the Dolomite (DLM) thin film and the phase-change material (PCM) of vanadium dioxide (VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) are utilized to design such a Fano resonator. The findings of this study can have multiple applications, ranging from biosensing and gas-sensing to the modulation of thermal emission.

articleTitle: A Dual-Polarized Ultra-Wideband Fully Inverted-L Element (FILE) Array
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A new dual-polarized ultra-wideband array is introduced, called the fully inverted-L element (FILE). Specifically, our dual-polarized FILE (DP-FILE) unit cell is comprised of two L-bent elements, which tightly couple to a common shorted via as well as to each other. Notably, the same shorted via is utilized to suppress the well-known common mode resonance. To lower the cost of our array, a close to optimal spacing of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.47\lambda_{h}$</tex> is utilized for reduced element number. Additionally, to increase its scanning capabilities, we properly (a) utilize a dual-layer superstrate, and (b) perforate both its substrate and superstrate. Our proposed element is simulated in an infinite array environment, demonstrating a 2.75 : 1 operational bandwidth (34 GHz to 94 GHz) with a maximum scan angle of 45° and orthogonal port coupling less than −10 dB for all principal E-, H- and D-planes.

articleTitle: Balanis' Career with the Advanced Helicopter Electromagnetics Research Program
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In addition and teaching classes in antenna theory and electromagnetics, Professor Balanis led many research efforts while at the Arizona State University. Most notably, the Advanced Helicopter Electromagnetics (AHE) research program formed in 1989 lasted over 28 years, serving the U.S. helicopter industry and government agencies that manage aircraft technology and development programs. This paper highlights some of Prof. Balanis' contributions to the longstanding AHE program that spanned nearly half of his distinguished career.

articleTitle: Efficient Singularity Expansion Method Implementation Using Characteristic Mode Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The Singularity Expansion Method (SEM) can be used to quantify and optimize the linear or nonlinear natural response of an antenna but can require complex numerical calculations. This work develops a highly simplified methodology to reconstruct the SEM late-time response of an antenna using purely Characteristic Mode Analysis (CMA) quantities and equivalent circuit techniques. The basis of the proposed technique is to link the resonant frequencies, damping coefficients, and pole residues of SEM with the modal weighting coefficients, quality factors, and characteristic currents of CMA, respectively. The accuracy of the proposed method is demonstrated by replicating the SEM results for a loop antenna with excellent agreement. Since CMA techniques are available in most common commercial electromagnetic solvers, the technique developed herein enables the adoption of SEM in new antenna and scattering applications.

articleTitle: A Multi-resolution Adaptive Encoding Method for 3-D Reconstruction of DPO-SDF
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Recently, the differentiable physical optics method (DPO-SDF) achieves high-precision 3-D reconstruction of perfect electric conductor (PEC) scatterers from scattered electric fields. Nevertheless, employing implicit neural networks directly as the 3-D representation of the reconstructed target results in significant memory consumption and high computational costs during training stage. This paper presents a multi-resolution adaptive encoding method to significantly reduce the number of parameters that require updating in each iteration. Numerical experiments demonstrate that our encoding method significantly reduces memory usage during the training stage while improving reconstruction speed without compromising accuracy.

articleTitle: Transparent Conductive Nanowire Antennas-Material Preparation, Characterization, and Notes on Antenna Design
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper is a summary of the latest development in optically transparent antennas designed from conductive nanowire networks. An overview of material preparation, characterization, and notes on antenna design with improved efficiency are presented.

articleTitle: Multimodal Radar for Epileptic Seizure Monitoring: Concept and Design
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Millimeter-Wave radar systems are emerging as a crucial technology for real-time patient monitoring, notably in detecting vital signs and bodily movements. Despite their potentials, the challenges lie in designing a singular system that can concurrently monitor subtle cardiorespiratory activities and rapid limb movements, all while providing spatial imaging. This paper focuses on leveraging radar technology for the precise observation of patients at pre-seizure and intra-seizure stages of epilepsy. We employ Range-Doppler analysis using variable observation window lengths and sampling rates to discern between low- and high-activity states, thereby achieving robust detection of parameters such as heart rate, respiration, and abrupt limb movements. Additionally, we address the impact of sampling limitations by examining the role of aliasing effects in the scenarios studied.

articleTitle: Capacitively-Coupled UHF Antennas for Wireless Temperature Monitoring of Bearings in Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This work introduces a capacitively-coupled telemetry system operating in the UHF band (868–960 MHz). It is based on two concentric C-shaped dipoles positioned at a millimeter distance. Numerical simulations have been employed to optimize the angular dimensions of the antennas, and the resulting arrangement ensures a stable link for any mutual orientation. Preliminary experiments conducted with a mock-up have demonstrated that sensing and communication through backscattering modulation can be achieved with only 400 μW of power.

articleTitle: A Three-State Polarization Reconfigurable Millimeter-Wave Horn Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper introduces a horn antenna structure that can reconfigure its polarization between three distinct states: linear, left-handed circular polarization, and right-handed circular polarization. The reconfigurable performance is obtained across the span of frequencies between 33 GHz and 37 GHz. The on-demand reconfiguration of polarization states is obtained by dynamically translating two passive helices between optimized strategic locations within the horn aperture. The antenna prototype along with its reconfiguration mechanism is fabricated and tested, where measurement results agree well with simulated data.

articleTitle: Electron Scattering at a Soft Temporal Potential Step
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: We solve the problem of electron scattering at a soft temporal potential step. Given the relativistic nature of the problem, we use the Dirac equation, with its spinor wavefunction. We find solutions in terms of hypergeometric functions, which demonstrate that the observed phenomenon of later forward-wave and backward-wave electron scattering previously reported for a sharp (Heaviside) temporal potential step can be obtained experimentally and applied to new electronic devices.

articleTitle: Data Generation and Analysis of USRP and OptiTrack for the Moving UGV Localization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive methodology for generating a dataset for localization experiments in a controlled environment. We utilized a Universal Software Radio Peripheral (USRP) with LabVIEW for signal transmission and an Unmanned Ground Vehicle(UGV) equipped with a receiving antenna and OptiTrack cameras to establish ground truth in a 3×3-meter grid divided into 9 blocks. The experimental setup involved a moving UGV with a receiving antenna, a stationary transmitting antenna at the grid's edge, and OptiTrack cameras for precise ground truth measurements.

articleTitle: A Wearable Flexible Loop Antenna for In-Body Beamforming
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a wearable flexible loop antenna array for use on the anterior and posterior torso. The antenna array that has been developed to assist in the detection of excess fluid in the lungs operates in the Medical Implant Communication System frequency Band. The antenna elements use a novel high-permittivity flexible substrate with dimensions of 70.5 mm x 59 mm x 2 mm. We investigate a simple beamforming technique to enable focusing the transmitted energy toward a specific lobe of the lung and also improve the low signal power at the receiver. Inbody beamforming is achieved by adding proper phase shifts to the transmitter antennas. Both the return loss values of anterior antennas and the transmission coefficients between the anterior and posterior antennas are presented.

articleTitle: A Compact High-Efficiency Rectifier With Lumped Band Stop Structure For Wireless Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a compact high-efficiency radio frequency (RF) rectifier based on band stop structure is proposed for wireless power transfer (WPT). The rectifier utilizes the voltage doubling topology, a dual band stop structure consist of two parallel lumped LC resonators is placed on the anode of the parallel diode, which can provide an infinite impedance to suppresses the second and third harmonics generated by the diode. To simplify the circuit design, two inductors are used for the input impedance matching. Then, a LC DC-pass filter is designed to suppress the RF signal at the DC output port. For verification, a rectifier was designed, fabricated, and tested based on lumped elements. The measurement results show that the maximum RF-DC conversion efficiency is 78.5% at 13 dBm input power. Meanwhile, the fabricated rectifying is compact only with 10.6 mm x6 mm.

articleTitle: LCPML-log: A New Locally-Conformal PML Method with Logarithmic Decay Function for Finite Element Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: We present a new locally-conformal perfectly matched layer method, called LCPML-log, for solving electromagnetic radiation and scattering problems using the finite element method (FEM). Unlike previous PML methods, the LCPML-log method has two advantages: (i) It achieves optimal PML performance without any parameter tuning, and (ii) it works well with even a single PML layer. Hence, the LCPML-log method offers a more cost-effective and robust PML technique.

articleTitle: Multi-Probe Partially Coherent Near-Field Measurements and Field Transformations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Conventional non-convex phase retrieval algorithms struggle with local minima and false solutions, in particular in the presence of noise. These issues are overcome with a linearized phase retrieval algorithm for multi-probe near-field measurements without global reference signal. We present measurement results to verify that this algorithm works well with noisy real-world measurement data, given a suitably designed probe array and sufficient oversampling.

articleTitle: Efficient Algorithm of Resonance Features Extraction Using Multiple Polarization Datasets
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The efficient approach of the modified matrix pencil method is investigated for the dielectric-coated objects with various polarization states of the incidence signal. The simulation analysis is conducted by considering linear, circular, and elliptical polarization states with all four vertical and horizontal components. The results indicate that the extra additional resonance modes get excited due to variations in the polarization which is validated by the parametric analysis.

articleTitle: Cross-Band De-Scattering and Decoupling for Dual-Band Shared-Aperture Dielectric Resonator Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper introduces an innovative design specifically tailored to reduce cross-band interference, including both scattering and coupling, between two dielectric resonator antennas (DRA) in a shared-aperture arrangement. Central to the design is the utilization of a conformal semi-transmissive ring metasurface, which effectively restores and reinforces the fields within each frequency band without the need for additional spatial allocation. The design also incorporates an enhanced feed structure that significantly improves the isolation between the elements, thereby ensuring their independent operation. This pioneering approach addresses cross-band scattering and coupling in collocated dual-band DRAs for the first time. The resulting DRA is suitable for installation on drones to support satellite communication.

articleTitle: Characteristic Basis Function Method Using Single High-Level Subdomain Basis Function for Efficient Analysis of Irregular Sparse Array Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel formulation of the Characteristic Basis Function Method (CBFM) tailored for the numerically efficient analysis of irregular sparse array antennas (ISAs) in radiating mode. This approach utilizes a single high-level CBF to represent the current profile on each antenna array element. The CBF is constructed by determining the current distribution on each antenna element by applying the Method of Moments (MoM) within the scope of a local problem defined by the element's radius of influence (RoI). The efficacy of this method is validated through the simulation of a 12-element ISA composed of log-periodic antenna elements. Results demonstrate excellent agreement with the MoM-based reference solution from a commercial Computational Electromagnetics (CEM) solver, but with the advantage of significant reduction in overall computational cost.

articleTitle: Ku-K Dual Band Antenna-In-Package Design of Array of Subarray for Beamforming Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A Ku-K dual-band antenna array is proposed for antenna-in-package beamforming applications, comprising eight subarrays integrated on an interposer board using ball-grid-array (BGA) packaging. The array incorporates commercially available beamforming chipsets and includes four Ku-band and five K-band miniaturized antenna elements within the novel dual-band subarray. Simulation results indicate potential array gains of 19.6 dBi in Ku-band and 21 dBi in K-band. Currently in the preliminary stage, the design will undergo fabrication as a proof-of-concept with planned improvements. Measured results will be presented at upcoming conferences, marking the next step in validating the proposed dual-band antenna array.

articleTitle: Wullenweber Antenna with ULPIL Element Antenna for Secondary Surveillance Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The Wullenweber antenna for the secondary surveillance radar is numerically analyzed. The unbalanced fed ultra low profile inverted L (ULPIL) antenna with its directivity of 7 dBi is used as element antenna. The directivity of ten-element phased array antenna mounted on the side of sixty-faced polygonal cylinder with its radius of 1,400 mm becomes to 22 dBi at the design frequencies from 1.03 GHz to 1.09 GHz.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Rather than reconstructing the properties or parameters of a medium as it is done in electromagnetic inversion, this work aims to classify objects with neural networks that are trained with scattered field data and labels (classes). The study demonstrates the feasibility of achieving an 86% accuracy, showcasing potential applications in robotics and environmental perception.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a 1-Bit Guided Wave Fed Transmitarray Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper we introduce a 1-bit guided wave fed transmitarray antenna based on the inherently low-profile substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) technology capable of one-dimensional, frequency independent and reconfigurable beam scanning. The antenna structure is composed of a 21-element, one-dimensional array of slot antennas whose radiating state is determined by PIN diodes soldered across the slots. The design of the antenna structure is discussed, and the beam scanning performance is verified by full-wave simulation.

articleTitle: Wideband Azimuth Angle Insensitive Cross-Polarization Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper proposed a wideband azimuth angle insensitive cross-polarization converter based on the dipole-via-dipole model. The design employs a couple of orthogonal dipole antennas to receive incident waves. Connecting the orthogonal resonators through metallized vias facilitates the transformation of the incident wave polarization mode into its cross-polarization mode. Irrespective of changes in azimuthal angles, this design achieves a high cross-polarization transmission efficiency in the 13-18.8 GHz range, with a relative bandwidth of 36.5%.

articleTitle: Polarizing Reflectarray Antenna in K and Ka Bands for Small Satellites
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This contribution describes a dual-band polarizing reflectarray antenna for small-satellite communications. The proposed antenna has been designed to generate a high-gain beam while converting the incident dual-linearly polarized field into dual-circular polarization in K and Ka bands. The unit-cell, based on orthogonal groups of dipoles, comprises two layers of metallization, where each layer is designed to independently operate at a different frequency. The polarization conversion process has been generalized to operate with non-stacked dual-polarization elements for each frequency, which allows to use a single layer per operating frequency. The simulated results show a maximum gain larger than 30 dBi and an axial ratio below 1.5 dB at both design frequencies (19.7 and 29.5 GHz).

articleTitle: Novel Microwave Snow Melting Waveguide Utilizing EBG to Prevent Electromagnetic Leakage
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel snow melting method that involves directing microwaves onto snow without outward electromagnetic wave leakage. The integration of the Electromagnetic Band Gap (EBG) structure into the waveguide successfully achieved to prevent unintended radio wave emission. The electromagnetic characteristics of the near field in the EBG combined waveguide for snow melting were analyzed, and the structure was devised to comply with radio wave protection guidelines. Measured results at the near-field of the prototyped the EBG waveguide demonstrated the effectiveness of EBGs in preventing electromagnetic radiation leakage. In this study, microwave energy intended for snow melting is recycled for wireless power transmission aimed at powering the snow melting device's mobility. For this purpose, a power receiving probe is incorporated into an EBG waveguide. The wireless power transmission efficiency was evaluated based on the S-parameters obtained by both analysis and measurements, which revealed an efficiency of over 40 %.

articleTitle: Advancements in ULF Transmitter Design: Metglas Modulation and Magnetic Field Dynamics
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a novel Ultra Low-Frequency (ULF) transmitter that utilizes a static permanent magnet to produce a time-variant magnetic field. By controlling the reluctance of the surrounding magnetic material, the magnetic field can be modulated without any mechanical movement, making it an easily scalable option. The transmitter was successfully developed and tested using a vector induction coil magnetometer, demonstrating a normalized field strength at the receiver that was 16.4 dB higher than the coil's leakage at an 800 Hz frequency. A biphasic sinusoidal signal modulated the magnet, operating at twice the source frequency.

articleTitle: State-Space Representation and Stability Analysis of Time-Domain GSTC-Based Metasurface Solvers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A continuous-time state-space formulation is pre-sented to analyze the stability and poles of the analytical Generalized Sheet Transition Conditions (GSTC) that characterize idealized metasurfaces. Furthermore, a discrete-time state-space formulation is also presented to analyze the numerical stability when the GSTC is discretized using a finite difference scheme in the time domain. A bilinear transform is applied to map between the continuous-time and discrete-time domains to examine the influence of finite time discretization to the poles and stability of the GSTC.

articleTitle: Efficient and Robust Optimization of Wearable Antenna Arrays with Multi-Objective Pareto Front
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This study presents an efficient technique for estimating the radiation characteristics of an antenna system by exploiting its scattering matrix. The method involves a series of radiating elements and probes positioned at strategic intervals, enabling the reconstruction of the S-matrix and subsequent radiation characteristic estimation. To illustrate the effectiveness of this approach, a test case is evaluated, demonstrating the optimization of radiated fields using the multi-objective Pareto front to achieve optimal trade-offs.

articleTitle: Development of High Optically Transparent Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface for 5G
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RIS) technology, aimed at improving radio coverage in 5G and 6G networks. We propose a new reflective element structure for RIS, designed to maintain over 80% transparency and excellent cross-polarization discrimination, without compromising aesthetic considerations. A prototype RIS was fabricated using a transparent conductive film with fine wiring, demonstrating the ability to alter the reflection angle from the frontal direction to 28 degrees in the 28 GHz band, while meeting the target cross-polarization discrimination value.

articleTitle: Switchable Multi-Band PIFA Antenna For IoT Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A reconfigurable antenna, the size of a business card, is presented in this paper. The antenna is constructed using a set of PIFA antennas, with each antenna designed for a specific frequency. The reconfigurability is achieved through the use of PIN diodes for control. The design of the antenna is simple and easy to tune, and it covers six frequency regions ranging from 433 MHz to 7.125 GHz. To achieve such a compact size while covering a wide range of frequencies, a meandering technique is employed. Additionally, the paper introduces the concept of combining two frequencies on the same antenna element. The antenna is thoroughly simulated, fabricated, and measured, demonstrating a high level of agreement between the simulation and measurement results. The design is implemented on Rogers RO 4003C substrate, but it can be easily adapted for other substrates.

articleTitle: Rotation-Driven Zooming Reconfigurable Holography Via Bilayer Cascaded Phase-only Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Metasurface-based holography has attracted widespread attention as a new means of realizing holographic displays. In the face of the growing reliance of modern science on big data, conventional metasurface-based holography shows great limitations. Here, we propose a rotation-driven reconfigurable holography strategy via bilayer spatially cascaded phase-only metasurfaces, which can realize reconfigurable holography in three-dimensional space. By rotating the first metasurface, different holographic images can be generated in different planes along the optical axis. In addition, a gradient descent-based inverse design method is proposed to establish a connection the between phase distribution of the bilayer phase-only metasurface and the predefined targets.
