As a proof of concept, we validate the zooming reconfigurable holography with five channels in the microwave region by simulation. We believe that the proposed scheme has great potential in reconfigurable meta-devices, high-capacity information encryption, and high-capacity information storage.

articleTitle: A SVM-Based Approach for Detecting Tendon Injury
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a solution for the fast detection of shoulder's tendon injury based on numerical modeling and machine learning (ML) algorithm is proposed. The synthetic data for the ML algorithm are the set of scattering parameters which are produced by solving Maxwell's equations for each transmitting antenna of the microwave imaging (MWI) system. The corresponding data of various healthy and injured models are categorized into two classes. Using support vector machine (SVM) for classification, an accuracy of 100% is achieved.

articleTitle: Effect of Coplanar Waveguide Feedline on Car Roof-Glass Integrated GNSS Antenna Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: An extension of the feedline is often needed when an antenna is integrated with the roof glass of a car. How much the extension affects the antenna performance depends on the type of antenna and feedline used. This paper studies the effects of coplanar waveguide feedline extension on the performance of a circularly-polarized square slot antenna. Simulation results show a general decrease in the antenna performance with the addition of the feedline. However, the negative effects of the extension on the axial ratio and total efficiency are periodic, indicating that these effects can be mitigated by optimizing the feedline length.

articleTitle: Detachable Impedance-Matching Boosters for FSS-Based Broadband Designs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Without modifying the unit-cell geometries of existing frequency-selective surfaces (FSSs) or metasurfaces (MSs), this paper proposed a simple but effective approach to improve impedance matching to the free space over a broad frequency spectrum. Specifically, a pair of free-standing dielectric slabs act as impedance-matching transformers, and the outermost equivalent circuit branches remain unaffected due to the air spacers. Through the application to a wideband bandpass filter, it has been verified that, with both a single dielectric material and more practically a stack of multiple available dielectric materials, the in-band energy transmission can be enhanced from 90% to 99% without trade-off in bandwidth or out-of-band rejections.

articleTitle: Butler Matrix-Based Beam Switching with Frequency-Tunable MIMO Array
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A frequency-adjustable dual-polarized Multiple Input Multiple Output (MIMO) antenna is designed with the aid of Substrate Integrated Waveguide (SIW) technology. A 1 × 4 linear array of this antenna is configured to provide the condition for beam switching with dual-polarization and frequency-tunability. Two separate Butler Matrixs with wide impedance bandwidth are utilized to do the beam switching. The simulated results verified that from 3.8 GHz up to 4.4 GHz, the operating frequency can be altered electronically. This structure is a suitable candidate for base station applications since dual-polarized beam steering can be achieved.

articleTitle: Machine Learning as Applied to EM - Trends, Advances, and Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Machine learning (ML) has paved the way for development of algorithms and statistical models that enable computers to perform tasks without being explicitly programmed. The availability of voluminous amount of data and high throughput graphics processing units (GPU) has led to the promising field of Machine Learning. The primary goal of machine learning is to enable computers to learn from data. Electromagnetic (EM) algorithms solve Maxwell's equations under various boundary conditions and for a variety of materials. EM algorithms serve as the kernel of EM simulation. Traditional EM simulators are commonly based upon the Finite Difference Method (FDM), Finite Element Method (FEM), Finite Difference Time Domain (FDTD), Method of Moments (MOM). Such simulations consume large amounts of CPU time and memory. Thus full-wave computational EM solvers are prohibitive for applications requiring a real-time response. Machine learning steps in as a game-changer. Machine learning techniques provides a platform to implement an end-to-end EM simulation driven solely by data functioning as a fast real-time EM simulator. This paper describes the progress in the field of electromagnetics contributed by penetration of computationally powerful machine learning methodologies.

articleTitle: Recyclable Near-Field Chipless-RFID Tags with High Data Capacity and Density
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a near-field chipless-RFID system with tags exhibiting a high data density (2.52 bit/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) and capacity (53 bits) implemented by means of sustainable materials, i.e., paper substrate and organic and carbon-based inks (specifically, PEDOT:PSS and carbon graphite). This high data density and capacity has been achieved by means of an encoding strategy that utilizes the rising and falling edges of a clock signal generated by the motion of the tag over the sensitive part of the reader.

articleTitle: Transfer of a Low-Cost Coaxial-Waveguide-Transition Concept to Larger Waveguide Standards
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper describes the transfer of a self-developed and published WR90 Coaxial-Waveguide-Transition (CWT) to a WR187 waveguide standard. The procedure briefly addresses the modified parameters and illustrates the results in the form of S-Parameters. A subsequent analysis and comparison of the deembedded results leads to better performance for larger waveguide standards but also the consistent conclusion of inadequate copper metallization and high tolerances in manufacturing for smaller waveguide standards.

articleTitle: A Microwave Focused Hyperthermia Technique through a Continuous Current Sheet based on a Tightly Coupled Cylindrical Array
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The purpose of this paper is the design of a Tightly Coupled Dipole Array (TCDA), intended for a microwave focused hyperthermia application at 915 MHz. The scope is focusing on a cancerous tumour, when each element is fed with the appropriate current (phase and amplitude). The required goal is to achieve a function similar to this of a concave lens, minimizing the occurrence of secondary hotspots while reducing the power density at the array's surface. This can be achieved by radiating the required power from a larger surface and directing it towards the cancerous area. The estimation of excitation currents follows a previous reported method based on the Reciprocity Theorem. The results are encouraging suggesting the potential array usage for microwave hyperthermia applications.

articleTitle: A Multifunctional Bianisotropic Frequency Selective Surface for Microwave Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a multi-functional bianisotropic FSS for microwave frequency bands. To achieve bianisotropic properties and multi-functionality in the proposed FSS, different types of unit cells with different geometrical configurations are designed on both sides. When a linearly polarized wave is incident on the proposed FSS, it acts as a beam splitter in the frequency band of 7 to 11 GHz, a pass-band filter between 13 and 18.5 GHz, and an absorber in the frequency band of 19.75 to 20.5 GHz. On the other hand, when it hits the opposite side of the FSS, it behaves as a beam splitter in the frequency band of 7 to 11 GHz and a broadband stop filter in the frequency band of 15 to 24 GHz. With these functionalities, the proposed FSS is a suitable candidate for absorption, filtering, and beam splitting applications.

articleTitle: High Efficiency 140 GHz SIW Slot Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a high-efficiency 140 GHz SIW slot array antenna is presented. A 5×4 element array is designed using an alternating phase-based feed network with bowtie shape feeding slot. A waveguide to SIW transition is also designed to feed the antenna. The antenna with the transition achieves radiation efficiency of more than 80% from 130 GHz to 143 GHz with a peak efficiency of 92.6%. The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\vert S_{11}\vert \leq-10\text{dB}$</tex> bandwidth of the array is from 130 GHz to 143 GHz. The gain of the antenna is more than 11 dBi from 130 to 147 GHz with a peak gain of 14.3 dBi at 140 GHz. The size of the antenna is 8.2 mm×6 mm.

articleTitle: High Power - High Efficiency Bandwidth Antennas Through FSK Direct Antenna Modulation (DAM)
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Electrically small antennas are a class of antennas where the electrical size of the antenna is significantly smaller than the wavelength of the frequency of operation. Often, such antennas are utilized on platforms where the physical real estate is significantly limited. Such antennas are inherently narrowband in impedance matching, but are also highly inefficient in radiation. To overcome these limitations, a using Direct Antenna Modulation (DAM) is utilized where the antenna is directly modulated at its peak energy moments through the use of a high-speed GaN transistor switch. Previous iterations were unable to attain high power transmission due to the coupling between the RF signal and the switching signal needed to directly modulate the antenna. In this work, we propose a symmetrical topology of DAM which allows high efficiency bandwidth transmission at high power, handling up to 42 dBm of RF power.

articleTitle: On-Chip Microstrip Antenna Array for Millimeter Wave Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Recently, On-Chip Antennas (OCA) have become one of the most extensively researched topics in the antenna community, particularly in the context of millimeter-wave and terahertz technologies. The integration of antennas with the remaining circuitry on a single chip and the potential for achieving high data rates, facilitated by the utilization of high frequencies, are two main factors behind the growing interest in this technology. This paper introduces an on-chip antenna array implemented on a high-resistivity silicon substrate. Additionally, it presents reflection coefficient measurements for four prototypes of a printed patch antenna array, conducted in a probe station environment at 60 G Hz. The measured results indicate a favor-able agreement between the on-wafer probe station environment's input match and the simulated counterpart.

articleTitle: Equivalent Circuit Modeling of Wearable Magnetoinductive Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: We recently introduced wearable magnetoinductive waveguides (MIWs) for wireless body area networks (WBANs) that exhibit several advantages compared to the state-of-the-art. These were analyzed via a full-wave numerical solver which can handle non-ideal conditions but has high computational cost. In this work, we present, for the first time, the equivalent circuit modeling of wearable MIWs using Advanced Design System (ADS) that can solve the same problem with a computational time of ~1 minute compared to several hours taken by the full-wave solver. Additionally, the proposed method provides several benefits that are not possible via a full-wave solver, or any other method used for such problems.

articleTitle: Numerical Validation of the Multi-Modal Transfer Matrix Method for Hexagonal Unit Cells
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this work, we present a modeling procedure for studying periodic structures with a hexagonal lattice. We extend two numerical methods to hexagonal unit cells: the multi-modal transfer matrix method and the method of moments. Both methods are capable of obtaining complex solutions of the eigenproblem. The results of the two methods are found to be in excellent agreement for both the passband and stopband modes.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of 5G-R Physical Layer Using Hardware-in-the-Loop Simulation Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: 5G network for railway (5G-R) emerges as a promising train-ground communication solution, concurrently facing ubiquitous connectivity and reliable transmission design challenges. This paper focuses on the impact of different channel models and Doppler effects on the physical layer transmission performance of the 5G-R communication system. Based on the 5G-R channel hardware-in-the-loop simulation platform, we measured and compared the performance of the 5G-R system in terms of bit error rate (BER) and error vector magnitude (EVM) across different scenarios. The measurement results reveal that non-line-of-sight propagation and Doppler effects during high-speed movement contribute to the deterioration of the system's BER and EVM. Nevertheless, enhancing the signal-to-noise ratio can mitigate the impact of these factors to some extent.

articleTitle: Phase Stable 2-Bit Reconfigurable Reflective Metasurface for 6G Wireless Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The present work proposes a novel reconfigurable metasurface topology, intended to be used as unit cell of a RIS. The designed metasurface is based on a Magneto-Electric Dipole topology, whose performance is enhanced by an annular parasitic patch. The latter element increases the phase tuning range, operated by only one varactor diode, and it extends the working band by stabilizing the phase derivative in the different tuning states. The MED based unit cell, realized in low cost design, is numerically characterized, and its performance is demonstrated through the simulation on a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$20\times 20$</tex> unit cells active RIS. Due to its good performance and low cost solution, the proposed MED based unit cell represents a promising candidate for the next generation of RIS, intended to support the future 5G and 6G telecommunication scenarios.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Dual-Polarized Shared-Aperture Base Station Antenna Based on Transparent Structures with Broadband Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: To accommodate various application scenarios in 5G era, the demand for multi-band shared aperture base station antennas is growing, which means the issue of cross-band coupling should be resolved urgently. This article introduces a dual-broadband dual-polarized base station antenna array. The proposed array comprises a high-band (HB) antenna operating at 3.3-4.2GHz and a modified low-band (LB) antenna with low scattering characteristics, operating at 1.63-2.63GHz. To eliminate cross-band coupling, two transparent structures, T-shaped strips and a circular ring with a cross-shaped strip are integrated in the LB antenna. The simulation results show that the scattering of LB antenna to HB radiation significantly reduces, which indicates the proposed base station antenna array can achieve stable radiation performance across two wide bandwidths with small frequency ratio.

articleTitle: POTR Over POTF Simulation — a Way to Check Compliancy with ARC Specs Prior Tag Measurement
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this work, we show how to benchmark the RF performance of a RAIN RFID tag against ARC specs' requirements on both forward (POTF) and return (POTR) links, utilizing a pure simulative approach. To enable this, the POTR values should be presented as a function of POTF values, as dictated by ARC spec threshold definitions. Simulated results are in good agreement with the measured data and thus are extremely useful, especially at the initial phase of tag antenna development against a certain ARC spec, before manufacturing and evaluation of the tag.

articleTitle: Elliptical Dielectric Lens-Based Two-Port Antenna for Ka-Band Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This communication presents a novel Two-port Ka-band antenna design with improved isolation, high gain, and wide bandwidth for 5G applications. The suggested design employs a diamond-shaped dense dielectric (DD) antenna as a source with an X-slot mounted on a substrate that is fully grounded. An elliptical dielectric lens was made with Rogers RT5880 to improve the gain placed above the source (DD). This novel design enhances the gain bandwidth and decoupling between ports, delivering isolation levels over 20 dB and gain exceeding 12 dBi. The design achieves this without adding to the antenna profile or incorporating intricate decoupling structures. This makes it a highly promising approach for millimeter-wave MIMO communication services.

articleTitle: A K-Band Beam Steerable Metal-Only Transmitarray Unit Cell Using Out-of-Plane Rotation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Mechanical actuation to achieve reconfigurability for transmitarrays is a simple, reliable, and cost-effective approach. In this paper, the unit cell design for a multi-layer mechanically reconfigurable metal-only transmitarray operating in K-band is presented. Six layers of frequency selective surfaces are stacked in parallel and rotated in elevation up to 75°. The unit cell of the transmitarray implements multi-slot elements and can achieve a total phase range of 282° to 391° and average loss of 0.5 dB between 24.5 and 27 GHz.

articleTitle: Multi-target Vibration Measurement using mmWave FMCW Radar for Industry 4.0
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This study measures multi-target vibration in Industry 4.0 environments where vibration can be harmful. Vibration measurement is done by using phase values that can be translated to displacement and multi-target detection is done by a newly-proposed detection algorithm. Abnormal behavior of machinery and working mode switching altercation be measured through this research. This study can be further extended into a factory monitor system where personnel could be saved from routine checks and failures of systems could be predicted.

articleTitle: A Series-Fed $2\times 2$ Filtering Microstrip Antenna Array with Second-Order Chebyshev Response
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A series-fed <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2\times 2$</tex> Filtering Microstrip Antenna Array (FMAA) with a second-order Chebyshev response is proposed. A feed line is coupled to novel Z-shaped resonators, which are also coupled to U-shaped patch antenna elements. The proposed structure behaves as a second-order Band-Pass Filter (BPF), and the response matches the Chebyshev prototype circuit. Moreover, the structure provides a flat broadside antenna gain response in the pass-band and two radiation nulls in the out-of-band. The measurements are consistent with the simulated results. Notably, the array size can be easily increased without altering the feed structure, and it does not compromise the filtering feature.

articleTitle: A Lightweight Flexible Microwave Absorber using 3-D Printed Honeycomb Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A three-dimensional (3-D) printed lightweight microwave absorber design is presented in this work. The geometry uses a perforated honeycomb made from Polylactic acid (PLA) material as the constituent dielectric, thus minimizing both the overall volume and weight of the structure. The unit cell geometry exhibits an absorption peak at 4.6 GHz with a peak absorptivity of 99.99%. The topology also shows polarization-insensitivity and angular stability. Further, the design has been investigated for planar as well as non-planar (cylindrical) surfaces, and its absorption performances are found satisfactory.

articleTitle: Intelligent Design for On-Demand Reconfigurable Reflectarray Elements
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a deep learning approach for the design of on-demand reconfigurable reflectarray elements. By leveraging microwave network analysis, our technique efficiently reduces the dataset size by half. We introduce a novel target function to obtain high-performance elements. The benefits of this approach are experimentally demonstrated by automatically generating an on-demand wideband 1-bit reconfigurable reflectarray element, significantly enhancing the bandwidth performance compared to conventional designs.

articleTitle: A New Method of Fault Detection and Location for Phased Array EMC Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The traditional fault detection and location method for phased array electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) needs a complex detection process with a larger number of data, which suffers from low efficiency with a long time for locating EMC faults. This paper presents a new method for fault detection and location of phased array EMC based on deep learning. It is used to extract the characteristics of induced current signals generated by interference sources on phased array antennas and fit the causalities between them. The proposed method enables rapid and precise detection and localization of faults, thereby presenting a novel approach to phased array EMC fault detection and location.

articleTitle: Doubly-Periodic Unit Cell Modeling of the Frequency-Dependent Transmission and Reflection Behavior of Large Aperture Antenna Radomes Wetted by Water Drops
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In quantitative precipitation estimation with point-to-point commercial microwave links, the observed path attenuation of interest can be strongly influenced by wetness on the antenna radomes. Wet antenna attenuation (WAA) can, therefore, cause considerable overestimation of rain rates. In order to better understand WAA, we investigate full-wave electromagnetic reflection and transmission simulations of randomly wetted antenna radomes utilizing a doubly-periodic unit cell model. The physical effects of scattering and absorption of energy by individual water residuals are fully considered in the simulation. We show minimum-maximum ranges of plane-wave transmission and reflection coefficients of the wet radome for different drop densities.

articleTitle: A Machine Learning-based Inverse Scattering Method for Biomedical Imaging Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a transformer-based neural network, for segmenting the images of human tissues obtained by inverse scattering method. Firstly, the distribution image of relative permittivity for the human tissue is obtained by the subspace-based optimization method (SOM). Then the obtained results are fed into a transformer-based network to output a segmentation mask. Numerical results verify that this method can get clear edges for different tissues, and it can achieve accurate classification for human tissue imaging.

articleTitle: Additively Manufactured Ultra-Wideband Cavity-Backed Stacked Patch Antenna for 5G mmWave Conformal Phased Array Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper introduces an innovative additively man-ufactured ultra-wideband cavity-backed stacked patch antenna, utilizing 3D printing and inkjet printing technologies. The pro-posed antenna configuration comprises three substrate layers, stacked top and bottom patches, a microstrip feedline, and a metal cavity. The design successfully achieves an extensive 62.3 % operational bandwidth spanning from 22.3 GHz to 42.5 GHz, covering the entire 5G mmWave frequency band. Leveraging the advantages of 3D printed flexible substrates, the resulting antenna element emerges as a suitable candidate for integration into conformal phased array configurations.

articleTitle: Miniaturized Planar Band-Pass Filter for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper explores a compact bandpass filter for low-band 5G base station applications. The proposed filter offers a passband spanning from 450 MHz to 1500 MHz, encompassing critical frequency bands such as n71, n5, n44, and various lower frequency 5G bands. With a remarkable attenuation exceeding 10 dB over the n66, n40, and n41 5G bands, the filter is designed to enhance signal quality within the specified frequency range. Implementation has been achieved on both low-cost FR4 substrate and the widely utilized Rogers R003 substrate. Notably, the substrate dimensions are reduced to a minimal 0.067λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>× 0.083λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>x 0.003λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>(Ao is the free space wavelength at 500 MHz), highlighting the compact nature of the proposed filter.

articleTitle: A Yagi-Uda Antenna as an Epidermal Strain Sensor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Advances in materials and production techniques create new design possibilities and applications for microwave sensors. In this work, the design of a Yagi-Uda antenna as a strain sensor for non-invasive muscle contraction detection is presented. To monitor epidermal strain, a highly flexible polyurethane substrate measuring <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{35}\ \mathbf{mm} \times \mathbf{20}\ \mathbf{mm} \times \mathbf{200}\ \mathbf{\mu} \mathbf{m}$</tex> is utilized. For a 10 % strain increase, the separation between the dipole elements increases by 0.1 mm. A 20 MHz shift in the resonant frequency of the antenna is observed for each 10 % step. The proposed Yagi-Uda antenna operates within the 2.4 GHz ISM band across strain values ranging from 0 % to 30 %.

articleTitle: A Novel Small Aperture Direction Finding System Based on Phase Mode Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A novel small aperture direction finding (DF) system based on phase mode antenna (PMA) is proposed to estimate the angle of arrival of (Ao <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A$</tex>) signal without ambiguity. The DF system is based on a single dual-port PMA, which can achieve beam scanning continuously in xoz plane. The aperture size of the DF system is only 0.4λ × 0.47λ at 2 GHz. The simulated results show that the maximum DF error is less 2.3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">○</sup>within the region of ± 60<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">○</sup>in xoz plane. This novel DF system is simple and compact, which presents high application potential in small wireless systems.

articleTitle: Adaptive Beamforming with Dipole Arrays on Drones
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Beamforming from an array of vertical dipole elements on a drone is considered. The dipole elements are located on a fixed “double-cross” layout consisting of a central element surrounded by eight neighbors. The double-cross layout is optimized beforehand, and the amplitudes and phases of the radiators are then optimized to give specified patterns. We use a fast optimization approach and also explore a simple iterative approach to obtain the complex dipole currents to achieve adaptive beamforming. Dynamic null steering is also explored, in which the central array element is used as a dynamic cancelling element to steer a pattern null on the fly.

articleTitle: Can Series or Parallel Switches Improve the Performance of Reconfigurable Reflectarray Elements?
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper employs microwave network analysis to theoretically show that the performance limit of 1-bit reconfigurable reflectarray (RRA) elements only depends on the imaginary/real impedance ratio of a single switch state and the ON/OFF impedance ratio between two switch states. Crucially, the performance limit is found to be independent of the absolute impedance values of the switches. Furthermore, it is demonstrated that series or parallel identical switches CANNOT improve the performance of RRA elements, challenging conventional methods of combining identical switches for performance improvement, and offering new insights into the design and optimization of RRA elements.

articleTitle: Spatio-Temporal Cluster Characterization in a Terahertz Device-to-Device MIMO Channel
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we present a spatio-temporal cluster-based statistical propagation model for a Terahertz (THz) device-to-device (D2D) Multiple-Input-Multiple-Output (MIMO) channel. The model was developed using data obtained from THz (300 - 312 GHz) 4 × 4 MIMO measurements conducted in an obstructed Line-of-Sight (OLOS) scenario in a data center environment. Spatio-temporal inter- and intracluster parameters (e.g. angle-of-arrival, time-of-arrival) were extracted with the former showing dependency and the latter showing independence. A model was developed and validated through comparison of the rms delay spread of the simulated model and the measured data.

articleTitle: A Broadband Metasurface Antenna Based on Characteristic Mode Analysis with Quasi-Minkowski Fractals
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A broadband metasurface antenna based on CMA with quasi-Minkowski fractals structure is proposed. The 2nd-order quasi-Minkowski fractal is used to reduce the antenna size. A slot-coupled feeding structure is employed to maintain the radiation pattern of the metasurface which comprises a 3-2-3 array of hexagon patch cells. The CMA method is used to analyze and guide the minimization of the metasurface cells. The simulated results validate that the proposed antenna covers the working frequency band of 6.68 ~ 8.63 GHz (|<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S$</tex><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>| < −10 dB) with a bandwidth of 25.5%. It has a gain of 6.3 ~ 7.2 dBi and can be applied in C-band satellite communication and radar systems.

articleTitle: Experiences from Teaching a Short-Term Course on Bioelectromagnetics
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper discusses the key experiences from delivering a short-term course on bioelectromagnetics at the SSN College of Engineering in India. The registered students were third and fourth-year undergraduates from the chemical engineering and electrical engineering programs. The overall feedback is highly positive, while a chemical engineering student's comments illuminate the potential of bio-electromagnetics to ignite interest in non-electrical engineering students as well. Comparisons with experiences from an earlier, online offering of the course are also reported. Future directions are, finally, discussed in terms of leveraging experiences from other bio-electromagnetics courses taught at other institutions.

articleTitle: A Tunable Glass-based Dual-functional Metasurface Design
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A novel tunable dual-functional metasurface based on glass is designed. This design can be widely implemented on transparent glass substrate for daily use. It can be switched between two status, including fully reflection and fully transmission, by tuning the bias voltage of positive-intrinsic-negative (PIN) diodes. The proposed design can cover a wide frequency band of over 400 MHz bandwidth centered at 2.6 GHz. The maximum transmittivity and reflectivity in two status can reach up to 98.7% and 97.5% respectively, showing its great potential in the application on shielding electromagnetic wave in the sixthgeneration (6G) wireless networks.

articleTitle: Balanis' Early Career at NASA Langley Research Center
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Professor Balanis started his professional career at NASA Langley Research Center in Hampton, Virginia after graduating from Virginia Tech in 1964. During this time, he worked in the areas of Microwaves and Antennas as well as developed an interest in teaching. During his tenure at NASA, Prof. Balanis also completed his M.S. and Ph.D. degrees. While Prof. Balanis moved on to teaching at West Virginia University and then eventually to Arizona State University, he always maintained connection to NASA Langley where it all started with continued collaboration to advance the antenna technology.

articleTitle: High Gain Wide Bandwidth 2D LWA with New Feeding for Radial Waveguide at Millimeter-Wave
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: New feeding for radial waveguide is proposed. The feeding maintains the propagation of Quasi-TEM mode inside the guide which is leaked through narrow slots at the top plate of the guide, resulting in frequency dependent high gain leaky-wave radiation. The antenna provides 22 dBi realized gain at 32.5 GHz with high radiation efficiency (89<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>) and has 33% impedance bandwidth. The new feeding allows for size reduction, easier fabrication, feeding network design, and better integration of the antenna with other systems.

articleTitle: Recent Advances on Static Passive EMSs for Fixed Wireless Access Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper explores the potential of passive, flat-patterned electromagnetic skins (EMSs) in enhancing point-to-point fixed wireless access links beyond the asymptotic free-space total path attenuation (TPA) limit. The work delves into the design methodologies, technological challenges, and potential applications of these proposed solutions. Additionally, selected proof-of-concept results to highlight the practical feasibility of the suggested solution strategy in real-world scenarios are discussed. The features and potentialities of the resulting architectural solution in non line-of-sight fixed wireless access scenarios are addressed.

articleTitle: Waveform-selective Huygens Metasurfaces for Antenna Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Huygens metasurfaces (HMS) are usually made of unit-cells composed of a cascaded configuration of impedance sheets returning a specific phase insertion for a fixed frequency. Here, we discuss the design of self-reconfigurable HMS exhibiting two different phase-gradients depending not only on the frequency of the impinging field but also on its temporal waveform. We show that the reconfigurability of the cells can be obtained by modifying the impedance sheet of just one layer, greatly simplifying the complexity of the fabrication process. As a case study, the HMS is designed to coat a conventional dipole antenna and introduce beamforming functionalities in the presence of a signal characterized by a very short pulse width, whilst the original omnidirectional pattern of the antenna is exhibited for a continuous waveform.

articleTitle: Integrated Antenna Module for Advanced Vehicle Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes the implementation of an automotive antenna system for vehicle communication based on a highly integrated antenna module. The proposed module is composed of specific antennas, each corresponding to either cellular or connectivity communication. This module is fully integrated with the modem and radio-frequency-integrated-circuit (RFIC), eliminating the need for RF cables. The entire vehicle communication system guarantees specific antenna beam-patterns for each of their respective applications, allowing for targeted direction. The measurement results for each antenna suggest that the proposed integrated system design meets the specific requirements of each application. Therefore, this paper presents an advanced, cost-effective solution for an integrated vehicle communication module that enhances performance using specific antennas.

articleTitle: Wave-Controlled RIS as Reconfigurable Reflective Lens for Focusing in the Fresnel Zone
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: We propose a reconfigurable metasurface-based lens that employs a novel method for biasing the varactors and reflecting incident rays at a desired focal point. The reconfig-urable intelligent surface (RIS) uses resonant standing waves on a biasing transmission line (TL) below the RF reflective surface. This novel biasing technique eliminates the need for separate external bias for each RIS element. We use an analytical RIS model to obtain the electric field distribution at the focal plane.

articleTitle: An Improved Adaptive Mesh Refinement Method Based on Boundary Condition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: For a posteriori error (PE) estimates obtained from single tetrahedron, the continuity between this tetrahedron and adjacent elements is ignored. This paper presents an adaptive mesh refinement method which improves the PE according to the boundary conditions. In this method, an error denoting the discontinuity of the finite element (FE) solution across the internal triangular faces is obtained and then, allocate the error on face to the original PE on both sides. At the same time, the scaling factor on vertices for mesh refinement is connected with the error on faces. Therefore, the PE will be more valid physically. Numerical results are presented and compared with original method to illustrate the performance of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Inverse-Designed Metal-type Antenna Superstrate for Shaped-Beam Radiation Pattern
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: An inverse-design method for metal-type antenna superstrate to get the desired shaped-beam radiation pattern is investigated by using the contrast source inversion method. The proposed inverse design method can avoid the shortcomings of the traditional forward-design methods in which antenna structure depends on a prior knowledge. Meanwhile, its feature of not relying on engineers' experience can greatly reduce the time cost in the design. Final results show that the proposed method has a good application prospect in antenna field.

articleTitle: A Tree-Based Scheme for the Numerically Stable Compression of Integral Equations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: When compressing the electric field integral equation with the adaptive cross approximation or related fast solvers, the resulting matrix can often be affected by numerical cancellations at low frequency in the computation of the scalar potential. This work theoretically studies the source of this instability and proposes a solution based on a tree scheme. Numerical results corroborate and confirm the theory and show the efficacy of the proposed solution.

articleTitle: Combining UHF Waves and Optical Waves in Tracking Systems for Safety Applications: State-of-the-Art Literature Survey
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A literature survey on monitoring and tracking systems that combine RFID and CV technologies is presented, in view of an ad-hoc development and implementation of a prototype of the AISAFETY Project: “Integrated smart system based on artificial intelligence for the management of operator safety in production processes”.

articleTitle: Radio Design Criteria in the Early XX Century: The Dawn of the Global Communication Era
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The early years of the XX century witnessed a series of milestone achievements in long-range wireless communications that paved the way for the activation of the first intercontinental radiotelegraphic commercial service in 1907, a fundamental step toward the development of the modern global radio communication network. This work illustrates the state-of-the-art in radio technology at that time and the relevant design criteria.

articleTitle: Preconditioning of EFIE Matrices when Using Additive High-Order Singular Bases
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Integral equations modeling complex electromagnetic structures are solved numerically using the method of moments and iterative solvers whenever the system matrix is large. Fast-solvers can be used if the system matrix is well conditioned, which only happens by using appropriate formulations, or by re-conditioning the system of equations with algebraic preconditioners. In the case of surface integral equations, well-established techniques exist if the expansion functions are low-order vector polynomials, for example RWG functions. This paper instead considers surface integral equations discretized by additive bases formed by high-order polynomials and singular functions, showing that the electric field integral equation (EFIE) can be successfully solved by using a special general-purpose algebraic preconditioner.

articleTitle: Elliptical Loaded Substrate Integrated Waveguide Thick H-Plane Horn Antenna in the K Band
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This exploratory study centers on the design, fabrication, and measurement of an elliptically loaded Substrate Integrated Waveguide (SIW) H-plane sectoral horn antenna tailored for the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{K}$</tex> radiofrequency band. The results from the simulation align well with those obtained from the measurements. Multiband operation is demonstrated with a stable peak gain observed from 20 GHz to 24 GHz.

articleTitle: W-Band Microstrip Comb-Line Antenna with Shaped Pattern at Low Cost
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Although various microstrip comb-line antennas (CLAs) have been proposed, a CLA with shaped pattern has not been reported. In this work, we investigate the reasons why shaped patterns are difficult to realize for conventional CLAs and succeed in designing a CLA with cosecant squared (CSC<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) shaped pattern as a proof of concept. Additionally, it is demonstrated that strong standing waves can persist in the feedline of a CLA even though the impedance matching at its input port is good. Hence, reflection cancelling slits (RCSs) are employed to suppress the reflected waves. To confirm this concept, a microstrip CLA with 16 elements for millimeter-wave (mm-Wave) radars is designed, fabricated, and measured. Its patterns agree well with the objective CSC<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> curve across 79 GHz - 81 GHz.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Shared Aperture Antenna with a Large Operation Frequency Ratio for 5G Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A shared aperture antenna is presented, which covers two widely separated frequency bands, Sub-6GHz and millimeter-wave (Sub-6GHz/mmWave), such as 3.5 and 28GHz. The overall antenna consists of a patch antenna that radiates at 3.5GHz, whereas the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1\times 4$</tex> CDRA (Circular Dielectric Resonator Antenna) array embedded in SIW (Substrate Integrated Wave-guide) radiates at the center frequency of 28GHz. To reduce the aperture antenna area, we use the stack layer technique. The overall dimension of the antenna is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.73\times 0.34\times 0.027\lambda_{L}^{3}$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda_{L}$</tex> is the low-frequency wavelength. The antenna performance achieves a bandwidth of 9.7%/9.46%, a maximum gain of 5.25dBi/10.5dBi, and an efficiency of 90.9%/88%.

articleTitle: Systematic Approach to Analyze the Surface Wave Propagation in Absorbing Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A systematic approach is presented to compute the surface wave propagation constant (SW-PC) in absorbing structure. This approach allows an accurate and efficient numerical analysis since it utilizes equivalent circuit theory to explain the effect of each element of the structure. Hence, the tuning and attenuating of SW-PC helps in controlling the surface electromagnetic (EM) wave coupling in the microwave devices.

articleTitle: A Frequency Perturbation Method for Cancelling the Antenna Coupling in a Simultaneous Transmitting and Receiving System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper aims to solve the problem of coupling signals due to insufficient isolation between the Tx and Rx antennas in simultaneous transmitting and receiving wireless relay system. First, the coupling signal is calibrated by introducing a frequency offset to the received signal. Then, the digital attenuators and phase shifters are used to generate the signal with equal amplitude but opposite phase to the coupling signals. Finally, the coupling signals are canceled by the generated signal, which can improve the antenna isolation.

Author Keywords: simultaneous transmitting and receiving (STAR) wireless system

articleTitle: CPW Based Reflectionless Notch Filter Using Graphene Pads
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a reflectionless notch filter designed using a CPW stub-based transmission line operating at 3 GHz. The transmission coefficient <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{S}_{21})$</tex> of the notch filter is around -35 dB at this frequency. The reflection coefficients <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{s}_{11}$</tex> and S22 at the “notch” frequency are reduced to less than 10 dB by biasing the circuit using graphene pads. DC current varying from 0 to 200 mA is given as bias to the graphene pads. Measured results showing the operation of circuit are presented.

articleTitle: Generation of Backscattering Time-Series by Ocean Surface Using Multi-Level Fast IPO
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Electromagnetic scattering computation from the sea surface is pivotal for maritime surveillance and navigational safety. This study employs the high-frequency approximation method known as Iterative Physical Optics (IPO), is utilized to predict the scattering attributes of the sea surface, especially those with substantial electrical sizes and textured complexities. The fast IPO methodology introduced here significantly streamlines computational efforts in expansive environments by implementing the Fast far-field approximation, thus elevating the efficiency of the analysis. Modeling of the sea surface was adeptly performed using the Fung & Lee spectrum, with the dynamic normalized Radar Cross Section of the sea surface being thoroughly analyzed. Additionally, this paper improves the IPO preprocessing by incorporating GPU acceleration techniques with Nvidia's OptiX, and such enhancements are anticipated to contribute to the performance improvement of maritime surveillance and defense systems.

articleTitle: Ultra Wide Band (UWB) Character of Wide Planar Monopoles and Their Potential Applications in Transparent Antenna Designs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a concise yet reasonably thorough analysis on the nature of the broad band behavior of a wide planar monopole antenna. Application notes on extending such a geometry to optically transparent antennas are outlined.

articleTitle: Gain Enhancement of Loop Antenna Arrays Proximity Coupled to a Coplanar Feedline
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Three series-fed array antennas are designed for a broadside beam of circular polarization. First, using the moment method, we present the radiation characteristics of a reference antenna whose feedline is excited at one end. Next, a present antenna whose feedline is excited at the center is studied to enhance the gain. It is found that the antenna exhibits a gain enhancement of 1.1 dB compared with that of the reference antenna. Last, a balanced feed at the feedline center is transformed into an unbalanced one to simplify the feed system without balun circuit design.

articleTitle: Multi-Band MIMO Antenna System with Mutual Coupling Reduction via Ring SRR Metasurface Wall
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This research uses circular SRR metasurface (MS) walls to improve mutual coupling in a multiple input multiple output (MIMO) antenna system. The array of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{two} \times \mathbf{two}$</tex> rectangular patches is positioned between the MS structure and the horizontal plane in a normal orientation. The EM simulator is utilized to test the recommended array. The impact of using the meta-surface wall is demonstrated by the result metrics. Mutual coupling is decreased by applying the recommended MS barriers.

articleTitle: The Design of a Simple Folded IFA for Wi-Fi 7 Laptop Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a small size laptop antenna for Wi-Fi 7 operations in the 2.4 GHz (2400–2484 MHz), 5 GHz (5150–5875 MHz), and 6 GHz (5925–7125 MHz) frequency bands. The proposed folded-IFA has a size of 28×4 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and it is mounted on a system ground of 300× 200 × 0.4 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, Due to its folded structure, the proposed IFA can excite three resonant modes (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f_{1}, f_{2}$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f_{3}$</tex>) to ensure complete coverage of the Wi-Fi 7 operational bands. Therefore, it is suitable for laptops that require thin frames or narrow bezels.

articleTitle: Augmenting the Efficiency Bandwidth Product of Electrically Small Antennas Using Direct Antenna Phase Modulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The effectiveness of Electrical Small Antennas (ESAs) in high bandwidth communications is constrained by the quality factor, as specified by Chu's Limit. There is growing need for ESA integration into cellular, biomedical implants, unmanned aerial vehicles, and IoT devices where a larger antenna would be impractical. In this work we propose a capacitively loaded loop antenna that can radiate high-bandwidth signals using a time-varying approach through Direct Antenna Modulation (DAM). The capacitively loaded loop antenna (CLLA) consists of an electrically small loop antenna design that is paired with a high figure of merit (FoM) transistors in a dual-pole dual-throw switch configuration. The antenna utilizes this switch to perform DAM, allowing high-bandwidth phase modulated signals to be radiated on a platform that would be typically constrained its size to a high radiation quality factor. In contrast to a time-invariant capacitively loaded loop antenna of the same form factor, the DAM antenna exhibits a considerably enhanced efficiency-bandwidth product.

articleTitle: Analysis of Total Ionizing Dose Effects in MOSFET with the Spectral-Element Time-Domain Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In order to analyze total ionizing dose (TID) effects in MOSFET devices, an accurate numerical method is presented in this paper. The physical model is constructed based on the drift-diffusion equation and discretized using the spectral-element time-domain (SETD) method. Through transient numerical simulations, the laws of motion with different particles inside semiconductor device can be obtained, including electrons, holes, protons, and hydrogen. Then we compare the changes in electrical characteristics and reveal the degradation caused by interface traps <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\boldsymbol{N}_{\boldsymbol{it}})$</tex>, such as the changing of the threshold voltage and the increasing of the drain current. The example of NMOS transistor validate the accuracy of this method compared to commercial software, we believe this method can provide an effective tool for guiding the radiation resistance design.

articleTitle: Design of Crescent Slot Octagonal (CSO) Dual band Integrated Bluetooth UWB Antenna for IoT Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A new type of antenna for Bluetooth and UWB applications has been proposed and studied in this paper. The antenna is designed to be compact and printed, with an octagonal shape and a crescent slot etched into the radiating patch. On the other side of the substrate, a Modified Ground Plane (MGP) is used to achieve the desired dual-band characteristics with the required bandwidth. The basic octagonal antenna operates over the UWB frequency band, while the crescent slot on the radiating patch resonates over the Bluetooth frequency band. The proposed antenna has been fabricated on an FR-4 substrate with dimensions of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$38\times 30\text{mm}^{2}$</tex>, with a feed by a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$50\Omega$</tex> microstrip line. The measured <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{S}_{11}$</tex> is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\leq-10\ \text{dB}$</tex> over 2.35-2.5 GHz and 3.1-12.5 GHz. The simulated and measured results of the proposed antenna are in good agreement, making it suitable for IoT applications.

articleTitle: Phase Synchronization in Triangular Ray Tube Tracing (TRTT)
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The electromagnetic scattering analysis is always complex and has great importance in civil and military fields. The common aim of all approaches proposed for the solution of scattering problems is to obtain accurate scattering values with small computational burden. In this study, the radar cross-section (RCS) values of objects whose dimensions are large compared to the wavelength are calculated with the Triangular Ray Tube Tracing (TRTT) method, which is a high-frequency technique. In scattering analyses, multiple bounces and shadowing are taken into account depending on the geometry of the target object. In multiple bounces, the phase synchronization that occurs during ray tube tracing should be handled carefully. In this study, the phase synchronization between the rays in multiple bounces is explained in detail.

articleTitle: A Frequency Selective Wi-Fi Blocking Wallpaper: Real-World Measurements and Design Improvements
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: We present the real-world measurements of a frequency selective Wi-Fi blocking wallpaper made by screen printing and curing conductive ink on a commercial wallpaper substrate. Based on the results of the real-world measurements, the FSS design is modified in order to provide a higher bandwidth in the 5G Wi-Fi band, which will enable a more consistent blocking of the Wi-Fi signal over both bands.

articleTitle: Reflection Characteristic Measurement of Indoor Walls in the 150 GHz Band
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Indoor high-speed wireless LANs are considered as a typical use case for communication systems using the sub-THz band, and MIMO transmission using indoor reflected waves is promising to achieve high-speed transmission. Therefore, it is an important issue to clarify the channel response characteristics of reflected waves in the communication band. In this report, we measured the frequency response of reflected waves in the 150 GHz band with varying polarization and incident angle on metal and plaster walls, which are typical indoor wall surfaces. As a result, it was confirmed that the variation of reflected power within the band increases as the reflected power decreases.

articleTitle: Non-Uniform Planar MIMO Array Optimization Criterion in Wavenumber Domain for Aliasing-Free Wideband Near-Field 3D Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Microwave/millimeter-wave imaging is widely desired in various applications, including remote sensing, integrated sensing and communications, security, and biomedical imaging. Sparse MIMO arrays, while cost-effective, often face aliasing artifacts due to spectral distortion in non-uniform sampling. This paper introduces an innovative optimization criterion for non-uniform planar MIMO arrays in the wavenumber domain, aiming at aliasing-free wideband near-field 3D imaging. We propose the wavenumber-range spectrum (WS) of the normal plane wave as a tool to evaluate spectral distortion in near-field non-uniform sampling. This approach utilizes the non-uniform-fast-Fourier-transform-based MIMO range migration algorithm with a modified non-uniform sampling function. Simulations show that the optimized array, with maximum peak sidelobe ratio (PSLR) in the WS, consistently maintains low sidelobe levels (SLL) in the point spread function (PSF) for central and edge targets, and thus achieves aliasing-free imaging.

articleTitle: An 8-Element MIMO Antenna Decoupled by Common and Differential Modes Cancellation for 5G Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper proposed a novel eight-element multi-input multi-output (MIMO) antenna for 5G application based on a mode cancellation method (MCM), which is composed of four identical folded antenna pairs. After introducing the stub and strips to adjust the CM and DM impedance independently to decouple. Simulated and measured results show that even if the antennas are very close to each other, they can all achieve good impedance matching and isolation larger than 10dB from 3.3 to 3.6 GHz (C-Band) and can reach 40dB at the decoupling frequency in eight-element antenna system. Also, simulated results show that the efficiency is over 74%, and ECC is less than 0.05.

articleTitle: Simultaneous Perfect Anomalous Reflection and Angle-of-Arrival Sensing Using Patch Arrays
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A novel optimization-based method tailored for the evolution of communication networks is presented, aimed at achieving a perfect power efficiency while accurately determining the angle of arrival of user-generated waves. Our approach involves optimizing aperiodic loaded structures, eliminating the constraints of electromagnetic periodicity while maintaining a fixed half-wavelength spacing. The proposed configuration employs practical square patches, each loaded with passive tunable elements. These load values can be dynamically adjusted, enabling a continuous scanning capability to capture user signals arriving from unknown angles.

articleTitle: Model-Based Design for Direction Finding with Phase Comparison
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Direction-finding is used in many applications to locate the source of emissions of RF and microwave signals. Direction-finding can be done using analog or digital techniques. The analog implementation using phase comparison is discussed in this paper. The system simulation for this direction-finding technique is also shown in this paper using the RF Blockset model. The antenna is integrated with the RF channel to simulate an entire system. Phase comparison can be achieved using many different antenna configurations and array architectures. This paper uses a linear array of spiral antennas at the receiver. The phase difference between the antennas is used to detect the angle of arrival (ADA). The model offers rapid prototyping for the antenna and RF components, and different scenarios can be easily simulated. The model also considers impedance mismatches between the blocks, and the power transmitted and received can be accurately modelled.

articleTitle: Ultra Wideband Antenna Elements on Non-Uniform Spaced Arrays
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In the design of wideband arrays, the bandwidth is generally determined by the separation between elements; the small separations can increase mutual coupling, and large separations can produce grating lobes. Non-uniform arrays can increase array bandwidth by removing the periodicity in the array, but most techniques are defined using point sources as the radiating element, and the effect of having real elements with frequency dependent impedance and radiation patterns is not considered. This work applied the non-uniform spaced technique developed by Harington to reduce sidelobe levels to an eight-element linear array of Archimedean spirals. It was found that the sidelobe reduction was achieved through the entire operational bandwidth with minimal impact to the elements VSWR.

articleTitle: Towards Energy-Efficient Beamforming for Terrestrial and Non-Terrestrial Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The conventional beamforming used for either terrestrial or non-terrestrial communication is usually based on the phase control of antenna elements in arrays, which typically results in a beam with a natural rolling pattern. The amplitude control is often used to achieve low side lobe levels (SLLs), regarded as sacrificing power or aperture efficiency. In recent research, it has been found that the flat-topped beam can be analytically synthesized through controlling both the phase and amplitude of array elements. In this conference paper, a numerical analysis is carried out to show that the flat-topped beamforming possesses the advantages of full-angle coverage with a small number of beams and small ripples during beam scanning. Hence, this type of beamforming can afford energy/power-efficient coverage for both terrestrial of non-terrestrial networks.

articleTitle: Gain and Impedance Bandwidth Enhancement of a Loop Antenna for X-Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents the new design for a rectangular loop antenna (RLA) with enhanced impedance bandwidth and realized gain. The newly proposed RLA includes a truncated rectangular loop and two parasitic elements positioned on either side of the loop, strategically employed to enhance bandwidth. Additionally, to concentrate radiated power, a metallic sheet is positioned beneath the antenna at a distance of 3.35 mm. Through simulations, the study illustrates that the suggested design achieves a notable 60% improvement in bandwidth and a gain enhancement of approximately 6.6 dBi. The antenna operates within the frequency range of 10.2 GHz to 11.7 GHz, achieving a maximum gain of 11 dBi at a resonance frequency of 11 GHz. Given its performance in the X-band frequency range, the proposed RLA emerges as a promising candidate for applications such as synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imaging.

articleTitle: Frequency-Modulated Continuous Wave Computational Imaging : Preliminary Results
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This study introduces an innovative method that associates analog multiplexing techniques with Frequency-Modulated Continuous-Wave architecture in the W-band. An array of 15 slot antennas is addressed by a leaky reverberant cavity associated with off-the-shelf transmission and reception chains, enabling two-dimensional imaging from a single, low-frequency beat signal. By solving inverse problems adapted to this new architecture, we convert a 10 MHz signal into an image captured by waves radiated in the 92–96 GHz band.

articleTitle: An Efficient Approach to Predicting Performance Metrics of Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper investigates the use of artificial intelligence in predicting the performance of a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS). For understanding the effectiveness of the RIS configuration, researchers compute the phase information according to formulas or simulation. However, with the increasing needs in flexibility, computational complexity needs to be reduced as low as possible. In this paper, we introduce a more efficient method, in which a convolution neural network (CNN) has been implemented, to work with different data conversion methods to find a better representation method for a multi-regression mission. The criteria of regression include the direction of arrival, maximum radiation angle, half power beam width, directivity, and side lobe level. On the RIS with 1225 unit cells, the CNN method can obtain accurate results faster than the formula with about a 85% reduction.

articleTitle: Point-Dense Measurement of 802.11g Radio Intensity Using Commercial Off-the-Shelf Hardware and Software-Defined Radio with Optical Marker-Based Positioning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents an evaluation of the Received Signal Strength Indicator (RSSI) of 802.11g, measured using a Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) WLAN adapter, and the Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR), measured using Software-Defined Radio (SDR) from an Access Point (AP) at 200 points in a given indoor environment. The study uses a custom Raspberry Pi 4-based system with ArUco markers for positioning, designed for embedding on mobile platforms like drones or robots to optimize the measurement process. The result is a point-dense radio signal strength heat map that may be used in communications infrastructure planning.

articleTitle: A Novel Single-Layer Quasi-Elliptic Frequency-Selective Surface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A novel design of frequency-selective surface (FSS) generating a quasi-elliptic frequency response is proposed in the paper. Each unit cell of FSS comprises a centered rectangular aperture with three closely spaced equal-height posts alternatively installed in the aperture center along its broad walls. Numerical and measured data are presented for X-band FSS providing a narrowband transmission of linearly polarized wave. In particular, the measured bandwidth of 5% centered at 8.16 GHz with transmission zeros separation ratio of 1.3 is achieved for the 45-degree incidence.

articleTitle: Low Profile Single/Two-Element Dual-Band Array Antenna for 5th Generation Mobile Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a compact microstrip patch antenna designed for 5G millimeter wave (mmWave) mobile communications. The planar antenna offers two configurations: a single-element design and a dual-band two-element array. The single-element configuration resonates at 38.24 GHz with a bandwidth of 2.89 GHz, while the two-element array antenna demonstrates dual-band resonance at 34.64 GHz and 40.64 GHz, with respective bandwidths of 1.24 GHz and 5.53 GHz. Both configurations maintain satisfactory VSWR range (VSWR < 2) across their operating bands. Each one constructed on a Rogers RT 5580 substrate (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{tan}\ \boldsymbol{\delta}=\mathbf{0.0009}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{\varepsilon}_{\mathbf{r}}=\mathbf{2.2}$</tex>). The two-element array, within its operating band (37.46 GHz - 42.99 GHz), demonstrates a peak efficiency of 82% and a significant gain of 8.78 dBi. Another band of that array, which ranges from 34.23 to 35.47 GHz, has a radiation efficiency of 61% and a gain of 4.14 dBi at its resonance frequency of 34.64 GHz. In comparison, the single-element antenna delivers efficiency ranging from 53% to 63% and gain varying from 3.8 dBi to 4.3 dBi.

articleTitle: Scattering Effects of Surface Discontinuities by Simulated Diagnostic Radar Images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The availability of reliable 3D full-wave numerical techniques allows the RCS engineer to implement high-fidelity simulations of Inverse Synthetic Aperture Radar (ISAR) acquisitions of complex constructive details also including radar absorbing treatments, producing diagnostic radar images in excellent agreement with measurement results. The aim of this paper is to review this capability as part of an RCS design process, showing simple representative examples including complex surface scattering mechanisms, and reporting simulation to measurement comparisons on ISAR images.

articleTitle: Wideband Polarization Insensitive Unit Cell for Binary Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A novel design of a circularly symmetric unit cell for binary reconfigurable intelligent surfaces is presented. The cell achieves a large relative bandwidth of 35% at 7 GHz. Stability in the operation bandwidth with respect to the wave polarization is perfectly achieved up to 20° incidence angle. The preceding figures are obtained through full wave simulations of the proposed cell using Floquet ports in commercially available electromagnetic simulation suite.

articleTitle: An Integrated OAM Antenna at Sub-THz Frequencies using a Leaky Wave Ring Resonator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A Leaky Wave Ring Resonator (LWRR) is designed and simulated using a coaxial transmission line with periodic slots. The device is designed specifically for the generation of Orbital Angular Momentum (OAM) modes on-chip and at sub-THz frequencies. A realistic stack-up is used, mimicking a 22nm FinFET process. This antenna is simulated to show three different OAM modes at 348GHz (l = +1, -1,±1). Each mode can be stimulated without the need for continuous phase control at the input (only +90°,-90°, or 0° is needed). The device is designed for compactness and simplicity of control, and it shows a maximum efficiency of 24%, which is acceptable for leaky wave antennas at sub-THz frequencies.

articleTitle: Coil Orientation Impact on Efficiency in Double-Sided WPT with Magnetic Field Coupling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The coils used in magnetic field-coupled wireless power transfer (WPT) exhibit a higher absolute coupling coefficient when the transmission and reception directions are reversed. In contrast, magnetic field-coupled WPT, which generates a symmetrical magnetic field on both sides of the transmitting coil, enables simultaneous power delivery to coils on both sides. This study investigated the influence of coil orientation in the case of simultaneous power delivery on both sides.
