Despite that both dual-received coils were coupled each other, the findings indicate that dual-side power delivery case with reversed coil orientation enhances coupling similar to single-side power delivery case. This results in an increase in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$kQ$</tex> product and improved wireless power transmission efficiency. We loaded the coil with inductance to resonate at the desired frequency location where the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$kQ$</tex> product is maximized. In this case as well, electromagnetic field analysis revealed that reversed-phase orientation leads to higher wireless power efficiency compared to in-phase orientation.

articleTitle: A Six-port Decoupled Antenna Using a Dielectric Decoupler for Compact MIMO Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A dielectric decoupler is employed in a six-port multi-input-multi-output (MIMO) antenna to increase the port isolations. This multiple-port decoupled antenna consists of six radiators and a hollow dielectric decoupler. By using this decoupler, a weak-field region can be obtained. When a radiator is placed at the weak-field region, a high isolation of more than 20 dB is found between the radiator and other radiators. These radiators are operated at 3.5 GHz with a bandwidth of 4.6%. Each port has quasi-boresight radiation patterns when other ports are terminated by a matched load.

articleTitle: Relative Array Element Axial Rotation for Power Pattern Synthesis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: An array pattern synthesis is presented using element axial rotation that fully replaces the element feeding phase for a beam shape with fixed characteristics. The antenna element is a circularly polarized (CP) circular microstrip antenna (CMSA) whose phase pattern follows a first-order orbital angular momentum (OAM) wave. Cosecant fourth and second power patterns are synthesized using a 13 ×2 rectangular array for different communication scenarios. Optimal rotation angles are obtained using a built-in MATLAB-based particle swarm optimization (PSO) function to fit the desired masks.

articleTitle: Attention U-Net for Binary Mask Generation in Medical Microwave Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Conventional microwave imaging as an inverse problem is ill-posed, non-linear, and requires large computational resources. To reduce that ill-posedness, an Attention U-Net model is proposed to generate a binary mask of the dielectric properties of the domain. The generated binary mask can be used to extract tissue regions, enabling the post-processing algorithms to focus on the target. In this work, the training images along with the ground truth labels are generated after a pre-processing of substantial simulation data. The ground truth labels are binarized before training. The testing results of the neural network indicate more than 82%, 70%, and 74% accuracy in the pixel properties estimation, Dice coefficient, and the mean intersection of the union. Those results indicate the potential of the proposed approach in medical microwave imaging.

articleTitle: In-Band Dual-Circularly Polarized Single-Element Patch with Pattern Symmetry by Multi-Port Feeding
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper reports on an approach to design an S-band dual-circularly polarized (DCP) single-element patch while exploiting a compact and multi-port feeding arrangement. In particular, the design features an eight-port feeding system by slot meandering and 50–Ω feeding with sequential phase excitation at the patch diagonals and edges, and this can offer DCP operation with high polarization purity. By proper design and optimization of the eight meandered slots, the peak gain of the circularly polarized (CP) states can be at the same frequency for in-band radiation. The narrow-band nature of this structure offers spectral efficiency, reduced interference, improved signal quality, and selective filtering. These benefits render the antenna well-suited for various applications, particularly in full-duplex and polarization diversity scenarios. The design can also be employed within an array for DCP beam-steering and where high polarization purity and pattern symmetry is required.

articleTitle: Parametric Matching of Electrically Small Antennas for Broadband and Low Noise Reception
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a novel matching technique that allows receivers with electrically small antenna to achieve low noise performance over a broad bandwidth is proposed. Specifically, we propose to match an electrically small dipole directly to a parametric amplifier, without using any inter-mediate matching network as it will contribute additional noise to the receiver. The parametric amplifier, which is driven by a high frequency pump voltage, exhibits a high impedance, time- varying capacitive load to the dipole. Therefore, the low frequency signal voltage from the dipole is detected at the input of the amplifier, being amplified and up-converted to the proximity of the pump frequency at the output with minimum contamination of noise in the process.

articleTitle: Circuit-Field Equivalence of Quality Factor for Spherical Wire Antennas with Material Cores
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: It has been shown that the quality factor of air-core spherical wire antennas carrying electric currents as predicted by the equivalent circuits of Chu, and by the field integration of Collin and Rothschild, and later Fante, are in complete agreement. This paper outlines an extension to this proof for the case of material cores, for either electric or magnetic current excitation.

articleTitle: Densely Placed Rectenna Array with Decoupling Slots for Far-Field Wireless Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a high-isolated antenna array through the use of decoupling to achieve miniaturization and mitigate polarization mismatch. The proposed antenna array consists of high-isolated antennas using a meander line defected ground structure (DGS) for high-isolation. A proposed high-isolated antenna array enables compact antenna size and the ability to receive a uniform power, regardless of the polarization of the transmitting antenna. For performance validation, the received power was calculated in a polarization mismatch environment. The proposed antenna array with a decoupling slot is matched at 5.8 GHz and can receive a uniform power in a polarization mismatch environment.

articleTitle: Balanis' Honorary Doctorate: The Highest-Level Academic Recognition from the Largest University in Greece
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Dr. Constantine Balanis was awarded from the Aristotle University of Thessaloniki, AUTh, Greece, with the “Honoris Causa Doctorate”. A supporting introductory statement of the principal grounds for the distinction contained: (1) A chronological, narrative account of his life and work. (2) An outline of his most significant achievements. (3) An assessment of his standing on a basis of international comparison and (4) His most coveted contribution in the authorship of his books. The very special presentation of Dr. Balanis and some details about the ceremony will be given.

articleTitle: Single-Mode Dual-Band Dipole Antenna with Consistent Patterns Using Lorentz Metamaterial
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A single-mode dual-band dipole antenna is proposed and implemented by employing Lorentz dispersive metamaterial. The primary concept behind the single-mode dual-band design is ensuring that the dipole has the same electrical size at two distinct frequencies. This is implemented by split-resonance rings (SRRs)-based Lorentz dispersive metamaterial. The SRR is used to offer a higher refractive index at a lower operating frequency and a lower one at a higher operating frequency of the antenna. This results in the same wavelength, or electrical size, at both frequencies. The same electrical size and the operation mode enable the attainment of consistent omnidirectional patterns at two frequencies simultaneously, ensuring excellent impedance matching.

articleTitle: Ultra-Wideband and Wide-Scanning Phased Array Antenna with Lower VSWR Designed by Knowledge-Based Artificial Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, an efficient knowledge-based artificial neural network (ANN) is proposed to optimize a tightly coupled dipole array (TCDA). When dealing with complex TCDA design, the full-wave simulation-based method is trapped in performance degradation. To realize the optimal bandwidth, VSWR, and scanning range, the dozens of physical parameters of TCDA should be optimized simultaneously. In this ANN model, two sub-models are used for the multiparameter modeling of the radiator and the feedline, respectively. The prior knowledge is integrated into the ANN for training time reduction. By applying the proposed model for parameter optimization, the maximum active VSWR of the TCDA is reduced to 2.8, while maintaining an 8.13:1 bandwidth inside the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 60^{\circ}$</tex> scan volume.

articleTitle: Quasioptics in Bioradar With 2×2 Microstrip Patch Arrays and a Dielectric Lens at 5.8 GHz
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The bioradar promises to revolutionize how vital signs are measured via wireless sensing. The chest wall displacement is detected through the micro-Doppler effect, hence, highly directive antennas are used so that the electromagnetic radiation is focused on such restricted area. In this study we propose to focus the energy using a dielectric lens in a quasioptical approach, which can increase the range of the bioradar and reduce the required power while increasing the quality of the signal. To verify its effect, respiratory signal measurements were successfully performed using a 2×2 microstrip patch array, with and without the lens, at 3 m.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Robustness of Compressive Phaseless Imaging Under Noisy Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The aim of this communication is to study the robustness of a novel imaging system based on compressive sensing and amplitude-only measurements, enabling a great reduction in the complexity of the system. In particular, the impact of the noise is studied by means of simulations conducted in Matlab to solve the direct and inverse problems for multiple noise levels. The method has successfully reduced the number of field measurements by 40% compared to uniformly spaced sampling according to Nyquist-Shannon criterion, achieving satisfactory results when SNR is above 20–25 dB.

articleTitle: A Novel Interpretative Model for Characteristic Modes in Frequency-Selective Surface Design
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a theoretical model for simulating the resonance of frequency-selective surfaces (FSSs) using characteristic modes (CMs). The derivation of the proposed model, based on the Poynting theorem, establishes a clear physical relationship between CMs and the resonance performance of FSSs. The model's validity is confirmed through full-wave simulations that focus on the resonance properties of a strip dipole FSS structure. The results clearly demonstrate the accuracy and utility of the proposed model, contributing to the enhancement of FSS design.

articleTitle: An Efficient Dual-Band Inverted-F Antenna Design for Aeronautical Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we present the design of a dual-band Inverted-F Antenna (IFA) specifically tailored for efficient operation in complex environments. The antenna is configured to operate within the aeronautical bands of 980 MHz and 1090 MHz, aligning with radio navigation applications in both Europe and the USA. Notably, the antenna is integrated into Printed Circuit Boards (PCBs) and features two extended arms. The excitation point of the antenna is connected to the chip output pin through a 50 Ohms coplanar waveguide (CPW). The inclusion of the two arms serves the purpose of adjusting the antenna's resonant frequency to align with the specified frequency bands. The concerted efforts in tuning the dimensions and positions of critical components have resulted in a well-matched impedance and elevated radiation efficiency, affirming the antenna's capability to perform effectively in the specified frequency bands within the complex electronic environment.

articleTitle: Polarization Diversity in V2I MIMO-UWB: Channel Characterisation in Outdoor Car Park
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This study involves using a 2×2 MIMO-UWB system deployed in an an outdoor car park for V2I application. Two different antenna arrangements are used to establish the efficacy of using polarization diversity in MIMO-UWB. The channel is characterized in terms of RMS delay spread, coherence bandwidth, and path loss. The results show that polarization diversity provides a small advantage in terms of path loss and marginal improvements in RMS delay spread / coherence bandwidth. The research contributes to the understanding of MIMO-UWB channel characteristics in vehicular environments and also the effect of polarisation diversity in such context.

articleTitle: Improved MM-Wave Rotman Lens Feeding Network for MM-Wave Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Antenna systems require not only high performance but also compactness, especially in millimeter-wave systems. In this work, a new method is presented by the transmission optics to reduce the size of mm-wave Rotman lenses without affecting the key performance of the lenses. The design principle and the improved lens are reported in detail below.

articleTitle: Advances in Microwave Sensors for Non-Destructive Monitoring of Plant Water Status
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents an innovative microwave sensor designed to detect plant water stress and preliminary results from a measurement campaign conducted on olive trees' branches are also reported. The sensor's design, characterized by a dual-layer structure, has been carried out to achieve a good sensitivity obtained through a Q factor optimization procedure. Moreover, this configuration leads to compactness, enabling its use on small branches. The experiment has been conducted on 42 olive plants randomly divided into two water treatments: T0(no-irrigation) and T100 (full-irrigation). In accordance with the theoretical expectations, the study shows an upshift in the sensor resonant frequency as the irrigation water decreased. The obtained experimental results encourage future research and represent a notable advancement towards the non-destructive evaluation of plant water status, thereby improving sustainable agricultural practices.

articleTitle: Driver Distraction Detection using mm- Wave FMCW Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a radar-based in-cabin sensing solution. We introduce a distracted driver detection method that swiftly calibrates to individual users prior to operating a vehicle. Our sensor accurately determines the driver's facing direction and evaluates their level of distraction while driving. Our proposed system overcomes the limitations of image-based sensors without compromising privacy or being affected by varying illumination levels. In contrast to existing systems that necessitate multiple sensors, resulting in a costly technique, our solution requires only a single radar board empowered by AI to monitor distracted drivers.

articleTitle: Unlocking Over-the-Air Efficiency Potential: Epoch-making Approach for Convex Optimization Algorithm-based Microwave Power Transmission Empowered by 256 Elements Antenna Arrays
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper introduces a Microwave Power Transmission (MPT) system that employs a convex optimization technique for efficient power transfer in a large array antenna. The MPT system, operating at 5.64 GHz, has been fabricated. We designed a 16×16 transmit array antenna, a 5×7 receive array antenna, and a microstrip series power divider. Transmitting circuits are integrated with each antenna element for adjusting phase and amplitude. Additionally, convex optimization is employed to transfer power effectively, maximizing Power Transfer Efficiency (PTE). The received RF power is measured for all antenna elements at various distances, achieving a total RF power of approximately 8.1 W received at a distance of 0.7 meters. The results experimentally validate the proposed MPT system, indicating its coverage in the radiative near-field region and emphasizing its potential for high-power charging in wireless applications.

articleTitle: Broadband and High-Gain Dual-Polarized Substrate Integrated Cavity Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this article, a dual-polarized substrate integrated cavity antenna featuring broadband and high-gain characteristics is developed. A square cavity and a pinwheel-shaped patch form a symmetrical radiator. The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$TM_{211}$</tex> mode is utilized within the cavity. Two orthogonal SIWs are introduced to feed the antenna through a cross slot. The simulation results indicate that an overlapped impedance bandwidth of 27.5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> is obtained, with a maximum gain reaching 11.3 dBi for both polarizations. Additionally, the isolation between two input ports is greater than 50 dB. The proposed dual-polarized antenna with its planar structure, broadband, high-gain, and high-isolation characteristics is attractive for millimeter-wave applications.

articleTitle: Diffraction in Presence of Angular Regions Filled by Arbitrary Linear Media
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this work, we present a novel and general spectral theory to handle complex electromagnetic scattering problems. The technique is based on transverse equations for layered planar and angular structures, characteristic Green's function procedure, Wiener-Hopf technique. According to our opinion, for the first time, the proposed mathematical technique extends the possibilities of spectral analysis of EM problems in presence of angular regions filled by complex arbitrary linear media.

articleTitle: L-Band Antenna with Frequency-Dependent Patterns Using an Optimized Parasitic Pixel Layer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A low-cost L-band patch antenna featuring frequency-dependent radiation patterns is presented. The antenna operates within the 1.20-1.38 GHz frequency range. Through optimization of a parasitic pixel layer, the radiating beams can be precisely controlled to exhibit distinct characteristics within the frequency band. Specifically, the designed antenna has a -30° directive beam, a wide-beam, and a +30° directive beam at 1.24, 1.28, and 1.34 GHz, respectively. This versatility enables selection of different radiation beams to achieve desired coverage ranges. The antenna with diverse radiation patterns holds significant promise for applications in wireless communication devices, observation systems, and satellite technology.

articleTitle: A Stable and Symmetric FDTD Subgridding Method with the LTS Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The local time stepping (LTS) technique has been seamlessly integrated into a stable and symmetric finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) subgridding method providing an effective and accurate solution for electromagnetic problems. The proposed approach employing a large time step in the coarse mesh region and a small time step in the subgridding region. Only spatial interpolation is represented at the subgridding boundaries without temporal interpolation. Numerical results validate that the proposed method is stable, accurate and efficient.

articleTitle: Coupling-Based Dual-Band Wireless Power Transfer: Design and Experimental Validation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This study focuses on the practical development of a dual-band wireless power transfer (WPT) system. There are several implantation challenges in scenarios considering biological tissues that are taken into account during the design. The coupled resonators of WPT are separated by a slice of pork meat during experiments. It is worthwhile to note that demonstrating efficiencies of 55% and 30% at two bands, the developed system offers valuable insights into robustness and real-world applicability.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Plane Wave Generator Synthesis with Reduced Number of Controls
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper investigates a technique to synthesize a plane wave generator that requires a limited number of control points for its operation and reconfiguration. The method is based on using concentric rings of equally spaced elements, and each one of the rings shares the same excitation signal (amplitude and phase). Using numerical simulation, we show that achieving excellent polarization purity and easy reconfiguring of the wanted quiet zone is possible.

articleTitle: A Beam-Steerable Reflector Antenna at W-Band Featuring Low Cross Polarization and Gain-Flatness over Scan Range
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Present work reports the development of a W-band reflector antenna with mechanical beam steering capability. The antenna yields 32 dBi of gain at 94 GHz with half-power beamwidth of 3.6° x 3.6° and cross-polar levels lower than 26 dB. The beam steering is realized by mechanically shifting the feed from its focal point to an offset point. Beam steering is measured over ± 25° for mechanical movements of the feed over ± 25 mm about the focal position. Over this angular scan-range achieved gain flatness is better than ± 1dB. Relevant experimental data are presented.

articleTitle: Resonance-Based Microwave Monitoring of Live/Dead Bacteria in a Microfluidic Channel
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this work, we have studied a highly sensitive microwave sensor for the detection of Escherichia coli (E. coli) bacteria at the single-cell level. The proposed system integrates a microwave sensor with a microfluidic channel for bacteria flow control. The microwave sensor is based on a planar microwave annular ring resonator working around 5GHz. Inside the channel, E. coli bacteria have been modeled using dielectric characteristics present in state-of-the-art literature. To enhance field confinement and achieve the highest electric field strength we have introduced two 50um gaps into the resonator. This approach holds great potential for different applications, including food safety control, healthcare diagnosis, and environmental monitoring, where the ability to detect a single E. coli cell is paramount.

articleTitle: Efficient Antenna Design and Simulation for Electrically Large Smart Home Appliances
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Next-generation home appliances will feature Wi-Fi connectivity to assist users in communicating with them remotely for management or telemetry from any location at any time. Therefore, understanding the electromagnetic radiation of antennas integrated within these appliances is an indispensable task. Efficient simulations are critical to shorten the product development process and meet customers' demands in a timely manner. In this paper, we investigate acceleration techniques through hardware for efficient design and simulation of antennas for these next-generation appliances. We specifically study the design and simulation of antennas for integration in refrigerators with electrically large dimensions compared to the antenna.

articleTitle: Toward the Development of a 3D SBP-SAT FDTD Method: Subgridding and Practical Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A three-dimensional subgridding method incorporated the summation-by-parts simultaneous approximation term (SBP-SAT) finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method is proposed to handle complex structure. The proposed subgridding method is the theoretically long-time stable, and can significantly improve the computational efficiency. A human head illuminated by a mobile phone is used to validate its accuracy and efficiency. Results show that the proposed 3D SBP-SAT FDTD method is accurate and efficient to model complex structures.

articleTitle: Full-Metal Tri-Band Shared Aperture Antenna with High Power Capacity and Co-Axial Phase Center
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a tri-band shared aperture antenna is proposed for the multi-band transceiver in high power sensing application. The antenna has three independent band, the low-band and middle-band is from 1–14 GHz and 14–18 GHz. The high-band is located within Ka-band from 30–40 GHz. The tri-band antenna has the co-axial phase center for each band, and the antenna features full-metal structure which enable the high structural strength and power-handling capacity.

articleTitle: Physical Origin of the Effective Parameters at Boundaries in Finite Difference Schemes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Using the Observable form of Maxwell's equations, we reveal that effective parameters at materials boundaries emerge naturally as anisotropic transfer functions. The complexity of the boundary dictates the order of these functions. Employing the residue-pole expansion, we describe the relation between field components as a system of ODEs solvable through the auxiliary differential equation approach. Not only can be used in Finite difference methods, the approach can be also employed to model complex surface structures.

articleTitle: Integrated Circularly Polarized S-Band Antenna for Space IoT Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper discusses the design of a miniature terminal including a Sband antenna for the communication between the terrestrial Internet of Things (loT) to Geostationnary earth Orbit (G EO) satellites. In the first part, we will focus on the GEO constraints and the antenna characteristics that are suitable for this application. Then, a miniature terminal design is simulated and measured to assess the predicted radiation performances. The integrated S-band antenna provide a 3.1dBic LHCP radiation toward zenith with a low coupling with the UHF and GNSS antennas.

articleTitle: A Polarization-Dependent Reflective Color Filter With Grating-Based Sb2S3 Phase-Change Material
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a reflective tunable color filter based on employing an antimony trisulfide <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\text{Sb}_{2}\mathrm{S}_{3})$</tex> grating structure. The design generates two different colors when illuminated by either one of two orthogonally polarized incident lights. Moreover, by adjusting the phase of the material, the resonances can be tuned, enabling the generation of different colors. This design offers a simple platform capable of generating four distinct colors across the visible spectrum.

articleTitle: The RF Impedance Of A Probe In A Plasma With Anisotropic Electron Neutral Collision Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract:
The impedance curve for a dipole antenna immersed in the ionospheric plasma can be used to infer the plasma properties such as electron density <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$n_{e}$</tex> and electron neutral collision frequency <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$
u_{en}$</tex>. In the previous research, it is always assumed the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$
u_{\mathrm{e}n}$</tex> identical around the dipole. However, at upper altitudes above 200 km, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$
u_{en}$</tex> can be anisotropic, with different values parallel and perpendicular to the ambient magnetic field of the earth. Here we propose the idea of two perpendicular dipole antennas to measure the nonuniform parameters due to anisotropic environment. FDTD simulations have been done to demonstrate the impedance magnitude and phase curve for different values of collision frequencies under parallel and perpendicular orientations of a dipole antenna with respect to the ambient magnetic field. The fact that the parallel component of collision frequency is greater or smaller than the perpendicular component can be recognized through the simulations, and hence through complementary measurements made in the ionosphere with two dipoles, one parallel to the earth's magnetic field, and the other perpendicular to it.

articleTitle: Liquid Classification Based on MMW Experiments and Multiclass SVM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: An innovative approach to liquid classification by combining Support Vector Machine (SVM) with cross-validation is proposed. Using a database extended by patch extraction, the model achieves 100% performance in differentiating various liquids in different configurations. The consistency of the results, highlights the robustness of the model, no matter the specific composition of the learning base. This method offers important implications for the safety of public spaces by providing an advanced solution for the accurate detection of liquids. Moreover this promising approach could be extended to more complex scenarios in the future, reinforcing its applicability.

articleTitle: Innovative AI Inversion Methods for Ground Penetrating Radar Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This work introduces an innovative Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven microwave imaging technique for ground penetrating radar (GPR) applications. The complexity of the non-linear/ill-posed subsurface inverse scattering problem (ISP) is addressed within the System-by-Design (SbD) framework by means of suitably chosen and interconnected functional blocks enabling both a smart definition of the solution descriptors and the interactive integration of a global optimizer with a machine learning (ML)-based surrogate model. An illustrative result is shown to assess the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: TARC, Mutual Coupling, Impedance Matching, and Coupling Compensation Matrix in Phased Arrays
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The process of designing antenna arrays is multifaceted and requires careful consideration of various parameters to achieve optimal results. This article comprehensively assesses crucial parameters, such as the Total Active Reflection Coefficient (TARC), Array Coupling Index (ACI), and coupling compensation matrix. By analyzing the intricate interplay between these parameters, this analysis provides a detailed overview that will prove valuable to those involved in designing antenna arrays. The aim is to help designers improve performance, reduce interference, and enhance the overall functionality of the antenna arrays. This article builds on prior research and delves deeper into the complex relationships between these parameters to offer a more nuanced understanding, facilitating effective and efficient array designs.

articleTitle: Reduction of Grating Lobes in Scanning Planar Phased Array Using Reconfigurable Element Spacing Synthesis Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper demonstrates the ability of dual-mode circular microstrip patch antennas to reduce grating lobes in a planar seven-element hexagonal scanning phased array with one-wavelength element spacing by combining a partially radiation-matched center element with the electronic displacement of the phase center in the outer elements in order to break the array's periodicity. This method is shown to reduce the grating lobe levels by at least 8 dB, and up to 16 dB for smaller scan angles.

articleTitle: Distortion of Focal Plane in Flattened 2D Luneburg Lens
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A parametric study of focal plane distortion in 2D flattened Luneburg lenses is studied. Numerical simulations show that directivity is strongly dependent on feed position near the flattened side of the lens. This paper demonstrates that this suboptimal directivity is the consequence of a non-planar focal surface for the Luneburg lens after deformation through transformation optics (QCTO). Simulation results show that the focal point shifts as much as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda/2$</tex> away from the flattened side of the lens and this focal plane distortion varies with lateral movement of the feed point as it moves along the lens.

articleTitle: Multi-Trace Integral Equation For The Vector Potential
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A global multi-trace Poggio-Miller-Chang-Harrington-Wu-Tsai (PMCHWT)-like method for the vector potential in scattering and transmission problems involving multi-domain structures potentially containing multi-material junctions is proposed. The system is discretized with Rao-Wilton-Glisson elements for the vector traces, first order Lagrange elements for the normal trace and piecewise constant functions for the divergence trace. Representative configurations are simulated, which all show a monotonic decrease in the error when the mesh becomes denser.

articleTitle: A Differential SIW Cavity-Backed Slot Antenna for V2V/V2X Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a differential substrate-integrated waveguide (SIW) cavity-backed slot antenna for vehicle-to-vehicle/everything (V2V/V2X) communication. The geometry comprises two rectangular patch antennas each of them being fed using an inset feed, which are connected through a meandered transmission line. This meander line reduces the antenna size as well as improves radiation characteristics. In addition, two U-shaped slots and four shorting pins are implemented to regulate the operating frequency and input impedance. The geometry resonates at 5.87 GHz, intending to operate at the dedicated short-range communication (DSRC) band (5.85-5.925 GHz). The structure has also been fabricated, and 10 dB return loss fractional impedance bandwidth (FIBW) of 2.38%, isolation of more than 7.43 dB, simulated gain of 4.58 dBi, efficiency of 73%, front-to-back ratio of 18.68 dB, and cross-polarization level below -11.4 dB have been achieved at 5.87 GHz.

articleTitle: Bianisotropic Metasurfaces for Bidirectional Arrays with Independent Reflected and Transmitted Beams
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This article proposes a method to engineer omega-type bianisotropic metasurfaces for the design of transmit-reflect-array cells. First, we prove that they can evenly split the power of a normally incident plane wave into a transmitted and a reflected wave and, at the same time, arbitrarily tailor their phase difference. Next, the metasurface constitutive parameters are determined to realize sixteen unit cells achieving a 2-bit phase quantization in transmission and reflection. Preliminary designs with three sheet impedances spaced by two dielectric slabs are analyzed. The numerical results confirm their suitability for the design of arrays with independent control of the propagation directions of the scattered waves.

articleTitle: Preliminary Results on the Feasibility of Flexible Space-Fed Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this communication, the feasibility of space-fed antennas as Transmitarrays or Reflectarrays, where the focusing transmitting/reflecting surface is flexible, is investigated, with the aim of obtaining configurations providing almost the same radiating features even when they are conformal to cylinders with different radii of curvature. Preliminary numerical results on both a reflectarray and a transmitarray confirm the possibility to realize such antennas.

articleTitle: A Fast SBR Method for Multipath Mitigation in Monopulse ToA EW Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Unlike for telecommunications signals, where multipath distortion is critical when the delays of the received signal replicas are comparable to the symbol duration time, in Electronic Warfare (EW) systems based on Time-of-Arrival (ToA) analysis the greatest criticalities occur when these delays are comparable with the duration of the rising front of the RADAR pulse. In this contribution a fast SBR-based method is presented to take into account multipath fading of RADAR signals in Direction-of-Arrival (DoA) calculations.

articleTitle: On the Exploitation of Computational Imaging for the Next Generation Through-the-Wall Sensing Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Compressive Radar Imaging, also called Computational Imaging (CI), has gained increasing importance in the last few years. CI enables to drastically increase the acquisition speed compared to conventional radar imaging systems (e.g., based on Synthetic Aperture Radar, SAR), which need to densely sample the area under investigation. However, the vast majority of research in CI has been devoted to free-space applications. Hence, this contribution highlights the opportunities and challenges of resorting to CI for through-the-wall sensing. In addition, these benefits and difficulties are illustrated by analyzing an application example, where a CI system is employed to detect targets hidden behind two different walls.

articleTitle: Closed-Form Expression for the Directivity of Circumferential Conical Microstrip Antenna Arrays
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper introduces a closed-form expression for the directivity of circumferential conical microstrip antenna arrays, offering a valuable resource for their analysis and design. The proposed expression eliminates the need for time-consuming numerical integration over the radiation sphere. By employing the magnetic current model and orthogonality relations for the associated Legendre functions, we evaluate the power radiated by the array through an analytical formula. Comparisons with directivities obtained using HFSS software demonstrate the accuracy of the derived expression.

articleTitle: Radiation Pattern Improvement of a Wide-Band Planar Monopole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A planar monopole antenna is described with a stabilized radiation pattern within a wide frequency range. The antenna uses a compact monopole structure and an elliptical ring branch in the ground to realize two resonant frequencies and can operate over the frequency range from 6.9 to 9.3 GHz. A semi-circular slot and two rectangular slots are embedded in the ground to adjust the antenna's impedance matching. A pair of slots terminated with radial slot stubs are introduced into the ground plane to improve the E-plane radiation pattern of the monopole antenna in the wide band. A prototype is fabricated and tested, and measured results are in good agreement with the simulated ones.

articleTitle: Research on Transmission Characteristics of Tapered Through Silicon via in Signal Integrity
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, the transmission characteristics of a tapered through silicon via (TSV) is analyzed at 0~100 GHz by using high frequency structure simulator (HFSS). The TSV signal transmission model is established in HFSS and the electrical attribute parameters of different materials, the solution frequency are introduced. The influences of upper radius, height of TSV, insulation layer thickness and silicon conductivity on signal transmission characteristics are analyzed. The results show that the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{S}_{21}$</tex> of TSV will decrease about 0.1 dB when the height increase 20 um and the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{S}_{21}$</tex> difference for each radius increase gradually with the increase of frequency. The increase of insulation layer thickness will reduce the signal transmission loss at 0~100 GHz. In addition, the increase of the conductivity of the silicon substrate in the high frequency band will decrease <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{S}_{21}$</tex> with about 0.8 dB for every 20 S/m increase in conductivity.

articleTitle: Effective Heights for Array Antennas for Radiation and Reception Characterization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Vector effective heights of array antennas are introduced. In addition to the conventional input current reference, the input voltage and the port incident current are considered. An array element effective height represents the far-zone pattern and polarization when only the given element is excited. Via reciprocity, the array's effective heights are related to the receiving properties.

articleTitle: Miniaturized Dual-Polarized 1-Bit Transmitarray Antenna Design Based on Characteristic Modes Theory
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A novel transmitarray (TA) based on a polarization rotator is presented by resorting to the characteristic modes theory (CMT). More in detail, two miniaturized unit cell types that provide a crosspolar transmission coefficient phase difference of 180° have been exploited as 1-bit spatial phase shifter. Their fourfold rotational symmetry allows achieving an azimuth-independent dual-polarized TA response. The TA panel relies only on two metallic layers with a very thin profile.

articleTitle: A Broadband Tunable Active Frequency Selective Surface Absorber
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a novel broadband active frequency selective surface (AFSS) absorber is designed. The AFSS absorber consists of top-layer FSS patches, an intermediate air cavity, and a metal ground. Within the top layer FSS, PIN diodes and resistors are embedded, and the bias network is implemented through vertical metal columns connected with the bottom ground. Furthermore, by varying the voltage across the PIN diodes, the entire structure can achieve continuous tuning between total reflection and absorption levels larger than −10 dB within the adjustable range of 2.1-5.7 GHz.

articleTitle: FEBI Simulation of Thin Wires and Inhomogeneous Penetrable Bodies in Anisotropic Layered Medium
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Electromagnetic simulations in explorations geo-physics can be very challenging, particularly when dealing with multiscale structures involving penetrable objects, metallic wires, and layered media. This problem can be efficiently addressed by extending the finite-element boundary-integral formulation and applying the thin-wire approximation. The use of layered medium Green's function within anisotropic medium further extends the model's capability to simulate the complex interactions within layered geological structures. The accuracy and efficiency of the proposed algorithm is verified through numerical examples.

articleTitle: A Surface Impedance Method with Synchronization in Time for FDTD Simulation of Thin Sheets
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A surface impedance method with synchronization in time for simulating thin conductive sheets is proposed, implemented, and validated. The simulation results showed that the proposed method is stable and accurate.

articleTitle: A Dual-Polarized Sub-THz Huygens' Metasurface with a Two-Layer Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes tilted beam formation using a novel double-layer dual-polarized Huygens' metasurface for the sub-THz frequency band. Firstly, the characteristics of a unit cell for the metasurface are investigated. It is revealed that the proposed unit cell realizes a transmission phase change of more than 360° when a plane wave impinges on the unit cell. Secondly, a square metasurface composed of numerous unit cells is placed above a fed horn antenna to form a high-gain tilted beam at an angle of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\theta=-45^{\circ}$</tex>. The simulation reveals that a tilted beam is formed in the designed direction and a gain of approximately 16 dBi is obtained at a design frequency of 170 GHz. The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\vert \mathrm{S}11\vert$</tex> of the horn antenna is less than -10 dB around the design frequency.

articleTitle: Support Vector Machine for Multiclass Contaminant Classification in Food Products Using Microwave Sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper introduces an innovative approach using microwaves (MW) enhanced with a machine learning (ML) clas- sifier to identify products contaminated with external intrusions and distinguish the contaminant type. The non-invasive MW sensing system is intended to function in real-time in a food production chain. For the multi-class classification, we use the Support Vector Machine (SVM) algorithm, training it on datasets generated from the scattering parameters acquired during the measurements phase. A precision of 100% accuracy is achieved for 200 measurement samples.

articleTitle: Enhanced Bandwidth and Continuous Phase Modulation in a Novel Varactor-Based RIS Design
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: We present a reflective type programmable Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface (RIS) by applying a varactor, which enable us to modify the phase of reflective wave continuously while keep the S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> around −1 dB. The designed RIS works at 8.5 GHz and has four nearly quantized phase that covers a 270-degree range. The constructed array of this RIS has a working bandwidth of 400 MHz, from 8.3 GHz to 8.7 GHz. By program the constructed array, we achieve 45° abnormal reflection and generated vortex beam of mode l = +1. In the future, our work could be applied to more practical situation.

articleTitle: An Electronically Tunable 28-34 GHz 2-D Steerable Leaky Wave Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a 2-D beam steering mm-wave antenna based on the leaky wave configuration is presented. Microstrip leaky wave antennas are known to exhibit beam rotation by changing the frequency. In this work, the microstrip leaky wave antenna is adopted and co-integrated with electronically tunable board components that periodically load the antenna. By independent control of variable capacitors and diodes, single-frequency 2-D beam steering across the bandwidth is achieved. The proposed antenna is fabricated in Rogers printed circuit board technologies and the simulation results exhibit a peak realized gain of 8 dBi, radiation bandwidth of 28–34 GHz, radiation efficiency of more than 80%, and more than 90° and 70° of beam rotation in the ϕ and θ directions.

articleTitle: K-factor analysis based on channel measurements from 24 to 40 GHz in a laboratory scenario
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The K-factor is commonly used to model the small-scale fading. In this contribution, the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex>-factor is analyzed in a laboratory scenario based on wideband channel measurements carried out at millimeter-wave (mmWave) frequencies, covering the 24–40 GHz frequency band. The value of the K-factor is estimated from the method of moments applied directly to the envelope of the measured complex channel transfer function (CTF). The dependence of the K-factor on frequency and distance has been investigated. The results are interesting to understand the selectivity behavior of the wireless channel in this particular scenario at mmWave frequencies.

articleTitle: Location-Dependent Frequency Conversion Based on Space-Time Transformation Optics
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: We propose a technique to generate a continuous spectrum with respect to the spatial coordinates of transmission lines. The temporal bi-anisotropic media induced by space-time transformation optics (TO) have the ability to convert a single wavelength into multiple wavelengths as well as continuous spectra over a spatial region. The ratio of differential elements is pre-designed to be the scaling relationship between wavelengths; as a result, the mapping between two spaces can be obtained with the temporal bi-anisotropic media required for conversion. We demonstrate the wavelength conversion by illustrating that signals can be converted to present different wavelengths and/or a spectrum as functions of the location of the transmission line. This proposal may offer new ways to design novel microwave and optical space-time systems and have applications in telecommunication, information security, cosmological emulations, etc.

articleTitle: A Compact Three-Port Pattern Diverse Dielectric Resonator Antenna for 5G MIMO Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a pattern-diverse dielectric resonator antenna (DRA). The antenna consists of three Huygens sources, each with a tilted pattern in 5G N78 band (3.3–3.8GBz). The three beams can completely cover the range of 360<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">○</sup>. The three Huygens sources are assembled through the side with a weak electromagnetic (EM) field distribution so that a high port isolation of lower than −20dB can be obtained in the band, based on which the three tilted beams can work independently.

articleTitle: On a U-Net Model for Generating Composite Scattering from Independent Background and Target Data Driven by Coupled Scattering
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A deep learning method based on coupled scattering has been investigated in this work. The aim is to obtain the composite scattering characteristics by using independent electromagnetic scattering data from both target and background. Compared to the data-driven techniques, the proposed novel method exploits the coupled scattering information as input to the U-Net neural network which effectively allows such neural networks to fully utilize all necessary information, including target individual scattering, background scattering, as well as coupled scattering between target and background. A reliable performance for predicting peaks has been demonstrated with the proposed network architecture that augers well for the optimized neural network designs.

articleTitle: Research on Electromagnetic Deception Stealth Technology Based on Antenna Mode Term Radar Cross Section Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to study the influence on radar imaging when the scattering response of stealthy target to radar detection wave changes rapidly with time. In this paper, based on the Radar Cross Section (RCS) regulation principle of antenna mode term, an ultra-wideband log-periodic antenna with large antenna mode term RCS is designed. At the same time, an ultra-wideband antenna load which can reconfigure the reflected phase in 360-degree coverage range is designed, so that the scattered waves of the antenna can be controlled effectively in the ultra-wideband range. Secondly, by testing the antenna scattering fields under different load control states and bringing the measured data into the Range-Doppler radar imaging algorithm, the imaging results show that for Linear Frequency Modulated Continuous Wave (LFM-CW) radar, high speed adjusting the scattering response of stealth targets to radar waves over time will interfere with radar imaging in the range direction, resulting in multiple scattering centers, so that the stealthy target can achieve the effect of electromagnetic deception stealth.

articleTitle: Newton-Raphson Nonlinear Solver for Electric Field Integral Equation and Resistive Boundary Condition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This contribution deals with the transient scattering of electromagnetic fields by conductors whose surface dynamics are captured by a strongly non-linear boundary condition. The scattering process is modeled by coupling the electric field integral equation with the non-linear current-field characteristic. The marching-on-in-time method is combined with a Newton-Raphson non-linear solver to produce an approximate solution. The method is demonstrated on an example exhibiting a negative differential resistance.

articleTitle: Enhancing mm-Wave Beam-Steering with Super Wideband Phased Array for Body Area Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In order to meet the demands of 5G NR/FR-2 wireless networks frequency bands, it is crucial to develop super wideband (SWB) phased array antennas with wide-scan and advanced beam steering capabilities for high speed data transmissions. This research focuses on a new beam-steerable phased array architecture that offers a broad bandwidth for 5G Body Area Networks and wireless IoT devices. The proposed phased array design consists of eight radiators arranged in an 8x1 linear shape, each equipped with separate small strip-line feedings. The proposed antenna array, composed on a substrate of Rogers RT6002, measures 64 mm by 9.51 mm by 1.52 mm in physical dimensions. This design offers a straightforward design approach, low complexity profile, wide impedance bandwidth, and stable characteristics, with a simulated operational frequency span from 21GHz - 50 GHz and a super bandwidth of 29GHz with a −10 dB threshold.

articleTitle: Algebraic Inverse Fast Multipole Method Based Fast Direct Solver for Capacitance Extraction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This article presents a new direct solver to solve integral equations arising out of large-scale computational electrostatics. The solver is based on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{H}^{2}$</tex> matrices that exploit the rank structure of matrices arising out of the discretization of the integral formulation. The key highlights are: i) The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{H}^{2}$</tex> matrix is constructed in a purely algebraic fashion using a new nested cross approximation. ii) A new and efficient way to compress the fill-ins that are encountered during the factorization phase of the solver is presented. iii) The linear complexity of the solver is shown by solving a capacitance extraction problem.

articleTitle: Fast Peak Localization of Beam-Steerable Phased Arrays in a Near-Field Setup
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, the main beam peak of beam-steerable phased arrays is measured in a faster way than conventional methods. By estimating the array element patterns, multiple array patterns can be synthesized without measuring each beam pattern. With the efficient reconstruction of multiple beams, the main beam peak can be quickly located with a direction error of ±1° and a gain error of ±0.3 dB, compared with the reference.

articleTitle: The Smart EM Environment: Vision, Methodologies, and Technologies
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The revolutionary Smart Electro Magnetic Environment (SEME) concept is transforming the landscape of wireless system design, surpassing the capabilities of current- generation systems. SEME utilizes a combination of technologies to control the electromagnetic wave propagation according to network-defined performance objectives. Within this framework, static and reconfigurable Electromagnetic Skins (EMSs) have emerged as a fundamental enabler of the SEME vision. This work aims at reviewing recent advancements in the exploitation of EMSs for SEME applications, offering insights into cutting-edge design and implementation strategies.

articleTitle: A Folded Dipole Embedded in a Flexible Solar Panel for Green Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this contribution, a shaped folded dipole antenna is presented, specifically designed to be fully embedded on a flexible device which hosts also a set of solar cells. The solar cells enable the realization of both the RF and DC paths while maintaining flexibility and providing DC output. The proposed device operates at 868 MHz, suitable for LoRa technology.

articleTitle: Wideband 1×2 Array Microstrip Patch Antenna for 5G-Millimeter-Wave Applications at 59 GHz
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a 1×2 array microstrip patch antenna is demonstrated for the fifth generation (5G) millimeter-wave (mmWave) applications that demand a wide range of bandwidth while taking the size constraint into consideration. The substrate chosen for this study is Rogers RT 5880, which has a thickness of 0.5 mm, relative permittivity of 2.2 and a tan δ of 0.0009. To achieve better impedance matching, return loss, gain, and wider bandwidth, a U-shaped slots adjustment was performed on the patch. The proposed antenna exhibits an operating frequency range from 50.38 GHz to 67.79 GHz, resonating at 59 GHz with a 17.4 GHz bandwidth. At the resonant frequency, the antenna achieves a radiation efficiency of 69% and a gain of 7.6 dBi. The maximum radiation efficiency of 73 % is observed at 62.52 GHz. Throughout the operational frequency range, the VSWR remains within the acceptance range of 1 < VSWR < 2. Altair FEKO was used to model and simulate the proposed antenna design.

articleTitle: A Ferrite-Loaded Large-Curvature Conformal Ultrawideband Tightly Coupled Dipole Array
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A ferrite-loaded ultra-wideband large-curvature conformal tightly coupled dipole array (LCC-TCDA) is presented in this paper. The conformal array element consists of 6 perfectly fitting tightly coupled dipoles upon the layer of the profile. To expand the operation bandwidth and reduce the profile, overlapping patches are used to enhance capacitive coupling between adjacent dipoles, and ferrite pieces with high relative permeability and permittivity characteristic are loaded above the metal ground plane. A novel multi-functional feeding network is designed carefully to steer the beam and transform the impedance simultaneously, by which only a single input port is needed. Consequently, the proposed conformal array element enables to adapt some limited installation spaces and reduces the number of required transmit/receive (T/R) modules. Simulation results show that this antenna is able to operate within 0.28-1.96 GHz with an active VSWR < 3.0 and scanning up to ±60°in the azimuth plane.

articleTitle: A Low Cross-Polarization and Wide Scanning-Range Dual-Polarized Planar Phased Array
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A novel dual-polarized planar tightly coupled dipole array (TCDA) is presented in this paper. By introducing <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pi$</tex>-shaped integrated balun, the metal cross-grids and mirrored pair feeding technique, the proposed antenna can obtain a low cross-polarization and wide scanning-range. An 8×16 dual-polarized array prototype is designed and measured. Both numerical simulation and measured results demonstrate the good performance of the proposed structure. The measured results show that the proposed array can obtain a scanning range of ±70° from 8–16 GHz in E-plane and ±50° from 10–16 GHz in H-plane with 3.5 dB gain fluctuation. The proposed planar phased array is a good candidate for wireless communication and sensing application.

articleTitle: Cutoff Frequencies of Arbitrarily Shaped Anisotropic Waveguides by a Local Point Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this work, the cutoff frequencies of arbitrarily shaped metallic waveguides, loaded with anisotropic material, are computed. To solve the problem, a local point technique is developed for anisotropic loadings. The anisotropy used in this work is of gyroelectric type. The developed local point technique satisfies the requisite boundary conditions at a predefined set of points on the waveguide's contour without the necessity to apply integration techniques. This is achieved by expanding the tangential-to-the-boundary components of the electric field in Chebyshev polynomials. To demonstrate the applicability of the method, non circular cross section structures are studied, such as elliptical and rounded-square waveguides. The results are validated by the HFSS commercial software.

articleTitle: Ultrawideband RCS Reduction and Performance Analysis Using Phase Gradient Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a unique phase gradient metasurfaces (PGMs) is introduced for ultra wideband radar cross-section (RCS) reduction. A 3×3 sub array is designed and simulated using electromagnetic (EM) simulator. According to the modeling results, the metasurface can sustain the RCS reduction of more than 10 dB over an ultra-broadband that spans from 6 GHz to 26 GHz at both normal and oblique incidence. A range of oblique incidence angles, from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-30^{\circ}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$+30^{\circ}$</tex>, was used to confirm the validity of the angle-insensitivity RCS reduction. Due to its broad incident angle, broadband capabilities, simple design without optimization, and polarization insensitivity the proposed PGMs improves both the monostatic and bistatic RCS reduction effectively and proves its significance in covert applications.

articleTitle: Feasibility Analysis of Acoustically Excited Chip Antenna to Realize High-Accuracy Positioning in Mobile Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper discusses the feasibility of integrating the acoustically excited antenna (AEA) with built-in chips in mobile devices to receive navigation signals and combining them with the positioning algorithm. By assessing AEA as the receiving antenna of the navigation system user terminal, the gain exceeds −18 dBi, which is expected to be applied to high-accuracy positioning applications.

articleTitle: Jurassic Park (of Antennas)
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In the early years of long distance wireless low frequencies and primitive generators called for enormous antennas which dwarf modern ones, except those for very specific applications like radio telescope and land-to-submarine communications. In this contribution a few of the most notable ones, at least one of which still standing, are collected in some sort of archaeological park.

articleTitle: Method of Enhancing RIS Performance for 6G Communications: Design, Verification and Future
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a horn-shaped unit-cell of reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) based on a PIN diode with enhancing performances for 6G communications. The unit-cell is composed of a main patch, a bull's head patch and two extended patches connected to ground. This novel structure induces a strong E-field near the sub-patch. It allows for a reduction in the length of the overall patch and a lower resonant frequency when the PIN diode is activated. Simulation results show that the reflection loss is better than −1 dB in 9.5 ~10 GHz range with the proposed horn-shaped structure. A sub-array of RIS, which consists of 4 × 4 array, fabricated and verified beam-forming capabilities in short-range wireless tests. Additionally, a RIS consisting of 4 sub-arrays was tested in a real environment. As a results, received signal strength is improved by +4 dB.

articleTitle: Numerical Assesment & Feasability Study of Farfield Automotive Antenna Measurement Concept
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a numerical assessment and feasibility study of a far-field (FF) measurement technique for vehicle-mounted antennas, employing a 3D movable plane wave generator (PWG). Given the physical size of standard vehicles, antennas can be considered small on a large platform, with their radiation predominantly contributed by the antenna and its immediate surroundings. This insight is leveraged to significantly reduce the size of the plane wave generator, enhancing its agility in movement. The method's feasibility is numerically investigated on a realistic vehicle with antennas in various locations. A physically displaceable PWG is employed to measure the 3D radiated performance in FF conditions. The paper details the test vehicle, introduces the 0.6-6GHz PWG, validates the assumption linking radiation to a limited area around the antennas, and reports the method's achievable accuracy through comparison with reference radiation.

articleTitle: Aerosol Jet-Printed Sensors on Doubly-Curved Multilayer Laminates
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Additive manufacturing has revolutionized RF fabrication processes, enabling antennas, transmission lines, and even SMD components to be directly integrated within existing systems. It is often desirable to integrate these features onto surfaces with high curvatures or surfaces internal to an existing part, which can be difficult to do without disturbing its existing structural properties. In this work, we utilize a novel multilayer insert-based approach to integrate an X-band signal detector to the inside of an ogive radome. Conductive structures, such as coplanar waveguides, were formed using silver nanoparticle ink atop a doubly-curved E-glass laminate with a 5-axis aerosol jet printing process. Electromagnetic properties of these printed structures were verified both experimentally and in Ansys HFSS. We hope to expand upon these techniques in future work to not only develop a fully functional detector system, but also lay a foundation for the integration of microcontroller technology and other sensors directly atop highly curved, nontraditional substrates.

articleTitle: A 92 GHz 16Tx-16Rx Miniaturized FMCW Phased Array Scanning Imaging Radar System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a miniaturized 92 GHz frequency modulated continuous wave phased array radar system is proposed for scanning imaging. The radar system is composed of 16 transmitter elements and 16 receiver elements integrated using silicon technology. The scalable hardware design of the radar system is given and the efficient imaging algorithm based on fast Fourier transform is developed. The result of scanning imaging experiment show that the radar system has a detection range of no less than 190 m in a filed of view ±40°.

articleTitle: Extraordinary Transmission Through an Infinite Periodic Array of Deep-Subwavelength Metal Slots on an Optically Plasma Induced Semiconductor Slab
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper theoretically investigates the extraordinary transmission of the electromagnetic waves through the infinite periodic array of deep-subwavelength perfect electric conductor (PEC) slots with electrically narrow period on the optically plasma induced semiconductor slab for application to the opto-electrically reconfigurable millimeter wave circuits.

articleTitle: Characteristic Mode Analysis Method for Thin Dielectric Coated Strucutres at Low Frequency
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A characteristic mode (CM) solver has been proposed to solve the CMs of perfect electric conductor (PEC) structures coated with thin dielectric sheet (TDS) at low frequencies. Electric field integral equation (EFIE) is well known that it suffers from the low frequency breakdown or inaccuracy. To overcome this problem, the TDS augmented electric field integral equation (TDS-AEFIE) is utilized and the TDS-AEFIE based CM equation is derived for the coated structures at low frequency. Numerical example demonstrates the accuracy of the proposed method.

articleTitle: An Approach for the Generation of Echos in Time-Domain
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: An approach for the generation of complex waveforms in time-domain is presented for a two-dimensional geometry. Numerical results provide a first assessment of the technique.

articleTitle: A Dental Dielectric Resonator Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a dental dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) is proposed. The implantable dental DRA is proved feasible by using real extracted human tooth as the dielectric resonator (DR). This human tooth structure is imitated by Ansys simulation software to agree with the measured results using real human tooth that resonance at 4.39 GHz. Optimization of the antenna structure has been conducted based on practical considerations on the dental structure. The proposed dental DRA is suitable for implantable medical devices to realize sensing and Wireless body area network (WBAN).

articleTitle: Parameter Study of Lowering the SLL of a Two-Way Pattern in Shared Aperture Radar Arrays
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A parameter study of lowering the SLL of a twoway pattern in planar shared aperture arrays is presented. The apertures are with discrete weight amplitude distribution. The ratio of the size between the receive and transmit apertures and their weight excitation are coming from imposing that: (1) A sidelobe of the transmit aperture pattern appears at certain null of the receive one. (2) The level of the two higher sidelobes of the two-way space factor are equal. The array elements are with amplitude taper or equivalent space taper or thinned taper with certain spatial density. Several cases of radar arrays show two way patterns with lower SLL and simpler networks than the ones obtained in the past.

articleTitle: Analytical Computation of Mutual Impedance Between Two Closely Spaced Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
