abstract: Mutual impedance between two closely spaced an-tennas is analytically computed using spherical harmonics and reaction theorem. When two antennas are closely spaced, a reaction surface that lies completely in the convergence region of spherical wave expansion of both antennas can not be found. In this study, a method that overcomes this problem is introduced. The mutual impedance is expressed as a summation of the product of spherical harmonic coefficients of antennas. The validity of the proposed method is confirmed by analyzing half-wave dipoles and printed dipoles. In the latter case, the results are also confirmed by measurement.

articleTitle: A Fast Ray Tracing Algorithm for Propagation Prediction in Urban Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a ray tracing (RT)-based electromagnetic propagation algorithm specifically designed for urban model scenarios. To expedite the ray intersection determination, we leverage Surface Area Heuristic (SAH) spatial partitioning and Single Instruction, Multiple Data (SIMD) acceleration techniques, enabling fast computations for general scenarios. Through comparisons across several typical scenes, we showcase the significant advantages brought about by SAH and SIMD. The enhanced RT program demonstrates superior performance, particularly in scenarios with a higher number of surface elements and intricate diffraction and scattering paths. It provides an effective tool for simulation and analysis in the field of electromagnetic propagation. This work holds substantial significance in enhancing our understanding of electromagnetic wave propagation characteristics in urban environments, especially considering the computational challenges posed by complex scenes and scattering effects in applications with significant computational demands.

articleTitle: Fan-Beam Printed Full-Wave Dipole Antenna Array with Wide Bandwidth and Beamwidth
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a wideband, wide-beamwidth printed dipole antenna array. The electric field across the two horizontal arms of the printed dipole gives an equivalent magnetic dipole. This equivalent magnetic dipole and the printed dipole forms an magnetoelectric dipole, which has a wide bandwidth and a wide beamwidth. To further enhance the beamwidth, a full-wave printed dipole antenna instead of a halfwave printed dipole is used. Parasitic and shorting strips are deployed to obtain a uniform current distribution and thus, widen the beamwidth. To verify the idea, a 1×4 array is designed, fabricated, and measured. A 10-dB impedance bandwidth of 34% (20.85-29.35 GHz) and a peak 3-dB of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H$</tex>-plane beamwidth of 192° at 25 GHz were measured.

articleTitle: Bulk Permittivity Estimation Using an Ultra-Wideband Wearable Antenna for Biomedical Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper explores average dielectric property estimation using an ultra-wideband (UWB) textile antenna that is designed for wearable microwave monitoring applications. The proposed antenna is a printed monopole, fabricated on a denim substrate and operates from 1.5 GHz to 5 GHz when in contact with dispersive material. To estimate permittivity, two identical wearable antennas were used, each in contact with the material under test (MUT). The transmission response was extracted in the frequency domain and then converted to the time domain. By measuring the difference in arrival time compared to a reference, the average dielectric property could be estimated. Testing on dispersive phantoms with known properties demonstrated that the proposed textile antenna has potential for hydration monitoring assessment.

articleTitle: A Frequency-Controlled Dual-Beam Reflector/Subreflectarray Antenna for Vehicular Radar Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A design methodology for a frequency-controlled beam-pointing high gain antenna based on a system of a large reflector and a subreflectarray at the 77-GHz band is presented. This system consists of a parabolic reflector whose aperture size is determined by the required beamwidth, and a subreflectarray made up of three-layer metal-patterned miniaturized-element frequency surfaces. The frequency-dependent subreflectarray is designed to produce two different image points of the antenna feed at two different frequencies around 76 and 81 GHz. The positions of the feed image at these frequencies create two distinct beams in elevation. The positions of the image feed points are chosen to produce 5° beam separation in elevation while maintaining the beamwidth at around 0.35°. To reduce the computational resources for analyzing the antenna, the simulation is performed initially using a MATLAB code and analytical formulations, and then the final radiation patterns are verified with Altair FEKO. This system is intended for monitoring the traffic and the road itself for improved safety.

articleTitle: CAD Formulas for the Circular Microstrip Patch Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper provides accurate CAD formulas for the circular microstrip patch antenna. Formulas are presented for input impedance, radiation efficiency, and bandwidth. These formulas are not empirical but are rigorous formulas that become more accurate as the substrate becomes thinner.

articleTitle: Design of Phased Array Antenna Based on Electronically Reconfigurable Metasurface and Cylindrical Reflector
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: An electronically reconfigurable metasurface based low-cost phased array antenna is presented in this paper. The antenna is composed of a parabolic reflector feeding network, a slotted waveguide antenna (SWA) array, and several electronically reconfigurable metasurfaces which are loaded in the waveguide. The cylindrical wave generated by the source in the planar plate waveguide (PPW) of the bottom antenna layer is converted into the plane wave by the parabolic reflector and used to excite the top SWA array. In order to realize low-cost beam scanning capability, the front end of each independent SWA is loaded with electrically reconfigurable metasurfaces with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{360}^{\circ}$</tex> phase modulation capability. The proposed antenna can realize a continuously <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm \mathbf{30}^{\circ}$</tex> beam scanning range with maximum -13.0 dB side lobe level (SLL) and a gain variation is -2.0 dB. Due to the advantages of low-cost and convenient beam scanning capability, the proposed antenna is very suitable for some low-cost radar and communication systems.

articleTitle: Low-Profile High-Density MIMO Antenna Module Incorporating a 16-Port Configuration for 6G Upper Mid-Band Mobile Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: An advanced high-density massive multi-input multi-output (MIMO) module featuring a 16-port configuration for beyond 5G, specifically optimized for the upper mid-band of 6G is presented. The proposed massive MIMO module integrates a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2\times 2$</tex> patch sub-array within a compact <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$25.7 \times 25.7 ~\text{mm}^2$</tex> footprint, enhancing its 6G MIMO capability. The whole massive MIMO system, featuring <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$62.5 \times 62.5 \times 1.016 ~\text{mm}^3$</tex>, is designed for seamless incorporation into the rear cover of a mobile device, catering to the sleek designs of a modern flip and bar-type handset. Through simulation, the module has been fine-tuned to maintain an impedance match below −6 dB throughout the entire frequency range, ensuring the antenna efficiency exceeding 60%, and verifying that envelope correlation coefficient (ECC) remains below 0.1.

articleTitle: Analysis of Shaped 3D-Printable Dielectric Lens Antennas Based on Generalized Superformula
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this work, an electromagnetic tool for studying a novel class of 3D-printed dielectric lens antennas is briefly presented. The geometrical shape of lens antenna is modeled using a generalized superformula. The electromagnetic analysis is based on both the geometrical and physical optics as well as tube tracing approaches. In this way, the multiple wave reflections within the lens region as well as the far field outside the lens can be calculated. Thanks to this electromagnetic tool it is possible to study complex lens antennas yielding non-conventional radiation patterns with low computational burden.

articleTitle: Accurate Prediction of Power Pattern of Planar Antenna Array with Elements Position Errors Based on Quadratic Relaxation Programming
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper extends the application of a method that can accurately evaluate the power pattern boundaries of antenna arrays in the presence of component position errors. It uses the second-order Taylor series expansion method to approximate the power mode of the error array, thereby deriving a box-constrained quadratic programming problem for tolerance analysis, and finally use convex optimization to solve the proposed problem after a series of equivalent transformations. This paper applies the method to planar arrays and provided a wider range of application scenarios for this algorithm.

articleTitle: A Novel RFID Sensor with Conductive Polymer for “Cold Chain” Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This work introduces Temperature Integrity Seals (TIS) - a novel sensor class designed for Cold Chain monitoring. TIS aims to ensure precise low-temperature maintenance, safeguarding sensitive products like food, pharmaceuticals, and vaccines. The implementation of TIS seeks to address the critical need for precise temperature control throughout the entire Cold Chain, thereby ensuring the reliability and quality of perishable goods during storage and transportation. Implemented with innovative organic semiconductors called “Photochromic Torsional Switch” (PTS), TIS sensors exploits the unique property of these semiconductors to become conductive through light activation, with a subsequent transition to a low-conductivity state after a specific time interval. The sensor consists of a standard HF RFID tag where a portion of one arm is partially replaced with a trace of the PTS compound, numerically modelled as a metal with a variable conductivity in CST Microwave Studio. A consistent variation of the tag input impedance can be observed when the PTS compound changes its state from ON (high conductivity state) to OFF (low conductivity state). This confirms the effectiveness of the device as a temperature integrity sensor.

articleTitle: Enhancing Self-bias Diode Characterization Through Power Correction for RF energy harvesting
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel method for characterizing RF diodes for RF-EH. While obtaining the input impedance through measurements is a common approach, it often relies on the assumption that the nominal source power and the diode's absorbed power are identical, leading to discrepancies. In order to mitigate this problem, a power correction method, combined with behavioral modeling, is proposed. This approach assigns the diode impedance with its actual power level, enhancing the reliability of impedance results without requiring specialized equipment. Harmonic balance simulation validates the effective-ness of this method, showing promising results with a 10dB improvement in impedance-matching performance.

articleTitle: Elliptical Metasurface Design for Dynamic Antenna System in mmWave Band
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A tunable metasurface element design is proposed for a dynamically reconfigurable antenna system. A bias feeding is employed to activate/deactivate the PIN diodes across the metasurface's capacitive gaps with the main surface of the microstrip line. The proposed structure operates in the millimeter band around 28 GHz. Good performance results are achieved with a remarkable decrease in the transmission coefficient to −2.59 dB for one unit cell. Upon activation of the proposed octa-concatenated metasurface unit cells, the structure retains the −10 dB return loss over the whole band. Additionally, a remarkable transmission coefficient resonance of −39.85 dB is achieved around 28 GHz which indicates the amount of radiative power level. Furthermore, different tailored radiation patterns are generated with beamwidths ranging from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$20.1^\circ$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$40^{\circ}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Circular to Linear Polarization Conversion of Branch-Line Coupler Fed Antenna at 3.5 GHz Using Magnetic Bias
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a technique to convert Circularly Polarized (CP) antenna to a Linearly Polarized (LP) antenna when the antenna is fed using a 3 dB branch - line coupler. The conversion is achieved by changing the relative phase of the signals fed into the antenna using a magnetically biased Yttrium Iron Garnet (YIG) based ferrite disc. Magnetic bias of 0.5 T is applied using small Neodymium (Nd) based magnets. Measured Axial Ratio in the frequency band of 3.3 to 3.535 GHz varied from 0.86 dB ± 2.1 dB in CP configuration to 4 dB ± 3dB in LP configuration. Measured gain in this frequency band is ~2 dB for CP and 2.83 dB for LP.

articleTitle: Fabry Perot Array Antenna Design Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we employ a machine learning-based approach to reduce the computational time and energy required for designing and optimizing the partially reflective surface (PRS) structure used in Fabry Perot (FP) antennas. This approach fits the relationship between the PRS geometry and relative permittivity chosen as inputs in terms of the phase gradient of the PRS reflection coefficient chosen as outputs. Subsequently, to validate our approach, we designed a flexible material-based FP antenna exhibiting an enhanced realized gain of 14 dB within a frequency band centered at 24 GHz, suitable for radar applications.

articleTitle: Scaled Wavelet for Hepatic Steatosis Classification Using Microwave Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: To address the challenge of classifying hepatic steatosis levels, a microwave-based technique as a non-ionizing and cost-effective method is proposed. This technique uses frequency-dependent scaled and lower bandwidth wavelet to extract features from microwave signals. The proposed technique achieves 85.5% mean accuracy and outperforms other state-of-the-art methods.

articleTitle: Plug-in Antennas for Telematic Control Unit
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Compact antenna modules for Long Term Evolution (LTE) and 5G technology, WIFI7, V2X, high-precision GNSS and SDARS are presented in this paper as extension of telematics control unit (TCU). The idea is that antenna modules and TCU follow independent production path and, at the end, they are assembled together with some mechanical tolerance. Easy and RF-reliable way of connecting them by means of contact-springs is proposed. Proposed antenna assembly operates at a wide frequency range from 617MHz to 7500MHz. Antenna prototype is fabricated and measured under a dedicated hole in the roof of a commercial vehicle. Results are shown in the paper in terms of VSWR and realized gain.

articleTitle: Asymmetric Manipulation of Wavefronts Using a Broadband Non-Interleaved Janus Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we introduce a new paradigm to enable asymmetric manipulation of transmitted wavefronts for incidences with distinct propagation directions through a Janus metasurface. The spatial symmetry is broken by controlling propagation phase and geometric phase simultaneously. Full-wave simulations coincide well with theoretically calculated results, showing that independent wave functionalities of twin vortex beams and twin pencil beams are generated for backward and forward left-handed circularly-polarized (LCP) incidence, respectively. Both functionalities maintain significant recognition from 23 to 31 GHz, indicating a broad bandwidth of 29.6%. The proposed concept may find potentials for antenna applications in future wireless and satellite communications.

articleTitle: Predicting Electromagnetic Field (EMF) Exposure Using Heterogeneous Graph Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we provide a novel heterogeneous graph neural network (GNN)-based approach to predict the electromagnetic field (EMF) exposure distribution in an indoor environment. The prediction model leverages the concept of heterogeneous graph that allows multiple distinct types of nodes and edges existing to represent a physical indoor environment, providing an improved accuracy compared to homogeneous GNN-based counterpart.

articleTitle: Non-Destructive Dielectric Characterization of Sample Leather via a Custom-Designed Open-Endend Coaxial Probe
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this work, we propose the application of a custom-designed open-ended coaxial probe to characterize the dielectric properties of tanned leather in a non-destructive way. This research represents the first step in filling a knowledge gap due to the lack of systematic dielectric characterization as relative humidity values vary. Over five consecutive days, we measured dielectric properties of tanned leather samples in a controlled environment. The adopted protocol and subsequent evaluation of permittivity and conductivity reveal a consistent reduction in dielectric properties with decreasing humidity levels, aligning with established literature. This work can pave the way for the integration of microwave technologies for remote sensing and monitoring applications in the tanning manufacturing process.

articleTitle: Compact Dual-Polarized Antenna with Dielectric Loaded Cavity for Torso Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A compact body-matched dual-polarized antenna with a dielectric-loaded cavity is designed for torso imaging. The antenna comprises two orthogonal bowtie radiators for horizontal and vertical polarization. Also, it incorporates edge metallization and parasitic elements to widen its impedance bandwidth. Further, the cavity dimensions are significantly reduced by loading a high-permittivity dielectric material. Those techniques result in a compact antenna with dimensions of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{75}\times \mathbf{75}\times \mathbf{15}\ \mathbf{mm}^{\mathbf{3}}$</tex>. The results demonstrate the antenna covers the broadband (0.48-1.65 GHz), equivalent to a 109% fractional bandwidth. The power flow intensities from the antenna inside a model of a human torso at distances of 100 mm are -14 dB, -16.3 dB, and -24 dB at 0.8, 1, and 1.2 GHz, respectively. These findings confirm the antenna's capability to penetrate the E-field inside the human model for successful deep torso imaging.

articleTitle: One-Dimensional Nonlinear Media Inverse Scattering Problem Based on Distorted Born Iterative Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Nonlinear media are the building blocks for non-linear optics. The parameter retrieval of nonlinear media is an important problem for nonlinear optics. However, the maturity and accuracy of nonlinear media retrieval methods lag behind that of the ordinary linear media retrieval methods because it is difficult to analytically solve the Maxwell equations containing nonlinear media. Since the material's electromagnetic (EM) parameter retrieval problem belongs to the EM inverse scattering problem, in this paper we generalize the distorted Born iterative method (DBIM), which is an popular EM inverse scattering method for linear media, to the second-order nonlinear media case. The numerical test shows that the nonlinear parameter distribution of a one-dimensional problem can be determined with the generalized DBIM.

articleTitle: Design of a Cylindrical Patch Array with EBG
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A microstrip-line fed cylindrical conformal patch antenna and array, loaded with an electromagnetic band gap (EBG) structure is investigated. A significant reduction in cross-pol in both principal planes is achieved for the single conformal antenna element. For the conformal array, a nearly omnidirectional pattern characteristic is achieved in the azimuthal plane. A reduction in cross polarization is also observed in the array with EBG configuration compared to the same without EBG. The antenna structures clearly demonstrate the significant improvement of the pattern characteristics with the EBG loading both for the single conformal antenna element and the array.

articleTitle: Fast Solutions of Electromagnetic Scattering by 2D Conducting Rough Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Electromagnetic (EM) scattering by rough surfaces can be formulated by integral equation method and the magnetic field integral equation (MFIE) is the most widely-used governing equation for the scattering by two-dimensional (2D) conducting rough surface. Due to the high computational costs, it is very desirable to accelerate the process. In this paper, we use the Nyström method to discretize the MFIE and incorporate the multilevel fast multipole algorithm (MLFMA) to accelerate the solutions. The MLFMA is much easier to incorporate the Nyström method than the traditional method of moments (MoM) and has not been applied to solve the rough surface scattering problems. Numerical examples are presented to demonstrate the approach.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Two Methods for Generating Realistic Turbulence for Electromagnetic Wave Propagation in the Atmospheric Boundary Layer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The 2D parabolic wave equation (PWE) is widely used to model terrestrial radiofrequency (RF) links. In this iterative method, the contribution of a turbulent atmosphere is classicaly modeled through a statistically homogeneous vertical phase screen generated from a Kolmogorov-type scintillation spectrum. This study proposes a comparison between two methods for generating phase screens representative of a marine atmospheric boundary layer (MABL), both based on large eddy simulation (LES) data. Preliminary results indicate that a purely statistical approach of turbulence tends to underestimate its impact on the propagation of RF signals.

articleTitle: Spin-Decoupled Metasurface for Dual-Phase Hybrid Linear Polarized Transmitarray with OAM Vortex Beams
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This article presents a novel meta-atom structure, which allows for mixed control of geometric phase and propagation phase by altering the length of the phase-delay line (PL) and the rotation angle of the transmit antenna (TA). The metasurface composed of these meta-atoms can decouple the left-handed circularly polarized (LCP) and right-handed circularly polarized (RCP) transmitted waves under the incidence of x-polarized plane waves, respectively generating vortex beams for OAM mode <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$l=2$</tex> and OAM mode <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$l=3$</tex>.

articleTitle: An All-Phase-Vector-Fitting-Based Self-Calibration Method for Elemental Digital Phased Array with Distributed Local Oscillators
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a self-calibration method based on all phase vector fitting for elemental digital phased array with distributed local oscillators is proposed. Firstly, aiming at the problem of the random phase caused by the distributed local oscillators, an elemental digital phased array with distributed local oscillators model is constructed. Then, the third-order fitting curve of the receiver reference power in all phase range is obtained by an external calibration, which is used as a reference to calibrate the transmission channel with random phase by the all phase vector fitting method. Finally, the self-calibration method is verified by using a four-channel elemental digital phased array. Based on this method, the calibrated mean absolute error of the phase difference among the phased array channels is reduced to 3.08°.

articleTitle: Tri-Band Shared-Aperture Base Station Antenna Based on AMC Decoupling Surface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Based on the shared-aperture antenna structure, the high-band antenna is designed as a dual-band base station antenna unit, which operates at 3.3-3.6GHz (HB1) and 4.8-5GHz (HB2), respectively. The low-band electromagnetic transparent antenna and AMC are used as a double-layer decoupling surface, in which the low-band antenna transmits in HB1 and partially reflects in HB2, while the AMC decoupling surface partially reflects in HB1 and transmits in HB2. While reducing the height of the antenna profile, the co-band mutual coupling of dual-band operating high-band antennas and the off-band cross-coupling between low-band and high-band antennas are improved. The final design of the tri-band shared-aperture base station antenna achieves good radiation characteristics, low profile and high isolation characteristics.

articleTitle: On-chip mmWave Antennas on a Piezoelectric ScAlN-Si Platform for 6G-grade Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this work, an on-chip Scandium Aluminum Nitride (ScAlN)-on-Silicon based mmWave meander line monopole antenna is presented. The device is co-designed and co-fabricated with an established, CMOS-compatible process flow developed for Microelectromechanical (MEMS) acoustic resonators, demonstrating the feasibility of multi-physics monolithic integration for mmWave wireless applications on piezo-on-silicon platforms. The proposed microstrip-fed meander line monopole antenna operates at a frequency of 36 GHz in a grounded configuration, exhibiting an estimated gain of 3.5 dB at its resonant frequency. In association with a high-performance microacoustic resonator, the fabricated platform poses a strong development for compact, monolithic, low parasitics wireless sensing techniques for next-generation IoT applications.

articleTitle: Passively Loaded Dipole Array Design for Surface Wave-Leaky Wave Conversion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: An efficient design methodology for a surface wave to leaky wave converter is presented. For an array antenna over a reactance surface, the load impedances connected to the elements are optimized to synthesize a desired pattern when excited by a feed surface wave. Compared with metasurface leaky-wave antennas, the proposed converter utilizes fewer elements, while providing a conversion efficiency close to unity. An example loaded dipole array with a 10-wavelength-long aperture is designed for 2-D TM-polarized wave conversion, which exhibits a high aperture efficiency of 98.3%.

articleTitle: A Low-Fidelity Characteristic Mode Analysis for Arbitrarily-Shaped Patch Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this work, a novel low-fidelity (LF) approach is proposed for obtaining characteristic mode analysis (CMA) information. Specifically, by utilizing (a) properly defined eigen-function expansions, and (b) two-dimensional (2D) CMA method of moment (MoM) solutions, we obtain any number <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L$</tex> of characteristic modal current solutions we desire for arbitrarily shaped patch antennas. Notably, our results show that the proposed method is capable of generating LF solutions with errors on the order of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${10}^{-2}$</tex> when compared to the traditional three-dimensional CMA solutions.

articleTitle: Investigating Second-Order Rytov approximation in two dimensions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Born and Rytov approximations are widely employed to simplify the scattering problem. However, to obtain better accuracies, second order approximations can be employed. Here, a 2D scenario is considered, modelled by a second order Rytov approximation. An analytical/numerical assessment is presented, to evaluate the improved performance of the second order Rytov approximation.

articleTitle: A Wideband Millimeter-Wave Circularly Polarized Metal Lens
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a design of a wideband circularly polarized (CP) metal lens for millimeter-wave applications. The element is designed based on a quadruple-ridged waveguide which can realize the polarization conversion from CP to CP but with the opposite handedness, therefore enabling a full 360° geometric phase controlled by the rotation of the ridges. For validation, a metal lens which can generate vortex beam with OAM mode of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$l=+1$</tex> is designed and simulated. The results show that a wide bandwidth can be obtained, and the mode purity of the generated vortex beam is as high as 0.99. Compared with conventional metal lens, the proposed work can obtain a wider axial ratio (AR) bandwidth since the CP performance can be improved by the geometric phase compensation. Moreover, the proposed element is also suitable for the design of a dual CP lens.

articleTitle: 3D Printed Triply Periodic Minimal Surfaces Lattices for Shielding Applications at Microwaves
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: 3D printing is changing the antennas and propagation, as well as the microwave devices worlds. The possibility of prototyping innovative geometries is pushing the designers to identify new topologies for microwave applications. In this framework, the modeling based on implicit surfaces such as triply periodic minimal surfaces has been underestimated. In this work we will numerically investigate 3D printed TPMS lattices in the MW range. By using dielectric data of a copper-loaded PLA, we studied different unit-cell size for TPMS structure and characterized the absorption and shielding behavior in the range 1–20 GHz. We identified that 3D printed TPMS lattices with 20% and 40% porosities could be useful for shielding in the X- and K-bands.

articleTitle: Smart Fatigue Monitoring using RF Sensing Employing A Deep Learning Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Fatigue can be a symptom of underlying health issues that may require medical attention and proper diagnosis. Human activity monitoring can be used to identify movements by using technology. Technology such as wearable devices can identify movements that indicate fatigue. However wearable devices have limitations such as battery life and the need to be worn regularly. Contactless solutions can remove these limitations. This paper makes use of RF sensing to be able to detect fatigue. The human movements consist of sitting and standing from a desk chair and a bed. Data is collected at a normal pace to simulate no fatigue and a slowed-down pace to simulate fatigue. A Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is proposed to differentiate the different movements at the two positions and if fatigue is present or not. The CNN model achieved an accuracy score of 98.07 %. This result shows that RF sensing has the potential to observe fatigue in individuals within their own homes.

articleTitle: Continuous Scanning Leaky-Wave Antenna Using Partially Radiating Substrate Integrated Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Antenna beam scanning can lead to a significant advantage for wireless systems. In this paper, an LWA with continuous main beam scanning through the broadside is presented and discussed. A partially radiating substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) consisting of inverted-T-shaped slots on the top plate is utilized to design the antenna. To short the top plate to the ground plane, the vias are arranged differently at each of the edges. An array of densely spaced vias is used on one edge, while the vias on the other edge are widely spaced, one at each end of the unit cell. The LWA has the ability to scan the radiating beam from backward through broadside to forward when the frequency of the source is swept.

articleTitle: An Aperture-Shared Dual-Broadband Antenna Array for 2G/3G/4G/5G Base-Station Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: An aperture-shared dual-broadband antenna array is developed for 2G/3G/4G and 5G-NR base-station applications. The dual-broadband antenna array consists of one low-band (LB) element for an ultra-broadband (0.69-1.52 GHz) operation and four (2×2) high-band (HB) elements for broadband (1.7-2.7 GHz) operation. The aperture-shared dual-broadband antenna array achieves an antenna gain of 7 dBi for the LB element and 11 dBi for a 1× 2 HB sub-array with stable broadside radiation patterns.

articleTitle: A Compact Radio-Frequency Localization System for Rescue Operations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This work presents a radio frequency compact system for rescue operations of missing people to reach in difficult or inaccessible areas not covered by radio or GSM services such as hills, mountains, woods and rural areas. The proposed system based on a high gain antenna, a compact software defined radio (SDR) receiver and a small elaboration unit. The system simulate a GSM base transceiver station and it is able to interrogate a nearby GSM mobile phone, carried on by missing people, and to detect the international mobile subscriber equipment (IMEI). The knowledge of International Mobile Subscriber Identifier (IMSI) and IMEI codes inform the rescue operators of the possible nearby presence of missing persons. The proposed rescue system is sufficiently compact to be mounted onboard of a small unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) in order to reach inaccessible, dangerous and unknown areas or easily transportable by hand. The obtained preliminary experimental tests show that this detection systems is able to successfully identify the presence of a GSM devices carried on by a victim, by retrieving its (IMSI) which permits to identify mobile users by their SIM card.

articleTitle: Antenna Reflection Coefficient Measurement Using Six-port Technique at Millimeter-wave Frequency Band
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a six-port simulation system and modelling are performed to estimate the antenna reflection coefficient at the millimeter-wave band, from 60 GHz to 65 GHz. The proposed six-port topology is built upon five H90° hybrid couplers whose measured scattering parameters are recomposed using the Data Access Components (DAC) tool available in the ADS (Advanced Design System) software. A proof of concept test is performed using as a device under test, the measured S- parameters of a millimeter-wave microstrip patch antenna prototype to accurately estimate the reflection coefficient through the power detection at the six-port reflectometer outputs.

articleTitle: Enhancing the Reading Range of MEMS-based Wireless Sensors through Intermodulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This article presents a method to enhance the reading range of MEMS-based wireless sensors in real environments through non-linearities. In such conditions, the main performance limitation is the presence of electromagnetic clutter, which interferes with the reading signal. Intermodulation allows circumventing this issue, by separating the interrogation and the reading frequencies. The inherent nonlinearities of the MEMS behavior generate the intermodulation of different harmonics of the interrogation signal, causing at the same time an actuation of the MEMS sensor and a modulation of the reading signal. As the reading is done at a different frequency than the interrogation, there is a better isolation from the clutter, and then an increased reading range in uncontrolled environment.

articleTitle: An SIE Formulation with Cut-Set Analysis for Impedance Extraction of Real-Life Circuits
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A surface integral equation (SIE) incorporated with the cut set analysis is developed to extract impedance of real-life circuits. By interpreting all quantities in the electromagnetic domain as circuit elements, a three-dimensional equivalent circuit for arbitrarily-shaped circuits is generated. The Kirchhoff's current law (KCL) is then enforced by the cut-set analysis and currents in the circuit are efficiently solved through the pre-corrected fast Fourier Transform (pFFT). Numerical results show that the proposed formulation can accurately model complex real-life circuits.

articleTitle: Uncommon Conductors and Dielectrics for Wearable Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Recent advances in materials science and additive manufacturing have facilitated the development of new conductors and dielectrics for radio frequency (RF) devices. Wearable technology is well positioned to benefit from alternative materials because devices must be conformal, lightweight, portable, and sometimes stretchable. This paper provides a summary of emerging stretchable conductors and engineered dielectrics with a focus on material characteristics and fabrication methods for wearable applications. In particular, stretchable conductors and engineered dielectrics have emerged as promising elements for novel RF sensors and antennas. Stretchable conductors can be fabricated from conductive threads (for easy integration into clothing) or liquid metals (for maximizing stretch potential). Dielectrics with high permittivities and additively manufactured lenses can improve the performance of antennas placed on or near the tissues. In the future, these uncommon conductors and dielectrics may find applications in several fields, beyond wearables.

articleTitle: Investigation of Non-Contact Bedsore Detection Using Electromagnetic Waves in the 5.8 GHz Band
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Bedsores, also known as pressure ulcers, are localized skin and subcutaneous tissue injuries resulting from prolonged pressure and reduced blood flow. Early intervention is crucial for shortening the treatment period. In this study, we placed an antenna between the bed and the mattress to explore non-contact microwave detection for early bedsore identification. In this paper, we replicated bedsores on the sacral region of a numerical human model (Taro) provided by NICT and employed 10.5 GHz and 5.8 GHz band patch antennas for detection. Our findings confirmed the effectiveness of both 10.5 GHz and 5.8 GHz patch antennas in detecting bedsores. Future work involves developing an early bedsore detection method and creating a phantom that more accurately simulates the human body.

articleTitle: Analysis of Performance and Radiation Regulation Compliance on a Miniature Ka Band Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: With the advancements in 5G, 5G-advanced, and 6G technologies, and an increasing number of satellite constellations, there is a greater demand for ground terminals to support non- terrestrial network (NTN) services, particularly earth stations on mobile platforms (ESOMP). For such ESOMPs to achieve global connectivity, low-cost, compact, and power-efficient user terminals are required. This paper analyzes the radiation performance and compliance of small Ka band satcom receiving antennas with European Telecommunications Standards Institute (ETSI) radiation standards.

articleTitle: Synthetic Electromagnetic Emissions: A New Approach to EMC Compliance Testing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: We propose a novel data-driven approach for synthesizing unintended emission signals that can then be used to improve and optimize regulatory thresholds. The main component of our approach is a GAN's generator which is trained with a collection of unintended emission and then, in the inference phase, is asked to produce new and similar signals. We demonstrate that, with correlation as the measure of similarity, the GAN-generated signals are similar to the dataset.

articleTitle: Toward Biodegradable Passive UHF RFID Tags
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: We report the design of a novel passive UHF RFID tag realized on a biocompatible and fully biodegradable substrate. The material used is based on Poly(3-hydroxybutyrate-co-3-hydroxyvalerate) (PHBV) polymer, and the fabrication technique involves thermal vapor deposition and UV laser ablation technique. It is shown with practical read range measurements that the realized tags of size 90 mm x 28.5 mm can operate up to 16m in the EU region.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Unit Cell for Electronically Reconfigurable Reflectarrays at mmWave
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we present a novel design for a reflective reconfigurable intelligent surface (R-RIS) unit cell operating in orthogonal linear polarizations on the V/W-bands. The R-RIS unit cell, featuring a period of 1.6 mm, comprises an octagon-shaped patch antenna and a loop element interconnected by a p-i-n diode. Each resonant element is meticulously crafted to achieve a dual-band behavior, with low reflection loss and a 180° relative phase shift (1-bit phase quantization). To analyze the performance of a reflectarray based on the proposed unit cell, we employed an in-house synthesis tool for numerical studies. The analysis has been validated through full-wave electromagnetic simulations, considering an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$8\times 8$</tex>-element reflectarray. The results confirmed the effectiveness of the designed R-RIS unit-cell in practical applications.

articleTitle: The Impact of a Textbook: Antenna Theory: Analysis and Design by Constantine A. Balanis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Few books have had the level of impact on a field as the textbook, Antenna Theory: Analysis and Design by Professor Constantine A. Balanis has had on antenna engineering. Its share of adoptions at universities around the world is extensive, and since its first publication in 1982, it has now maintained this dominance through four editions for over 40 years.

articleTitle: Hierarchical Matrices Accelerated Topology Optimization of Patch Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Integral equation method-based topology optimization (IEM-TO) may result in excessive computational burden due to the fully populated matrices generated during the discretization process. To extend the applicability of IEM-TO to large-scale problems, with many degrees of freedom, hierarchical matrices (H-matrices) can be used to drastically reduce the overall computational burden. Exploiting this concept, high-resolution topologies can be obtained at the end of the optimization process.

articleTitle: Discrete Metasurface-Based Leaky Wave Antenna: Simultaneously Enhancing Radiation and Aperture Efficiencies
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Traditional leaky wave antennas (LWAs) with a matched termination at the end suffer from poor radiation efficiency, from having power absorbed by the matched load. The alternative - having a long LWA from which most of the power radiates without reaching the end, suffers from low aperture efficiency. We propose a novel concept of LWAs based on discrete metasurfaces. A reflector is placed at the end of the LWA to reflect the remaining power. A special discrete metasurface is designed and placed as the leaky facet of the LWA to leak power from the forward- and backward-travelling waves to the same radiation direction. Finally, the antenna length is tuned to realize a constructive interference between the waves leaked by the forward- and backward-travelling waves. To verify the concept, we design an LWA which realizes broadside radiation. Compared to an LWA of the same length terminated by a matched load, the proposed LWA achieves a 3.5 dB gain enhancement.

articleTitle: Design of Switchable AT/AR Frequency Selective Rasorber with Transmission/Reflection in X Band
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, the simulation study of a switchable polarisation insensitive AT/AR FSR has been carried out. It consists of two layers where the top layer acts as a lossy layer and the bottom layer acts like a lossless layer housing pin diodes thereby offering switchability. The OFF state offers an absorption from 3.41 GHz to 7.48 GHz and a transmission band from 8.31 GHz to 9.37 GHz with insertion loss of -0.6dB at 8.91 GHz. In the ON state, the FSR behaves as a absorber in the frequency range of 3.48 GHz to 7.3 GHz with 90% absorption along with a reflection band. The design is compact and low profile with a thickness of 0.093 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda_{L}$</tex> and periodicity of 0.19 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda_{L}$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda_{L}$</tex> corresponds to the lowest operating frequency. The design offers stable oblique incidence performance upto 30°.

articleTitle: A Novel Wide-Band Unit Cell Design for Monolithic Integration with Electric Field-Induced VO2 Switches
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a wideband 1-bit unit cell, compatible with electrically actuated Metal Insulator Transition VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> switches, is introduced for reconfigurable intelligent surfaces operating in Ka-band frequencies. The unit cell, comprising a patch working in higher order modes and enhanced by a loop structure, has been meticulously fabricated and tested. Measurements are carried out to evaluate reflection phase and magnitude properties within a waveguide setup. The measured results closely match the numerical simulations, showing a phase shift range of 134 to 186 degrees and a return loss of less than 2 dB across the 29.7 to 35 GHz frequency range, indicating a bandwidth exceeding 16%. Additionally, a distinct fabrication process is developed to effectively integrate VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> switches into unit cells. A DC test is performed to demonstrate the feasibility of actuating these switches in a series configuration by applying direct DC voltage.

articleTitle: A DC Stable, Well-Conditioned and Low-Frequency Regularized Time-Domain PMCHWT Equation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper introduces a low-frequency regularized time-domain PMCHWT equation, which is obtained by lever-aging a multiplicative preconditioning and the quasi-Helmholtz projectors. The new formulation is free from all numerical issues of the standard time-domain PMCHWT equation at low frequencies, including dense grid breakdown, large-time step breakdown, DC instabilities, and the loss of solution accuracy. Those properties are corroborated by numerical experiments.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Dual-Band Gap for Printed Gap Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Any microwave circuit will naturally contain several discontinuities, for instance, a splitter, power divider, coupler, bent transmission line, and a feeding network for antenna arrays. However, studying the discontinuity of the strip-ridge bend is crucial since it provides design suggestions and knowledge about active or passive microwave components. An electromagnetic dual-band gap (EDBG) unit cell comprises a double dielectric substrate layer and an air gap for Electromagnetic (EM) wave propagation. The periodic surface acts as a high-impedance surface. Inserting a ridge in the periodic structure allows the waves to propagate along the ridge within the EDBG and suppress propagating waves in other directions. The EDBG cell period is 1.8 mm. A dual-band ridge line with two 90° bend lines and dual-band power divider are proposed for high frequency and millimeter frequencies. The designed geometry and simulated results are presented.

articleTitle: Design of a Wideband Ring Microstrip Antenna Fed by Two L-Probes with a Rat-Race Coupler
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents design of a wideband ring microstrip antenna (MSA) fed by two L-probes with a rat-race coupler. The proposed antenna consists of a square ring patch, two feeding L-shaped probes (L-probes) to excite the ring patch, and a rat-race coupler on the ground plane. The two L-probes are fed by the rat-race coupler differentially and unwanted radiations from the vertical portions of the two L-probes are cancelled out each other. Therefore, cross polarization in H-plane pattern of the proposed antenna, which is a typical phenomenon of the wideband MSA fed by an L-probe, can be reduced. The design frequency of the proposed MSA is around 0.6 GHz. In order to make the ring patch and the rat-race coupler equal in size, the rat-race coupler is miniaturized by bending the rat-race circuit. To achieve wideband characteristics at around the design frequency, dimensions of the proposed antenna are tuned by using electromagnetic simulator IE3D. It is confirmed by the simulation that fractional bandwidth less than −7.4 dB reflection is approximately 34%. Very low cross polarization in H-plane pattern below −30 dB is also confirmed by the simulation.

articleTitle: Ka-Band 3D-Printed Dielectric GRIN Planar Lens Antenna with Beam Forming Capabilities
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The manuscript describes the design of a planar dielectric graded index (GRIN) lens antenna for 5G applications operating in the 28 GHz Ka-band. The seven parallel slabs comprising the designed lens each have a distinct relative permittivity value. The required refractive indexes for each section are obtained through the arrangement of their relative permittivity values. The lens antenna demonstrates a maximum gain of 16.2 dBi in the broadside direction. The proposed lens antenna exhibits a beam-scanning capability of ± 30° and a gain exceeding 14 dBi in 60-degree scan range. The lens can be manufactured through the utilization of 3D-printing technology, employing low-loss high <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varepsilon_{r}$</tex> dielectric filaments. In order to produce the distinct permittivity values for each slab, the infill percentage of the sections utilized during the 3D printing procedure will be varied accordingly.

articleTitle: An On-Body Flexible Wireless Energy Harvesting Metasurface Operating in 5.8 GHz Band
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: An on-body flexible energy harvesting system oper-ating in the 5.8 GHz ISM band is proposed, which is comprised of an energy harvesting metasurface (EHM) and three rectifiers. The proposed EHM is composed of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3\times 3$</tex> unit cells cascaded into three columns, and a direct-current (DC) domain combination is adopted to collect the energy harvested by the three columns of unit cells by using three rectifiers. A flexible substrate is used for implementation of both the EHM and rectifiers to achieve flexibil-ity. The simulation results show that the proposed EHM achieves an energy harvesting efficiency of 82.8% for the EHM in plane form and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$> 60\%$</tex> in bending form with a bending radius <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$> 40$</tex> mm, demonstrating good on-body robustness. The designed rectifier achieves a rectification efficiency of 33.4 % with 1 V voltage output under 0 dBm input. The proposed EHM has a small size of 66 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${}^{*}66^{*}1.22 \text{mm}^{3}$</tex>, suitable for daily wearing on the chest or back by humans for house care or hospital monitoring applications.

articleTitle: Mutual Coupling Reduction Techniques for mmWaves Antenna Arrays
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The 5G Era demands delivering high speed, ultra-low latency and exceptional reliability. MIMO Antennas are a key enabler for such performance. However, mutual coupling (MC) is a reality that degrades the overall system's performance. This work focuses on comparing antenna decoupling techniques presenting six different structures all with four identical radiating elements, but each one of the arrays has a different approach to reduce MC. A basic original structure is shown as a reference and then five alternatives are presented: i) 45° rotation of the patches, ii) shielding vias, iii) parasitic L-shaped elements, iv) crossed and v) rectangular slots. Besides this, the alterations in resonance, bandwidth, directivity and efficiency will be analyzed.

articleTitle: Multistatic Scattering Matrix for Describing Electromagnetic Scattering from Cylinders with Arbitrary Cross-Sections
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The multistatic scattering matrix is derived and calculated using two techniques previously developed by the authors [1]–[3]. SPM and Direct SPM formulate the scattering problem by defining the boundary conditions in terms of projections of spectral signatures. The two methods are used to derive the multistatic scattering matrix and to show the equivalence of both techniques. The multistatic scattering matrix electromagnetically defines the object completely at a given frequency. It is shown that this matrix is symmetric and that it may be used to synthesize targets with specified scattering patterns.

articleTitle: Analysis of Electrically Small Resonators for Multiple Feature Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Resonant microwave sensors have ability to sense different physical properties such as materials characteristics, material content, geometrical features etc. Using multiple resonators for detecting more than one feature is required. In this study a new approach for analysing electrically small resonators for multiple feature extraction is presented. A distribution dissimilarity definition is introduced to identify ability of resonators for extracting permittivity and permeability of materials.

articleTitle: Performance Improvement of Automotive Radar Antennas Located Behind Car Bumpers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Automotive radars are often required to be placed behind a car bumper. The bumper layers can produce significant degradation to the radar antenna gain and hence to the maximum detectable range of the radar. It is shown that by adding a dielectric matching layer or/and by tilting the bumper with respect to the antennas, it is possible to reduce the gain degradation across the radar field of view. The idea is illustrated via a concrete example of a printed patch antenna located behind a bumper sample taken from a car. Good agreement is demonstrated between simulations and measurements.

articleTitle: Measurement of Solar Noise Temperature in Ku-Band Using a Satellite Broadcast Receiver
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Twice per year, every geostationary communication satellite is seen from the Earth with the Sun transiting behind it, causing the receivers whose beams are directed towards this satellite to pick up an interfering noise due to the solar microwave radiation. The assessment of this additional noise is of great importance not only in satellite broadcasting, but also in nowcasting and climate change monitoring applications, when opportunistic rainfall measurement based on satellite downlinks is employed. As matter of fact, the latter case requires accurate real-time measurement of the received signal level and prompt management of non-rain related alterations. This paper illustrates an experimental campaign, carried out during a solar transit behind a Ku-band broadcasting satellite, and provides a numerical evaluation of the Sun noise temperature.

articleTitle: Enhancement of Non-Destructive Measurement Resolution with Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Similar to image sharpening, the resolution of measured electromagnetic fields can be enhanced with machine learning. We numerically demonstrate that a λ/10 spatial resolution is achievable even with probes that are a few wavelengths wide, while maintaining a maximum relative error of less than 3%.

articleTitle: Accurate Computation of the Radar Cross Section by Increasing the Geometric Approximation Order in Boundary Integral Equations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: It is well-known that high-order finite element methods offer significant gains in terms of accuracy and computation time. However, due to some difficulties related to their implementation for boundary integral equations in electromagnetism, their integration into industrial codes is not very popular. In this work, we present a simpler approach, giving quite good results, which only consists in increasing the geometric approximation order instead of the Galerkin approximation space order.

articleTitle: Small Antenna Q and Gain – 80 Years of Progress
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The understanding of small antennas has evolved tremendously since the initial investigations close to 80 years ago. In this presentation, we highlight some fundamental results on Q-factor, bandwidth, and gain.

articleTitle: Broadband $4\times 4$ MIMO Antenna Based on Parasitic Patches Decoupling for Smart Terminals
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A broadband terminal <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{4}\times \mathbf{4}$</tex> multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) antenna based on parasitic patch decoupling is reported. The proposed MIMO antenna consists of two MIMO pairs, with each pair consisting of two monopole antennas. Then, a parasitic patch is loaded on the top blank area between the two monopole antennas of each MIMO pair, with another parasitic patch loaded on the corresponding bottom blank area. In this way, decoupling can be achieved as the mutual coupling current between antennas and the current on parasitic patches are with equal amplitude but out-of-phase. A lumped inductive-capacitive (LC) resonator is also loaded between each feeding port and the monopole antenna to adjust the resonance. To verify the design concept, a prototype is realized. The measured results indicate that the central frequency is 3.4GHz, with a bandwidth of 600MHz, a return loss over 10dB, an isolation better than 15dB and a realized gain about 4.55dBi. Moreover, it exhibits opposite semicircular radiation directions in the operation band as well, illustrating good potential for practical terminal applications.

articleTitle: Transition-Based Mutual Coupling Calibration for Phased Array Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Accurate control of the direction and shape of the radiation pattern in a phased array antenna necessitates the ability to accurately set the phase and amplitude at each element. In these arrays, calibration techniques are often employed to account for dissimilar signal chain components. This paper presents a transition-based mutual coupling calibration technique that is used for calibrating a phased array after deployment. Prior to deployment, mutual coupling parameters between elements in the array are determined through a far-field calibration scheme. The measured results showed that this technique is capable of determining the phase offset present with a mean error of less than 1° and a standard deviation of around 5°.

articleTitle: A Compact 915 MHz PCB Antenna for RFID Tag
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents an inverted-F antenna (IFA), characterized by its high compactness, cost-effectiveness, and suitability for easy integration into printing processes. The passband is 902.97-927.03 MHz with a maximum gain of 1.77 dBi. It is specifically designed for radio frequency identification (RFID) or internet of things (IoT) applications within the 915 MHz industrial scientific medical (ISM) band. Optimized for short circuits and feed lines, it demonstrates favorable impedance matching characteristics <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathbf{47.3}-\mathbf{j}\mathbf{0.27}\ \mathbf{\Omega})$</tex> and can be seamlessly integrated into printed circuit board (PCB) designs with an overall size of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{12}\times \mathbf{5}\times \mathbf{0.87}(\mathbf{L}\times \mathbf{W}\times \mathbf{H})$</tex>.

articleTitle: End-to-End Transmissive Metasurface Design from Far-Field Masks Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: We present a deep learning (DL) based framework for the design of lossless and passive transmissive metasurfaces. The DL framework takes the user-defined lower and upper far-field (FF) masks along with the incident field data. It then outputs a metallic trace design for the metasurface such that the resulting power pattern (PP) resides within the specified masks.

articleTitle: Multi-channel Phase Synchronization Method for Independent Asynchronous Local Oscillators Based on Pre-Calibration Matrix
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: There is a random phase difference between multi-channels in the locking of independent local oscillators (LOs), which limits its application. In this paper, a synchronization method based on pre-calibration matrix (PCM) is proposed to solve this problem. The PCM method takes full advantage of the channel characteristics without additional calibration network. The research shows that the phase synchronization error of PCM is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm \mathbf{5}^{\circ}$</tex>, which provides a good idea for scenarios that are inconvenient to use common LO such as distributed arrays.

articleTitle: A Novel Bayesian Optimization Framework for RIS-Assisted Wireless Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface (RIS) emerges as a promising technology for shaping the wireless propagation environment. In this paper, we introduce a novel Bayesian optimization framework to address the challenge of joint channel estimation and optimization in complex wireless environments. To reduce the dimensionality of large-scale RIS, the framework incorporates a unique physics-informed structure embedding utilizing angular and spatial domain basis vectors. We validate our approach through laboratory experiments conducted with software-defined radio equipment, considering scenarios where the receivers are located in near-field or far-field regions. The results demonstrate superior channel gain per iteration compared to existing methods.

articleTitle: Analysis of a TEM Cell Designed for Real-Time Observation of Pulsed Microwave-Induced Thermoelastic Tissue Expansion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: We design and evaluate the performance of a TEM cell for dosimetry applications in the UHF band with design modifications to allow real-time monitoring of tissue expansion due to microwave pulse absorption. We introduce an aperture for high-speed microscope-based imaging inside the waveguide and assess the aperture's impact on power absorption homogeneity and dosage level in tissue samples positioned at the site of the aperture. We consider both pure borosilicate and ITO-coated glass plates covering the aperture. Our results indicate that microwave absorption homogeneity and dosage are highly dependent on the microwave-frequency properties of the optically transparent plate covering the aperture and the ratio between the aperture and tissue sample radii. These findings pave the way for further investigations into the thermoelastic expansion of tissue induced by pulsed microwave exposure.

articleTitle: 3D-Printed Conformal Meta-Lens with Multi-Mode Orbital Angular Momentum (OAM) Generation and Beam-Steering Capabilities
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper introduces a 3D transmitting cylindrical conformal meta-lens designed for height-to-phase-controlled electromagnetic beam control, specifically Orbital Angular Momentum (OAM) generation and beam-steering functionalities. Comprising 40 × 20 independently tunable unit cells using 3D printing, the meta-lens achieves full 360° phase compensation. CST Microwave Studio is employed for unit cell and full structure analysis, with a probe antenna illuminating the meta-lens. The proposed antenna achieves both OAM modes generation and beam-steering by evaluating necessary phase compensations for each meta-atom. Simulation results demonstrate two distinct OAM beam scanning techniques—single-beam and dual-beam steering—at different angles. This capability can be extended to enable wider 2D beam scanning, showcasing the meta-lens as a potential low-cost candidate for high-gain beam-steering mm-wave communication systems.

articleTitle: Accurate Computation of RIS Scattered Field Patterns Based on Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The unit cells of a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) do not work in locally periodic environments due to the varying states of their neighboring cells. Hence, the RIS cell-to-cell coupling is very different from periodic structures, where coupling effects can be precisely evaluated using periodic boundary conditions. We present a novel method based on convolutional neural networks to predict RIS scattered field patterns, fully considering the non-periodic nature of RISs. Our trained model is capable of predicting RIS patterns with an accuracy comparable to finite-element analysis at all angles and for any configuration of the RIS.

articleTitle: Scalable Dual-Polarized Stacked-Patch Antenna Array for In-Band Full-Duplex Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Directional in-band full-duplex (IBFD) systems can utilize phased arrays to generate high amounts of isolation at the aperture level by creating transmit and receive subarrays that support multifunction operation. This paper presents the design of an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{8}\times \mathbf{8}$</tex> dual-polarized stacked-patch antenna array that can be used for scalable IBFD applications. A prototype array was fabricated and evaluated to operate from 2.7 to 3.5 GHz with a maximum element gain of 4.6 dBi on average and a maximum element-to-element coupling of -15 dB for adjacent elements, which represents an important metric at the boundary between the subarrays and dictates the design of subsequent cancellation techniques.

articleTitle: A Gain-Enhanced Method Based on Metamaterial Crystals and High Permittivity Material for Dual-Polarized Base Station Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a gain-enhanced method based on metamaterial crystals and high permittivity material for dual-polarized base station antenna is proposed. The gain-enhanced superstrate structures consist of a one-dimensionally periodic layered metamaterial crystal slab with three unit cells and a high permittivity slab. The superstrate structures are loaded above a compact dual-polarized base station antenna element and a linear antenna array including four antenna elements to improve their realized gains. The simulated results shows that the realized gain of the antenna is enhanced from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$7.45\pm 0.15\text{dBi}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$9.02\pm 0.18 \text{dBi}$</tex> in 1.71-2.17GHz band and realized gain of the 1x4 array is enhanced from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$13.5\pm 0.5\text{dBi}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$14.6\pm 0.4\text{dBi}$</tex>. These two examples show the feasibility of the proposed method, which contributes to the research of accurate beamforming of base station MIMO antenna array and deserves further study.

articleTitle: FSS Design Approach for Low-E Glass Target Using Micro Metal Patch
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, the Micro Metal Patch(MMP), designed to enhance the poor radio wave propagation characteristics of low emissivity(Low-E) glass by employing a small-sized metal patch compared to the wavelength, has no impact on the radio wave characteristics of standard glass. Extending these results, simulations validate that MMP does not affect the propagation characteristics of the Frequency Selective Surface(FSS) used as a spatial filter. These results indicate the appropriate application of FSS to Low-E glass that requires a high Metal Filling Ratio(MFR).

articleTitle: Compact Pattern Reconfigurable DR Antenna for Smart IoT Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a pattern reconfigurable, compact dielectric resonator (DR) antenna based on a biased feeding approach. In a sandwich-like structure, the DR is divided into two parts with a cross-shaped metallic strip in the center. The cross-shaped strip is connected to a copper probe running through the bottom half of the DR, forming a top capacitively loaded monopole structure. A parallel capacitive effect is generated between the strip and the ground, thus producing a good vertical polarization. To obtain multiple switchable beams, the cross-shaped strip is cut and the four branches are connected with PIN diodes. By controlling the working states of the diodes, a total of eight directional beams and one omnidirectional beam can be obtained. The measured overlapping -10 dB impedance bandwidth is 2.35-2.8 GHz (17.5 %), with an efficiency higher than 90 % on the operating band. The antenna well suits miniaturized 2.4 GHz WIFI band and smart IoT applications.

articleTitle: A Polarization-Reconfigurable Magnetoelectric Dipole Antenna for 5G Millimeter-Wave Application
