publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a polarization-reconfigurable magneto electric (ME) dipole antenna with a wide axial ratio (AR) bandwidth and good gain for 5G millimeter-wave (MMW) applications. The radiation structure of the antenna is a ME dipole composed of four vertical metallic pins and four horizontal patches. In order to generate circular polarization (CP) radiation, an additional small metallic strip and four p-i-n diodes are introduced in this design to connect two patch sections located at diagonal positions. The polarization type is switched between right-hand circular polarization (RHCP) and left-hand circular polarization (LHCP) by altering the states of the p-i-n diodes. Simulation results indicate that the proposed antenna achieves a wide overlapped bandwidth from 24.9GHz to 28.6GHz with S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> ≤ −10dB and axial ratio ≤ 3dB and a maximum gain of 7.8 dBic.

articleTitle: A Novel Ultra-Wideband Low-Profile and Wide-Angle Scanning Tightly Coupled Microstrip Array (TCMA) with FSS Superstate
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a novel tightly coupled microstrip array (TCMA) with frequency selective surface (FSS) superstate is proposed. The present unit-cell consist of a modified L-probe patch with four parasitic patches, which introduces three resonance points, ensuring the matching performance within the impedance band. Furthermore, to improve the scanning performance, a wide angle impedance matching (WAIM) layer etched with periodic frequency selective surface is utilized. The proposed antenna array has a low profile height with a maximum thickness of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{0.054}\lambda_{low}$</tex>. The infinite-array simulations indicate a bandwidth of 2.94:1 (3.33 GHz to 9.46 GHz), or a relative bandwidth of 95.8%, with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{VSWR} \leq \mathbf{3.0}$</tex> for a maximum scan-angle of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 60^{\circ}$</tex> in E-,D-planes and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 45^{\circ}$</tex> in H-plane.

articleTitle: A Compact PDMS Based Ultra Wideband Antenna for Wireless Body Area Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this work, a multiple stub loaded patch antenna is presented which is designed by using flexible substrate material as Poly-Di-Methyl-Siloxane (PDMS). The antenna offers a small size of 15 mm x 25 mm with simplified structural geometry. The antenna performance parameters have been analyzed and are compared with recently published designs. Results show that the proposed design exhibits ultra- wideband response and offers high gain up to 6.6 dBi, which is achieved by loading multiple stubs to the CPW feed resonator. The presented design is suitable for future wireless body area networks (WBAN).

articleTitle: A Bistatic Measurement Scheme for Revealing Signatures of Tree Defects in Radar B-Scans
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a bistatic measurement scheme to reveal the signatures of tree defects (e.g. cavities and decays) in radar B-scans. In this scheme, the transmitter and receiver are placed separately at two sides of the trunk, away from the trunk surface, and moved along the same direction on straight trajectories while obtaining the B-scans. The obtained B-scans are then processed using a Kaiser window and singular value decomposition. In the processed B-scans, the defect signatures appear obviously, demonstrating the advantage of the proposed scheme for defect detection. Compared with other measurement schemes, the proposed scheme allows obtaining defect signatures with a 17 dB signal-to-noise ratio improvement in radar B-scans.

articleTitle: IFA Miniaturization Strategy Using Magneto-Dielectric Materials in UHF Band for IoT Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This article presents a strategy of miniaturization for electrically small Inverted-F Antenna (IFA) using Magneto Dielectric Material (MDM). The loading strategy is studied in order to strengthen the interaction of antenna's magnetic and electric near fields with the properties of the material. Following this strategy, a tradeoff is established with electrical size of the antenna and its radiation properties.

articleTitle: A Novel Technique for Magnetic Particle Separation Using Current-Carrying Slotted Plate
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a novel method for separating and trapping different magnetic particles is presented. Changes in the current-carrying structure yield disturbing the generated magnetic field. Here, slots were innovatively crafted on the current-carrying plate positioned beneath the microchannel, resulting in a non-uniform magnetic field distribution. This breakthrough enables the separation of different particle types using a constant and low electric current for the very first time, leading to a significant advancement in the field. More importantly, this proposed technique offers several advantages, including the generation of low levels of current and heat, ease of construction, and the ability to control the magnetic field produced by the electric current. In this study, the capability to effectively separate various particle types using a constant electric current was demonstrated with a remarkable separation efficiency of about 100%. By applying a 100[mA] electric current to the plate that carries electric current, the separation of two particle types M-450 and M-280 was achieved at a velocity of 2[μm/s].

articleTitle: Numerical Solution of the 3D Eikonal Equation by the Fast Marching Method for Electromagnetic Problems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: We present a numerical scheme based on the Fast Marching Method to solve the eikonal equation in 3D for a direct electromagnetic problem. The eikonal equation is discretized using a Cartesian grid and a second order Godunov upwind finite differences is adopted.

articleTitle: A Low-Cost Indoor Signal Redistribution Solution Based on Active Frequency Selective Surface Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: We combine reconfigurable and active frequency selective surface (AFSS) techniques to provide a low-cost solution for indoor signal redistribution. The scheme consists of a low-cost elliptical cylindrical AFSS reconfigurable operating at 2.5 GHz/5.2 GHz and a shortcut algorithm to control its operating frequency bands and radiation beams. It is important to note that in order to meet the Wi-Fi requirements, the proposed AFSS radiation beams can be realized by independently adjusting the transmission coefficient and phase of the different frequencies of the AFSS.

articleTitle: Low Profile and Wideband AMC-Based Connected Slot Array Antenna-in-Package for Millimetre-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a low profile and bandwidth enhanced slot based connected antenna array (SCAA) is presented for millimeter wave (mm-wave) applications. A single connected slot is etched out on the ground plane, which is excited by four exciters. For achieving directional radiation from the on-package SCAA, backing reflector (BR) is placed beneath the slot plane. A patch-based artificial magnetic conductor (AMC) layer is inserted between the connected slot and the BR layers to make it both low profile and achieve bandwidth enhancement. The multi-layer stacked SCAA has a bandwidth of 2.3 GHz. The low profile SCAA has a realized gain of 9.54 dBi and the total efficiency is 85%. The beams from the structure are steerable up to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 36^{\circ}$</tex> degrees. The smaller dimension in the Z direction makes this suitable for placement even on the thinner edges of mobile and handheld terminals.

articleTitle: Efficient and Wideband Ka-Band Waveguide Array
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: To address the power combining loss and fabrication challenges of conventional Ka-band array, a wideband waveguide horn array was designed and fabricated. The prototype array demonstrates better than 80% efficiency and about 20% bandwidth.

articleTitle: A Novel Dual-Beam High Gain Beam Scanning Fabry-Perot Cavity Antenna Based on Bidirectional Asymmetric Transmission Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A dual-beam high-gain wide-band beam-scanning Fabry-Perot-Cavity-Antenna (FPCA) is proposed in this article. By configuring a single reflection-mode (R-mode) FP cavity with two external feed antennas operating at the same frequency band, the proposed antenna can simultaneously generate two high-gain beams with different steering angles. The beam scanning angle of the two beams is equal to the excitation angle of the feed antenna to the R-mode FP cavity. The two high-gain beams of the antenna can be deflected independently by changing the irradiation angle of the two feeds to the R-mode FPC independently. The proposed dual-beam antenna consists of a Janus PRS which is constructed by a bidirectional asymmetric transmission metasurface, a metal ground, and two external feed antennas. For a demonstration, we analyze the beam scanning performance of the proposed dualbeam R-mode FPCA in four different planes in 3-D space. The simulation results indicate that the proposed antenna can realize a beam scanning angle of 30° for each beam. The deflected beams in the four scanning cases all behave as high-gain pencil beams. The proposed dual-beam R-mode beam-scanning FPCA can be potentially applied in the 5G communication systems to enhance the communication capacity and spectrum utilization efficiency.

articleTitle: Integration of Image-Based Ray Tracing in UHF RFID Propagation Modeling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The progression of real-world deployments has greatly improved the field of Ultra-High Frequency (UHF) Radio-Frequency Identification (RFID) propagation and development is still underway. This study presents inclusion of image-based ray tracing in modeling propagation of the UHF RFID systems with the emphasis on the ground reflection phenomena. Image-based ray tracing is the cornerstone of the most accurate electromagnetic wave behavior simulation, especially for the ground reflections. This technique immensely improves the accuracy of UHF RFID signal propagation prediction tailored to different environmental terrain and surface types. The study thoroughly investigates different ground materials, receiver elevations and methodically reveals their impacts on signal propagation. Applying this method not only perfects the theoretical models but also to a great extent simplifies the practical realization of RFID system.

articleTitle: Integrating Statistical Methods and Machine Learning Classifiers for Accurate Landmine Detection Using Ground Penetrating Radar A-scan Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach for landmine detection utilizing Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) A-scan signals. The proposed method combines statistical techniques with Machine Learning (ML) classifiers to enhance the accuracy of landmine detection. Employing the statistical approach, relevant features are extracted from A-scan signals, providing insights into the subsurface characteristics of the soil and buried landmines. The study employs various ML classifiers, including Random Forest (RF), Support Vector Machine (SVM), and XGBoost (XG), are leveraged for classification purposes. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed method, a real dataset is constructed through a comprehensive measurement campaign that includes a diverse range of objects, including surrogate Improvised Explosive Devices (IEDs). Classifier performance is assessed using accuracy as the primary metric. The experimental results showcase a notable effectiveness rate of 98%.

articleTitle: Design of Low-Sidelobe and Low-RCS Tightly Coupled Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The low-sidelobe and low-RCS tightly coupled antenna array based on sparse array method and antenna mode RCS cancellation is proposed in this paper. The radiation and scattering field of the 1×16 tightly coupled antenna array are calculated based on the unit excitation active element pattern method and verified by full-wave software. The positions of the sparse units are optimized by the genetic algorithm to achieve the low-sidelobe property. Furthermore, the sparse units are shorted and connected to delay lines with optimized different lengths to obtain the desired antenna mode RCS to cancel out the scattering field energy of the total array. The final proposed array can achieve over 8 dB sidelobe reduction and 13.3 dB RCS reduction at the same time at the center frequency of 10 GHz.

articleTitle: Phase Center Analysis of Wideband Continuous Transverse Stub Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This work analyzes the phase center stability of a continuous transverse stub (CTS) antenna. The excitation of the slots/stubs is assumed ideal and equivalent to the field distribution provided by a pillbox beam former for corporate feed networks. The phase center variation is then derived analytically and validated numerically with full-wave simulations for a single stub/slot and a finite array. Numerical results validate the stability of the phase center within a wideband operation.

articleTitle: Hybrid Metal-Topological Insulator Terahertz Metasurface for Ultrasensitive Refractive Index Biosensing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Terahertz thin film Sensing systems lack sensitivity due to small interaction length between Terahertz waves and biological samples. Terahertz metasurfaces provide electromagnetic field confinement and strong light-matter interaction by exciting surface plasmon polaritons (SPP) at the interface between dielectric substrate and metal-based resonators. In this paper we propose a hybrid Terahertz metasurface based on a metal- topological insulator resonator for refractive index (RI) biosensing. 2D Dirac plasmon polaritons (DPP) can be excited in the Terahertz range in Bismuth Selenide (a topological insulator). By coupling the DPP in Bismuth Selenide to the SPP in Gold, a plasmon induced transparency (PIT) resonance is excited whereby only non-radiative losses are present. Through simulation the proposed metasurface has a high theoretical sensitivity of 683GHz/RI with a Q-factor of 6.55. Showing the possibility of using topological insulators as a material platform for Terahertz Metasurface Biosensors.

articleTitle: In-Band Suppression of Spoof Surface Plasmon Polaritons Based on Mode Switching
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this work, a strategy to generate in-band suppression of spoof surface plasmon polaritons (SSPPs) is proposed by switching between the first two modes. Mode switching is realized by using a modified substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) with modulated boundaries. Unlike existing methods, in-band suppression is achieved by converting the fundamental mode to a first higher order mode, rather than the principles of reflection and absorption. The simulated passband is from 4.5 GHz to 14 GHz with a return loss higher than 15 dB. The relative bandwidth of the notch-band is 10.6%, and the maximum attenuation in the notch band is 28 dB at 9.4 GHz. This work provides a new way to design notched-wideband (NWB) bandpass filter (BPF) based on SSPPs.

articleTitle: Miniaturized Top-Metalized 3D-Printed Rectangular Dielectric Resonator Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel top-metalized Dielectric Resonator Antenna (DRA). The inclusion of top metallization induces a modification in the boundary conditions, resulting in a frequency reduction in the fundamental mode of the DRA. A prototype is designed for the 2.45-GHz WiFi band with a -10-dB bandwidth from 2.40 to 2.51 GHz. The radiation maxima occur in the top and bottom directions, with a gain of 1.81 dBi at 2.45 GHz. The proposed DRA is specifically designed for manufacturing using commercially available materials and additive manufacturing techniques.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of an Ultra-Wideband Low Side-Lobe High-Gain Omnidirectional Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The advancement of the latest WiFi standard has spurred the development of a novel antenna design. A novel antenna design with broadband, low side-lobe, and high-gain omnidirectional radiation is proposed in this paper to achieve high-speed WiFi signal transmission. This design involves an innovative modification of the ground plane in a rectangular microstrip patch antenna, effectively achieving ultra-wideband, low side-lobe, and omnidirectional radiation characteristics. A 1 × 4 series-fed array, composed of antenna units with these attributes, is utilized to attain the antenna's high-gain feature. Simulation results using CST Microwave Studio® demonstrate that the designed antenna array can achieve a reflection coefficient of less than -10 dB in the range of 3.5 GHz to 10.4 GHz, and the side-lobe levels are consistently below -10 dB in the range of 3.8 GHz to 6.2 GHz, with gains exceeding 6 dBi. The electric field distribution analysis of the patch units substantiates the antenna's omnidirectional radiation capability. The designed antenna possesses advantages such as compact size, light weight, and ease of implementation, making it suitable for WiFi 7 applications and other similar areas.

articleTitle: Deep-Learning-Based Antenna Impedance Modeling With Output Nonlinear Normalization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A rectangular spiral loop antenna (RSLA) impedance is efficiently modeled over a wide frequency range of 2 - 7 GHz using a deep neural network (DNN) encoder inspired by computer vision (CV) principles for regression problems. After detecting the common pattern from 500 training impedance responses, the model predicts the impedance responses corresponding to new dimensions that have never been seen. As RSLA is a multiple-resonance structure, its analytic and surrogate-based modeling is challenging. However, applying the nonlinear normalization technique to the impedance model's output substantially improves the training process. This study advocates integrating machine-learning based algorithms with full-wave simulators transitioning from conventional to smart agents, leveraging their ability to generate reliable datasets.

articleTitle: Efficient Analysis of Antenna Array Around Electrically Large Platforms Using Hybrid ACA-PO Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The Adaptive Cross-Approximation (ACA) technique is presented to speed up the conventional MoM-PO for analyzing antenna array in the vicinity of an electrically large platform. In the hybrid ACA-PO method, the ACA technique, which is based on the specific properties of the Green's function, can be employed to compress the self-impedance matrix of the MoM region, as well as the interaction matrices between the MoM and PO regions. By introducing the ACA into MoM-PO, the initial dense matrices are compressed which resulting in a substantial reduction in memory consumption. In addition, the hybrid ACA-PO method utilizes the decomposed low-rank matrix to solve the current, which can efficiently perform matrix-vector multiplication (MVM) related to MoM and PO regions. Several numerical examples are given to illustrate the efficiency and accuracy of the proposed hybrid method in comparison to the conventional MoM-PO and Adaptive Cross-Approximation (ACA) methods.

articleTitle: A Low-Profile High-Efficiency Dual Circularly-Polarized Reflectarray Based on Phase-Modulated Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a low-profile high-efficiency dual circularly-polarized (DCP) reflectarray (RA) based on phase-modulated metasurface. The proposed DCP RA achieves independent beamforming for CP waves with opposite handedness. The DCP phase compensation is achieved by dual-phase hybrid metasurface unit-cells that integrate both Berry phase and dynamic phase. As a proof of concept, a low-profile RA is designed and simulated, with asymmetrical DCP beams of (φ=0○, 0=-10°) and (φ=0○, 0=30°) for left-handed and right-handed circularly-polarized (LCP and RCP) waves input, respectively. This RA exhibits excellent characteristics such as high efficiency, low profile and high polarization purity. The proposed DCPRA is a promising candidate for various wireless and satellite communication systems.

articleTitle: Pattern Reconfigurable Multi-Beam SIW Antenna for mm-Wave Radar Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This article proposes a 4-port reconfigurable Substrate Integrated Waveguide (SIW) travelling wave antenna for 24 GHz (ISM band) radar applications. Unlike the conventional beamforming architecture, the designed prototype can generate single, dual and quad-beams based on the excitation of specific ports. The SIW antenna structure with an overall size of 2.8 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda_{0} \times 2.8\lambda_{0}$</tex> has a radiating circular slot positioned on a closed loop circular waveguide. The multi-port-fed circular waveguide excites the slot to generate the desired beam patterns. The length of the circular slot is chosen as an integer multiple of the guided wavelength, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda_{\mathrm{g}}$</tex>. The waveguide structure is designed to propagate the dominant mode of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$TE_{10}$</tex>. The proposed SIW structure is numerically analysed with the 3D EM solver of ANSYS HFSS. It is observed that with single port excitation, the generated beam has a tilt of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$10^{\circ}$</tex> from the end-fire direction. Both the polarization and the gain patterns of the antenna can be changed with suitably selected excitations for the proposed multi-port structure, with maximum realized gain of 10.7 dBi when all ports are excited with equal magnitude and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$90^{\circ}$</tex> phase shift.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Self-Decoupled MIMO Antennas Using Hybrid Modes Cancellation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a dual-band self-decoupled MIMO antenna design scheme based on hybrid modes cancellation is proposed for mobile terminals. For common mode excitation, the proposed antenna presents a monopole mode at the low band and a dipole mode at the high band. Differently, for differential mode excitation, it presents an inverted-F antenna (IFA) mode at the low band and an open slot mode at the high band. By delicately optimizing the antenna geometry, these modes are probable to be canceled out with each other so that a dual-band self-decoupling can be achieved naturally. The results show that - 10 dB impedance matching and 20 dB isolation can be achieved in both the N78 band (3.4 - 3.6 GHz) and the N79 band (4.8 - 5 GHz). What's more, the simulated total efficiency ranges from 80 to 89 % while the ECC is lower than 0.01.

articleTitle: Wideband Circularly Polarized Double-Armed Helix Antenna for GNSS Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A double four-armed helix antenna integrated with phase shifters at 0<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">○</sup>, 90<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">○</sup>, 180<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">○</sup>, and 270<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">○</sup>is presented. The proposed design aims to achieve a broadband circular polarization performance. The impedance matching bandwidth above 10dB return loss is approximately 890MHz, ranging from 0.98 GHz to 1.87 GHz. The 3dB Axial Ratio bandwidth is approximately 774MHz (about 53%) from 1.076 GHz to 1.85 GHz, with 1.463 GHz being the center frequency. This ensures coverage across all operating frequencies of GNSS systems.

articleTitle: Recovering Speech Signals from Millimeter Wave Radar by Mining the Intrinsic Properties of Passive Sound Sources
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a novel vibration measurement method based on acoustic waves and millimeter waves is proposed. The feasibility of using millimeter wave radar to extract vibration information from the surface of an object is analyzed. An experiment was designed to detect the frequency response of different passive sound sources to chirped speech signals using millimeter wave radar. In the experiment, the vibration frequency information and induced vibration modes of water glass and aluminum foil under the influence of 0–2 kHz chirp voice frequency signals were measured. The comparison reveals that different objects produce different vibration frequencies and vibration modes due to their inherent properties. The results of the study help to mine acoustic features that are more applicable to the vibration of object surfaces in the process of recovering speech information from the surfaces using millimeter wave radar.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Assisted Design of EM Skin Meta-Atoms within the System-by-Design
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: An innovative System-by-Design (SbD) method is proposed for the design of non-parametric electromagnetic skin (EMS) meta-atoms. The developed technique leverages a smart encoding of the unknowns allowing to exploit physics knowledge and to enable a favorable environment for the optimization-driven solution of the arising synthesis problem. This latter is efficiently solved by means of a customized SbD implementation relying on a Deep-Learning (DL)-based Surrogate Model (SM) of the pixel-based reflective meta-atom and the exploration of the solution space by means of an Integer-Coding Genetic Algorithm (ICGA) strategy. A preliminary proof-of-concept is shown to assess the capabilities of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Quasi-Dual Formulation of Homogenized Integral Equation for Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The impedance boundary condition (IBC) is a well known and convenient approximation of metasurfaces. When used with the Integral Equation formulation (MoM) it leads to the Electric Field Integral Equation-IBC (EFIE-IBC) format. While very convenient, this formulation has conditioning issues when the surface impedance has inductive values. In this communication, we present an approximate formulation that employs the dual of the EFIE and the admittance; this formulation is shown to improve the conditioning problem of the EFIE-IBC.

articleTitle: Assessing the 28 GHz Channel Capacity Enhancement in NLOS Mine Tunnels Through RIS Deployment
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This work evaluates the use of Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RIS) in underground mine tunnels to enhance channel capacity under high fading conditions at 28 GHz. We focus on the absorptive and reflective modes of RIS in mitigating communication challenges in these Non-Line-of-Sight (NLOS) environments. Using 3D ray launching simulations, we model a mine section to assess a profitable positioning of the RIS and its impact on specific propagation paths. Results indicate that reflective RIS can boost channel capacity in scenarios with significant path loss, while absorptive surfaces are effective in high multipath scenarios. This study underscores the potential of RIS in complex, constrained environments, highlighting the necessity of real-world validation.

articleTitle: Imaging Performance of Extended Rytov Approximation With and Without Phase Data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The recently proposed extended phaseless Rytov approximation for lossy media (xPRA-LM) has been shown to have good potential as a phaseless inverse scattering technique for strong scattering and low-loss conditions. xPRA-LM's linear phaseless form along with its large validity range makes it a practically feasible inverse scattering technique for real-world applications. In this work, we provide the with-phase form of xPRA-LM under strong scattering, low-loss media and compare its performance with the original phaseless form. xPRA-LM has opened up a new paradigm of practically feasible inverse scattering frameworks that can be used for large-scale radio and microwave imaging applications (such as indoor imaging using Wi-Fi signals). Hence, formulating and comparing its with-phase form can be highly useful in evaluating further research directions.

articleTitle: Thermal Response of CO2-Loaded Zeolite 13X Subjected to High Power Microwave Illumination
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper and subsequent presentation describes a procedure to measure the thermal response of fresh, humidified and CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-loaded Zeolite 13X subjected to high power microwave illumination. We describe the experimental configuration and present results of temperature measurements as a function of time, intensity of RF exposure and position in the test cell.

articleTitle: Analytical Formulation of a DNZ Rectangular MTM Unit Structure for mm Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The analytical formulation using an equivalent circuit model derived in terms of RLC circuits of a rectangular Double Negative (DNZ) Metamaterial (MTM) unit cell for millimeter-wave (mm Wave) applications is presented in this article. The double-split dual-ring unit cell is designed on a 0.254 mm-thick substrate material Rogers RT/duroid 5880. It has an overall size of 3.05 mm × 2.85 mm. The model is developed considering all the losses, especially taking into consideration finite conductivity of conducting materials, finite resistivity of the dielectric material and the presence of dielectric substrate with metallic rings on top. It is possible to predict the exact resonance frequency of this particular structure by exploiting the proposed model. The numerical method shows 99% agreement to the analytical one which establishes the structure to be compatible for mmWave applications.

articleTitle: Modelling of Thick Conducting Wires with Macro Basis Functions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper concerns accurate and efficient method of moments (MoM) modelling of finite-conductivity wires of an appreciable electric thickness, for which conventional thin-wire MoM solvers yield inaccurate results. A macro basis function (MBF) approach is followed, which accounts for circumferential current components and variations, intended to yield similar accuracy to general surface MoM, but requiring fewer degrees of freedom. Preliminary results show that MBF solutions correspond closely with general surface MoM solutions.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Enabled Wide-Beam Metasurface Antenna for Wide-Angle Scanning Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A machine learning-enabled wide-beam metasurface (MTS) antenna is proposed for the wide-angle scanning array using a fully-connected neural network. The wide-angle scanning based on MTS antenna elements feature the challenges of not only rich degrees of freedom but also the requirements of port matching and specific radiation patterns so that the multi-objective-multi-parameter optimization suffers from high complexity and high computing costs. To alleviate these challenges, an inverse model mapping the performance into the structural parameters is constructed, trained, and verified. With the aid of the inverse surrogate model, the proposed MTS antenna achieves a 3-dB beamwidth from 100° to 125° with a 20% operating bandwidth and is used to construct an eight-element linear array with equal spacing. The designed ML-enabled MTS antenna array achieves beamscanning from −62° to 62° with stable peak gains from 14.2 to 14.5 dBi and scan loss from 2.4 to 2.9 dB over the band ranging from 6.6 to 7.4 GHz.

articleTitle: Single Layer Polarization Insensitive Wideband Time Modulated Frequency Selective Surface for Radar Countermeasure
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This manuscript proposes a single-layer polarization insensitive wideband time-modulated Frequency Selective Surface (FSS) to modulate the impinging electromagnetic (EM) waves in the frequency range of 3 GHz to 6 GHz (66%). The time modulated FSS is specifically engineered to modulate EM waves that are reflected from it, resulting in the formation of number of harmonics within the spectrum of frequencies exhibited by the modulated wave. The unit cell design incorporates a PIN diode to achieve the switchable characteristic of the FSS. Through the application of a periodic biasing signal to the PIN diodes, a time-varying reflection coefficient is achieved. The proposed structure has been fabricated and measured. The obtained results are in good agreement with the simulated outcomes.

articleTitle: Ultra-Thin and Flexible Metasurface Absorbers Mounted on a Highly Conductive CFRP Substrate
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: We propose two ultrathin, flexible and polarization-insensitive metasurface absorbers (MAs) for radar-cross section (RCS) reduction in UAV applications. Both absorbers are formed by resistive patches, which are arranged on a PET substrate of thickness 0.27 mm, classifying the MAs as ultrathin. A uniform MA is designed to achieve maximum absorption and serves as a starting point to synthesize a broadband periodic non-uniform and polarization-insensitive absorber. Both absorbers are mounted as a coating on carbon-fiber reinforced polymer (CFRP). The measurements of the fabricated MA samples are in very good agreement with the corresponding simulations, and corroborate the MA's high absorption and broadband behavior.

articleTitle: Tuning of Multilobate Patch Antennas Using the Cavity Model in a Space Mapping Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The space mapping algorithm is applied here to the design of patch antennas considering the cavity model as the coarse model. The simple cavity model adopted here does not take into account the feed position, yet when applied in the space mapping method, it is effective in tuning the patch antenna. The feed position is then optimized separately, directly evaluating the fine full-wave model. The framework is applied to patch antennas with a multilobate contour.

articleTitle: Feed Design Synthesis Using Shorting Pins Illustrated by Characteristic Mode Analysis to Achieve Dual Resonances
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper discusses altering characteristic modes using shorting pins to achieve dual resonance. The two shorting pins were introduced in the structure such that one shorting pin is used to alter the horizontal current mode, and the other changes the vertical current modes. The systematic adjustment of shorting pins helped control the antenna's impedance matching and dual frequency resonance. It is also shown that variation in Xpin parallel to horizontal currents and away from the origin increased the lower order frequency. Then, the variation in Ypin parallel to the vertical currents but towards the origin lowered the higher-order resonant frequency such that the dual resonance was achieved.

articleTitle: A New Fly Ash Carbon Measurement System Based On A Cylindrical Cavity Resonator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This article introduces a system for detecting carbon content in fly ash using a cylindrical microwave resonant cavity operating in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$TM_{010}$</tex> mode. By employing the principle that particulate matter in a semi-fluid can change the resonant frequency of a microwave cavity, this method provides a rapid, cost-effective, and accurate means of measuring carbon content in fly ash, along with real-time online monitoring capabilities. It addresses the complexity and high costs associated with traditional methods of measuring dielectric properties. This technology demonstrates high precision, with its regression model achieving a coefficient of determination <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(R^{2})$</tex> of 0.9907, and shows significant potential for the measurement of other types of materials.

articleTitle: Analysis of Factors Influencing Resolution Accuracy in Millimeter-Wave Holographic Imaging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Imaging resolution is a crucial performance indicator for millimeter-wave imaging systems, requiring careful design considerations for practical applications. This paper addresses the resolution issue in the millimeter-wave holographic reconstruction algorithm. The theoretical resolution limit is derived based on the phase difference values of echo data received by receivers positioned at both ends of the scanning array. The results demonstrate that the imaging resolution is influenced not only by the wavelength of the transmitted signal but also by the sampling length and imaging distance.

articleTitle: Are All the MFIE-Related Antisymmetric Gram Matrices Singular?
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In the numerical solution of the magnetic field integral equation (MFIE), the identity operator is discretized into a Gram matrix. It has been long believed that the Gram matrix is always singular provided that the Galerkin testing method is used. We provide a class of nontrivial counterexamples to this stereotyped misconception.

articleTitle: Arbitrarily-Shaped Dual-Linear Polarization Reflectarray Elements Independently Controlled for Dual-Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes arbitrarily-shaped unit-cell elements that can suppress mutual-coupling effects in the design of a dual-band dual-polarized single-layer reflectarray. The unit-cell elements, which are generated by genetic algorithm-based optimization, provide reflection phase characteristics required for two bands. As a design example, a reflectarray operating at the 14-GHz and 28-GHz bands are presented, and the effectiveness of the designed is numerically verified.

articleTitle: Study on “±1” Excitations for Low Sidelobe Antenna Array Designs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A method to design low sidelobe antenna arrays is introduced, where the array elements are uniformly excited, but a subset of them are fed 180<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">○</sup> out of phase. A phase-reversed (PR) element can be easily realized by mirroring feed line of the antenna element. To find the optimal positions of the PR elements for sidelobe suppression, a binary gray wolf optimizer is adopted. Then, numerical experiments on linear arrays of isotropic elements are conducted. After that, full-wave simulations on dipole arrays are carried out to validate the correctness of the optimized results.

articleTitle: High-Gain UWB Planar Antenna Array Designs with FSS Reflector for $\mathrm{S}-\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{u}}$ Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: High-gain, wideband, conformal printed monopole array designs are presented. In this work, we demonstrate the ability to implement multiple monopole designs to achieve a series of high gain, ultra-wideband compact arrays for sensing applications. The proposed designs include a printed rectangular combination monopole antenna (PRCMA) and printed elliptical combination monopole antenna (PECMA). The arrays consist of four elements, and yield fractional bandwidths of over 160 % and an average realized gain of 11 dBi. The proposed designs operate at frequencies of 2.0 GHz - 20.0 GHz with a feed structure composed of general connectorized power splitters. The arrays are coupled with a simple slot monopole-based frequency selective surfaces (FSS) to achieve enhanced gain.

articleTitle: A Migration-Assisted Deep Learning Scheme for Shape and Permittivity Reconstruction of Tree Defects
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a migration-assisted deep learning scheme to reconstruct the positions, shapes, and permittivities of trees' internal defects via radar B-scans. First, a structural similarity index measure (SSIM)-based autofocusing technique (AFT) is proposed to determine the effective permittivity of tree trunk's wood layers. The migrated image obtained via setting the effective permittivity retains most of the shape information of the defect. Then, a U-shaped convolutional neural network with the multiple receptive field module is used to denoise the migrated image and reconstruct the shape and permittivity of irregular defects. The preliminary results demonstrate that the proposed scheme successfully reconstructs the images of the tree defects with a mean square error of 0.0059 and an SSIM of 0.9283.

articleTitle: A Novel Miniaturized Spoof Surface Plasmon Polaritons-Based Monopulse Antenna for Advanced Target Detection and Tracking
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A compact high gain monopulse antenna for target detection and tracking using spoof surface plasmon polaritons (SSPPs) is proposed. SSPPs-based comparator circuit having high field confinement is designed for feeding the proposed antenna, which consists of 2 × 2 radiating array to radiate at 10 GHz. The simulated results shows that, the sum <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\sum)$</tex> beam at port1 with a gain of 14dB, whereas the difference <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\overline{\triangle})$</tex> beam at port2 (for azimuth) with a gain of 11.5 dB, and port3 (for elevation) with the gain of 12.5 dB is achieved. Moreover, the null depth at the two ports are recorded as -8 dB and -14 dB respectively. The proposed model proves its potential for target detection and tracking application in X-band.

articleTitle: High Gain Elliptic Lens Antenna at D-Band for 6G Multi Gbps Data Transmission
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The present work reports the development of a homogeneous lens antenna with an elliptic profile. The antenna exhibits 32 dBi of gain at 142 GHz with half-power beamwidth of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{3.2}^{\circ} \times \mathbf{3.2}^{\circ}$</tex>. A pair of such antennas were used to establish a line-of-sight (LOS) link at 142 GHz. Using this link, data transmission at a rate of 55 Gbps was experimentally demonstrated. Relevant experimental data are presented.

articleTitle: A 2D Transmitarray-Augmented Luneburg Lens Antenna for Millimeter-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper demonstrates a circular transmitarray- augmented Luneburg lens antenna for beam-forming at a millimeter-wave (mmWave) regime. The proposed structure is comprised of an augmentation of 80 dielectric cubes phase correction layer and two semi-circular 10-layer Luneburg lenses. The circular transmitarray-augmented Luneburg lens antenna is fed by a 9 dBi horn antenna at normal incidence and an oblique incidence of −150. The beam is successfully transmitted with an angle up to +45°. When the feed is oriented in normal incidence, a pencil beam is transmitted at 166°and 151°with a realized gain of 20.3 dBi, and sidelobe level (SSL) below −10.0 dB, at 28 GHz.

articleTitle: Effects of Volcanic Particles on Satellite Links at Ka, Q/V, V and W band
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The atmospheric attenuation affects satellite links causing a signal degradation that increases with frequency. The presence of hydrometeors induces both attenuation and depolarization effects that are not negligible for frequencies above 10 GHz. Due to an increasing demand for high data rates, satellite communications work at Ka band and above. The impact of volcanic particles during explosive eruptions represents an additional source of signal degradation. This work describes the effects of finest volcanic ash particles in terms of attenuation and depolarization at Ka, Q/V, V and W band.

articleTitle: Wide-Angle Direction Finder using a Modified Partial Maxwell Fisheye Lens
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This study presents the design, development, and evaluation of a novel radio frequency (RF) direction-finding system for wide field-of-view applications. Combining a novel graded index lens based on a Modified Partial Maxwell Fisheye permittivity distribution, and a custom power detection module we demonstrate nearly hemispherical direction-finding capabilities over the Ka-Band (26–40 GHz).

articleTitle: Design and Evaluation of Lightweight, Broadband, Radar Absorbing Material for X Band
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Radar absorbing materials (RAMs) play a very important role in both civilian and military applications for electromagnetic wave absorption. However, their weight presents a significant challenge. Consequently, broadband, lightweight RAMs are in high demand. In this article, we design single-layer and two-layer RAMs based on multiwalled carbon nanotube (MWCNT)-reinforced glass micro-balloon (GMB) syntactic foams and compare their performance (in terms of -10 dB absorption bandwidth in the X-band and weight) to that of MWCNT composite RAM. Our findings indicate that MWCNT-reinforced syntactic foam offers a lightweight and broadband solution. Additionally, a two-layer MWCNT-reinforced syntactic foam can provide a weight reduction of 1.0661 kg/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> compared to a two-layer MWCNT composite RAM.

articleTitle: Simultaneous Multibeam Clustered Phased Arrays by Using Mixed Antenna Element Factor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A preliminary study concerning the design of a simultaneous multibeam antenna system is addressed. The exploitation of radiating elements with different radiation patterns is at the basis of the novel phased array design strategy. A trade-off between good radiative multibeam performance and low complexity is offered by adopting a subarray partitioning scheme based on Penrose tessellation.

articleTitle: Hybrid Potential-Field Formulation for Densely Discretized Composite Conductors with Open and Closed Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper examines accurate and efficient analyses of densely discretized composite conductors consisting of open and closed surfaces. A novel surface-integral-equation formulation, namely the hybrid potential-field formulation (HPFF), is proposed by appropriately employing field and potential formulations on composite problems. HPFF is not susceptible to both low-frequency breakdowns and internal-resonance problems. Numerical examples show the superior performance of HPFF compared to other available formulations, specifically for densely discretized structures with both open and closed surfaces.

articleTitle: Employing Deep Learning to Enhance Angle Resolution of Directional-of-Arrival (DoA) Systems Using Rotman Lens
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper introduces an innovative direction-of-arrival (DoA) estimation method for millimeter wave (mmWave) wireless, overcoming the accuracy limitations of phase data and algorithmic complexities found in existing studies. We propose a deep learning-based DoA estimation system, optimized for inexpensive processors, and demonstrate its effectiveness through empirical measurements. The research methodology includes data collection across various angles, neural network training, and real-world measurement validations, revealing the high accuracy and robustness of the DoA estimation system against diverse signal source positions. With these methods, we achieved an accuracy rate exceeding 99.55% under the assumption of an error margin within 1 degree. These advantages offer more accessible and efficient DoA estimation solutions for contemporary communication systems, enabling devices requiring DoA information to independently comprehend and control electromagnetic wave.

articleTitle: Mutual Coupling Compensation Algorithm for Arrays with Single-Mode Antenna Elements
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A novel excitation algorithm to compensate for the effects of mutual coupling in antenna arrays is proposed. By manipulating the array's impedance matrix, the algorithm generates a normalized current excitation for each individual element in the array. This is done by taking advantage of the single mode operation of dipole antennas, often referred to as the single mode approximation, to simplify the analysis of mutual coupling and array synthesis. Simulations of half-wavelength dipole arrays are presented to show the effectiveness of the algorithm when compared to uncompensated excitations. The algorithm produces a far field radiation pattern with increased main beam gain, and decreased side lobes and nulls.

articleTitle: Effective Dielectric Properties Reconstruction of Biopsy Excised Tissue
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This work describes the numerical analysis and analytical reconstruction of the dielectric properties of a biopsy excised cancer tissue sample, performed by adopting an open-ended coaxial probe. Specifically, a metallic coating hosting the excised tissue during the biopsy procedure has been adopted and used as an extension of the coaxial probe with the aim of reconstructing the dielectric properties more effectively. The proposed solution avoids the biopsy sample alteration during the reconstruction procedure, allowing the pathologists to perform their analysis and minimize the uncertainties.

articleTitle: Predictive/Robust Microwave Sensor Using LSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This contribution introduces a microwave sensor for instant glucose measurement in microfluidic channels, enhancing diabetes management. The sensor overcomes the discrepancies caused by delays and malfunctions in traditional systems. The proposed sensor offers a real-time response, which is correlated with the glucose level within the interstitial fluid (ISF). The key innovation is the integration of machine learning, particularly a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network that enables predictive monitoring and anomaly detection. This method, validated through in vitro experiments, offers high accuracy and improved reliability in predicting glucose level, significantly contributing to robust environmental monitoring.

articleTitle: Using Electrically Small Electromagnetic Sources for Breast Cancer Detection in Low Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper explores the imaging of a realistic numerical breast phantom model through the utilization of low-frequency electromagnetic sources. Employing electrically small sources, specifically electrically small dipole antennas or electrically small loop antennas, we investigate the minimum observable contrast (resolution) in the captured images. This investigation is crucial as these sources can excite biological electric and magnetic dipole moments within the tissues. Our findings demonstrate that, within the near-field region of the object under test, the resolution reached ⋋/1500.

articleTitle: Toward Clinical Applications of Portable Electromagnetic Torso Scanning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The pathway taken towards the clinical realization of portable electromagnetic torso scanners is discussed. Specifically, the requirements for the imaging antennas and their design methods, phantoms for reliable lab tests, and potential and limitations of processing and imaging algorithms are all explained. Also, a summary of the initial clinical results using the systems developed over the past decade by the electromagnetics innovation research group at The University of Queensland is presented and discussed. This paper highlights various aspects of hardware and software requirements and their interrelation with the final aim of building an integrated and portable electromagnetic torso scanning system.

articleTitle: Full-Duplex Substrate Integrated Gap Waveguide Circulator Antenna System for Ka-Band Radars
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This work uses an integration technique to design an antenna with a circulator forming a full-duplex communication system based on substrate-integrated gap waveguide (SIGW) technology. The SIGW circulator covers a wide frequency range from 27–33 GHz, with an excellent return loss and isolation level over the frequency range. The antenna considered for this work is a PCB-based dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) augmented with rings providing wide bandwidth and high gain.

articleTitle: Excitation of On-Body Creeping Wave Propagation Using a Low-Profile TEM Horn Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper explores the excitation of on-body creeping waves using low-profile TEM horn antennas at 2.80 GHz. The investigation simulates key parameters such as reflection and transmission coefficients versus various frequencies and distances. It compares the creeping wave transmission path loss around the human torso at 2.80 GHz for both monopole and horn antennas. Through simulations, the study reveals that the horn antenna consistently outperforms the monopole antenna across these parameters. The superior performance of the horn antenna underscores its potential as a more effective choice in scenarios where creeping wave characteristics play a crucial role. These findings contribute valuable insights for applications requiring reliable and efficient signal propagation for body area communications where creeping waves are significant.

articleTitle: Mechanically Reconfigurable Dielectric Resonator Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A new type of dielectric resonator antenna (DRA), where the resonator body consists of small multiple building blocks, is proposed and implemented. A simplified method of forming a resonator on a grounded dielectric substrate allowed for design flexibility and reduced fabrication cost. Reconfigura-bility via changing the shape of the resonator is demonstrated theoretically and experimentally.

articleTitle: Design of a Beam Reconfigurable Flexible SIW Slot Array Antenna Using ANN-Based Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A beam-reconfigurable Multiple-Input-Multiple-Output array antenna is presented using flexible PET materials <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\varepsilon_{r} =3.08, \tan\delta=0.03)$</tex>. The antenna is physically foldable, enabling beam adjustment without external components. Machine learning optimizes slot positions, achieving three-fold states: a single beam at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\theta=\pm 0$</tex>, two beams at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\theta=\pm 45$</tex>, and four beams at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\theta=\pm 45, \theta=\pm 135$</tex>. The system maintains stable reflection/transmission coefficients and a realized gain of approximately 15 dB around 24 GHz, suitable for radar monitoring.

articleTitle: A Compact Full-duplex Antenna with High Isolation Using Neutralization Line
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A compact full-duplex antenna consisting of two identical patches is proposed with high isolation. The patches are placed in close proximity and connected through a neutralization line, which enhances the isolation between the antennas. Measurement results show that the proposed antenna exhibits a −10 dB impedance bandwidth, spanning from 2.35 GHz to 2.45 GHz. With a small antenna element separation of 0.05λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>, the measured isolation of the proposed antenna peaks at 53.6 dB at 2.16 GHz. The proposed antenna is suitable for use in portable full-duplex communication systems.

articleTitle: An Ultralong-Range,Compact UHF RFID Tag with a pair of curved F-type arms
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: An ultra-long range planar UHF RFID tag with a compact footprint of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$57.6 \times 27.5mm^{2}$</tex> is proposed in this letter. The tag is based on a T-matching network, which introduces a pair of curved F-type tuned impedance arms to adjust the tag's resistance and reactance for the first time, in which the curved F-tuned impedance arm is divided into an inner arm and an outer arm, and the impedance of the antenna can be simply adjusted by the three parameters of the inner arm and the outer arm. The simulation results show that due to the good conjugate matching, the power transmission coefficient of the proposed tag reaches 98.00%, while the input reflection coefficient (S11) is −38 dB. After analysis and optimization, the tag achieves a maximum gain of 2.71 dB and its read range can reach 22.18 m at 920 MHz.

articleTitle: A New Linear Approximation for 3D Scalar Inverse Scattering Problems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A new linearized approach for the 3D inverse scattering problem based on a convenient decomposition of the relevant Green's function is proposed. In particular, the 3D scalar problem is addressed as it is propaedeutic for the fully vectorial one and is significant in several applications. A preliminary result with simulated data is reported to show the performance of the proposed linear procedure as compared to more classical approximations.

articleTitle: An Improved Entropy Regularization Method for Defect Detection in 3D Composite Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Microwave time reversal is applied here for non-destructive testing of composites backed by metal in a 3D situation. The entropy regularization method, as a typical and effective localization method, failed in this case because of the strong reflection from the composite-metal interface, which leads to wrong localization of defect. An improved ERM is proposed by combining the information provided by the target response signal. Numerical simulations based on 3D finite-difference time-domain method are carried out to verify its effectiveness.

articleTitle: Explainable Planar Multiband Antenna Designer with Wasserstein Generative Adversarial Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In the antenna design process, predicting return loss via electromagnetic (EM) simulation is crucial for understanding the antenna's behavior. As EM simulation can be time-intensive, its role is often confined to simulating the response, and not extended to proposing alternative designs. To address this, we propose a novel artificial intelligence (AI) framework for antenna design. It comprises a regressor for accurate and fast response prediction, a generative designer for proposing a vast number of new designs that meet users' requirements, and an explainer for analyzing the impact of design parameters. Application of the proposed AI framework to the design of planar multiband antennas has demonstrated its accuracy and capability.

articleTitle: Drone-Measurement-Based Antenna Analysis: Multipath Effects on Radiation Patterns
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This study explores the multipath effects on the radiation pattern measurements of a fan-shaped beam right-handed circularly polarized antenna, tailored for diversity applications in satellites operating at a central frequency of 19 GHz. Utilizing a Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV), we measure the radiation pattern at three elevation angles, inducing different scenarios with different obstacles. Our results demonstrate that various obstacles, including the ground, contribute to multipath, significantly distorting the radiation pattern characteristics like main beam and side lobe levels.

articleTitle: Adjoint Sensitivity Analysis Based on Well-Conditioned Asymptotic Waveform Evaluation for Fast Frequency Sweep
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The well-conditioned asymptotic waveform evaluation (WCAWE) method is incorporated into adjoint sensitivity analysis for fast frequency sweep (FFS). The WCAWE method is a model order reduction (MOR) technique, which can quickly calculate the approximate results of all frequency points by using the solution of a single frequency point. The WCAWE-based adjoint sensitivity analysis avoids repeatedly solving linear matrices with different frequencies, which greatly reduces the computational cost. In order to verify the accuracy of WCAWE-based adjoint sensitivity analysis, a ultrawideband (UWB) antenna is simulated and analyzed. The simulation results show that the computational time required for the FFS is only 14.8% of the discrete frequency sweep.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Defected Ground Structure Antenna for 6G and Beyond Cellular Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a dual-band antenna using defected ground structures (DGS) is presented to operate on 20 GHz and 28 GHz bands with a footprint of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$10\times 10\times 0.76\ \text{mm}^{3}$</tex>. The frequency band-I is from 19.6-20.6 GHz, and Band-II is from 21.4-31.9 GHz because of integrating DGS square-ring slots in the partial ground. The realized gain at 20.32 GHz is 3.11 dBi and at 27.488 GHz is 4.74 dBi with an omnidirectional radiation pattern. The antenna efficiency is above 80% in both bands. The proposed antenna is well-suited for the 6G and beyond networks, wireless hotspots and short-range wireless links in smart cities.

articleTitle: Compressive Sensing Based Cyclic Autocorrelation Estimation Through the Sparsity
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The performance of cyclic autocorrelation (CA) estimation based on compressed sensing (CS) in non-stationary signal processing is affected by the value of time lag. A methodology for updated value of time lag constrained by sparsity (S-CS-CA) is proposed by this paper, which could result an appropriate parameter for CA estimation under sparse sampling. Selected experiments results are provided to assess the potentialities and features of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Backward to Forward Radiating Leaky Wave Antenna on a Half Mode Corrugated SIW
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The paper presents a backward-to-forward beam scanning leaky wave antenna (LWA) with enhanced gain based on a via-less half mode corrugated substrate integrated waveguide (HMCSIW). Two off center longitudinal slots are optimized to match the impedance over frequency without any open stop band and continuous scanning. Grooved step-down profile of corrugation has been realized to achieve low SLL. The proposed antenna is shown to operate from 24.5 to 32 GHz with a peak gain of 15 dBi and beam scanning of -54° to 20° and can be used for applications in Beyond-5G communications.

articleTitle: An Investigation of Microwave Imaging with Metasurfaces Performing Analog Computations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper investigates the application of analogcomputing metasurfaces to the microwave imaging (MWI) problem. The metasurface is designed to output a field quantity that is equivalent to the contrast of the object being imaged (OI). We show simulation results for single illumination imaging with a low-contrast target under the Born approximation.

articleTitle: Beamformer Calibration with Distributed Reference Noise for the ALPACA Imaging Array
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: For wide-field astronomical phased array feeds, accurate beamformer calibration is required. Temperature variations and other environmental factors cause drifts in the phase and amplitude responses of the analog front end and RF- over-fiber signal transport system. To correct for these drifts and eliminate gain reductions and pattern drift in the formed beams, we have developed a distributed noise reference system that allows phase and amplitude recalibration. To validate the system, we use the reference system to correct the phase in a signal transport channel for the Advanced L-band Phased Array Camera for Astronomy (ALPACA) with a length of fiber inserted to mimic phase drifts.

articleTitle: Development of a Compact Terahertz Band Absorber with Enhanced Q-Factor for Biomedical Applications Requiring High Sensitivity
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Meta-materials-based absorbers (MMA) have attracted significant attention due to their impressive absorption properties, making them well-suited for terahertz (THz) band sensing and high-speed communication applications. This paper introduces a novel multiband absorber tailored for the THz band, specifically emphasizing enhancing its quality factor (Q-factor) for biomedical sensing applications. The antenna exhibits improved absorption characteristics when operating on a polyamide substrate with gold for both the ground and patch materials. Simulation results highlight a notable enhancement in the Q-factor of 130. These findings signify a technical advancement and hold promise for propelling THz applications forward, particularly in the domain of biomedical sensing.

articleTitle: Experimental Assessment of Energy Harvesting in 868 MHz Indoor Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) are relevant for many applications ranging from environmental monitoring to security and human health, but require efficient power man-agement to ensure long-lasting networks. Energy Harvesting of Radio-Frequency (RF) available energy in the surroundings can help retrieve the necessary power. Furthermore, in indoor environments, a strong variability of the propagation channel due to multipath effects is present. This study faces an experimental evaluation to analyze the available power distribution in indoor settings when considering an 868 MHz WSN. The probability density function of the received signal voltage at each position provides insights into potential energy collection associated with the exposure time and relative location of the energy source and sensor node.

articleTitle: Ultra-Wide Band Antipodal Vivaldi Antenna with a Metamaterial Structure for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents an ultra-wide band antipodal Vivaldi antenna that is designed to operate across a frequency range from 15 GHz to 40 GHz, making it suitable for 5G, mm-wave bands, microwave imaging, and IoT applications. The unique features of this antenna include circular cuts and a metamaterial structure, which improve input reflection coefficient and gain. Finally, the ultra-wide band antipodal Vivaldi antenna was experimentally validated and showed a good correlation with simulation results in terms of input reflection coefficient with a −10 dB level ranging from 15 GHz to 40 GHz.

articleTitle: A Dielectric Linear-to-Circular Polarization Converter Exploiting Uniaxial Anisotropy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A linear-to-circular polarization converter, consisting of a suitable arrangement of thin periodic airdielectric slabs, is presented. The uniaxial nature of the periodic structure, highlighted by the field propagation matrix representation, is exploited to perform the required field polarization conversion. The performances of the proposed polarizer are illustrated by analyzing the radiative performance in terms of impedance bandwidth, axial ratio and realized gain of a horn and a wideband planar slot lens antenna.

articleTitle: Efficient Neural-Network Based Solution of Integral Equations for Electromagnetic Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Existing neural network (NN) based methods for solving Maxwell's equations focus on partial differential equations (PDEs). Integral equations (IEs) are seldom studied in the machine learning framework. Furthermore, prevailing methods employ a multi-objective loss that separates the loss associated with PDEs from the related boundary conditions. In this work, we construct a physics-informed loss by integrating the loss from equations and boundary conditions, which greatly enhances the convergence performance of an NN-based solution. We also devise an NN architecture to facilitate accurate and efficient learning. Equally applicable to PDEs, we underscore the success of proposed work in solving both surface- and volume-based IEs for electromagnetic analysis.

articleTitle: An Acceleration Method for Ray-Tracing in Modeling Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface Propagation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents an acceleration method for the reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) coverage model based on the image method. The approach constructs multipath clusters on the basis of dynamically partitioning RIS subarrays, significantly reducing the number of rays required for RIS propagation modeling. This compression leads to a model that combines high simulation accuracy with computational efficiency. By simulating a typical RIS propagation process, the proposed acceleration method is analyzed with regard to the relationship between the size of RIS subarrays and prediction accuracy.

articleTitle: Longitudinally Slotted Substrate Integrated Waveguide Leaky-Wave Antenna in Low-Temperature Co-Fired Ceramic Substrate
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
