abstract: A slotted substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) leaky-wave antenna (LWA) in a low-temperature co-fired ceramic substrate for 79 GHz band is investigated The antenna is categorized as a periodic leaky-wave antenna (PLWA). The antenna is designed so that -1st order space harmonic radiates into the backward quadrant. This leads to the achievement of a wide scan angle in a limited bandwidth. The design of the antenna with 100 series radiating slots is demonstrated. The simulated beam scan angle of the designed antenna is 28.3 degrees over the bandwidth from 77 GHz to 81 GHz.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Based Radio Environment Map Construction for Cellular Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Radio environment maps (REMs) can characterize a parameter of interest in a communication channel such as the reference signal received power (RSRP) at every point in a given geographical region. High-precision REMs have substantial potential for managing wireless resources and monitoring the spectrum. In this work, we explore various machine learning (ML) models, including an ensemble approach, to construct REMs by first estimating RSRP values in a long-term evolution (LTE) network. The simulation results indicate that the proposed ensemble approach exhibits great accuracy in RSRP estimation in LTE networks.

articleTitle: RF Transparent Coatings for Conformal Circuits
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Additive manufacturing (AM) has enabled the usage of nontraditional surfaces and form-factors when designing radio frequency (RF) electronics. Traditional fabrication techniques of RF electronics require less attention towards surface roughness of the substrate because the deposited copper is etched away from the surface. However, AM techniques, such as Direct Ink writing, require smooth printing surfaces to ensure proper deposition of the utilized ink and durability of the device. Conformal surfaces also require a method to protect the integrated circuitry from abrasion and corrosion. To meet these needs, expanding the capabilities of additive manufacturing techniques is necessary. This research describes various methods for applying RF compatible polymers to decrease the surface roughness of these substrates and provide circuit encapsulations. The developed methods and materials have shown increased stability and resilience for flexible heterogeneous circuits utilizing modern IC package technology.

articleTitle: Space Diversity Performance Analysis for S/Ka Band Communication in Tunnel Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, the space diversity performance of 5G-R communication in S band and 38 GHz millimeter-wave communication in Ka band under the tunnel environment of high-speed maglev train are modeled and simulated. The simulation result shows that 38 GHz millimeter-wave communication has higher and smoother received signal power over distance under the condition of same antenna aperture. The result also shows maximal ratio combining has better performance than selection combining, which could provide more stable communication.

articleTitle: Improvement of the Multifactorial Stability of the Wavelia#2 Microwave Breast Imaging Scanner: Towards Enhanced Scan Repeatability Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this article, the technical developments carried out on the second-generation prototype of the Wavelia™ Microwave Breast Imaging (MWBI) scanner, aiming to improve the stability of the measurements, are presented. The measurements variability results from the combination of several sources of errors, and their mitigation is key for performing repeatable scans. The progress made in terms of measurement stability, evaluated during the preparation of the ongoing clinical investigation with Wavelia#2, has been confirmed by repeated scans and imaging results of anthropomorphic breast phantoms.

articleTitle: Transparent ITO-Coated PET Based Wideband and Wideangle Microwave Absorber
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this document, a wide-band transparent microwave absorber is proposed. The proposed absorber consists of two patterned layers and one continuous layer of resistive ITO (Indium Tin Oxide)-coated PET (Ployethylene Teraphthalate) sheets. The design is simple, and hence it offers ease of fabrication. The proposed absorber exhibits more than 95% absorption for 4.13 GHz-25.17 GHz and more than 90% absorption for 3.60 GHz-26.90 GHz, covering C, X, Ku and K bands. The -15 dB bandwidth and -10 dB bandwidth is 143.6% and 152.8% respectively. More than 95% absorption is maintained up to incident angle 30° and more than 90% absorption is maintained up to 45°, for both TE and TM modes. The structure is polarization-insensitive due to its 4-fold symmetry.

articleTitle: Design of Metamaterial Wave-Absorbing Sensor Based on Improved Ant Colony Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: To address the limitations of traditional metamaterial wave-absorbing sensor methods that rely on manual design and optimization, consuming significant time and computer resources, this paper proposes the design of metamaterial wave-absorbing sensors with high absorption and high quality factor (Q-factor) based on an improved ant colony optimization algorithm. Electromagnetic simulation results demonstrate that the proposed metamaterial wave-absorbing sensor achieves a remarkable absorption rate of 99.98% at a frequency of 0.2752 THz and a Q-factor of 47.38, exhibiting robust frequency selectivity and stability against incident angles. The methodology not only mitigates the drawbacks of previous approaches but also holds significant potential for diverse applications in RF stealth and detection sensing.

articleTitle: Eco-Friendly Materials for Facile Sensors in Wearable Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Electronic waste (e-waste) production is increasing day by day, polluting the environment and causing life-threatening scenarios. Non-rechargeable batteries are a major source of e-waste because of the increasing demand for battery-powered devices. Here, we report the utilization of abandoned batteries in recycling to develop graphite-based conductive paste for textile-based flexible strain sensors. A modified interdigitated electrode (MIDE) structure is developed on fabric using a facile and solvent-free fabrication process. The strain sensors are utilized in wearable applications to monitor the movement of body joints at different angles. The sensors efficiently detect the stain applied by human wrist, knee, and elbow joints with high sensitivity GF > 350. The proposed facile paste from e-waste is a promising candidate for developing green electronics for wearable applications.

articleTitle: Stable Solutions of Transient Electromagnetic Scattering by Penetrable Objects Based on Time-Domain Müller Equations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Electromagnetic (EM) interaction with homoge-neous penetrable objects are usually described by Poggio-Miller-Chang-Harrington-Wu-Tsai (PMCHWT) equations. The Müller equations (MEs) can also be used to describe the same problem but they are less addressed although they are free of spurious solutions and hypersingularity. For transient problems, the time-domain MEs (TDMEs) are proposed so that the merits of MEs can be explored. Also, the TDMEs are solved by a hybrid scheme in which the Nyström method is used to discretize the space domain while the Galerkin's method is employed to discretize the time domain. The former can simplify the implementation while the latter can remove the late-time instability. Numerical examples demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the approach.

articleTitle: A Compact Self-Duplex Antenna for Leadless Pacemakers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a compact and highly isolated two-port leadless pacemaker duplex antenna, operating at 915 MHz (when Port-1 is active) and 1300 MHz (when Port-2 is active). For compactness, a high-dielectric substrate, shorting pins, and capacitive slots are used. A high isolation level between the transmit and receive units is obtained by etching rectangular slots on the ground plane and introducing a series of vias between them. Consequently, the designed antenna has a compact size of π × 4.48<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> × 0.13 = 8.19 mm3 and a high isolation level of 34.6 dB. It maintains a suitable gain of -25.6 dBi at 915 MHz (when Port-1 is active) and -19.7 dBi at 1300 MHz (when Port-2 is active). The suggested design is suitable for wireless leadless pacemakers, thanks to its compact design, highly isolated uplink and downlink wireless channels, and high gains.

articleTitle: Experimental Validation of a Cylindrical Antenna Applied to Omega 360 Ubiquitous 4D Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper is focused on the features obtained with a cylindrical antenna. This antenna is applied to an ubiquitous 4D radar, called Omega 360, capable of a rose of adjacent simultaneous staring beams which allow a continuous tri-dimensional coverage of the controlled space. The signal received by every column of the array is amplified, digitally down converted, and combined to form independent simultaneous beams in azimuth that are continuously tilted in elevation. The configuration of the antenna creates 192 simultaneous beams which make possible the ubiquitous surveillance over 360 degrees. Attention is paid to the measured values of the antenna pattern characteristics after Digital Beam Forming. An experimental result with the OMEGA360 radar confirms the validity of a cylindrical antenna with ubiquitous surveillance to obtain an extremely long period of observation which is essential for the search, classification, and recognition of small, slow and light (SLL) drones.

articleTitle: mmWave Phased-Array Antenna Modules
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: By designing low-loss interconnects with low mutual couplings, compact power dividers/combiners, and multi-layer antennas that utilize artificially perfect magnetic conductors, stacked patches/rings, and LGA airgap, high-performance phased array antenna modules are developed. The modules operate over 57–71 GHz, or 24–44 GHz. Based on the phase shifter resolution, a set of phases/amplitudes are optimized to maximize gain and coverage while minimizing the latency. Heatmap diagrams are shown to represent beam selections and its deviation with the ideal case. By manipulating phase/amplitude of front-end blocks, semi-omni radiation patterns are achieved for link initiation, side-lobe levels are reduced, and ideal far-field feed sources are realized for reflector antennas. To experimentally analyze the performance, connectorized evaluation boards were designed and implemented. The outputs of these modules were later used to define the realized gain of the antennas. The antenna modules were evaluated in different anechoic chambers, including a compact antenna test range chamber. The measured results were compared with simulation achievements, showing excellent agreements with EIRPs up to 48 d <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B$</tex> m over 57–71 GHz, and 51 d <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B$</tex> m over 24–44 GHz. The radiation patterns are stable over the entire bandwidth and the beam can be scanned up to±60° with less than 4 d <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$B$</tex> gain drop.

articleTitle: SAR Investigation on 2.1 GHz Microstrip Antenna with Different Patch Size and Grounding
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This article presents a microstrip antenna with a modified patch size and ground that operates at 2.1 GHz. The initial size of the patch is decreased, following the implementation of slots at the patch and ground, to enhance the gain and efficiency of the antenna. The antenna is designed using a Rogers RT/Duroid 5880 substrate with a coaxial feeding technique. The optimized antenna performs well in terms of reflection coefficient, gain, and efficiency, which are -37.35 dB, 2.544 dBi, and 77.46%, respectively. In addition, the designed antennas are positioned 10 mm distance from the head phantom with a fixed excitation power of 20.41 dBm for the SAR investigation. This study demonstrates that the small patch and ground sizes improve the antenna performance, which subsequently lead to the increasing of SAR. All the designs and studies are performed via the use of CST Microwave Studio.

articleTitle: Compact Anti-Metal Tag Antenna Loaded with Four Parasitic Capacitive Patches
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Miniaturization technique by incorporating a tag antenna with multiple loaded parasitic patches is proposed. Here, the reactance of the tag antenna is increased by loading it with multiple parasitic patches on the same surface. By making the antenna capacitive, a compact tag antenna with a miniature size <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(30\ \text{mm}\ \times 30\ \text{mm}\ \times 1.6\ \text{mm}\ \text{or}\ 0.0915\lambda\times 0.0915\lambda)\times 0.0049\lambda)$</tex> is designed for anti-metal applications. It has been demonstrated that the tag resonant frequency can be significantly reduced by appending the antenna structure with four capacitive patches. A tag prototype has been fabricated, and it achieves a maximum read range of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 8.4\mathrm{m}$</tex> with 4W EIRP when mounted on metal.

articleTitle: Inverse Scattering Problem with Multi-Frequency Data and Evanescent Wave as Incident Field
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The inverse scattering problem is well known and studied in the literature, especially with far-zone data, i.e., with scatterers in the radiation zone. This paper addresses the near- zone inverse scattering problem with an evanescent wave as the illuminating field. In details, we studied the linearized near-field scattering operator for mono-dimensional inhomogeneous media from multi-frequency data in a 2D configuration. Using estab-lished mathematical results, the eigenspectrum of the operator is derived in closed form.

articleTitle: High-Selectivity Circularly Polarized Frequency Selective Surface with Ultralow Profile and Continuous Phase Modulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, an ultrathin circularly polarized (CP) high-selectivity frequency selective surface (FSS) with continuous phase modulation is proposed. Based on an antenna-filter-antenna (A-F -A) structure, two circular patches etched with rectangular slots and a stripline filter are cascaded to achieve high roll-off and high selectivity characteristics of FSS. On the other hand, conventional high-selectivity FSS rarely focuses on phase modulation. Continuous and precise phase modulation can be implemented by rotating the A patch in this design. An FSS element operating in the C-band is analyzed and simulated. The results show that this CP FSS, with a thickness of only 0.077 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda$</tex>, implements a high-selectivity bandpass response along with good phase modulation. The proposed design can be applied to communication systems to improve electromagnetic compatibility, effectively control interference, and optimize signal transmission.

articleTitle: In-Body Antenna for Biomedical Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This study presents the design and simulation of a miniaturized in-body antenna tailored for biomedical applications. The significance of this study lies in the critical miniaturization of in-body antennas, contributing to enhanced patient outcomes by reducing implant rejection and minimizing patient discomfort. Moreover, the developed antenna facilitates the timely identification of diseases at their initial stages, underscoring its potential impact in the realm of biomedical research and health care. The overall size achieved for the antenna is 3 mm x 3 mm x 0.5 mm after modification in the shape ground and patch, addition of superstrate and adjustment in the position of coaxial feed. The antenna demonstrated an operating frequency of 5.8 GHz within the ISM band, accompanied by a return loss of -25.39 dB and a gain of -20.06 dBi in free space. The overall efficiency calculated is -21.06 dB, with radiation efficiency -21.11 dB in free space. For validation of in body environment, the antenna is placed inside the simplified human body model.

articleTitle: Shape Quality Factor for Bilinear Surfaces in Method of Moment Solution of Surface Integral Equations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Definition of the shape quality factor is extended to arbitrarily shaped bilinear surfaces, including concave and crossed ones. An application of the shape quality factor is demonstrated on the example of mesh refinement.

articleTitle: Electrodynamics of Accelerated Space-Time Engineered-Modulation Slabs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: We present an analytical resolution of the problem of an Accelerated Space-Time Engineered-Modulation (ASTEM) slab. For this purpose, we apply the tools of General Relativity and specifically consider a constant proper-acceleration, or Rindler, slab. We obtain closed-form solutions, whose different terms correspond to the intricate multiple/chirped scattered waves traveling in the slab. Such a solution represents an essential step in the future analysis of ASTEM crystals and may find wide applications in microwave and optical chirp-based devices.

articleTitle: Bandwidth Enhancement by High Permittivity Substrate for Microstrip Antenna with Small Ground Plane
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Microstrip antennas (MSAs) exhibit a wider bandwidth when using substrates with a lower permittivity in general. Low permittivity realizes a large volume of the radiating element and brings a low Q-factor. However, it was found that the bandwidth may be wider when using a substrate having a high permittivity if the ground conductor is as small as the radiating element. In this paper, the bandwidth of MSA is discussed with the permittivity of the substrate and the size of the ground plane as parameters. MSA is designed at 30 GHz with the ground plane which size is 4.5 mm × 4.5 mm. A lower unloaded Q-factor (Qu) of 10.2 is obtained when using a higher relative permittivity <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varepsilon_{\mathrm{r}}$</tex> of 4 than <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Q_{\mathbf{U}}$</tex> of 17.2 by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varepsilon_{\mathrm{r}}$</tex> of 1. In the same way, a wider bandwidth of 14.4% is obtained for a return loss of -10 dB or less with the higher permittivity than 8.3% with the lower permittivity.

articleTitle: Enhancing Beam Steering Performance Using Phased Array Technology for FWA Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a compact beam steerable fully dielectric reflector antenna for FWA application. It consists of a fully dielectric reflector illuminated by a probe-fed 2X2 circular patch antenna array. A peak realized gain of 28.6 dBi and 50.41% aperture efficiency are achieved at 27 GHz. To achieve beam steering the array is moved along the azimuth plane and a scan range of ±23° is obtained with a −1.2 dB scan loss.

articleTitle: A Novel Super Resolution Method Using One Bit Channel Time Reversal
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, we introduce an novel method to address the challenge of dense multi-channel communication. By employing the time reversal technique and the CLEAN algorithm, we can actively control the peak voltage of pulses. Simulation trials are conducted in a multipath environment using a configuration with a single transmit antenna and three receive antennas. Within the setup of three <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{0.0333}\lambda$</tex> spaced antennas, the central receiving antenna achieves an impressive resolution of 2.7576 dB. Simultaneously, our proposed method enhances the antenna gain on both sides by 19.14 dB.

articleTitle: Bridging the Digital Divide through Public and Community Wi-Fi
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The “Digital Divide” is the gap between those who have “Access” to communication technology and information and those who don't. In this paper, the role of public and community Wi-Fi in reducing this gap is reviewed.

articleTitle: IEEE Milestones in Antennas and Propagation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Since its inception in 1983, the IEEE Milestones program has become IEEE's most valuable intangible asset. As of the end of 2023,270 Milestones have been approved and dedicated. At present, however, relatively few existing Milestones fall within the field of interest of the IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society. Here we review these existing Milestones, identify gaps and omissions, and propose a strategy by which the Antennas and Propagation Committee can increase the number of Milestones relevant to the society while remaining true to the program's goal of being a grassroots movement.

articleTitle: A Novel Efficient Ray-Tracing Method for Designing Non-Resonant Partially Reflective Surface Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Non-resonant partially-reflective surface (PRS) antennas present promising alternatives in antenna design. This paper tackles the intricacies of their design by introducing a novel, efficient ray-tracing method for computing compensation phases. Emphasizing simplicity without sacrificing effectiveness, our approach is validated through Ansys HFSS simulations, confirming practicality and performance. The proposed method streamlines the non-resonant PRS antenna design process, highlighting the importance of accessible methodologies in advancing antenna technology.

articleTitle: An Additively Manufactured mm-Wave Foldable and Bend-Resilient Interconnect for Morphing RF
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A fully additively manufactured foldable mm-wave dual-band antenna operating at 28 GHz and 35 GHz is presented. The inkjet-printed structure utilizes a foldable interconnect design that can be bent repeatedly without mechanical degradation. The RF performance of the fabricated prototype is characterized at different bend angles, and mechanical reliability is demonstrated over repeated bend cycles.

articleTitle: Holographic Inspire Reflectarray for Orbital Angular Momentum Multiplexing Using Optimization Based on Support Vector Regression
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This work introduces a design methodology for reflectarrays based on holographic theory to generate multiple Orbital Angular Momentum (OAM) modes at the same operating frequency, enabling OAM multiplexing. This methodology directly provides the element geometry for dual-polarized multi-feed configurations. To do so, the holographic theory is combined with Support Vector Regression (SVR) models of the unit cell to fully characterize the element response. A numerical example of a reflectarray fed by two feeders to generate four OAM modes is presented, reaching a high degree of purity in each of them.

articleTitle: A Novel Miniaturized Conformal Antenna for Bluetooth-Enabled Hearing-Aid Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The use of hearing aids is one of the primary methods for individuals with hearing loss to regain perception of the world. Bluetooth hearing aids operating in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2.4\sim2.5$</tex> GHz frequency range have gained popularity among manufacturers and users. To address the challenges in Bluetooth antenna design for hearing aids, we have developed a novel, cost-effective, and miniaturized conformal antenna. This paper presents the simulation data for this antenna. Furthermore, we have fabricated and manufactured this antenna, and the hearing aid equipped with this antenna has demonstrated satisfactory Bluetooth working range, validating the effectiveness of our design.

articleTitle: Manufacturing Approaches for Experimental Validation of Numerically Designed Conformal Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Three manufacturing approaches for numerically designed conformal metasurfaces are presented. A fabricated antenna of each approach is shown along with simulated and measured results., which strongly validate the numerical design methods used.

articleTitle: An Optically Transparent and Flexible Ultrawideband Metasurface-Based Linear-to-Circular Polarization Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: An optically transparent & adaptable metasurface intended for ultrawideband linear to circular polarization (LCP) conversion is presented in this work. The metasurface, composed of an indium tin oxide (ITO)-based elliptical ring pattern on a polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) substrate with a polyethylene-terephthalate (PET) supportive layer, addresses the narrow bandwidth and angle insensitivity issues associated with traditional flexible metasurface. Simulated results show an axial ratio <3dB within a 70% fractional bandwidth (12.92 to 25.96) and sustained LCP performance at a 25° oblique incident angle. Moreover, a conformally bent array of 5×5-unit cells exhibit stable axial ratio performance under different radii of curvature (Ψ). The proposed LTC polarization converter is simple to design and fabricate, showing great promise for practical applications as a circularly polarized wave generator.

articleTitle: Investigations on Radiation Behavior of Single-Mode Resonant Sectorial Monopole Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The radiation behavior of the single-mode resonant (@2.4 GHz) sectorial monopole antenna is studied in this paper. At first, a compact, sectorial monopole antenna operating at TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3/5,1</inf> mode within flared angle of 150<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">○</sup> is designed. Then, the relationship between the position of feeding points and radiation characteristic in xy-plane is investigated and analyzed. It is revealed that the antenna could exhibit omnidirectional or backfire radiation characteristic by adjusting the ratio ϒ= x0/R0, where xo is the feeding position and Ro is the radius of the monopole. As is validated, the gain non-uniformity within the azimuth plane deteriorates and the antenna tends to exhibit backfire radiation as ϒ increases.

articleTitle: Field-Conformal Septa in Circular Waveguides
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper introduces an innovative approach to waveguide polarizer design, utilizing field-conformal septa. The septa can be either dielectric or conducting, to enhance polarization control, and depending on the required application. The key enabler of this design approach is the advent of high-precision 3D printing technology, allowing for the accurate fabrication of complex, field-conformal shapes tailored to specific waveguide requirements. A detailed analysis based full-wave simulations is presented. This paper demonstrate the potential of field-conformal septa to significantly facilitate the design and improve the performance of waveguide polarizers.

articleTitle: Dual-Polarized Anomaly Detection System Based on Millimeter-Wave Lens Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Security in today's society is constantly under threat. Human anomaly detection refers to the identification of whether a person is carrying hidden objects, which is in high demand. Current human security methods include manual and machine detection, which have issues with efficiency and cost. Taking advantage of the excellent penetrability of millimeter-waves, we designed a dual-polarized human anomaly detection system based on lens antennas. In addition, we introduce cross-polarization to obtain polarization rotation information. By comparing the different polarization signals in the echo signal, we can realize the detection of hidden objects.

articleTitle: A Periodic Slotline Leak-Wave Antenna with Bidirectional Radiation and Continuous Scanning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a slotted frequency beam-scanning antenna with bidirectional radiation. To achieve continuous backward-to-forward beam scanning, seven pairs of periodic modulated slot elements are added to the slotline. Additionally, the use of double slots enhances the radiation gain level by forming a binary array. Transversal asymmetric structures provide an excellent impedance match and effectively suppress the open stopband (OSB) phenomena. The proposed slotline leaky-wave (LWA) antenna prototype was fabricated and tested for experimental validation. The measured results indicate the LWA can scan from −35° through broadside to 11° with the band varied from 4.2 to 6.6 GHz. The measured maximum gain reaches 12.5 dBi at 5.9 GHz. The experimental results further prove that the OSB issue has been solved successfully.

articleTitle: Design of an RF Touch Sensor for On-Body Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: We propose an RF touch sensor based on split-ring resonators (SRRs) as a control device intended for integration with RF systems. Design optimization is performed using circuit-based and full-wave electromagnetic simulations. The results are validated by measurements of the fabricated prototype, emphasizing modeling challenges.

articleTitle: Compact Implantable Antenna Design for Leadless Cardiac Pacemaker System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper details an implantable antenna for leadless cardiac pacemaker (LCP) applications operating in the Industrial Scientific Medical (ISM) frequency band (2.4-2.48GHz). The antenna uses a shorting pin to achieve an improved simulated 10dB fractional bandwidth of 20%, compared to similar literature designs. It implements a spiral-shaped meander pattern in an ultra-compact 3×3×0.5 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> footprint. The calculated maximum specific absorption rate (SAR) values comply with IEEE C95.1-2005 and C95.1-1999 safety guidelines.

articleTitle: LPI/LPD Communications Using Antenna Arrays with Rapid Side Lobe Time Modulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: We present a method for realizing low probability of intercept/detect (LPI/LPD) secure communications. The proposed method relies on the rapid side-lobe time modulation (SLTM) achieved by a linear antenna array providing fast beam forming and shaping. Leveraging the SLTM, the signal transmitted in the side-lobe directions is scrambled while the signal in the main lobe direction is not significantly changed. We also design a 1-bit reconfigurable patch antenna, embedded with two high-speed PIN diode switches, as the array element. By pseudorandomly and alternatively controlling the array elements at high speed, the signal radiated from the SLTM array is unchanged in the main lobe direction but is completely distorted along the side-lobe directions.

articleTitle: Some Often Overlooked Elements of Electromagnetic Information Theory
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: We comment on some elements of EIT that are often overlooked in the literature, but that could provide further insights in the application of the theory in practical settings.

articleTitle: Radar-based Human Pulse Sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: There has been an increased interest in the use of radars in wearables for human health monitoring. These applications are challenging both in terms of radar specifications, and physiological variance. CAD-generated digital twins have shown potential in generating datasets that could be fed to machine learning algorithms for detection and classification. This work demonstrates the feasibility of using numerical CAD tools to model pulse sensing using a commercial mm-wave radar. The time-domain reconstructed pulse waveforms had very good agreement with the input waveform, hence, this demonstrates the feasibility of using mm-Wave radars for pulse sensing and the potential of using digital twins for generating diverse datasets to train radars on the signatures of various diseases and health conditions.

articleTitle: A High Roll-Off, Wide Rejection FSS-Based Bandpass Filter for L-S Bands
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This study proposes a comprehensive investigation on the design of a high roll-off., wide rejection bandpass filter based on a multi-layered configuration of frequency selective surfaces (FSSs) with miniaturized elements. The filter is meant to operate in L-S bands., and it is conceived by extensively recurring to the transmission line theory. Specifically., the filter aim is to totally reject the L band., while guaranteeing a large passing band between 2 and 4 GHz. The filter's functionality relies on the combined action of two distinct FSSs. The first is represented by a standard grid., acting as a high-pass element., fundamental to reject the lower frequencies. Conversely., the other FSS is configured as a Hilbert unit-cell shape., acting as an extremely selective bandpass element. By performing full-wave simulations., this design demonstrated a bandpass response spanning from 2.2 to 3.7 GHz for TE polarization with maximum insertion loss of − 1.7 dB., for incidence angles up to 30°. Moreover., the filter exhibits a high roll-off with a transmission coefficient transition from −10 dB up to −1 dB in a span of 130 MHz.

articleTitle: 77 GHz SISL based Dual-circularly Polarized Filtenna for Automotive Radar Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this article, a dual-polarized antenna array has been deigned for 77 GHz automotive radar application. A three-pole Chebyshev bandpass filter has been designed ranging from 76.82-78.93 GHz. The filter has a sharpcut-off and a 3 dB bandwidth of 2.11 GHz. The filter has then been integrated into the antenna without expanding its footprint. The resulting structure shows a good filtering characteristics with S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> from 76.48-78.53 GHz, a gain of 13.52 dBi and an axial ratio bandwidth covering the entire impedance bandwidth.

articleTitle: Measuring the Noise Figure of Active Integrated Receivers Inside a Reverberation Chamber
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Measuring the noise figure is an important part of the development of sensitive radio receivers. This paper introduces a method to measure the noise figure of active integrated receivers inside a reverberation chamber. The method differs from others as it does not need a noise source. Measurements show an agreement of 0.3 dB between the reverberation chamber method and a reference measurement.

articleTitle: A mm-Wave 16 × 16 elements Near Field Array
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A 16 × 16 elements mm-wave near field (NF) focused array is designed with a compact two dielectric stackup. The feeding lines, whose lengths have been initially obtained by using conjugate phase approach have been subsequently refined by considering the actual geometry of the delay lines. The feeding network is connected to radiating patches through vias. The near field electric field distribution computed by using the analytical procedure agrees well with CST results ones that the lengths of delay lines are corrected by considering realistic effects of phase non-linearity and amplitude drop.

articleTitle: Design of a Compact Combined OAM Modes Uniform Circular Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents the design of an all-angular momentum (AAM) antenna array system to radiate OAM beams with combined modes. The antenna array has four elements which are sequentially rotated to set the phase difference between them. The individual element radiates a fourth-order left-hand circular polarized (LHCP) OAM beam which is combined with the angular momentum of the array. The orthogonality property of the OAM beam makes different modes to be transmitted independently along the same channel at a given frequency. The antenna resonates in the frequency range of 5.12GHz with a narrow band and is highly suitable for modes multiplexing of different data streams in high resolution and computational imaging with greater channel capacity and spectral efficiency.

articleTitle: Dual Band Millimeter-Wave Artificial Magnetic Conductor Based Antenna for 5G Wearable Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents a dual-band millimeter-wave (mmWave) planar dipole antenna featuring a via-integrated balun and backed by a dual-band artificial magnetic conductor (AMC). A novel dual-band AMC unit cell is designed to achieve zero-reflection phase at both 28 GHz and 38 GHz frequencies relevant to 5G communication. The dipole antenna is backed by a 2×2 AMC array to enhance gain and maintain low specific absorption rate (SAR) values below 1.6 W/Kg. Achieved gain exceeds 6.5 dBi in both frequency bands. Furthermore, this design utilizes a semi-flexible substrate, making it suitable for 5G mmWave wearable applications as well.

articleTitle: Improved Equivalent Circuit Model of p-i-n Diodes for Amplitude and Phase Controllable mmWave Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: An improved equivalent circuit model (ECM) of p-i-n diodes is developed and applied to amplitude and phase controllable mmWave reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs). The proposed ECM takes into account the variable junction resistance and capacitance of forward-biased p-i-n diodes in the transition state (instead of a conventional simplified resistance model) that is critical at mmWave frequencies. The flip-chip AlGaAs p-i-n diodes have been characterized in a 2-port coplanar measurement setup. Both the improved ECM and the electromagnetic model are constructed and validated. The ECM is used for a 28-GHz RIS design with amplitude and phase control of the reflection coefficient. The observed non-linear performance combined with an additional phase shift of up to 84° introduced by the variable junction capacitance indicates the value of the proposed model.

articleTitle: Four Element Dielectric Resonator Antenna Array with Quasi Antipodal Radiation Pattern for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This article presents the design results of a four element array of dielectric resonator antennas (DRA). The antenna geometry includes a conformal open-loop feed for each of the four elements. The four antenna elements, independently fed, aim to provide diversity in radiation patterns through the use of phase shifters at their ports. Electromagnetic simulation results show that the antenna has a bandwidth of 464 MHz (3.37 - 3.81 GHz), which is suitable for fifth-generation (5G) mobile communication applications. The isolation between the antenna ports is greater than 10 dB across the entire operating bandwidth. Antipodal radiation patterns across the entire band exhibit directional changes when phase shifts of 0 degrees, 90 degrees, 270 degrees, and 360 degrees are interleaved.

articleTitle: Non-Intrusive Polynomial Chaos Expansion for Uncertainty Quantification in Specific Absorption Rate Calculations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Specific absorption rate (SAR) is the metric applied for evaluating human exposure to electromagnetic fields, particularly in the context of wireless communication technologies. The non-intrusive polynomial chaos (NIPC) expansion method is proposed as an efficient solution to systematically investigate and quantify uncertainties associated with computational SAR assessments. By treating indeterminate parameters as stochastic variables represented as polynomial chaos expansions, the NIPC expansion method provides a structured framework for studying the stochastic characteristics inherent in SAR values. Through meticulous simulations that account for variations in the dielectric properties of the tissue equivalent liquid used for SAR compliance assessment, such as the relative permittivity and the conductivity, the methodology adeptly captures uncertainties, yielding profound insights into the nuanced distribution of SAR values and their associated probabilities.

articleTitle: Contribution of Prof. L. B. Felsen to the Theory of Time-Domain Floquet Waves
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: We describe the theory of time domain Floquet waves that is one of the several contributions of Prof. Leopold B. Felsen to the literature. The results provide an intriguing interpretation of wave phenomena when short pulses are in-volved in periodic materials, leading to time domain Floquet waves arising all from the same directions and having different instantaneous frequencies. Here, we briefly review the theory and provide examples. During the oral presentation, We will also discuss the link between the physics of time domain Floquet waves and the waves involved in the recent topic of time crystals.

articleTitle: Wideband Low-Loss Feed Design for the DSA-2000 Ambient Temperature Array in Radio Astronomy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The Deep Synoptic Array (DSA-2000) is the next generation ground-based radio astronomical array that will consist of 2000×5 m reflectors equipped with an ambient temperature feed package and electronics covering 0.7-2 GHz. The quad-ridge choke horn (QRCH) feed developed for the DSA-2000 is a wideband, low-loss, and low-cost design providing a wide radiation pattern to illuminate the deep prime-focus reflector. We present the predicted noise temperature contributions for the feed, low-noise amplifiers, and surrounding brightness - resulting in a remarkable 25 K system noise at ambient temperature.

articleTitle: A 2-Bit Phase Reconfigurable Aperture Coupled Pixel Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A novel 2-bit phase reconfigurable pixel antenna is proposed. By implementing multi-objective genetic algorithm (GA) optimization, two layers of parasitic pixel surfaces mounted with three switches are optimized to achieve a 90° phase shift. Integrated with another 1-bit aperture coupled patch radiator, the proposed pixel antenna can realize 2-bit phase reconfigurability. From 2.37 to 2.42 GHz, the phase differences of four states remain relatively stable with 2-bit phase distribution and a maximum radiation gain of 7.41 dBi. These results preliminarily verify the potential of utilizing pixel antennas to implement phase reconfiguration for beam steering applications.

articleTitle: Stable and Broadband Technique for Accurate Characterization of Dielectric Material
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The electromagnetic (EM) properties of dielectric material are extracted through experimental measurements conducted by using a vector network analyzer (VNA) and a waveguide system. The test sample was introduced into an X-band waveguide, and the scattering parameters were measured. A Nicolson-Ross-Weir (NRW) method is implemented to extract the electrical permittivity and the loss tangent. Furthermore, the phase ambiguity problem of the NRW algorithm is solved by implementing an iterative and stable technique correcting the phase shift of the propagation factor. Moreover, the NRW algorithms were compared with the NIST iterative method for validation.

articleTitle: Charge Pump Stage Optimization for 2.4 GHz/5.8 GHz Dual-Band Rectifier
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper simplifies the dual-band rectifier design at 2.4 GHz and 5.8 GHz by only using Skyworks SMS7630 Schottky diodes, high-Q capacitors, and 4 microstrip lines for tuning. The dual-band rectifiers with 2, 4, 6, and 8-stage charge pumps are simulated and optimized in Keysight Advanced Design System (ADS) on Rogers RO3003 substrate. Results showed that the 4-stage design presents the best option for a dual-band rectifier.

articleTitle: An Excitation Optimization Method for Edge Effects Suppression in Finite Ultrawideband Tightly Coupled Arrays for Wideband Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, an effective post-processing complex excitations optimization method is proposed for the suppression of edge truncation effects in finite ultrawideband tightly coupled antenna arrays (TCAAs) when transmitting a wideband signal. Based on the formulas in terms of active voltage standing wave ratio (VSWR) and array gain patterns, a non-convex optimization problem in terms of complex excitations for joint consideration of array gain and active ARC as well as amplitude dynamic range ratio (DRR) are established within a desired instantaneous signal bandwidth. By the use of quadratic operations and first-order expansions, the non-convex problem can be effectively addressed by transforming it into a sequence of interconnected convex problems. The simulated results of a 6×10 TCAA operating at 0.2GHz-2GHz show that the maximum active VSWR of all array element are suppressed to be less than or equal to 3.05 within a 200MHz instantaneous signal bandwidth.

articleTitle: Investigating Temperature Dependency of Dielectric Properties in Grey and White Matter for Brain Phantoms: A Preliminary Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Oil-in-gelatin dispersion tissue mimicking materials are widely used in literature during proof-of-concept studies for hyperthermia, non-invasive temperature monitoring and simulation models. Therefore it is essential to list their temperature dependency behavior. In this work, white and grey matter of the brain tissue mimicking phantom is manufactured and its temperature dependency is investigated over a temperature span from 25 to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$50^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex> between 0.5 GHz – 10 GHz. The measured data is fitted in to two-pole temperature dependent Cole-Cole equation and temperature dependency is modeled by using second-order polynomials. The results indicates that these materials is able to imitate the temperature dependency of the biological tissues and can be used for testing applications where microwave electromagnetic waves interact with biological tissues.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic-Thermal Performance Trade-Offs in Phased Arrays with Shaped Elevation Patterns
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Both thermal and electromagnetic performance of substrate-integrated waveguide (SIW) and microstrip line-fed shaped-beam arrays with slot and patch radiating elements are conducted. Three array types operating at 26 GHz band, namely SIW slot array, SIW array with patches, and proximity coupled patch array, are considered. The array performances regarding shaped radiation pattern stability with frequency and maximal temperature at the power amplifier chips are discussed. The study highlights intriguing trade-offs between radiation pattern performance and cooling ability in phased arrays.

articleTitle: A Miniature Low-Profile MHMIC Antenna Array For Millimeter-Wave Identification Readers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a high directive miniature 60-GHz 8-by-1 microstrip antenna array is presented and analyzed. To achieve a reduced size and ease of integration into MMID reader devices, the proposed antenna array has been designed on a thin ceramic substrate <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\varepsilon_{r}=9.9,\ h=127\mu\mathrm{m})$</tex>, using an MHMIC (Miniature Hybrid Microwave Integrated Circuits) fabrication process. The proposed array configuration has exhibited excellent performance in terms of realized gain (peak gain of 14 dB) and radiation efficiency (around 75%). All those features make it a suitable candidate for integrated MMID readers to locate transponders in high-density sensor networks.

articleTitle: Octa-Port MIMO Antenna System for 5G Smartphone Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper presents an octa-port MIMO antenna system for applications of the smartphone. A single element consists of an L-shaped patch and a partially defected ground system (DGS). The operating frequency of the proposed compact antenna is 28 GHz, offering a 10-dB impedance bandwidth of almost 4 GHz without using any decoupling structures and maintaining a compact size of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$37.7 \times 90.3\text{mm}^{2}$</tex>. The MIMO parameters of the stated system fall within the required range, certifying that the device is a suitable candidate for 5G applications.

articleTitle: A Wideband, Low Profile Antenna Array for mm-Wave 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a wideband, low-profile, 2 × 2 antenna array is designed and simulated which continuously covers the two commonly used mm-wave frequency bands (24–29 GHz and 37–43 GHz) required for the fifth and sixth generation of communication systems. The return loss of the array is above 10dB from 25GHz to 45GHz at all four ports for broadside radiation. The tightly coupled array is realized in a 6mm × 6mm area generating 3–7 dB gain over the entire frequency range. The total thickness of the array is 1.2mm and it can be simply fabricated by a low cost PCB manufacturing process.

articleTitle: A GRIN-Lens-Coupled Nonlinear Receiver for Ultra-Low-Energy Large-Area Millimeter-Wave Mobile Wireless Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This work presents a low-energy, low-cost beam-steering 1 Gbps receiver operating in the millimeter-wave (MMW) band and consuming 1.15 milliwatts (mW). The receiver comprises a 31 dBi GRIN lens antenna coupled to a 39 GHz Schottky diode detector and baseband amplifier. The inclusion of the lens provides passive gain which dramatically increases range for the same power consumption. Using 8b10b encoding, the receiver achieves 800 Mbps with an uncoded bit error rate (BER) of 1 ×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup> at a range of 3.7m from a 7dBm EIRP transmitter. BER is below 1 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup> for beam angles out to ±25° and 5 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup> out to ±50°. Results suggest that ultra-low-power Gbps MMW communications can be extended from centimetre-scale to meter-scale using pre-amplifying passive lens antennas.

articleTitle: Permittivity Determination of Polymers at 900 MHz Using the Transmission Line Method Coupled to a CSRR
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This study focuses on a complementary split ring resonator (CSRR) used to measure the permittivity of a dielectric material. The CSRR studied is etched in a ground plane and excited by coupling via a microstrip line. Its resonant frequency shifts when loaded with a material under test (MUT). Using commercial 3D electromagnetic simulation software, a numerical model linking the resonant frequency to the permittivity of the MUT is proposed. We have designed and validated this CSRR in the frequency band around 900MHz for the characterization of unknown permittivity of materials at this frequency such as polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) filled with carbon particles (5, 17 and 25<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>). Experimental results show that the permittivity can indeed be determined, then confirmed by the values obtained by the developed numerical model.

articleTitle: Reduction of Radiating Elements in a Plural Circular Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The reduction of radiating elements in a plural circular array antenna is proposed. The total excitation such as the current to each element is kept constant. Decreasing the element number on the outermost circular array, radiation patterns are analyzed. It was shown that Airy pattern was deformed gradually from the larger angle region, but the main beam is not changed even with the element decreased to 3.

articleTitle: Dual/Triple Frequency Bands Reconfigurable Monopole MIMO Loaded with SRR Metamaterial
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This work presents a triple/dual bands frequency reconfigurable metamaterial antenna. The antenna is implemented as a monopole antenna loaded with split ring resonators made of the metamaterial. P-I-N diodes are put in the gaps of two square split-ring resonators loading the monopole to provide a frequency-reconfigurable characteristic. The electromagnetic full wave simulation-supported design principles are provided. The findings demonstrate that an antenna may be changed to convert from a dual-band that are centered at 15.7 GHz and 17.5 GHz to triple bands that are at 13.8 GHz, 16.2 GHz, and 18.2 GHz. The antenna is also somewhat tiny (40*70 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>).

articleTitle: Gain Enhancement Using Superstrate of Microstrip Patch Antenna Array for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This article presents the design of a rectangular patch antenna array operating in the millimeter-wave range. The antenna is placed on a Rogers RT-duroid 5880 substrate with a dielectric constant of 2.2, ensuring resonance at approximately 28 GHz. The proposed work enhances the antenna's gain by placing a superstrate at a specific distance of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.5\ \lambda$</tex> from the radiator. This placement enables the reflection of electromagnetic waves between the two substrates and resulting in an overall gain enhancement. Consequently, the proposed method achieves a gain enhancement of around 2.3 dB, making it suitable for automotive applications in the mm-wave band.

articleTitle: Research and Implementation of S-Band Active Phased Array Antenna Beam-Forming System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, in order to solve the problem of frequency band discontinuity and dynamic delay in the detection and communication integrated system, we design an 8-element S-band wideband Vivaldi array antenna, and verified its reliability in S-band through simulation analysis. At the same time, the physical antenna is processed, and the beam control system platform is designed to realize the low sidelobe and wide zero trap. The test results show that at the selected test frequency, the test curve is consistent with the simulation curve. The sidelobe of the low-sidelobe scanning beam decreases obviously, and the zero trap widens from one point to an interval, which verifies the reliability of the array antenna system.

articleTitle: Radar Cross Section Enhancement in RFID Tags Using Inactive Redundant Elements
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach for Radar Cross Section (RCS) enhancement by incorporating inactive redundant traces on Radio-frequency Identification (RFID) tag circuit. Efforts were made to ensure that these redundant elements do not compromise the functionality of the circuits. Two RFID tag designs (meander and double spiral topology) were utilized in this work. Simulations on meander RFID and double spiral typologies reveal RCS enhancement of approximately 5 dBsm using a bistatic interrogator configuration while a gain of 0.45 dBsm was observed with a monostatic interrogator setup. This work will aid RFID tag design by providing a means to improve its RCS.

articleTitle: Fault Detection of Feeder Lines in DAS Systems Based on LFMCW
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: To address the challenge of timely fault localization in Distributed Antenna Systems (DAS), this paper introduces Linear Frequency Modulated Continuous Wave (LFMCW) radar technology into DAS diagnostics to facilitate the detection of feedline lengths (fault locations). The tests indicate that the system proposed herein can effectively accomplish feedline length measurement and fault detection.

articleTitle: Thermally Tunable Terahertz Bifunctional Metasurface Based on Indium Antimonide
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A metasurface with thermal tunability using Indium Antimonide (InSb) is proposed, showing dual functionalities of absorption and polarization conversion. In its metallic state at a temperature of 280K, the system operates as a single-band absorber, exhibiting a peak absorptance of 100% at the frequency of 0.408 THz which is composed of a InSb square with a cross-shaped hole array, a silica <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\text{SiO}_{2})$</tex> substrate, and a InSb film. It holds broad applicability for band-stop THz filters. In the insulating state of InSb at a temperature of 200K, the system functions as a cross-polarization converter, adept at transforming linear plane waves into their corresponding cross-polarized counterparts with high efficiency in the frequency range of 0.6-0.8 THz, composed of a one-dimensional gold (Au) strip array, a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{SiO}_{2}$</tex> substrate, and a gold (Au) film. The proposed metasurface emerges as a promising candidate for contemporary devices focused on polarization control.

articleTitle: Effect of Antenna Loading Conditions at Array Level: Investigation of an SKA-Low Prototype
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This study deals with the impact of the receiver input impedance on the response of the antennas composing an array, in particular for radio astronomical applications. The model used for the simulated antenna patterns assumes that the load impedance of all antennas is equal to a given reference impedance independent of frequency. The effect of this assumption on the antenna patterns, the radio frequency path calibration and the array total efficiency is investigated for the SKA-low prototype Array Verification System Version 2.0 (AAVS2.0).

articleTitle: Multi-Band 7.1/8.5/20/30-GHz Horn Antenna with Spline-Taper and Coaxial-Groove Walls
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper proposes a new horn antenna with a coaxial-groove structure using a spline-taper with small protrusion four bands of 7.1/8.5/20/30 GHz. This horn has a good VSWR and low cross-polarization characteristics at the designed frequencies, yet for 20/30 GHz the electric field is controlled to pass near the center without affecting the discontinuities near the aperture plane.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of a Dual Circularly Polarized Receiving Antenna Array for UHF Band
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper describes a receiving antenna array operating in dual circular polarization for innovative bistatic radar systems, with a specific focus on space debris detection application. The proposed solution, designed to operate at 412 MHz, comprises 19 circular patch antennas arranged in a hexagonal configuration to mitigate the effect of grating lobes. Each radiating patch has two slots sector notches on opposite sides and is coaxially fed in two different points to achieve both right-hand and left-hand circular polarizations. The results demonstrate a gain value of about 17 dBi and an Axial Ratio (AR) less than 3 dB inside the 16° Half Power Beamwidth (HPBW). The Side Lobe Level (SLL) has a value of approximately −17 dB. The radiation parameters of the array align with the specified requirements for the intended application.

articleTitle: Highly Selective Polarization Insensitive Wideband A-T-A Frequency Selective Rasorber
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This manuscript introduces a wideband, polarization-insensitive, highly selective frequency selective rasorber with A-T-A performance. The structure comprises three layers within two substrates. 10 dB Wideband absorption is provided by the proposed unit cell over the frequency ranges of 4.3 to 7.1 GHz and 8.2 to 11.4 GHz. The upper layer consists of lumped resistors that are responsible for the absorption. The bottom substrate consists of two layers that allow transmission at 7.61 GHz with a high level of selectivity with a 3 dB transmission band from 7.3 GHz to 7.9 GHz. The designed structure has been fabricated and assessed, and the measured outcomes correspond with the simulated results.

articleTitle: An Edge-Tapered Antipodal Beam Switching Antenna with 360° Azimuthal Beam Steering
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A low profile, compact, and wideband electronic beam-switching antenna (EBSA) array is presented that can scan 360° in the azimuthal plane by using only four switching states. This antenna array is pattern reconfigurable and planar, which confirms its suitability for wideband applications in the X/Ku band such as satellite, radar, and vehicular communications. The proposed design can produce almost a flat gain with a half-power beamwidth greater than 90°, requiring only 4 array elements for 360° beam switching. The proposed EBSA offers an impedance bandwidth of 60% while maintaining a mutual coupling below -30 dB between array elements. Gain is maintained between 6-8dBi with a slight fluctuation over the scanning angles and intended frequency band.

articleTitle: On the Regularization of the High Order Time Domain EFIE with Quasi-Helmholtz Projectors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this work, we present a quasi-Helmholtz projector-based preconditioning and stabilization of the time domain electric field integral equation when discretized with high-order basis functions and high-order convolution quadrature schemes. The proposed approach effectively cures the ill-conditioning at large time steps that the original scheme suffers from along with the late time instabilities caused by the static solenoidal nullspace. This stabilization is achieved through a generalization of the quasi-Helmholtz projectors adapted to the high-order space basis functions and the high-order implicit schemes used by the convolution quadrature method.

articleTitle: A Dual Band Pole Shaped Planar Antenna for WLAN and WiFi 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper introduces a dual band planar microstrip antenna designed to operate within the frequency bands 2.25 - 2.75 GHz and 5.39 - 5.57 GHz, specifically tailored for WLAN and WiFi 5G devices. The proposed design features a single antenna element on RO4350B substrate with dimensions measuring 67 × 45 ×1.52 mm3. The dual band functionality is achieved by incorporating a T-shaped radiator on the feedline and adding another with longer arms positioned atop the initial radiator. The impedance bandwidth is enhanced by adjusting the length and width of the arms of T-shaped radiator. The antenna demonstrates a peak gain of 2.4 dBi at 2.25 GHz and 4.68 dBi at 5.57 GHz respectively. Furthermore, its radiation efficiency surpasses 90% across the entire operating bands.

articleTitle: Propagation of Electromagnetic Waves Excited by a Capacitive Coupler in a Cylindrical Water
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: The electric near field generated by a capacitive coupler rapidly decays in air, but if a dielectric is placed within the range where the near field spreads, some electromagnetic waves are excited in and on the dielectric material. The wave propagates through the dielectric as a transmission line and carry electric power. It is found that common materials such as water can be used as a cable to deliver microwave. In this study, a longitudinal electric field generated from a coupler resonating at 2.45 GHz was injected into a column of fresh water to investigate the propagation characteristics of electromagnetic waves propagating through water by simulations. Water has high permittivity and can be a low-loss transmission line in GHz band. A cylinder of water 16 mm in diameter and 1 m long could transmit power at 2.45 GHz with a path loss of −4.2 dB.

articleTitle: Towards Superdirectivity of Printed Dipole Arrays Using Loaded Complementary Split Ring Resonators
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper discusses enhancing conventional printed dipole antenna arrays towards superdirectivity. By geometrically augmenting the dipole with loaded complementary split ring resonators, the surface current is tuned to increase the benchmark element directivity to from 3 to 5.5 dBi and the 3-element linear array directivity from 6.2 to 9.5 dBi at 30 GHz.

articleTitle: Moisture Sensing in Cutaneous Tissues Using Terahertz and Millimeter-Wave Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, the reflection properties of cutaneous tissues were investigated under three moisture conditions (wet i.e. water moistened, greased, dry). Using bistatic radar setups, reflection properties of the moistened tissues were garnered at millimeter-wave (mmWave) and Terahertz (THz) frequencies. Specifically, measurements were conducted at 32–34 GHz, 147–151 GHz, and 200–204 GHz. We show in our analysis that the water moistened cutaneous tissue exhibited higher reflection coefficient when compared to greased and dry skin conditions. Furthermore, dry skin exhibits the lowest reflectivity, with greased skin showing slightly higher levels. It was also observed that the maximum reflection loss (measured in dB) increased with increasing frequency i.e. from mmWave to THz. This work will aid the remote assessment of moisture conditions of cutaneous tissues at mmWave and THz frequency bands.

articleTitle: Compact RF Measurements in GTEM Cells for Electrically Small Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Electrically small antennas continue to be a topic of research for design of compact transmitters and receivers for physically limited volumes and frequency of operation at large wavelengths. One practical challenge in the difficulty of quantifying their far-field performance is that such antennas could necessitate large anechoic chambers. This paper presents a compact manner in which electrically small antennas could be assessed through the use of a Transverse Electromagnetic Mode (TEM) cell, specifically one of which that could operate in the lower GHz range. Three electrically small antennas, 100 MHz, 435 MHz and 1000 MHz are assessed using the GTEM-cell, and their radiation efficiency is measured using conventional gain-substitution methods. This demonstrates that GTEM-cells could be a potential solution for a benchtop measurement system in analyzing and assessing electrically small antennas.

articleTitle: Wideband Frequency Selective Surfaces-Based Absorber with Improved Bandwidth-to-Thickness Ratio
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: An ultrathin microwave absorber with a high bandwidth-to-thickness ratio (BTR) using frequency selective surface (FSS) is designed in this paper. It is a simple model developed using diagonal placement of lumped resistances at the corners of the square loop. To improve the impedance matching, the square loop has been loaded with the circular disc. The total thickness of the model is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{4.3}\ \mathbf{mm} =\mathbf{0.071}\boldsymbol{\lambda}_{\mathbf{L}}$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{\lambda}_{\mathbf{L}}$</tex> is the operating wavelength at the lowest operating frequency of 5.0 GHz. The proposed absorber has a −10 dB reflectivity in the 5.0-11.3 GHz operating band with a fractional bandwidth (FBW) =77.78%. The structure has been rigorously analyzed, simulated, and fabricated to validate the concept of designing an enhanced BTR. A few results are incorporated in the paper, and the remaining will be presented during the conference.

articleTitle: Designing Interpretable AI-Driven Propagation Models for Advanced Wireless Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This study draws inspiration from successful applications in biomedical data analysis, where guiding neural networks (NNs) with domain knowledge has proven effective in enhancing model performance through the integration of expert-derived representations [3]. While existing models in this domain excel in interpretability by aligning learned features with established domain expertise, our proposed method takes a unique approach. We introduce a novel domain knowledge-guided deep neural network that goes beyond the conventional application of domain knowledge. This pioneering effort seamlessly integrates domain knowledge into neural networks specifically designed for radio propagation modeling. The approach aims to enhance interpretability in this context, presenting a promising avenue for advancing the understanding and performance of neural networks in wireless communication scenarios.

articleTitle: Initial Study of Detection and Repeatability of Microwave Imaging with Monopole Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: We are building a new Microwave Imaging (MWI) prototype to image both the breast and the axillary region, to be used as a potential complementary method for breast cancer diagnosis. In this work, we evaluated our antennas performance with simplified breast phantoms, while testing the effect of plastic in phantoms on imaging results and the repeatability of our system. Results suggest plastic has no significant effect on imaging performance. We also observed operator's interference may hinder repeatability of the system.

articleTitle: A Metamaterial Composite Sensor that Simultaneously Detect Multiple Physical Quantities
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
