abstract: A theory of a composite sensor is proposed that can simultaneously detect temperature, strain and pressure. The sensor uses changes in dielectric constant to detect temperature, changes in cavity thickness to detect pressure, and separation distances between units to detect strain. The distinct electromagnetic energy regions associated with the three sensing mechanisms facilitate easier decoupling. This sensor design incorporates textured closed surfaces and frequency-selective surfaces, both of which were employed in simulations, demonstrating excellent independent sensing performance.

articleTitle: High-Sensitivity K-Band Dielectric Sensors Using Multi-Coupled Complementary Split-Ring Resonators
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper introduces a highly sensitive dielectric sensor designed for permittivity measurement in the K-band, specifically for substrate characterization. Through theoretical sensitivity analysis, an enhanced design with multiple complementary split-ring resonators (CSRRs) in odd mode configuration improves sensitivity. Experiment results demonstrate an 88% improvement (from an average sensitivity of 4.2% to 7.5%), enabling effective detection of subtle variations in dielectric coefficients for relative permittivity values ranging from 1 to 10 in K-band applications.

articleTitle: High Gain Circularly Polarized Antenna for Millimeter Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: A design of high gain circularly polarized antenna based on printed ridge gap waveguide technology is proposed. The design depends on using a hybrid coupler to feed two spatially orthogonal magneto-electric dipoles. Simulation results reveal a maximum gain of 11.8 dBi with 23.7% relative band-width at 29.5 GHz. Additionally, the axial ratio obtained from simulations is effectively less than 3 dB over the band. These are powerful figures for many applications demanding CP antennas with high gain to achieve effective performance.

articleTitle: Implementation and Applications of Antenna Utilizing Hinge of Foldable Mobile device
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Foldable mobile devices have become a mainstream topology in recent years. This study aims to utilize the hinge section of such devices to augment the performance deterioration of antennas especially at high frequencies. Specifically, by integrating an Antenna-on -Display (AoD) operating in the mmW Ka band, we address challenges posed by folding/unfolding conditions and enhance antenna performance through simultaneous operation in semi-folded states. For closed-states, the Antenna-on-Hinge (AoH) is realized through an Aperture-coupled antenna situated within the hinge region. This enables the combination of the Antenna on Hinge (AoH) with Antenna-on-Display (AoD) in foldable phones, allowing the formation of Broadside-Endfire beamforming.

articleTitle: 2-Bit Vialess Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface Design for Dynamic Beam Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This study presents a novel 2-bit vialess Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface (RIS) design for beam steering in the mmWave frequency band. Utilizing four distinctive coding sequences and an embedded varactor, tunability for phase control at 28.5GHz is achieved. RIS arrays with different coding patterns were developed, demonstrating flexibility in terms of dynamically controlling electromagnetic waves and showing a strong correlation with the desired beam steering. The proposed design offers potential advantages including simplified fabrication processes and reduced losses, making it promising for 5G network applications.

articleTitle: A Wideband Circularly-Polarized Reflectarray Element with 1-Bit Phase Resolution
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a wideband circularly-polarized(CP) reflectarray element with 1-bit phase resolution is proposed to realize flexible beam-scanning capability. The unit cell consists of a split square ring with two attached metallic line and an intact square ring, which are printed on a single-layer dielectric sheet, thus enjoying the advantages of low-profile and easy to manufacture. Two groups of PIN diodes are introduced into the splits to alter the operating situation of element and change the reflection phase. The simulation results shows that the proposed element exhibits wide bandwidth characteristic from 10.3 GHz to 18.5 GHz, corresponding to 57% relative bandwidth.

articleTitle: On the Bandwidth Capabilities of Connected Slot Arrays
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Connected arrays constitute an appealing solution of phased arrays for their ultrawideband properties and their compact, planar structure. In this work, we introduce a unit-cell for a connected slot array, which explores the limits of this architecture both in terms of bandwidth and field of view. Five artificial dielectric layers (ADLs) cover the radiating aperture, matching the antenna to free space. The resulting design operates from 5–20 G Hz and is able to scan up to 60° in elevation along the E-, D-, and H-planes while being suitable for fabrication in PCB technology. Finally, the numerical results are compared against a theoretical low-frequency limit introduced recently in the literature.

articleTitle: Electro-Optic Heterodyning Technique for 79 GHz Automotive Radar Antenna Measurement
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a precise and compact antenna measurement system for automotive radar antenna operating at 79 GHz is proposed. A planar field imaging system with an electro-optic sensor is developed to measure magnitude and phase in the reactive near-field region of the array antenna. A detailed electro-optic heterodyning technique to measure vectoral electric field distribution at the W-band is discussed. To validate the performance of the proposed planar imaging system, a comb-line array antenna characterization at 79 GHz is conducted. The radiation far-field pattern and gain, calculated from the near-field measurements, are in good agreement with each other according to a comparison of these outcomes.

articleTitle: A mm-Wave Wireless Pressure Sensor Array based on Thin Metamaterial Passive Resonators
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Pressure represents a fundamental parameter in a large number of applications. Often it is necessary to understand not only the value of the pressure but also the point at which it is applied. This can be achieved with an array of sensors. In this work, a completely wireless pressure sensor array which does not require any electronic components is proposed. The array comprises four blocks and each block is made up of a 4 × 4 periodic surface. By exploiting the different length of the resonators in each block it is possible to detect the pressure thanks to the shift of the resonance peak.

articleTitle: An Additively Manufactured Orthomode Transducer for Satellite Communications Antenna Feed Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: This paper describes a wideband 3D-printed orthomode transducer (OMT) designed for the X-band satellite communication band. The OMT architecture is based on a symmetrical turnstile junction with a rectangular waveguide network. Notably, the symmetrical design gives a natural isolation between orthogonal polarisations, achieving a greater operational bandwidth. The fabrication is completed by 3D printing together with manual in-house conductive painting. The measurements align well with simulations, proving the viability of the theory. The fabricated OMT realises complete coverage of the SATCOM X-band from 7.2 to 8.6 GHz. The return loss is larger than 20 dB at the two rectangular waveguide ports, where the isolation is greater than 35 dB. Measurements indicate this structure meets the requirements of a feeding system for modern satellite communication antennas. 3D printing also showcases the promising application of additive manufacturing technology, with comparable performance to traditional metal machined components.

articleTitle: High Gain Off-Body Antenna for WBAN Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a novel high-performance off-body antenna design is presented for wireless body area network (WBAN) applications. The antenna is composed of three layers: an AMC substrate, a planar monopole, and an FSS superstrate. The integrated design was placed around an arm of human body model with optimal separation distance. Simulation results reveal that the antenna exhibits an impedance bandwidth of 3.13% (5.74–5.92 GHz), a peak gain of 10.73 dBi and total efficiency of 88.64% at 5.8 GHz ISM band. These characteristics show that the suggested antenna is a good candidate for off-body wearable applications.

articleTitle: Bandwidth and Gain Enhanced SIW Cavity-backed Slot Antenna with Simple Stacked Parasitic Patch
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a broadband and high gain substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) cavity-backed slot antenna has been developed with a stacked configuration. The proposed antenna comprises a rectangular cavity with a bow-tie slot, an SIW, a microstrip line-to-SIW transition, and a stacked parasitic patch. An additional resonance is created at a higher frequency by properly optimizing the parasitic patch above the cavity-backed slot, improving the bandwidth and gain significantly. Compared with the SIW cavity-backed slot antenna, the impedance bandwidth and peak gain are increased from 5.12% (for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\vert S_{11}\vert \leqslant - 10 dB$</tex>) to 19.7% and 7.4 to 8.67 dBi, respectively. The overall size of the proposed antenna is 14 mm × 12 mm × 0.85 mm. The proposed design technique is easy to implement and promises to overcome the limitation of the narrow bandwidth of cavity-backed slot antenna without increasing its overall footprint.

articleTitle: Machine-Learning-Based Design of Space-Time-Coding Digital Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Digital metasurfaces employing space-time coding have proven to be a powerful platform for joint spatial and spectral control of electromagnetic waves. Despite their effectiveness, the general design of these metasurfaces poses significant computational challenges. In this study, we tackle this issue by introducing a generalized autoencoder based on deep neural networks. This innovative approach allows for the simultaneous and independent synthesis of harmonic scattering patterns, offering precise control over harmonic tapering and phasing, and improving spectral efficiency.

articleTitle: Reflectance Measurement Method with a Large Incident Angle Based on Two-Ray Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: In this paper, a far-field reflection coefficient measurement method with a large incident angle to meet the measurement requirements of millimeter-wave channels is proposed based on two-ray model. Accurate on-site measurement of reflection coefficients in the millimeter-wave frequency range is achieved using this method. The simulation results indicate the angle error is below 1% when the incident angles are greater than 87 degree. Compared to traditional methods, this measurement approach is more accurate, operationally convenient, and does not require measurement signal phase, which meets the demand of on-site reflection coefficient measurements under large incident angle conditions effectively.

articleTitle: Welcome Message from the General Co-Chairs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and INC/USNC‐URSI Radio Science Meeting (AP-S/INC-USNC-URSI)
abstract: Dear colleagues and friends, It is our great pleasure to welcome you to the beautiful city of Florence for the 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation and ITNCUSNC-URSI Radio Science Meeting, at the “Fortezza da Basso“ Convention Center from July 14 to 19, 2024. This conference will be an exciting and informative event that will bring together leading researchers, engineers, and practitioners from around the world to share their knowledge and expertise on the latest advances in antennas and propagation, radio science and electromagnetic engineering. The event is cosponsored by the IEEE Antennas and Propagation Society (IEEE AP-S), the Italian National Committee (ITNC) and the US National Committee (USNC) of the International Union of Radio Science (URSI).
